title: BLOCKER: Android file dialogs completely non-functional (Open/load/save) — app unusable
description:
On the Pixel device, NO file dialog appears for any file operation: main Open (DXF/SVG/project), machine-setup load/save, tool-library load/save, project save, G-code/STL export. App is unusable for real work without this. No visible error toast was reported either.

ATTEMPTED (round 5, did NOT fix — built blind):
- Capability windows:[main]→[*]. NOTE: gen/android assets/tauri.conf.json shows the Android webview label IS 'main' (app.windows[0].label='main'), so the original [main] already matched — the label theory was WRONG; capability scope is likely not the cause.
- content:// SAF URI handling in openAny/openFile (read via plugin-fs + content-sniff + content-based loader).
- Collapsed multi-dot filter extensions; wrapped dialog calls in try/catch → reportError.
None changed the symptom.

CONFIRMED FACTS:
- @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog ^2.7.1, plugin-fs ^2.5.1 installed; tauri_plugin_dialog::init()/fs registered unconditionally in lib.rs.
- Android conf: withGlobalTauri:false (─ __TAURI_INTERNALS__ is still injected regardless), security.capabilities:[] (inline caps; file-based caps in capabilities/ are compiled via generate_context!).
- file_ops.openAny: if isTauri() → plugin-dialog open(); else → hiddenOpenInput().click() (a web <input type=file>).

TOP HYPOTHESES (verify on-device, in order):
1. isTauri()/transport: if window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ is absent on Android, isTauri()=false → file ops fall to the web hidden-<input> path, which likely does nothing in the Android System WebView AND raises no error (matches 'dialog does nothing, no toast'). resolveApiChoice would also pick wasm/http instead of tauri. CHECK FIRST.
2. Dialog plugin SAF activity-result path not wired (plugin returns/throws). If isTauri() IS true, open() may throw → confirm whether ErrorToast even renders on the phone layout (it may be hidden), so failures could be invisible.
3. Capability ACL not actually compiled for the mobile target (despite files present).

REQUIRED NEXT STEP — ON-DEVICE DIAGNOSTICS (cannot be fixed blind):
- adb logcat while tapping Open (filter RustWebView/Tauri/chromium) to capture the JS error / plugin response.
- chrome://inspect remote-debug the WebView: evaluate typeof window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__, check the active transport, call the dialog open() directly and read the rejection.
- Add a temporary on-screen debug readout (isTauri, transport, last error) to the About screen so state is visible without a cable.
Then fix the identified cause. This is the #1 priority for the next session.
notes: PROGRESS (round 9): After the onActivityCreate fix, dialog OPENS but .dxf files are unselectable ('keine Elemente'/greyed). Cause: dialog plugin maps extension filters -> MIME via MimeTypeMap.getMimeTypeFromExtension; .dxf/.ngc/.plt have no registered MIME so they're dropped from EXTRA_MIME_TYPES => unselectable. FIX: added isAndroid() (env.ts) and openFilters() helper (file_ops.ts) that passes an EMPTY filter array on Android for openAny/openFile/openProject => intent.type=*/* with no EXTRA_MIME_TYPES => all files selectable; we already content-sniff bytes after picking. Empty array (not omitted) because the Kotlin filters field is non-null. Frontend gates green (svelte-check 0, eslint/prettier clean). Rebuilt+staged 19:38. AWAITING confirm: select example.dxf from Downloads should now load.
close_reason: Fixed on-device (commits c1df245, 64dc5e9): registered the plugin activity-result launcher via MainActivity.onActivityCreate, and drop SAF extension filters on Android so .dxf etc. are selectable. Verified on Pixel: Open (DXF/SVG/project), STL export, machine JSON save all work.

title: Non-finite coords emit poison G-code: fmt_num_dp lacks is_finite guard
description: crates/ivac-core/src/gcode.rs:1867 fmt_num_dp formats every X/Y/Z/I/J/F/R word with no is_finite check. NaN->'XNaN', inf->'Xinf' = invalid G-code rejected mid-program. Add is_finite guard at the formatter.
close_reason: Closed

title: cargo-deny advisories gate red: serde_yaml RUSTSEC-2024-0320 not ignored
description: xtask depends on serde_yaml 0.9.34+deprecated (RUSTSEC-2024-0320, unmaintained). Not in deny.toml ignore list, so 'cargo deny check advisories' — run by ci.yml and scripts/pre-release.sh — fails on a clean tree. Fix: add ignore entry with justification, or drop serde_yaml from xtask.
close_reason: False positive. Verified locally: 'cargo deny check' and 'cargo deny check advisories' both pass (exit 0, 'advisories ok'). serde_yaml 0.9.34+deprecated is present (xtask dev-dep only) but is NOT flagged as a failing advisory by the current advisory DB / cargo-deny defaults. No ignore entry needed; adding one for RUSTSEC-2024-0320 would be speculative noise. Re-evaluate only if cargo-deny actually goes red.

title: CRITICAL: Scene3D leaks most GPU geometry/materials on every 2D<->3D pane swap
description: components/Scene3D.svelte:507-554. onDestroy disposes only 3 of ~8 owned groups; importedLinesObject, toolpathLinesObject, arrows, assignmentOverlayObjects, tabsGroup, approachGroup, fixturesGroup, warningGroup all leak. renderer.dispose() does NOT walk the scene graph to free those buffers. Scene3D unmounts on every pane swap (comments line 57-60), so each swap on a large DXF leaks a full toolpath + wireframe. disposeGroup() helper already exists, just not wired into teardown. Same .clear()-without-dispose bug leaks per-edit in updateTabs (1392-1448) and updateApproach (1455-1487). FIX: disposeGroup over all groups + standalone line objects in onDestroy; replace .clear() with disposeGroup in the two update fns.
close_reason: Fixed in 10e85dd: dispose geometryGroup/fixtures/tabs/approach/warning groups in onDestroy; disposeGroup broadened to THREE.Line; updateTabs/updateApproach use disposeGroup not .clear().

title: CRITICAL: redo after coalesced slider/number drag restores FIRST value not final — silent data corruption
description: state/history.ts:96-106. On coalesce, cmd.apply(state) runs but the new command is never pushed; only the first wrapper survives, and its apply captured original->first-value. Drag depth 0->100: undo correctly gives 0, but redo gives 1 (reviewer reproduced: 'expected 1 to be 100'). Corrupts EVERY coalesced field (op fields, stock dims, work offset, machine, text, transforms) on the common edit->undo->redo path. Existing coalesce test only asserts undo, so it slipped through. FIX: point retained wrapper's redo target at the latest apply closure; add a redo-after-coalesce test. Verified in source.
close_reason: Fixed in 1f9715e: repoint retained entry's apply at latest coalesced command so redo replays final value. Regression test added.

title: CRITICAL: fixed-sensor post-change probe drops Z before XY traverse to sensor — rakes new tool across table
description: pipeline.rs:2065-2068. Emit order is rapid_machine_z(pz) -> rapid_machine_xy(px,py) -> probe. Head descends to sensor approach height pz while still parked at tool-change XY, then traverses XY across the table at that low Z. Any clamp/fixture/part between change pos and sensor gets hit. XY-first-at-safe-Z then Z-down is universally correct. FIX: swap the two calls — rapid_machine_xy first, then rapid_machine_z. Verified in source.
close_reason: Fixed in a71cc92: swapped to XY-first-at-safe-Z then Z-descend in emit_post_change_z FixedSensor. Updated ordering test.

title: CRITICAL: GRBL fixed-sensor probe applies NO tool-length offset — first cut off by full tool-length delta
description: gcode/grbl.rs:260-268. On GRBL/grblHAL set to FixedSensor, pipeline emits a real G38.2 probe (probe_toward_z -> inner G38.2), then apply_probed_tool_length emits ONLY a comment '; tool length offset set by controller ($341 tool-measure)'. But $341 is grblHAL's own M6 macro — it is NOT triggered by our hand-rolled G38.2. So the machine physically probes the tool and continues cutting with ZERO compensation: first cut off by the full tool-length delta = crash or scrapped part. FIX: emit a real offset-setting sequence for grblHAL, OR hard-block GRBL+FixedSensor with a pipeline error like the i185 guard does for GRBL+ATC. Verified in source.
close_reason: Fixed in a71cc92: critical grbl_fixed_sensor_no_offset pipeline warning blocks Generate when GRBL+FixedSensor would emit an uncompensated cut; honest GRBL comment. Test grbl_fixed_sensor_without_template_warns.

title: audit 2026-05-23: external thread helix is geometrically tangent — no engagement, no thread cut
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/op_drivers/thread.rs:128-171
REPRO: Thread op with internal=false, stud radius 3.0mm, single-point cutter dia 2.0mm (tool_radius 1.0). Final pass sets pass_radius = helix_radius = bore_radius + tool_radius = 4.0. Cutter centerline at distance 4 from center; inner edge at 4-1=3 = stud_radius. Tooth just KISSES stud surface — zero radial engagement, zero profile cut.
CONSEQUENCE: External threads emit clean-looking helical toolpath that cuts nothing. User gets polished stud with no thread.
FIX: For external threading, helix_radius = stud_radius + tool_radius - thread_depth so cutter's inner edge sits at stud_radius - thread_depth. Add thread_depth_mm to OpKind::Thread (or derive from pitch via ISO 0.6495*pitch for 60°). Update internal too: helix = bore - tool + thread_depth.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: drill peck G83 R-word anchored at start_depth, not at top of hole when start_depth != stock top
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:436-437 (emit_drill_block); crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/linuxcnc.rs:550-565 (drill_peck)
REPRO: Pocket with stock proud of Z=0 (e.g. start_depth=+2 but stock at +3). emit_drill_block sets r=setup.mill.start_depth. For G83/G73, R = retract plane after each peck. If R BELOW stock surface, bit retracts inside chip-clogged hole, defeating peck. If R high above stock, every peck wastes G83's rapid down to R.
CONSEQUENCE: Slow, chip-clogged, snapped drill bit when start_depth doesn't match stock top. co8b re-entry clearance is decoupled from LinuxCNC G83 path.
FIX: Separate 'retract plane R' (just above stock top, measured from stock surface) from 'entry plane' (start_depth or fast_move_z). Emit R = max(start_depth, stock_top_z + small_clearance).
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: laser never turned ON during cuts (mode != Mill gates exclude laser)
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:372, 438, 610 (call sites of spindle_on)
REPRO: Project with mode=Laser + Engrave op + LaserBeam tool. emit_toolchange_envelope DOES call post.spindle_cw at program start. But every emit_offset/emit_drill_block/emit_vcarve_block gates spindle_on behind 'mode == Mill'. NO per-cut laser-on, no power-modulation, no M3 S0 for rapids.
CONSEQUENCE: Either (a) laser never fires for any cut (single-laser single-op cache hit path) — silent no-cut, or (b) laser fires at full power from program-start through every G0 rapid between ops — burns everything in head's path.
FIX: Replace 'mode == Mill' gates with laser_pulse(power) post hook emitting M3/M4 S<power> on cut entry + M5 (or M3 S0) on cut exit. Wrap G0 rapids in laser-low/off envelope.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: Project.work_offset (i5g4) unreachable from frontend — feature is dead code
description:
FILE: frontend/src/lib/api/build-project.ts:381-388 (WireProject), 770-784 (buildProject)
REPRO: WireProject has no work_offset field. ProjectFile / ProjectState carry no work_offset state. Generated TS shows field exists in OpenAPI but FE doesn't use it.
CONSEQUENCE: WCS-origin warning in pipeline-warnings can be raised but user CANNOT set WorkOffset to silence it. Sim heightmap stays misaligned when machine zero differs from geometry origin. Entire i5g4 MVP is unreachable.
FIX: Add workOffset to ProjectFile + ProjectState defaults, surface 'Work offset' sub-section in MachineDialog or new ProjectSettings panel, pass through buildProject when non-default.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: new ToolEntry fields (spindle_direction/stickout/kerf) silently dropped at FE→Rust
description:
FILE: frontend/src/lib/api/build-project.ts:103-146 (WireToolEntry), 451-510 (buildTool); frontend/src/lib/state/project-types.ts:93-188
REPRO: Any user-set spindle_direction / stickout_length_mm / kerf_mm can NEVER reach the pipeline. Wire schema and buildTool() omit all three. FE ToolEntry lacks the fields.
CONSEQUENCE: z1y0 (left-hand cutters never emit M4), q0kc (stickout never reaches sim holder check), mmu8 (kerf stays at legacy 0.15mm default) — three Rust-side features shipped but unreachable.
FIX: Add three optional fields to FE ToolEntry interface + WireToolEntry interface + buildTool() spread (skip-on-default).
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: Pause op emits raw M3 ignoring tool.spindle_direction (CCW programs restart CW)
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs:740
REPRO: Project with CCW tool, Pause op in middle. Pause emits M5...M0 M3. M3 = CW; tool was CCW. After operator presses Cycle Start, spindle restarts CW. Also no S<rpm> → controller may stall or run at last-known.
CONSEQUENCE: Wrong direction on resume + indeterminate RPM. Resume state doesn't match pre-Pause direction.
FIX: After M0, do post.reset_state() so the next op's spindle_on re-emits with the right direction. Currently the raw M3 pre-empts that.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: prev_tool_id pessimistically set to finish_id even when no actual swap happened
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs:911-915 (fresh path), 802-806 (cache hit)
REPRO: Op A has tool_id=1, finish_tool_id=2 but produces NO finish offsets (cascade carved only boundary, dual_tool falls through to single-emit). prev_tool_id still set to Some(2). Op B has tool_id=2 → tool_changes = (Some(2)!=Some(2)) = false. NO envelope emitted. Machine state: still tool 1 in spindle.
CONSEQUENCE: Wrong-tool cut. Comment at line 905 claims 'safety-biased' but only safety-checks case where next op asks for ROUGH tool, not when next asks for finish_id.
FIX: Track whether dual_tool/stufenfase actually emitted internal toolchange (return bool) and only update prev_tool_id on real swap.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: emit_toolchange_envelope hardcodes M3 — CCW tools (z1y0 regression) cut wrong direction
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs:1065, 1108
REPRO: Tool with spindle_direction=Ccw. Envelope calls post.spindle_cw(t.speed, 0) unconditionally. Post stores last_speed=Some(speed). When cut block calls spindle_on(Ccw)→spindle_ccw, dedupe check last_speed != Some(speed) is FALSE → M4 elided. Net: M3 emitted, M4 never emitted.
CONSEQUENCE: Every CCW tool that crosses M6 (= every CCW tool not first-only) runs CW. Left-hand drills/threads cut backwards or self-extract. Z1Y0 fix only protected first-op path via spindle_on; the toolchange envelope was never routed through it.
FIX: Read tool.spindle_direction in emit_toolchange_envelope and route through central spindle_on dispatcher.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: timing.rs treats GRBL G4 P-value as seconds but GRBL P is milliseconds
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/sim/timing.rs:112-152
REPRO: GRBL gcode containing G4 P500 (= 0.5 s on GRBL). sum_g4_dwell_seconds treats P as seconds, credits 500 s.
CONSEQUENCE: Severe timing overestimate on every GRBL post — drill peck dwell, spindle warmup, etc — sim says program 8+ minutes longer than actual. Doc comment incorrectly claims 'P is canonical seconds (LinuxCNC, GRBL)'.
FIX: Make unit decision flavor-aware: read machine flavor/dialect, divide by 1000 for GRBL-style.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: pocket_zigzag with nocontour=true leaves tool-radius-wide uncut stripe at every wall
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:1264-1270 (call) + 549-554 (zigzag self-inset)
REPRO: Pocket op with HATCH-equivalent layer, pocket_nocontour=true, zigzag strategy. boundary = parallel_offset_inward(obj, rough_delta) already insets by tool_radius. Then pocket_zigzag insets ANOTHER tool_r. Without wall ring (skipped on nocontour), outermost stroke sits 2·tool_r from original wall.
CONSEQUENCE: A tool_radius-wide ring of uncut stock left along every wall. Often unnoticed until part fails clearance.
FIX: Pass un-inset polygon points (so pocket_zigzag's self-inset matches the wall) OR pass tool_diameter=0.0 so strokes go up to inset edge.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23: trochoidal pocket bail-bridge cuts full-slot through uncut stock
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/cam/trochoidal.rs:147-156
REPRO: Hard-material trochoidal pocket on non-convex (L/U) shape where loop disc fails disc_inside_polygon at any centerline vertex. Also: first centerline vertex always falls through bail (no prev_exit).
CONSEQUENCE: 'Bail' emits Segment::line(prev, p) along centerline at FULL tool stepover — exactly the radial-engagement spike trochoidal is designed to prevent. At trochoidal feed/RPM (which assume thin chips), full-immersion cut → chatter, broken cutter, scrapped part. Every trochoidal cut starts with a non-trochoidal plunge.
FIX: End toolpath at previous loop exit + surface trochoidal_incomplete warning, OR insert ramp-down/clearance lifts between safe sub-spans.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-23 EPIC: re-audit for fitness of purpose — find regressions, gaps, real-world correctness issues missed in 2026-05-22 pass

title: audit 2026-05-22 EPIC: fitness-for-purpose audit findings (119 issues across 6 domains)
description:
Tracking epic for the six-domain fitness-for-purpose audit run on 2026-05-22.

The audit was scoped to algorithm correctness and real-world G-code usability — can this tool, as it stands today, produce G-code that runs on real LinuxCNC / GRBL hardware against real stock without surprising the operator?

## Filed (119 issues, by priority)
- 12 P0 — silently wrong gcode or missed collisions that can break tools / parts
- 25 P1 — wrong toolpath on common geometry, controller rejects program, or wrong feedback on the common case
- 39 P2 — edge-case wrong, missing safety check, real-world UX-as-correctness gap
- 36 P3 — missing convenience feature, telemetry gap, polish-level
- 7  P4 — micro / cosmetic

## Domains audited
1. Polygon offsets + pocket strategies + chaining (`cam/offsets.rs`, halfpipe, source_combine, chaining, geometry_cache, inscribed, trochoidal) — 16 issues
2. V-carving / chamfer / thread / halfpipe medial-axis family — 21 issues
3. G-code emission core (walk, linuxcnc, grbl, arc_fit, leads, entry, z_schedule, order, post_profile, hpgl) — 25 issues
4. Drill cycles + tabs + wirbeln — 13 issues
5. Pipeline orchestration + setup resolution + cache — 20 issues (incl. 1 closed-as-invalid in sim epic shared count)
6. 3D simulation + safety checks (sweep, holder, fixture, rapid_check, heightmap, timing) — 22 issues + 1 closed

## Headline P0 cluster (must-fix before any production use)

**Tool-change envelope safety (5 issues):**
- `k2ew` — NO M6 emitted between consecutive ops with different tools (silently keeps cutting with wrong tool)
- `eaeq` — dual_tool toolchange emits M6 with spindle still on (P1)
- `m8sq` / `rwv8` / `y7uu` — dual-tool and stufenfase M6 paths skip M5 + safe-Z (P1)

**Vertical / no-reach plunges on shaped tools (3 issues):**
- `pmpk` — V-bit plunges vertically at every medial-axis chain start (no angled approach)
- `uo1t` — chamfer ignores tool reach; width > diameter/2 drives shank into stock
- `00ia` — chamfer forced single-pass to full depth on deep V-bit chamfers

**Thread milling fundamentally wrong (2 issues):**
- `7nd2` — external climb direction inverted
- `7388` — no radial retract before pull-up; gouges thread crest on exit

**Sim does not catch real collisions (4 issues):**
- `hrex` — holder check false-positive on every fresh cut → trains users to ignore warnings
- `w84n` — fixture check ignores Z-extent of tool body (shank/holder strikes invisible)
- `50eq` — rapid_check ignores shank/holder hitting stock at G0 speed
- `3oly` — TSlot cutter modeled as flat endmill at head diameter

**Common-case toolpath wrong (1 issue):**
- `y9ho` — rectangle tab plunge-back-down uses cut feed instead of plunge feed (snaps small endmills)

**Laser / non-mill (1 issue):**
- `gd2x` — laser pierce dwell at fast_move_z (above stock), thick stock never pierces

## Cross-cutting P1 themes
- **Modal-state hygiene**: missing G17/G40/G94 prologue (sbtg), no G80 between drill blocks (olpn), full-circle G2/G3 rejected by GRBL (3p7v)
- **Units & WCS**: Inch flips G21/G20 pragma but does NOT convert numbers (w9hd); sim assumes stock-origin = gcode-origin (i5g4)
- **Island awareness**: pocket_zigzag and spiral bridges cut through islands (gp2a, kqsl)
- **Start-depth / second-op**: lead-in plunges to literal Z=0 (lyq6)
- **Safety gate broken**: blockOnCriticalSimWarnings ignores pipeline-level warnings (94sf)

## Cross-cutting opportunities
- Tool geometry beyond flat endmill (T-slot, compression, form, engraver, drag-knife) is mostly mis-modeled in sim
- Post-portability: drill cycle P-word (seconds vs ms), comment styles, axis-renaming in arc emit
- Coverage gap: no golden-corpus snapshot tests for drill / tabs / wirbeln

## Overall verdict
The geometry math (arc fit, lead direction, helix planning, Z schedule, medial axis) is largely sound. The bugs cluster around:
1. Tool-change envelope safety (spindle still spinning during M6, no safe retract)
2. Modal G-code state hygiene at program start, between ops, between cycles
3. Tool-geometry beyond flat endmill (V-bit, ball-nose, T-slot, engraver, drag-knife, laser)
4. Collision-detection completeness (shank/holder not swept, false-positives killing the warning channel)
5. Island-aware pocketing (most common real-world case)

Single-tool / mm / flat-endmill / no-islands programs on LinuxCNC may produce usable G-code today. Anything beyond that risks broken tools, ruined parts, or crashed machines.

**Recommended fix sequence**: P0 cluster first, then the P1 modal-state + units + island P1s. After that, revisit the verdict.

## Search
All issues filed with title prefix `audit 2026-05-22`. Use `bd search "audit 2026-05-22 <area>"` to filter by domain.
acceptance_criteria: P0 cluster (12 issues) closed, then re-audit verdict to decide whether to ship as P1 backlog or pause for P1 burn-down.
notes:
2026-05-22 fitness-for-purpose audit complete. All 119 issues closed across 5 rounds of parallel-agent fixes:

Round 1 — P0 cluster (12 issues): vertical V-bit plunge, missing M6/M5/safe-Z toolchange envelope, wrong thread direction + retract gouge, sim collision-detection gaps, rectangle tab plunge feed, laser pierce at wrong Z.

Round 2 — P1 cluster (25 issues): full toolchange envelope at 3 M6 call sites, G17/G40/G94 prologue + G80 after drill, Inch units now scale numbers, RPM clamp at machine ceiling, op-order warning, WCS-origin sanity, pipeline warnings wired to safety gate, sim shank/holder/fixture Z-extent + TSlot neck.

Round 3 — P2 cluster (39 issues): pocket+islands honoured by zigzag and spiral, vcarve medial-axis pruned + angled lead-in + below-tip warning, halfpipe corner-aware Z + flute reach, HPGL VS feedrate + arc tessellation, GRBL paren→semi rewriter, 180° arc split, program_end XY park, sim stickout + per-cell collision list + dwell estimation + ToolProfile::Compression/FormProfile/Engraver/TSlot, hash_machine + text_layers in cache key.

Round 4 — P3 polish (36 issues): GRBL G10/G92.1 z-shift, finish_step sign normalization, leadin open-contour demotion, arc-fit precision improvements, -0 suppression, per-tool spindle direction (M3/M4), HPGL newlines, BullNose f64 math, laser kerf from tool, dragknife dragoff applied, heightmap origin sampling, modal F walker, tool-changes from state not grep, frame envelope holes-aware, polar pattern tab-anchor, build_tool_index, snapshot tests for drill/tabs/wirbeln, drill P-word ms switching, wirbeln renamed to face_mill_overlay, thread start_angle + helix_radius=0 guard, vcarve medial-axis cycle walk + chord-vs-region check, source_combine layer/color inheritance, bbox-adaptive chaining tolerance, stock_to_leave field.

Round 5 — P4 polish (7 issues): pocket_cascade cap 1024→4096, approach-point warning, peck retract clearance offset, M7/M8 dedup, F-before-G0 elided, tools HashMap index.

Pipeline cache invariants maintained throughout. ~50 commits on main. 557 lib tests + 292 vitest tests pass. Open follow-ups (not audit-scope): ~16 agent-filed bd issues for adjacent features (true thread-whirling, spring-pass, frontend UI for stickout, etc.).
close_reason: All 119 audit findings fixed across 5 rounds; verdict revisited by the 2026-05-23 re-audit (ib5v) and 2026-06-01 review (7iej)

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: no M6 toolchange between consecutive ops with different tools
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs:586-778 (run_per_op loop) and crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:428-454 (program_begin).

**Problem:** The per-op orchestrator only emits post.tool(n) (which writes T<n> M6) in two places: (1) dual-tool rough->finish split inside one Pocket op (pipeline/op_drivers/dual_tool.rs:64), (2) Stufenfase chamfer-after-drill (pipeline/op_drivers/drill.rs:137). Between two distinct ops with different tool_id, NO M6 is emitted. Worse, program_begin does not call post.tool() either, so the first op never asserts a tool number. linuxcnc::tool() writes T<n> M6 unconditionally — there is no suppression. The fix is to invoke it at op boundaries; currently it is just never called between ops.

**User-visible failure:** Multi-tool programs (Op1 6mm endmill rough -> Op2 3mm endmill finish in separate ops; Drill -> Profile chain) physically keep cutting with the previous tool. Snapped cutter / scrapped part / crash. First op silently uses whatever tool is in the spindle.
acceptance_criteria: run_per_op tracks previously-emitted tool_id; at every op boundary where the next op's effective primary tool_id differs (and for the FIRST op when machine.supports_toolchange is true), emit comment + post.tool(new_id) + tool_z_shift before the op's body. Two-op project (tool 1, tool 2) emits T1 M6 ... T2 M6 in declared order; same-tool two-op project emits at most one M6 (or zero for non-toolchange machines).
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-laser-pierce: dwell happens at fast_move_z (above stock), not at cut Z
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:527-562 (`emit_offset` lead-in match arms).

**Problem:** `pierce_sec` is a laser-specific dwell intended to burn through stock before motion begins. The current sequence is:

```rust
post.move_to(Some(from.x), Some(from.y), Some(setup.mill.fast_move_z));  // rapid XYZ
if pierce_sec > 0.0 { post.dwell(pierce_sec); }                          // dwell at fast_move_z!
post.linear(None, None, Some(0.0));                                       // then plunge to z=0
```

The dwell fires while the laser head sits at `fast_move_z` (commonly 5–25 mm ABOVE the work surface). At that distance the beam is defocused; piercing won't happen — the dwell wastes time, the next G1 starts cutting before the spot has burned through, and the first cut yanks unmelted material.

The correct sequence per every commercial laser CAM (Lightburn, T2Laser, Estlcam laser plugin): rapid to XY at safe height with laser OFF, plunge to cut height, dwell at cut height with laser ON, then start cutting motion.

**Worked example:** laser tool with `laser_pierce_sec = 0.6`, fast_move_z = 10, cut at z=0:
- Wiac emits: `G0 X10 Y0 Z10\nG4 P0.6\nG1 Z0\nG1 X20 Y0` — dwell at 10 mm above the stock; cut starts at z=0 immediately with no pierce.
- Expected: `G0 X10 Y0 Z10\nG1 Z0\nG4 P0.6\nG1 X20 Y0` — head reaches focus, dwells to pierce, then cuts.

Also: M3 (laser ON) is currently fired in emit_offset before the rapid; in practice that fires the laser at full power during XY traverse — actively scorching the workpiece along the rapid path. The standard laser sequence is M3 S0 (laser armed, zero power) for traverse, then S<power> AT pierce time.

**Real-world impact:** A real diode/CO2 laser running this gcode either scorches the workpiece during the rapid (M3 issued before traverse) AND/OR fails to pierce thick stock (dwell at wrong Z) and stalls the first cut on uncut material.
acceptance_criteria: The pierce dwell is emitted AFTER the plunge to z=0, not before. New test `laser_pierce_dwells_at_cut_z` verifies the line ordering: G1 Z0 appears BEFORE the G4 P<pierce_sec> in the emitted lead-in. Optional follow-up: emit M3 S0 for laser-mode rapids and S<power> just before pierce.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 tabs: rectangle tab plunge-back-down uses cut feed instead of plunge feed
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/tabs.rs:184-189 in fn emit_line_with_tabs (non-ramp branch); same defect at lines 73-81 (arc branch). **Problem:** After walking across a tab footprint at tabs_z, the cutter drops back to cut_z via post.linear(None, None, Some(cut_z)). The active feedrate is rate_h (cut feed) — set at gcode.rs:803 before emit_path_with_tabs. The drop is a vertical move at horizontal cut feed (often 2-5x the safe plunge rate). **Real-world impact:** Every tab traversal slams the cutter down through residual stock at cut feed; on hard stock or a 3mm endmill this snaps the cutter at the first tab. Affects all Profile/Pocket ops using Rectangle tabs (the default).
acceptance_criteria: The drop from tabs_z to cut_z is emitted at plunge feedrate (rate_v); feedrate restored to rate_h before the next cut move. Snapshot test pins a Profile op with a tab and shows F<rate_v> before the drop and F<rate_h> resumed after.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: TSlot cutter modeled as flat endmill at HEAD diameter — undercut head + narrow neck not represented
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/heightmap.rs:329 (`ToolKind::TSlot | Compression | FormProfile => ToolProfile::Endmill { r }`). HolderProfile (`sim/holder.rs`) also doesn't read `tslot_neck_diameter_mm` / `tslot_neck_length_mm`.

**Problem:** T-slot cutters have a wide cutting head (the full `diameter`) sitting on a narrow neck (`tslot_neck_diameter_mm`). When the sim collapses this to a flat endmill at the head diameter, two things go wrong:
1. **False clearance on the neck**: The neck portion above the head can clear the slot opening (which is the entry kerf cut by the head). The sim doesn't know the neck is narrower than the head, so the heightmap (carved at head radius) makes the kerf appear as wide as the head — masking the case where the neck would actually drag against a tall wall.
2. **False collision on the head when retracting**: After cutting the slot, retracting the cutter requires the head to exit through the entry kerf (which it can, because the head cut it). The sim doesn't separately model 'first the head goes down, then the neck stays in the kerf while the head sweeps sideways', so any sideways move once the head is engaged will look like the cutter is grinding against the wall above the kerf entry.

`HolderProfile::from_tool` only stacks (flutes, shank, holder); the TSlot **neck above the cutting head** is omitted entirely, so the holder check can't tell whether the neck clears the slot it's working in.

**Real-world impact:** TSlot operations are exactly the kind of multi-axis-Z operation where a sim is most useful — undercutting is non-trivial to visualize manually. Today the sim either green-lights cuts that will jam the cutter or red-flags safe cuts. `Compression` and `FormProfile` likewise collapse to a generic endmill; an undercut form tool gets simulated as a straight cylinder.

**Acceptance:** `ToolProfile` gains a TSlot variant that models head + neck. HolderProfile from_tool prepends the neck (narrow) section above the head before the shank, so the holder/wall check sees the neck radius at `z ∈ [head_thickness, head_thickness + neck_length]`. A new test `tslot_neck_clears_kerf_above_head` covers an undercut slot.
acceptance_criteria: ToolProfile::TSlot variant exists; HolderProfile encodes the neck. T-slot cuts no longer collapse to a flat endmill at the head diameter.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: rapid_check uses cutting-flutes profile only — shank/holder slamming into stock at rapid speed is invisible
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/rapid_check.rs:32 (`check_rapid_against_stock` is called with the `ToolProfile` only, no `HolderProfile`); sim/sweep.rs:179.

**Problem:** Rapid-through-material only walks cells inside the cutting radius (`for_each_swept_cell` uses `profile.radius()`). A G0 that drops the spindle below the un-cut stock surface clearance — common when the post emits a single G0 X Y Z over a workpiece taller than the retract plane assumed by the operator — will slam the **shank or collet** into the stock at full rapid speed even though the cutting flute itself happens to skim a previously-cleared channel.

Concrete scenario: deep pocket carved 30 mm into a 50 mm stock, then a rapid travels XY across the top of the stock at z=15 (above the pocket floor but below stock top). The rapid passes over uncut stock on either side of the pocket. The cutter tip is at z=15, above the cleared channel — Clear, but the **20 mm holder** above hits the surrounding 50 mm-tall stock walls. A real G0 at 5000 mm/min hitting the holder is a violent collision.

**Real-world impact:** The single most common cause of a broken collet on a hobby machine is exactly this: 'the rapid was supposed to be above the stock' but the post-rapid clearance Z was set wrong. The sim is the user's check, and it can't see it.

**Acceptance:** rapid_check additionally walks the swept footprint inflated by holder.max_radius() and tests whether holder-envelope-at-r is intersected by any cell_z that lies above the (rapid_pz + holder_z_at_r). Emit RapidThroughMaterial with a new `subkind` field (or a new ShankRapid warning) when the holder/shank is the culprit so the user knows what to fix.
acceptance_criteria: A rapid that clears the cutter tip across stock but drags the shank through tall uncut walls emits a Critical warning. New test rapid_shank_through_stock_emits_warning covers it.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: fixture check ignores Z extent of the tool body — only the segment XY centerline + tool radius is tested against fixture height band
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/fixture_check.rs:53–61.

**Problem:** The Z gate uses only `segment.from.z.min/max(segment.to.z)` — the **tip** Z range. The shank / holder / tool body above the tip can extend many tens of mm upward and still strike a fixture (clamp, vise jaw, dog) that sits above the cutter tip's range. Example: cutter tip travels at z=-10 across a workpiece; a vise jaw with `z_top = 30` sits next to the part. The cutter shank (say flute_length=25 + holder above) absolutely sweeps through `z=-10..+30`, but the Z gate sees `seg_z_max = -10 < z_bottom = 0` and returns Clear.

The check also only inflates the segment by `tool_radius` (cutting radius) — not by `holder.max_radius()` — so a wide ER-collet nut close to a clamp is never tested at all.

**Real-world impact:** Clamps, vise jaws, work-holding stops, and fixed dogs above the stock surface are invisible to the fixture check. The user sets up a clamp that the spindle nose will smack at full rapid feed, and the sim says 'no collision'. This is the canonical 'looked safe → tool / spindle wrecked' failure mode.

**Acceptance:** Z gate also passes when the tool body (from tip up through flute_length + shank + holder.total_length) intersects `[z_bottom, z_top]`. XY inflation uses `max(tool_radius, holder.max_radius())` for the Z range above the flutes. New test `shank_strikes_fixture_above_tip` asserts a clamp at z_top=30 collides when the tool tip is at z=-10 with shank+holder extending 60mm up.
acceptance_criteria: Tool body Z extent (flutes + shank + holder) is gated against fixture z band. Inflation uses holder max radius above the flutes. shank_strikes_fixture_above_tip test passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 chamfer: forces single-pass; deep chamfer plunges V-bit beyond safe depth in one shot
acceptance_criteria: Chamfer step schedule uses the tool default DPP (or user step) to ramp down to final chamfer Z over multiple passes when |z| exceeds DPP. Cutter walks the contour at each intermediate Z, deepening on each lap. Existing chamfer test (chamfer_op_emits_constant_z_pass_at_computed_depth) updated to expect multi-pass for deeper chamfers. The contour-following at FINAL Z still happens once; only the depth schedule changes.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P0 fixes on main (chamfer reach+multi-pass: a35bd62, thread direction+retract: 3b0d490). 419 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: holder check fires false positive on every fresh cut (cutter envelope treated as holder envelope at r < cutting_r)
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/holder_check.rs:173 (`lowest_z_for_radius`) + sim/sweep.rs:63 (warnings fire BEFORE carve).

**Problem:** `lowest_z_for_radius(holder, r)` for any `r <= cutting_r` returns `points[0].0 = 0` (the tip Z) because the very first holder sample is `(0, cutting_r)`. The diagnostic pass runs before the segment carves, so for a fresh cut into uncut stock, every cell directly under the cutter still reads `cell_z = top_z`, giving `wall_height = top_z - cutter_pz > 0`. Combined with `holder_lower_z = 0` this trips the `required > 0` branch and emits a HolderCollision warning for every plunge / engagement into uncut material. The check conflates the **cutter** envelope (`r <= cutting_r` is what the cutter itself sweeps) with the **holder** envelope (everything above the flutes), so material the cutter is *meant* to remove is treated as a wall about to slam the shank.

This is masked in tests because every existing holder-check test pre-builds an already-carved pocket via `build_pocket` before invoking the check. The first plunge of any real toolpath would emit a critical-severity warning the user has to learn to ignore.

**Real-world impact:** Once the user sees holder collisions flagged on every drill / pocket / engage, the warning channel becomes noise — the user mutes or learns to dismiss it, and then a *real* holder crash sails through unnoticed. Worst case = the bit goes in, the holder strikes the wall, work piece launches.

**Acceptance:** First plunge / engage into uncut stock with a Cylinder-holder tool produces zero HolderCollision warnings. The deep-narrow-slot test still fires. A new test 'fresh_plunge_does_not_emit_holder_collision' covers it: a single Plunge segment into uncut stock with a holder set must produce `d.count(holder_collision) == 0`.
acceptance_criteria: No HolderCollision warning emitted for cells whose radial offset r <= cutting_radius (those are the cutter, not the holder). New test fresh_plunge_does_not_emit_holder_collision asserts d.count(holder_collision)==0 on plunge into uncut stock with a holder.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 chamfer: no tool-reach check; width > diameter/2 drives shank into stock
description:
Where: crates/wiac-core/src/cam/chamfer.rs:45-52 chamfer_depth + crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/setup_resolver.rs:285-303.

Problem: chamfer_depth(width, angle) = -width / tan(angle/2) with no upper bound. A V-bit physically engages stock only down to z = -(diameter/2) / tan(half) — past that, the shank starts scraping. The chamfer width that hits that limit is width_max = diameter/2 (for any angle). 

Example: a 6.35mm V-bit at 60° has diameter/2 = 3.175. If user sets chamfer width = 5mm, chamfer_depth returns z = -8.66mm — well past the bit s reach. Setup runs with that z (line 287), build_z_schedule emits a single pass to z=-8.66, the gcode drives the V-bit + shank into the workpiece at full feed. Result: shank scrape, melted/burned shank, ruined workpiece.

vcarve.rs handles this properly via tool_reach_r and effective_r_cap (op_drivers/vcarve.rs:58, 86-89). chamfer.rs does not.

Real-world impact: Broken/melted V-bit shanks; deep gouge through the workpiece edge instead of a clean chamfer.
acceptance_criteria: chamfer_depth (or its caller) caps width to (tool.diameter/2 - tool.tip_diameter/2 maybe) and warns when the user-requested width exceeds the cap. Setup_resolver also stops setting setup.mill.step = z when |z| exceeds the safe single-pass depth; instead computes a multi-pass step schedule. Unit test: chamfer_depth(10, 60) on a 6mm V-bit emits a warning + returns z clamped to the physical reach.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P0 fixes on main (chamfer reach+multi-pass: a35bd62, thread direction+retract: 3b0d490). 419 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 thread: no radial retract before pull-up, gouges just-cut thread on exit
description:
Where: crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/op_drivers/thread.rs:113-124 and crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:331-348 emit_vcarve_block.

Problem: helix_waypoints ends at the angular position the helix wound to at bottom_z, which is still at helix_radius from center (i.e. touching the just-cut thread crest). emit_vcarve_block then issues post.move_to(None, None, Some(fast_z)) which is a G0 straight up to safe Z. The cutter retracts vertically while still engaged radially against the freshly cut thread crest, scraping/galling the thread on its way out.

Production thread mills retract by: (a) spiral-out lead arc back to bore centre at constant Z, then (b) G0 up. Or at minimum: a radial G1 to centre, then G0 up.

Real-world impact: Damaged thread crests on exit; in aluminium produces a visible witness mark; in steel can pull the cutter off-axis and snap it. Threads that fail thread-gauge inspection on the last revolution.
acceptance_criteria: Thread driver appends a centre-retract waypoint (helix angular position → bore center at bottom_z) before emit_vcarve_block lifts to fast_z. For external threads, retract is a radial-outward move to a clear position. Add a unit test asserting the last cutting waypoint lies on the bore center XY before the G0 lift.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P0 fixes on main (chamfer reach+multi-pass: a35bd62, thread direction+retract: 3b0d490). 419 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 thread: external climb direction inverted; right-hand spindle climbs CW outside, not CCW
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/thread.rs:112 (dir computation) + crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/op_drivers/thread.rs:97-120 (driver passes through user climb regardless of internal flag).

**Problem:** For a right-hand spindle (M3, CW from above):
- Internal threading (cutter inside bore): climb = cutter moves opposite spindle rotation at the contact point = cutter walks CCW around the bore center = +Δθ. The current code matches this.
- External threading (cutter around stud): climb at the contact point = cutter walks CW around the stud center = -Δθ.

But helix_waypoints uses  (CCW when climb=true) UNCONDITIONALLY. The op driver passes  straight through (line 119) without flipping it for external. So an external thread with climb=true winds CCW, which is CONVENTIONAL cutting (cutter rotation same direction as feed), not climb. Result: every external climb thread is silently a conventional cut, and every external conventional setting is a climb cut — load direction reversed, chip thinning reversed.

For users running aluminium with climb selected to avoid built-up edge: getting conventional-cut force into the helix can chatter or break the thread mill at the contact face.

**Real-world impact:** External threads cut with wrong direction = wrong chip load profile, chatter, broken thread cutters, scrapped parts. The bug is silent — gcode looks right but cutting forces are inverted.

Estlcam Prog_Thread distinguishes IG (internal) vs AG (external) and reverses the helix winding accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) helix_waypoints takes an  and reverses dir when external XOR (NOT climb), or (b) the op driver flips climb before calling helix_waypoints based on . Existing tests still pass (they're all internal-style). New tests: external+climb produces CW winding (second waypoint y < 0); external+!climb produces CCW (y > 0).
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P0 fixes on main (chamfer reach+multi-pass: a35bd62, thread direction+retract: 3b0d490). 419 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 vcarve: no angled approach at chain endpoints; V-bit plunges vertically into stock
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/vcarve_emit.rs:102-104 (path push at top-of-stock) + crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:331-348 in emit_vcarve_block.

**Problem:** ratchet_emit emits the chain's first waypoint at z=0 (line 103), then the ratchet sweep drives the bit deeper-and-deeper along the spine. The bit enters at z=0 at the chain endpoint by lateral travel from a previous chain — no vertical plunge yet. BUT each chain in emit_vcarve_block goes: G0 to fast_z → G0 to (sx, sy) → G1 down to start_depth at rate_v → G1 along chain. When start_depth ≠ 0 (e.g. project start_depth = -1mm), this is a vertical G1 plunge of a V-bit. Even with start_depth=0, the ratchet's first forward sweep at level=-dpp will plunge the V-bit's tip vertically by dpp (1mm typical) on the FIRST cut move because the bit is sitting at z=0 and the next emitted point has z=-dpp.

The medial-axis chains terminate at boundary-touching vertices (R ≈ 0), so the chain endpoint sits IN the corner — the dpp-deep first plunge is in solid stock with zero clearance. A V-bit has zero tip area; vertical plunge into solid wood at dpp=1mm = tip snap or burn.

V-Carve practice (Estlcam Prog_Carve, Vectric Aspire) angles the entry: cutter rides above the surface and ramps down following the chain's spine while moving along XY, never plunging vertically.

**Real-world impact:** Snapped V-bits when DPP > the bit's safe vertical plunge depth (which is ~0 for sharp V-bits). User reports as 'wiac broke my £40 bit'.
acceptance_criteria: ratchet_emit (or a wrapper) inserts an angled lead-in over the chain's first N points so the first cut Z follows an XY-correlated ramp instead of a vertical drop. Document the ramp length in terms of bit's safe-plunge angle. Test: synthesized straight medial-axis chain has no segment whose horizontal projection is zero and vertical drop > some threshold.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 697b75e: ratchet_emit prepends an angled 10° lead-in ramp before the first cut, ensuring the V-bit never plunges vertically into the R≈0 chain endpoint. New unit test first_plunge_uses_angled_lead_in guards the invariant. Follow-ups filed: wiaconstructor-n3hn (chain-to-chain G1 plunge), wiaconstructor-ksq0 (per-tool angle config).

title: Fix: rebuildGeometry fired on every playhead frame, blocking pan/zoom during playback
description:
rebuildGeometry() reads project.playhead at the past/future fade computation. Svelte 5's fine-grained reactivity auto-tracks reads inside effect bodies (even via function calls), so the rebuild effect re-fired 60×/sec during playback. Each rebuild also reset the camera (target, position, near/far, controls.update) — fighting OrbitControls so user pan/zoom was cancelled on every frame.

Fix: bake colors at full intensity in rebuildGeometry; track per-toolpath-segment color ranges (toolpathColors); add a delta-only applyToolpathFade() that runs from the playhead $effect and mutates the color attribute slice between appliedHead and the new head. Same in-place pattern as 0jo's selection delta.

Also: move the camera fit-to-view out of rebuildGeometry into a dedicated $effect that watches only project.imported, so layer toggles / Generate / op edits no longer snap the camera back to the default angle.
acceptance_criteria: user can pan/zoom/rotate freely during preview playback
close_reason:
rebuildGeometry no longer reads project.playhead — colors are baked at full intensity at rebuild time and a new applyToolpathFade() walks only the slice between appliedHead and the new head on each playhead change, mutating the color attribute in place (attr.needsUpdate=true).

Camera fit-to-view moved out of rebuildGeometry into a dedicated $effect that watches only project.imported. Layer toggles, Generate, op edits, drag-and-drop reorders, etc. no longer snap the camera back. fitCameraToScene() is now a named helper that could be wired to a 'frame view' button later.

svelte-check 0 errors; vite build clean (Scene3D 549KB).

title: i18n infra: locale runes store, t(), en.json catalog, key codegen + drift guard, Settings language picker, auto-detect/persist
description:
Build the i18n foundation. No strings are migrated here — this lands the
machinery the extraction sweeps and tests depend on.

## Concrete workload

- frontend/src/lib/i18n/i18n.svelte.ts:
  - `locale` as a $state rune; supported list ['en','de'].
  - `t(key, params?)`: reads locale state (reactive), {name} interpolation,
    fallback active -> en -> key.
  - detect(): if stored setting is 'auto'/unset, map navigator.language
    (de* -> 'de', else 'en').
  - load/persist via existing Tauri plugin-store (key alongside ivac.settings).
- frontend/src/lib/i18n/messages/en.json + de.json (seed with a handful of
  keys to prove the pipeline; bulk comes in the sweeps).
- frontend/scripts/i18n-codegen.mjs (Node built-ins only): en.json -> keys.ts
  (`export type MsgKey = ...`). Add pnpm scripts: i18n:codegen, i18n:report.
- Wire drift guard like the OpenAPI one: regenerate + `git diff --exit-code`
  in .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/pre-release.sh.
- AppSettings: add `language: 'auto' | 'en' | 'de'`
  (frontend/src/lib/state/project.svelte).
- SettingsDialog.svelte (Appearance tab): Language dropdown -> updateSettings.

## Onboarding

- Plan: docs/i18n/PLAN.md (architecture section).
- Mirror schema codegen drift-guard pattern already in ci.yml.
- Settings state slice: frontend/src/lib/state/project.svelte (AppSettings);
  persistence already uses @tauri-apps/plugin-store.

## Blocks

Extraction sweeps (A/B/C), coverage tests, backend error catalog, docs recipe.
acceptance_criteria: t('key') works reactively in Svelte 5 markup; en.json exists; pnpm run i18n:codegen generates keys.ts; missing/typo keys fail svelte-check; CI/pre-release drift guard added; Settings has Auto/English/Deutsch; auto-detect from navigator.language; choice persisted via Tauri plugin-store; switching language updates UI live (no reload).
close_reason: Closed

title: i18n: German translation + extensible multi-language framework
description:
Ship a German translation of everything user-facing in ivaCAM, with an
extensible, coverage-tested i18n framework. Auto-detect language from the
desktop/browser locale with a manual override in Settings. Project files MUST
stay language-agnostic (load/save identically regardless of language).

## Onboarding (read before starting any child issue)

- **Full plan + architecture:** docs/i18n/PLAN.md (durable reference).
- **No existing i18n** in the repo today; clean slate. ~500-800 hardcoded
  user-facing strings across 56 .svelte components.
- **Glossary seed (German):** refs/viaconstructor/viaconstructor/locales/de/LC_MESSAGES/base.po
  (304 vetted entries). Reconciled terminology lives in docs/i18n/glossary-de.md.
- **Existing patterns to mirror:** schema codegen + `git diff --exit-code`
  drift guard (schema/openapi.yaml -> frontend/src/lib/api/generated.ts);
  dev scripts like frontend/scripts/ensure-wasm-fresh.mjs.

## Decisions locked

- Zero runtime deps: in-house i18n on Svelte 5 runes + plain JSON catalogs.
- Codegen typed keys: en.json -> keys.ts (Node built-ins only); missing keys
  become svelte-check errors.
- Scope: Svelte UI + Rust-surfaced errors/warnings + CLI.
- English base = plain English; German = established German CAM terminology.

## Quality gates (Definition of Done for the epic)

- `cd frontend && pnpm exec svelte-check` clean; `pnpm test --run` green.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude ivac-tauri` green.
- i18n codegen drift guard + coverage/parity tests wired into
  .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/pre-release.sh.
- README.md links README_de.md at the top; both kept in heading-sync.
- A new language can be added by dropping in one JSON file + one list entry.

## Per-session protocol

Follow CLAUDE.md session-completion: commit each logical change on main, push,
verify clean tree. Update child issue status as you go (`bd update <id> --claim`,
`bd close <id>`). `bd epic status` to see completion.

title: Android: intercept system back gesture for exit confirmation
description: Edge-swipe / system back exits the app abruptly from the root activity. User wants a confirmation (e.g. left-edge pull on first screen → confirm exit). Needs native onBackPressed handling in the Tauri WryActivity to emit an event to the frontend instead of finishing the activity — no stable Tauri 2 JS API for it. Deferred from round 5; the deliberate Exit menu item ships now.
design:
NEW-SESSION QUICK START — onboarding (build/deploy/logs/files): see epic ivac-7jug design + docs/BUILDING.md section "Android (Tauri mobile)".

SCOPE: intercept the Android system-back gesture natively and route it through the frontend instead of finishing the activity.

ALREADY DONE: top app-bar "< screen >" swipe navigation (swipeHorizontal action on activity-nav) — the practical fix, since the left-edge swipe is eaten by system back.

REMAINING (native + frontend):
  1. crates/ivac-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/org/opcenter/ivacam/MainActivity.kt — in onCreate register an androidx.activity OnBackPressedCallback on the OnBackPressedDispatcher; in the callback EMIT a Tauri event to the webview rather than calling finish().
  2. Frontend listener: @tauri-apps/api/event listen("android-back", ...) wired into the activity-nav state. Routing: not on first screen -> go to first screen; on first screen -> show exit-confirm; a second back -> allow finish/exit.
  3. Explore predictive-back (Android 14+) BackEvent.swipeEdge to map left/right edge -> back/forward screen (the user-requested gesture).

GOTCHA: gen/android is regenerated by cargo tauri android init; MainActivity.kt is force-tracked so the edit survives — keep it minimal and re-apply if init is rerun.

ACCEPTANCE (on device): system back from a non-first screen returns to the first screen; from the first screen it prompts confirm; confirming exits.
notes: DESIGN DECIDED (user): system back -> first screen, then exit (with confirm) on a second back; AND swipe/flick the top '‹ screen ›' panel to move between screens. Top-panel swipe DONE+staged (commit: swipeHorizontal action on activity-nav; APK 20:18) — this is the practical fix since edge-swipe is eaten by system back. REMAINING (native, separate): intercept system back in MainActivity (OnBackPressedCallback) to go to first screen / confirm-exit instead of finishing; explore predictive-back BackEvent.swipeEdge (Android 14+) to derive left/right edge => back/forward screen as the user suggested.
close_reason: Implemented native back interception (MainActivity handleBackNavigation=false + onWebViewCreate OnBackPressedCallback dispatching DOM 'android-back') and frontend routing (App.svelte -> first screen, else confirmExitApp three-way + plugin-process exit). Build-verified aarch64 debug APK (commit fa1e87e). Predictive-back swipeEdge mapping deferred. On-device validation tracked by ivac-q5ej.
