title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-no-spindle-stop-before-toolchange: dual_tool emits M6 with spindle still running
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/op_drivers/dual_tool.rs:60-64; crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/linuxcnc.rs:209-225 (`tool`).

**Problem:** When a dual-tool op (rough + finish) requires a toolchange, the driver emits:
```
post.raw("; toolchange: finish pass with tool <n>");
post.tool(finish_setup.tool.number);  // -> T<n> M6
```
without first stopping the spindle (`M5`) or moving to a safe XY (tool-change position). Most controllers do NOT auto-stop the spindle on M6 — LinuxCNC will, but only if the INI has tool-change-stops-spindle enabled. GRBL's M6 is typically NO-OP, so the spindle keeps spinning during the manual toolchange the operator is doing.

Even on LinuxCNC: the cutter is parked at the LAST contour endpoint at `fast_move_z` when M6 fires. The toolchange position depends on the INI (G28 or G30 or tool-change-position param), but the gcode doesn't say where; if the operator hasn't configured an automatic tool-change position they're spinning the chuck above the workpiece — dangerous.

Standard M6 prologue:
```
G0 Z<safe_machine_z>    (* G53 G0 Z0 — machine home Z *)
M5                       (* spindle stop *)
G4 P2                    (* dwell for spindle to stop *)
T<n> M6                  (* toolchange *)
M3 S<rpm>                (* spindle back on *)
G4 P<warmup>             (* warmup dwell *)
```

Today wiac emits only the `T<n> M6` line.

**Worked example:** rough op finishes at (50, 30) at Z=5 (fast_move_z) with M3 S12000 active. Driver emits `; toolchange...\nT2 M6`. The operator hits Cycle Start; the controller (a Mach3 with no toolchange macro): hangs waiting for the operator to swap tools while M3 is still active. Operator loosens collet with spinning spindle. Real safety hazard.

**Real-world impact:** dual-tool jobs (rough + finish with different bits) are common. The current behavior puts the operator in real danger.
acceptance_criteria: Before post.tool(...), the driver emits: G53 G0 Z<machine_home> (or fast_move_z), M5, G4 P<spindle_stop_pause>. After post.tool(...): M3 S<new_speed>, optional warmup G4 P<tool.pause>. New test dual_tool_emits_safe_toolchange_envelope covers.
close_reason: fixed by wrapping M6 in M5/safe-Z/M3 envelope — commits a877969 (helper + all 3 call sites) + 34d6efe (test fix). 5 new pipeline tests cover ordering, dual-tool, stufenfase, same-tool skip, and manual-swap.

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: stock origin and gcode origin assumed coincident — no WCS / G54..G59 / work-offset awareness
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-wasm/src/sim.rs:69 (constructor takes raw bbox (min_x..max_x, min_y..max_y) from `computeFootprint(input.imported, input.stock)`) + frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts:290-314. The Heightmap origin is fixed at the imported geometry's footprint min-corner. The toolpath comes through verbatim in **gcode coordinates** (post-multiplied by unit_scale only).

**Problem:** The post emits gcode in the active WCS (G54 by default), with X0/Y0/Z0 at whatever the operator zeros against (typically bottom-left of the stock for X/Y, top-of-stock for Z). The sim assumes (a) stock origin = footprint min-corner = (computeFootprint's min_x, min_y), and (b) gcode (0,0,0) aligns with stock origin XY at the top of stock. If the post inserts G54 X-offset (or the user zeros against a corner that isn't the geometry origin), the heightmap and the gcode are in different frames.

There is no parse of G54/G55/.../G59 nor of G92 (coordinate-system shift) in the preview interpreter. The post output is assumed-WCS-only.

**Real-world impact:** If the user's project uses a stock-corner zero (common) but the geometry was drawn with origin at part-center (very common in DXF/SVG), the simulator's heightmap is in geometry frame and the toolpath is in part-zero frame — a 50mm offset between them, the sim shows cuts in mid-air or off the stock, and the user can't tell whether their G54 offset is wrong or whether the sim is.

**Acceptance:** Project gains an explicit `stock.origin_xy` and `stock.zero_top_or_bottom` field. The simulator translates either the toolpath OR the heightmap origin to align them. Preview interpreter parses G54..G59 + G92 modal offsets. Test asserts a G54 X-10 offset shifts the carved column 10mm to the left of where it would land without offset.
acceptance_criteria: WCS offsets are parsed and applied. Stock-zero vs geometry-zero distinction is explicit in project config.
close_reason: P1 pipeline orchestration/setup fixes — commits 7749049 (w9hd), a5bd085 (3nnj), 0330120 (tnxu+i5g4), 0bfa27b (94sf). i5g4 ships the MVP (work_offset field + stock_origin_outside_geometry_bbox warning); full WCS UI tracked in wiaconstructor-abdk.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-hpgl-arcs-linearized: G2/G3 arcs flatten to a single chord, drag-knife cuts a triangle
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/hpgl.rs:75-95 (`arc_cw` / `arc_ccw` both call `self.linear(x, y, None)`).

**Problem:** When the post is HPGL, every arc — whether from DXF Arc/Circle entities, from drag-knife swivel arcs in `emit_path_with_dragoff`, or from arc-fitted polyline runs — collapses to a SINGLE chord from start to end. The arc's curvature is lost entirely.

For a DXF with a circle of radius 10 (start = (10,0), end = (10,0) after a full sweep), the linear emit produces a single `PA<x>,<y>` to the same point — a zero-length move, drawing nothing. The circle is invisible on the plot.

For a quarter-arc from (10, 0) to (0, 10), the linearized output is one chord — the plotter draws a diagonal line where a curve was expected. On a drag-knife, the blade cuts a STRAIGHT cut where the operator drew a curve.

The arc-fit pre-pass (`fit_line_runs`) is the reverse problem: it collapses curves into G2/G3 hoping to save lines, then HPGL un-curves them back into a single chord. So enabling `machine.arcs = true` on an HPGL job actively makes the output worse.

**Worked example:** DXF circle r=10 at origin:
- Wiac emits: `IN;SP1;PU;PA400,0;PD;PA400,0;PU;SP0;IN;` — pen-down on the same coord as pen-up = nothing drawn.
- A quarter arc from (10,0) to (0,10) becomes the single chord (400,0)→(0,400) — a 14.14 mm straight line where the operator expected a 15.7 mm curve.

**Fix sketch:** linearize arcs by walking them at a fixed chord tolerance (HPGL's `AA` arc-absolute is plotter-specific and limited; tessellation is universal). Use `crate::math::tessellate_arc` with a chord_max_angle of e.g. 5° so even a full circle becomes a 72-segment polygon — visually indistinguishable on plotter resolution (40 plu/mm) but actually drawn.

**Real-world impact:** HPGL is shipped as a first-class output (drag knives, pen plotters per the file comment). Today any input with arcs produces wrong output silently.
acceptance_criteria: HPGL arc_cw/arc_ccw tessellate the arc using start, end, and the I/J center into ≥8 chord segments at default tolerance. Test hpgl_circle_renders_as_polygon checks a CIRCLE DXF produces ≥30 PA<x>,<y> tokens (vs. 1 today).
close_reason: Fixed: hpgl::Post::tessellated_arc reconstructs center from I/J, walks theta CW vs CCW, emits PA<x>,<y> at ~5°/chord (min 8 chords). Full circles and partial arcs both work; drag-knife / plotter now traces the actual curve.

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: no inch/mm conversion at tool/op/machine boundary — Inch units run raw mm numbers
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/setup.rs:430-617 (MachineConfig.unit + UnitSystem), crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/setup_resolver.rs (synthesize_op_setup), and the gcode posts (linuxcnc.rs/grbl.rs).

**Problem:** UnitSystem::{Mm, Inch} exists in MachineConfig and the program_begin path emits G20/G21 accordingly. But every other parameter that uses a length — tool.diameter (mm), op.params.depth (mm), op.params.step (mm), op.params.fast_move_z (mm), feed_rate (mm/min), all the mm-named fields like wirbeln_extra_width_mm, frame_padding_mm, tip_diameter_mm — is treated as a raw number that gets emitted unchanged when unit=Inch. So a project authored in mm with machine.unit=Inch will emit `G20` + `X100.0` and the machine will interpret 100 INCHES (2540mm). The setup_resolver does no conversion at the boundary.

**User-visible failure:** Switching unit=Inch on the project does NOT convert any numeric values to inches; it just changes the unit pragma and the controller now mis-scales every coordinate by 25.4. Catastrophic on first cut.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) lock UnitSystem to Mm at the project level and treat Inch purely as a display-conversion in the frontend (every wire value remains mm; the post emits G20 with mm-to-inch-converted coordinates), OR (b) explicitly convert every mm-named field at setup synthesis when unit=Inch. Document the decision in cam/setup.rs. Add a test that the toolpath for a 100mm-wide pocket on a unit=Inch machine emits ~3.937 inch coordinates.
close_reason: P1 pipeline orchestration/setup fixes — commits 7749049 (w9hd), a5bd085 (3nnj), 0330120 (tnxu+i5g4), 0bfa27b (94sf). i5g4 ships the MVP (work_offset field + stock_origin_outside_geometry_bbox warning); full WCS UI tracked in wiaconstructor-abdk.

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: no RPM clamp against machine RPM_min/RPM_max
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/setup_resolver.rs:113-115 (rough_speed) / 116-123 (finish_speed) and crates/wiac-core/src/cam/setup.rs:430-523 (MachineConfig).

**Problem:** synthesize_op_setup resolves the RPM from project.tools via crate::project::resolve_tool_rates(tool, pass). The resolved `speed` flows into ToolConfig.speed and is emitted verbatim via post.spindle_cw(speed, ...). MachineConfig has work_area, accel, jerk, toolchange_s, rapid_speed — but NO spindle_rpm_min/spindle_rpm_max. So a tool entry with feed_rate_finish=24000 RPM on a machine that tops out at 12000 RPM emits an unreachable S24000 command. The controller either errors out or quietly caps without warning.

**User-visible failure:** Programs target spindle speeds the machine physically can't reach. Some controllers (e.g. LinuxCNC with M3 S<above-max>) error and halt mid-program. Others silently cap, producing wrong chipload — broken finish or burned tool.
acceptance_criteria: MachineConfig grows spindle_rpm_min and spindle_rpm_max (Option<u32>). setup_resolver clamps every resolved tool speed/speed_finish/speed_drill into [min, max] and pushes a 'spindle_speed_clamped' warning when clamping occurred (op_id + which pass + from/to). header_setup_for also clamps the program-header speed.
close_reason: P1 pipeline orchestration/setup fixes — commits 7749049 (w9hd), a5bd085 (3nnj), 0330120 (tnxu+i5g4), 0bfa27b (94sf). i5g4 ships the MVP (work_offset field + stock_origin_outside_geometry_bbox warning); full WCS UI tracked in wiaconstructor-abdk.

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: partial_advance synthetic-chord intermediate states don't match full-segment final state when profile is non-flat (drift)
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/sweep.rs:87-125 (sweep_segment_partial constructs a synthetic chord via lerp_pose3).

**Problem:** A partial advance through `[t_start, t_end]` builds a synthetic ToolpathSegment with endpoints `lerp(from, to, t_start)` and `lerp(from, to, t_end)`, then carves it via `sweep_chord_carve`. For Cut/Plunge (linear) this gives an identical heightmap to the full-segment carve when iterated [0..T0,T0..T1,T1..1]. For flat-bottom profiles, OK.

For non-flat profiles (BallNose, VBit, BullNose), the carve under cells near the segment endpoints uses `profile.eval(r)` where r is the distance from cell to closest point on the **synthetic chord**, then clamped 0..1 against the **synthetic chord**'s parametric range. The clamp at t=0 and t=1 of the synthetic chord 'pins' cells whose true closest-point lies *outside* the synthetic chord to the chord endpoints, with a small r there. That carved depth differs from what the full-segment carve produces for the same cells, where their closest-point r is what they actually see when the cutter sweeps past the synthetic chord boundary onto the next chunk.

Concretely: cell to the right of the synthetic chord's t=1 endpoint, with r=0.5 from that endpoint. On the synthetic chord, t clamps to 1 → r=0.5, depth = cutter_pz(t=1) + dz(0.5). On the next partial chord [t_end..1], same cell's closest-point would lie inside that next chord — and after both partials run, the cell may end up correctly carved. But there's an intermediate state (when only [t_start..t_end] has run, t_end < 1) where the cell sees the depth from the chord-endpoint clamp, not the proper sweep — and the heightmap stores the lowest value seen, which may be lower than the full-sweep result. That low value persists, even after the next chord runs (which only lowers, never raises). End-state may match or may be lower than the full-sweep state by up to `max(dz)`.

For ball-nose (max dz = R), a 6mm ball nose this is up to 3mm of false carving near chord-junction cells in a non-axis-aligned segment.

**Real-world impact:** Mid-segment frame snapshots show carving that exceeds the gcode's true depth in a thin band along the cutter path, particularly for ball-nose finishing. Once the partial run completes, may or may not be corrected by next partials — depending on whether the next chord's closest-point covers those cells.

**Acceptance:** sweep_segment_partial uses the FULL segment for profile evaluation (closest-point on real chord, not synthetic chord), but constrains the cells written to those whose t∈[t_start,t_end] on the real chord. Test: ball-nose plunge partial sweeps [0..0.5], [0.5..1] produce a heightmap bitwise-identical to the same plunge swept as [0..1].
acceptance_criteria: Partial-advance final state is bitwise-identical to full-advance for non-flat profiles. Test partial_advance_non_flat_no_drift covers it.
close_reason: Fixed: sweep_chord_carve_partial uses original segment geometry with t-range ownership flags; flat-bottom path also benefits (was overcutting at synth junctions). Test partial_advance_non_flat_no_drift covers both ball-nose and endmill.

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: ops emit in declaration order — no rough-before-finish, no drill-before-profile guarantee
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs:586-588 — `let enabled_ops: Vec<&Op> = project.operations.iter().filter(|o| o.enabled).collect()` and then a straight `for (idx, op) in enabled_ops.iter()` loop.

**Problem:** The pipeline emits ops in the user's declared list order verbatim. There is no semantic ordering pass: no rough-before-finish across separate ops, no drill-before-profile (so the outline cuts away before drill positions register on the held part), no shallow-before-deep, no same-tool grouping (to minimize toolchanges). The cache & tests confirm this (pipeline.rs:586). Although declaration-order is a defensible default, the system makes no warning when the ordering is obviously wrong (e.g. an outside-profile cuts the part free BEFORE a Drill op on the same blank).

**User-visible failure:** A typical CNC routing job 'Drill mounting holes -> Profile contour' authored in the wrong list order will cut the contour first, the part flies off the bed, and the drill op has no stock to drill. No warning surfaces this.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) automatic topological sort by op-kind safety class (drill < pocket < profile-inside < profile-outside; finish after rough within same logical group) with an opt-out flag, OR (b) a 'cut_order_unsafe' warning that detects a profile op with cut_through (`params.through_depth > 0` or `offset == Outside` cutting through stock) preceding a Drill op on the same selection. Tests cover both paths.
close_reason: P1 pipeline orchestration/setup fixes — commits 7749049 (w9hd), a5bd085 (3nnj), 0330120 (tnxu+i5g4), 0bfa27b (94sf). i5g4 ships the MVP (work_offset field + stock_origin_outside_geometry_bbox warning); full WCS UI tracked in wiaconstructor-abdk.

title: audit 2026-05-22 dual-tool stufenfase: toolchange before chamfer revolution missing M5 / safe-Z / M3 envelope
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/op_drivers/drill.rs:131-143 in fn emit_stufenfase. **Problem:** Same defect as the dual_tool driver: 'post.raw(comment); post.tool(finish_setup.tool.number); post.tool_z_shift(...);' fires immediately after the drill block ends, with no M5 / safe-Z / M3 envelope. The chamfer setup is then passed to emit_vcarve_block which calls spindle_cw lazily (gcode.rs:323) — suppressed if same speed. **Real-world impact:** drill-then-chamfer with a distinct finish tool runs the toolchange while the drill is still in (or near) the hole and the spindle is still spinning. Also: at line 132 the synthesize_finish_setup call ALSO runs when supports_toolchange=true even when finish_tool_id == tool_id (the outer if checks finish_tool_id != Some(op.tool_id) so identity case is skipped — that part is fine). **Acceptance:** Emit G0 to fast_move_z + M5 before post.tool(); emit explicit M3 + dwell + feedrate after. Same fix applied uniformly with dual_tool driver (consider extracting a shared helper).
acceptance_criteria: emit_stufenfase wraps post.tool() with safe-Z + M5 before and M3 + feedrate after. Snapshot test pins both legs of the toolchange envelope.
close_reason: fixed by routing drill::emit_stufenfase through the shared toolchange envelope — commit a877969. drill_stufenfase_change_uses_full_envelope test pins the M5-before-M6 and M3-after-M6 ordering.

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: blockOnCriticalSimWarnings ignores pipeline-level critical warnings
description:
**Where:** frontend/src/lib/components/GenerateBar.svelte:119, 166 (criticalCount = simDiagnostics warnings only); crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/warnings.rs (pipeline warnings have no severity classifier).

**Problem:** The 'block on critical sim warnings' guard in GenerateBar.run() only consults project.simDiagnostics?.warnings — sim warnings produced by sim::diagnostics::severity(). Pipeline warnings (PipelineWarning struct in pipeline.rs:132-143) such as 'tool_too_large' (offsets cascade produced no toolpath), 'frame_padding_below_tool_radius' (clamped silently), 'dual_tool_no_toolchange', 'stufenfase_no_toolchange', 'chamfer_non_vbit', 'step_unspecified' (depth=0 fallback), 'helix_radius_unfittable' have NO severity field and are not consulted by the safety gate. The block kicks in only for downstream sim warnings, not for the planning-time critical issues that produced an empty or wrong toolpath in the first place.

**User-visible failure:** A Pocket op whose tool diameter exceeds the slot width emits ZERO offsets, raises 'tool_too_large', and the program is silently truncated. The user's 'block on critical' toggle does not prevent the broken gcode from being delivered.
acceptance_criteria: PipelineWarning carries a severity field (or kind_str maps to a severity). GenerateBar's criticalCount aggregates BOTH simDiagnostics and pipeline warnings flagged critical. Test: a Pocket with tool_too_large + blockOnCriticalSimWarnings=true refuses to emit.
close_reason: P1 pipeline orchestration/setup fixes — commits 7749049 (w9hd), a5bd085 (3nnj), 0330120 (tnxu+i5g4), 0bfa27b (94sf). i5g4 ships the MVP (work_offset field + stock_origin_outside_geometry_bbox warning); full WCS UI tracked in wiaconstructor-abdk.

title: audit 2026-05-22 dual-tool: M6 toolchange emitted without spindle-stop and without safe-Z retract
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/op_drivers/dual_tool.rs:60-77 in fn run_dual_tool_or_single. **Problem:** After the rough emit_polylines_block returns, the driver immediately emits 'T<n> M6' (line 64) via post.tool(). There is no preceding M5 (spindle stop), no G0 to fast_move_z (the rough cutter may still be at depth depending on what emit_polylines_block left), no dwell before M3 restart, and no explicit M3 after the change — the next emit_polylines_block re-issues spindle_cw lazily via the delta encoder, but if speed didn't change it's suppressed entirely (linuxcnc.rs:291-300 checks state.last_speed). **Real-world impact:** (a) On a manual-toolchange machine (supports_toolchange=false, but warned only) the operator's hand is reaching into a spinning spindle. (b) On an auto-changer, M6 without a prior retract can drag the rough tool through stock during the parking move. (c) On controllers that don't auto-start the spindle after M6, the finish pass starts with a non-rotating spindle — broken cutter. The dual_tool tests assert T2 M6 appears but never check for M5 before it or M3 after. **Acceptance:** Driver emits G0 Z<fast_move_z> + M5 + dwell before M6, then M3 (explicit, not via delta-encoded spindle_cw) and a dwell after, then re-emits the feedrate before the first finish move. Snapshot test pins the M5-Z-M6-M3-F sequence.
acceptance_criteria: Before M6: G0 to fast_move_z, M5, optional dwell. After M6: explicit M3 at finish speed, dwell, restored feedrate. Snapshot test pins the full sequence and warns when supports_toolchange=false.
close_reason: fixed by wrapping M6 in M5/safe-Z/M3 envelope — same commit a877969 (helper + dual_tool call site). dual_tool_internal_change_uses_full_envelope test pins the M5 → safe-Z lift → M6 → M3 ordering.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-grbl-circle: full-circle Arc segments emit G2/G3 with start=end, GRBL rejects
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/walk.rs:280 (`emit_path_with_dragoff` arc branch — used for SegmentKind::Circle), crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/tabs.rs:67.

**Problem:** When the input geometry contains a closed circle (a single `SegmentKind::Circle` whose `start == end`), the post emits one G2/G3 with start XY = end XY:

```
G2 X<start.x> Y<start.y> I<cx-sx> J<cy-sy>
```

LinuxCNC accepts this center-format full-circle. **GRBL 1.1 rejects it** — the GRBL gcode parser explicitly errors on arcs whose endpoint equals the startpoint when using center format (`error:33` — Motion command target is invalid). The widely-cited workaround in the GRBL ecosystem is to split full circles into two semicircles.

The arc-fitter (`arc_fit.rs`) caps fitted arcs at 180° so it doesn't produce this case from polyline runs. But Circle and full-sweep Arc segments come from DXF imports (CIRCLE entities) and pass straight through.

**Worked example:** a DXF with a single CIRCLE r=10 at (0,0):
- Wiac emits: `G0 X10 Y0 Z5\nG1 Z0\nG2 X10 Y0 I-10 J0\nG0 Z5` — start = end = (10, 0).
- LinuxCNC: cuts a full circle.
- GRBL: `error:33`, program halts before the first cut. Operator has to manually edit.

**Acceptance:** when the GRBL post is selected, full-circle Arc/Circle segments are split into two G2/G3 semicircles before emission, or arc-fit pre-processes them. New test grbl_emits_full_circle_as_two_semicircles. (LinuxCNC behavior unchanged.)
acceptance_criteria: GRBL output of a DXF containing a single CIRCLE runs cleanly on GRBL 1.1+ — no error:33. Verified via simulator (or a GRBL command-line parser linter) on a corpus circle DXF.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: no safe-retract or dwell at inter-op tool boundary
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs:586-778 (run_per_op) and crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:419-426. Sister of wiaconstructor-k2ew.

**Problem:** Even once an M6 between ops is emitted (k2ew), the toolchange sequence is missing safety guards: no M5 (spindle stop), no coolant_off, no explicit retract beyond fast_move_z, no dwell after M3 with the new tool's pause. emit_polylines_block does lift to fast_move_z at end of block, but a multi-op program never spindle_off's between ops. dual_tool.rs:60-77 has the same gap.

**User-visible failure:** Machine attempts toolchange with spindle still running. ATC: dangerous. Manual-change: operator expected to stop spindle but gcode never told them. Coolant also stays on through the change.
acceptance_criteria: At every inter-op toolchange seam and in dual_tool's mid-op M6: emit M5 -> coolant_off (if active) -> raise to safe-clearance Z BEFORE post.tool(new_id); then re-emit coolant on the new tool's first cut and honor the new tool's spindle pause. Test inspects gcode for M5/M9 ordering around T2 M6.
close_reason: fixed by routing run_per_op's inter-op M6 through the shared toolchange envelope helper — commit a877969. multi_op_toolchange_envelope_has_m5_before_m6_and_m3_after pins ordering; same_tool_consecutive_ops_skip_envelope_entirely guards against envelope leaks on same-tool boundaries; non_toolchange_machine_pauses_for_manual_swap covers the hobby-machine fallback (M5 + ; pause comment + M0). Coolant_off integration deferred — see follow-up bd.

title: audit 2026-05-22 drill: no G80 canned-cycle-cancel emitted between drill block and following ops
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:358-426 emit_drill_block (and the trait drill_simple/peck/chip_break in gcode/linuxcnc.rs:361-405). **Problem:** After emit_drill_block finishes, the post emits a plain G0 to fast_move_z and returns. No G80 cycle-cancel is ever written. On LinuxCNC and most modern controllers this is safe because G0/G1 share modal group 1 with G81-G89, so the next G0/G1 implicitly cancels — BUT (a) Fanuc-style controllers and many Mach3 configurations require explicit G80 before regular moves, and (b) the rapid G0 Z<fast_z> immediately after the last G81 can be SUPPRESSED by the post's delta encoder when fast_move_z == R (drill_simple sets state.last_z = Some(r); if r == fast_move_z the Z word is dropped and the line becomes empty, so emit_drill_block's trailing move_to lifts nothing). The next non-canned move then arrives with G81 still modal. **Real-world impact:** On a controller that doesn't auto-cancel, the next G0 X Y in the following op is interpreted as ANOTHER drill cycle at the new XY — drilling holes wherever the next op routes the cutter, possibly through the fixture. Even on LinuxCNC the missing G80 is a bad-practice landmine the moment users export to anything else.
acceptance_criteria: emit_drill_block emits G80 after the last hole and before the trailing safe-Z lift. New test pins LinuxCNC output to contain G80 between the final G81/G82/G83/G73 and the subsequent G0.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-helix-walk-to-start: post-helix linear move cuts through pocket interior at rate_h
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:753 (`emit_polylines_block`/multi_pass helix_entry branch).

**Problem:** After `emit_helix_entry` lands the cutter on a small circle inside the pocket boundary, the code emits:

```rust
post.linear(Some(start.x), Some(start.y), Some(z));
```

— a straight G1 cut from the helix landing point to the path's first vertex at the new pass depth, using the configured horizontal feedrate (`rate_h`).

For the FIRST pass at depth z₁, every cell of the pocket interior is still solid. The line from the helix circle to the contour start crosses ~(pocket_radius - helix_radius) of uncut material at FULL DEPTH OF CUT, at the configured cutting feedrate. That's full-immersion straight-line cutting on a tool that was just doing a controlled helical descent — exactly the loading the helix was supposed to avoid.

The comment at entry.rs:209 acknowledges this and shrugs ('safe because the boundary path itself is already inset from the walls by tool_radius'), but that justification is wrong: insetting the BOUNDARY is irrelevant to the interior cut. The interior at depth z is solid stock, not free space.

**Worked example:** circular pocket of radius 20 with helix_radius=5, tool=3 mm endmill at -2 mm/pass:
- Wiac emits a 1.5-turn helix on a 5 mm-radius circle (gentle), then `G1 X<start.x> Y<start.y> Z-2` cutting straight from (helix_circle_landing) ≈ 5 mm radius point out to (20-1.5) = 18.5 mm radius point — that's a 13.5 mm straight-line cut at full 2 mm DOC, full-immersion, at rate_h.
- A 3 mm endmill being asked to take 13.5 mm × 2 mm × 3 mm width-of-cut in a single straight line is many multiples over typical MMR for that tool. Result: stalled spindle, broken cutter, or stalled axis.

**Real-world impact:** Helix-entry is supposed to be the safe option for small-diameter cutters that can't plunge straight. The current implementation has it then cut full-engagement laterally at the same rates the user picked for finish-quality contour cuts. The user picks helix to save the cutter, and the post then loads it harder than a direct plunge would.

**Fix sketch:** emit the post-helix walk as either (a) a spiral that ramps from helix radius outward to the contour at constant z (Archimedean), or (b) a series of incremental engagements, or (c) at minimum drop the feed to rate_v for that single segment. Option (c) is the smallest patch and prevents the worst loading.
acceptance_criteria: The post-helix walk-to-start uses a feedrate appropriate for full-immersion cutting (rate_v at minimum), OR is replaced by a stepover spiral. A new test gcode_helix_walk_to_start_uses_safe_feed exercises the rate change.
close_reason: Fixed: post-helix path now lifts to fast_move_z (G1 Retract), G0 rapids to contour start, plunges at rate_v. Avoids the full-immersion horizontal G1 cut through unmilled stock at the new pass depth.

title: audit 2026-05-22 timing: cycle-time uses single feedrate per segment, ignoring distinct plunge_rate vs feed_rate transitions
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/timing.rs:118-124 (`feed_mm_min = feeds_mm_min.get(i)`). The per-segment feed comes from the modal F value in the gcode at that segment's line — but G81/G83/canned-cycle plunges and G1 plunges all share whatever F was last set, with no awareness of the tool's distinct `plunge_rate` vs `feed_rate` modes.

**Problem:** The post emits one F per cut/plunge transition; if the post uses `F<plunge_rate>` on the plunge G1 and `F<feed_rate>` on the subsequent G1 cut, modal-F tracking in feeds_per_segment recovers them correctly. But if the post writes a single `F` at the start of an op (typical for short hand-written gcode), the **plunge G1 inherits the cutting feed**, and the time estimator predicts the plunge happens at full feed_rate instead of the (much slower) plunge_rate. For drill operations where the bit plunges at 100 mm/min and rapids at 5000 mm/min, the timing error per hole is ~50x in the plunge phase, easily 30%+ total on a drilled part.

Additionally, the estimator's `MoveKind::Plunge` accounting doesn't fall back to the tool's `plunge_rate` when the modal F is missing or absurdly high — it uses the modal F regardless of kind. There's no cross-check that 'F on a Plunge segment should be capped at tool.plunge_rate'.

**Real-world impact:** Time estimates for drill-heavy projects under-predict by 20-50%. The shop floor schedules around the displayed estimate; jobs run long, parts collide with downstream operations. Trust in the estimate is the chief gain of the kinematic integrator — getting it 30% wrong undermines that.

**Acceptance:** estimate() clamps the per-segment feed to `tool.plunge_rate` for MoveKind::Plunge and to `tool.feed_rate` for MoveKind::Cut when a tool reference is available (extend the signature). New test `plunge_segment_uses_plunge_rate_when_modal_f_is_cutting_feed` covers it.
acceptance_criteria: Plunge segments use tool.plunge_rate (capped by modal F if lower). Drill cycle-time test within 10% of analytical hand-computed time.
close_reason: Fixed: added estimate_from_gcode_with_rates that clamps per-segment feeds to tool's plunge_rate (rate_v) on Plunge segments and feed_rate (rate_h) on Cut/Arc. Pipeline builds the op_rates lookup from project.operations + tools.

title: audit 2026-05-22 wirbeln: per-segment phase reset discards stride residual at chord boundaries
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/wirbeln.rs:226-238 in fn walk_chord. **Problem:** consumed_since_last_step is set to len - (next_stamp_at - stride) at line 233, then overwritten to 0.0 at line 238 after stamping the chord endpoint. The endpoint stamp blindly advances winkel by schritt_rad regardless of how short the chord is. Effect: spiral phase is discontinuously bumped by one stride step at every segment vertex and the carry-over from the previous chord is discarded. **Real-world impact:** Contradicts the module doc ('continuous rotation Estlcam's Flooper accumulates') and the closed_square_produces_continuous_rotation test (which only asserts start/end XY differ by <2mm — doesn't catch phase glitches at corners). Visible flat spots at corners and uneven engagement on long polylines with many short segments.
acceptance_criteria: walk_chord carries consumed_since_last_step across chord boundaries; endpoint-stamp does not unconditionally advance winkel. New test asserts winkel after N unit chords equals N·(schritt_rad/stride)·stride within FP tolerance, independent of how the total length is split.
close_reason: Fixed: walk_chord carries the stride residual across chord boundaries via consumed_since_last_step (was being reset to 0 + winkel bumped one full step at every endpoint). Test asserts continuous phase accumulation independent of chord splitting.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-start-depth: lead-in hardcodes plunge to Z=0, ignores mill.start_depth
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:534, 545, 561 (`emit_offset` lead-in branches all write `post.linear(None, None, Some(0.0))`).

**Problem:** The plunge-from-safe-Z target is the literal `0.0`, not `setup.mill.start_depth`. The Z-schedule then builds passes from `start_depth` (e.g. -3.0 if the user has already pre-machined a -3 mm recess) but the plunge into the first pass plunges from `fast_move_z` through Z=0 at horizontal feed and stops there — leaving the cutter dangling at Z=0 for the start of the first pass which expects to begin at `start_depth`.

For a positive start_depth (the user has stock proud of the global zero — e.g. start_depth = +1 because there's 1 mm of skin to clear), the plunge to 0.0 actually crashes the cutter INTO the proud stock at G1 feed.

For a negative start_depth (recess case, start_depth = -3), the plunge stops at 0 — well above where the first cut is supposed to begin (-3 - step) — and the first pass walks the contour at Z=0, NOT at start_depth - step. The result is the first pass cuts air for the first pass and the depth-schedule never reaches the intended floor.

**Worked example:** setup.mill.start_depth = -3.0, step = -1.0, depth = -5.0:
- Wiac emits: `G0 X0 Y0 Z5\nG1 Z0\nG1 Z-4\n...` — the cutter dives at G1 plunge feed from Z=5 to Z=0 (5 mm of full-immersion plunge into uncut stock above the recess), then to Z=-4 for the first scheduled pass.
- Expected: `G0 X0 Y0 Z5\nG1 Z-3\nG1 Z-4\n...` — plunge stops at the surface plane the user defined.

**Real-world impact:** Anyone using start_depth ≠ 0 (multi-stage parts, faced stock with known proud, second-op fixtures) gets either a free crash (positive start_depth) or an empty first pass (negative). Both are silent — the user only finds out from the broken cutter or the un-cut part.
acceptance_criteria: The lead-in plunge target is setup.mill.start_depth, not 0.0. A new test gcode_plunge_targets_start_depth covers both positive (proud stock) and negative (recess) start_depth values.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: arc tessellation chord scallop visible in ball-nose finishing pass heightmaps
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/preview.rs:272 (~10°/chord arc tessellation) + sim/sweep.rs (carves chord-by-chord).

**Problem:** Arcs reach the sim as already-chorded ToolpathSegments with ~10° per chord (chord error r(1-cos(5°)) ~ 0.0038*r). For a ball-nose finishing pass on a curved surface, the sim heightmap carves chord-by-chord, leaving discretization residuals up to chord_error visible in the heightmap — but those scallops are a sim artifact, not a real machining outcome, because the actual G2/G3 motion on a real machine traces the smooth arc. When a user dials cell_size below the chord error to inspect finish quality (3D mesh export, scallop test), the visible scallops don't match reality.

**Real-world impact:** Surface-finish verification via the sim is unreliable for arcs. User sees 0.04mm scallops on a 10mm arc and either: (a) cranks XY-overlap down to 'fix' a non-existent problem and burns hours of cycle time, or (b) ignores all scallops and misses a real one when the gcode actually steps coarsely.

**Acceptance:** Document the chord-tessellation residual in sim/mod.rs (bounded by preview tessellation). Optionally: emit an Arc kind that the sim resolves with a finer step than the wireframe, or document the floor for surface-inspection accuracy.
acceptance_criteria: sim/mod.rs docstring states the chord-error bound and recommended cell_size floor; one test asserts arc heightmap matches analytic surface within 2*chord_error.
close_reason: Fixed: preview now tessellates arcs at ~2°/chord (was ~10°). Chord error drops from 0.04 mm to 0.0015 mm on a 10 mm arc — well below cell quantization noise. sim/mod.rs documents the floor.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-emit-prologue: missing G17/G40/G94 modal-state preamble
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:428 (`program_begin`).

**Problem:** The emitted prologue sets only `G21` and `G90`, leaving plane-select / cutter-comp / feed-mode as 'whatever the controller booted with'. Real LinuxCNC sessions get this from the INI, but the gcode file is supposed to be self-contained — when a user loads it on a different machine, or after a homing/E-stop reset on a machine whose user-set modal state is non-default, the emitted program can run in an unexpected plane (G18/G19 lathe defaults → XY arcs swing in YZ/XZ instead) or with cutter compensation still active from the last job (G41/G42), gouging the part.

Specifically missing:
- `G17` (XY plane) — wiac emits I/J arcs and helices that REQUIRE G17. On a controller booted in G18 (lathe-config) the arcs are reinterpreted in XZ. Catastrophic.
- `G40` (cancel cutter comp) — leftover G41/G42 from a previous program offsets every subsequent move by the controller's wear-offset register. Random gouging.
- `G94` (units/min feed mode) — LinuxCNC default is G94, but a controller left in G93 (inverse-time) interprets `F800` as 800 inverse-minutes; nonsense feed.

**Worked example:** controller booted in G18 + G42:
- Wiac emits: `G21\nG90\nF800\nG0 Z5\nM3 S12000\nG0 X0 Y0 Z5\nG1 Z0\nG2 X10 Y0 I5 J0` (semicircle).
- Real machine interprets G2 in XZ plane (G18 still active): cutter sweeps in Z while the operator expected XY.
- Expected: `G21\nG90\nG94\nG17\nG40\nF800\n...` so the gcode is self-contained.

GRBL also defaults to G17 but accepts G17/G40/G94 — emitting them is free and removes the silent-failure mode.
acceptance_criteria: program_begin emits `G17` (XY plane), `G40` (cancel cutter comp), `G94` (units/min) BEFORE the first motion line. Both LinuxCNC and GRBL posts emit them; HPGL ignores. Golden corpus updated. New test linuxcnc_emits_modal_safety_preamble checks the three G-words are present in that order before any G0/G1.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 halfpipe: ball-nose at re-entrant corner produces wrong Z (medial-axis r is incircle, not corner radius)
description:
Where: crates/wiac-core/src/cam/halfpipe.rs:40-70 fn depth_at.

Problem: depth_at uses v.r (inscribed-circle radius at the medial-axis vertex = perpendicular distance to nearest boundary) to compute floor depth z = -(R - sqrt(R^2 - r^2)). This is correct for a STRAIGHT slot where the medial axis is the centerline at constant half-width. But at a 90 corner where two long walls meet, the medial axis bends and v.r tapers down to 0 along a 45 bisector running INTO the corner.

When the ball-nose tries to trace that 45 bisector toward the corner: at distance d from the corner along the bisector, r = d (inscribed circle just touches both walls at distance d). depth_at computes z = -(R - sqrt(R^2 - d^2)).

But the actual floor a ball-nose can leave at the corner is NOT a smooth half-pipe bend — the ball cannot reach the corner; the closest it can fit is when its centre is at distance R from each wall (i.e. r = R*sqrt(2) along the bisector). For r < R, the math returns valid z values but those positions are UNREACHABLE without scrubbing the wall.

For r > R (slot wider than pipe), code caps at z = -R (line 49), which is the half-cylinder bottom — but in the corner case, the slot is NOT half-cylindrical near the corner regardless of r.

Real-world impact: Halfpipe op on a rectangular pocket leaves the four corners with miscut floors — too deep or with ball wall-grazing as it sweeps in. The user expected a smooth half-pipe along the centerline that gently faded at the corners; got a divot or a wall scrape instead.
acceptance_criteria: depth_at considers both inscribed-circle radius r AND local medial-axis curvature/branchness. At branches and near boundary tangency where the ball cannot trace a smooth half-pipe, fade z toward 0 (or to the floor of the half-pipe centered farther from the corner). At minimum: emit a warning that halfpipe quality is only correct on straight-spine regions. Test: a 20x20 square halfpipe with profile R=5 shows z = -R along most of the centerline, fading toward 0 within R distance of corners.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P1 CAM-algorithm commits on main (offsets island-aware: 2cda450, vcarve pruning + below-tip warning: e97e9a1, halfpipe corner-aware Z + 10% radius gate: 985e9ea). 453 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 halfpipe: tool-radius vs profile-radius mismatch threshold too loose, allows wrong-floor gcode
description:
Where: crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/op_drivers/halfpipe.rs:62-71.

Problem: The halfpipe op uses the PROFILE radius (HalfpipeProfile::CircularArc.radius_mm) to compute the floor depth, not the tool radius. The intent is "ball-nose with radius == profile R", and the warning at line 62 fires when |tool_r - radius_mm| > 0.5 * radius_mm.max(1.0). For a profile R=5mm:
  threshold = 0.5 * 5 = 2.5mm
  Mismatch up to 2.5mm = no warning.

So a 6mm ball-nose (tool_r = 3) on a 5mm-R profile passes silently. The emitted gcode tells the controller to put the ball CENTER at z = -(R - sqrt(R^2 - r^2)). But the BALL is 3mm radius, not 5mm — the actual contact point sits 2mm lower than expected. The cut floor depth is wrong by up to 2mm everywhere across the slot.

The depth math is fundamentally a function of the BALL radius (the cutter that touches the workpiece), not the desired pipe radius. The profile R is the DESIRED floor curvature; it can ONLY be matched by a ball whose radius equals R. With any other ball, the floor traced is the ball s envelope, which is a different curve.

Real-world impact: Half-pipe slots come out wrong shape and depth, mismatching downstream features (a pipe nesting, an aesthetic shape). Visual + functional spec violation.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) tighten the warning threshold to ~0.1mm and document that tool radius MUST equal profile R, or (b) reformulate the math to derive floor depth from tool_radius and treat profile R as a separate envelope check. Document the geometry in the module header. Test: 6mm ball on 5mm-R profile emits the halfpipe_radius_mismatch warning.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P1 CAM-algorithm commits on main (offsets island-aware: 2cda450, vcarve pruning + below-tip warning: e97e9a1, halfpipe corner-aware Z + 10% radius gate: 985e9ea). 453 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: spiral bridge-containment check ignores islands
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:1086 in fn bridge_stays_inside_polygon, called from stitch_rings_to_polyline:1056.

**Problem:** The containment guard between consecutive spiral rings only tests `bridge_stays_inside_polygon(end, first, outer)` — it walks 8 samples on the bridge segment and verifies each is inside the outer ring. Islands aren't checked. On a pocket with an island, the cascade rings step inward around BOTH outer and island, but the straight bridge between consecutive rings can cross over an island that the rings themselves avoided.

**Reproduction / evidence:** stitch_rings_to_polyline takes only `rings` (which are clipper2 output of the boundary minus inflated islands — the rings DON'T cross islands). But the bridge from ring[k].last to ring[k+1].first is a literal straight line whose only check is against rings[0] (the outermost inset). If an island sits between consecutive ring start/end points, the bridge cuts through it. trochoidal.rs::disc_inside_polygon does check islands; spiral does not.

**Why this matters:** Spiral pocket strategy on island-containing pockets can emit gcode that plunges through a raised feature mid-cut. The check is needed for safety, not just spiral-fallback cosmetics.
acceptance_criteria: bridge_stays_inside_polygon (or stitch_rings_to_polyline) accepts an islands slice and returns None when any bridge segment crosses an island, mirroring trochoidal's disc_inside_polygon island-check. Regression test: pocket with one island where a bridge would cross it must trigger fallback to cascade.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P1 CAM-algorithm commits on main (offsets island-aware: 2cda450, vcarve pruning + below-tip warning: e97e9a1, halfpipe corner-aware Z + 10% radius gate: 985e9ea). 453 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 vcarve: medial axis has no branch pruning, produces hairy spurious branches
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/vcarve.rs:107-319 in fn medial_axis_cancellable.

**Problem:** The Voronoi-of-densified-samples approach inherently produces a spurious branch at every densified boundary sample because the sample-rate (BOUNDARY_SAMPLE_MM = 0.1mm) is finite. Every smooth boundary curve emits dozens of tiny medial-axis spurs perpendicular to the boundary; these spurs run from the true spine out toward each sample point with r → 0 at the tip. There is no pruning step: medial_axis returns ALL polylines including these hair-spurs.

Downstream effects:
1. emit_vcarve_block treats every spur as a separate polyline → many G0 lifts to fast_z + plunges to start_depth back into the same region, multiplying cycle time by 10-100x.
2. Each spur's ratchet sweep drives the V-bit tip from z=0 down to z=-(local r)/tan(half) and back at every spur — vertical plunge into a corner that's already cut.
3. The spurs' tips approach the boundary samples (r → 0); they form micro-zigzag toolpaths near every smooth curve.

Standard medial-axis CAM (Estlcam, Aspire, Carbide Create) prune branches whose maximum r is below some epsilon (e.g. r_max_along_branch < tool_tip_radius + 0.05 mm) or whose length is below the sample step × N.

**Real-world impact:** V-Carve on text or any curved geometry produces enormous gcode files with hundreds of redundant plunges. Bit lifetime collapses; surface finish gets pockmarks at every spur tip.
acceptance_criteria: After building the polylines vector, prune any branch (endpoint-to-junction chain) whose max r along the chain is below a configurable threshold (default = tip_radius + epsilon) AND whose length is < N × BOUNDARY_SAMPLE_MM. The plus_shape regression test still passes; new test verifies a 20×4 rectangle returns ONE polyline (the centerline) instead of one centerline + many short stubs.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P1 CAM-algorithm commits on main (offsets island-aware: 2cda450, vcarve pruning + below-tip warning: e97e9a1, halfpipe corner-aware Z + 10% radius gate: 985e9ea). 453 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: pocket_zigzag ignores islands, carves through them
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:336 in fn pocket_zigzag (and :294 pocket_zigzag_angled), called from pocket_for_object at :847.

**Problem:** pocket_for_object passes only the inset boundary points to pocket_zigzag_angled — no islands. The zigzag scanline uses even-odd crossings on a single boundary polygon, so any closed contour that should be preserved inside the pocket (raised feature / island) is invisible to the algorithm and the cutter sweeps straight through it.

**Reproduction / evidence:** offsets.rs line 847: `let strokes = pocket_zigzag_angled(&pts, step.max(0.1), tool_radius * 2.0, angle_deg);` — `islands` from the caller is dropped on the floor. Cascade + spiral + trochoidal all forward islands; only Zigzag does not. There is no test for zigzag + island.

**Why this matters:** A user who picks the Zigzag pocket strategy on any pocket-with-island (very common: text inset on a plate, logo cavity around a boss) gets gcode that destroys the island. No warning fires — pocket_fill_incomplete only warns when cascade fits no rings.
acceptance_criteria: pocket_zigzag (or a new pocket_zigzag_with_islands wrapper) accepts an islands slice and either (a) splits scanline strokes at island crossings using a combined even-odd over outer + holes, or (b) refuses to emit and the pipeline emits a warning + auto-falls-back to cascade. Add a regression test: 30x30 outer + 10x10 island, run Zigzag, assert no stroke crosses the island interior.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P1 CAM-algorithm commits on main (offsets island-aware: 2cda450, vcarve pruning + below-tip warning: e97e9a1, halfpipe corner-aware Z + 10% radius gate: 985e9ea). 453 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 vcarve: polyline_to_z double-clamps r to tip plateau silently
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/vcarve.rs:366-402 in fn polyline_to_z.

**Problem:** When the user sets carve_max_width_mm such that effective_r_cap (= min(user_cap, tool_reach_r)) is ≤ tip_radius_mm, the function first clamps r to the cap (line 379-384, setting depth_limited=true) and THEN the r <= tip_r branch (line 387-389) produces z=0 — i.e. no cut. The pipeline driver in op_drivers/vcarve.rs handles this defensively for the perimeter path (lines 189-202, vcarve_below_tip_radius warning), but the full-medial-axis path at lines 167-182 does NOT — it silently outputs a polyline of all-zero Z waypoints that the gcode emitter then drives at cutting feedrate across the surface, producing only the depth_limited warning. Result: user sees 'depth limited' message but the gcode is actually 'no cut at all', not just clipped.

**Real-world impact:** Full-medial-axis V-Carve with a small carve_max_width and a flat-tipped V-bit produces gcode that traces the spine at z=0 (workpiece surface), wasting time and giving zero cut. User may not realise the gcode is dead until they inspect 3D preview.
acceptance_criteria: Full-medial-axis V-Carve with effective_r_cap ≤ tip_radius_mm either (a) skips the chain entirely with a clear warning matching the perimeter branch, or (b) raises a hard error. polyline_to_z documents this case; a unit test covers it.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P1 CAM-algorithm commits on main (offsets island-aware: 2cda450, vcarve pruning + below-tip warning: e97e9a1, halfpipe corner-aware Z + 10% radius gate: 985e9ea). 453 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit-dh1n init effects loop via Svelte 5 dep tracking
description: MachineDialog and ToolLibraryDialog's dh1n init effects called snapshotKey()/JSON.stringify(draft) AFTER writing draft. Svelte 5 tracks reads inside the effect body (including reads via called functions) as dependencies, so the write-then-read pattern made the effect schedule itself. After ~1000 self-runs Svelte threw effect_update_depth_exceeded, killing the reactivity scheduler — every onclick still fired but visible state stopped updating (the exact 'X / Cancel / OK don't close' symptom the user reported). Fixed by computing the snapshot from local vars before assigning the $state proxies.
close_reason: Closed

title: App close needs unsaved-work confirmation
description: Closing the app window (X / Cmd-Q / Alt-F4) discards in-progress edits with no warning. Should intercept Tauri's CloseRequested when project.dirty, show an in-app confirmation, and require explicit confirm before quitting.
close_reason: Closed

title: MachineDialog cannot be closed (X / Cancel / OK all unresponsive)
description: User reports the Machine Settings window cannot be closed via any of its three exits: the header × button, the footer Cancel button, or the footer OK button. Root cause: close() uses window.confirm() which is unreliable in the Tauri/WebKitGTK build (audit-C10 already flagged this), and commit()'s JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(draft)) was unwrapped so any serialise throw aborts the function before onClose() fires.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-16: HTTP transport drops structured Error fields (kind, recovery_hint, auto_fix, span)
description:
Error envelope diverges across transports:

- `crates/wiac-server/src/main.rs:403` — `AppError` keeps only `status` + `message`. **Drops kind, recovery_hint, auto_fix, span.**
- `crates/wiac-tauri/src/commands.rs:259` — `serialize_error()` returns full `wiac_core::Error` JSON via String.
- `crates/wiac-wasm/src/lib.rs:163` — `structured_error_to_js()` returns full `wiac_core::Error` via JsValue.

Frontend recovery-hint / auto-fix paths silently degrade when the user runs against the HTTP transport. Frontend devs writing error-recovery UX have to remember the matrix.

## Fix
HTTP server: return the full `wiac_core::Error` JSON as the response body; map only the HTTP status code at the response layer. All three transports converge on the same JSON shape; frontend handles one error type.

## Acceptance
- HTTP /generate failing on UnknownTool returns body { kind, message, recovery_hint, auto_fix } matching Tauri/WASM.
- Frontend `api/client.ts` strips its transport-specific error normalization.
close_reason: Closed

title: Regression: stepped BufferGeometry mesh shows 3D solids only partially
description:
After the lcu5/6tmz stepped-mesh + partial-upload landing, users report the 3D preview shows the solid only partially. Likely candidates:

1. Partial-upload range bug — addUpdateRange args don't cover all touched verts (top + walls + fringes).
2. Existing users with maxSimulationCells=4M (persisted) push the stepped mesh to 1.15 GB GPU memory; partial allocation failure.
3. Bounding sphere wrong, frustum culling kicks in.
4. Per-cell triangle winding bug — but DoubleSide should mask that.
5. Missing bottom plane — the InstancedMesh-of-boxes had a closed bottom; the stepped mesh leaves it open.
close_reason: Resolved by auim (commit 3e6fdfe, 2026-05-14) which dropped the default maxSimulationCells from 4M to 1M. The stepped voxel mesh is ~280 bytes/cell of GPU memory, so 4M cells = ~1.2 GB — that exceeded integrated-GPU memory and caused the partial-render symptom (candidate #2 from the ticket). User confirmed (session 2026-05-17) that later AppImage builds render the 3D preview correctly. Existing installs with a persisted 4M setting can lower it via Settings; the hint text now surfaces the per-cell memory cost.

title: 3D-sim audit #2: replace InstancedMesh-of-boxes with stepped BufferGeometry
description:
frontend/src/lib/sim/heightfield_mesh.ts — the stepped voxel mesh uses one BoxGeometry per cell (12 triangles each). At maxSimulationCells = 4M that's 48M triangles per frame; even typical 200×200 grids draw 480k triangles where the old PlaneGeometry drew ~80k.

## Fix

Custom indexed BufferGeometry:
* Per cell: 4 unique top-face vertices at the cell corners, all at cell.Z. 2 triangles per cell top face.
* Walls: emit a 4-vertex / 2-triangle quad ONLY where adjacent cells differ in Z by more than a small epsilon. For a typical pocket op ~5-15% of cell boundaries are walls.

Triangle count vs the InstancedMesh approach:
* Boxes: 12 × cols×rows
* Stepped sparse walls: ~2.4 × cols×rows (typical) … ~6 × cols×rows (worst case)

Right algorithm; ~5× fewer triangles in the common case. Walls remain vertical (preserves the so70 fix). Drop the BoxGeometry, drop `frustumCulled = false`.
close_reason: Closed

title: 3D-sim audit #1: WASM advance() re-deserializes full segment array per frame
description:
crates/wiac-wasm/src/sim.rs:104-115 — `advance(segments, tool, from_idx, to_idx)` deserializes the FULL segment array on every call but only uses [from..to). For a 50k-segment program scrubbing at 60 fps that's millions of serde-wasm-bindgen field accesses per frame.

## Fix options

a) Pass only the slice [from..to) from JS — driver already knows the bounds.
b) Cache the segments on the Simulator at toolpath-set time (one new method, e.g. `set_toolpath(segs)`); subsequent `advance(from, to)` calls index into the cached vec without deserialization.
c) Flat Float32Array binary protocol — flatten segments to (fx,fy,fz,tx,ty,tz,kind_u8,...) bytes and parse in Rust without serde.

Option (b) is cleanest: segments rarely change (only on Generate), so caching once eliminates the cost entirely.
close_reason: Closed

title: 3D preview shows slanted walls with cylindrical (endmill) tool
description:
3D preview of machining leaves visible slanted walls on pocket / profile cuts that use an Endmill (cylindrical) tool. The user confirms it is NOT a perspective artifact.

Suspects:
- sweep.rs:for_each_swept_cell uses cutter_pz = lerp(from.z, to.z, t) along segment XY projection. For a segment whose from.z != to.z (ramps, helix entries, retract from cut to safety), this carves a sloped floor across the cells under the path — physically correct for the gcode but unexpected when the user thinks of contour passes as flat-Z.
- Heightfield mesh rendering may smooth across grid cells (PlaneGeometry interpolates between vertices), making any single-cell wall appear as a slope.

## Fix direction
- Audit each cut-segment kind:
  - constant-Z cut → fine, lerp returns flat
  - ramp / helix entry → lerp is correct
  - feed-rate connector or retract-while-still-below-top → should NOT carve. Check whether sweep_segment correctly skips these.
- Alternatively, render heightmap with stepped (flat-bottomed) cells instead of interpolated vertices so walls between adjacent cells look vertical.
close_reason: Closed

title: Outside-pocket frame padding < tool diameter gives unreasonable results
description:
In Outside Pocket op, when frame_padding_mm is smaller than the cutter radius, the synthesized frame is too tight against the selection. With Inside tool_offset, the cutter walks INSIDE the frame's bbox+padding boundary, which means it crosses INTO the selected geometry instead of staying outside it.

## Repro
- Pick an object, set Op = Pocket outside, frame_shape=Bbox, frame_padding_mm=1.0
- Set tool diameter = 6mm (radius=3mm)
- Pad (1mm) < radius (3mm) → cutter offsets inside the selection

## Fix
In synthesize_pocket_outside_objects (pipeline.rs ~L881), clamp padding to at least tool_radius + small_slack and emit a PipelineWarning when bumped.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI lockup after first DXF import — workspace writes inside Svelte 5 $effect bodies abort the scheduler
description:
Symptom: after the first DXF loads, every toolbar button stops working, canvas selection breaks, 2D/3D toggle dies, file picker for a second DXF opens but the loaded file never propagates. All event handlers still fire but visible state stops updating.

Root cause: two $effects wrote to workspace state inside the synchronous Svelte 5 effect-body flush:

1. `project.persistPerProjectState` (project.svelte.ts:352) — called from App.svelte's per-project persistence $effect on every visibleLayers / selectedOpId / playhead / activeProjectPath change. Calls workspace.setPerProject → notify → ReactiveWorkspaceStore subscriber bumps workspace.version ($state) **inside the running effect**.

2. `workspace.setLastPostProcessor` (GenerateBar.svelte:56) — called from a $effect that tracks `post`. Same pattern: $state write inside the effect body.

When the first DXF imports, setActiveProjectPath runs through a cascade (sets activeProjectPath → restores visibleLayers/selectedOpId/playhead). The persistence effect fires, calls setPerProject, which mutates workspace.version. Svelte 5 detects the cross-effect mutation, throws (silently — no exception bubbles to the console), and the reactivity scheduler aborts. After that point, state still mutates, handlers still run, but the DOM never re-renders.

Fix shipped:
- Both call sites now defer the workspace write via queueMicrotask, escaping the synchronous effect flush. Try/catch belt-and-suspenders so any future throw is logged, not swallowed.
- Added window.addEventListener('error') + 'unhandledrejection' in App.svelte's onMount so this class of silent failure is now visible.

Pattern to enforce: $effects MUST NOT synchronously mutate $state owned by other reactive nodes. Use queueMicrotask, or use `untrack` from svelte to isolate the read.
close_reason: Closed

title: Profile/Pocket on circles looked like 'cut on line' — preview interpreter emitted single chord per G2/G3
description: preview::interpret produced ONE ToolpathSegment per G2/G3 line, going start→end as a chord. For a half-circle that's a horizontal line across the diameter. Both the 3D wireframe and the heightfield simulator (sweep_segment) treat ToolpathSegments as straight lines, so a profile-Outside cut on a circle showed as a chord crossing the part center, looking like 'cut on the source line'. Fix: parse I/J in preview, tessellate arcs into ~10°/chord segments (4+ minimum) before emitting.
close_reason: Closed

title: XY overlap (stepover) knob for Pocket; fix cascade default that left small pockets uncut
description:
Cascade and Spiral strategies use delta=tool_radius for the inward inflate. For pockets where the tool barely fits the boundary offset, the next inflate produces an empty result → 0 cascade rings → only the wall is cut. Zigzag is unaffected because it rasters at tool_diameter*0.9 regardless.

User asks for a configurable 'overlap in XY' similar to step/pass in Z. Adding xy_overlap_fraction to OperationParams (default 0.5 = 50% overlap = step is half the tool diameter). For a 6mm tool that's 3mm cascade step. Tighter overlap = smaller step = more rings even on tight geometry. Used by both cascade (step between rings) and zigzag (stride between rasters), unifying the knob.

Range: [0.05, 0.95] — at the limits the cascade either takes forever or leaves stripes, so we clamp.

Wire schema: new field on OperationParams with serde_skip on default. UI: number input in OpPropertiesPanel beside the existing Pocket strategy picker. Tooltip explains 0.5 = 50% overlap = standard / safe.

Tests:
- new pocket_with_low_overlap_emits_extra_rings: same 50x50 pocket, default 0.5 → N rings; 0.7 → > N rings.
- existing pocket regressions stay green at default 0.5.
close_reason:
XY overlap knob landed end-to-end:
- new OperationParams.xy_overlap field (clamped 0.05..0.95, default 0.5 = 50% overlap = step is half the tool diameter)
- pipeline computes xy_step = tool_diameter * (1 - overlap) and threads it into pocket_for_object
- pocket_for_object passes it to both pocket_cascade_with_islands (as the inflate delta — was previously hardcoded tool_radius, which left tight pockets uncut) and pocket_zigzag (as the stride — was hardcoded tool_diameter*0.9)
- pocket_zigzag now takes (boundary, stride, tool_diameter) — the tool_diameter param stays for the half-tool-diameter inset at the polygon edges
- UI: number input in OpPropertiesPanel under the Pocket strategy picker, with a tooltip explaining the trade-off
- new test higher_xy_overlap_emits_a_longer_cut_path verifies 0.7 → ≥20% more cut length than 0.3 on the same 50x50 geometry
- existing pocket regressions stay green at the new 0.5 default

99 wiac-core lib tests green; svelte-check 0 errors; vite build clean.

title: Plunge strategy: direct vs ramp
description:
Today every Z descent is a straight plunge (rapid to fast_move_z, then plunge feed straight down to cut depth). For most endmills this is fine on a soft material at low depths but dangerous on harder materials or with non-center-cutting bits. Add an explicit per-op plunge strategy:

- Plunge { kind: Direct }                  — current behavior, straight down
- Plunge { kind: Ramp, angle_deg: f64 }    — descend along a 1°..15° ramp into the first cut move; the ramp eats into material along the toolpath direction so the cutter takes a chip both Z and XY simultaneously
- (future) Plunge { kind: Helix, radius: f64 } — for pockets, spiral down inside the boundary

Wire schema:
- new PlungeStrategy enum on OperationParams (default Direct)
- ramp angle stored alongside; default 3° (a conservative angle most endmills handle on plywood / aluminium)

Algorithm: gcode emitter's emit_polylines_block already handles the start of each cut. For Ramp, we walk the first ~ramp_length (= depth_step / tan(angle)) of the cut, bumping Z down linearly along the path until we reach cut depth, then continue at constant Z. The leftover material is finished by the rest of the cut as today.

Tool-kind awareness: Drill / DragKnife / Engrave force Direct (Ramp doesn't apply). V-bit / engraver default to Direct (the geometry IS the ramp). Endmill / ball nose default to Direct in v1, opt-in to Ramp via the picker.

UI: a new 'Plunge' field in the Cut fieldset of OpPropertiesPanel: select { Direct, Ramp } + a number input for ramp angle when Ramp is picked.

Tests:
- ramp emits a sequence of cut moves with monotonically decreasing Z reaching depth at the expected ramp length
- direct emits a single plunge move at start (current behavior, locked in by golden corpus)
- mode switch round-trips through .vc-project
close_reason:
Plunge strategy shipped end-to-end (direct + ramp).

Wire schema:
- new PlungeStrategy enum in cam::setup with Direct (default) and Ramp { angle_deg } variants; serde-skipped on default
- MillConfig.plunge field added; OperationParams.plunge mirrors it
- pipeline.rs synthesize_op_setup propagates op.params.plunge into setup.mill.plunge
- schema regenerated → openapi.yaml → openapi-typescript

Algorithm in gcode.rs:
- multi_pass picks ramp_angle_deg from setup.mill.plunge; computes ramp_length = step / tan(angle), tracks ramp_from = previous Z (defaults to start_depth on the first pass)
- new emit_ramp_pass walks segments while linearly descending Z over the first ramp_length of arc length, then continues at to_z for the remainder. Line segments are *split* mid-segment when they cross the ramp_length boundary so the ramp angle is honored even if the first edge is longer than ramp_length. Arc segments use per-endpoint interpolation (mid-arc splitting punted to v2 — common geometry never starts on a long arc anyway since corner offsets are small).
- ramp falls through to direct plunge when path < ramp_length (path too short) or when the pass needs tabs (tabs walker is authoritative — handling both ramp + tabs cleanly is a v2 ask).

Tests:
- ramp_plunge_descends_z_during_first_cuts: 100×100 outside profile + Ramp 10° → first move starts at Z≈0, Z reaches -1 within ±25% of expected 5.67mm horizontal length
- direct_plunge_keeps_default_behavior: locks in the existing semantics (first cut already at depth before XY motion)

UI in OpPropertiesPanel:
- new Plunge select (direct/ramp) inside the Cut fieldset, only for Profile + Pocket
- when 'ramp' is picked, a Ramp angle number input appears (clamped 0.5..45°, default 3°)

title: Tool-fit warnings (cutter doesn't fit the geometry)
description:
When the chosen tool can't physically perform the op the user asked for, show a clear warning before they Generate (or alongside the warnings GenerateResponse already returns). Common failure modes:

1. Slot narrower than the tool diameter — Profile Inside or Pocket where the tool can't fit between two walls. Detect via clipper inflate by tool radius: if the inflated boundary has zero area or vanishes, the slot doesn't fit.
2. Pocket whose minimum inscribed circle is < tool radius — even a fat slot can have a corner the cutter can't reach.
3. V-bit / drag knife / drill used on a Pocket with Cascade or Zigzag (kind mismatch).
4. Tip diameter ≥ shank diameter on a tapered cutter (impossible geometry).

Where:
- backend: a new check_tool_fit(project, op, objects, setup) -> Vec<ToolFitWarning> called in run_pipeline before the per-op driver; warnings flow through GenerateResponse.warnings (already exists) tagged with op_id.
- frontend: surface warnings in the OperationsList status badge (we already have the warn/bad tones from 6cz) and in a new sidebar panel listing all warnings for the active project.

Acceptance:
- 'pocket a 4mm slot with a 6mm endmill' → warn before Generate
- 'profile inside a 2mm slot with a 3mm endmill' → warn
- existing valid configs continue to Generate without warnings
- warnings are op-scoped so a multi-op project shows which op is the problem
close_reason:
Tool-fit warnings shipped end-to-end:

Wire schema:
- new PipelineWarning { op_id?, kind, message } in wiac_core::pipeline
- PipelineResponse.warnings: Vec<PipelineWarning> (serde-skipped on empty)
- schema regenerated

Backend in pipeline.rs:
- push_tool_fit_kind_warnings() — runs at the top of build_op_offsets:
  - tip_diameter ≥ shank diameter → 'tool_geometry_impossible'
  - Drill on Pocket / Profile, DragKnife on Pocket → 'tool_kind_mismatch'
- push_tool_fit_size_warning() — runs after offset cascade for ops that need offsets (Pocket / Profile-Outside / Profile-Inside): if at least one closed object was selected but no offsets came back, the cutter doesn't fit → 'tool_too_large' with the actual diameter in the message
- both functions take a &mut Vec<PipelineWarning>; threaded through run_per_op + build_op_offsets so each monomorphisation (linuxcnc/grbl/hpgl) accumulates the same warnings list

Frontend in OperationsList.svelte:
- statusFor() reads project.generated.warnings, filters by op_id, escalates to ✘ (bad tone) for kind_mismatch / geometry_impossible and ⚠ (warn tone) for fit issues; the row's title attribute exposes the message text on hover

Tests:
- pocket_with_oversized_tool_emits_tool_too_large_warning: 4mm box pocketed with a 6mm cutter → exactly one tool_too_large warning at op_id=7
- pocket_with_drill_bit_warns_about_tool_kind: Drill on Pocket → tool_kind_mismatch present

title: Climb vs Conventional cut direction (with finishing-pass override)
description:
Today the pipeline emits each PolylineOffset with whatever winding cavc / clipper2 happens to produce — so the cut is climb on some contours and conventional on others, depending on input order. Per industry practice we want explicit control:
- main op: choose Climb or Conventional (default Conventional — safer on machines with backlash)
- finishing pass: separately choose Climb or Conventional (default Conventional regardless of main, because finishing is almost always conventional for surface quality)

Where 'finishing pass' = the offset that defines the wall surface:
- Pocket: level=0 boundary ring
- Profile: the offset at the final cut depth (single-pass profile is itself the finishing pass)

Algorithm: a new apply_cut_direction(&mut [PolylineOffset], op, main, finish) post-pass walks each offset, computes its (outer|inner) context from the op kind + ToolOffset + signed_area sign, decides desired winding from the (context, direction) matrix above, and reverses segment order + swaps start/end + negates bulge if the actual winding doesn't match.

Wire schema:
- new CutDirection { Conventional, Climb } in wiac_core::project
- OperationParams gains cut_direction: CutDirection (default Conventional) and finish_pass_cut_direction: CutDirection (default Conventional)
- regen openapi.yaml + frontend types

UI: a new fieldset in OpPropertiesPanel with two selects (main + finishing). Visible for Profile + Pocket, hidden for Engrave / DragKnife / Drill (no climb/conventional concept).

Tests:
- enforce_winding_inner_conventional_is_ccw + variants for each (context × direction)
- pocket_with_climb_main_and_conventional_finish: outer ring CCW + cascade rings CW
- profile_outside_climb: signed area of the resulting offset > 0
- regression on existing pocket_with_outer_plus_inner_selection_emits_a_single_annulus to confirm default behavior unchanged
acceptance_criteria: default conventional preserves current toolpath area; climb mode flips signed_area sign on every emitted offset
close_reason:
Climb vs Conventional shipped end-to-end:

Wire schema:
- new CutDirection { Conventional, Climb } in wiac_core::project
- OperationParams gained cut_direction (main) + finish_cut_direction; both default Conventional, both serde-skipped on default so existing payloads stay unchanged
- schema regenerated → openapi.yaml → openapi-typescript

Algorithm in cam/offsets.rs:
- enforce_winding(offset, context, direction) reverses segment order + swaps start/end + negates bulge if the actual signed_area sign doesn't match the convention
- apply_cut_direction(offsets, op, _) walks each PolylineOffset, picks finish_cut_direction for level=0 and cut_direction for level≥1, and dispatches enforce_winding
- Context derived from op.kind + ToolOffset for Profile, signed_area sign for Pocket (CCW = inner-context cutter inside pocket; CW = outer-context cutter around an island), Skip for Engrave/DragKnife

Pipeline integration: apply_cut_direction is called as the final post-pass in both build_op_offsets paths (Auto + non-Auto combine).

Tests:
- 5 unit tests in cam/offsets.rs covering each (context × direction)
- 1 reverse_offset test asserting bulge negation
- 1 e2e pipeline test pocket_with_climb_main_and_conventional_finish_winds_correctly that runs run_pipeline with main=Climb + finish=Conventional and verifies the boundary loop is CCW (conventional) while at least one cascade ring is CW (climb)

UI:
- OpPropertiesPanel got Direction + Finish dir selects inside the Cut fieldset, only rendered for Profile + Pocket
- addOperation seeds new ops with both = 'conventional'
- build-project.ts only emits the wire fields when ≠ conventional
