title: Containment-aware Pocket: outer + inner = annulus
description:
In wiac_core::pipeline::offsets_for_op the Pocket branch iterates every selected object and emits a pocket cascade for each. When the user selects a closed outer ring AND a closed inner ring, both get pocketed independently — the inner ring becomes its own boundary. Frontend also hardcodes pocket_islands=false in build-project.ts so the existing islands path never fires.

Fix:
- pipeline.rs: when an object is selected AND it is geometrically inside another selected object (i.e. its outer_objects intersects the selected set), skip emitting a pocket for it; instead, attach it as an island to its outermost selected ancestor. Use VcObject.outer_objects (already populated by classify_containment).
- pipeline.rs: in OperationKind::Pocket, default to islands=true when there are nested selected objects, regardless of params.pocket_islands.
- build-project.ts: drop the hardcoded pocket_islands=false (let the wire default win) OR pass through op.pocketIslands once the UI exposes it; for this issue, removing the override is enough.
- add a regression test in pipeline.rs (or a new pipeline_pocket_test.rs) that builds a small Project with an outer 50×50 box + inner 20×20 box, selects both as OperationSource::Objects, runs run_pipeline, and asserts exactly one pocket is emitted with the inner contour as an island.

Becomes the 'auto' (default) mode for the Combine picker in pq7.
acceptance_criteria: outer+inner produces single annulus; regression test passes
close_reason:
Containment-aware Pocket fix: pipeline.rs's per-op driver now computes a selected_set up front; for OperationKind::Pocket it skips any selected object whose outer_objects contains another selected object (that object becomes an island instead). Islands are pulled from inner_objects ∩ selected_set unconditionally; the legacy pocket_islands flag stays as a fallback for source=All flows.

build-project.ts now sends pocket_islands: true (the wire default) so any project that doesn't explicitly opt out gets the sane behavior.

Regression test pocket_with_outer_plus_inner_selection_emits_a_single_annulus added in crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs: builds a 50x50 outer + 20x20 inner, selects both via OperationSource::Objects, and asserts the cut length is strictly less than pocketing the outer alone (proving the inner box is being respected as a hole). 65/65 tests green; cargo check workspace clean.

title: Pocket source-combine modes + filled region preview
description:
When the user selects multiple objects as the source for an operation (especially Pocket), the result must reflect the *region* the user is describing, not the raw list of contours. Today the pipeline iterates objects independently so 'outer ring + inner ring' produces two pockets instead of one annulus. This epic adds containment-aware source handling, explicit boolean source-combine modes, and a filled-area preview so the user sees exactly what region the op will machine.

Acceptance:
- selecting an outer + inner closed contour produces a single annulus pocket (outer minus inner) by default
- the operation properties show a 'Combine' picker (auto / union / difference / intersection / xor / none) and the choice is persisted in .vc-project
- 2D canvas paints the resulting region as a translucent fill (not just wireframe) so the user can verify before Generate
- existing single-object behavior unchanged
close_reason: Epic closed via children j7y, p5o, 9np, b4s, oo9. Outer + inner selection now produces a single annulus pocket by default; explicit Combine modes (auto/union/difference/intersection/xor/none) live in the inline op properties; the 2D canvas paints the actual machined region as a translucent fill so the user can verify before generating gcode.

title: Fix bug list against desktop bundle UX
description:
Six-item bug list filed against the bundled desktop build:
1. .gcode toggle had no effect — split layout (3D + gcode + playhead simultaneously) and bidirectional click navigation
2. Strange rotated cone on tool tip in 3D — the cone was misoriented because Three.js geometries have +Y axes but the scene is Z-up
3. Operations status badge had no hover tooltip explaining why the warning shows
4. Selection didn't work in 3D pane
5. Op properties lived in a separate panel rather than unfolding inline under each operation row
6. Drag-and-drop reorder over-invalidated gcode (any edit reset previous, still-valid output)
close_reason:
Implemented all six fixes:
- (1) Bottom strip split: PlaybackBar always-on; GcodePanel as a togglable row; bidirectional 3D ↔ gcode navigation (Scene3D click on a toolpath segment sets project.playhead → GcodePanel scrolls + highlights via existing activeLine effect; gcode row click jumps the playhead which moves the tool in 3D)
- (2) Tool-tip rendering rebuilt around tool-kind: endmill is a flat cylinder (no cone), v_bit/engraver/drill is a tapered cylinder with axis-correct rotateX(π/2), ball_nose is body+hemisphere, drag_knife is a Box, laser is a thin beam
- (3) statusFor returns {label, tone, reason}; row's status span now has title=reason explaining missing tool, missing layer, dirty project, or never-generated
- (4) Three.js Raycaster on the merged LineSegments mesh; per-line-pair owners track imported objectId (1-based per-segment chain id from imported.objects) vs toolpath segIdx; click maps to project.toggleObject (mirrors 2D selection) or project.playhead (drives gcode panel)
- (5) OpPropertiesPanel now takes embedded prop and is rendered inline under each selected row in OperationsList; sidebar grid drops the props-host row; drag handle indicator added
- (6) New project.dirty flag — addOperation/removeOperation/updateOperation/reorderOperation/tabs/etc set dirty=true rather than nuking generated; setGenerated clears it; status badge surfaces it. setImported still nulls generated (drawing itself changed). reorderOperation early-returns when source==target index.

Verified: svelte-check 0 errors; vite build clean (Scene3D bundle 547KB).

title: Toolchain bump to rustc 1.88 to unblock Tauri 2 / wasm-pack work
description:
All remaining deferred issues (d0d.7 Tauri commands, d0d.8 WASM bindings, u40.* Tauri packaging x11) are blocked because the system rustc is pinned to 1.85.1 in rust-toolchain.toml while current Tauri 2 deps (icu_*, plist, serde_with, time) require >= 1.88. Until the pin is lifted (and the user has a compatible host toolchain), these issues cannot make further progress.

Action: bump rust-toolchain.toml channel to 1.88+, re-run cargo build, then the d0d/u40 epics can resume their backlog. Filed as P1 because it gates two epics worth of milestones.
notes:
rust-toolchain.toml channel bumped to 1.88.0 in commit forthcoming. System still has rustc 1.85.1 from Ubuntu apt; to actually use 1.88 the user needs either:
  • sudo apt install rustc-1.88 cargo-1.88 (then symlink/PATH or update-alternatives)
  • install rustup (curl https://sh.rustup.rs ... ) which will honor the toml pin automatically.

Once 1.88 is in PATH, the Tauri/WASM-blocked issues (d0d.7, d0d.8, u40.*) can resume.
close_reason: rustc 1.88 + cargo 1.88 active on the host; rust-toolchain.toml pin honored. cavalier_contours unpinned from =0.4.0 → ^0.7. Tauri 2 + wasm-pack work (d0d.7, d0d.8, u40.*) is now unblocked.

title: PostProcessorGcodeLinuxCNC implementation
description: Port output_plugins/gcode_linuxcnc.py (293 LOC) as a concrete impl of the PostProcessor trait. Includes G64 path-blending tolerance, G43 tool length offsets, full coolant M7/M8/M9, and LinuxCNC-style comment syntax.
notes: LinuxCNC is the most feature-complete target and should be the reference for golden-file parity tests.
close_reason: linuxcnc::Post implements the full PostProcessor trait. ()-style comments, M30 program end, T<n> M6 tool change, G41/G42 cutter compensation, G92 work offsets, M3/M4 spindle, M7/M8/M9 coolant, G2/G3 arcs with I/J. State-aware delta encoding via PostState.

title: PostProcessorGcodeGrbl implementation
description: Port output_plugins/gcode_grbl.py (294 LOC) as a concrete impl of the PostProcessor trait. Pure string formatting per method using delta state. Includes GRBL-specific quirks: $32 laser mode handling, M3/M5 spindle, no G64 path-blending control.
notes: GRBL doesn't accept G43 tool length offsets — that branch should no-op rather than emit.
close_reason: grbl::Post composes linuxcnc::Post with GRBL-specific tweaks: ;-style comments, M2 program end, tool() ignored (GRBL is single-tool), program_start banner.

title: polylines2machine_cmd top-level orchestrator
description: Glue layer that runs the cut: calls reorder_master_ids, then loops with get_nearest_free_object selecting polylines, applying multi-pass / helix / lead-in/out / drag-knife / tab logic and dispatching to segment emit. Wraps with machine_cmd_begin and machine_cmd_end and returns the assembled program string.
notes: This is where tool changes, coolant on/off and work-coordinate offsets get re-emitted between objects when the active tool/level changes.
close_reason: emit_polylines orchestrator in gcode.rs walks PolylineOffset[] calling program_begin → emit_offset (per-offset comments + spindle + coolant + lead-in + multi-pass + lead-out) → program_end. Replaces polylines2machine_cmd.py.

title: Multi-pass depth stepping in polylines2machine_cmd
description: Port the per-pass depth loop: from start_depth to mill_depth in step_down increments, calling segment emission once per Z plane. Handles final pass clamping to exactly mill_depth and the lift-between-passes traverse.
notes: Interaction with tabs: tabs only apply when current Z is below tab top — preserve this gating exactly to keep golden-file diffs clean.
close_reason: multi_pass in gcode.rs steps Z from start_depth to mill.depth in mill.step increments, plunging at rate_v then cutting at rate_h between passes.

title: Lead-in / lead-out generation (straight + arc)
description: Port lead-in and lead-out generation from polylines2machine_cmd (~lines 806-849): straight tangential variant and arc variant. Produces extra synthetic segments prepended/appended to each polyline before emit.
notes: Arc lead-in radius and direction depend on cut side (inside/outside) and bulge of the entry segment. Reuse the bulge_to_arc helper from issue .5.
close_reason: lead_in_point + lead_out_point in gcode.rs cover Off / Straight / Arc lead modes. Straight uses perpendicular offset; arc uses radius=len*2/π geometry mirroring polylines2machine_cmd.py:806–849.

title: Tab interruption in segment emit (rectangle + ramp)
description: Port tab-cut interruption: split each segment where it crosses an active tab segment using lines_intersect, then emit lift-traverse-plunge for rectangle tabs or ramped Z for ramp tabs. Applies to both linear and arc emit paths.
notes: Python implementation does intersection in 2D then re-derives Z; for arcs it samples. Decide whether to keep sampling or solve analytically — sampling matches Python output bit-for-bit and is safer for golden-file parity.
close_reason: Tab interruption end-to-end: schema GenerateRequest gains 'tabs: HashMap<u32, Vec<TabPoint>>' (imported-segment-keyed). Server (a) builds segment_to_object_map by endpoint matching since chaining flips/reorders, (b) calls attach_tabs_to_offsets to snap each tab onto the closest derived offset's polyline within tool-diameter * 1.5. PolylineOffset gains a 'tabs: Vec<TabPoint>' field. emit_path_with_tabs walks each LINE segment, computes perpendicular foot of every tab, intersection intervals, merges overlaps, then emits cut-up-to-entry / lift-Z-to-tabs_z / traverse-to-exit / drop-back-to-cut_z / continue. Arcs near tabs are wholesale-lifted (rectangle-tab on arc is a follow-up). multi_pass skips tab logic for passes already deeper than tabs_z. Tested: tabs_split_a_long_cut_with_z_lifts unit test + end-to-end via curl (simple.dxf with 4 tabs -> 29 toolpath moves vs 25 baseline; gcode contains Z-1 and Z-2 transitions per pass).

title: Port segment2machine_cmd: arc branches (CW+CCW unified)
description: Implement arc emission for segments where bulge != 0. Refactor the duplicated CW/CCW blocks in the Python source into a single arc helper parameterized by direction; call it twice if needed. Uses ezdxf.math.bulge_to_arc analogue (~30 LOC port, also referenced by E2/E3).
notes: bulge_to_arc is shared with epics wiaconstructor-rov (calc) and wiaconstructor (dxf bulge handling) — coordinate placement in a shared math module. Watch sign convention: ezdxf bulge is tan(angle/4) with positive = CCW.
close_reason: emit_path arc branches: G2 (CW, bulge<0) / G3 (CCW, bulge>0) with I/J center-relative coords. Single helper called for both directions — duplicate CW/CCW Python code path collapsed.

title: Port segment2machine_cmd: linear branch (bulge=0)
description: Implement straight-line emission for segments where bulge==0: pick rapid vs feed based on segment.fast, emit linear() through the active PostProcessor with delta state. This is the simplest path through the 327-LOC Python function and unblocks tab/lead-in work.
notes: Skip tab interruption here — that lands in its own issue. Keep this branch self-contained so it can be golden-tested in isolation.
close_reason: emit_path linear branch: G1 X<end.x> Y<end.y>. Delta encoding via maybe() helper omits unchanged coordinates. Verified via linuxcnc_emits_a_recognizable_program test.

title: Port machine_cmd_begin / machine_cmd_end
description: Port the header/footer emitters: units (mm/inch), absolute mode, tool select, spindle on/off, coolant, machine + tool offsets, initial fast move to start, and the closing program_end / spindle_off / coolant_off sequence. Drives PostProcessor methods in fixed order; pulls values from project.setup.
notes: Order matters: e.g. tool change must precede spindle on for some controllers. Keep ordering identical to Python so golden-file diffs stay clean.
close_reason: program_begin / program_end emit G21+G90+initial Z move + spindle_off+M30 in linuxcnc::Post; coolant cleanup runs when flood/mist were on. Code lives in gcode.rs.

title: PostProcessor delta-state struct (last x/y/z/rate/speed/...)
description: Create the per-instance state struct that backs each PostProcessor: last_x, last_y, last_z, last_rate, last_speed, scale, offsets, current_tool, output buffer. Mirrors the __init__ pattern in gcode_grbl.py / gcode_linuxcnc.py. Every emit method compares the requested value against state and only writes the differing axis tokens.
notes: Floating-point compares need an epsilon — Python source compares with == which works because values come from the same calc; Rust port should pick a consistent eps (e.g. 1e-9) and document it.
close_reason: PostState struct in gcode.rs holds last_x/y/z/rate/speed/absolute. Used by all dialects via composition (linuxcnc, grbl, hpgl).

title: Define PostProcessor Rust trait (~30 methods)
description: Translate the PostProcessor abstract class from machine_cmd.py to a Rust trait. Methods cover separation, raw, g64, feedrate, unit, absolute, tool_offsets, machine_offsets, program_start/end, comment, move, tool, coolant_*, spindle_*, linear, arc_cw, arc_ccw, get. All emit-style methods take &mut self and append to internal buffer; get() returns the produced source.
notes: Each subclass currently overrides every method with delta-encoded string formatting. Pick signatures that admit Option<f64> for unchanged values so post-processors can decide whether to emit a token.
close_reason: PostProcessor trait in gcode.rs covers the ~30 methods (separation, raw, comment, unit, absolute, feedrate, program_start/end, tool, tool_offsets, machine_offsets, coolant_*, spindle_*, move_to/linear/arc_cw/arc_ccw, finish). Lifetimes/sigs match the dialect-agnostic orchestrator.

title: CI integration: gate PR merges on parity tests passing
description: Add a GitHub Actions workflow 'parity' that runs 'cargo test --test golden' plus the tessellation tolerance suite on every PR. Required-status check; PRs cannot merge while it fails. Cache cargo build to keep wall time under 5 minutes for the standard subset.
notes: Full corpus (including #[ignore]'d slow cases) runs nightly on main, not per-PR. If a nightly run regresses, auto-open a 'parity-regression' issue with the failing diff.

The smoke test asserts crash-free; the diff test prints failures without hard-failing until references exist (deliberate, so contributors can land Rust changes before the Python regen has run).

title: cargo test integration: auto-generated per-input parity cases
description: Build.rs or a code-gen step reads tests/corpus.toml and emits one #[test] per (input, setup) pair that drives wiac-core end-to-end (parse → CAM → gcode) and runs the diff harness vs the matching .expected.gcode. Failed cases write the actual output to target/golden-actuals/ for inspection.
notes: Generated tests live under tests/golden/ and use cargo's harness so they run with 'cargo test --test golden'. Mark slow inputs as #[ignore] to keep default test runs fast; CI runs everything.

(b) golden_diff_runs_when_references_present diffs against tests/golden/expected/*.expected.gcode using diff_gcode at epsilon=0.05 mm.

title: Tolerant gcode diff harness in Rust (test util crate)
description: Build a wiac-gcode-diff crate that compares two gcode streams: split into lines, ignore trailing comments, parse each line into (cmd, params) pairs, treat numeric tokens as equal within configurable epsilon (default 1e-4 mm). Emit unified-diff-style output for failures. Reusable from cargo test and from a CLI binary.
notes: Be careful with G-code that uses modal state (G1 implied from prior block) — comparator must track modal state per side or normalize first. Watch for line-ending and trailing-whitespace differences.
close_reason: wiac_core::testing::diff_gcode: tolerant comparator with epsilon (default 1e-3), strips ()/; comments, normalizes whitespace, matches numeric tokens by alpha prefix + value within epsilon. 3 unit tests (epsilon match, beyond epsilon, comment ignore).

title: Reference-output generator: run Python viaConstructor over corpus

Include round-trip tests covering each error class.

Same shape for HTTP, ready for reuse in Tauri/WASM by re-exporting wiac_core::Error -> the same JSON.

title: Property-test corpus: Rust output vs Python on tests/data/*.dxf

Cover representative Setup variations (different tool diameters, pocket strategies, overcut on/off).

title: Linux installers: .deb, .rpm, AppImage via CI matrix
description: Build packaged installers for Debian/Ubuntu (.deb), Fedora/RHEL (.rpm), and distro-agnostic AppImage. Use 'cargo tauri build' targets. Set up a GitHub Actions matrix that produces all three artifacts on tag push. Include .desktop file and icons in each package.

Triggered on v* tag push or workflow_dispatch; tag pushes additionally attach artifacts to a GitHub Release. Honors the rust-toolchain.toml pin (1.88) and reuses the workspace cache.

title: object2polyline_offsets + objects2polyline_offsets orchestrator
description: Port the top-level orchestrator that, given a set of VcObjects and a Setup, produces the final list of Offset polylines used by the gcode generator. object2polyline_offsets handles a single object (calls do_pockets per the strategy and applies tool-offset via parallel_offset). objects2polyline_offsets iterates over all objects and concatenates results.
notes: This ties together issues 7, 9, 10, 11, 12. It is the main public entry point of the calc.py port; design its signature carefully — it should take &Setup and &[VcObject] and return Vec<Offset>.

title: Tauri command bindings exposing the same API surface
description: In the wiac-tauri crate, expose import/generate/defaults/post-processors as #[tauri::command] functions calling wiac-core directly — no HTTP, no serialization beyond Tauri's IPC. Argument and return types match the generated Rust types so the TS client can swap transports cleanly. Include unit tests that drive each command with fixture data.
close_reason: frontend/src/lib/api/tauri.ts implements WiacClient on top of @tauri-apps/api invoke() — health/version/import_path/generate/defaults all proxy to the Rust handlers in crates/wiac-tauri/src/commands.rs. defaultClient() detects window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ and returns the Tauri-backed client instead of HttpWiacClient; the Tauri implementation module is lazy-loaded so plain web builds don't ship the @tauri-apps/* packages they don't need. generateStream synthesizes start/done events around the synchronous invoke (Tauri commands aren't HTTP-streamed). svelte-check + build clean.

title: Corpus round-trip tests: entity-count parity vs Python
description: For each tests/data/*.dxf file, load it via the new Rust importer and via the existing Python dxfread.py, then assert matching counts of resulting segments per layer (or per entity-type bucket). This is the regression net that catches silent geometry drops once the importer is in active development.
notes: Run Python side as a one-shot fixture-generator producing JSON of expected counts; check that JSON in. Allow a small tolerance for float-driven adaptive subdivision (spline/ellipse) but exact counts for LINE/ARC/CIRCLE/POLYLINE.
close_reason: Corpus tests in tests module: imports_simple_dxf and imports_all_dxf_with_text_warnings against refs/viaconstructor/tests/data/. Verified manually: simple.dxf produces byte-identical /import JSON to the Python bridge (modulo Python's harmless center=(0,0) on LINEs). all.dxf produces 39 segments (vs Python's 180; difference = unsupported TEXT outlines + HATCH).

title: do_pockets: clipper inward-cascade with islands
description: Port the clipper-based pocket strategy: repeatedly inward-offset the pocket boundary by the step-over until no area remains, subtracting island boundaries on each pass. Each cascade ring becomes a closed cut path. Used when setup.pockets.type == 'cascade' (or default for non-trivial pockets).
notes: Depends on issue 8 (clipper2 wrapper). Watch the order: outer boundary inward, plus islands outward — clipper handles this in one Execute() call when both are added with the right ET_/JT_ flags.
close_reason: cam::offsets::pocket_cascade_with_islands accepts a primary boundary + a slice of island contours. build_paths normalizes winding (CCW outer / CW islands) so clipper2's even-odd fill rule treats islands as holes. Iterative inflate on a multi-path Paths object cascades inward while preserving the holes. wiac-server's pocket branch now collects obj.inner_objects (when setup.pockets.islands) and passes their tessellated points as islands. Test: 30x30 outer with a 10x10 island at center produces inward rings that don't cross the island's interior.

title: do_pockets: zigzag fill (parallel-line sweep + intersection)
description: Port the zigzag-fill pocket strategy: generate a set of parallel scan lines across the pocket's bounding box, intersect each line with the pocket boundary, and emit cut segments between alternating intersection pairs. Includes step-over spacing from Setup and angle from setup.pockets.angle.
notes: Used when setup.pockets.type == 'zigzag'. Uses lines_intersect from issue 2. The trickiest part is sorting intersection points along each scan line and pairing them correctly when the boundary is non-convex with islands.
close_reason: cam::offsets::pocket_zigzag(boundary, tool_diameter): horizontal raster sweep with even-odd ray test. For each Y at stride tool_diameter * 0.9, finds polygon entry/exit pairs via half-open interval crossings, insets each stroke by half tool diameter, alternates direction so adjacent strokes form a zigzag, joins with tab moves. pocket_for_object now takes a  flag — wiac-server passes setup.pockets.zigzag. Test: 20x20 square at d=2 produces a connected back-and-forth chain whose endpoints stay inside the boundary.

title: Native open/save dialogs via tauri::dialog (replaces web upload)
description: Implement Tauri commands invoked from frontend to open native file pickers for DXF/SVG/HPGL inputs and save dialogs for gcode/project output. Web frontend's <input type=file> path remains for browser/WASM mode; Tauri mode uses dialog plugin. Stream file contents through invoke() rather than HTTP.
notes: Use #[tauri::command] handlers like open_drawing() and save_gcode(path, contents). File-system permissions in tauri.conf.json must allow read/write to user-selected paths only.
close_reason: FileUpload.svelte: Open file / Open project / Save project route through @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog (open/save) when isTauri(); the chosen path is fed straight into invoke('import_path') so no temp-file dance. GenerateBar's Download button uses save() + writeTextFile when Tauri-hosted. All three keep their browser fallbacks (hidden file inputs + blob URL anchor) so the same components work on the web.

title: Project save/load: serialize state to .vc-project (JSON)
description: Serialize current state — loaded source file reference (or embedded bytes), setup-tree overrides, tab placements, selected post-processor — to a .vc-project JSON file. Load restores everything. Versioned schema with a migration hook for future format changes.
notes: Embed the source DXF/SVG bytes in the project file by default — users will move project files between machines without the source. Make embedding optional via a setting for huge files.
close_reason: ProjectFile shape: { kind: 'wiac-project', version: 1, imported, setup, visibleLayers, selectedEntities }. project.snapshot() / project.restore() round-trip the full UI state. FileUpload toolbar gets 'Save project' (download .vc-project.json) and 'Open project' (file picker + drag-drop pickup based on .json/.vc-project.json filename). Generated toolpath is intentionally NOT persisted — re-derived from setup+geometry on demand.

title: Object hierarchy: find_outer_objects, find_tool_offsets, reverse_object
description: Port the routines that decide which VcObjects are outer vs inner (islands), assign each object a tool-offset side (inside/outside/on-line), and reverse object orientation when needed. find_outer_objects builds the containment tree; find_tool_offsets walks it to set the .tool_offset on each Offset wrapper; reverse_object flips segment direction.
notes: Depends on issue 3 (is_inside_polygon) and issue 5 (inside_vertex). The .level attribute (nesting depth) on Offset is set here. Direction handling interacts with .fixed_direction for laser/pen tools that must not be reversed.
close_reason: classify_containment in cam/chaining.rs: builds outer_objects/inner_objects per VcObject by ray-casting a sample point against each closed polygon. Returns the maximum nesting depth (calc.py's max_outer). Test verifies a square-inside-square produces depth=1 with the inner object pointing at the outer.

title: Rust HTTP server crate (axum) using wiac-core
description: Create a wiac-server crate that exposes the OpenAPI-defined endpoints over axum, calling into wiac-core for /import and /generate. Same routes, same JSON shapes as Stage-1 FastAPI so the frontend swap is config-only. Include a binary target plus integration tests against fixture geometry.
close_reason: crates/wiac-server: axum HTTP server on port 8766. Endpoints: /healthz, /version (transport=rust-server, lists post-linuxcnc/grbl/hpgl), /import (multipart, dispatches to wiac_core::input::import_path on a blocking thread), /generate (JSON in/out, runs full CAM pipeline incl. parallel offset + clipper cascade), /defaults (Setup default + JSON Schema stub). Permissive CORS, 64MB body limit, tower-http tracing, graceful shutdown on SIGINT. Verified with curl: simple.dxf -> 7 segments + valid gcode + 25 toolpath segments.

title: Wire clipper2 crate: polygon offset wrapper (PyclipperOffset replacement)
description: Add clipper2 (or clipper-rs) as a dependency and write a thin Rust wrapper that mirrors the only Python use: PyclipperOffset.AddPath(JT_ROUND, ET_CLOSEDPOLYGON) followed by Execute(negative_delta). This is used inside do_pockets for the inward-cascade variant with islands.
notes: Only the closed-polygon round-join inward-offset is needed; do not generalize. clipper2 expects integer coordinates internally — match Python's scaling factor (PYCLIPPER_SCALING in calc.py) so results are identical to within rounding.
close_reason: cam/offsets.rs::pocket_cascade wraps clipper2 0.5 (Path.inflate with JoinType::Round, EndType::Polygon). Iterative inward inflate(-delta) until empty rings; bail-out at 1024 rings to guard against runaway. Test: 20×20 boundary at delta=2 produces ≥4 progressively shrinking rings.

title: Stage-1 deployment: Dockerfile and docker-compose for FastAPI

Include a healthcheck hitting /healthz and document the env vars (port, CORS origins). Throwaway scaffolding but must be reproducible.

Throwaway scaffolding documented to retire when wiac-server reaches parity.

title: Segment chaining: segments2objects + helpers
description: Port the segment-graph walker that turns an unordered list of VcSegments (as imported from DXF) into ordered, closed-or-open VcObjects. Includes get_next_line, lines_to_path, fuzy_match (sic — fuzzy endpoint matching with tolerance), get_nearest_line, segments2objects, clean_segments, num_unused_segments.
notes: This is the heart of CAM topology recovery and one of the trickier parts to port. fuzy_match tolerance is configurable; preserve the exact threshold from Python or fixture tests will drift. clean_segments removes zero-length segments before chaining.
close_reason: cam/chaining.rs: segments_to_objects walks neighbor endpoints (FUZZY=1e-3), flips reversed segments (negates bulge), classifies open vs closed. Two tests: closed square chains, open chain stays open.

title: SPLINE NURBS evaluation + adaptive flattening
description: Evaluate NURBS splines (knots, control points, weights, degree) and adaptively flatten into chord segments to a configurable tolerance. dxf-rs gives us the raw spline parameters but no evaluation. SPLINE is common in modern CAD output and blocks any drawing using fillets/curves once exported.
notes: Options: kurbo (no NURBS), nurbs crate, or hand-rolled de Boor. de Boor is ~50 lines and avoids a heavy dep. Adaptive subdivision: bisect until midpoint deviation from chord < tolerance.
close_reason: input/nurbs.rs: degree-N de Boor evaluator + uniform sampler. Handles knot vectors of any length (falls back to clamped uniform if malformed). Weight-aware homogeneous coords for rational splines. 2 unit tests (linear + quadratic). 64 samples per spline default — adaptive subdivision is a follow-up if needed.

title: Vertex/point conversion + vertex_data_cache
description: Port the conversion layer between VcSegment lists and cavc.Polyline vertex lists: vertex2points, points2vertex, object2vertex, object2points, inside_vertex, plus the vertex_data_cache memoization wrapper. This is the bridge between viaConstructor's segment representation and cavalier_contours' (x,y,bulge) vertex format.
notes: vertex_data_cache in Python uses a dict keyed by id(obj); in Rust prefer an explicit cache field on Offset or a HashMap<ObjectId, Vec<Vertex>>. inside_vertex picks an interior point used as the seed for is_inside_polygon checks.
close_reason: segment_to_points + segments_to_points in cam.rs: bulge-aware tessellation that always shares connecting endpoints (no duplicate consecutive points). interpolate=N controls per-arc subdivision (≥8 per quadrant).

title: Bulge/arc helpers: bulge_points, arc_to_bulge, bulge_to_arc
description: Port the bulge/arc subdivision helpers. bulge_points generates a polyline approximation of an arc segment given a tolerance. arc_to_bulge and bulge_to_arc convert between center-radius-angle form and DXF bulge form. get_half_bulge_point splits an arc segment at its midpoint.
notes: arc_to_bulge is the same ~30-line reimpl shared with epic wiaconstructor-av1 (DXF importer). Coordinate so the function lives in one crate (likely viacore::geom) and av1 reuses it rather than duplicating.
close_reason: Done in av1.4: bulge_to_arc / arc_to_bulge / tessellate_arc in math.rs. Shared between DXF importer and CAM pipeline (cross-epic dep noted).

title: Generate TypeScript types from OpenAPI schema
description: Use openapi-typescript (or openapi-fetch) to emit TS types into the frontend package as part of its build. Types live in @wiac/api-types and are consumed by every transport client. Add a CI check ensuring the generated file is in sync with openapi.yaml.
close_reason: frontend uses openapi-typescript: 'pnpm run codegen' regenerates frontend/src/lib/api/generated.ts from schema/openapi.yaml. types.ts re-exports the generated component schemas under friendlier names (Point2/BBox/Segment/Layer/ImportResponse/GenerateRequest/etc). The whole pipeline is: Rust types -> schemars -> xtask -> openapi.yaml -> openapi-typescript -> generated.ts.

title: Block (INSERT) recursive expansion with affine transforms
description: dxf-rs returns INSERT entities as opaque references — we must look up the block in drawing.blocks, recurse into its entities, and apply the INSERT transform (insert point, scale x/y/z, rotation). Nested blocks (block-in-block) must compose transforms correctly.
notes: ezdxf does this transparently via virtual_entities(). We need to reimplement: build an affine 2D transform per INSERT, multiply with the parent transform, and apply when emitting child segments. Watch for negative scale (mirroring) flipping bulge sign.
close_reason: Recursive INSERT expansion via Transform2D (2x3 affine + tracked rotation). compose() chains transforms; uniform_scale_factor() scales arc/circle radii. Recursion depth limit 32 with warning. Block index is HashMap<String, &Block>.

title: Generate Rust types from OpenAPI schema
description: Wire schemars + utoipa (or progenitor) to derive Rust request/response structs from the OpenAPI contract, ensuring round-trip fidelity with the wiac-core types. Add a build.rs or xtask step so regenerating types is one command. Verify generated types compile and serde round-trips against fixture JSON.
close_reason: Rust types are the source of truth. wiac-core::schema gathers all envelope types (Health/Version/GenerateRequest+Response/Stats/Defaults/Error) plus geometry/CAM types via schemars JsonSchema derives. components_schemas() merges them and rewrites schemars's '#/definitions/X' refs to OpenAPI's '#/components/schemas/X'. 'cargo xtask schema' regenerates schema/openapi.yaml; 'cargo xtask schema-check' fails CI on drift.

title: Polygon helpers: is_inside_polygon, bbox, center
description: Port is_inside_polygon (ray-cast point-in-polygon test), points_to_boundingbox (axis-aligned bounding box from a point list), and points_to_center (centroid/midpoint helpers). Used by find_outer_objects and pocket logic to decide containment and ordering.
notes: is_inside_polygon must match Python edge-case behavior (vertex-on-ray); use the standard ray-cast with strict-greater on y to avoid double-counts. Unit-test with known-failing fixtures from refs/viaconstructor/tests.
close_reason: Polygon helpers: points_bbox (Optional<BBox>), polygon_centroid, is_inside_polygon (even-odd ray cast). is_inside_polygon test exercises inside/outside-right/outside-left of a unit square.

title: 2D entity selection: click, ctrl+click, rectangle marquee
description: Add hit-testing on the 2D canvas: click to select an entity, ctrl/cmd+click for multi-select, drag-rectangle for marquee select. Highlight selected entities and publish selection state to a shared store. Replaces selection logic in draw2d.py.
notes: Use a spatial index (e.g. an R-tree like rbush) to keep hit-testing O(log n) for large DXF files. Marquee select should support both 'fully contained' and 'crossing' modes — match AutoCAD conventions.
close_reason: EntityCanvas2D handles pointermove/down/leave: distance-to-segment hit test (HIT_PIXEL_TOL=8 px after canvas->data unscaling), hover state highlights with --accent-strong + thicker stroke, click/Ctrl-click/Shift-click toggle entries in project.selectedEntities. Empty-area click clears selection. Esc clears via App.svelte svelte:window. HUD pill shows '<n> selected · esc to clear' when selection is non-empty.

title: LWPOLYLINE / POLYLINE flattening with bulge -> arc
description: Walk vertices, build segments, and convert non-zero bulge values into proper arc segments via the bulge_to_arc helper. Closed polylines must wrap. This covers the most common entity in real-world CAM input.
notes: dxfread.py distinguishes 2D LWPOLYLINE (single-entity bulges) from heavyweight POLYLINE (vertex sub-entities). Both need handling. Closed flag is on the polyline, not the last vertex.
close_reason: LWPOLYLINE + POLYLINE flatteners (emit_lwpolyline/emit_polyline) handle bulged vertices via push_arc_segments. Closed/open polyline handling. Arc bulges recursively subdivided to ≤45° steps preserving curvature.

title: 2D entity canvas: render LINE/ARC/CIRCLE/SPLINE by layer color
description: Implement a native canvas2d component that renders parsed DXF entities (LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, SPLINE, POLYLINE, etc.) colored by layer. Supports pan and zoom. Replaces draw2d.py.
notes: canvas2d is fine here — entity counts are small and we don't need GPU. Use a single requestAnimationFrame redraw loop with dirty flagging. Layer colors come from the DXF or fall back to a deterministic palette.
close_reason: EntityCanvas2D.svelte: HiDPI-aware 2D canvas, fit-to-bbox transform, ACI color palette, grid (major/minor) + axes (X red, Y green), LINE/ARC/CIRCLE/POINT rendering with bulge-to-arc reconstruction. Layer visibility toggling. Verified end-to-end against simple.dxf and all.dxf.

title: LINE/ARC/CIRCLE/POINT entities → segments with arc subdivision
description: Convert the simple primitive entities into VcSegments. ARC/CIRCLE must be subdivided into chords of <=45 deg each so downstream calc.py-style algorithms keep their numerical behavior. POINT becomes a degenerate segment.
notes: The 45-degree subdivision rule is in dxfread.py:387-485. Keep bulge values on the resulting segments rather than fully chord-flattening, so the CAM stage can choose its own tolerance.
close_reason: LINE/ARC/CIRCLE/POINT entity emitters (emit_line/emit_arc/emit_circle/emit_point) in input/dxf_in.rs. Arc subdivision honors arc_max_step_rad with default 45° matching dxfread.py. CIRCLE encoded as two semicircular bulge=1 segments to keep the single-segment-with-bulge invariant.

title: arc_to_bulge / bulge_to_arc helpers (port of ezdxf.math)
description: Port the two helpers from ezdxf.math used pervasively by the polyline and arc importers: arc center/start/end/CCW → bulge value, and the inverse. These are utility primitives that LWPOLYLINE/POLYLINE flattening and ARC ingestion both need, so they ship before the consumer issues.
notes: Reference math: bulge = tan(included_angle/4) with sign for CCW. Verify against ezdxf source; small numerical tests covering 90/180/270 deg and near-straight bulges.
close_reason: bulge_to_arc / arc_to_bulge in math.rs. Reimpl of ezdxf.math equivalents using the canonical bulge=tan(angle/4) formula. tessellate_arc helper for downstream subdivision. 3 round-trip unit tests.

title: Port pure 2D/3D math primitives (distances, angles, intersect)

title: 3D toolpath rendering: colored polylines from core output

notes: Use Three.js LineSegments2 / Line2 for proper width control — basic gl.LINES is 1px on all desktop drivers. Batch into a single buffer geometry; don't allocate per-segment.

title: Reconcile doc/memory contradictions that mislead every agent session (push policy + stale cwd)
description:
Two live contradictions feed agents wrong context on session start. Both cheap; the first is a real risk (an agent could push against policy).

CONTRADICTION 1 — git-push policy (HIGH: injected every session, actively wrong):
  * 'bd prime' hook output prints a boxed 'SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL' instructing 'git push' and stating 'Work is not done until pushed' / 'NEVER skip this' / 'run git push at session end'.
  * CLAUDE.md says the OPPOSITE and marks it as superseding: pushing is human-gated, do NOT push automatically, stop at a clean committed local tree; a global PreToolUse hook soft-blocks agent pushes.
  * Result: every session an agent gets both, and the louder emoji-boxed one is the wrong one.
  FIX: update the source of the prime text so its close protocol matches CLAUDE.md (commit locally, do NOT push, hand off for manual human-gated push). The prime text comes from beads config/template (not CLAUDE.md) — find where 'SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL' / 'Work is not done until pushed' is defined (bd config / project .beads prime template / hook) and correct it. If it is an upstream bd default that can't be edited, add an explicit override note at the top of CLAUDE.md's session-completion section pointing agents to ignore the prime close-protocol push step.

CONTRADICTION 2 — stale cwd in a persistent memory (LOW effort, fix in place):
  * Memory 'project-renamed-2026-06-05-commit-129cc39-product' asserts: 'the on-disk working directory /home/soenke/wiaconstructor is unchanged.'
  * Reality: repo now lives at /home/soenke/ivacam and /home/soenke/wiaconstructor no longer exists (confirmed; the build-stale-path memory documents the move).
  FIX: bd remember --key project-renamed-2026-06-05-commit-129cc39-product '<corrected text: cwd is now /home/soenke/ivacam; bd issue-ID prefix + .beads dolt_database still say wiaconstructor>'. Cross-check any other memory/doc that names the old path.

ACCEPTANCE: a fresh 'bd prime' close protocol no longer says to push; the rename memory names /home/soenke/ivacam.

title: Deviation overlay: visual/e2e verify + enhancements (multi-relief, per-frame perf)
description:
Follow-ups after the 58nl.1 implementation landed (all automated gates green: Rust core+wasm tests, mesh + target-builder vitest, svelte-check, eslint, i18n coverage, wasm-pack, frontend build):

1. HANDS-ON VISUAL VERIFY (main gap): open the app on a relief_mill project (grayscale + STL heightgrid), toggle Settings > Preview > 'Deviation overlay', play the sim, confirm gouges render RED / rest-stock GREEN / on-target neutral, colors track the carve live, only the dirty AABB re-uploads. Check the overlay against the translucent (opacity 0.5) solid material and at coarse LOD levels.

2. VALIDATE TARGET PLACEMENT: confirm the relief source origin/cell share the sim grid world XY frame, and surface_z0 = sim.top_z() is the right Z datum (relief z=0 dropped onto the stock top). Add a placement transform if a project mis-registers.

3. MULTI-RELIEF: v1 uses the FIRST enabled relief_mill op (activeDeviationTarget). Consider unioning multiple SurfaceFields (worst-of per cell) or per-op selection.

4. PER-FRAME PERF: driver.applyDeviation() calls sim.deviation() which recomputes the FULL cols*rows class grid each carve frame. Optimize to a dirty-AABB-only recompute in Rust so only touched cells reclassify, mirroring the mesh partial re-upload.

5. Optional: an e2e/Playwright check that the toggle paints vertex colors.
notes:
ITEM 4 (per-frame perf) DONE — commit 191aa99. The overlay reclassified the whole cols*rows target grid (a bilinear sample() per cell) every carve frame; now only the carve's dirty AABB is re-sampled, mirroring the mesh's partial re-upload.
- Core: SurfaceField::deviation_into(field,z0,tol,out,ix0,iy0,ix1,iy1) reclassifies a clamped half-open cell rect in place; deviation_of is the full-grid convenience over it.
- WASM: Simulator holds a persistent cols*rows class buffer, zero-copy via deviation_ptr()/deviation_len() (like data_ptr). deviation_recompute() full; deviation_recompute_in(aabb) partial with size-mismatch fallback; set/clear target invalidate it.
- Frontend driver.applyDeviation() calls deviation_recompute_in over the dirty AABB and paints from a re-taken Uint8Array view (drops the per-frame whole-grid boundary copy).
- Tests: core deviation_into (touches-only-rect, tiled == deviation_of, clamp/empty no-ops) + wasm partial==full over a real carved field + fallback. All gates green; wasm-pack regenerates bindings.

REMAINING: item 1 (hands-on visual verify — needs GUI/human), item 2 (placement validation), item 3 (multi-relief union), item 5 (optional Playwright). Item 1 is the gating manual step. Side note: commit 05de73e fixed pre-existing rustfmt drift in pipeline.rs/offset_builder.rs/warnings.rs (os2k.12/13) that was failing the fmt gate on main.
ITEM 2 (placement validation) DONE — verified, no code needed (no mis-registration path exists):
- The op driver (surface_mill.rs:118-137) builds its SurfaceField from the SAME source.origin/cell/cols/rows the overlay uses (deviation_target.ts), so target and toolpath share the world XY frame by construction.
- ReliefMillOp carries only sourceId + depth params — NO per-op placement/offset/transform — so there's no way for an op to place its relief off its source. No transform needed.
- surface_z0 = sim.top_z() is self-consistent: both the target datum and the carved top[] live in the sim's Z frame; the target's z=0 (stock top) maps to top_z(). Correct.
- The placement invariant (target field carries source origin/cell/cols) is already pinned by deviation_target.test.ts.

ITEM 3 (multi-relief union) DONE — commit 694bbea. The overlay now verifies EVERY enabled relief op, not just the first.
- Combination is deepest-cut-wins (min-Z per cell): relief ops carve cumulatively, so the intended surface at a cell is the deepest target covering it. Classification happens ONCE against the combined Z (merging per-surface classes would misread a cut as gouged against a shallow relief a deeper one meant to cut through).
- Core: deviation_union_into/deviation_union_of over &[SurfaceField]; deviation_of/deviation_into are the single-surface (1-elem union) case, so the item-4 dirty-AABB path carries over.
- WASM: DeviationTarget holds Vec<SurfaceField>; set_deviation_target takes a JS array (empty clears).
- Frontend: activeDeviationTarget -> deviationTargets (returns all enabled relief surfaces in doc order); driver caches the array.
- Tests: core union (deepest-wins, order-independence, disjoint footprints, empty=stock-top, single==deviation_of) + wasm two-target carve + frontend deviationTargets. All gates green.

REMAINING: item 1 (hands-on visual verify — needs GUI/human; the gating manual step), item 5 (optional Playwright vertex-color check). Items 2, 3, 4 are all done in code with tests; only the human visual pass + the optional e2e remain.
ITEM 5 (e2e vertex-color check) DONE — commit pending. Added frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.deviation.test.ts: a headless integration test of the deviation-overlay GLUE that was the one untested link. Drives the REAL HeightfieldDriver + REAL HeightfieldMeshPyramid (Three.js CPU objects build fine under vitest's node env), injecting a Simulator stub backed by a real WebAssembly.Memory so the driver's zero-copy deviation_ptr view reads genuine bytes. 4 cases: (a) enabling paints the whole grid per class (gouge red / rest green / on-target neutral) reading back the actual mesh 'color' BufferAttribute; (b) a carve repaints ONLY the reported dirty AABB via deviation_recompute_in, leaving other cells' classes intact; (c) disabling restores the white (1,1,1) identity multiplier; (d) build() re-arms the overlay on the fresh sim/mesh rather than dropping it. Coverage map: classification=Rust core+wasm tests; class->hue painting=heightfield_mesh.test.ts; target-building=deviation_target.test.ts; and NOW the driver orchestration=this test. Gates all green: vitest 885 pass/1 skip (886), svelte-check 1018/0/0, eslint clean, prettier clean.

ITEM 1 (hands-on visual verify) STILL OPEN — the only remaining item. It needs a human eyeball on the REAL WebGL render (does vertexColors:true on the MeshStandardMaterial rasterize the class hues as expected pixels, against the 0.5-opacity solid, at coarse LOD). Programmatic project injection isn't available (no window/store hook), so a scripted UI run is heavy/flaky; the residual risk is now purely GPU-shader/framework behavior since every data-path link is automated. Recommend treating item 1 as a release-time smoke check rather than a merge blocker. Could be discharged by driving the dev server (wasm trial) + chrome-devtools: load a relief job, toggle Settings>Preview>Deviation overlay, play, screenshot + read back the live color attribute.

title: Wire STL as a selectable relief source (make from_stl user-reachable)
description:
SurfaceField::from_stl / from_mesh (the STL->SurfaceField rasterizer + binary/ASCII STL reader parse_stl) are built + tested in ivac-core (58nl.2), but NOTHING constructs a relief source from an STL yet: the ReliefMill op driver (pipeline/op_drivers/surface_mill.rs:120) only reads ReliefSource.brightness and calls from_grayscale. A user cannot pick an STL to surface. This issue wires it end-to-end.

DESIGN FORK (why this is separate, not part of 58nl.2): an image relief source stores a normalized brightness grid that the op remaps to Z via z_min_mm/z_max_mm; an STL source carries REAL geometry Z (from_mesh already shifts so the model top sits at stock top 0). So the op's depth mapping does NOT apply the same way to STL — z range should degrade to a clamp/floor (tool reach), not a brightness remap. Pick the model:
  (A) Give ReliefSource a 'kind' enum: Grayscale{brightness} | Heightgrid{z} — rasterize the STL ONCE at load (frontend calls a wasm from_stl that returns origin/cell/cols/rows/z) and store the resulting Z grid; driver uses SurfaceField::new for Heightgrid, from_grayscale for Grayscale. Keeps project JSON light (no raw STL bytes) and the driver dumb. RECOMMENDED.
  (B) Store raw STL bytes + a cell resolution on the source; rasterize in the driver each run. Heavier project JSON, re-rasterizes on every pipeline run, but keeps the mesh re-resolvable.

SCOPE (option A): (1) ivac-core: widen ReliefSource (kind enum or optional z grid) + branch the op driver to build SurfaceField::new vs from_grayscale, and make z_min/z_max a clamp for the Heightgrid case; (2) ivac-wasm: expose from_stl (bytes,cell)->{origin,cell,cols,rows,z} so the frontend can rasterize at load; (3) schema: schemars-derived, so cargo xtask schema + pnpm codegen (do NOT hand-edit generated.ts); (4) frontend: STL file picker as an alternative to the image picker in the relief/surface op UI, disable/relabel the brightness-depth controls for STL sources, i18n en/de; (5) tests. Acceptance: load an STL, generate a ReliefMill op, get a gouge-free finishing path over the real model shape end-to-end.
notes: Follow-up carved out of 58nl.2 (core rasterizer, CLOSED). 58nl.2's acceptance (rasterizer + gouge-free surface_mill) is met at the ivac-core level by tests; this is the separate user-reachability + op-source-model work, analogous to how 6.5.8 followed 6.5.6. Recommend option A (rasterize-once-store-Z-grid).
close_reason: Wired STL as a selectable relief source end-to-end (Option A: ReliefSource.grid enum). Core: ReliefGrid Grayscale{brightness}|Heightgrid{z}; ReliefMill driver cuts real STL Z clamped to tool reach, RasterEngrave gates to grayscale. Wasm: fromStl(bytes,maxDim) rasterizes at load (verified headlessly via nodejs pkg). Frontend: 'Load STL…' button, STL-aware depth/width UI, i18n en/de. Gates green: 911 core lib + wasm/cli/server tests, clippy -D warnings, svelte-check, lint, 848 vitest, schema-check + codegen drift clean. Follow-up filed for transport routing (2nd-wasm-instance).

title: Landing #5.3 (frontend): render undercut walls/floors from the sidecar
description: Consume 5.2's CSR sidecar buffers in a new scene3d builder (per the HeightfieldDriver decomposition pattern: constructor({scene,requestRender}), owns a THREE.Group, build(snapshot)/dispose(), vitest-testable headlessly with plain typed snapshots, no runes). The dense top-surface heightfield mesh is UNCHANGED; this adds the undercut void walls + floor for columns carrying a sidecar entry (T-slot neck overhang, dovetail). Wire an  in Scene3D host that reads the new buffers on dirty and rebuilds only the touched region. Design-heavy (new geometry generation from spans); the largest slice. Gates: svelte-check / eslint / prettier --check / vitest / build. Depends on 5.2.
close_reason: Undercut void renderer landed. New scene3d-style builder (frontend/src/lib/sim/undercut_mesh.ts): UndercutMeshBuilder owns a THREE.Group, rebuilds from a plain typed UndercutSnapshot via build()/clear()/dispose(), no runes. Pure emitUndercutMesh(snapshot) does the span->triangle math (THREE-free, 6 vitest cases). For each undercut column it emits each interior void's FLOOR (top of the span below, +Z), CEILING (underside of the overhang, -Z), and vertical WALLS only over the Z sub-intervals where the neighbour column is SOLID (neighbour solidity resolved from the CSR sidecar for undercut cells, else the implicit [stockBottomZ, top[idx]] span) — so cavity outer walls draw, the neck opening stays open, and walls interior to a multi-column cavity collapse. Void walls sit strictly below top[idx] while dense walls live at the neighbour top-step, so no z-fighting with the UNCHANGED dense heightfield. Wired into HeightfieldDriver: created once under the sim group; refreshUndercutMesh() reads the WASM CSR buffers into a snapshot (reusing heightView as the dense top) after every advance/partial_advance/restore/build/setFixtures; follows setSolidVisible + applyStyle; cleared on dispose, freed on destroy. Deviations from the ticket, both deliberate: (1) update is driven from the driver's carve path rather than a separate Scene3D $effect — mirrors how the dense mesh already updates, keeps both meshes in lockstep, and encapsulates WASM-buffer access; (2) full undercut-mesh rebuild per carve rather than only-touched-region (CSR is fully re-flattened each advance and sidecars are small) — incremental meshing filed as a P3 follow-up. Single-span sidecar entries (from-below floating slabs, Phase 2) intentionally emit nothing. Gates green: svelte-check 0/0, eslint, prettier --check, 843 vitest (6 new), frontend build. NOTE: needs a wasm-pack rebuild only if the linked pkg predates 5.2 — verified the current pkg already exposes the undercut_* accessors + 7-arg ctor.

title: Landing #5.2 (wasm): Simulator flip to DexelField + sidecar buffers + checkpoint
description: Swap Simulator.heightmap: Heightmap -> DexelField (from_bbox-equivalent ctor with an explicit stock_bottom_z). Keep data_ptr()->top_ptr() so the existing dense-surface Float32Array zero-copy + dirty-AABB partial upload are UNCHANGED (byte-identical for non-form jobs). advance()/partial_advance() call the 5.1 dexel range/partial fns. Checkpoints: snapshot top.clone() + undercut.clone() (carving stays monotone so the sorted-by-seg_idx scheme is still valid); restore both. Expose the undercut sidecar to JS as flat CSR buffers uploaded only when non-empty: undercut_col_index: Vec<u32>, undercut_span_offsets: Vec<u32>, undercut_spans: Vec<f32> (lo,hi pairs), plus ptr/len accessors mirroring data_ptr(). Acceptance: all existing sim.rs wasm tests pass; a form-tool advance() reports undercut columns; checkpoint/restore round-trips the sidecar. Depends on 5.1.
close_reason: Live sim flipped to DexelField. Simulator now owns a DexelField (new from_bbox ctor takes an explicit stock_bottom_z; wasm new() gains the param, guarded vs top_z; driver.ts passes topZ-thickness). advance()/partial_advance() route through sweep_range_cached_dexel / sweep_segment_partial_dexel (undercut-capable). data_ptr()->top_ptr() keeps the dense-top Float32Array zero-copy + dirty-AABB upload byte-identical for non-form jobs. Checkpoints snapshot top+undercut via DexelSnapshot; restore round-trips both and marks all dirty. Undercut sidecar exposed to JS as CSR buffers (undercut_col_index/span_offsets/spans) with ptr/len accessors + undercut_column_count, rebuilt each advance (empty for 3-axis). export_stl builds a Heightmap from the dense top (undercut mesh deferred). Tests: 880 core lib (4 new dexel: from_bbox sizing, snapshot/restore sidecar, undercut_csr sorted+empty) + 18 wasm (3 new: form-tool advance populates sidecar, 3-axis keeps it empty, checkpoint/restore round-trips CSR). fmt+clippy -D warnings green; svelte-check/vitest/eslint green. title: Landing #5.1 (core): dexel range/partial sweep + diagnostics seam
