title: P3 Phase 1 landing #1: Span + interval algebra + eval_interval (pure, zero-regression)
description:
First reviewable slice of the multi-span Z-dexel core (design in ivac-58nl.6). PURE primitives only — no field, no sweep wiring, no new deps — so it cannot regress the 3-axis hot path.

Scope:
1. New module crates/ivac-core/src/sim/dexel.rs with:
   - Span { lo: f32, hi: f32 } (invariant lo < hi, Z up)
   - subtract_interval(spans: &mut Vec<Span>, a, b): 1-D interval difference (split when interior)
   - merge_adjacent(spans: &mut Vec<Span>): coalesce touching/overlapping spans, keep sorted+disjoint
   - unit tests: disjoint, partial-overlap top/bottom, interior split, full cover -> empty, associativity (subtract [0,t] then [t,1] == subtract [0,1]) mirroring sweep.rs partial_advance_non_flat_no_drift.
2. ToolProfile::eval_interval(r) -> Option<(f32,f32)> in heightmap.rs: lo = eval(r), hi = +inf for every current kind (FormProfile upper surface deferred to landing #4). Test that .0 == eval(r) for all kinds and .1 is +inf.

Explicitly OUT of scope (later landings): DexelField hybrid field (byte-identity vs Heightmap), form_upper for T-slot undercuts, sweep_chord_carve_dexel, WASM/mesh sidecar.
design: Keep Vec<Span> (not SmallVec) for slice 1 to avoid adding a workspace dep before DexelField needs it. subtract_interval + merge_adjacent must be associative so the partial-t bitwise-identity guarantee (sweep.rs:1305) carries from min() to intervals. Full sketch attached to parent ivac-58nl.6 NOTES.
acceptance_criteria: dexel.rs compiles; cargo test -p ivac-core sim::dexel passes; eval_interval test green; cargo clippy --workspace clean; no change to existing heightmap/sweep tests (zero regression).
close_reason: Landed pure interval algebra (Span, subtract_interval, merge_adjacent) in sim/dexel.rs + ToolProfile::eval_interval (lo=eval, hi=+inf). 13 new tests incl. associativity (partial-t identity) and top-down==monotone-min. cargo test/clippy -D warnings/fmt all green; zero regression (856 lib tests pass).

title: P3: Material-model evolution — multi-dexel/voxel sim for undercuts, dual-surface & 4/5-axis
description:
The single Z(x,y) heightmap (sim/heightmap.rs:19-32, monotone-min, one Z per column) is the ROOT limitation of the destructive terrain. It cannot represent undercuts/overhangs, so it structurally cannot honestly simulate: T-slot necks & dovetail undercuts (heightmap.rs already down-grades a T-slot to 'carve the widest disk'), ball-nose steep-wall side cuts, two-sided/flip parts (ivac-rt1.11 blocked on exactly this — see rt1.11.1 gate: 'if a real voxel/SDF model is needed, that is a much bigger feature'), and any future 4/5-axis or lathe removal.

This issue is the design decision for the next-gen material model. Candidate representations: (A) multi-span Z-dexel (list of solid [z_lo,z_hi] spans per column) — cheapest step up, gets undercuts + flip; (B) tri-dexel (three orthogonal dexel stacks) — industry standard (ModuleWorks/CutSim), gets arbitrary orientation incl. 5-axis, needs dual-contouring meshing; (C) dense/sparse voxel + surface nets — simplest to reason about, heaviest memory. Must preserve current wins: incremental partial-t carve @60fps, dirty-AABB partial GPU upload, LOD, checkpoint/replay scrub, WASM single-thread + browser memory budget.

Deep design writeup attached separately (agent research 2026-07-10). Migration note: the current heightmap IS a degenerate 1-span dexel, so (A) is an incremental, back-compatible evolution. Prerequisite for a CLEAN ivac-rt1.11 dual-surface sim and for P5 (4/5-axis verification).
design:
# P3 — Material-model evolution: the voxel/dexel question

*Design analysis for `ivac-58nl.6`. Grounds the decision the `ivac-rt1.11.1`
dual-surface spike defers to. Author: research pass 2026-07-10.*

## 0. Framing — what actually forces this

The single `Z(x,y)` heightmap (`sim/heightmap.rs:19-32`, one `f32` per column,
monotone-min) is **optimal for pure 3-axis top-down machining** — which is most
of ivaCAM today. Do **not** replace it to chase generality we don't need. The
upgrade is justified by exactly four concrete capabilities it *structurally*
cannot deliver, each already visible in the codebase or tracker:

| Capability | Why the single heightmap fails | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| T-slot / dovetail **undercut** neck | one Z per column; the overhanging lip has material *above* a void | `heightmap.rs` already downgrades T-slot to "carve the widest disk"; `from_tool_tslot_as_form_profile_carves_head_radius` |
| **Two-sided / flip** parts | field is "only ever lowered from top_z" → single-sided; a from-below carve has nowhere to live | `ivac-rt1.11` scope note; `ivac-rt1.11.1` gate |
| Ball-nose **steep-wall side cut** honesty | wall material removed by the flank isn't a top-down projection | implicit in 2.5D limit |
| Future **4/5-axis / lathe** removal | tool axis not vertical → removed volume isn't a `Z(x,y)` graph | `P5`, `GrblGru` kinematic lead |

Key reframing that makes this tractable: **the current heightmap is a degenerate
1-span Z-dexel.** Every migration below is a superset of today, so the 3-axis
hot path can stay byte-for-byte identical.

## 1. The representation spectrum

Memory is the deciding axis. For a surface-oriented process, **dexel memory
scales with surface area (~N²); dense-voxel memory scales with volume (~N³).**
That single fact is why every production CNC verifier (ModuleWorks CutSim,
hbmoco, Vericut's core) uses multi/tri-dexel, not dense voxels. Worked numbers
for a representative ivaCAM job — 200×200 mm stock, 0.2 mm cell (auto =
`tool_dia/15`), i.e. 1000×1000 columns:

| Model | Structure | Carve op | Mesh | Mem @ example | Unlocks | WASM fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Today: 1-span Z-map** | `Vec<f32>` `cols*rows` | `min()` per cell | stepped heightfield | **4 MB** | 3-axis top-down | ✅ zero-copy flat array |
| **A. Multi-span Z-dexel** | per column: sorted `[z_lo,z_hi]` spans | 1-D interval subtract | extended stepped mesh (iterate spans) | ~6–12 MB (1.5–3× top-down; only undercut cols pay) | + undercuts, + **flip**, honest T-slot | ✅ with CSR layout / hybrid sidecar |
| **B. Tri-dexel** | 3 orthogonal dexel grids | ray vs swept-vol, ×3 dirs | **dual contouring** of Hermite data | ~40–60 MB | + arbitrary orientation, **5-axis** | ⚠ heavier; remesh dirty bricks |
| **C. Dense voxel** | `N³` occupancy/SDF | per-voxel CSG | MC / surface nets | **≥125 MB–1 GB** | (same as B) | ❌ infeasible at fine cell |
| **C′. Sparse voxel (VDB/octree)** | narrow-band bricks | brick CSG | MC / DC | ~surface-proportional | (same as B) | ⚠ pointer-chasing, alloc churn — WASM-hostile |

Dense voxel (C) is out on arithmetic alone: 1000³ = 1e9 voxels; even 1 bit each
is 125 MB and you must mesh the whole volume. Sparse voxel (C′) recovers the
memory but trades it for allocation/pointer patterns that fight WASM's
single-thread, single-linear-heap model and buy nothing over tri-dexel for a
surface process. **The real choice is A vs B, and the answer is "A now, B only
if 4/5-axis lands."**

## 2. Option A — multi-span Z-dexel (the recommendation)

### 2.1 Why it's the right first step
- **Strict superset / back-compatible.** 1 span == today. The existing
  `sweep.rs` per-cell `min()` becomes "subtract an interval from the top span,"
  which for a top-down cut *is* the current behavior.
- **Unblocks flip machining cheaply.** A two-sided part needs **exactly two
  spans** per column (top carve descends from `top_z`; back carve ascends from
  `top_z - thickness`). This is ONE field → ONE watertight solid, which directly
  dissolves the `rt1.11.1` "two floating sheets vs one solid" risk *without*
  going to full voxels. `export_stl` already drops walls to `stock_bottom_z`
  (`driver.ts:73`), so the watertight precedent exists.
- **Preserves every current win** (§4).

### 2.2 The tool generalization that makes carving fall out
Today `ToolProfile::eval(r) -> Option<f32>` returns the **lower** cutter surface
(dz above tip) at radius `r`. Generalize to a **removed interval per radius**:

```
eval_interval(r) -> Option<(lo_dz, hi_dz)>   // material removed between tip+lo and tip+hi
```

- Endmill/ball/V/bull: `lo = current eval(r)`, `hi = flute_length` (or +∞ up to
  stock top) → a solid column, identical result to today for the top span.
- **T-slot / dovetail**: the `FormProfile` already stores `(z_above_tip, r)`
  samples — it just gains a second surface, so the disk removes
  `(disk_bottom(r), disk_top(r))` at `r ∈ [neck_r, disk_r]` and **nothing** at
  `r < neck_r` above the neck → the overhang is preserved. Undercut, honestly.

Carving one segment becomes: for each swept cell, compute `(lo,hi)` at that
cell's `r` and `cutter_pz`, then **interval-subtract** `[pz+lo, pz+hi]` from the
column's span list (merge adjacent). Interval subtraction is associative, so the
`partial_advance` bitwise-identity property (`owns_t_lo/hi`, `sweep.rs:1305`)
carries over — arguably cleaner than the `min()` case.

### 2.3 Storage layout for zero-copy — the hybrid sidecar
The current WASM contract is a flat `f32` array viewed directly by JS
(`data_ptr()/data_len()`, re-viewed each advance because the heap may grow —
`sim.rs:415`). Variable-length spans break a naive flat view. Two options:

1. **CSR / ragged** — `col_offsets: Vec<u32>` (len `cols*rows+1`) + flat
   `spans: Vec<f32>`; expose both pointers, JS slices per column. General but
   every column pays an indirection.
2. **Hybrid (recommended)** — keep the **dense top-surface `Vec<f32>` exactly as
   today** (unchanged hot path, unchanged zero-copy, unchanged LOD min-pool) and
   add a **sparse `HashMap<cell, SmallVec<[Span;2]>>` sidecar** for the <1% of
   columns that actually have undercuts. 3-axis jobs allocate *zero* sidecar and
   run at today's speed/footprint; only T-slot/flip columns cost more. This is
   the single most important design idea here: **pay for generality only where
   geometry uses it.**

### 2.4 Meshing
Extend the stepped heightfield mesh (`heightfield_mesh.ts`): per column, emit the
top of each span and the bottom of each span, plus undercut side-walls where a
span boundary is exposed relative to neighbors. Dirty-AABB partial upload
survives (a column's span count changing just re-emits that column's quads).
Flat-shaded axis-aligned normals still hold for the common case; undercut walls
get their own normals. No marching cubes needed for A.

## 3. Option B — tri-dexel (defer, gate on 4/5-axis)

The literature is unanimous that **tri-dexel is the correct model for multi-axis
material removal** (raycast the swept volume analytically against three
orthogonal ray sets; extract the surface with marching cubes or, better,
**dual contouring of Hermite data** to preserve tool-mark sharp edges MC rounds
off — see the 2024 "Enhanced Dual Contouring for CNC" work). But for ivaCAM it's
a much bigger lift than A:
- 3× the field; general ray/swept-volume intersection for a tilted tool of
  revolution (the analytic-raycasting papers) rather than the closed-form
  vertical-ray case A enjoys;
- meshing must move to dual contouring / surface nets over a Hermite grid, which
  **abandons the cheap axis-aligned incremental upload** — you remesh dirty
  *bricks*, a real re-architecture of `heightfield_mesh.ts`;
- the checkpoint/replay and zero-copy stories both get more complex.

Nothing in the current 3-axis + drag-knife roadmap needs it. **Adopt B only when
`P5` (kinematic 4/5-axis) is greenlit**; until then it's cost without payoff.
When that day comes, A is not wasted — a Z-dexel is one of the three stacks.

## 4. Preserving the current wins (hard constraints on any choice)

| Win today | How A keeps it |
|---|---|
| Incremental partial-t carve @60 fps | interval subtract is associative → identical splitting |
| Dirty-AABB partial GPU upload | unchanged; span-count change re-emits that column only |
| LOD mip-pyramid (MIN-pool) | top-span dense array pools exactly as now; undercuts are detail at fine LOD |
| Checkpoint/replay scrub (12 snaps) | snapshot dense array + sidecar; carving still monotone (material only removed) so snapshots remain valid |
| WASM zero-copy read-back | dense array untouched; sidecar is a second, small exposed buffer |
| Collision checks (rapid/holder/fixture) | operate on the top span; undercut spans add cases, not rewrites |

## 5. Recommended phasing (maps to the tracker)

- **Phase 0 — `ivac-rt1.11.1` spike (exists).** Cheap dual-Simulator prototype.
  Its real question is now reframed: *not* "two sheets or one solid" but
  "confirm a 2-span dexel renders as one watertight solid." De-risks Phase 2.
- **Phase 1 — multi-span Z-dexel core.** `ToolProfile::eval_interval`, hybrid
  dense+sidecar field, interval-subtract sweep, extended stepped mesh. Ships
  honest T-slot / dovetail sim. Fully back-compatible; 3-axis unchanged.
- **Phase 2 — dual-surface / flip.** From-below carving as a second span;
  watertight single-solid render. **Unblocks `ivac-rt1.11` without voxels.**
- **Phase 3 — tri-dexel + dual contouring (deferred).** Only if `P5` 4/5-axis
  verification is greenlit. Re-architects meshing; reuses the Z-dexel as one
  stack.

## 6. Bottom line
Do **not** introduce a voxel grid. Introduce a **multi-span Z-dexel** (Option A),
implemented as a hybrid *dense-top-surface + sparse-undercut-sidecar* so the
3-axis common case stays exactly as fast and compact as today. It is a strict,
incremental superset of the current heightmap; it directly unblocks two-sided
machining (`ivac-rt1.11`) and honest T-slot/dovetail sim; and it defers the
genuinely expensive tri-dexel + dual-contouring work until — and only if —
multi-axis kinematics (`P5`) makes it pay.

### Sources
- Multi-dexel material removal + cutting force, GPGPU — ScienceDirect S0965997811002262
- Tri-dexel cutter-workpiece engagement for 5-axis (validation) — ResearchGate 369299997
- Tri-dexel iso-surface / feature-preserving extraction — ResearchGate 382541364
- Surface reconstruction from three orthogonal ray (dexel) sets — ResearchGate 275383285
- Enhanced Dual Contouring for real-time CNC surface reconstruction (2024) — ResearchGate 379691947
- Ju, Losasso, Schaefer, Warren, "Dual Contouring of Hermite Data", SIGGRAPH 2002
acceptance_criteria: A written ADR selecting a representation (A/B/C or hybrid) with a phased migration plan from the current heightmap, meshing strategy, memory/perf budget vs current, and how it preserves incremental carve + scrub.

title: P2a: STL -> SurfaceField rasterizer (unlock STL 3D surfacing)
description:
Rasterize a triangle mesh (STL) into a SurfaceField (Z(x,y) max z-buffer) so the EXISTING drop-cutter surfacing engine (cam/surface_mill.rs) can finish real 3D models, not just grayscale reliefs.

cam/surface.rs:9-12 already declares the seam: 'The surface SOURCE is pluggable ... the first one is a grayscale image ...; a future STL rasterizer feeds the very same type.' This issue implements that future.

NOTE: ivaCAM's drop-cutter is already MORE accurate than GrblGru's here — surface_mill.rs uses proper tip_drop_offset for ball/bull/flat, whereas GrblGru's SmartMesh.GetMaxDepth models a flat-endmill ring only and Tool.GetToolProfile has no ball-nose case.

PLUG-IN: new SurfaceField::from_stl (or from_mesh) alongside from_grayscale in cam/surface.rs; reuse sim/stl.rs mesh loading. Handle triangle -> grid z-max, orientation, and units. Est ~1 wk.
acceptance_criteria: A test STL rasterizes into a SurfaceField whose sampled Z matches the mesh within cell tolerance; ReliefMill/surface_mill produces a gouge-free finishing path over it.
notes:
BUILT the core rasterizer + STL reader (2026-07-13). Acceptance criteria met at the ivac-core level by tests. Delivered:
(1) crates/ivac-core/src/sim/stl.rs — an STL READER (input counterpart to the existing exporters): parse_stl(bytes) with size-based binary-vs-ASCII detection (84+50n binary layout; header may itself start with 'solid', so leading-byte sniffing is avoided), a binary facet parser, and a lenient ASCII parser (collects every 'vertex x y z' triple, ignores normal/loop keywords, tolerant whitespace + scientific notation). Public StlTriangle type + StlError (Truncated/BadAscii via thiserror). 7 tests.
(2) crates/ivac-core/src/cam/surface.rs — SurfaceField::from_mesh(tris, cell): z-max rasterization of triangles into the target Z(x,y) grid (barycentric interpolation over each triangle's covered cell-centers, skip vertical/degenerate tris), sized to the mesh XY bbox, then shifted so the mesh top sits at stock top (0) with relief downward — the same drop-onto-stock-top convention from_grayscale bakes in. Uncovered cells (holes / bbox gaps) stay at SURFACE_TOP_Z (no gouge). Returns None for empty/edge-on meshes. Plus SurfaceField::from_stl(bytes, cell) convenience. 7 tests incl. the acceptance cases: heightmap -> heightmap_to_stl_binary -> parse_stl -> from_mesh reproduces the original top shape within cell tol, and a drop-cutter surface_mill pass over a from_mesh dome is gouge-free (every emitted tip Z >= sampled target).
Gates: 909 ivac-core lib tests (was 895; +14), fmt clean, clippy --all-targets clean, ivac-{core,wasm,cli,server} build.
REMAINING (separate, filed as ivac-qxkf, P2): making from_stl USER-REACHABLE — wiring STL as a selectable ReliefSource. Carved out because it carries a real design fork (an STL source has real geometry Z, so the op's brightness->Z depth mapping degrades to a clamp) + schema/frontend work. Same core-vs-wiring split as 6.5.6/6.5.8.
close_reason: Core STL->SurfaceField rasterizer + STL reader delivered and tested to the issue's acceptance criteria (rasterize-matches-mesh + gouge-free surface_mill). User-reachable relief-source wiring split into ivac-qxkf.

title: P1: Target-surface deviation overlay (gouge / rest-stock red-green verify)
description:
Compare the carved sim Heightmap against the target SurfaceField cell-for-cell and color the terrain: RED = gouge (carved below target), GREEN = stock remaining above target beyond tolerance, neutral = on-target. A verification capability GrblGru structurally cannot offer (it never carves).

WHY LOW-COST: the two grids already share origin/cell/cell-center conventions on purpose — cam/surface.rs:38 says 'matching the simulator heightmap's cell-center convention so the two grids align.' Data already lives in WASM.

PLUG-IN:
- Rust: add Heightmap::deviation_vs(&SurfaceField, tol) -> per-cell class, in sim/heightmap.rs. Expose over the WASM boundary next to advance() in ivac-wasm/src/sim.rs.
- Frontend: per-cell vertex color in frontend/src/lib/sim/heightfield_mesh.ts, driven off the dirty AABB already uploaded each advance.

Turns 'destructive terrain' from an animation into a correctness tool. Est ~1-2 wk.
acceptance_criteria: Terrain view can toggle a deviation colormap; gouges and remaining stock are visible and match a hand-checked case; only dirty-AABB cells re-upload.
close_reason: Implemented end-to-end: Rust core SurfaceField::deviation_of (hand-checked classification), cached WASM Simulator target (set_deviation_target/deviation), per-cell red/green terrain colormap in HeightfieldMesh + LOD worst-wins pooling, relief->SurfaceField target builder, driver wiring (dirty-AABB re-upload), and a Settings > Preview toggle + tolerance (en/de). All automated gates green: cargo test (core 916 + wasm), clippy, fmt, mesh+target vitest, full frontend vitest (866), svelte-check, eslint, i18n coverage, wasm-pack (debug+release), frontend build. Hands-on visual verification + placement validation + multi-relief + per-frame perf tracked in ivac-58nl.1.1.

title: GrblGru comparison: 3D CAM + simulation material-model roadmap
description:
Follow-ups from an in-depth GrblGru V6.38.0 (decompiled) vs ivaCAM comparison of toolpath generation + material-removal simulation.

KEY FINDING (corrects ~/grblgru/GRBLGRU_ASSESS_01.md): GrblGru has NO volumetric/voxel material-removal sim. DoJob3DRoughingSimple/DoJob3DFinishing are empty stubs; zero usage of geometry3Sharp MarchingCubes/DenseGrid/ImplicitDifference in the decompiled C#. Its 'simulation' is a kinematic replay drawing a tool-tip polyline trail; the stock mesh is never carved. ivaCAM's destructive terrain (sim/heightmap.rs) is therefore STRICTLY AHEAD on material-removal verification.

GrblGru genuinely leads on exactly three things:
1. 3D toolpaths from real STL meshes (waterline Z-level roughing + drop-cutter finishing). ivaCAM's only 3D path reads a grayscale image (cam/surface.rs from_grayscale; STL is TODO).
2. Kinematic machine simulation (4/5-axis, lathe, foam, robot IK) + a 139-config machine library (.tco + Machine.dat).
3. Breadth of machine classes as first-class targets.

Where ivaCAM already beats GrblGru: real material removal, ball/bull-nose contact accuracy (GrblGru's drop-cutter models a flat-endmill ring only; Tool.GetToolProfile has no ball-nose case), scallop-driven stepover, collision checks vs carved stock, trochoidal roughing, portability.

Children P1-P5 chase the real gaps. Flip/two-sided machining is already tracked at ivac-rt1.11; the material-model work here (P3) is the 'much bigger feature' that ivac-rt1.11.1's decision gate foreshadows.

title: i18n: localize sim/pipeline warnings (warn.<kind> templates + params)
description:
Split from ivac-os2k.6 (error half shipped in commit 24a7e8a). Localize the GUI-surfaced PipelineWarning text.

## Seam (designed, not yet landed)
- Add params: BTreeMap<String,String> to PipelineWarning (crates/ivac-core/src/pipeline.rs) + a new()/for_op()/with_param() builder; backfill the ~35 construction sites across pipeline/{warnings,selection,tabs,setup_resolver}.rs. NOTE: adding the field breaks all struct-literal sites (Rust requires all fields), so the field + full backfill must land together.
- kind already IS the stable code; frontend renders warn.<kind> against params, falling back to message. Render sites: GenerateBar.svelte (599/616), OperationsList.svelte (179 tooltip), PhoneWarnings.svelte (49/172), ReportDialog.svelte (303), report-markdown.ts (101). Add a pure warning-display.ts helper (mirror error-display.ts) gated on MSG_KEYS membership so unknown kinds fall back to message.
- Schema regen (xtask schema + pnpm codegen); both drift guards.

## Design blockers found while scoping (must solve, not mechanical)
1. Pluralization: messages bake English plurals via a {plural} arg (e.g. 'N cut move{s}'). Our i18n has no plural-rule support; German pluralizes differently. Either add minimal plural support (count-based key variants, e.g. warn.out_of_work_area.one/other) or pass raw {count} and accept simple phrasing. Decide before backfilling.
2. Composed substrings: {where_line} ('at line N' suffix) is built in Rust and embedded — nested composition. Pass the raw line number as a param and compose 'at line {line}' inside the template (own phrasing per language); template needs a no-line variant.
3. Duplicate kinds with different messages: op_order_suspect (warnings.rs 480/518) and op_source_empty (selection.rs 151/209) each appear twice — one warn.<kind> template must cover both via params, or the kind is overloaded. Reconcile.

## Cross-check (recommended)
No test currently ties en.json warn.<kind> placeholders to the Rust params keys. Add a regression test (e.g. extend existing warning unit tests in pipeline/{warnings,selection}.rs) that substitutes a constructed warning's params into the en template and asserts it matches the English message — catches param/template drift across the language boundary.

## Onboarding
Plan: docs/i18n/PLAN.md (backend section). Mirror the error seam landed in ivac-os2k.6 (crates/ivac-core/src/errors.rs + frontend/src/lib/components/error-display.ts).
close_reason: Localization SEAM + infra + first batch shipped. PipelineWarning gained a params BTreeMap + new/for_op/with_param builder (mirrors the Error seam); all 73 construction sites migrated to the builder; schema regen. Frontend warning-display.ts renders warn.<kind> against params with an MSG_KEYS membership fallback to the English message, wired into GenerateBar/OperationsList/PhoneWarnings/ReportDialog (report-markdown left English as an export artifact). 14 clean single-param kinds localized in en+de. Drift guards: a Rust test asserts a site populates op_name, a vitest asserts warn.* templates only use provided params. All gates green: core 916 + frontend 870 tests, clippy, fmt, svelte-check, eslint, i18n coverage/parity/no-dead-keys, schema+codegen drift. Field was 73 sites/~66 kinds (2x the ~35 estimate); the remaining ~52 kinds (incl. the hard tail: tool_kind_mismatch reason-switch, plurals, Debug-slices, composed where_line/neck) are tracked in ivac-os2k.13 — they fall back to their English message until then.

title: i18n coverage tests + CI/pre-release gates
description:
Make translation coverage enforceable.

## Concrete workload
Frontend vitest (co-located under src/lib/i18n/):
1. locale parity: keys(de) === keys(en); list missing/extra.
2. no empty/untranslated: no "" values; warn de==en non-proper-nouns.
3. placeholder parity: {…} tokens match en for each locale.
4. no dead keys: every MsgKey referenced in src/.
5. hardcoded-string guard: scan .svelte markup for un-wrapped user-facing
   literals + allowlist (this is the "find everything" net; sweep C uses it).
Rust cargo test:
6. CLI catalog parity (de keys == en keys).
7. project-file locale-invariance: load tests/fixtures/*.vc-project.json under
   both locales, round-trip, assert byte-identical.
CI: add i18n codegen drift guard + the above to .github/workflows/ci.yml and
scripts/pre-release.sh, beside schema-check / codegen-drift.

## Onboarding
- Plan: docs/i18n/PLAN.md (coverage section). Mirror existing vitest + ci gates.
acceptance_criteria: vitest: locale parity, no-empty, placeholder parity, no-dead-keys, hardcoded-string guard. cargo test: CLI catalog parity + project-file locale-invariance round-trip. All wired into ci.yml and scripts/pre-release.sh.

title: Sweep for drifted desktop/phone handler pairs (duplicate-logic bug class)
description:
Two platform-specific bugs this session both traced to the SAME root cause: a piece of logic implemented twice (once for desktop, once for phone/touch) where the copies drifted, so one platform worked and the other didn't.

KNOWN INSTANCES (already fixed):
- stock_origin_outside_geometry_bbox Apply-Fix: GenerateBar.applyWcsBboxSnapFix (web, keyed off transformedImport -> null for text-only -> button disabled + early-return -> no-op) vs PhoneWarnings.fixWcsOrigin (used computeFootprint(stockSizingImport) + regenerate -> worked). Fixed by extracting project.snapWorkOffsetToFootprint() (commit 5868f65).
- Canvas context-menu op creation: EntityCanvas2D vs Scene3D pickFromCtx, deduped into state/op_creation.ts createOpFromSelection (commit 1b5493e).

SWEEP TARGETS — audit these desktop/phone (or 2D/3D) component pairs for logic that should be one shared helper in state/ rather than two inline copies:
- GenerateBar.svelte (desktop) vs PhoneWarnings.svelte (phone): warning aggregation (simWarnings/pipeWarnings/critical/total), stale detection (simDiagnostics + data.dirty), the status-chip state machine (chipClass/chipLabel/chipGlyph vs cls/glyph/text/title), canGenerate + generateBus.request triggering, and warning copy-to-clipboard (copyWarnings/warningsText). High likelihood of drift.
- EntityCanvas2D.svelte vs Scene3D.svelte: remaining duplicated context-menu lifecycle (open/close/clamp/keyboard) and selection->op flows (see ivac-xydr notes — intentionally deferred there).
- Any other component with an isPhone/touch branch that reimplements a desktop handler instead of sharing one.

APPROACH: for each confirmed pair, extract the shared logic to a testable state/ module or a ProjectState method (the pattern used for snapWorkOffsetToFootprint + createOpFromSelection), then have both call sites delegate. Add a unit test for the extracted helper. Prioritize correctness-affecting logic (fixes, generate triggers, validation) over pure presentation.

Found during pre-release cleanup 2026-06-19; relates to ivac-xydr (canvas dedup) and ivac-bzpt (god-component split).
design:
═══ QUICK-START / ONBOARDING (read first in a new session) ═══

WHAT THIS IS: a cleanup sweep. The frontend renders some features twice —
once for desktop, once for phone/touch (or 2D vs 3D canvas). Several of
those pairs were copy-pasted and then drifted, so a fix landed in one
copy but not the other → "works on Android, broken on web" bugs. Goal:
find the remaining drifted pairs and collapse each to ONE shared helper.

REPO: /home/soenke/wiaconstructor (local-only, no git remote — commit to
main, do not push). Frontend lives in frontend/ (Svelte 5 runes + Vite).
State slices: frontend/src/lib/state/*.svelte.ts. Components:
frontend/src/lib/components/*.svelte. bd is the tracker (bd show ivac-t5dq).

BUILD / VERIFY (run from frontend/):
  pnpm install                 # first time
  pnpm exec svelte-check       # type + unused-CSS/import gate (expect 0/0)
  pnpm test --run              # vitest (~808 tests today)
  pnpm exec prettier --write <files>   # format before commit
Whole-repo pre-tag gate: scripts/pre-release.sh (from repo root).

RUN THE APP to eyeball a fix: from frontend/ run `pnpm dev`. IMPORTANT —
dev defaults to the HTTP transport proxied to a local ivac-server on
:8766, so EITHER also run `cargo run -p ivac-server`, OR open the URL
with ?api=wasm (e.g. http://localhost:5173/?api=wasm) to use the
in-browser engine with no backend. (First dev run may rebuild the wasm
pkg — a few minutes.)

═══ THE PROVEN PATTERN (copy these two commits) ═══

1. ivac-core-free shared logic → a ProjectState method or a state/*.ts
   function. Example: commit 5868f65 added
   ProjectState.snapWorkOffsetToFootprint() in
   frontend/src/lib/state/project.svelte.ts and made BOTH
   GenerateBar.applyWcsBboxSnapFix (desktop) and
   PhoneWarnings.fixWcsOrigin (phone) delegate to it, then
   generateBus.request().
2. Pure logic with no project-state deps → a plain state/*.ts function +
   unit test. Example: commit 1b5493e (state/op_creation.ts
   createOpFromSelection, shared by EntityCanvas2D + Scene3D pickFromCtx).
Always: delete the now-unused imports, run svelte-check (it flags unused
imports/CSS), add/extend a vitest for the extracted helper, prettier,
commit one pair per commit.

═══ STEP-BY-STEP FOR EACH CANDIDATE ═══
  a. Open both copies side by side; diff the logic. Decide the CANONICAL
     behavior (usually the one that handles more cases — e.g. the phone
     WCS fix used stockSizingImport, which also covers text-only).
  b. Extract the canonical logic to one helper (pattern above).
  c. Replace both call sites with a delegating call.
  d. Remove dead imports; svelte-check 0/0; add a unit test; prettier.
  e. Commit (msg: `refactor(frontend): dedup <X> across desktop/phone`),
     reference this issue id.

═══ CONCRETE CANDIDATES (audit in priority order) ═══
P1 — GenerateBar.svelte (desktop) vs PhoneWarnings.svelte (phone), the
     two warning bars. Both reimplement, likely drifted:
       • warning aggregation: simWarnings / pipeWarnings / criticalCount /
         totalWarningCount (GenerateBar ~L180-216) vs critical / total
         (PhoneWarnings ~L24-38).
       • stale detection: simDiagnostics != null && data.dirty
         (GenerateBar simStale L379 vs PhoneWarnings stale L33).
       • status-chip state machine: chipClass/chipLabel/chipGlyph
         (GenerateBar L373-405) vs cls/glyph/text/title (PhoneWarnings
         L72-105) — SAME severity→label/color logic, two copies.
       • generate gating + trigger: canGenerate + generateBus.request
         (PhoneWarnings L70/110; GenerateBar run()/L306).
       • copy-warnings-to-clipboard: PhoneWarnings copyWarnings/
         warningsText L41-47 — check if GenerateBar has a twin.
     SUGGESTED HELPER: a state/warnings-summary.ts (pure) exposing
     {sim, pipeline, critical, total, stale, severity, chipState} from
     project.gen + project.data.dirty, unit-tested; both bars render it.
P2 — EntityCanvas2D.svelte vs Scene3D.svelte: remaining context-menu
     lifecycle (open/close/viewport-clamp/keyboard) — see ivac-xydr
     notes; pickFromCtx already done. Drag-snap was intentionally left.
P3 — grep for other isPhone/touch branches that reimplement a desktop
     handler:  grep -rnE "isPhone|pointer: coarse|touch" frontend/src/lib/components
     and check each for a desktop twin.

DONE-WHEN: each confirmed pair has one shared, unit-tested helper; no
behavioral divergence remains; svelte-check 0/0 and full vitest green.
notes:
P3 AUDIT COMPLETE (2026-06-19) — no remaining drifted desktop/phone handler pairs found.

Method: grepped components for narrow/touch LOGIC branches (layout.isNarrow / isPhone / isTouchDevice / pointerType==='touch'), excluding pure @media(pointer:coarse) CSS and phone-only widgets, then checked each for a duplicated desktop twin.

Findings — all clean:
- PhoneWarnings is the ONLY Phone* component, and it's already collapsed against GenerateBar via state/warnings-summary.ts (P1, commit 1a3c1a3).
- FloatingPanel is a SINGLE shared component used by BOTH GenerateBar and PhoneWarnings panels (already the shared abstraction, not a pair).
- SettingsDialog adapts responsively as one component (class:narrow / embedded) — no twin.
- EntityCanvas2D's touch branches (stock gizmo narrow-only, TEXT_TOUCH_TOL vs HIT_PIXEL_TOL, touch overlay buttons) are that component's own adaptations; the only 2D/3D pairing is the EntityCanvas2D/Scene3D context-menu, already assessed under P2 as genuine 2D-vs-3D divergence (not copy-paste drift; deferred to ivac-xydr).
- Touch detection is NOT duplicated: layout.isNarrow is a single source (tested isNarrowTier in state/layout.ts); isTouchDevice (maxTouchPoints) is defined once, used only in EntityCanvas2D.

CONCLUSION: P1 done (warnings dedup, unit-tested helper). P2 = genuine divergence, deferred to ivac-xydr. P3 = no actionable drift. Sweep done.
close_reason: Sweep complete: P1 warnings dedup landed (warnings-summary.ts, commit 1a3c1a3); P3 audit found no other drifted desktop/phone pairs (the only Phone* component is already collapsed, FloatingPanel/SettingsDialog are single responsive components, touch detection is single-sourced); P2 canvas context-menu is genuine 2D/3D divergence tracked under ivac-xydr.

description: README.md:48 states 'viaConstructor and Estlcam inspired the scope and feature set — no code from either is used.' But core module headers describe themselves as ports: cam.rs:1 ('port of viaConstructor's calc.py'), gcode.rs:1 ('port of viaConstructor's machine_cmd.py'), math.rs:4 ('helpers from viaConstructor's calc.py'). 'Port of' implies derived work; viaConstructor is GPL. For a public GPL-3 release this wording must be reconciled to accurately reflect provenance (either soften README to acknowledge derivation, or adjust comments if they overstate it). Needs the maintainer's call on actual provenance. Surfaced during pre-release slop/staleness sweep 2026-06-19; all mechanical gates (fmt/clippy/tests/svelte-check) were green.
design:
PROVENANCE (verified 2026-06-19): viaConstructor (GPL, open) is genuinely derived — port headers in cam.rs:1, math.rs:4, cam/chaining.rs:1, cam/offsets/mod.rs:5, cam/setup.rs:1, gcode.rs:1 (calc.py / machine_cmd.py / setupdefaults.py). Estlcam (closed-source) is behavioral/terminology inspiration only; no code. So README:48 'no code from either is used' is TRUE for Estlcam, FALSE for viaConstructor.

PROPOSED README:48 REPLACEMENT:
"ivaCAM's CAM core is in part a Rust port of [viaConstructor](https://github.com/multigcs/viaconstructor)'s geometry and toolpath routines (calc.py, machine_cmd.py, setupdefaults.py), and is distributed under the GPL accordingly. [Estlcam](https://www.estlcam.de/) inspired parts of the feature set and terminology, but is closed-source and contributes no code."

OPTIONAL README:42 ADDITION:
"ivaCAM inherits this licence from its partial derivation of viaConstructor."

OPEN BLOCKER (not a wording fix): verify viaConstructor's exact GPL version. ivaCAM is GPL-3.0-or-later; compatible only if viaConstructor is GPL-2.0-or-later or GPL-3.0. If viaConstructor is GPL-2.0-only, GPL-3 redistribution is a license violation — must resolve before public release.
close_reason: README wording applied (commit) — viaConstructor credited as partial port, Estlcam separated as code-free inspiration. Verified viaConstructor is GPLv3 (refs/viaconstructor/LICENSE), compatible with ivaCAM's GPL-3.0-or-later: no licensing blocker.

title: Touch: overlapping objects unselectable under stock handle/midpoint; cycle-tap or flyout
description: On touch, when a stock resize handle/midpoint (or another object) sits on top of a small object (e.g. midpoint centered on a small circle), the underlying object can't be selected — the tap hits the handle/top object. Proposed: tap-cycling — repeated taps in the same small region cycle through stacked objects (tap 1 selects topmost, tap 2 deselects it and selects the next under it, …). Alternative: a flyout disambiguation menu listing the objects under the tap. If too complex, document the zoom-in workaround (zoom until objects are individually selectable). Desktop is unaffected (precise cursor).
notes:
FULLY ADDRESSED — both stacking cases fixed:
1. Object-on-object (commit 510861b): tap-cycling via pure queryHitObjects + cycledHitObjectId; repeat plain taps step through stacked objects nearest-first, wrapping. 5 unit tests.
2. Stock-handle/midpoint OVER an object (commit 95522c3): the handle grab is now deferred (tap-vs-drag). A press over a handle parks in pendingStockGrab; it promotes to a resize drag only once the finger leaves the tap tolerance, and a stationary tap-and-release falls through to object selection (commitEntityTapSelection, which also drives the cycling). So the object under the handle is selectable, and stacked objects under it cycle. Tap over empty stock stays a no-op (no selection clear). Second-finger pinch clears the parked grab.

Both: svelte-check 0/0, full frontend suite green (819). Caveat: touch interaction — on-device verification still advisable (logic verified by reasoning + unit tests; the rune/pointer glue isn't mountable in vitest).
close_reason: Both overlap cases fixed: object-on-object via tap-cycling (510861b), stock-handle-over-object via deferred tap-vs-drag grab that falls through to selection (95522c3). svelte-check 0/0, frontend suite green (819). On-device verification advisable for the touch feel.

title: Android: native lib not 16 KB page-size aligned (libivac_tauri_lib.so LOAD segment mismatch)
description: On the Pixel (Android 17), installing the debug APK shows an Android compatibility warning: 'This app is not 16 KB compatible. ELF alignment check failed. lib/arm64-v8a/libivac_tauri_lib.so: LOAD segment mismatch.' The app still runs (warning is dismissable on this device's compat mode), but Android 15+ devices with 16 KB memory pages require native .so libraries aligned to 16 KB or they won't load. Need to build with 16 KB ELF alignment (NDK r27+ defaults / -Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384, AGP/Tauri config). See https://developer.android.com/16kb-page-size. Surfaced while fixing wiaconstructor-0gu0.
close_reason: Added -Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384 for all Android targets in .cargo/config.toml. Verified with llvm-readelf: all LOAD segments in libivac_tauri_lib.so are now 0x4000 (16 KB) aligned. Staged in APK 20:18.

title: [H5-followup] Adopt cam::spatial in trochoidal disc-guard + apply_overcut reflex-corner scans
description:
The H5 fix (wiaconstructor-ryan.5) added a reusable cam::spatial module (SegmentNearestGrid for nearest-segment-distance, RegionInsideIndex/PolygonRayIndex for point-in-region). The H5 onboarding noted two sibling geometry findings with the same all-pairs boundary-scan pattern that this module would also resolve:
- trochoidal disc-guard re-scan: crates/ivac-core/src/cam/trochoidal.rs (~line 200)
- apply_overcut per-reflex-corner boundary scan: crates/ivac-core/src/cam/offsets/parallel.rs (~line 765)
Adopt SegmentNearestGrid (or a suitable spatial query) there. Keep output identical (accelerator only) and add equivalence tests as in H5. Verify against cam tests + volume_validation.
notes: Progress 2026-06-16 (session 2): DONE — L2 trochoidal disc-guard (commit 2508f09). Added cam::spatial::PolygonRayIndexEps, a row-bucketed index reproducing geometry::point_in_polygon (the boundary-robust epsilon variant the disc guard uses — the epsilon-matching variant the earlier investigation noted was missing). Safe-by-construction: query re-applies the exact per-edge crossing formula, edges filed under a y-slop-widened superset of scanline rows so none active is dropped; bit-identical output. Wall+island indexes built once per pocket pass, queried from disc_inside_indexed instead of re-scanning rings per centerline vertex. Equivalence tests: dense + exact-vertex-y sweep vs point_in_polygon; disc_indexed_matches_raw vs verbatim pre-index logic. REMAINING — L3 apply_overcut reflex-corner scan (parallel.rs:765): confirmed NOT a point-in-polygon or nearest-segment query — it casts an outward ray from each sharp-reflex corner and needs the nearest ray-vs-segment hit (min 'along'). Needs a NEW DDA grid-ray-traversal query, and reproducing the exact nearest value is fiddly: must match BOTH the endpoint-hit path (with perp_tol slack, so hits can come from segments whose body is far from the ray) AND the mid-edge Cramer path, with distance-monotonic early termination. Narrower benefit (only sharp right-turn corners, a minority of vertices) + higher correctness risk than L2 — left for a focused session.
close_reason: L3 done (commit bc2725f): SegmentRayGrid accelerates apply_overcut's reflex-corner ray probe; bit-identical (superset + identical arithmetic), 60×300 random exact-equality test. L2 was 2508f09. Both findings of this issue complete.

title: [M7] 2D pan drag repaints full wireframe per pointermove — no rAF coalescing
description:
## Problem
2D pan drag repaints the entire imported wireframe per `pointermove`, with no requestAnimationFrame coalescing.

`frontend/src/lib/components/EntityCanvas2D.svelte:624` (panDrag branch mutates `userPanX/Y`) → effects at `:168` and `:194` both depend on `userPanX/Y` → `drawBackground()` (`:1503 drawImportedWireframe`) re-strokes all segments on the bg canvas (O(N) ctx ops) + a full overlay repaint. Svelte batches effects, but the redraw itself isn't rAF-coalesced and the bg can't be cheaply scrolled.

Wheel-zoom (`onWheel:759`) has the same full-repaint profile but is naturally lower-frequency.

## Complexity
O(N) ctx stroke ops per pointermove. Panning a 50k-segment DXF on a low-end iGPU stutters because each frame restrokes 50k line segments.

## Fix
- Coalesce `drawBackground` into one `requestAnimationFrame` (drop intermediate frames under load — schedule a redraw, don't redraw synchronously per pointermove).
- Or translate the existing bg bitmap by the pan delta and only re-stroke the newly-exposed margin (dirty-region / blit redraw).

Expected: pan frame cost bounded to one redraw per frame; smoother on big files.

## Onboarding
- Files: `frontend/src/lib/components/EntityCanvas2D.svelte`. The component already splits bg/overlay canvases — leverage that.
- rAF coalescing pattern: keep a `redrawScheduled` flag; on pan, set the new transform + `requestAnimationFrame(() => { redrawScheduled=false; drawBackground() })` guarded so only one is queued.
- Build/test: `cd frontend && pnpm exec svelte-check && pnpm test --run`; verify with `pnpm dev` by panning a large DXF.
- Don't break the coordinate mapping — pan/zoom math must stay exact (hit-testing depends on it).
close_reason: The two EntityCanvas2D reactive draw effects now schedule via an rAF-coalesced scheduler (scheduleBackground/scheduleOverlay → one bg + one overlay paint per frame, intermediate frames dropped) instead of synchronous drawBackground/drawOverlay per pointermove. Effects still void all deps synchronously so reactivity is unchanged; pending frame cancelled on destroy; one-shot triggers (resize/theme/mount/fitView) keep direct draws. svelte-check 0 errors, 749 vitest green, eslint/prettier clean. NOTE: manual pan-a-large-DXF verification recommended (couldn't run browser headlessly).

title: [M6] timing.rs strip_comment per-line String alloc + double line scan
description:
## Problem
Two related per-line/per-pass allocation issues in the gcode time-estimate path (`crates/ivac-core/src/sim/timing.rs`):

1. **Per-line String alloc** — `timing.rs:647 strip_comment` builds a fresh `String` for **every** gcode line; called from `feeds_per_segment` (`:589`) and `sum_g4_dwell_seconds` (`:159`). For L lines that's L heap allocations per estimate.
2. **Double scan** — `feeds_per_segment` (`:585`) does `gcode.lines().count()` (full scan) then re-iterates `:588` to fill `feed_by_line` (second full scan).

The estimate runs once per Generate (`pipeline.rs:549`), not per frame — hence MEDIUM, not on the playback hot path.

## Complexity
(1) O(L) allocations + O(L) char copies per estimate. (2) 2× full scan vs 1×. Large gcode (10^5–10^6 lines) → 10^5–10^6 short-lived String allocs per Generate; noticeable on low-end PCs during the post step.

## Fix
1. Make `strip_comment` return comment-stripped slice boundaries (or a `Cow<str>` that borrows when there's no comment), or scan in place without allocating. `scan_modal_f`/`scan_g4` already operate on `&str`.
2. Drop the `count()` pre-pass: `push` into the `Vec` during the single fill loop instead of pre-sizing via `count()`.

Expected: (1) L allocations → ~0; (2) halves the scan work in `feeds_per_segment`.

## Onboarding
- Files: `crates/ivac-core/src/sim/timing.rs` only. Self-contained.
- Build/test: `cargo build --workspace && cargo test --workspace --tests`. Timing has tests — verify estimated times are unchanged (pure speedup).
- `strip_comment` semantics: gcode comments are `;`-to-EOL and `(...)` parenthetical — preserve exact stripping behavior when switching to slices/Cow.
close_reason: strip_comment returns Cow<str> (borrows whole line / prefix-before-; ; allocates only for rare (...) paren lines, semantics preserved). feeds_per_segment dropped the lines().count() pre-pass and pushes into the Vec in a single scan. Pure speedup, estimates unchanged. 21 timing tests green, clippy/fmt clean.

title: [M5] order_offsets greedy-nearest is O(n²) — bites on drill grids
description:
## Problem
`order_offsets` greedy nearest-neighbor is O(n²) over offsets/holes.

`crates/ivac-core/src/gcode/order.rs:63-113` (`greedy_nearest_among`), called from `gcode.rs:850` (`emit_drill_block`) and the contour emit path. Classic greedy NN: for each of n offsets, linear-scan all remaining to find the closest → O(n²) distance computations.

## Complexity
n = offsets/holes. A drill grid with hundreds–thousands of holes, or a dense many-contour job, makes n² noticeable: 2000 holes → 4M distance evals per Generate. Drill grids and dense profile sets routinely hit hundreds–low-thousands of points on low-end PCs.

## Fix
For large n, use a spatial index (k-d tree / uniform grid bucketed by cell) so each "nearest remaining" query is ~O(log n) or O(1) amortized → overall O(n log n). At minimum, gate the existing O(n²) path behind a size threshold (small n is fine — greedy NN on a handful of holes is cheap) and fall back to a grid-accelerated order for large n.

Note: a reusable spatial-grid helper would also serve the V-carve (H5) and offset findings — consider sharing. Existing pattern: `build_endpoint_index` grid in `cam/chaining.rs:147`.

Expected: large drill/contour sets order in a fraction of the time; no change for small n.

## Onboarding
- Output ordering affects gcode but NOT correctness of the cut — however, keep the result deterministic (stable tie-breaking) so regression tests and downstream caching stay stable. The grid path should produce a sensible travel order; it need not be identical to greedy NN, but pick a deterministic rule.
- Files: `crates/ivac-core/src/gcode/order.rs`, callers in `gcode.rs`.
- Build/test: `cargo build --workspace && cargo test --workspace --tests`. Add a test that the large-n path returns a valid permutation of all inputs (no dropped/duplicated holes) and is deterministic.
- Verify travel order is reasonable on a real drill-grid project (no wild cross-table jumps).
close_reason: greedy_nearest_among: for n>128, grid-accelerated nearest-neighbor (uniform bucket grid over start points, expanding-ring search, picked points removed from cells) → ~O(n) amortized vs O(n²). Byte-identical to the linear scan: shared offset_better comparator + ring-stop margin ≥ the 1e-12 tie tolerance reproduce the exact winner (distance→level→finish→lowest-index). Small n keeps the plain scan (tests/fixtures untouched). Randomized grid-vs-linear equivalence test (30 large inputs, coincident points + mixed level/finish), valid-permutation, determinism. 833 ivac-core tests green, clippy/fmt clean.

title: [M4] apply_cached_op re-splits body String into Vec per cache hit
description:
## Problem
On every cache **hit**, `apply_cached_op` (`crates/ivac-core/src/pipeline.rs:1050-1055`) re-splits the stored body `String` back into a `Vec<String>`:

```rust
.lines().map(to_string).collect()   // then out_extend_lines pushes them
```

So every cache hit re-allocates one `String` per line of the op body. Additionally `PipelineCache::get` already `.cloned()` the entire `OpCacheValue` (including the unused `toolpath` Vec — see H3) under the mutex.

## Complexity
Per hit: O(lines_in_op) String allocations, on what is supposed to be the *fast* path. The cache hit re-parses and re-allocates the body it just had as a contiguous String, plus clones a large unused toolpath vector.

## Fix
- Store the body as `Vec<String>` (or `Arc<[String]>`) in `OpCacheValue` so `out_extend_lines` can `extend_from_slice` directly with no re-split.
- Drop the `toolpath` clone (coordinate with H3, which removes that field).
- If the joined `String` is genuinely needed elsewhere, keep both representations but don't round-trip on the hot path.

Expected: cache-hit cost from O(lines) allocs → ~O(1) + a slice copy.

## Onboarding
- Same file/region as H3 and H4 — ideally sequence these three together (all touch `pipeline_cache.rs` / `OpCacheValue`). H3 removes the dead `toolpath` field; this issue changes `gcode_body` representation; H4 fixes the key. Do H3 first.
- Build/test: `cargo build --workspace && cargo test --workspace --tests`; run `crates/ivac-core/src/pipeline/tests.rs`.
- Verify: Generate twice (warm the cache), confirm second Generate produces identical gcode and is faster. The whole point is the cache-hit path — measure it.
close_reason: OpCacheValue.gcode_body (String) -> gcode_lines (Vec<String>). store_op_cache hands the post line vec in directly (no join); apply_cached_op replays via out_extend_lines(&cached.gcode_lines) — no per-line re-split/alloc on cache hits. Joined String had no other reader. 831 ivac-core tests green, clippy/fmt clean, workspace builds.

title: [M3] Hoist fit_line_runs out of per-pass loop in multi-pass emit
description:
## Problem
`fit_line_runs` (arc fitting) is re-run on every Z pass of a multi-pass cut, though its input is identical across passes.

`crates/ivac-core/src/gcode/emit.rs:567,622,667,712` call `walk.rs:85 fit_line_runs(segments, setup)` *inside* the per-pass `for (pass_idx, &z) in z_schedule` loop. The `segments` are the same across all passes (only Z changes), but the arc-fit (`fit_arc_run`, point accumulation, segment cloning) reruns from scratch each pass.

## Complexity
P = pass count (deep pockets / small step-down → 20–80 passes), N = segments per contour. Cost O(P·N) where O(N) (computed once) would do. Multiplies arc-fit work by pass count on every contour of every Generate (not cache-shortcut on a miss).

## Fix
Compute `let fitted = fit_line_runs(segments, setup);` **once before** the pass loop and reuse across passes. The ramp/helix branches that pass `pass_segments` need the reversed fit — precompute at most two Vecs (forward + reversed for `!closed_path`), not P.

Expected: arc-fit cost ÷P on multi-pass cuts.

## Onboarding
- Files: `crates/ivac-core/src/gcode/emit.rs`, `crates/ivac-core/src/gcode/walk.rs`. Localized, low-risk change.
- Watch the reversed-path case: when `!closed_path`, some branches consume reversed segments — reverse the *fitted* result once rather than re-fitting reversed input each pass.
- Build/test: `cargo build --workspace && cargo test --workspace --tests`. Emit has good test coverage. Verify gcode output is byte-identical before/after on a multi-pass pocket project (this must be a pure speedup, zero output change).
- Run `scripts/pre-release.sh` before done.
close_reason: fit_line_runs hoisted out of emit_multipass's per-pass loop. Precompute fitted_forward once + fitted_reversed once (from reverse_chain(segments), open paths only); fitted_for(reversed) helper selects per pass + for ramp cleanup. Byte-identical output (reversed fit computed exactly as per-pass code did). Arc-fit cost O(P*N)->O(N). 831 ivac-core tests incl. volume_validation multi-pass gcode checks green; clippy/fmt clean.

title: [M2] Debounce/matrix-preview file-transform — re-transforms all segments per keystroke
description:
## Problem
`transformedImport` (`$derived`, `frontend/src/lib/state/project.svelte.ts:251`) re-transforms every segment on any file-transform change, and consumers then fully rebuild.

Chain: `transformedImport` → `combineImports` (`file-transform.ts:194`) → `applyFileTransform` (`file-transform.ts:30`, `imp.segments.map(transformSegment)` + `recomputeObjectMetaBbox`). Each recompute allocates a brand-new segments array (O(N) object allocations) and recomputes all per-object bboxes (O(N)).

When it changes, downstream:
- the two 2D draw `$effect`s (`EntityCanvas2D.svelte:168`/`:194`) repaint all segments, AND
- Scene3D's `importedBuilder.build()` (`Scene3D.svelte:495`) rebuilds the **entire** fat-line GPU buffer and re-uploads it.

Triggered by LayerList transform inputs (`LayerList.svelte:296-377`: X/Y/rotate/scale). A spinbox hold or drag fires this per event with no debounce on the transform itself → re-transform 10k–100k segments + full GPU re-upload per event.

## Complexity
O(N) re-transform + O(N) bbox + full GPU re-upload, per transform event.

## Fix
- Debounce/throttle `patchFileTransformForImport` writes (e.g. 16–50ms trailing) so a spinner hold collapses to one recompute on settle.
- And/or apply the transform as a cheap draw-time matrix for live preview: translate/rotate the 2D ctx and the THREE.Group, baking into segments only on commit. The point-drag handlers already use this matrix trick conceptually — extend it to file-transform.

Expected: per-event cost from O(N) re-transform + full GPU re-upload → O(1) during the interaction; one bake on commit.

## Onboarding
- Frontend conventions: `$state` slices under `frontend/src/lib/state/`; pure logic in plain `.ts`. Don't hand-edit `generated.ts`.
- Files: `frontend/src/lib/state/project.svelte.ts`, `frontend/src/lib/file-transform.ts`, `frontend/src/lib/components/{LayerList,EntityCanvas2D,Scene3D}.svelte`.
- Build/test: `cd frontend && pnpm exec svelte-check && pnpm test --run`. Verify with `pnpm dev`: drag a transform spinbox on a large DXF — confirm smooth live preview and that the committed geometry/bboxes are correct (matrix preview must match the baked result exactly).
- Extract the debounce/matrix-preview logic into a testable `.ts` helper.
close_reason: Added tested leading+trailing Throttle helper (state/throttle.ts, 7 unit tests) and routed the four high-frequency LayerList file-transform inputs (X/Y/rotate/scale) through it at ~30 Hz keyed per (import, field). Leading edge = instant first response; trailing edge guarantees final value lands; onDestroy flush applies pending. Mirror checkboxes stay direct (low-frequency). Per-event O(N) re-transform + full GPU re-upload during a spinner hold/drag collapses to ~30/s. svelte-check 0 errors, 756 vitest green, eslint/prettier clean. (Chose the debounce/throttle approach over draw-time matrix preview — simpler, self-contained, exact committed result.) NOTE: manual drag-a-spinbox-on-large-DXF verification recommended.

title: [M1] Cache per-segment sim diagnostics across re-sweep (holder/fixture/rapid)
description:
## Problem
Cache-miss diagnostics (fixture/holder/rapid checks) re-run for every segment on every re-sweep.

`crates/ivac-core/src/sim/sweep.rs:70/:122 run_segment_warnings` is invoked once per `sweep_segment`. Inside it:
- `check_segment_against_fixtures` (`fixture_check.rs:51`, O(F) per segment)
- `check_segment_holder_against_walls` (`holder_check.rs:82`) — walks the holder-radius footprint, a **second** per-cell pass over a footprint typically *larger* than the cutter's (`holder.max_radius()` often ~10mm vs a 3mm cutter)
- `check_rapid_against_stock` for rapids (`rapid_check.rs:66`)

These are deterministic for a fixed heightmap prefix, yet recomputed from scratch on every scrub-back re-sweep (see H2 sibling — full prefix re-sweep).

## Complexity
Combined with the H2 re-sweep, the holder pass alone is O(M · C_holder) per re-sweep, where C_holder (holder radius footprint) is ~10× the carve's cell count. It dominates the re-sweep cost.

## Fix
Cache per-segment diagnostics in `SimDiagnostics` keyed by `segment_idx`; on replay/scrub-back over already-simulated segments, skip recompute. Run the warning pass only on **forward progress past a segment for the first time**. Tie to the H2 heightmap checkpoint so a restored checkpoint also restores its accumulated warnings.

Expected: eliminates the larger-than-carve holder pass entirely on scrub-back.

## Onboarding
- Strongly coupled to H2 (heightmap checkpointing) — ideally do H2 first or together; the checkpoint snapshot should carry the diagnostics state for the same segment range.
- Files: `crates/ivac-core/src/sim/{sweep.rs, fixture_check.rs, holder_check.rs, rapid_check.rs}`. `SimDiagnostics` is the accumulator type — find its definition and add per-segment keying.
- Correctness: a cached diagnostic must be invalidated if the heightmap prefix changes (it won't during pure scrub, but a project edit / re-Generate must clear it).
- Build/test: `cargo build --workspace && cargo test --workspace --tests`. Verify holder/fixture/rapid warnings still appear correctly after scrubbing back and forth.
close_reason: Added SegmentWarningCache + sweep_range_cached (sim/sweep.rs): cache hit replays a segment's stored warnings + carves only (skips holder/fixture/rapid recompute); miss computes via sweep_segment and captures the pushed warnings. Carve always runs → heightfield identical; replay byte-identical to recompute (deterministic checks, monotone sweeps). wasm Simulator owns the cache, uses it in advance(), clears on set_toolpath/clear_toolpath/set_fixtures. With H2 (prefix skipped entirely), scrub-back does ~zero holder recompute. 15 ivac-wasm tests (2 new) + 833 ivac-core green; clippy/fmt clean.

title: AppImage: bundle the GStreamer media framework — appsink warning persists on user machines
description: Follow-up to qn75: the enable-media=false webview setting was not sufficient — tester still sees 'GStreamer element appsink not found' from the AppImage. Root cause analysis: linuxdeploy bundles the BUILD machine's GStreamer core libraries (libgstreamer-1.0, libgstapp-1.0, …) as webkit transitive deps; at runtime they shadow the user's system copies via LD_LIBRARY_PATH, and the user's system plugins (absent, or built against a different core version) fail WebKit's appsink probe. Unreproducible on the build machine (its plugins match its own libs — hidden-plugin xvfb repro stayed silent even pre-fix). Fix: tauri bundle.linux.appimage.bundleMediaFramework=true ships the matching plugin set inside the AppImage so the probe always succeeds and nothing depends on the user's system GStreamer; keep enable-media=false so the stack stays dormant.

title: Tool↔machine-mode compatibility: filter, validate, never delete (plasma_torch kind, mode-switch notice, generate backstop)
description:
Today the tool library is mode-blind: a mill library survives switching machine.mode to plasma, ops keep referencing endmills, and the program generates — plasma pierce/cut-height fields are gated on machine mode and attach to ANY selected tool because no plasma ToolKind exists. 2. Filter, do not hide-lose: op tool pickers + ToolLibraryDialog default view show only mode-compatible tools, with a visible 'N tools hidden (incompatible with <mode>) — show all' row. A mode switch never mutates the library.

Principles: a settings toggle must never destroy or invisibly orphan data; invalid states visible-and-explained, not impossible; spend the UX at the moment the inconsistency is created. Subset of (and prerequisite for) the machine-profiles feature.

title: Pocket: residual material left along CONCAVE sections of inner island boundary (0.9mm endmill)
description: On refs/testdxf/Epropulsion_SpiritEvo_Batteriestecker_01_bite.dxf, a pocket between an outer ring and an inner ring (island) leaves uncut residual along CONCAVE sections of the inner path; CONVEX sections mill correctly. Tool: 0.9mm endmill (r=0.45). The island wall pass added in 2cdf583 (wiaconstructor-25dj) emits ONE tool-center ring along the knd4-inflated island, but at concave island features the cascade rings and the island-wall ring may not overlap up to the wall, leaving a ribbon/uncut region. Need to reproduce against the actual DXF geometry, inspect cascade vs island-wall rings near concavities, and determine whether it's an unavoidable inner-corner fillet (r=0.45) or a genuine clearing gap. Files: cam/offsets/pocket_fill.rs (island wall pass ~813-859), cam/offsets/parallel.rs (cascade/inflate ~405-455, over-inflate ~595).
notes:
CORRECTION + DECISION: the concave feature is ~0.96mm, i.e. WIDER than the Ø0.9 tool, yet left uncut. So it is NOT the 'narrower than tool' physical limit. Sweep showed the clearing threshold sits slightly ABOVE the tool diameter (cleared at 1.0mm, not at 0.8mm; the exact cutoff is between). Root cause is offset ACCURACY: island inflation uses clipper2 inflate_paths_d with arc_tolerance=0.25mm and precision=4 (JoinType::Round) — the coarse 0.25mm chord tolerance rounds/bridges concave features within ~tool_dia, so a 0.96mm slot gets closed off in the inflated keep-out boundary even though the tool would physically fit. A finer arc_tolerance (e.g. 0.01-0.05mm) on the island inflation would lower the threshold toward the true 0.9mm tool diameter.

DECISION (user, 2026-06-08): accept current behavior, do NOT change the implementation now. Documented as a known accuracy limitation. Leave clipper tolerances as-is.
close_reason: Accepted as known accuracy limitation per user decision — concave clearing threshold sits slightly above tool diameter due to clipper2 island-inflation arc_tolerance=0.25mm. Keeping current implementation; no code change.

title: Wire/config types live in cam/setup.rs, not project/ — newcomers look in the wrong place
description: cam/setup.rs (~1016 prod) defines MachineConfig, ToolConfig, MillConfig, TabsConfig, LeadsConfig, ToolChangeStrategy, AxisLimits — 18 JsonSchema derives — while ARCHITECTURE.md and schema.rs treat project/ as the wire-type home (schema.rs:93 even reaches into cam::setup). The name 'setup' implies runtime resolution, not schema defs. FIX: move the JsonSchema config types into project/machine.rs + project/config.rs; leave cam/setup.rs holding only the runtime-resolved Setup bundle.
design:
JUNIOR-READY PLAN (verified 2026-06-07)

== Goal / end-state rule ==
Make `crate::project` the single home for the JsonSchema wire/config
types. After this change the rule is crisp: **cam/setup.rs exports ONLY
the runtime-resolved `Setup` bundle**; every schema-bearing config type
lives under project/. This matches ARCHITECTURE.md:102, which ALREADY
documents MachineConfig as a project.rs wire type, and extends the
existing precedent at cam/setup.rs:388 (`pub use crate::project::params::{
LeadKind, LeadsConfig, TabType, TabsConfig}` — project is already the home
for the tab/lead types).

== Pre-flight facts (already checked for you) ==
- cam/setup.rs imports ONLY `schemars::JsonSchema` + `serde`. Every other
  reference in the file is a fully-qualified `crate::...` path, so moved
  code carries its paths with it — each new file needs just those two use
  lines.
- schemars keys generated schema on the TYPE NAME, not module path. Moving
  these types produces ZERO schema drift: schema/openapi.yaml and
  frontend/.../generated.ts stay byte-identical. (Verify anyway via the
  xtask schema-check + codegen drift guard in scripts/pre-release.sh.)
- No machine<->config cycle: MachineConfig's fields reference only the
  machine-group enums + AxisLimits. The config-group types touch
  MachineMode only in a doc comment (cam/setup.rs:100), not in code. The
  two new files are mutually independent.

== The split (12 real defs move; Setup stays) ==
NEW FILE  project/machine.rs  (machine capability/config):
  MachineConfig (+ impls/Default), AxisLimits (+impl), ToolChangeStrategy
  (+impl), PostChangeZStrategy (+impls/Default), UnitSystem, MachineMode.
  Move these private helpers with it: deserialize_toolchange,
  default_toolchange_s, is_default_toolchange_s, default_use_kinematic,
  is_default_use_kinematic, default_work_area, is_default_work_area,
  default_decimal_separator_char, is_default_decimal_separator,
  is_false_bool. Also move the `toolchange_strategy_tests` #[cfg(test)] mod.
NEW FILE  project/config.rs  (cut/tool op config):
  ToolOffset, ToolConfig (+impls/Default), MillConfig (+Default),
  PlungeStrategy (+Default), ObjectOrder, PocketConfig. Move helpers:
  default_tip_angle_deg, default_true, deserialize_helix_radius.
STAYS in cam/setup.rs: `Setup` + its `is_default_wcs` helper ONLY. Add at
  top: `use crate::project::{MachineConfig, ToolConfig, MillConfig,
  PocketConfig, TabsConfig, LeadsConfig};` (Setup's field types). DELETE the
  now-redundant line-388 `pub use ...params::{...}` re-export — those types
  reach Setup via the new `use` instead, and importers go to project:: too
  (see step 4).

== Wiring (project.rs) ==
Add alongside the existing submodule block (project.rs:28-38):
  pub mod machine;  pub mod config;
  pub use machine::*;  pub use config::*;
project.rs already flattens submodules (`pub use params::*` etc.), so all
moved types become reachable as `crate::project::<Type>` (and
`ivac_core::project::<Type>` for the transports/tests).

== Importer rewrite (the bulk of the work) ==
Surface: ~79 `use` sites across ~22 files + ~10 inline `crate::cam::setup::X`
fully-qualified paths. RULE for every site: `Setup` stays at
`cam::setup::Setup`; EVERY other name (the 12 moved types + LeadKind/
LeadsConfig/TabType/TabsConfig) moves to `crate::project::` (or
`ivac_core::project::` outside the crate). NOT a blind sed — many lines
import Setup together with moved types and must be SPLIT, e.g.
  use crate::cam::setup::{MachineMode, Setup, ToolOffset, UnitSystem};
becomes
  use crate::cam::setup::Setup;
  use crate::project::{MachineMode, ToolOffset, UnitSystem};
Inline paths: `crate::cam::setup::PlungeStrategy` -> `crate::project::PlungeStrategy`,
etc. (offset_builder.rs and setup_resolver.rs hold most of these).
8 sites live OUTSIDE ivac-core/src (ivac-cli/src/main.rs, ivac-core/benches/
pipeline.rs, and 6 ivac-core/tests/* files incl. golden_corpus.rs,
common/mod.rs) — they use the `ivac_core::cam::setup::` prefix; same split.
Lean on the compiler: after moving defs + adding the project wiring, run
`cargo build --workspace` and let unresolved-import errors enumerate every
remaining site. Iterate to zero.
ALSO update schema.rs:93 `crate::cam::setup::PlungeStrategy` ->
`crate::project::PlungeStrategy`, and refresh ARCHITECTURE.md prose if it
still points at cam::setup for these (line 102 already says project — good).

== Lower-effort fallback (only if churn is unwanted) ==
Move the defs to project/{machine,config}.rs but keep a single
`pub use crate::project::{machine::*, config::*};` re-export in cam/setup.rs
(mirrors line 388). Then importers compile UNCHANGED and only schema.rs +
the two new files change. This fixes the canonical-home complaint (grep
finds the defs in project/) but leaves the `cam::setup::X` indirection the
issue names. RECOMMENDED is the full rewrite above; this is the escape hatch.

== Acceptance criteria ==
1. cam/setup.rs's public surface is `Setup` only (plus private helpers).
2. All 12 types + the 4 params re-exports resolve via `crate::project::*`.
3. schema/openapi.yaml + frontend generated.ts BYTE-IDENTICAL (xtask
   schema-check + codegen drift guard green).
4. cargo test --workspace --tests green (807 lib + golden_corpus +
   integration). cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings clean.
   cargo fmt --all -- --check clean.
5. Run scripts/pre-release.sh — full gate, incl. frontend, since the schema
   seam is in scope.

== Effort ==
~2-3 h for the recommended full rewrite (mechanical but ~22 files; the
Setup/moved-type use-splits are the fiddly part). ~30 min for the fallback.
close_reason: Moved 12 JsonSchema config types into project/machine.rs + project/config.rs; cam/setup.rs now exports only the runtime Setup bundle. ~79 use-sites repointed to crate::project::. Schema byte-identical (schema-check + codegen drift green), 807 lib + integration tests pass, fmt + clippy -Dwarnings clean, zero new pedantic errors vs baseline. Pre-existing pedantic gate failures tracked in og56.

title: Split cam/offsets.rs (2304 prod lines) — 5 responsibilities jammed together
description: Mixes (1) offset primitives (parallel_offset_*, pocket_cascade), (2) pocket-fill (pocket_zigzag/_angled, pocket_for_object — a single ~320-line fn), (3) tab attachment, (4) winding/direction (enforce_winding, apply_cut_direction, approach-rotation), (5) overcut. 'Where is cut-direction decided' vs 'where is the zigzag stride' are in the same 2300-line file. FIX: split into cam/offsets/{parallel,pocket_fill,winding,tabs}.rs at those seams.
design:
JUNIOR-READY PLAN (verified 2026-06-07)

== Strategy: file -> directory module, re-export to ZERO external churn ==
Convert cam/offsets.rs (3852 lines; ~2316 prod + ~1536 test) into a
cam/offsets/ DIRECTORY. cam/offsets/mod.rs keeps the SHARED CORE + a
`pub use <submodule>::*` for each cluster, so all 46 external `cam::offsets::X`
import sites across 19 files (pipeline/*, gcode/*, cam/{tabs,trochoidal,
geometry_cache}, schema.rs, golden_corpus, benches, ivac-cli) resolve
UNCHANGED. This mirrors the project.rs hub pattern (pub use submodule::*)
and the gcode/emit.rs split (cula). Internal reorganization only.

== mod.rs KEEPS (shared core every cluster needs) ==
- PolylineOffset (the central type) + is_false serde helper.
- The diagnostics aggregation: OffsetDiagnostics, take_offset_diagnostics,
  and ALL 6 thread-local RefCell sinks + their take_*/record_* fns
  (PARALLEL_OFFSET_PANICS, POCKET_CASCADE_TRUNCATIONS,
  NOCONTOUR_ALLOWANCE_IGNORED, ZIGZAG_STRIDE_DEGENERATE, APPROACH_POINT_FAR,
  + the structs ParallelOffsetPanic/PocketCascadeTruncation/
  NocontourAllowanceIgnored/ZigzagStrideDegenerate/ApproachPointFarRotation)
  and the consts POCKET_CASCADE_RING_CAP, APPROACH_POINT_WARN_MM. These are
  cross-cutting (pushed from deep in parallel + pocket_fill + winding); keep
  them central rather than scatter. (NB: 7iej.18 wants these threaded as a
  struct instead of thread-locals — OUT OF SCOPE here; this issue is pure
  relocation, do 7iej.18 separately.)
- The shared math helpers used by >1 cluster: signed_area, offset_signed_area,
  reverse_offset. Keep in mod.rs.

== Module split (move these items into cam/offsets/<file>.rs) ==
parallel.rs (offset primitives + clipper cascade):
  object_signed_area, parallel_offset_inward/_outward/_object,
  pocket_cascade, inflate_islands_by_tool_radius, inflate_islands_by_delta,
  over_inflate_islands_for_high_overlap, boundary_offset_inward,
  pocket_cascade_with_islands, build_paths, vc_to_pline, pline_to_segments,
  small_circle_drill.
pocket_fill.rs (zigzag/spiral fill + the ~320-line pocket_for_object):
  pocket_zigzag_angled, pocket_zigzag, pocket_for_object, PocketEmit,
  segment_crosses_any_polygon, segment_intersects_polygon_edges,
  segments_intersect, orient, horizontal_crossings, stitch_rings_to_spiral,
  stitch_rings_to_polyline, bridge_stays_inside_polygon,
  bridge_crosses_any_island.
winding.rs (direction / approach rotation):
  CutContext, enforce_winding, rotate_offsets_to_approach_point,
  apply_cut_direction.
tabs.rs (tab attachment — the most self-contained, do FIRST as the pilot):
  TabPoint, attach_tabs_to_offsets, snap_to_offset, closest_point_on_segment.
overcut: only 2 fns (apply_overcut_to_offsets, apply_overcut) — fold into
  parallel.rs OR a tiny overcut.rs; issue lists 4 target files, so put these
  in parallel.rs to avoid a 2-fn file, OR add overcut.rs if you prefer.

== Visibility / imports (the fiddly part) ==
1. Each submodule starts with EXPLICIT `use super::{...}` of the shared core
   items + sibling-cluster fns it calls (e.g. pocket_fill uses
   parallel_offset_object, PolylineOffset, the diagnostics record_* fns). Do
   NOT use `use super::*` — clippy::pedantic flags wildcard_imports (learned
   in cula). Let the compiler enumerate: drop the glob, build, add the
   listed names. Also each needs its external `use crate::geometry::...`,
   cavalier_contours, clipper2_rust imports (copy the relevant subset from
   the current offsets.rs header, lines 28-30 + the #![allow] block).
2. Items called from OUTSIDE the crate-internal cluster set stay `pub`
   (re-exported). Items only used within the module tree can be `pub(crate)`
   or `pub(super)`.
3. TESTS: keep the #[cfg(test)] mod in mod.rs. Only 4 PRIVATE fns are tested
   and they move to submodules — mark these `pub(super)` so the mod.rs test
   mod still reaches them: horizontal_crossings (->pocket_fill), signed_area
   (stays mod.rs), offset_signed_area (stays mod.rs), reverse_offset (stays
   mod.rs). Everything else the tests touch is the public API (stays
   re-exported). If a moved private fn turns out tested, widen it to
   pub(super) — compiler errors will name them.

== Execution order (incremental, each step builds + tests green) ==
A. `git mv crates/ivac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs crates/ivac-core/src/cam/offsets/mod.rs`
   (Rust resolves cam/offsets/mod.rs as the `offsets` module identically.)
   Build + test to confirm the pure move is inert.
B. Extract tabs.rs (4 items) — the pilot seam. Add `mod tabs; pub use tabs::*;`
   to mod.rs. Build, fix imports, test. Commit.
C. Repeat for winding.rs, then parallel.rs, then pocket_fill.rs (biggest).
   One commit per seam keeps the diff reviewable.

== Acceptance ==
1. Emitted G-code BYTE-IDENTICAL — golden_corpus.rs green. (Pure relocation;
   PolylineOffset/TabPoint stay in mod.rs so schema is untouched — no
   schema-check/codegen concern, but run them anyway.)
2. cargo test --workspace --tests green (809 lib + integration).
3. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -W clippy::pedantic -D warnings
   clean (explicit imports, no wildcard) AND the plain -D warnings gate.
4. cargo fmt --all -- --check clean.
5. All 46 external `cam::offsets::X` sites UNCHANGED (grep to confirm).

== Effort ==
~3-4 h for all 4 seams incl. the full gate. The pilot (move + tabs.rs) is
~45 min and de-risks the rest. Single area (cam/offsets/), but the
pocket_fill cluster (pocket_for_object ~320 lines + 7 fill helpers) is the
bulk. Geometry hot path — lean on golden_corpus after every seam.

title: renderTextLayer re-sends the entire font on every call (742KB number[])
description: Every renderTextLayer call marshals the full font (DejaVuSans ~742KB) as a number[] of byte values across the worker/IPC boundary, then decodes it backend-side. For text EDITS (type a char, change size/spacing/font) this means a ~1s round-trip per debounced render — the live preview feels sluggish even though origin drags are now free (k9cz made origin a draw-time translation, so this no longer affects dragging). Fix direction: register/cache the font once by content hash (send bytes the first time, reference by hash after), or send font_bytes as compact binary (Uint8Array/base64) instead of a JSON integer array, or keep a backend-side LRU of decoded faces keyed by font hash. Frontend toWire() in text_preview.svelte.ts builds the number[]; transports in api/{tauri,wasm,wasm-worker-client}.ts pass it through. Surfaced while fixing k9cz.
close_reason: font_bytes now marshals as a base64 string (serde codec, Vec<u8> unchanged in Rust) instead of a 742KB JSON integer array — FE passes its existing bytes_b64 straight through, ~3x smaller payload, no per-keystroke array build. Deserializer accepts legacy array form for back-compat with saved projects. schema+generated.ts regenerated; full gate green (811 Rust tests, 596 vitest, schema-check, pedantic clippy, cargo-deny).

title: Cross-platform CI breakers: dump_stl hardcodes /tmp; unused event var on non-Linux
description: Sanity check for Windows/macOS portability found two issues invisible to the local Linux pre-release gate (which only lints/tests on Linux): (1) tests/common/mod.rs dump_stl() writes to a caller-supplied /tmp path and panics on failure — on Windows /tmp doesn't exist, so ~8 volume-validation tests panic under 'cargo test --workspace' (ci.yml runs the matrix on windows-latest + macos-latest). All /tmp STL writes funnel through this one helper. Fix: write the basename into std::env::temp_dir(). (2) wiac-tauri/src/main.rs .run(|_app, event|) consumes 'event' only inside a #[cfg(target_os="linux")] block, so on non-Linux it's an unused variable → 'cargo clippy -D warnings' fails on the win/mac matrix lanes. Fix: cfg-guard a 'let _ = &event'. Neither affects the shipped Windows app; both block the project's intended cross-platform CI. App code is otherwise portable (no path-sep hacks, line-endings are user config, Ctrl/Cmd handled, only the Linux WebKit workaround is platform-gated).
close_reason: Fixed in f7408cb: dump_stl now writes to std::env::temp_dir() (portable; Linux behaviour unchanged, test passes); non-Linux 'let _ = &event' guard keeps clippy -D warnings green on the win/mac CI lanes. Audit otherwise clean — no path-sep hacks, line-endings are user config, Ctrl/Cmd handled, only the Linux WebKit workaround is platform-gated. App code is portable.
