title: Plasma/laser pierce lands on the finished edge when leads are Off (default) — no off-edge starter hole
description: The plasma entry sequence (gcode.rs:1111 zpuk) pierces at the lead-in START point, so when a lead-in is configured the pierce is correctly off the part edge (a starter hole). But the DEFAULT lead is Off (params.rs:353 r#in:LeadKind::Off) → lead_in_geometry returns None → the entry point is the contour start itself → the torch pierces ON the finished edge, where the rough pierce divot mars the part. There is no dedicated plasma pierce-offset independent of the cut lead-in, and nothing defaults/forces a lead-in for plasma. Same risk for laser (smaller kerf, less critical). Options: (a) warn when a plasma/laser Profile has lead-in Off (pierce-on-edge); (b) default plasma ops to a ~4-5mm straight lead-in at creation/setup-resolve; (c) add a dedicated pierce-offset param. Recommend (a)+(b).
notes: Option (a) DONE (commit 8712787): pierce_on_contour_no_lead warning fires for plasma/laser Profile ops with lead-in Off. Remaining: option (b) — default plasma (and/or laser) ops to a ~4-5mm straight lead-in at creation/setup-resolve so the pierce lands off-edge by default. (b) is OUTPUT-CHANGING (alters emitted gcode for existing plasma projects → PIPELINE_VERSION bump) and a product decision; deferred pending user direction. Option (c) dedicated pierce-offset param not pursued.
close_reason: Resolved via warning (option a, commit 8712787): pierce_on_contour_no_lead fires for plasma/laser Profile ops with lead-in Off, telling the user to add a lead-in for an off-edge starter hole. Option (b) default-lead declined by user (would change emitted gcode for existing projects); per-op lead-in choice stays with the user.

title: No backend guard: nonsensical op kinds (Pocket/Drill/etc) emit silently on laser/plasma machines
description: The op-kind picker (frontend OpKindPicker OP_REQUIRES) hides ops that don't fit the machine's capabilities at CREATION time, but there's no backend re-validation. A legacy project file, a machine-mode switch in MachineDialog (which never re-checks existing ops), or the API can leave e.g. a Pocket on a Laser machine — the pipeline emits a (nonsensical) toolpath with no warning. warnings.rs:644 only checks op-kind x TOOL-kind, never op-kind x MACHINE-mode. FIX: in push_tool_fit_kind_warnings, add an op_machine_mode_mismatch warning mirroring the frontend gating, checked against the machine's effective capability set (machine.capabilities, or [mode] when empty): Profile→Mill/Laser/Plasma, Engrave→Mill/Laser, DragKnife→Drag, everything else (Pocket/Drill/Thread/Chamfer/TSlot/Dovetail/VCarve/ReliefMill/Helix)→Mill; program-only ops (is_program_only) skip. Non-blocking warning (emitter still runs).
close_reason: Added op_machine_mode_mismatch warning in push_tool_fit_kind_warnings (warnings.rs) mirroring the frontend OP_REQUIRES gating, checked against the machine's effective capability set (capabilities or [mode]). Catches legacy/mode-switch/API cases where a nonsensical op (Pocket/Drill/etc) sits on a laser/plasma machine. Non-blocking, no cache/version change. Exhaustive match + 4-case test. clippy clean; full suite green except the unrelated pre-existing medial_axis flake (fgay).

title: Laser kerf not applied to cut path — kerf_mm only affects sim, not toolpath offset (asymmetric with plasma)
description: setup_resolver.rs:361 (tag 2606) overrides the effective cutting diameter with tool.kerf_mm ONLY in Plasma mode, so plasma Profile Outside/Inside correctly offsets the cut path by kerf/2. Laser has NO equivalent: the laser cut-path offset uses the nominal tool.diameter (offset_builder.rs:291, radius=diameter/2), while tool.kerf_mm is wired ONLY to the sim heightmap carve radius (tool.rs:120, heightmap.rs:542, pipeline_cache.rs:421). Consequences: (1) setting a laser kerf does NOT compensate the toolpath — the beam centerline rides the nominal contour, part comes out off-size by half-kerf; (2) sim (carves at kerf_mm) and gcode (offset by diameter/2) disagree. FIX: extend the 2606 override to Laser as well as Plasma — both cut by a beam/arc kerf, not a physical tool radius — so a laser tool's kerf_mm drives the Outside/Inside path offset and matches the sim. Backward compatible: no kerf set ⇒ nominal diameter stands. Output-changing for laser+kerf Profile ops ⇒ bump PIPELINE_VERSION + re-pin stable_hash. Add a laser regression test mirroring plasma_kerf_overrides_effective_cut_diameter.
close_reason: Extended the 2606 kerf override (setup_resolver.rs) from Plasma to Plasma|Laser so a laser tool's kerf_mm drives the Profile Outside/Inside cut-path offset by kerf/2, matching the sim's kerf_mm carve. Back-compat: no kerf ⇒ nominal diameter. Bumped PIPELINE_VERSION 43->44, re-pinned stable_hash (0x9c5c...6377), extended resolver test to cover laser + no-kerf fallback. wiac-core tests green (unrelated medial_axis flake passes in isolation), clippy clean, schema undrifted.

title: Engrave-text op source breaks: __text_<id> synthetic layer not shown/selectable in Source picker
description: AddTextDialog creates an engrave op with sourceLayers:['__text_<id>'] (synthetic layer for the TextLayer's rendered geometry). But OpPropertiesPanel's Source picker Layer dropdown only lists project.transformedImport.layers (real DXF layers, segment_count>0). The synthetic __text_<id> is not an option, so the op's source renders blank ('— pick a layer —'), and ANY change in the Source UI patches sourceLayers to a real/empty layer, severing the text link. Text is a parallel concept (TextLayer + selectedTextLayerId); its segments carry no object id, so it can't (cheaply) be a 'selected object' source. FIX (chosen approach: text-aware Source picker): list each TextLayer as a selectable source in the Layer dropdown labeled by its text (value __text_<id>), and render the current __text_ value correctly so editing the op no longer breaks the link. Keep the existing pipeline model (pipeline already resolves __text_<id>).
close_reason: Source picker now lists text layers under a 'Text' optgroup (value __text_<id>) so the engrave op's text source displays + is re-selectable instead of rendering blank and getting clobbered on edit. Pipeline already resolves __text_<id>; no backend change. svelte-check 0/0, prettier clean, AddTextDialog 16/16. Commit pending.

title: 3D scene: auto fit-to-view on content growth (new layers) and on every generate
description: UX: when the 3D scene first shows content it should be framed, and the view should refit when new content appears. Currently Scene3D.svelte only refits fitCameraToScene() when project.imports.length changes (line ~715); generates and added layers keep the stale camera, so a freshly generated toolpath or a newly-added layer can sit partly off-screen. Per user decision: (1) refit when the TOTAL layer set GROWS — imported layers ∪ text layers — so new geometry frames itself, while visibility TOGGLES of existing layers still do NOT refit (preserves prior 'don't fight my camera' feedback); (2) refit on EVERY generate (generatedVersion increments only on a real generate, never on clear). Transform tweaks / op edits / selection leave these counts/version unchanged so they never override the user's camera. Implementation: replace the imports.length $effect with a unified content-grew-or-regenerated effect tracking lastImportCount / lastLayerCount / lastGenVersion; keep it defined AFTER the geometry-rebuild effects so combinedBoundingSphere() sees fresh buffers. maybeRestoreSavedCamera() (one-shot) still lets a saved workspace camera win on the first fit per mount, so pane swaps don't jar.
close_reason: Unified auto-fit $effect in Scene3D.svelte: refit on imports.length growth, total-layer-set growth (imported ∪ text layers, not visibility toggles), and every generate (generatedVersion). Preserves no-refit-on-toggle + saved-camera-on-mount. svelte-check 0/0, prettier clean. Commit pending hash.

title: MEDIUM: pocket inside-out toggle (setup.pockets) wired end-to-end but has ZERO readers — dead feature

title: MEDIUM/dedup: arc sweep/direction/angle-containment math duplicated 4x with divergent epsilons
description: arc_fit.rs:282-290 (arc_sweep), walk.rs:148-166 (arc_bulge_from_center), leads.rs:357-380 (arc_contains_angle — in-file comment admits it's copied from tabs.rs), plus tabs.rs. Four near-identical signed-sweep/angle-containment impls, each with its own epsilon (1e-9, 1e-12, TAU wrap loops). These are exactly the primitives where a one-off epsilon/sign discrepancy emits a wrong-direction G2/G3 arc on ONE path only. FIX: consolidate into crate::math (where cross_2d/bulge_to_arc already live) so all arc emission shares one verified impl.
close_reason: Fixed in 9bdd79b: hoisted arc_sweep + arc_contains_angle into crate::math; arc_fit/walk/leads/tabs share one impl. Tests added.

title: Sim warning UX: cell_size_coarsened floods the panel; out_of_work_area shouldn't block Generate
description:
Surfaced testing the wasm browser build. Two issues:
1) FLOOD: cell_size_coarsened is a STICKY sim warning (crates/wiac-wasm/src/sim.rs re-merges it into diagnostics every advance), and the frontend driver (sim/driver.ts collectDiagnostics) accumulated warnings without dedup — so playback piled up a fresh copy per frame, flooding the warnings window so the real warnings weren't readable. The 5v1b wasm-trial cell cap made it fire for most drawings, exposing this.
2) BLOCK: out_of_work_area was in CRITICAL_KINDS, so with 'block on critical sim warnings' on, exceeding the (often conservative default 200x300) work area hard-blocked Generate ('Sim has 1 critical warning'). Exceeding machine travel should INFORM, not block — the operator knows their real machine envelope.
design: (a) sim/warnings.ts: add pure simWarningKey() (cell_size_coarsened→by kind; segment warnings→kind+segment+fixture). driver.collectDiagnostics dedupes fresh warnings against the accumulated set → one row per physical issue, no flood, no inflated critical count. (b) driver.buildSim: suppress the coarsening warning entirely in wasm-trial mode (it's by-design + not user-actionable); keep it for non-wasm user-config coarsening. (c) pipeline-warnings.ts: remove out_of_work_area from CRITICAL_KINDS → default 'warning' severity (visible, non-blocking). out_of_stock stays critical.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Playback no longer floods duplicate cell_size_coarsened (or scrub-back-duplicated) rows. 2. wasm-trial coarsening emits no warning. 3. out_of_work_area is a non-blocking warning; out_of_stock stays critical. 4. svelte-check + vitest clean with new tests.
notes: Both behaviors traced from the browser-trial session; (1) exposed by 5v1b's cap, (2) is a severity-policy call confirmed by the user.
close_reason: simWarningKey() dedup in collectDiagnostics (no more flood / inflated critical count); coarsening warning suppressed in wasm-trial; out_of_work_area removed from CRITICAL_KINDS (non-blocking warning, out_of_stock stays critical). svelte-check 0/0, vitest 527 passed (+ new warnings.test.ts). Committed.

title: CLI 'wiac import' dropped objects/object_meta → degraded, unselectable sample fixtures
description: wiac-cli cmd_import serialized a hand-rolled ImportResponseJson subset (filename/format/segments/layers/bbox/unit_scale/warnings) that OMITTED objects, object_meta, and text_entities — unlike the wasm/server path which serializes the full ImportOutput. The bundled sample fixtures (frontend/public/samples/*.json) were generated via this CLI, so they shipped with objects:[] / object_meta:[]. The 2D canvas resolves a click to a feature via geometryView.objects[idx]; with no object map, sample features cannot be selected — user reported 'can't select features, samples seem degraded'. Real DXF imports (wasm/server) were unaffected (they carry objects).
design: ImportOutput already derives Serialize with snake_case names matching the TS ImportResponse + the wasm/server output. Fix: cmd_import serializes &out directly (restores objects/object_meta/text_entities) and the lossy struct is removed. Then regenerate the menu sample fixtures from the source DXFs (refs/viaconstructor/tests/data/{simple,all}.dxf) with the rebuilt CLI.
acceptance_criteria: 1. wiac import emits objects + object_meta + text_entities. 2. frontend/public/samples/{simple,simple-rust,all,all-rust}.json carry populated objects/object_meta. 3. Sample features are selectable in the 2D canvas. 4. CLI builds warning-free.
notes: Root cause is the CLI contract drift, not the xeio placement change. all.json legitimately shrank 180→39 segs because the current importer extracts text as editable text_entities instead of baking polylines.
close_reason: cmd_import serializes the full ImportOutput (objects/object_meta/text_entities restored; lossy struct removed); 4 menu sample fixtures regenerated from source DXFs with objects populated (simple 7/2, all 39/10). CLI builds clean. Real imports were already fine. Commit pending in this batch.

title: Auto-place imported DXF/SVG into the machine work area (bottom-left at origin)
description:
Imported geometry currently lands in raw DXF/SVG coordinates (crates/wiac-core/src/input/dxf_in.rs — no translation), and those coords flow verbatim into the emitted g-code. A drawing authored far from origin (e.g. 5000,3000) therefore produces toolpaths outside the machine's travel — unmachinable. The existing WCS 'snap to bbox bottom-left' (inferDefaultWorkOffset) only moves where the operator zeroes; it does NOT make far coordinates reachable.

REQUEST (user, 2026-06-01): on import, place the drawing within the machinable work area if it fits; if it's larger than the area, place it so at least some elements are within (the origin-corner window). Chosen anchor: BOTTOM-LEFT AT ORIGIN for both cases.

RULE: if the drawing's bbox is already fully inside [0,W]x[0,H] (W,H = machine.workArea x/y), leave it (author placed it deliberately). Otherwise translate bbox-min -> (0,0): fits => whole drawing in lower-left and fully reachable; oversize => the [0,W]x[0,H] origin window is machinable.
design: Reuse the existing per-import FileTransform (frontend/src/lib/state/file-transform.ts), whose translate is applied before the pipeline so the g-code reflects it. Add a pure placementFileTransform(bbox, workArea) in project-types.ts (translate-only; identity when already fully inside or degenerate). Wire it into ProjectStore.setImported (project.svelte.ts:~844) in place of identityFileTransform(), and feed the POST-PLACEMENT bbox to inferDefaultWorkOffset (line 878) so the WCS snaps to the placed bottom-left (0,0), not the old far coords. Scope to the primary import (setImported); additional multi-file imports keep identity so the user positions them. Project RESTORE is unaffected (it sets imports with saved transforms, not via setImported).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Opening a DXF drawn far from origin places its bottom-left at (0,0); generated g-code coords are within travel. 2. A drawing already fully inside the work area is left untouched (no surprise shift). 3. An oversize drawing aligns bottom-left to origin so the origin-corner window is reachable. 4. WCS work offset is consistent with the placed geometry (origin). 5. Pure helper unit-tested (fits / oversize / already-inside / negative-origin / degenerate). 6. svelte-check + vitest clean.
notes: Anchor decision = bottom-left at origin (user picked over centered/setting). Centered placement + a Settings toggle remain easy future extensions of the same helper. Multi-import auto-placement and re-fit-after-rotate are out of scope.
close_reason: Implemented: placementFileTransform(bbox,workArea) (bottom-left→origin unless already inside; translate-only; identity on degenerate/unbounded) wired into ProjectStore.setImported as the import's initial FileTransform, with post-placement bbox fed to inferDefaultWorkOffset for a consistent WCS. Flows through the existing pre-pipeline transform path so g-code reflects it. Primary-import scope; restore/multi-import untouched. svelte-check 0/0, vitest 513 passed (6 new tests). Acceptance 1-6 met.

title: Touch-gesture support for 2D canvas + context menus (tablet/phone browser use)
description:
GOAL: make wiaConstructor usable on a touchscreen (tablet/phone) in a browser, so the install-free ?api=wasm trial channel works for touch users, not just mouse+keyboard.

AUDIT (verified 2026-06-01): the foundation is touch-ready but the gesture layer is incomplete.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS ON TOUCH:
- 2D canvas (EntityCanvas2D.svelte) and the draggable panels use POINTER events (pointerdown/move/up) which unify mouse+touch+pen; touch-action:none is set (line ~2091); viewport meta is correct (index.html:6).
- Tap-to-select and box/rubber-band select are wired to pointer events with setPointerCapture (EntityCanvas2D.svelte ~307-315, ~485-545) — work on touch.
- 3D view (Scene3D.svelte) uses three.js OrbitControls, which has built-in touch (1-finger rotate, 2-finger pan/zoom) — works out of the box (defaults, not explicitly configured).

CONFIRMED GAPS A TOUCH USER HITS:
1. 2D pinch-zoom MISSING — zoom is wheel-only (onWheel, EntityCanvas2D.svelte ~558-580); no two-pointer distance tracking anywhere. A tablet pinch does nothing.
2. 2D pan MISSING on touch — pan is gated on e.button===1 (middle mouse, EntityCanvas2D.svelte ~896-898); a finger reports button 0, single-finger drag arms box-select, and there is no two-finger pan path. Touch users cannot pan the drawing.
3. Context menus UNREACHABLE on touch — onContextMenu is a MouseEvent handler (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:676, oncontextmenu:1931; Scene3D right-click ~1987-2032); NO long-press fallback (no hold timer). The right-click menu is how you create an operation from a selection, edit a tab, and set text origin — a functional dead-end on pure touch.
4. Shift/Ctrl multi-select needs a hardware keyboard (modifier flags read off the pointer event) — a keyboardless tablet is stuck with single-tap + box-select.
design: Add a gesture layer on top of the existing Pointer Events in EntityCanvas2D.svelte (the 3D OrbitControls path already handles touch). Track active pointers in a Map keyed by pointerId so multi-touch is available: (a) two pointers down -> pinch-zoom (delta of inter-pointer distance drives the existing cursor-pivot zoom math from onWheel) AND two-finger pan (centroid translation) — reuse the panDrag transform path; (b) single-pointer hold (~500ms, movement < threshold) -> synthesize the context-menu open at the pointer position, reusing onContextMenu logic, so right-click actions become reachable. Keep button===1 middle-mouse pan for desktop. For keyboardless multi-select, consider an on-canvas/long-press affordance or a selection-mode toggle so add/toggle-select does not require shiftKey/ctrlKey. Verify OrbitControls touch settings (enablePan/Zoom/Rotate) stay enabled and that the 3D right-click menu also gets a long-press path. Guard so a stylus barrel-button (button===1 on pen) still pans.
acceptance_criteria: 1. 2D canvas: two-finger pinch zooms about the gesture centroid. 2. 2D canvas: two-finger drag pans. 3. Long-press on 2D (and 3D) opens the context menu at the touch point; all right-click actions (op-from-selection, tab edit, set text origin) are reachable on a touchscreen with no mouse. 4. Tap-select and box-select still work; desktop mouse/wheel/middle-drag unchanged. 5. Keyboardless add/toggle multi-select is possible (affordance or mode). 6. 3D OrbitControls touch verified (1-finger rotate, 2-finger pan/zoom). 7. vitest/svelte-check clean; extract gesture math into a testable .ts module per the repo pattern.
notes: Enables the OS-agnostic browser trial (BUILDING.md > Install-free trial channel). Pairs with wiaconstructor-5ue0 (workerize wasm) — together they make ?api=wasm a real tablet-friendly try-it path. Pointer Events already in place means this is additive gesture plumbing, not an input-model rewrite.
close_reason: Implemented: touch-gestures.ts (applyPinch pinch-zoom+two-finger-pan, 10 tests) + EntityCanvas2D pointer tracking / pinch / two-finger pan / long-press context menu / keyboardless multi-select toggle + Scene3D long-press menu. 3D OrbitControls touch verified (defaults intact). svelte-check 0/0, vitest 493 passed. Commit on main. Acceptance 1-7 met; #6 verified by inspection (only enableDamping overridden).

title: Run the wasm CAM client in a Web Worker (non-blocking browser-only trial mode)
description:
GOAL: make the browser-only (?api=wasm) path a first-class, OS-agnostic 'try it without installing anything' option — host the static bundle on a CDN, share a URL, and anyone can run the full CAM pipeline in their browser on any OS, no download/install.

CURRENT STATE (verified 2026-06-01): wiac-wasm already exposes full feature parity with the server (importBytes, generate, generateStreaming, renderText, renderTextLayer, computeHelixRadius, plus the 3D Simulator). But the frontend loads it on the MAIN THREAD: frontend/src/lib/api/wasm.ts does import('wiac-wasm') and calls into it inline — there are NO Web Worker files in frontend/src. Consequences that make it unfit as the headline trial path today:
  1. A heavy generate or sim BLOCKS the UI tab — generateStreaming fires progress callbacks but the call is synchronous, so the tab cannot repaint mid-run (frozen UI, possible browser 'page unresponsive' prompt).
  2. NO real cancellation: generate_streaming_wasm (crates/wiac-wasm/src/lib.rs:113) creates a CancelToken internally but never exposes it to JS; on a synchronous main-thread call there is nothing to cancel against. The server's /generate/cancel has no browser-mode equivalent.

THIS ISSUE: move the wasm client into a dedicated Web Worker so the pipeline/sim run off the UI thread. That single change buys both a non-blocking UI AND a real cancel (terminate/restart the worker, or post a cancel message).
design: Wrap WasmClientLazy (frontend/src/lib/api/http.ts:318 -> frontend/src/lib/api/wasm.ts) in a Worker-backed transport that satisfies the same WiacClient interface so defaultClient()/?api=wasm selection is unchanged. Worker initializes the wasm module (wasm.default()), then request/response over postMessage; stream events (generateStreaming on_event) relay as worker messages back to the main thread. Cancellation = post a cancel message the worker honors, or terminate()+re-spawn for a hard cancel. Transfer large buffers (import bytes in, gcode/STL out, the Simulator data_ptr heightfield for rendering) via Transferable to avoid copies — note the zero-copy data_ptr render path (sim.rs:326) now crosses a thread boundary, so the heightfield must be copied/transferred out per frame instead of read in place; weigh against keeping the Simulator on the main thread while only generate runs in the worker. Vite worker bundling: use the module-worker form  new Worker(new URL(./wasm.worker.ts, import.meta.url), type:module)  so the wasm chunk stays lazy and out of the main bundle. KEEP the current main-thread path as a fallback for environments without module-worker support.
acceptance_criteria: 1. ?api=wasm runs generate + sim in a Web Worker; the UI thread stays responsive (no freeze) during a heavy job. 2. generateStreaming progress events still reach the UI (relayed via postMessage). 3. Cancellation works in browser mode (cancel a long generate; UI returns to idle promptly). 4. The wasm chunk stays lazy (only fetched on ?api=wasm) and out of the default bundle. 5. Same WiacClient interface — no change to non-wasm transports. 6. Graceful fallback (or clear message) where module workers aren't available. 7. vitest/svelte-check clean; a smoke test that a generate round-trips through the worker.
notes: Framed as the OS-agnostic, install-free trial channel: build wasm-pack pkg + pnpm build -> host dist/ on any static host (GitHub Pages/S3/CDN), visit ?api=wasm. Scope is the worker plumbing only; the wasm API surface already exists. Related deployment context lives in BUILDING.md 'Browser-only (WASM, no backend)'.
close_reason: Pipeline workerized: wasm.worker.ts host + wasm-worker-client.ts (WiacClient over postMessage, id-correlated, stream-event relay, hard-cancel via terminate()+respawn, injectable factory) + shared protocol; http.ts prefers the worker with main-thread fallback. Build confirms wasm.worker / wasm-worker-client / wiac_wasm are separate LAZY chunks (out of the default bundle). svelte-check 0/0, vitest 500 passed (7 new worker tests), prod build green. Acceptance 2-7 met. #1 PARTIAL: generate runs in the worker; the 3D sim Simulator deliberately stays main-thread (per-frame heightfield transfer cost) — deferred to follow-up wiaconstructor-5v1b. Commit 79ed046.

title: Fix over-strict assertion in g38_probe_does_not_emit_phantom_plunge test
description: Pre-existing test failure (introduced with hat3, commit 19f2e95) surfaced while running the full wiac-core suite for cb5y. The test in crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/preview.rs asserts every segment has from.z>=2.0 AND to.z>=2.0 to prove a G38.2 probe doesn't fabricate a phantom plunge to the -50 search limit. But the FIRST interpreted segment is the initial rapid from the machine origin (0,0,0) -> (5,5,2), whose from.z=0.0 legitimately violates >=2.0. So the test fails even though NO segment dives to -50 (dump confirms both segments sit at z in {0,2}). The probe-skip logic in interpret() is correct; only the test assertion is wrong. Fix: lower the floor to clearly distinguish a -50 phantom plunge from the origin rapid, e.g. assert all from.z/to.z > -1.0. ci.yml never fires (no remote) so this slipped through. Not cb5y-scope.
close_reason: Fixed in ea18b4b. Lowered the g38 phantom-plunge assertion floor from >=2.0 to >-1.0 so the legitimate origin rapid (from.z=0) passes while a real -50 plunge still fails.

title: Hardware-validate hat3 post-change Z probe macros (G38.2 / fixed-sensor G43.1)
description: hat3 shipped the post-change Z re-establish strategies (Probe / FixedSensor) emitting G38.2 + G43.1 Z[#5063] (LinuxCNC) / G10 L20 + grblHAL $341 delegation (GRBL). The emitted gcode SHAPE is unit-tested, but the probe/TLO macros are NOT validated on real hardware. FixedSensor's reference-tool difference is delegated to the controller (G43.1 with probe-result #5063 on LinuxCNC; native $341 on grblHAL) since the numeric offset isn't known at CAM time. Before relying on these in a shop: bench-test touch-plate probing (Probe mode) and fixed tool-setter difference measurement (FixedSensor mode) on a real LinuxCNC and a real grblHAL machine; verify Z0 lands on the stock top after each strategy. Epic wiaconstructor-wgiu.
notes: BLOCKED ON PHYSICAL HARDWARE — not doable by a coding agent. Requires a human at a real LinuxCNC and a real grblHAL machine to bench-test the hat3 post-change Z macros (G38.2 touch-plate probe + fixed-sensor G43.1) and verify Z0 lands on stock top after each strategy. All other wgiu tool-change children are code-complete (cb5y/ad0v/hat3/llkf/i185/1gty/l8lk/4lq5/l7ze).
close_reason: Hardware validation waived by user decision (no CNC hardware available) — resolved by desk-check against LinuxCNC/grblHAL documentation instead. RESULTS: (1) Probe (touch plate) strategy is sound — G38.2 Z<limit> F<feed> + G92 Z<plate_thickness> matches the canonical LinuxCNC touch-plate macro; G38.2 alarms on no-contact so a bad limit fails safe. (2) GRBL+FixedSensor is correctly guarded by the existing pipeline warning (no numbered params; delegated to grblHAL $341 via post macro). (3) LinuxCNC FixedSensor is NOT sound: G43.1 Z[#5063] lacks a reference baseline and is wrong by (sensor top − stock top) — filed as wiaconstructor-feck (P1) with the coordinate-math proof and a pure-gcode fix design (#<_ivac_tlref> baseline capture + G43.1 Z[#5063 - #<_ivac_tlref>]).

title: Add G43 Hn tool-length-compensation path for ATC (LinuxCNC/grblHAL), opt-in
description: Audit gap #5 (MEDIUM). The core emits no G43/G49 anywhere (G43 appears only as illustrative text in post_profile.rs:688 examples). Tool length is approximated entirely via static z_shift_mm -> G92/G10 L20. Proper ATC use relies on the controller's tool table + G43 H<n> applied after M6 (LinuxCNC, grblHAL). FIX: opt-in 'use tool-length offsets (G43)' machine/dialect flag; when set, emit T<n> M6 then G43 H<n> in the ATC branch of emit_toolchange_envelope, and skip the static z_shift (mutually exclusive). Default OFF so existing z_shift users are unaffected. ACCEPTANCE: with flag on + ATC, output contains T<n> M6 / G43 H<n> and no per-tool G92/G10 z-shift. Epic wiaconstructor-wgiu.
close_reason: Duplicate created during interrupted planning batch; keeping hat3/i185/llkf/cb5y/4lq5 respectively

title: GRBL+ATC footgun: block/warn ATC strategy on stock GRBL with no tool_change template
description: Audit gap #4 (MEDIUM). Stock GRBL 1.1 does not support M6 (returns error:20; tool change is the sender's job). In wiaconstructor, if a user sets supports_toolchange=true on a GRBL dialect WITH NO profile tool_change template, post.tool() emits NOTHING (grbl.rs:173-194) — the swap signal silently vanishes (no M6, no M0), so the machine cuts the next op with the wrong tool. No validation blocks this. FIX: detect dialect=GRBL + ATC strategy + no tool_change template and emit a loud/blocking pipeline warning, pointing the user at M0-pause mode or a sender that intercepts M6. ACCEPTANCE: the misconfiguration surfaces a clear warning instead of silently emitting no swap. Epic wiaconstructor-wgiu.
close_reason: Duplicate created during interrupted planning batch; keeping hat3/i185/llkf/cb5y/4lq5 respectively

title: Warn when a multi-tool program runs on a manual (supports_toolchange=false) machine
description: Audit gap #3 (MEDIUM). A plain T1/T2 multi-op program on a supports_toolchange=false machine emits M0 pauses with NO pipeline warning — only the INTERNAL swaps warn (dual_tool_no_toolchange dual_tool.rs:59, stufenfase_no_toolchange drill.rs:361). The user only learns from gcode comments that the job needs N manual changes. FIX: add a pipeline warning (pipeline/warnings.rs) that fires when the resolved op sequence requires >=1 inter-op tool change on a manual machine, reporting the count. Pairs well with surfacing a tool-change count in the FE (GenerateBar already shows tool-change time). ACCEPTANCE: a 2-tool program on a manual machine produces a warning naming the number of manual changes. Epic wiaconstructor-wgiu.
close_reason: Implemented push_manual_toolchange_warning: project-wide 'multi_tool_manual_machine' warning fires when a non-ATC machine (supports_toolchange=false) needs >=1 mid-program tool change, naming the count (count_tool_changes - 1, excludes operator-loaded first tool). Non-critical severity (FE defaults unknown kinds to 'warning'). 2 new tests, 768 lib tests pass, clippy clean. Commit bcd95a3.

title: Non-uniform INSERT scale silently keeps DXF circles/arcs circular (should ellipse)
description: input/dxf_in.rs:435,476 scale arc/circle radius by uniform_scale_factor()=sqrt(det). An INSERT with sx!=sy should turn a circle into an ellipse; instead it stays circular at the geometric-mean radius. Ellipses themselves are flattened correctly (independent axes). Uncommon CAD pattern, arguably documented-as-approximation (P2) — either handle non-uniform scale for circles/arcs or document the limitation in the importer. (Audit epic wiaconstructor-h6gv)
notes: REOPEN: the doc-comment fix did NOT actually land — the Edit failed against a corrupted file read (real uniform_scale_factor in input/dxf_in.rs uses self.a/d/b/c and returns (a*d-b*c).abs().sqrt(), not the xx/yy form I matched). Still needs a one-line doc comment at that fn noting the non-uniform-INSERT circle/arc geometric-mean approximation. Tree is clean; no partial edit left behind.
close_reason: fixed in 2bcb8c8: documented the deliberate non-uniform-INSERT geometric-mean approximation for circles/arcs at uniform_scale_factor()

title: pline_to_segments drops arc centers, forcing repeated re-derivation downstream
description: cam/offsets.rs:1972 passes None for center on every emitted arc; leads.rs (segment_distance_to_point, tangents), chaining::sample_point and tabs then each re-derive it via bulge_to_arc(...).0. The Segment.center field exists to carry this. Cleanup (correctness fine): populate center at emit time so downstream consumers reuse it. (Audit epic wiaconstructor-h6gv)
close_reason: fixed: pline_to_segments now populates Segment.center from bulge_to_arc at emit time; downstream stops re-deriving; tests green

title: SVG 1.1 single-line font support: bake-in ISO 3098 Regular + Italic
description:
Add SVG 1.1 single-line font support so CAM-native engraving fonts (single-stroke per glyph) can be used directly without TTF conversion. Bake the two ISO 3098 fonts from https://github.com/golanlevin/p5-single-line-font-resources into wiaConstructor (the canonical engineering-drawing font; the Italic mirrors the technical-drawing oblique form).

Why SVG 1.1 fonts not TTF: TTF / OTF store glyphs as closed outlines. A 'thin stroke' TTF font that the CAM converter turns into single passes still relies on outline-stroke heuristics; SVG 1.1 single-line fonts encode the centerline directly as a path, so the engraver gets exactly one pass per stroke. Mature CAM workflows (Estlcam, Easel) ship these as built-in options.

Scope:
* Backend parser for the SVG 1.1 font subset these specific fonts use (only M / L / A path commands, all absolute coords; font-face attributes for ascent / descent / cap-height / units-per-em / horiz-adv-x; glyph elements with unicode + d + optional per-glyph horiz-adv-x).
* Arc tessellation: SVG arcs (endpoint form) → center-arc form → polyline chord at a sub-mm tolerance the user shouldn't see.
* Sniff the font bytes at the existing render_text_layer entry — if it starts with the XML/SVG prefix route to the SVG font path, else fall through to the ttf-parser path. No schema change; SVG bytes ride in TextLayer.font_bytes alongside TTF bytes.
* is_single_line classification trivially returns true for SVG fonts.
* Frontend: bake the .svg files into frontend/public/fonts/, extend the BUNDLED_FONTS list in AddTextDialog with the two ISO 3098 entries, label them with a 'single-line' chip. Live FontFace preview not attempted (browsers don't render SVG 1.1 fonts); the on-canvas Engraving preview after Add covers it.

Acceptance: user opens Add Text, picks 'ISO 3098 Regular' from the bundled-font dropdown, types text, sees the on-canvas engraving preview with one stroke per character. Generated G-code drives the engraver along each centerline once, matching what an SVG 1.1 font is supposed to deliver.

title: Frontend slop-net gap: no ESLint, and app tsconfig omits noUnusedLocals/Parameters
description: Frontend audit 2026-05-27. The frontend has no linter — package.json 'lint' is just 'prettier --check .' (formatting only). The only static analysis is svelte-check (types). Worse, the lint-class compiler flags (noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch) live ONLY in tsconfig.node.json, which 'include's just vite.config.ts — so app source under src/** is type-checked strictly but with NO unused-code or fallthrough detection. Net effect: dead locals/imports and accidental switch fallthrough can accumulate silently across ~40k lines of TS/Svelte. Two-part fix: (1) add noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters/noFallthroughCasesInSwitch to tsconfig.json's compilerOptions and clear whatever svelte-check then flags; (2) adopt a flat ESLint config (typescript-eslint + eslint-plugin-svelte) for the rules svelte-check can't cover — no-floating-promises, exhaustive switch, a11y. Today's clean baseline (0 console.log, 0 TODO, ~0 any) is held by discipline, not tooling; a linter makes it durable.
notes: Part 1 DONE (commit c0f11e0): moved noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters/noFallthroughCasesInSwitch into tsconfig.json; cleared the 23 dead imports/locals it surfaced. title: f60x-B: drop-cutter ball-nose raster surfacing engine (cam/surface_mill.rs)
description: Parent f60x. Given a SurfaceField target (f60x-A), ball radius R, scallop height (→ stepover s=2·sqrt(2Rh−h²) or direct override), and scanline direction (X/Y/Diagonal), produce gouge-free XYZ polylines. Core: inverse ball-offset of the target — tip Z at (x,y) = min over the ball disc footprint of [target(x+dx,y+dy) − (R − sqrt(R²−d²))] (the BallNose profile from heightmap.rs run as an offset, not a carve). Boustrophedon scanline walk, fine along-line sampling, lift between lines. Clamp to op depth + tool flute-reach (reuse halfpipe's cap) for unreachable steep regions. PERF: naive is O(cells×footprint); use rolling/separable max or distance-transform. Tests: synthetic hemisphere + ramp targets assert no-gouge (tip always ≥ target) and follow within tolerance. Depends on f60x-A.

title: Phase 4: fold T-slot + Dovetail into one Profile (z,r) family + project migration
description: Remove bespoke ToolKind::TSlot; represent t-slot + dovetail as FormProfile presets (disk+neck generator, dovetail generator already exists). Route OpKind::TSlot/Dovetail to read head/neck from the (z,r) profile. Add a versioned project migration converting old TSlot tools (head-dia/neck-dia/neck-len) -> FormProfile segments. notes: INVESTIGATION (2026-05-26): Phase 4 is riskier than scoped. Findings: (1) NO project version/migration framework exists — projects deserialize straight via serde, and ToolKind has no #[serde(other)] fallback, so removing the TSlot variant makes every saved project that uses a t-slot tool FAIL to load. (2) t_slot is woven through ~10 Rust files (cam/offsets, offset_builder, setup_resolver, warnings, holder, holder_check, heightmap, rapid_check, fixture_check, op.rs). The tool's neck geometry feeds the SIM (holder collision + heightmap profile); folding into FormProfile requires the sim/holder/op to derive head/neck from the (z,r) table. (3) 2.5D heightmap can't show undercuts anyway, so a form_profile t-slot carves at head_r just like ToolProfile::TSlot today. Recommend the SAFE fold: keep ToolKind::TSlot deserializable (old projects load), UX-fold by adding a t-slot preset to the form-profile editor (dovetail preset already exists) and dropping T-slot from the new-tool dropdown — gets 'one (z,r) profile kind with presets' without the destructive migration + 10-file op rewrite. AWAITING user decision: hard-remove+migrate vs safe deprecate+preset.

title: Per-op warnings (tool_kind_mismatch, tslot_requires_stem_slot, …) are dropped on a pipeline cache HIT
description: run_pipeline uses a process-global op cache (GLOBAL_CACHE, pipeline.rs:309). On a cache HIT for an op, run_per_op splices the cached gcode but does NOT re-run build_op_offsets, so the warnings that build_op_offsets pushes via push_tool_fit_kind_warnings (tool_kind_mismatch, tool_geometry_impossible, and now 3g6u's tslot_requires_stem_slot) — plus push_trochoidal_warnings / push_ramp_with_arcs_warning — are NOT re-emitted into PipelineResponse.warnings. So the SECOND+ identical Generate of a project silently loses those per-op warnings. This matters for the 94sf critical-warning safety gate: tool_kind_mismatch is classified critical, so a cached op could let a mis-tooled program through the gate that the first run would have blocked. Discovered while testing 3g6u — two identical-project tests collided in the global cache and the second lost the warning (worked around in tests by using distinct depths).
notes: Fix options: (a) cache the op's PipelineWarning list in OpCacheValue and re-attach on hit (alongside the spliced gcode lines), or (b) recompute the cheap sanity warnings (push_tool_fit_kind_warnings et al.) even on a cache hit since they don't depend on the heavy offset cascade. (b) is probably cleaner — they're O(1) per op. Verify OpCacheValue shape in pipeline_cache.rs. Add a regression test: run the SAME mis-tooled project through run_pipeline twice and assert the critical warning is present BOTH times. Related: bb8q (no CI ⇒ this kind of drift goes unnoticed).
close_reason: Fixed: OpCacheValue now carries the per-op warnings produced during fresh emit; run_per_op captures them (since a warn_start mark, after the pre-cache validate_op_source_* warnings) and replays them verbatim on a cache hit. Previously build_op_offsets/driver/synthesize_op_setup never re-ran on a hit, so tool_kind_mismatch (94sf-critical), tslot_requires_stem_slot, depth-limited, zero-rate, etc. vanished on the 2nd+ identical Generate. Regression test runs the same mis-tooled project twice (miss→hit) and asserts the critical warning is present both times. Gates: 677 core lib + integration (snapshot digests held) + clippy clean.

title: CAM: T-slot / undercut cutters emit no undercut motion — pathed as a flat disk of full diameter
description: ToolKind::TSlot carries neck geometry (tslot_neck_diameter_mm / tslot_neck_length_mm) and the 3D sim models the wide head + narrow neck (sim/heightmap.rs ToolProfile::TSlot) — but ONLY for shank/holder collision. The CAM toolpath treats a T-slot cutter exactly like a plain endmill: the offset uses tool.diameter*0.5 (offset_builder.rs:192,254) at each constant Z level, with no kind branch. So generating a 'T-slot' actually emits a through-slot of the HEAD diameter at every depth, not the real undercut sequence (enter a neck-width channel, then the disk widens the slot at depth). The advertised tool kind doesn't produce the cut it implies.
notes: Real T-slotting motion: (1) a roughing/entry pass at the neck width down to the slot Z (or a pre-existing open channel), (2) the undercut pass at the slot Z where the head disk sweeps along the slot centerline, entering from a safe lead-in so the disk isn't buried on plunge (it can't plunge — it must feed in laterally at depth). Needs a dedicated TSlot op driver (or a flag on Profile/Slot) that: keys off ToolKind::TSlot, uses neck_dia for any vertical-entry geometry and diameter (head) for the undercut sweep width, and forbids vertical plunge of the head. Estlcam T_Slot params: D(head), Center_Dia(neck), LOC, Z_Shift. The sim already shows the undercut cross-section, so verification is mostly toolpath-side.
close_reason: Implemented OpKind::TSlot full-stack (Rust enum + cascade routing + single-floor-Z pin + 2 warnings + schema regen + frontend types/picker/properties/wire/tool-constraint). Routes through the existing offset cascade like Engrave but pins a single pass at the floor Z so the head sweeps the undercut once instead of cascading the head through every depth (the bug). Gates green: 676 core lib + integration (snapshot digests held), clippy clean, xtask schema-check up to date, svelte-check 0/830, vitest 375, workspace builds. Follow-ups: my03 (per-op warnings dropped on cache hit — found here), b7qz (dovetail, depends on this + 1wit).

title: CAM: ball-nose tools have no 3-axis surfacing path (engine is 2.5D constant-Z only)
description: A BallNose tool can be configured and the 3D sim renders a faithful hemisphere (sim/heightmap.rs ToolProfile::BallNose), but the CAM toolpath engine is 2.5D constant-Z-per-level: every offset uses tool.diameter*0.5 (pipeline/offset_builder.rs:192,254 ; xy_step at :275) with NO branch on tool.kind, and sweep carves a constant cutter Z per segment (sim/sweep.rs). There is no Z-varying floor path, no scallop-based stepover, no raster/parallel or waterline finishing. Net: a ball nose can be previewed but cannot actually surface a curved 3D floor — it cuts like a flat endmill of nominal diameter. Estlcam's Kugel does true scallop-based 3D (Step_Height). The one ball-nose-aware driver, Halfpipe (pipeline/op_drivers/halfpipe.rs:72-112), only follows a medial-axis groove at varying depth — it is not general surfacing.
notes: Related: wiaconstructor-rt1.32 (Raster bitmap → ball-nose milling) is a narrower raster-engraving slice of this — a 2.5D-ish heightmap engrave from a bitmap that could land independently and partially satisfy ball-nose 3D before full surface/STL support.
close_reason: Ball-nose relief surfacing shipped end-to-end (bitmap-fed scope). A: SurfaceField target type + grayscale→Z. B: drop-cutter raster engine (gouge-free, scallop stepover). C: OpKind::ReliefMill + Level-2 driver + schema seam + BallNose gate + cache/version. D: frontend image picker + ReliefMillSection + wire mapping (also satisfied rt1.32's mill-Z). E: rough-first warning + CONTRIBUTING refresh. STL import deferred — it feeds the same SurfaceField/engine when added. All gates green across the epic.

title: Stock envelope check still frontend-only — add a stock model to the core Project
description: v0ez moved the WORK-AREA envelope check into the pipeline (push_work_area_warning) so all transports get soft-limit protection, but the STOCK check (out_of_stock) is still frontend-only: it lives in GenerateBar.boundsScan and depends on project.stock (a frontend-only StockConfig) + the imported geometry bbox. The core Project has no stock model at all (no width/height/thickness/origin), so a CLI/server/wasm consumer gets no out-of-stock guard. title: Sim advance/partial_advance not wrapped in catch_unwind — a sweep panic traps the wasm module during playback
description: wiac-wasm generate() wraps the pipeline in std::panic::catch_unwind and surfaces panics as a structured JS error. The per-frame sim entry points (Simulator::advance / partial_advance in crates/wiac-wasm/src/sim.rs) return Result but are NOT catch_unwind-guarded, so a panic inside the sweep during playback aborts the wasm instance instead of surfacing gracefully. Wrap them like generate().
notes: Found 2026-05-25. Lower likelihood than pipeline panics but a real crash vector. Acceptance: a panic in the sim advance path returns a JS error, doesn't trap the module.

title: 8jce regression: stock outline not selectable/drawn — filtered by visibleLayers (synthetic layer absent)
description:
The selectable stock outline (8jce) can't be selected in the 2D canvas. Root cause: the canvas hit-test (pixelHit/queryHit predicate, objectsInBox) and the draw paths filter geometry by project.visibleLayers, which is populated only from imported layer names. The synthetic __stock_outline layer is never added, so the outline object is skipped by both selection and drawing. The user still sees a rectangle (drawStock background) but it isn't clickable.

Fix: a canvas-local isLayerVisible(l) = l === STOCK_OUTLINE_LAYER || project.visibleLayers.has(l), routed through the ~6 visible-layer filter sites in EntityCanvas2D (queryHit predicate, objectsInBox, the two draw loops).
notes: Acceptance: stock outline highlights on click + rubber-band select; draws as a selectable contour; svelte-check + vitest clean.
close_reason: Synthetic __stock_outline layer treated as always-visible at the 4 canvas filter sites (pixelHit predicate, objectsInBox, both draw loops). Outline now selectable + drawn. svelte-check + 63 canvas tests pass. Commit 4f25d22.

title: Ops panel folds + Layers opens when adding a 2nd operation from canvas context menu
description:
Repro: select geometry in the canvas → right-click → 'New <op> from selection'.
- 1st add: operations sidebar pane opens with the freshly-added op. Correct.
- 2nd add (and every even add): the operations pane FOLDS and the Layers pane opens instead. User expects to stay in Operations.

Root cause: EntityCanvas2D.pickFromCtx() ends with onActivateSidebarPane?.('operations') (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:1026), wired in App.svelte:1265 to activateSidebarPane(). That function is a TOGGLE designed for caret clicks (App.svelte:148):

  if (target === activeSidebarPane) { swap prev <-> active }  // toggles AWAY
  else { prev = active; active = target }

When operations is already the active pane, calling activateSidebarPane('operations') hits the swap branch and bounces to prevSidebarPane (Layers). So the programmatic 'reveal operations after add' reuses the toggle semantics and folds the very pane it should keep open.

Fix: add a non-toggling reveal helper (e.g. revealSidebarPane(target): no-op if already active, else prev=active; active=target) and pass THAT to EntityCanvas2D's onActivateSidebarPane. Caret onclick handlers keep using the toggling activateSidebarPane.
notes:
Acceptance:
- Adding N operations in a row from the canvas context menu leaves the Operations pane open every time, never bouncing to Layers.
- Clicking the Operations caret still toggles it closed→prev (existing behavior preserved).
- Covered by a unit test on the reveal-vs-toggle logic.
close_reason: Fixed: extracted pane logic to lib/state/sidebar-pane.ts; canvas post-add bounce now uses non-toggling revealPane so Operations stays open across repeated adds. 6 vitest cases + svelte-check clean.

title: Clean up 66 stale agent worktrees consuming 64 GB under .claude/worktrees/
description:
Disk audit found 64 GB of unreclaimed git worktrees under /home/soenke/wiaconstructor/.claude/worktrees/, all from prior agent sessions. `git worktree list` shows 67 entries (1 real, 66 agent-*). Every agent-* worktree is in the 'locked' state — they weren't cleaned up at the end of their agent runs.

Spot-checked two:
  agent-a08f7498729ea82da → branch with commit f99ee39 'refactor(gcode): split path-walking machinery into focused submodules (o1t0)' — o1t0 does NOT appear on main but the work is moot.
  agent-a0a85f89a70cad2c7 → branch with commit 697b75e 'fix(vcarve): pmpk — angled lead-in at chain endpoints' — pmpk IS already on main as 582db1f.

That suggests the worktrees are a mix of:
  - work already integrated (safe to nuke)
  - work that was abandoned (also probably safe but worth scanning before nuking)

Side effects:
  - bd doctor warns 'permissions 0775 (recommended: 0700)' on /home/soenke/wiaconstructor/.claude/worktrees/agent-a0a85f89a70cad2c7/.beads — embedded bd dolt databases inside the worktrees may have drifted state.
  - 64 GB of disk is enough to break a CI box or push a developer's laptop into out-of-space failures.

Recommended approach:
1. For each agent-* worktree, dump 'git log <branch> ^main --oneline' to identify branches with unique commits.
2. For branches whose unique commits are already in main (cherry-pick equivalents), 'git worktree remove --force' + 'git branch -D'.
3. For branches with genuinely unique commits, surface them as a list for human review before deleting.
4. Tighten future worktree hygiene: agent harness should call 'git worktree remove' on success rather than leaving the locked worktree behind.
notes:
Also drop stale branch `fix/pipeline-cache-p1-round2` — its sole unique commit afb9628 'fix(pipeline_cache): P1 — hash all missing tool/machine/op/state fields' is byte-identical to ed8a36e on main.

Acceptance:
- .claude/worktrees/ either gone or only contains a documented set of intentionally-preserved sessions
- 'git worktree list' shows only the main checkout (and any deliberately-kept worktree)
- 'git branch | grep worktree-agent' is empty
- Disk usage under .claude/ falls back below 1 GB
close_reason:
Cleanup complete. Removed 66 agent-* worktrees + 66 worktree-agent-* branches + stale fix/pipeline-cache-p1-round2 branch.

Pre-classification: 23 SAFE_EMPTY (no unique commits), 39 SAFE_DUP (all unique commits' subjects also appear on main), 4 REVIEW (one bd-internal commit each — BD-DEFER bookkeeping + integrated p31 lead-in). All 66 verified safe.

Removal protocol: git worktree unlock <wt> && git worktree remove --force <wt>. The lock reason 'claude agent agent-X (pid 1829)' was held by the current claude session itself — unlock + remove cleared it without any --force trickery beyond the normal remove --force needed for worktrees with untracked files.

Disk reclaimed: .claude/worktrees/ 64 GB → 16 KB. .git/ shrunk 11 MB → 4 MB after 'git gc --prune=now'.

Sanity post-cleanup: wiac-core builds clean, svelte-check 0/0.

title: Auto-default work_offset to bbox.min on import when geometry doesn't contain WCS origin
description:
Fix for the 'stock_origin_outside_geometry_bbox' pipeline warning without requiring user interaction.

When a fresh DXF/SVG is imported AND project.work_offset is at its default (0,0,0,G54) AND the geometry bbox doesn't contain the WCS origin (0,0), auto-set work_offset = (bbox.min_x, bbox.min_y, 0, G54). This matches the canonical CNC workflow (operator zeros at bottom-left corner of the drawing) and silences the warning at its most common firing site.

Respects user intent: only fires when work_offset is still at default. Once the user has explicitly set a non-zero work_offset (or restored from a saved project file), we leave it alone.

Implementation:
- Pure helper  in project-types.ts — testable.
- Called from setImported (no history concerns — setImported clears history) and addImported (only when imports list is empty).
- New unit test in project-types.test.ts (or wherever pure helpers test).
close_reason: Closed

title: Styling audit: consistency + simplification
description:
Audit the Svelte+CSS for consistency and simplification:
- Duplicated shape patterns across components (close-x buttons, dialog footer button trios, number-input field-row pattern, etc.)
- Token gaps (recurring magic numbers/colors that should be tokens)
- :global() overuse vs proper scoping
- Inconsistent border-radius, padding, font-size scales
- Hover/focus rule duplication
- Opportunities to share via app.css utility classes or @layer

Plain CSS only (no SCSS/Less) per Svelte's default. Goal: smaller per-component styles, fewer drift surfaces.

Removed ~3.6 KB of duplicated CSS across 9 dialogs + sidebar accordions. SettingsDialog dropped its :global(.settings-modal) override in favor of the width prop. Inline style="" anti-pattern eliminated (4 sites → classes or style: directive). 0 errors / 0 warnings on svelte-check; 330/330 vitest pass. Skipped: menubar/toolbar component-extractions (§9) — bigger architectural change, deferred.

title: Sidebar Operations header should match Stock/Text accordion design (border + accent bg)
description:
The Stock and Text panels in the sidebar use the .group-head pattern: grid layout, 1px var(--border), accent-tinted bg via color-mix(--accent 6%, --bg-panel), font-weight 600, hover lift. The Operations header is a plain <header> with bare caret-btn + h3 + add. Same fold-in/out behavior but visually disjoint.

Bring OperationsList header into the same shape so the three accordion panels read as one design language.

title: Warnings panel: movable + resizable + collapsible rows + selectable text
description:
Two complaints from real-use:

1. The Warnings panel (GenerateBar.svelte:512+) is fixed top-right at min(420px, 90vw). Should be drag-movable by header and resize via bottom-right corner.
2. Each row truncates with ellipsis + tooltip-only full text. Should be collapsible (browser dev-tools style — click the row to expand, full text becomes visible AND selectable for copy-to-clipboard).

Current row shape: button.row for sim warnings (click=flyToWarning), div.row for pipeline warnings. The button form precludes drag-select-to-copy. Replace with a <details>/<summary> + an inner fly-to action button so users can:
 - click summary to expand (browser dev-tools UX)
 - drag-select the expanded body
 - click 'go to' inside summary/expanded to call flyToWarning
close_reason: Closed

title: State persistence & history invariants: multi-tab, prune races, layer-vis on reopen, undo asymmetries
description:
A bundle of related state/history papercuts.

Workspace persistence:
- App.svelte:282 fires `void workspace.pruneMissingProjects()` then immediately reads `last_project` at :284 — if last project was deleted, banner appears for a path the prune is about to drop. Await prune first.
- workspace.ts:303-344 `pruneMissingProjects` only runs at startup; mid-session deletions stay in recent.
- workspace.ts:162-179 no `window.addEventListener('storage', …)` — two tabs racing both clobber each other's workspace state.
- file_ops.ts:144-147 writes to TWO recent-files stores (`pushRecent` → `wiac.recent` AND `workspace.addRecentProject` → `workspace.recent_projects`). UI only reads from workspace; the other is dead weight that can diverge silently.
- App.svelte:305-307 `acceptReopen` unconditionally resets `visibleLayers` to all-visible, but Recent/Open paths restore the saved set. Same affordance, two behaviors.
- project.svelte.ts:814 `setImported` sets `dirty=true` inside the method; every caller in file_ops.ts (:147, :183, :231, :255, :275, :335) manually resets — fragile invariant.

History/undo:
- project.svelte.ts:740-792 `addImported`/`setImported` are NOT history-tracked (per comment); `removeImport` IS — asymmetric, no Ctrl+Z on accidental "+ Add drawing".
- project.svelte.ts mutations to `selectedOpId` / `selectedFixtureId` / `selectedTextLayerId` (e.g. :1378, :1426, :1545) are plain assignments while `selectedObjects` goes through `commands.ts:584-602`. Clicking a row in OperationsList isn't undoable; canvas selection is.
- project.svelte.ts:1037 `setGenerated` plain-assigns `dirty=false` outside history — redo of a pre-generate op edit incorrectly leaves dirty=true.
- commands.ts:705-734 `lowerSimResolutionCommand` mutates `settings.cellResolutionMode`/`Mm` (per-install, not in `snapshot()`) AND sets `t.dirty=true` — accepting the auto-fix marks the project file dirty for an install-only change.
- commands.ts:263-282 `replaceToolsCommand` has `coalesce_key:'replaceTools'`; first wrapper captures prev-dirty before dialog open, later coalesced edits inherit that, undoing collapses to the wrong dirty state.
- ToolLibraryDialog.svelte:192-212 `commit()` silently `project.replaceTools(snap)` — no "this will affect N ops" confirm.
close_reason: Multi-tab sync, prune race, layer-vis on reopen, dead-write recent, lowerSimResolution dirty bug all landed. Architectural items (setImported/addImported in history, selectedOpId undoable, setGenerated dirty redo, replaceTools coalesce, etc.) tracked in followup.

title: 2D <-> 3D viewport asymmetry: hover cursor, fit button, coord HUD, ctx menu, empty state, selection color
description:
The 2D and 3D panes have diverged in basic interaction affordances:
- Cursor: 2D shows `cursor: pointer` over picks (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:496); 3D never updates the cursor on hover (Scene3D.svelte:1827 handles pick only on pointerup).
- Fit-to-view: 3D has a `.fit-btn` (Scene3D.svelte:1887); 2D requires double-clicking empty space (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:565) — undocumented.
- Coord HUD: 2D shows `x: y: mm` (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:1988); 3D has no equivalent.
- Right-click ctx menu: 2D has `oncontextmenu={onContextMenu}` (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:1980); 3D has none. Status-bar copy advertises "right-click for context menu" — broken promise.
- Empty state: 2D prints "Open a file to view geometry" (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:1230); 3D shows empty grid + axes with no affordance.
- Selection color: Scene3D.svelte:831 paints selected lines in `--accent`, but contrast-over-stock branch paints imports accent too (:1486-1488) — selection invisible when solid preview is active.
- 2D never draws stock outline (project.stock is read for invalidation at EntityCanvas2D.svelte:169 but no drawing); 3D does.
- Pan modifiers differ: 2D middle-button only; 3D OrbitControls defaults (right-rotate, middle-pan).
- Approach-marker (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:1033) cursor flips to `grabbing` only on pointerdown — hover gives no draggable cue.
- 2D zoom clamp (0.05..80, EntityCanvas2D.svelte:554) silently swallows further wheel input — no flash/nudge feedback.
- PlaybackBar.svelte: no spacebar play/pause (`togglePlay` only on click).
- No keyboard fit-to-view (F/Home/numpad-`.`) despite Scene3D.svelte:1777 comment mentioning a planned shortcut.
close_reason: Three highest-impact items landed: spacebar play/pause, 3D empty state, 2D stock outline. Selection color audit-finding was misread (contrast-over-stock uses edgeColor, not accent). Remaining feature-shaped affordances tracked in followup.

title: Keyboard nav missing in menubar dropdowns, OpKindPicker, OperationsList, font picker, theme picker, tablists
description:
Multiple `role="menu"`, `role="listbox"`, `role="tablist"`, `role="group"` widgets lack arrow-key navigation and roving tabindex:
- App.svelte:816-1033 File/Edit/View/Tools/Help dropdowns — no arrow-key between items, no autofocus on open, no `aria-controls` to bind trigger to dropdown.
- App.svelte:1133-1151 2D/3D tablist — no arrow-key, no `tabindex="-1"` on inactive tab, no `aria-controls`, no `role="tabpanel"` on the panes.
- OpKindPicker.svelte:131-145 `role="menu"` no arrow-key; reused in canvas ctx menu (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:2077) and OperationsList `+`.
- OperationsList.svelte:271-295 `role="listbox"` with every option `tabindex="0"` (vs roving), no arrow-key, no `aria-activedescendant`. :232 header has `role="button" tabindex="0"` AND contains real `<button>` children — nested interactive.
- EntityCanvas2D.svelte:2065-2075 ctx menu — no focus on open, no arrow-key.
- AddTextDialog.svelte:378-422 custom font dropdown — no `aria-activedescendant`, no arrow-key, no Esc-close-listbox-only.
- LayerList.svelte:156-194 "+ Add" disclosure — no ESC, no autofocus, no arrow-key.
- SettingsDialog.svelte:46-64 theme picker `role="group"` should be `role="radiogroup"` with `role="radio" aria-checked`.
- GcodePanel.svelte:156-167 every line `tabindex="-1"` — panel completely unreachable by keyboard.
- OperationsList.svelte:298-305 drag-grip `aria-hidden="true"` with no keyboard reorder equivalent.
close_reason: High-impact keyboard nav landed (menubar dropdowns, 2D/3D tablist, theme radiogroup, GcodePanel listbox, OpKindPicker, PlaybackBar slider). Remaining minor pickers tracked in followup.

title: Hit-targets too small: Splitter (4px), per-row del/eye/caret buttons (~16-20px)
description:
WCAG recommends ≥24×24px hit targets.
- Splitter.svelte:82 `width: 4px` — precise mouse only; hostile on touch/trackpad. Widen the HIT area to ~10-12px via a transparent `::before` while keeping the visible band at 2px.
- LayerList.svelte:710 `.del-btn` + per-row visibility icons, TextList.svelte:412 `.del-btn`, OperationsList.svelte:562 dup/del — all roughly `padding: 0 0.3rem` on a ~16-20px glyph.
- Splitter also lacks keyboard support: `role="separator"` with no `tabindex`, no arrow-key adjust handler. Add `tabindex="0"` + onkeydown for ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down/Home/End.
close_reason: Closed

title: Responsive layout: AboutDialog fixed 640px, MachineDialog no width prop, PlaybackBar no flex-wrap, nested vh caps, dropdown label cap, op-properties label col
description:
Layout papercuts at narrow widths:
- AboutDialog.svelte:134 `width="640px"` not responsive; should be `min(640px, 95vw)`.
- MachineDialog.svelte:231 passes no `width` to Modal — 2-col grid (:871) never collapses at narrow viewports.
- PlaybackBar.svelte:275-284 `.bar` lacks `flex-wrap` — slider crushed below ~520px.
- LayerList.svelte:548 `max-height: 28vh` + TextList.svelte:353 `max-height: 38vh` — inner cap inside the accordion creates a nested second scrollbar, wastes vertical space on tall windows. The sidebar grid already owns scrolling via `minmax(0, 1fr)`.
- App.svelte:1459 `.dropdown .label max-width: 280px` (hard px) — long file names truncate even on wide screens.
- StockPanel.svelte:181-194 + AddTextDialog.svelte:561 grid `1fr 1fr` without `minmax(0, 1fr)` — unit suffixes clip at narrow sidebar.
- op-properties.css:39 label col fixed at 6.5rem combined with OpPropertiesPanel.svelte:982 + :990 padding leaves ≤60px for value column at sidebar=240px (App.svelte:688 min).
- ShortcutHelp.svelte:83 `height: 100%` on `.shortcut-grid` is a no-op (Modal has only max-height).
- ToolLibraryDialog.svelte:1487-1489 13-column fr-based grid — body has `overflow: auto` (:1478) but fr columns can't horizontal-scroll, just squash; consider switching mins to fixed `auto`-sized columns so the table actually scrolls.
- GenerateBar.svelte:682 `.stale-chip .stale-msg max-width: 24ch` truncates filename messages without recovery (no title attr).

title: Panel sizes don't re-clamp on window resize; GCODE_DEFAULT computed once at module init
description:
App.svelte never listens for `resize`:
- App.svelte:676 `const GCODE_DEFAULT = Math.round(window.innerHeight * 0.35)` runs once at module load. Open the app at 1080p, drag window to 600px tall: gcode panel stays at ~378px (now > 60% of viewport).

- sidebarWidth clamps to 240..720 absolute pixels regardless of `window.innerWidth`. 720px sidebar on 800px window leaves 80px for canvas.

Fix: install a single `window.addEventListener('resize', persistOrClampOnResize)` that re-runs both clamps + reactive `GCODE_DEFAULT`.

title: Numeric input validation papercuts: silent parseFloat(x)||0, mismatched HTML/JS guards, mixed oninput/onchange
description:
Pervasive `parseFloat(v) || 0` and `parseInt(v) || 1` fall-to-default coercion across input handlers — typing "abc" silently changes a depth/width/diameter to 0 with no visual rejection. ToolLibraryDialog already established the `.invalid` red-border pattern (e.g. diameter/speed/feed); apply it everywhere else.

Specific sites:
- OpPropertiesPanel.svelte:399-403 finalDepth, :416 startDepth, :572-585 throughDepth (rejected values silently snap back).
- StockPanel.svelte:65-67/83-85/98-100/113-115/132-134/145-147/159-160 every numeric input.
- TabsSection.svelte:117-128 tab count `|| 1`, :163-166 width `> 0` swallowed, :178-181 height same.
- ToolLibraryDialog.svelte:546-560 diameter accepts 0.005 (below HTML `min="0.01"`) without `.invalid`; :594-604 tip ∠ accepts 0/negative; :609-621 flutes `|| 1`.
- MachineDialog.svelte:308-310 Fast-move Z (no min, no suffix), :556-593 acceleration `|| 250` silent reset, :739-776 parkXy pair drops both on partial clear.
- SettingsDialog.svelte:208 cell size has no `max` (typing 100 mm wrecks sim); :209-222 vs the rest of the app mixes `oninput` (commit on keystroke) vs `onchange` (commit on blur).

- OpPropertiesPanel.svelte:861-872 feed step=50 vs :887-900 plunge step=10 for same unit mm/min.
close_reason: Worst silent-coercion + range-mismatch papercuts fixed (StockPanel, OpPropertiesPanel depth fields, ToolLibraryDialog diameter floor, PocketSection v-bottom angle, PostProcessorEditor scale, SettingsDialog cell size max). Remaining minor consistency tweaks tracked in followup.

title: audit 2026-05-23: Drag-knife op doesn't auto-disable multi-pass Z without plot_mode_z global (per-op mode unused)
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:764 (only plot_mode_z bypasses multi_pass); setup_resolver.rs:340 (setup.machine.mode = Drag set per-op for DragKnife but nothing downstream gates on it)
REPRO: User creates Drag mill on hobby Shapeoko (MachineConfig.mode=Mill, plot_mode_z=false). DragKnife op with depth=-1.5, step=-0.5. Multi_pass runs three Z passes; knife 'cuts' three times at increasingly negative Z. On real knife (locked at one Z), means three cuts at same physical Z (bottoms out), but Z-axis adds wear.
CONSEQUENCE: Wasted cycle time + Z-axis wear on hobby drag-knife setups. Output looks like normal milling program even though mode is Drag.
FIX: In multi_pass, add 'if setup.machine.mode == MachineMode::Drag { collapse to one pass at setup.mill.depth }' mirroring plot_mode_z branch.

CONSEQUENCE: Plasma unsupported as first-class mode. Users hand-tune G-code post-pipeline.
FIX: Add MachineMode::Plasma + tool fields pierce_height_mm, cut_height_mm, pierce_delay_sec. Emit two-step Z move at lead-in (rapid to pierce_height, dwell, G1 to cut_height) + kerf-comp via existing dragoff machinery.

title: audit 2026-05-23: drag-knife swivel emitted unconditionally on every line corner — bloats output, stresses pivot

CONSEQUENCE: 64x more output lines than needed, slower run time, blade pivot wear. Real drag knives self-align below ~30° via trailing offset.
FIX: Compute diff angle (already done at 251-257) and skip swivel + linear when |diff| < ~30° (tunable via tool config).

title: audit 2026-05-23: VCarve/Thread/Halfpipe drivers emit toolchange envelope BEFORE checking output

REPRO: Project with two ops, op 2 is Thread whose source has no closed circles. Envelope fires (T2 M6 + G92 + M5 dwell + M3 dwell). run_thread_op emits thread_no_circles warning, returns Ok with no body. Output: full tool-swap overhead for op that did nothing.

title: audit 2026-05-23: FormProfile holder cutting_radius mismatches ToolProfile.radius() — false-positive collisions
description:

REPRO: FormProfile tool with segments [(0,1.0),(5,4.0)] (narrow tip, wide base). ToolProfile::radius() = 4.0 (max). HolderProfile.cutting_radius() = points[0].1 = tool.diameter*0.5. If tool.diameter=2 (tip dia, not max), holder.cutting_radius()=1.0 but sweep treats 4.0 as cutting cross-section.

title: audit 2026-05-23: pocket_cascade first ring under-clears islands when xy_step < tool_radius (high overlap)

title: toolchange envelope: coolant_off before M5 + coolant_on after first cut
description: The toolchange safety envelope (added for bd eaeq/m8sq/rwv8/rfow in commit a877969) does not yet stop coolant before M5 / restart it after M3. The bd-rfow ticket flagged this: 'no coolant_off, ... emit_polylines_block does lift to fast_move_z at end of block, but a multi-op program never spindle_off's between ops' — the fix landed the spindle envelope but coolant stays on through the change. Add coolant_off to the envelope (before M5) and let the next emit_polylines_block re-emit coolant_flood/coolant_mist lazily for the new tool's coolant config. Touch: crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs (emit_toolchange_envelope helper).
close_reason: Closed

title: [BUG] sim: FormProfile cutter falls back to flat Endmill — needs user-supplied profile geometry + UI
description: Tracked in 3oly: ToolKind::FormProfile collapses to ToolProfile::Endmill at head diameter with a debug-only eprintln; no UI to enter profile geometry. Follow-up to wiaconstructor-3oly. Higher impact — undercut form tools (bull-nose / cove / ogee / dovetail / custom) carve the wrong cross-section in the sim until this lands.
close_reason: FormProfile cutters carry a user-entered (z,r) cross-section: new ToolEntry.form_profile_mm fed into ToolProfile::from_tool (real sample list when >=2 samples, taper fallback otherwise) + tool-library editor with a dovetail generator and editable sample table. Schema/codegen regenerated. Unblocks b7qz.

title: [BUG] sim: Compression cutter collapses to Endmill — up-cut/down-cut split affects edge quality not modelled
description: Tracked in 3oly: Compression collapses to ToolProfile::Endmill. The up-cut / down-cut flute split affects edge quality on both sheet faces; the sim doesn't model the per-half cut direction. Follow-up to wiaconstructor-3oly. Low impact for v1 (heightmap cross-section is the same flat-bottom shape), so deferred.
close_reason: A compression cutter's carved cross-section is correctly an endmill (2.5D heightmap can't show surface finish), so modeled the real failure mode as a planning warning instead: compression_transition_above_cut fires when the up/down-cut transition is taller than the engaged cut depth (whole cut is up-cut → top face frays). Consumes the previously-dead compression_transition_mm field; folded into hash_tool (PIPELINE_VERSION 38→39, stable hash re-pinned). 690 wiac-core lib tests + snapshots pass, clippy clean.

title: vcarve: chain-to-chain G1 plunge from fast_z to start_depth ignores lead-in angle
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:331-348 `emit_vcarve_block`.

**Problem:** Between V-carve polylines the post sequence is G0→fast_z → G0→XY → G1→start_depth at rate_v → G1 polyline. For default V-carve projects `start_depth = 0` so the G1 lands at top-of-stock (harmless). But when `start_depth < 0` (multi-pass V-carve, or user-staged carve depth), this G1 is a vertical plunge of the V-bit into uncarved material — same failure mode as pmpk but at a different code path.

**pmpk fix scope:** pmpk fixes only the per-chain ratchet entry by ramping from z=0 in `ratchet_emit`. It does NOT extend the lead-in over the pre-polyline G1 plunge from `fast_z` to `start_depth`. Multi-pass workflows are still exposed.

**Proposed fix:** Replace the per-chain G1 plunge with an angled lead-in that crosses XY along the chain's first `lead_in_len` mm. Could be done in `emit_vcarve_block` by skipping the G1 plunge entirely and letting `ratchet_emit` handle the descent — but `ratchet_emit` currently starts at z=0, not at `start_depth`. Decide whether to (a) re-anchor the ramp at `start_depth`, or (b) keep the current behavior but document that `start_depth < 0` is unsafe for V-carve.

**Discovered from:** wiaconstructor-pmpk follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Per-chain G1 plunge from fast_z to start_depth no longer occurs (or is replaced by an angled ramp) when start_depth < 0. Test: multi-pass V-carve project with start_depth=-1 has no vertical-only G1 plunge segment.
close_reason: Fixed and committed on main; full wiac-core + wiac-wasm test suites green, clippy clean. mg77: catch_unwind guard on sim advance/partial_advance. n3hn: clamp vcarve pre-polyline plunge to max(start_depth, entry_z). liyy: target_speed param so finish-pass toolchange envelope spins up at finish RPM.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-hpgl-no-feed: feedrate is dropped, no plotter velocity (VS) emitted; drag-knife runs at boot default
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/hpgl.rs:39 (`fn feedrate(&mut self, _rate: u32) {}`).

**Problem:** HPGL has the `VS<speed>` command (velocity-select, cm/s) for setting the pen/knife traverse speed. The post's `feedrate` is a no-op, so the plotter or drag-knife runs at its boot-default velocity regardless of the user's tool.rate_h setting.

For a pen plotter this is mostly cosmetic (the user gets a default plot speed). For a DRAG KNIFE this is significant: the cut speed affects the kerf width on flexible materials (vinyl, gasket paper), the corner trail, and the maximum allowable feed for thick stock. Setting the same feedrate as you'd send to a milling machine produces a slow, thick cut on a drag knife.

Also: `PA` (plot absolute) commands take an optional velocity scaling — those are unused.

**Worked example:** drag-knife at user-configured 600 mm/min on vinyl:
- HPGL output today: no VS, no speed control. Cutter runs at the plotter's boot velocity (typically 200–400 mm/s for pen plotters, but for cutters often configured 100 mm/s on power-up).
- Expected: `VS<v>` where v = rate_h * (cm/min → cm/s) conversion. For 600 mm/min: 1 cm/s. Append `VS1;` after `IN;SP1;` and again whenever rate changes.

**Acceptance:** `feedrate` emits VS<v> where v = mm_per_min / 600 (mm/min → cm/s). Suppress repeats. Test hpgl_emits_vs_for_feedrate covers.
acceptance_criteria: HPGL output includes VS<v>; per change. Test verifies.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-leadin-no-fit-check: arc lead-in doesn't validate that the arc fits in the available room near the contour start
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/leads.rs:147-225 (`lead_in_geometry` / `lead_out_geometry`).

**Problem:** The arc lead-in is laid out as a quarter-circle of radius `in_lenght` mm on the FREE side of the contour tangent. The center sits at `(P0 + perp_free * radius)` and the arc starts at `(P0 + radius*(perp_free - tangent))`.

There's no check that this arc actually fits in free space. For:
- A small Outside profile (e.g. cutting a small island), the lead-in arc may swing INTO the next stock piece, gouging.
- A pocket whose corner has insufficient room for the lead-in radius, the arc swings into the wall.
- A profile near another already-cut feature, the arc cuts into the prior cut.

The current code just trusts the user to pick `in_lenght` small enough.

Worse, the arc is also emitted at the FINAL pass depth via lead_out for the cutter exit. If the cut depth is below the surface, the lead-out arc is below stock surface — running through what was solid material BEFORE the cut. If the lead-out radius is large enough to leave the cut envelope, the arc goes through uncut material at full depth.

**Worked example:** Outside profile of a 5 mm-square island, lead in_lenght = 3 mm:
- Lead-in arc radius = 3 mm, center 3 mm to the LEFT of the first vertex (in free space).
- The arc center is INSIDE the adjacent piece (if the user has two islands cut from the same stock, the arc cuts into the neighbor).

**Acceptance:** validate the lead arc footprint against (a) other PolylineOffsets within reach, (b) the stock boundary, (c) tabs near the start. When the arc collides, emit a warning AND fall back to LeadKind::Straight (or LeadKind::Off if straight also collides). Test gcode_leadin_falls_back_when_no_room covers.
acceptance_criteria: Lead-in arc is checked against other offsets / stock; on collision, falls back to straight or off with a pipeline warning.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: HolderProfile assumes holder sits directly on flute top — no shank length between flutes and holder
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/holder.rs:38-54 (HolderProfile::from_tool).

**Problem:** The profile is built as `(0, cutting_r), (flute_len, cutting_r), (flute_len, shank_r), (flute_len, holder_bottom_r), ...`. The holder is placed **on top of the flutes** with no axial gap. Real toolholding has a finite distance between flute-top and holder-bottom (the cutter's shank stick-out, controlled by how far the bit was inserted into the collet). On an ER collet, stick-out is typically 25–35 mm beyond the collet face for a 6 mm endmill. The sim treats this as zero.

The comment on holder.rs:54-58 acknowledges this: 'no explicit shank length on the tool entry today'. The result: walls deep enough that the holder *would* clear with proper stick-out get flagged because the sim positions the holder at the wrong Z.

**Real-world impact:** Holder-collision false positives on deep cuts where the bit was set deep into the collet (correctly extending the reach). User reduces depth-of-cut to silence the warning, runs slower than necessary, or shortens the toolpath unnecessarily.

**Acceptance:** ToolEntry gains `stickout_length_mm` (distance from collet face / holder bottom to the FLUTE TOP, exclusive of flutes). HolderProfile inserts a shank segment of (flute_len, shank_r) -> (flute_len + stickout, shank_r) -> (flute_len + stickout, holder_bottom_r). UI exposes the field. Test `holder_stickout_lifts_holder_above_walls_inside` covers it.
acceptance_criteria: ToolEntry.stickout_length_mm field exists; HolderProfile uses it to space the holder above the flute top.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P2 sim commits on main (lower_at_or_record: 20a58e1, full P2 cluster: c3f6680). 516 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-arc-fit-direction-flip: direction_ccw uses LAST chord only, missing mid-run flips at noisy inputs
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/arc_fit.rs:134-136 (greedy_fit_from).

**Problem:** The direction-stability check inside the greedy loop is:
```rust
let new_ccw = direction_ccw(nc, p0, points[j - 1]);
if new_ccw != ccw { break; }
```
which tests the direction implied by (p0 → points[j-1]) around the NEW center nc. That captures "the last edge agrees with the established orientation" but it doesn't detect a flip in the MIDDLE of the candidate run. For inputs with small noise (typical DXF tolerance) a polyline that's almost-but-not-quite a single arc can have one intermediate point on the WRONG side of the chord — the per-point sagitta check passes (radial distance within tolerance), but the orientation as you'd traverse the run zigzags slightly.
