When the fitter then accepts the run as a single arc, the controller sweeps a smooth curve that's nominally within tolerance of every point — but the actual TRAJECTORY may cut through a point that was on the OTHER side of the chord, so on noisy convex/concave-mixed inputs the cutter visits an XY ~tolerance off from the polyline at a mid-arc point.

This is mostly fine when tolerance is tight (0.01 mm). It becomes visible when tolerance is loose (0.1 mm and a wiggly chord chain): the cut path can deviate from the polyline by significantly more than tolerance because the arc smooths over a bump that the original polyline went around.

**Acceptance:** the direction check should run on EVERY new point, not just j-1. For each pair (points[j-1], points[j]), verify direction_ccw(nc, points[j-1], points[j]) == ccw. Test arc_fit_rejects_mid_run_direction_flip covers.
acceptance_criteria: A polyline with one inward bump (point on the inside of the chord by tolerance) fits to ≥2 arcs, not 1.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: no warning when feed_rate / plunge_rate / RPM are zero — silently emits F0 / S0
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/setup_resolver.rs:113-167 and crates/wiac-core/src/project/mod.rs (resolve_tool_rates fallback chain).

**Problem:** ToolEntry carries u32 fields for speed, plunge_rate, feed_rate (and *_finish, *_drill variants). u32 = 0 is a legal value. resolve_tool_rates passes 0 through; per-op override (op.params.feed_rate_override, plunge_rate_override) takes priority but those are Option<u32> — None falls back to tool's value. The result: a tool entry with feed_rate=0 silently produces an emitted F0 / M3 S0 — the spindle stays off, the cutter sits at depth with no feed.

setup_resolver doesn't validate. No 'feed_rate_zero' / 'spindle_speed_zero' warning is pushed. Compare with step_unspecified which IS warned (effective_step in pipeline.rs:793-803).

**User-visible failure:** Tool with one missing field -> the program runs silently. The cutter dives, stops, and the user wonders why nothing's cutting.
acceptance_criteria: setup_resolver emits a PipelineWarning (kind='feed_rate_zero' / 'plunge_rate_zero' / 'speed_zero') for every op whose RESOLVED feed/plunge/speed is 0, naming the offending pass (rough/finish/drill). gcode is still emitted (don't break working projects that intentionally set 0 for laser-mode? — actually laser mode might want speed=0; gate the warning on machine.mode != Laser).
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8ea3276 (P2 audit 2026-05-22 batch).

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-post-profile-axes-arc: I/J use AxesConfig X/Y mapping but emit literal 'I'/'J' letter when renamed
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/linuxcnc.rs:332-358 (`arc_cw` / `arc_ccw`); axis_for at line 126.

**Problem:** When a PostProfile renames axes (e.g. X→A for a rotary-Z setup, or Z→B for a milling-head with B as the swing axis), the per-axis renaming applies to X/Y/Z coordinates but the I/J center offsets are renamed via axis_for('I') / axis_for('J') which look up AxesConfig.i / .j independently.

So a profile that renames X to A and Y to B has TWO independent settings for I/J: if the user updates X.name='A' but forgets to also update I.name='A' (or vice versa), the post emits `A<x> B<y> I<i> J<j>` — a contradiction: I/J are by definition deltas in the X/Y plane, so when X is renamed to A, the arc center must be relative to A/B not I/J.

This is a footgun in the PostProfile spec: AxesConfig should derive I/J from X/Y (rename and scale follow the X/Y axes by construction) OR the profile validator must enforce that I.name matches X.name and J.name matches Y.name.

**Worked example:** profile with axes.x.name="A", axes.y.name="B", axes.i.name="I" (default), axes.j.name="J" (default), default scale.
- emit a G2 arc from (0, 0) center (5, 0): `G2 A10 B0 I5 J0`
- The controller reads A and B as separate (rotary?) axes, and I/J as XY-plane center offsets — but there's no XY arc in this kinematic context, so the controller behavior is undefined.

Also: scale on I/J is applied independently of X/Y scale. If the user scales X by -1 (flip), they must remember to scale I by -1 too — otherwise the arc center is on the wrong side. Probably worth deriving I/J formatting from X/Y at config-validation time.

**Acceptance:** AxesConfig validation: I.name and J.name must equal X.name and Y.name when the user customizes axes; I.scale and J.scale must equal X.scale and Y.scale. OR I/J formatting is computed from X/Y at render time, not separately stored. Test post_profile_arc_center_letters_match_xy covers.
acceptance_criteria: A profile that renames X but not I emits I/J using the renamed letter, OR the profile fails to validate at load with a clear error message.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: nested closed contours not auto-detected as donut/annular region under OpSource::All
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/offset_builder.rs:340-413 (Pocket containment-aware loop) and crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/regions.rs:49-58 (build_region_previews).

**Problem:** When an op uses OpSource::All on a project with one outer rectangle + one inner circle (geometrically nested), the containment-aware Pocket loop builds an annular pocket correctly via the inner_objects/outer_objects list — but only when pocket_islands flag is true OR when the inner object is explicitly in selected_set. The legacy comment in offset_builder.rs:373-393 says: 'pocket_islands ON + source=All -> include ALL nested closed children as islands.' So a user with pocket_islands=false + source=All gets a SOLID pocket cut through the inner circle (treating it as an open path, not a hole). That's surprising: most users intuitively expect that two nested closed contours selected as one Pocket mean 'donut'.

The audit prompt explicitly asked: 'Are nested closed contours (donuts) detected as a single annular region by default?' — Today the answer is no, only when pocket_islands is explicitly enabled.

**User-visible failure:** Author a frame plate with a center hole, drop a Pocket op with default settings -> the gcode pockets across the center hole (clear-through cut). User has to know to flip pocket_islands. The region-preview also won't show the hole.
acceptance_criteria: Either flip pocket_islands default to true (and add a 'solid_pocket' bool for the rare 'I really want to mill THROUGH the inner closed contour' case), OR auto-detect: when ALL inner_objects are closed and source=All, treat them as islands by default. Update build_region_previews to mirror. Tests cover: (a) two nested closed contours with default Pocket op cuts a donut by default; (b) flipping pocket_islands=false (or solid_pocket=true) restores the legacy solid-cut behavior.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: resolve_op_segments for OpSource::Objects skips ids not in current objects list — silent under pattern expansion
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/selection.rs:27-46 and crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline_cache.rs:188-191 (segments folded into cache key).

**Problem:** resolve_op_segments for OpSource::Objects { ids } walks 1-based ids and silently skips ids that fall outside the current `objects` set. The header comment acknowledges this and links it to pattern expansion replacing the chain. The implication: when a prior op's pattern expansion would have grown the objects set, the cache key for a downstream op pointing at object-id N would either hit (N exists in expanded set) or silently empty out (N out of range). Today's pipeline never propagates pattern-expanded objects to downstream ops (each op gets the original objects slice — confirmed at offset_builder.rs:108-148 where pattern_expanded lives only inside build_op_offsets), so this is moot in production.

The cache hashes the RESOLVED segments. With `segments_to_objects` deterministic, the resolved order is deterministic. Caching is correct.

The latent concern: if an op references an Object id that was deleted from the project, the segment list silently empties → cache key changes, the op produces zero offsets, NO warning is raised. The user sees a silently-missing op.

**User-visible failure:** Delete an imported object that's referenced by an Op (via id) -> the op silently produces nothing. No 'op_source_missing' warning.
acceptance_criteria: resolve_op_segments or ordered_selection pushes a 'op_source_missing' warning when one or more selected ids resolve to no object in the current set. Test: an op selecting id=99 against a 3-object import emits the warning.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8ea3276 (P2 audit 2026-05-22 batch).

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-program-end: no return-to-machine-home or safe XY before M5/M30
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:456-464 (`program_end`).

**Problem:** Program-end emits only a Z lift to `fast_move_z`, spindle_off, coolant_off, then the post-specific footer (M30/M2). The cutter is parked at WHATEVER (x, y) the last operation finished at, with the spindle still spinning down (no dwell after M5). The operator typically wants the cutter to be at a known safe park position (e.g. far X, near Y for tool-change access, or G53 absolute machine home).

Specifically missing:
- No XY move to a 'home' or 'tool change' position. Lifted to Z but parked over the part — when the operator goes to load the next part, the cutter dangles in the workspace.
- No G53 G0 X<home> Y<home> rapid (LinuxCNC standard for 'go home').
- No M9 if coolant was off-by-default (no leak there).

LinuxCNC convention: `G0 Z[#5422 + 5]` (above the work top), then `G53 G0 Z0` (machine Z home), then `G53 G0 X<safe> Y<safe>`, M5, M30. Mach3 / GRBL use simpler 'park at end' macros.

**Worked example:** a 4-op job ending with a finish pass at (200, 100) on a 300×200 stock:
- Wiac emits: `G0 Z5\nM5\nM30` — spindle stops while still over the workpiece at (200, 100).
- Operator removes the part with the cutter 5 mm above its center — collision-prone.

**Acceptance:** add a configurable `MachineConfig.park_position: Option<(f64, f64)>` that program_end honors with a final `G0 X<px> Y<py>` rapid after the Z lift. Default is None (current behavior); when set, the post emits the park rapid. (For now this is config-only; eventually the post should also emit G53 G0 Z home for LinuxCNC.)
acceptance_criteria: MachineConfig has a park_position; when set, program_end emits a final XY rapid before M5. New test gcode_parks_at_configured_xy covers.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: rapid_check returns 'worst' cell with smallest excess, not the most-violated cell
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/rapid_check.rs:53-60.

**Problem:** Looking at the math: `excess = cell_z - cutter_surface_z` (positive means cell sticks above the cutter surface). The match `Some((best, _, _, _)) if excess <= best => {}` **rejects** new candidates whose excess is less-than-or-equal — i.e. it KEEPS the minimum, not the maximum. The condition reads as 'keep the smallest excess', so the worst cell reported is the one barely-colliding, not the one most deeply colliding.

For a rapid that grazes the top of a wall (excess 0.01mm) AND slams through a tower (excess 20mm), the warning's worst_cell_z reports the 0.01mm graze location. The user sees a 'small' problem and may dismiss it, missing the catastrophic one.

**Real-world impact:** User dismisses 'minor' rapid-collision warnings because the reported worst cell looks shallow. The actual worst case is hidden in the same warning's metadata; the warning's text (e.g. 'rapid through material at z=-0.01') under-states severity.

**Acceptance:** Flip the condition to `if excess >= best` so worst tracks the most-violated cell. Test `rapid_through_two_walls_reports_taller_wall` covers it.
acceptance_criteria: rapid_check.worst reports the maximum-excess cell. Test passes for a rapid hitting two walls of different heights.
close_reason: Self-audit error — the condition 'if excess <= best => {}' is the SKIP branch (do nothing when new is not larger), so the update runs only when excess > best. worst correctly tracks the MAX excess. Closing as invalid.

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: header_setup_for picks first enabled op's tool — wrong if it's also a Pause op or program starts on a different tool
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/setup_resolver.rs:386-477 (header_setup_for) and crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs:570-579.

**Problem 1:** header_setup_for(project) finds 'the first enabled op' (project.operations.iter().find(|o| o.enabled)). It uses op.tool_id without checking op.kind. OpKind::Pause carries an arbitrary tool_id (the project's default) since the Pause variant doesn't actually run a tool — yet the header would emit feed/speed/tool from THAT phantom tool_id. If the first enabled op is a Pause, the program-header rates are nonsense (the Pause op never actually runs a spindle).

**Problem 2:** Even for non-Pause first ops, the header emits ONE feed/speed and then no further toolchange between ops (see wiaconstructor-k2ew). If the user reorders ops so the new first op uses a different tool, every cached gcode body downstream still wants the original RPM (which post.spindle_cw remembers via last_speed), but the header now claims a different starting speed. The cache invalidation correctly bumps for each affected op (their hashes change), but the PROGRAM HEADER itself isn't cached and re-derives on every run — so this is consistent.

**Problem 3:** The rt1.30 z_shift application in pipeline.rs:573-579 picks 'first.tool_id' verbatim and applies its z_shift_mm. Same Pause-op caveat: a Pause first-enabled op carries a tool_id whose z_shift would be applied at program_begin.

**User-visible failure:** Program-header feed and Z shift come from a Pause op's bogus tool reference when Pause is the first enabled op. Minor today (Pause is uncommon as the first op) but a footgun.
acceptance_criteria: header_setup_for and the z_shift block in run_per_op skip Pause ops when picking the 'first enabled' op; both look for the first NON-Pause enabled op. If every enabled op is a Pause (degenerate), fall back to project.tools.first() as today. Test: a Pause-first project's header uses the second op's tool rates.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8ea3276 (P2 audit 2026-05-22 batch).

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: holder check picks single worst cell, hides all other collision cells from the warning stream
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/holder_check.rs:147-150 (Match worst, single-warning emission at sim/sweep.rs:155-171).

**Problem:** `check_segment_holder_against_walls` tracks a single `worst` cell per segment — the cell with the largest `required_clearance_mm`. If a single segment passes through two distinct wall geometries (e.g. between two clamping bosses), only the deeper one is reported. The user sees one HolderCollision warning, fixes that one issue, re-runs, and now the *other* boss shows up.

This is a UX-as-correctness issue: the user trusts that 'no warnings = no problems' and that 'X warnings = X distinct problems'. Hiding additional collisions behind a 'worst-only' filter teaches the user that warnings are partial — and once they learn that, they stop trusting the empty list.

**Real-world impact:** Iterative debugging. User runs sim, fixes one collision, re-runs, finds another. Three-collision setups take three sim cycles instead of one. Worse: if the user dismisses a fixed warning and the second pops up at the same segment_idx, they may think the fix didn't take.

**Acceptance:** Emit one HolderCollision warning per **distinct cluster** of wall cells (clustering: cells within ~2*max_r are one cluster). Or: emit one per segment but the warning carries a `Vec<(x, y, clearance)>` of all colliding cells. Test `two_clamping_bosses_emit_two_collisions` covers it.
acceptance_criteria: Multiple distinct wall clusters per segment produce multiple HolderCollision warnings (or one warning with a vec of cluster contacts).
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P2 sim commits on main (lower_at_or_record: 20a58e1, full P2 cluster: c3f6680). 516 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-grbl-comments: setup.machine.comments leaks paren comments via raw() and templates
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/grbl.rs:31-36 (`comment` rewrites to `;`) BUT `raw(cmd)` passes the string through verbatim. `crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/linuxcnc.rs:182-194` (template program_start) — if a user supplies a paren-style template, GRBL's inner.program_start writes it as-is.

**Problem:** GRBL 1.1 supports both paren `(...)` and semicolon `;...` comments per the spec — the file's header note "GRBL strips parentheses-wrapped comments" is outdated. So the conversion in `comment()` is defensive but harmless. The actual hole is:

1. `raw(cmd)` doesn't transform — the dual_tool driver emits `post.raw(format!("; toolchange: ..."))` which is fine, but `emit_offset`'s `post.comment(...)` does go through the override, while any direct `raw("(some paren comment)")` from a future caller wouldn't.

2. When the user attaches a custom PostProfile to GRBL (which delegates to `inner.program_start` etc.), template strings flow through verbatim — `linuxcnc_default()`'s built-in "(generated by wiaConstructor)" header is paren-style and GRBL gets it. Today `grbl_default()` ships its own "; ..." template, but the moment a user switches their profile to one that has parens in `program_start` (Mach3 etc.), GRBL emits parens.

GRBL 1.1+ accepts parens, so this is not a hard fail today, but pre-1.1 firmware (still common on cheap CNC machines from AliExpress) treats "(" as an unknown character and errors. The post claims to be GRBL-aware; it should defensively rewrite paren comments to semicolons in the GRBL path.

**Acceptance:** any line emitted by the GRBL post that starts with a literal "(" gets rewritten to "; " before write(). Or every paren-style comment path in inner LinuxCNC routes through a comment-format trait method that GRBL overrides. Test grbl_rewrites_paren_comments_from_templates exercises a profile whose program_start contains parens.
acceptance_criteria: Pasting Mach3's default profile onto GRBL produces a program with no paren-style comments. New test verifies.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: dual-tool toolchange skips spindle stop + safe retract before mid-op M6
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/op_drivers/dual_tool.rs:42-77 and crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/op_drivers/drill.rs:120-146.

**Problem:** Inside one Pocket op with finish_tool_id != tool_id, the dual-tool driver does (after the rough block):
1. `post.raw('; toolchange: finish pass ...')`
2. `post.tool(finish_setup.tool.number)` -> emits T<n> M6
3. Optional `post.tool_z_shift(shift)`
4. `emit_polylines_block(&finish_setup, ...)` — which calls spindle_cw on entry to the first cut.

There's no M5 / spindle_off, no coolant_off, no explicit retract above fast_move_z before the M6. The rough block's tail did 'lift back to safe Z = fast_move_z' (gcode.rs:425) but the spindle is still running. On any controller with an automatic toolchanger, this is a crash risk. Same gap in drill.rs's Stufenfase toolchange. Sister of wiaconstructor-rfow.

**User-visible failure:** Dual-tool Pocket / Drill+Stufenfase programs spin the spindle through the tool exchange. Coolant stays on. ATC crash risk; on manual machines, operator confusion (the gcode never said 'stop and change').
acceptance_criteria: Both dual_tool.rs and drill.rs emit M5 + coolant_off + post.move_to(None, None, Some(machine.toolchange_z_or_max(fast_move_z))) BEFORE post.tool(...). After M6, re-enable coolant on first cut and honor the new tool's pause. Test: dual_tool gcode shows M5 ... T2 M6 ... M3 S<finish>.
close_reason: Superseded by P1 commit 003ff46 — emit_toolchange_envelope wraps every M6 site (inter-op in pipeline.rs:664, dual_tool rough->finish in op_drivers/dual_tool.rs:73, Stufenfase chamfer in drill.rs) with safe-Z + spindle_off + stop_dwell BEFORE the M6, then T<n> M6 + tool_z_shift + spindle_cw(new_rpm) + start_dwell. Verified by reading pipeline.rs:972-1080 and op_drivers/dual_tool.rs:46-80.

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: cell_size is auto-coarsened by maxSimulationCells but no warning emitted — quietly hides tool-engagement issues
description:
**Where:** frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts:301-306 (effectiveCellSize doubled when grid exceeds maxSimulationCells).

**Problem:** When the user's stock + tool combo would produce a heightmap larger than `settings.maxSimulationCells`, the driver silently scales cell_size up by `sqrt(cellCount / cap)`. A 2mm endmill on a 600x400mm stock at 0.2mm/cell = 6M cells; cap = 1M → effective cell = 0.49mm. The 0.5mm-wide tool engagement near a wall (or a 0.3mm tab) becomes invisible at 0.49mm cells.

This affects every downstream check that reads the heightmap: holder-vs-wall (will miss thin walls < cell), engagement metering, rapid-through-stock. The user is given no signal that the sim accuracy was downgraded for performance, only the sim showing 'no warnings' on a setup that would warn at full resolution.

**Real-world impact:** User dials in tab settings (3mm tabs by default) on a large stock and the sim shows clean cuts. Coarse cells subsume tabs into the surrounding lowered region, and a holder collision with a tab goes undetected because the tab cell is sub-cell-size.

**Acceptance:** Driver surfaces `effectiveCellSize > requestedCellSize` as a SimWarning::CoarseningApplied (new variant, severity Info). UI shows a banner when the warning is set. New test on the wasm side asserts the warning is emitted.
acceptance_criteria: SimWarning::CoarseningApplied fires when driver scales the cell size. Banner shown to user with the from/to cell size.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P2 sim commits on main (lower_at_or_record: 20a58e1, full P2 cluster: c3f6680). 516 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: frame envelope is built from raw selection, ignoring tabs/leads/cut_direction-driven outward growth
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/frame.rs:33-67 and crates/wiac-core/src/cam/source_combine.rs (build_frame).

**Problem:** synthesize_pocket_outside_objects builds the frame from `frame_selection: Vec<&VcObject>` — the raw selected islands' geometry. The frame padding is clamped to >= tool_radius (good). But the envelope is the bbox/hull of the SOURCE islands, not the envelope of the islands + their lead-in/lead-out + tab regions. When a leads.in_lenght/out_lenght is set on the inner-island side of the difference, the cutter approach/retract can land OUTSIDE the frame's interior pocket if the frame is tight against the bbox. Result: the cutter enters into uncut stock that should be outside the frame, but the frame envelope didn't account for it. Same issue with outwards-projecting tabs.

For multi-island selection, build_frame must form the right outer envelope. The comment says it does (kbx5 step 2 + tool_radius clamp). Whether 'Rectangle' or 'RoundedRectangle' picks an actual hull or just an axis-aligned bbox isn't clear from the call site; the FrameShape enum suggests axis-aligned only, which is wrong for rotated islands (Polar pattern, sketches authored at an angle).

**User-visible failure:** Pocket-outside around a rotated/multi-island selection cuts a non-tight envelope, leaving uncut material on the long axis or — worse — overcutting into stock on the short axis.
acceptance_criteria: build_frame, with FrameShape::Rectangle, computes the tightest axis-aligned bbox of the WHOLE selection (incl. all islands); RoundedRectangle does the same with the user's corner radius. Document that the envelope is axis-aligned. Add a test covering a Polar-pattern source where the source extent at 45° exceeds the islands' bbox center-to-edge — the frame must include the rotated extents. Frame must also grow by leads.in_lenght/out_lenght when leads are active on the outer islands' side.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8ea3276 (P2 audit 2026-05-22 batch).

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: pipeline_cache hash_segment ignores per-segment metadata (group/source_id), text_layers not in op key
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline_cache.rs:244-264 (hash_segment) and crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs:380-396 (text rendering pre-pass).

**Problem 1:** hash_segment hashes only {kind, start, end, bulge, center, layer, color}. If Segment has any other fields (group_id, source_id, original_object_index, …) they don't participate. Check Segment struct for fields beyond these. If none, no issue — but the audit memory says the hash MUST cover EVERY field that affects output, and the rule needs reviewing against the current struct.

**Problem 2:** project.text_layers are NOT directly hashed into the op_cache_key. They flow through resolve_op_segments AFTER rendering — but the rendered segments only get hashed when they actually intersect the op's source selection. A text layer that an op references via OpSource::Layers gets its segments correctly hashed via resolve_op_segments because the renderer appends to project.segments before run_per_op runs. BUT: text_layers content (font, size, rotation, origin, content string) is hashed indirectly via the produced segments. If two TextLayer configs happen to produce byte-identical segments (extremely unlikely), they'd collide — acceptable. The real risk: text-render errors (PipelineError::TextRender) bypass caching entirely and the cache would NOT reflect a text re-render — but run_per_op runs the renderer EVERY generate, so the cache never serves stale text. Lower-risk than first scan suggests; still worth a comment.

**User-visible failure:** Hard to trigger today. Defensive change to prevent the next refactor from accidentally introducing stale-cache.
acceptance_criteria: Audit Segment struct for unhashed fields; if any present, hash them and bump PIPELINE_VERSION. Add a top-of-file comment in pipeline_cache.rs noting that text_layers flow into the key via resolve_op_segments, not via a direct text_layers hash.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8ea3276 (P2 audit 2026-05-22 batch).

title: audit 2026-05-22 tabs: short contour with N tabs places them inside each other's footprint
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/tabs.rs:178-189 auto_tab_ts + crate::pipeline::tabs::build_op_tabs_by_object. **Problem:** auto_tab_ts returns N evenly spaced parameters with no minimum arc-length check. A 5mm-perimeter closed contour with count=4 yields tabs at 0, 1.25mm, 2.5mm, 3.75mm — each tab's footprint (setup.tabs.width, default 10mm) is wider than the SPACING. emit_path_with_tabs merges overlapping intervals per segment but the cutter still lifts for an essentially continuous distance, defeating the purpose. **Real-world impact:** User dials in 'a few tabs to hold the part' on a small inset and finds the whole perimeter has lifted (no part separation) OR the merged intervals span multiple segments and gaps appear. **Acceptance:** auto_tab_ts (or its caller in pipeline/tabs.rs) clamps count downward when perimeter / count < 1.5 × tab_width, surfaces a PipelineWarning ('contour too short for N tabs; reduced to M'), and emits whatever count fits.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: ToolKind::Compression and FormProfile silently collapse to flat Endmill — non-uniform cross-sections invisible
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/heightmap.rs:329 (Compression | TSlot | FormProfile arm).

**Problem:** Compression bits (split up-cut bottom flutes + down-cut upper flutes) and FormProfile bits (user-defined arbitrary contour) both fall through to ToolProfile::Endmill { r }. This is a footnote behavior in the source comment, but the user has no signal that the simulated profile is wrong — the heightmap looks correct but only because the renderer drew a flat-bottom column. If a FormProfile tool is, say, a half-round bullnose for radius generation, the heightmap will show a flat-bottom cut when the actual cut is a radius.

**Real-world impact:** FormProfile and Compression operations look like flat-bottom endmill cuts in the sim. The user authors a custom-profile tool, runs the sim, sees a flat result, assumes their op is configured wrong, debugs the wrong layer. Compression specifically is fine (the floor IS flat — up-cut bottom flutes cut as an endmill); FormProfile is the actual problem.

**Acceptance:** FormProfile gains a tool-side polyline-of-(r, dz) field; ToolProfile::FormProfile { samples } evals piecewise-linearly. Compression keeps Endmill mapping but a comment explains why. Test `formprofile_radius_bit_carves_radius_not_flat` covers a hand-defined radius tool.
acceptance_criteria: FormProfile carves the user-defined cross-section. Compression mapping documented as intentional.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P2 sim commits on main (lower_at_or_record: 20a58e1, full P2 cluster: c3f6680). 516 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: pipeline_cache MachineConfig hash misses work_area, capabilities, name
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline_cache.rs:358-416 (hash_machine) vs crates/wiac-core/src/cam/setup.rs:430-523 (MachineConfig).

**Problem:** hash_machine writes: unit, mode, comments, arcs, supports_toolchange, arc_fit_tolerance_mm, decimal_separator, line_number_start, plot_mode_z, post_profile. It does NOT hash: work_area, capabilities, name. accel/jerk/toolchange_s/rapid_speed/use_kinematic_time_estimate are intentionally skipped (estimator-only) and have a regression test (estimator_only_machine_fields_do_not_change_key). work_area however IS planning-relevant: the audit comment in cam/setup.rs:466-471 says it 'drives the stock's auto-mode fallback when no geometry is imported (the stock then sizes to the work-area XY footprint), and surfaces as the soft-limit reference in future sim warnings'. capabilities affects which op-kinds the frontend allows but the backend pipeline doesn't read it — probably safe. `name` is informational.

The PIPELINE_VERSION = 27 has been held stable across several hash-impl additions (rt1.15, rt1.36, rt1.10, rt1.20, rt1.27, rt1.29 …). Each of those rolled in via discriminator bytes; bumping PIPELINE_VERSION is the cleaner check. Existing wiaconstructor-h3o flags 'no linter for hash-impl field completeness'.

**User-visible failure:** Changing machine.work_area on a stock=auto project does NOT invalidate the cache → the stock-footprint-derived pocket auto-fallback (if/when implemented per the comment) won't update. Today the failure surfaces only in transitive logic. Low impact NOW; medium impact as soon as the auto-stock path lands.
acceptance_criteria: hash_machine writes work_area (each axis); document why capabilities/name are skipped or hash them too. PIPELINE_VERSION = 28 with snapshot bumped.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 8ea3276 (P2 audit 2026-05-22 batch).

title: audit 2026-05-22 tabs: auto-tabs on closed contour place first tab at t=0 (segment-start vertex / corner)
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/tabs.rs:182-185 in fn auto_tab_ts (closed branch). **Problem:** For closed contours, auto_tab_ts returns (0..count).map(i / n) which puts the first tab at t=0 — exactly on the first polyline vertex. For a closed rectangle that vertex IS a 90° corner. Tab footprint then straddles two perpendicular segments; the per-segment intersection math (gcode/tabs.rs:108-131) computes a foot perpendicular to ONE segment only, so the tab is missed on one half and the cutter doesn't lift correctly across the corner. **Real-world impact:** Tabs placed on corners 'half-work' — the cutter lifts only on the segment whose foot detected the tab and slams sideways into residual material on the perpendicular leg. Frontend vertexAndMidpointTs honors this layout in the picker; users see the corner tab as a valid choice. **Acceptance:** Closed-contour auto_tab_ts offsets the first tab by 0.5/count (or by an arc-length distance equal to tab width / 2) so tabs land in the middle of an edge, not on a vertex. Round-trip / hash tests for serialized projects updated to match.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: ToolKind::Engraver mapped to VBit at full bit diameter — true engraver cutting edge is at tip_diameter only
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/heightmap.rs:287-300 (ToolKind::VBit | ToolKind::Engraver share the same arm).

**Problem:** A V-bit and an engraver have fundamentally different cutting geometry: a V-bit cuts along the full conical flank; an engraver (e.g. a 60° pyramid with a 0.1mm flat tip) cuts only at the very tip and the first fraction of mm above. The sim treats both as the same VBit profile — eval at r > tip_r returns positive depth-above-tip, meaning the sim assumes the side of the engraver is sharp/cutting. In reality the side is dead — material engaged at r > engaging_radius is rubbing, not cutting.

For depth-of-cut prediction (3D scoring on a finished surface), the engraver carve depth is bounded by its **engaged** depth at the engraving radius (typically very shallow), not by the full bit diameter. The sim will show a 6mm-diameter engraver carving a 6mm-wide V-groove at full depth, whereas real engraving cuts maybe 0.5mm wide.

**Real-world impact:** Engraver previews mis-show effective groove width. User selects an engraving feed/speed for what they see in the sim, but the real cut is much narrower. Off-by-10x material removal estimate and visual mismatch.

**Acceptance:** ToolKind::Engraver builds a VBit profile capped at `tool.engraving_max_diameter_mm` (new field, defaulting to ~1mm for engraver tools). Side flanks above that radius eval to None. New test `engraver_profile_caps_at_engaging_radius` covers it.
acceptance_criteria: Engraver profile differs from VBit at radii > engaging_max. Visual sim no longer carves the full bit diameter for engraving ops.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P2 sim commits on main (lower_at_or_record: 20a58e1, full P2 cluster: c3f6680). 516 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 tabs: Mixed mode appends manual placements without merging with auto positions
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/tabs.rs:70-74 in fn build_op_tabs_by_object. **Problem:** In Mixed mode, manual placements are appended verbatim to the auto-generated TabPoint list per object via .extend(v) — no deduplication, no minimum spacing check. A manual placement that lands within a few mm of an auto position (or on the same vertex) creates two overlapping tab footprints. Downstream emit_path_with_tabs merges overlapping intervals (gcode/tabs.rs:135-145) on the SAME segment, but if the two tabs straddle adjacent segments the merge logic doesn't apply and the cutter does two adjacent lifts. **Real-world impact:** User who Auto-spaces 4 tabs then nudges one in Mixed mode ends up with 5 tabs on the contour, two of them adjacent — wastes machining time and may leave a tab island too narrow to hold. Brief specifically called out 'mixed mode duplicate tabs' as an audit target. **Acceptance:** Mixed mode dedupes any manual placement whose t parameter is within (1.0 / auto_count) / 4 of an auto position on the same object. New test fixture: auto_count=4 (t=0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) plus manual at t=0.26 should produce 4 tabs, not 5.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 halfpipe: no tool-reach cap; ball-nose flute / shank-clearance not modeled
description:
Where: crates/wiac-core/src/cam/halfpipe.rs:40-70 + op_drivers/halfpipe.rs.

Problem: For HalfpipeProfile::CircularArc the depth formula z = -(R - sqrt(R^2 - r^2)) goes down to z = -R at the cap. There is no check that the ball-nose tool can physically reach -R: the flute length, shank diameter, and stickout from the collet are not consulted. For a 6mm ball-nose with 20mm flute length on a profile R=15, depth goes to -15mm — past the flute length — and the shank starts dragging in the slot.

vcarve_op handles this via tool_reach_r = tool.diameter * 0.5 (line 58 in op_drivers/vcarve.rs) folded into effective_r_cap. halfpipe has no equivalent.

Real-world impact: Ball-nose halfpipe with R > tool_flute_length scrapes the shank into the workpiece at the deepest point of the cut, producing a wider/deeper cut than designed and risking tool breakage.
acceptance_criteria: halfpipe_op computes tool_reach_z (= tool.flute_length or tool.diameter/2 if no flute length recorded) and caps |z| accordingly. Surfaces halfpipe_tool_reach_exceeded warning. Test: a halfpipe op with profile R=20 and a tool with 5mm flute clips Z to -5mm and emits the warning.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-arc-fit-half-pi: sweep cap at exactly π allows ambiguous-direction single-arc emission
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/arc_fit.rs:140 (`greedy_fit_from` cap: `arc_sweep(...) > π + 1e-9`).

**Problem:** The sweep cap is strictly greater than π, so a polyline run that fits exactly a 180° arc is emitted as a SINGLE G2/G3. When start, end, and center are colinear (sweep = π exactly, chord = diameter), the controller has no way to disambiguate which side of the chord the arc is on — the I/J vector points perpendicular to the chord, but two arcs satisfy that geometry. Different controllers handle this differently: LinuxCNC picks one based on the sign of I/J, Mach3 frequently picks the wrong one, GRBL is mostly fine but reportedly drops to chord at very high feeds, and older Smoothieware errors out.

The greedy fitter is also slightly over-eager because the inner direction-stability check (`direction_ccw(nc, p0, points[j-1]) != ccw`) loses precision near 180° — the cross product underflows and the orientation can flip due to FP error in the LAST point of the run, producing a 'success' that's actually on the wrong side of the chord.

**Worked example:** semicircle of radius 10 from (10, 0) → (-10, 0) tessellated into 30 chord points:
- Wiac emits: `G3 X-10 Y0 I-10 J0` — a single 180° arc. Center is at origin, but both an upper-half and lower-half arc satisfy 'CCW from (10,0) to (-10,0) around (0,0)'.
- Mach3 on this line: picks the lower-half arc roughly half the time. Cutter sweeps below the part instead of above. Gouge.
- Expected: split at ~90° (or any non-180° sweep) into two G3 arcs so each arc is unambiguous.

**Acceptance:** the cap is lowered to ~179° (say π - 0.05 rad), and the splitter falls back to two arcs when the candidate exceeds that. New test arc_fit_splits_at_just_under_pi covers a 180° semicircle producing 2 arcs.
acceptance_criteria: Polylines that span exactly 180° of arc fit to ≥2 sub-arcs. Test covers both inputs that mathematically span exactly π and noisy inputs that round up to π.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: timing has no G4 dwell handling — explicit P-seconds pauses invisible to time estimate
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/timing.rs:114-187 (loop over segments). The preview interpreter (`gcode/preview.rs`) only emits ToolpathSegments for motion gcodes — G0/1/2/3/73/81/82/83. G4 P<sec> dwell commands produce no segment, so the time estimator never sees them. Same for M0/M1/M2 program pauses, M3 spin-up after toolchange, and any explicit `(DWELL 2.5)` post-emitted timing comments.

**Problem:** Operations like drill peck (when not using G83), thread tapping, and spindle direction changes typically emit G4 P0.5 etc. None are counted. A 20-hole peck-drill operation with G4 P0.3 per peck loses 6 seconds, or per cycle if multiple pecks: 20*4 = 80 G4 dwells of 0.3s = 24s missing.

**Real-world impact:** Drilling and tapping cycle time estimate under-predicts. The bigger concern: when a project leans on G4 pauses to manage thermal cycles or chip clearance, the user can't see the pause cost — they assume the estimator is wrong by 10% across the board and lose trust.

**Acceptance:** Preview emits a Dwell pseudo-segment (length 0, kind Dwell, dwell_seconds field) for each G4 P. Timing accumulates dwell_s into a new TimeEstimate.dwell_s component. Test: a path with two G4 P0.5 commands adds 1.0 s to total_s.
acceptance_criteria: TimeEstimate.dwell_s field exists, populated from preview Dwell segments. dwell_two_pauses_adds_correct_total test passes.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P2 sim commits on main (lower_at_or_record: 20a58e1, full P2 cluster: c3f6680). 516 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 timing: M3/M6 dwell + spindle warmup applied as flat sum; no per-tool-change dwell tracking
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/timing.rs:189 (toolchange_s = tool_changes * machine.toolchange_s) and call sites passing pre-summed `spindle_warmup_s`.

**Problem:** Toolchange cost is a global flat multiplier — `n * machine.toolchange_s`. Real machines have widely different M6 dwell (manual change at workpiece-zero-touch + new height probe = 60–120 s; ATC change = 3–8 s). The estimator has no per-toolchange variance, and no awareness of which tools triggered the change. Worse, the spindle-warmup is a single pre-summed scalar passed in by the caller, with no link to which tool's `pause` field contributed — so changing one tool's pause and re-estimating doesn't update the warmup component.

Additionally, M3 spin-up at the start of each operation (typical 2–5 s with high-rpm spindles) isn't modeled at all — only `tool.pause` per tool. If three sequential ops share a tool but pause between each (typical for finishing/drilling pairs), the M3 dwell isn't applied.

**Real-world impact:** On a 10-toolchange manual-ATC job the estimate is off by 5–10 minutes (M6 alone) plus the M3 pauses. Operator schedules tighter than the part can run.

**Acceptance:** Per-toolchange dwell becomes `sum over (tool_a, tool_b) transitions` with optional per-tool-change override. Spindle warmup is computed from a vec of (segment_idx, tool_id) markers inside the estimator, not pre-summed by the caller. Test asserts a 3-tool, 2-toolchange path with different per-tool pause values gives the per-segment-aware sum.
acceptance_criteria: estimate() takes a toolchange-marker list (segment_idx, from_tool, to_tool) and applies machine.toolchange_s + tool.pause per change. Total time matches a hand-computed reference within 1 s.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P2 sim commits on main (lower_at_or_record: 20a58e1, full P2 cluster: c3f6680). 516 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 vcarve: ratchet emitter outputs travel moves at z=0 across uncut stock, scraping non-flat tip across surface
description:
Where: crates/wiac-core/src/cam/vcarve_emit.rs:120-126.

Problem: ratchet_emit forward sweep at current_level: when no new material is cut at point i (next_z >= cut_z[i]), the else branch at line 120-126 emits a position-move at the current cut depth cut_z[i]. At the first forward pass with current_level=-dpp, cut_z[i] is 0 for ALL points until material is actually cut. So the bit walks along the surface at z=0, AT FEED RATE rate_h (the gcode emitter sets feedrate rate_h before the polyline loop at line 341 of gcode.rs).

A V-bit at z=0 with feed > 0 will scrape across the workpiece surface. If the chain is a long shallow medial axis (e.g. a thin slot whose deepest point is barely beyond DPP), the FIRST forward sweep can travel meters of surface scrape before any actual cut. For sharp pointed V-bits this lightly mars the surface; for flat-tip V-bits this drags the tip across the surface at feed.

Worse: at the end of the forward sweep, the reverse sweep at line 135-137 also emits points at cut_z[i] (still 0 at most points if not much cut), retracing the surface scrape.

Real-world impact: Surface marking on workpiece tops; for delicate work (e.g. inlays where the surface is the visible face) this leaves witness lines along every medial-axis chain.
acceptance_criteria: Forward and reverse sweeps emit position moves only when cut_z[i] < 0 (i.e. actual cut has happened). Above the surface, sweeps lift to fast_z. Or: the emitter skips the "no progress at this point" branch entirely until the first cut at this point. Test: a 20x4 rectangle V-Carve with DPP > the inscribed radius produces zero gcode moves at z=0 with x changing.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 sim: heightmap.lower_at strict '<' write ties dirty AABB to value-change not visit
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/sim/heightmap.rs:82-91. Strict-less-than write + dirty-tracking gated on same condition: a re-sweep at same Z value does NOT update dirty AABB. Latent landmine for any future code reading dirty AABB as a 'segment touched material' signal. **Real-world impact:** Order-dependent answers for any future caller. **Acceptance:** Document contract on lower_at; one regression test.
acceptance_criteria: docstring documents contract; regression test re_pass_at_same_z_dirty_aabb_unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P2 sim commits on main (lower_at_or_record: 20a58e1, full P2 cluster: c3f6680). 516 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 thread: no feed compensation for outer-edge speed on tight bores
description: Where: crates/wiac-core/src/cam/thread.rs:113-122 + op_drivers/thread.rs:137 (uses emit_vcarve_block whose feed = setup.tool.rate_h). When cutter centre walks at feed F on helix radius helix_r, the outer cutting edge at radius (helix_r + tool_r) moves at F * (helix_r + tool_r)/helix_r. Internal: outer_edge_speed = F * bore_r/(bore_r-tool_r). M6+3mm tool: outer=2F. M10+6mm: outer=2.5F. Conventional CAM auto-reduces feed by helix_r/(helix_r+tool_r). wiac dumps rate_h ignoring the multiplication. Real-world impact: poor thread finish, broken cutters in tough materials.
acceptance_criteria: Thread op driver computes compensated feed and overrides rate. Test: M6 internal with rate_h=300 emits gcode F=150 (per the compensation formula).
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 thread: no multi-pass radial scheduling; full thread depth in single helix is too aggressive
description: Where: crates/wiac-core/src/cam/thread.rs:60-122 + op_drivers/thread.rs:97-124. helix_waypoints emits ONE helix at helix_radius (bore-tool_r). Full thread profile cut in a single revolution = full radial engagement. Estlcam Prog_Thread schedules Anzahl Gewindegaenge (multiple passes); wiac does not. M10x1.5 in aluminium with a 6mm thread mill = 1.5mm profile in one helix on 4mm-radius helix = full chip load on every flute. Chatter + broken cutters in metal. Real-world impact: Thread-mill failures in tough materials; users have no way to soften the pass without editing gcode.
acceptance_criteria: OpKind::Thread gains radial_passes: u32 (default 1). Op driver emits one helix per pass at scaled helix_radius. Test: 3 passes -> 3 helices at 33/67/100%.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: parallel_offset catch_unwind hides cavalier_contours panics, returns empty silently
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:254 in fn parallel_offset_object.

**Problem:** The std::panic::catch_unwind wrapper turns a cavalier_contours panic into an empty Vec + tracing::warn. tracing::warn goes to stderr / a logger but is invisible to the user driving the UI. Returning Vec::new() for a closed object means the offset path is just dropped — no segments, no rings, no drill substitution. The op silently emits an empty path.

**Reproduction / evidence:** Any DXF whose HATCH boundary trips cavalier_contours' 'repeat position vertexes' assert that the up-front dedupe in vc_to_pline didn't catch (e.g. an ELLIPSE flattening that drops a near-coincident vertex AFTER the dedupe). Pipeline returns successfully with no segments for that object. The user sees nothing in the preview, no warning, and ships gcode missing that contour entirely.

**Why this matters:** Silent gcode omission is the worst failure mode for a CAM tool — the user thinks the preview matches the part. The warning needs to be surfaced to the pipeline's warnings.rs so it appears in the UI.
acceptance_criteria: parallel_offset_object's panic recovery path emits a structured warning through the pipeline's warning channel (warnings.rs) instead of just tracing::warn. Object index, layer, and a hint ('cavalier_contours rejected this contour — try simplifying or re-tessellating') in the warning. Regression test stubs a panic and asserts the warning is captured.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: inscribed-circle plunge point can land in narrow passage of non-convex pocket
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/inscribed.rs:22 in fn inscribed_circle, used by pipeline's plan_helix_entry.

**Problem:** inscribed_circle walks all medial-axis vertices and picks the one with max r. That's the largest disc center, which is correct for FITTING the helix. But the returned (cx, cy) is fed back through plan_helix_entry to find a cut path between center and the actual contour start. For an L-shaped or H-shaped pocket, the medial axis traverses BOTH arms; the strict-improvement tie-break (`v.r > b.r`) picks the wider arm's vertex (correct), but the helix-entry plan must still get the cutter from the helix-circle perimeter to the contour start — that hop is currently emitted as a straight G1 in gcode.rs:752–753 (`post.linear(Some(start.x), ..., Some(z))`). That linear can cross a re-entrant wall in non-convex pockets.

**Reproduction / evidence:** L-shaped pocket with wide arm on left (where the helix fits) and a contour that starts in the right arm. helix lands at center of left arm; linear from that center to the contour-start in the right arm cuts through the corner of the L = into uncut stock at full depth.

**Why this matters:** A user picking 'Helix' plunge on a non-convex pocket gets a tool-breaking move (full-depth linear crossing the inset boundary). The check should sample the linear hop the same way bridge_stays_inside_polygon does and abort to Ramp if the hop crosses the wall.
acceptance_criteria: The helix-to-contour hop is validated against the boundary; on failure, fall back to Ramp or Direct plunge. Regression test: L-shaped pocket with Helix plunge does not emit a linear that crosses the inset wall.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: pocket_zigzag silently emits joiner Lines that may cross uncut stock
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:386 in pocket_zigzag — joiner segment between stroke pairs.

**Problem:** Between strokes pocket_zigzag pushes `Segment::line(prev, a, ...)` where prev = previous stroke's end and a = next stroke's start. With non-convex pockets where even-odd produces multiple disjoint stroke groups on a single scanline, the joiner can span a 'wall' between two pocket arms (a hole in the polygon, or the inset between an outer and an island). The cutter runs that joiner at cut depth — straight through stock.

**Reproduction / evidence:** A U-shaped pocket. At y just below the cross-bar, the scanline gives 4 crossings → 2 strokes, left arm and right arm. The joiner between right-arm.end and (the next y level's first stroke) can cross over the top of the cross-bar. Even worse: when an island sits inside a square pocket, even-odd on the BOUNDARY ONLY (zigzag ignores islands per separate bug) produces a straight stroke through the island.

**Why this matters:** Same root issue as the island bug (gp2a) but for non-convex outer shapes alone — the joiner is unconditional. Should validate the joiner stays inside the boundary.
acceptance_criteria: pocket_zigzag tests each joiner against the boundary (and islands when wired through): if it leaves the safe interior, lift to safe Z, rapid across, plunge back. Regression test on a U-shaped pocket asserting no joiner crosses the cross-bar.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 chamfer: ignores V-bit tip flat (tip_diameter), overshoots z by tip_radius/tan(half)
description:
Where: crates/wiac-core/src/cam/chamfer.rs:45-52.

Problem: Real V-bits often have a small flat tip (0.1 to 1mm tip_diameter for sign-making bits and engravers). The chamfer math z = -width/tan(half) assumes a perfectly pointed cone. For a flat-tipped V-bit, when the bit is at z = -D, the cone radius at z=0 is tip_radius + D * tan(half), not D * tan(half).

Correct: width = tip_radius + D * tan(half), so D = (width - tip_radius) / tan(half).
Current: D = width / tan(half) — overshoots by tip_radius/tan(half).

For a 0.3mm-tip flat 60 V-bit cutting a 1mm chamfer: correct D = (1 - 0.15)/tan(30) = 1.47mm. Current code emits D = 1/tan(30) = 1.73mm = 0.26mm too deep, producing a chamfer width of 1.15mm instead of 1mm. Cosmetic on small chamfers; on a 30 engraver bit with 0.5mm tip the error is larger.

vcarve.rs polyline_to_z (line 387-391) already does this correctly via tip_radius_mm subtraction. chamfer.rs does not.

Real-world impact: Chamfer widths are wider than the user specified; the spec mismatches the part. Visual mismatch on signs. Functional fit problems when the chamfer is a relief/clearance and width matters.
acceptance_criteria: chamfer_depth takes (or reads from the tool) the tip flat diameter and applies width = tip_radius + D*tan(half). Existing tests updated to either pass tip_diameter=0 explicitly or accept the new signature. New test: chamfer_depth(1.0, 60.0, tip_diameter=0.3) returns z such that the actual chamfer width is 1.0mm.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 chaining: sample_point uses chord midpoint, lands ON the boundary for arcs
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/chaining.rs:189 in fn sample_point.

**Problem:** classify_containment picks a probe point per object using sample_point, which returns the midpoint of the first segment's CHORD endpoints. For a Line segment, that's a point ON the line — not strictly inside or outside any polygon. For an Arc segment, segment_to_points(s, 1) returns just [start, end] — again, chord midpoint, ON the line between two arc endpoints. is_inside_polygon with even-odd rule is ambiguous for points exactly on an edge — depending on FP rounding, the test may flip in or out arbitrarily.

**Reproduction / evidence:** Two circles touching at one point (common in DXF: tangent holes). Object A's first segment is a half-arc whose endpoints sit on the touch point. sample_point picks the chord midpoint = circle center of A. Asking 'is A inside B' tests whether A's center is inside B — fine for non-touching circles, but for tangent geometry the probe lands on B's boundary itself when the touch point IS the circle's diameter endpoint. classify gives non-deterministic outer/inner classification.

**Why this matters:** Tool-offset direction (Inside vs Outside) is decided by containment. A misclassified pair makes the wrong polygon get offset outward, taking the cutter across the part. The probe should sit clearly INSIDE the object — either the polygon centroid for closed objects, or a point offset by epsilon along the inward normal at the midpoint.
acceptance_criteria: sample_point for a closed object returns a point strictly inside its polygon — e.g. polygon_centroid (which already exists in cam.rs) with a fallback to inward-offset of first-segment-midpoint when centroid lies outside (re-entrant shapes). Add a regression test for two tangent circles and assert deterministic outer/inner.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: build_paths handles only depth-1 island nesting, deeper levels collapse
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:515 in fn build_paths (pocket_cascade_with_islands feed).

**Problem:** build_paths forces the outer boundary CCW and every island CW unconditionally before feeding to clipper2 inflate_paths_d. Two issues:

1. clipper2 with EndType::Polygon and FillRule for inflate treats CW rings as holes, but the function does not preserve relative nesting — if an island contains a sub-island that should be machinable (island-in-hole-in-island), the sub-island is flipped to CW and becomes another hole. Result: hierarchical features are corrupted.

2. pocket_cascade_with_islands is called from pocket_for_object only with the top-level islands the per-op driver assembled; the caller in source_combine + auto containment passes only direct children. But combined regions from boolean ops (PolyTreeD nesting deeper than 1) flatten to the same single-level scheme at polytree_to_regions:425 — `top.children()` is taken as direct holes, but the grandchildren (re-entrant outer inside a hole) are dropped.

**Reproduction / evidence:** polytree_to_regions in source_combine.rs:412 iterates only top-level outers and their direct children as holes; the children's children (deeper outers) are never reified into separate regions. A donut-inside-a-hole-inside-an-outer becomes a single annulus.

**Why this matters:** Auto-combine with nested DXF (e.g. a plate with a window with a label boss inside the window) produces gcode that pockets the entire window including the boss.
acceptance_criteria: polytree_to_regions walks the FULL PolyTreeD and recurses into grandchildren, emitting a CombinedRegion per outer at every odd nesting level (with its direct hole-children). Regression test: depth-2 nested polygons (outer with hole with inner outer) yields two CombinedRegions.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: apply_overcut only anchors to boundary endpoints, misses long-wall reflex corners
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:1313 in fn apply_overcut — boundary probe loop.

**Problem:** The dip distance for an offset-polyline reflex corner is determined by the nearest boundary ENDPOINT lying within 0.25 mm perpendicular distance of the outward bisector ray. Real CAD inputs commonly have long flat boundary edges whose endpoints fall far from the bisector — for example, the reflex corner of an L-shaped pocket whose vertical wall is 50 mm long: the bisector ray emerges from the inside corner toward the geometric corner of the L, but the boundary endpoints sit 25 mm away from the ray on either side. No anchor is found, overcut is silently skipped, the corner remains uncut.

**Reproduction / evidence:** apply_overcut iterates `for p1 in [seg.start, seg.end]` and rejects with `if perp > 0.25 { continue }`. There's no projection onto the boundary segments themselves — only vertex endpoints are sampled. A square corner with 1-mm sides will overcut (vertex within 0.25 of the ray); a 50-mm-side corner will not.

**Why this matters:** Inside-corner overcut is the user-visible reason corners look 'crisp' in CAM output. Without it the cutter leaves a fillet at every concave corner equal to the tool radius. The current implementation works on tiny test geometries (the test uses a 10-mm L) but fails on real parts.
acceptance_criteria: apply_overcut projects each boundary SEGMENT (not just endpoints) onto the outward bisector ray, picks the nearest intersection within `perp_tol` of the ray. Regression test: an L-shaped boundary with arms ≥ 30 mm and an inward-offset of 2 mm with tool_radius 2 produces an overcut dip at the reflex corner.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: small_circle_drill leaves dead zone for tool_radius * 0.95..1.0
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:1201 in fn small_circle_drill — `if radius >= tool_radius * 0.95 { return None; }`.

**Problem:** A circle of radius r where `0.95 * tool_radius <= r < tool_radius` does NOT trigger the drill-substitution branch, but ALSO can't be pocketed (parallel_offset_inward of a r-radius circle by r mm collapses to nothing — the cavalier_contours offset returns an empty result). The cascade loop bails on `if boundary.is_empty() { return out; }` at line 816, and the function returns an empty Vec with no diagnostic. The hole is silently skipped.

**Reproduction / evidence:** Circle of radius 2.85 mm with a 3 mm tool. small_circle_drill returns None (2.85 < 0.95*3 is FALSE, 2.85 >= 2.85). parallel_offset_inward by 3 mm of a 2.85 radius circle returns empty (negative radius). pocket_for_object returns Vec::new(). No warning, no drill, no gcode for that hole.

**Why this matters:** Bolt-pattern DXFs commonly have a mix of holes — some smaller than the tool, some at-or-near tool diameter. Holes at the tool's exact diameter should drill straight down (the same single-plunge fallback used for smaller holes). Silently dropping them produces a part with the wrong number of holes.
acceptance_criteria: When the inward offset of a closed object produces empty geometry AND the object encloses an area large enough for a plunge (>= tool_radius * 0.5 say), emit a drill at the centroid OR fire a pipeline warning identifying the un-machinable feature. Regression test: 3 mm tool against a 2.9 mm-radius circle yields a single drill at center (or a clearly-labelled warning).
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: horizontal_crossings drops odd-count crossings silently (chunks_exact)
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:360 in fn pocket_zigzag — `crossings.chunks_exact(2)`.

**Problem:** chunks_exact silently discards the last element when the count is odd. horizontal_crossings is designed to produce even counts (entry/exit pairs under even-odd rule), but a scanline that grazes a vertex can produce an odd count due to the half-open `y >= hi.y - 1e-12` rule when the same y is near multiple coincident vertices, or when input polygons are not exactly closed (consecutive points within FUZZY of each other). The remainder() of chunks_exact is dropped without a warning, leaving an unpaired entry crossing that would have indicated 'enter pocket, never exit' — manifests as a missing stroke and uncut stock at that y.

**Reproduction / evidence:** Construct a polygon whose top edge has a near-horizontal-but-not-exactly-horizontal segment that ends right at a scanline. Run pocket_zigzag with the matching stride. The unpaired crossing is dropped without diagnostic. No assertion, no warning.

**Why this matters:** Degenerate inputs from imported DXF/SVG are common. Silent uncut stock is worse than a hard failure because the user ships gcode that leaves uncut material and only finds out at the part inspection.
acceptance_criteria: When horizontal_crossings yields an odd count, either (a) log a warning + skip the offending scanline, or (b) collapse the unpaired vertex by snapping crossings within FUZZY together. Regression test: vertex-tangent scanline must either emit a connected stroke or produce a pipeline warning.
close_reason: Closed

title: Open-file flows: REPLACE semantics + dirty-check prompt
description:
Recent → DXF used to call addImported(), stacking the new drawing on top of the current project. Ops from the previous project stayed bound to their original object IDs and silently re-evaluated against stale geometry. No dirty-check existed anywhere; loading a recent project on top of an unsaved one was destructive without warning.

Fixed: new project.clearProject() resets ops + fixtures + textLayers + stock + selections + dirty (preserves tools + machine — those are per-user/shop, not per-project). All open-file flows (loadFromPath, openFile, loadProjectPath, openProject, loadFile, loadProjectFile, loadSample) now clearProject() before importing. Dirty-check prompts (window.confirm) added to user-initiated open paths (File menu, Recent submenu, Sample picker); the OS file-association / reopen-banner paths still bypass since they're already cold-start scenarios.

A separate addDrawingPath() is kept for future multi-drawing 'overlay' workflows; not exposed in any menu today.
close_reason: Closed

title: Perf jzpl Phase 2: intern Segment.layer / VcObject.layer as Arc<str>
description:
Segment.layer is a heap-allocated String per segment. Typical DXFs have 4-10 distinct layer names spread across thousands of segments. Every `segment.clone()` allocates a fresh String for the layer field — the dominant cost of segment-heavy operations (pattern expansion, offset builder reuses).

## Fix
- geometry.rs: `Segment.layer: String` → `Arc<str>`.
- cam.rs: `VcObject.layer: String` → `Arc<str>` (or keep String — only one per object, smaller win).
- Segment constructors (`Segment::line`, `::arc`, etc.) accept `impl Into<Arc<str>>`.
- Importers (dxf.rs / svg.rs / text rendering): intern layer names through a small `HashMap<String, Arc<str>>` so all segments on the same layer share one allocation.
- Serde: Arc<str> has built-in serde support — wire format unchanged.
- Audit ~30 call sites that compare `.layer` against `&str` literals (mostly works via Deref).

## Why
Every Segment clone becomes a refcount bump on the layer field instead of a String allocation. Phase-1's drop of per-op clones still leaves pattern expansion and offset_builder's internal segment clones; Phase 2 makes those near-free.

~250 LOC across 8-10 files. MSRV-safe (Arc<str> stable since Rust 1.21).
close_reason: Arc<str> for Segment.layer + VcObject.layer + PolylineOffset.layer + CombinedRegion.layer + ImportedObject.layer. Workspace serde gets 'rc' feature. ~50 call sites updated (clones via .clone() refcount bump; comparisons via .as_ref()). Wire format unchanged (Arc<str> ↔ JSON string). cargo test 373/373, clippy strict clean, openapi regenerated. PIPELINE_VERSION not bumped — wire bytes identical. Follow-up wiaconstructor-ojh3 filed for importer-side interning. Commit d0d0ee0.

title: Perf jzpl Phase 1: drop per-op .to_vec() clone in run_standard_op / run_halfpipe_op
description:
op_drivers.rs:71 currently calls `build_op_offsets(op, project, &mut objects.to_vec(), ...)` — a full Vec<VcObject> clone every op. For a 50-op project on a 5000-segment DXF that's 50× full-vec clones per Generate.

The defensive clone exists because build_op_offsets internally does `*objects = expanded` in two paths (pattern expansion and frame synthesis) and the caller wants its input pristine for the next op.

## Fix
- build_op_offsets signature: `objects: &mut Vec<VcObject>` → `objects: &[VcObject]`.
- Pattern expansion produces a locally-owned `Option<Vec<VcObject>>` instead of mutating `*objects`.
- Frame synthesis: same shape.
- `let effective_objects: &[VcObject] = frame_expanded.as_deref().or(pattern_expanded.as_deref()).unwrap_or(input);` picks the right view.
- Downstream code reads `effective_objects` instead of `objects`.
- Vestigial `for obj in objects.iter_mut() { obj.tool_offset = setup.mill.offset; }` at offset_builder.rs:205: delete (the field has no production reader; only a test assertion).
- run_standard_op (op_drivers.rs:71): drop `&mut` + `.to_vec()`, pass `objects` directly.
- run_halfpipe_op (halfpipe.rs): same if applicable.

## Why
50-op project goes from 50× full Vec<VcObject> clone → 0 clones. Ops with no pattern/frame become zero-allocation per call.

Mechanical refactor, ~150 LOC. Test coverage already exercises pattern + frame + standard paths.
close_reason: build_op_offsets now takes &[VcObject]; pattern + frame expansion produce locally-owned Vecs. run_per_op and the three-arm match downgraded from &mut to &. work_objects clone gone; per-op .to_vec() gone. Vestigial obj.tool_offset loop deleted. cargo test 373/373, clippy strict clean. 50-op project: 51 full-vec clones → 0 (unless op carries pattern/frame, then still locally bounded). Commit 36d1c30.

title: Perf: EntityCanvas2D draw $effect tracks 18 deps; hover redraws full canvas
description:
The single draw $effect (EntityCanvas2D.svelte:114-135) lists 18 dependencies including hoverIdx, ghostTab, userZoom/Pan, regionsVisible, etc. Every hover or selection-box drag triggers a full retessellate + repaint of every imported segment, region, text preview, fixture, and HUD overlay.

## Fix sketch
Split into layers:
1. 'background' — bg + grid + imported geometry + text-preview. Memoized to an OffscreenCanvas / cached path; only invalidated on imported / textLayers / previewVersion / theme / userZoom / userPan changes.
2. 'interaction overlay' — selection highlights, hover halo, ghost tab, approach point, fixture handles, box-select rect. Cheap per-frame redraw composited on top.

When hover changes, only the overlay redraws; the geometry stays cached.

## Why
Hover should be sub-millisecond. Currently every hover triggers a full canvas redraw including draw region preview.
close_reason: Split into bg + overlay canvases stacked via CSS. bg paints heavy static layer (geometry, regions, grid, axes, work area, text previews) on geometry/zoom/pan/theme deps only. overlay paints state-bearing items (selection/hover/op-assignment halos, fixtures, tabs, ghost tab, approach point, box-select) on a transparent canvas with pointer-events:none. Hover/box-select no longer invalidates the heavy layer. svelte-check 0 errors, tests 201/201.

title: Perf: Scene3D.rebuildGeometry full-mesh teardown on every signal
description:
rebuildGeometry (Scene3D.svelte:1344) clears geometryGroup and rebuilds the entire vertex buffer on every change to transformedImport / visibleLayers / generated / operations / textLayers / previewVersion. On a 5k-segment DXF, every op edit or playhead motion causes a measurable hitch.

## Fix sketch
Split into two passes:
1. 'staticPass' — imported segments + text-layer previews. Rebuild only on transformedImport / visibleLayers / textLayers / previewVersion changes.
2. 'dynamicPass' — toolpath wireframe + selection highlight + tab markers. Rebuild on generated / operations / selectedObjects changes.

Keep each pass in its own Three.js Group with its own LineSegments buffer; updates only re-upload the relevant buffer.

## Why
Per-op editing should NOT retessellate 5k DXF segments. Selection highlight should NOT teardown the toolpath buffer.

Related: cw23 audit notes the LOC, but the perf angle is new.
close_reason: Split into rebuildImportedGeometry + rebuildToolpathGeometry, two LineSegments objects, two effects with independent dep sets. Editing operations no longer teardowns imported buffer; toggling layers no longer teardowns toolpath buffer. Selection delta + playhead fade + sim-warning tints now target the correct buffer. Raycaster intersectObjects both. Combined bounding sphere for fit-to-view. svelte-check 0 errors, tests 201/201.

title: audit 2026-05-17: write ARCHITECTURE.md — junior-dev onboarding map
description:
No top-level `ARCHITECTURE.md`. The seams exist (transport → core → state → UI; op-driver dispatch; state slices; command-bus undo; PostProcessor trait) but a new contributor has to grep around to discover them. CONTRIBUTING.md already covers the two extension recipes (new op kind, new post-processor) but not the architecture.

## Fix
Write a focused 1-2 page `ARCHITECTURE.md` covering:
- Layer diagram (4 transports + wiac-core + frontend + schema seam)
- Data flow: user action → state mutation → command-bus undo → API client → transport → wiac-core::run_pipeline → response → state update → UI re-render
- Patterns with one-line "when to use":
  - State slice (frontend/src/lib/state/) with proxy getter/setter
  - Op-driver dispatch (pipeline/op_drivers/)
  - Post-processor trait (gcode/)
  - Command-bus undo (commands.ts)
  - Schema codegen seam (`cargo xtask schema && pnpm codegen`)
- Anti-patterns with one-line "why":
  - $state write-then-read-via-function-call inside $effect (dh1n)
  - window.confirm in Tauri (C10)
  - Raw JSON.parse on a Svelte 5 proxy (MachineDialog history)
  - Hand-editing api/generated.ts

Recipes ("how do I add X") for: new state slice, new dialog. (Op kind / post-processor live in CONTRIBUTING.md already; link there.)

## Why
Junior-onboarding gap. Lowest-risk, highest-leverage piece of the audit-2026-05-17 sweep.

## Related
Part of kt2 (User onboarding & documentation) epic.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-17: split project.rs (1562 LOC) by domain
description:
`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs` is 1562 LOC mixing wire types (`Project`, `PipelineRequest`, `PipelineResponse`), the `Op` / `OpKind` / `OpParams` model, the `ToolEntry` / `ToolKind` model, `MachineConfig`, fixture types, text-layer types, and all the serde derives + custom deserializers. A junior dev who wants to add a tool field has to scroll past op variants, machine config, and pipeline wire types first.

## Fix
Split into:
- `project.rs` — `Project` struct + `PipelineRequest` / `PipelineResponse` wire types only.
- `project/op.rs` — `Op`, `OpKind`, `OpSource`, `PatternConfig`, `PocketStrategy`, `HalfpipeProfile`, `DrillCycle`.
- `project/params.rs` — `OpParams` (with mill/laser defaults).
- `project/tool.rs` — `ToolEntry`, `ToolKind`, `Coolant`.
- `project/machine.rs` — `MachineConfig` (already a separate file in cam/setup.rs — re-export or move).
- `project/fixture.rs` — `Fixture`, `FixtureKind`.
- `project/text.rs` — `TextLayer` + related.

Re-export everything from `project.rs` so external call sites stay unchanged. Tests stay co-located with the type they exercise.

## Why
Same pain as gcode.rs / pipeline.rs but for the data model. Also unblocks kbx5 (OpParams junk drawer → per-kind variants on OpKind): much easier to do once OpParams + OpKind have their own files.

## Related
Blocked by: nothing. Blocks: kbx5 (cleaner once params + op are in separate files).
Sibling of 55o4 (pipeline split) and the proposed gcode.rs split.
close_reason: committed; project.rs 1562 → 163, 5 submodules, schema byte-identical, 388 tests

title: audit 2026-05-17: split gcode.rs (2858 LOC) per post + per block kind
description:
`crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs` is a god file at 2858 LOC mixing the `PostProcessor` trait, three full post-processor implementations (LinuxCNC, GRBL, HPGL), the post-profile token substitution layer, and the per-shape block emitters (drill, polylines, vcarve). A junior dev who wants to add a new post-processor or fix a single emitter has to scroll through everything else first.

## Fix
Split into:
- `gcode.rs` — trait `PostProcessor`, shared types (`Move`, `Coolant`, …), the dispatcher `emit_polylines` / `emit_drill` / `emit_vcarve_block` shells, public re-exports.
- `gcode/linuxcnc.rs`, `gcode/grbl.rs`, `gcode/hpgl.rs` — one per dialect (mirror what already exists for post_profile.rs).
- `gcode/emit/drill.rs`, `gcode/emit/polylines.rs`, `gcode/emit/vcarve.rs` — per-shape block emitters.

Tests stay co-located with the code they exercise (mirror what we did in pipeline/op_drivers/). Visibility: `pub(crate)` for cross-module helpers, `pub` only for the trait + public emit fns + post structs.

## Why
Highest-leverage god-file split left. Touching one post or one emit kind shouldn't require reading 2858 lines. Mirrors the established pipeline/op_drivers split — sets the same pattern in the gcode layer.

## Related
Sibling of 6cpl (pipeline split). Unblocks future post-processors (Mach3, Centroid, etc.) without each one growing the god file.
close_reason: committed in 845c375; gcode.rs 2858 → 1386, 6 new submodules, 365 tests green, clippy clean

title: 6cpl step 4: extract ProjectDataState slice — interacts with commands.ts
description:
After 0z4q (GeneratedState, closed) and the selection-slice commit, the remaining 'project-data' slice of ProjectState owns:

  imported, operations, selectedOpId  // selected* now lives in SelectionState
  tools, machine, stock, fixtures, textLayers
  dirty, visibleLayers, regionsVisible
  settings

These are the fields the undo/redo command bus mutates (commands.ts). Splitting them requires:

* Either: every Command receives a typed slice handle instead of the full ProjectState. Cleanest but touches every command in commands.ts.
* Or: keep ProjectState as the command target, but route commands' field accesses through a dedicated `data: ProjectDataState` slice with proxies. Less invasive but adds an indirection layer.

The choice depends on whether we want the command bus to operate on a narrower interface (the slice) or stay broad (ProjectState). Discuss before doing the work.

## Acceptance

* Tests + svelte-check green.
* commands.ts compiles unchanged OR its CommandTarget type narrows cleanly.
* project.svelte.ts shrinks below 1000 LOC.

This is the heaviest remaining 6cpl step — defer until the proxy-getter pattern has been live for a release or two to make sure the reactivity behaves as expected in production.
close_reason: committed; ProjectDataState slice extracted with proxy getter/setter pattern, CommandTarget unchanged

title: 6cpl step 2: extract GeneratedState slice from ProjectState
description:
Phase 1 (f1f4cc9) extracted pure types from project.svelte.ts. The remaining work is splitting the ProjectState class itself. The cleanest first slice to extract is everything generate-related, because:

* none of these fields are touched by commands.ts (no undo/redo concerns)
* they share a coherent lifecycle (idle → running → completed/cancelled/failed)
* there's already a small method surface (beginGenerate / notePipelineEvent / endGenerate / finishGenerate / failGenerate / cancelGenerate) wrapping the state mutations

## Concrete fields to move

```
generated, generating, generatedVersion
pipelineState, pipelineProgress
lastGenerateCachedCount, lastGenerateOpCount
toolpathCumLen, toolpathTotalLen
simDiagnostics  (sim is downstream of generated)
```

## Approach

* Create `lib/state/generated.svelte.ts` with a `GeneratedState` class owning the above `$state` fields + the six generate methods.
* In `ProjectState`, replace the fields with a single `gen = new GeneratedState()` instance.
* For backwards compat, add proxy getters/setters on ProjectState that forward to `gen`: `get generated() { return this.gen.generated; } set generated(v) { this.gen.generated = v; }`. Keeps the ~30 `project.generated` call sites unchanged.
* When all call sites read through getters, the next step can switch them to `project.gen.generated` directly and drop the proxy layer — that's a follow-up issue.

## Acceptance

* All workspace + frontend tests still pass (388 + 180).
* No call site needs to change.
* project.svelte.ts loses ~150-200 lines.
* GeneratedState has a self-contained vitest covering at least the state-transition invariants (beginGenerate → 'running', endGenerate → 'completed', cancelGenerate from 'running' → 'cancelling', etc.).

Subsequent slice extractions (selection slice, project-data slice) follow the same pattern as separate sub-issues.
close_reason: Closed
