title: clippy --workspace fails on main: 567+ pedantic warnings treated as errors
description:
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (the gate in .github/workflows/ci.yml:32) returns 567+ errors on the current main commit. CI's `RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings` (line 10) plus clippy's full pedantic level (Cargo.toml workspace lints: `pedantic = warn`) means every pedantic suggestion becomes a hard error.

## Sample
```
warning: this function's return value is unnecessarily wrapped by `Result`
warning: doc list item overindented
warning: redundant closure: `|s| s.to_ascii_lowercase()`
warning: items missing backticks in documentation
warning: bindings with single-character names in scope
warning: this argument is passed by value (clippy::needless_pass_by_value)
```

## Discovered while
Working on luf1 (HTTP error envelope). The 567+ warnings predate my changes; my edits don't introduce any new ones.

## Likely cause
Same as qfsz (fmt drift): a recent rustc / clippy version bump tightened pedantic lints. The codebase hasn't been bulk-cleaned since.

## Fix options
1. Bulk-fix with `cargo clippy --fix --workspace --all-targets` (one big commit), or
2. Demote the noisiest pedantic lints in Cargo.toml workspace.lints.clippy (e.g. `needless_pass_by_value`, `doc_markdown`, `similar_names`).

Option 2 is cheaper and probably wiser — many pedantic lints are stylistic preferences, not defects.
close_reason: Closed

title: cargo fmt --check fails: 247 diffs across 46 files on main
description:
`cargo fmt --all -- --check` returns 1 with 247 diffs in 46 files on the current main commit (8d019ba). Pre-commit cargo-fmt hook would reject any commit that includes a touched Rust file. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:31) is presumably also red but somehow has been passing — likely the CI runner's rustfmt version differs from the local 1.88.0 toolchain pin, or the matrix's macOS/windows runners use a different default channel and only ubuntu has been failing silently / branching out.

## Repro
```
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check; echo $?
1
```

## Likely cause
Rustfmt's wrap/indent decisions changed between the rustfmt version contributors are running locally and the version that last formatted the codebase. Without an rustfmt.toml pin, every minor toolchain bump silently drifts.

## Fix
1. Run `cargo fmt --all` once on a clean main (one large commit).
2. Add an `rustfmt.toml` with at least `edition = "2021"` so format is stable.
3. Consider `max_width`, `fn_call_width` etc. if the team prefers a different cap than rustfmt's default 100.

## Discovered while
Working on audit 2026-05-16 / 4y5y (pre-commit schema-check). Pre-commit cargo-fmt would block any new Rust-touching commit; the schema-check work landed touching only YAML/MD/just so it didn't trip on this — but the next dev who touches Rust will.

title: audit 2026-05-16: pre-commit schema-check to catch enum/type drift locally
description:
CI runs `cargo xtask schema --check` and fails on drift, but there is no pre-commit hook. A dev who adds a new `OperationKind` variant or `PostProcessorKind` arm and forgets to regenerate the schema only finds out after pushing — and the failure is silent at runtime for the HTTP transport in the meantime (Tauri/WASM pass the typed enum, HTTP deserializes from string and 422s in production).

## Fix
1. Add a justfile target: `just regen-schema` → `cargo xtask schema` + frontend codegen (`pnpm --filter ./frontend run codegen`).
2. Add a pre-commit hook step in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` that runs `cargo xtask schema --check` (fast; just compares against checked-in YAML).
3. Update `CONTRIBUTING.md` to mention 'after touching JsonSchema-deriving types, run `just regen-schema`'.

## Related
Distinct from izup, which is about the hand-maintained registry inside schema.rs. This issue is about the dev workflow that surrounds it.
close_reason: Closed

title: 3D-sim audit #4: specialize for_each_swept_cell per ToolProfile (drop sqrt)
description:
crates/wiac-core/src/sim/sweep.rs:216-220 — inner cell loop always computes `r = r_sq.sqrt()` to call `profile.eval(r)`. For Endmill / Drill / Laser / DragKnife profiles `eval(r)` returns `Some(0.0)` for `r ≤ rr` — already implied by `r_sq ≤ r_tool_sq`. Sqrt is purely overhead in those cases.

## Fix

Two paths in sweep:
* Flat-bottom profile (Endmill/Drill/Laser/DragKnife): `dz = 0`, just lower the cell to cutter_pz. Skip sqrt + eval.
* Profiled tool (BallNose/VBit): sqrt + eval path stays.

Dispatch outside the cell loop so the per-cell branch predicts perfectly. Profile expects ~20% sweep speedup on the dominant flat-bottom case.
close_reason: Closed

title: 3D-sim audit #3: partial instanceMatrix upload via updateRange
description:
frontend/src/lib/sim/heightfield_mesh.ts:144 — `instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true` re-uploads the entire matrix buffer to GPU (cols×rows × 16 bytes; for 4M cells = 64 MB) even when the dirty AABB is one segment's footprint (~150 cells).

## Fix

After replacing with custom BufferGeometry (#2), expose the dirty cells' positions/normals as flat Float32 arrays and set `positionAttr.updateRange = { offset, count }` for the touched range before `needsUpdate = true`. Or store the position attribute as multiple smaller ranges in a single buffer indexed by AABB. Three.js will then upload only the slice.

title: audit 2026-05-2: epic — architecture audit findings consolidated
description:
Architecture audit run on the current main (after the text-engraving / stock-first / UX-polish work landed). Three parallel deep-dives covered the Rust backend, frontend state + transport, and frontend UI / canvas.

### Frontend perf hot paths

- text_preview cache never invalidated on layer delete / project switch (fy32)
- HeightfieldDriver setTimeout outlives destroy() (eo7f)

- State helpers leaking into project.svelte.ts surface (h0bw)

### A11y

### Catchall
- Low-priority polish basket (pgxb)

title: audit 2026-05-2: Scene3D rebuild keys too coarse — fixture color & op edits trigger full mesh rebuild
description:
Two over-broad reactive dependencies in \`frontend/src/lib/components/Scene3D.svelte\`:

1. **L472-555 (sim-rebuild effect)** — stringifies \`JSON.stringify({…, fixtures: project.fixtures})\` to detect changes. Toggling fixture color rebuilds the JSON key + triggers the 1s debounce timer. Comment promises fixture color shouldn't rebuild, but the JSON includes the whole fixture.
2. **L374-381 (geometry effect)** — depends on \`project.operations\`; any op patch (depth, feed, etc.) rebuilds the entire linesObject geometry even though only color stamps change.

## Fix

Track a structurally-relevant fingerprint as a derived state (positions + radii for sim; \`operations.map(o => \`\${o.id}:\${o.color}\`)\` for geometry), depend on the fingerprint not the raw arrays.

title: audit 2026-05-2: EntityCanvas2D draw() — full-redraw per hover + theme-getComputedStyle 20×/frame
description:
Three concrete perf issues in \`frontend/src/lib/components/EntityCanvas2D.svelte\`:

1. **L76-98** — single mega-effect with ~18 reactive deps; hover during pan triggers a full \`draw()\` including re-rendering every text-preview layer. Split into geometry-deps vs. overlay-deps effects, or move overlays to a second canvas.
2. **L984-1116 (draw)** — resizes \`canvas.width = w*dpr\` every frame (allocates backing store, clears it twice) and calls \`getComputedStyle(container)\` 10-20× per redraw via \`themeVar()\` (synchronous style recalc). Only resize the backing store on ResizeObserver; cache resolved theme colors in a state map invalidated by the theme MutationObserver already in place.
3. **L1059-1100** — inner segment loop calls \`project.visibleLayers.has(seg.layer)\` and \`project.selectedObjects.has(objId)\` per segment; for N=10k segments these fire reactive proxy traps each time. Snapshot the Sets into local \`Set\`s at the top of \`draw()\`.

## Impact

A 5000-segment DXF redraws at ~5 fps on hover. Should be 60+ trivially.

title: audit 2026-05-2: restore() drops lastImportPath — source-file watch + Reload toast die after project load
description:
\`frontend/src/lib/state/project.svelte.ts:836\` — \`setImported(file.imported, null)\` resets the imported path to null. The source-file watcher (Tauri filesystem watch) + the "Reload changed file" toast both key off \`project.lastImportPath\`, so they go dead after every project load.

Persist the absolute source path in ProjectFile, OR fetch it from the per-project workspace state when restoring. Even simpler: just pass \`file.imported.filename\` (and require that to be an absolute path on Tauri).

title: audit 2026-05-2: HeightfieldDriver setTimeout outlives destroy() — disposed-mesh access
description:
\`frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts:488\` — \`scheduleEdgeRebuild\` never stores or clears its setTimeout handle. \`destroy()\` at L448 doesn't cancel it.

## Impact

title: audit 2026-05-2: text-preview cache never invalidated on layer delete / project switch
description:
\`text_preview.svelte.ts\` exports \`invalidatePreview(id)\` and \`resetPreviewCache()\` but no caller invokes either. \`removeTextLayer\` / \`restore\` / \`setImported\` don't drop entries (file: frontend/src/lib/state/text_preview.svelte.ts:145-162).

title: audit 2026-05-2: clone() churn in pipeline hot path
description:
Three concrete spots in \`pipeline.rs\` that clone non-trivial Vec<VcObject> repeatedly:

1. **L390-431** — \`objects.clone()\` is passed three times for the three PostProcessorKind match arms, even though only one runs. Hoist \`let mut work = objects.clone();\` outside the match, or pull \`run_per_op\` into a trait-object call so the clone happens once.
2. **L695** — \`build_op_offsets(.., &mut objects.clone(), ..)\` clones the entire object list per enabled op inside the hot per-op loop. 50-op project on a 5000-segment DXF clones 50× a Vec<VcObject> with non-trivial Segment children. Take \`&[VcObject]\` and let pattern/frame expansion build a local Vec only when needed, or use snapshot/restore on \`objects\`.
3. **L937-975** — pattern expansion clones every object once per instance (10×10 grid × 100 selected = 10 000 clones). Pre-allocate a single Vec<Segment> arena and copy ranges.

## Why this matters

These are the hottest paths for large DXFs / heavy patterns. Multi-MB clones every Generate.
notes: Partial: hoisted the three-arm-match objects.clone() to one named work_objects (commit 235d4de). The bigger wins (build_op_offsets per-op clone, pattern expansion per-instance clone) are by-design isolation boundaries — left for a future refactor that uses Arc<str> for layer names or a shared segment arena.

title: audit 2026-05-2: segments_to_objects O(n²) — quantized-endpoint spatial hash
description:
\`cam/chaining.rs:16-57\` — \`find_neighbor\` scans every untaken segment for each chain extension. A 5000-segment DXF is 25 million probes.

## Fix

Build a spatial hash keyed on quantized endpoint coords (FUZZY=1e-3 quantization). Neighbour lookup becomes O(1) amortized; 5000-segment DXF goes from 25M to ~10k probes.

title: audit 2026-05-2: classify_containment O(n²) — bbox-bucket before polygon-inside
description:
\`cam/chaining.rs:64\` does a full polygon-inside test per ordered pair of closed objects. Each \`polys\` is tessellated at interpolate=6 (8·6=48 pts per arc), so a 200-object DXF is 40 000 tests × 48-pt polygons.

## Fix

Bucket objects by bbox, only test pairs whose bboxes overlap. Typical n=200 case drops from 40k tests to a few hundred. The same bbox can be reused for the \`segments_to_objects\` neighbour search (see sibling issue).

title: Dual-tool roughing + finishing per op (T1 rough + TS finish with auto toolchange)
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.5 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's _I.cs every cut-path item carries TWO tool slots:
- T1 (Tool 1) — used for the roughing pass.
- TS (Tool Schlichten / finish) — used for the finishing pass.

When TS != T1, the gcode emitter automatically inserts M6 between rough and finish passes. The user picks the right combo per op (e.g. 6 mm rougher + 3 mm finisher on a contour); the toolchange is hidden.

wiac's Operation has one tool_id. To get the same effect today, a user has to duplicate the op (using rt1.x's new duplicate button), swap the tool on the copy, and adjust finish_step manually. Workable, but error-prone and breaks if the user later changes the depth.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs Operation: add finish_tool_id: Option<u32> (None = use the rough tool_id for the finish pass too — current behavior).

2. pipeline.rs::run_pipeline op loop: when finish_tool_id is Some(ts) AND ts != tool_id:
   - After the roughing offsets emit, emit a synthetic toolchange (M6 + spindle warmup) for the finish tool.
   - Run the finish pass (the level=0 wall-defining offset) with the finish tool's tool_radius, feed, speed.
   - Pick finish-pass feed/speed from the new per-tool finish-set fields (rt1.27).

3. Frontend OpPropertiesPanel: a second tool dropdown labeled 'Finish tool (optional)' below the existing tool select. Default empty = inherit. When set to a different tool, surface a tooltip 'toolchange will be inserted before the finish pass'.

4. Interaction with eb8.1 streaming: each tool gets its own OpProgress event so the user sees 'roughing — 6 mm endmill' followed by 'finishing — 3 mm endmill' on the progress bar.

5. Tests:
   - finish_tool_id_emits_toolchange
   - finish_tool_id_none_uses_single_tool
   - finish_tool_id_eq_rough_tool_id_skips_toolchange
   - round-trip serde

Estimated: 1 week. Algorithm is light; the per-tool finish-set integration (rt1.27) needs to land first OR be implemented in parallel.

Dependencies: rt1.27 (per-tool finish speeds/feeds) is the natural pair — without it, the finish tool inherits its general feeds which is usually wrong.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs lines 27-29 (T1/TS fields), 1259-1261 (auto-finish-with-same-tool case), 3380-3390 (Finishing_Same_Tool helper).
close_reason: Operation.finish_tool_id added; pocket_for_object now takes finish_ring_radius — dual-tool emits the wall ring at the finish tool's radius (smaller than rough); run_pipeline op driver detects dual-tool and splits the offsets list at is_finish, emits rough block with rough_setup, T<n> M6 toolchange, then finish block with finish-tool's setup; synthesize_finish_setup helper builds the second setup; finish-tool's finish-set rates win on the finish block (rt1.27 integration); supports_toolchange=false emits dual_tool_no_toolchange warning; op_cache_key_with_finish folds finish tool entry into the cache key so its props invalidate; PIPELINE_VERSION bumped to 4; OpPropertiesPanel: 'Finish tool' dropdown (pocket-only); 4 new tests (toolchange + finish feed, same_id skip, none skip, serde round-trip); 269 wiac-core + 94 FE tests pass.

title: File picker advertises hpgl/plt/ngc/stl but backend rejects — restrict to dxf/svg or add importers
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.4.

UX bug: FileUpload.svelte's open-file dialog filter lists `{ name: 'CAD/CAM input', extensions: ['dxf', 'svg', 'hpgl', 'plt', 'ngc', 'stl'] }` (App.svelte and tauri picker both). User picks an .hpgl file → backend's import_path returns 'unsupported file format' as a generic error.

Two paths:

**Option A (quick fix — file this issue as P2)**: filter the picker to the formats wiac actually supports today (dxf, svg). One-line change in FileUpload.svelte and the App.svelte dialog filter.

**Option B (longer)**: implement the importers. NGC re-import lets users preview existing gcode. HPGL/PLT covers laser/plotter workflows. STL is filed as 7f3 (deferred). Each is its own follow-up issue:
- NGC: parse G0/G1/G2/G3 via the existing preview interpreter, emit ToolpathSegments. (rt1.12+ish.)
- HPGL/PLT: read PD/PU/PA commands, emit lines. Niche; defer unless user demand.

Recommendation: ship Option A now (P2 — visible bug for user trials), file Option B importers as a P4 follow-up bundle.

Concrete plan for Option A:

1. frontend/src/lib/components/FileUpload.svelte line ~104 (Tauri filter) + line ~294 (input accept): keep only dxf, svg.
2. Re-check whether the .ngc workflow has any other entry point (it doesn't currently).

References:
- crates/wiac-core/src/input.rs lines 90-104 (only dxf/svg dispatch).
close_reason: FileUpload.svelte: file picker filter narrowed from [dxf,svg,hpgl,plt,ngc,stl] to [dxf,svg] (matches input.rs dispatch); input element accept= and drop-zone hint also updated. byd/rt1.32 remain as future-format follow-ups; when those land, re-extend the filter. FE typecheck + 94 tests pass.

title: Per-tool roughing / finishing / drilling speed-feed-plunge variants (3 distinct sets)
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.3 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's _TP enum carries THREE sets of speed/feed/plunge per tool:
- F / Fz / Rpm / Dpp (general / roughing)
- F_F / Fz_F / Rpm_F / Dpp_F (finishing pass)
- Fz_D / Rpm_D / Dpp_D + Peck (drilling)

Plus Tool_Wrapper.cs T_F / T_FZ / T_RPM / T_DPP accept a (bool F, bool D) pair so callers fetch the appropriate variant based on pass type.

wiac's ToolEntry today: a single speed / plunge_rate / feed_rate + default_step. The finish pass at op-level only varies Z step (finish_step). Hard-material workflows on hobby machines depend critically on a slower finish RPM / feed for surface quality.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs ToolEntry: extend with three optional override sets, each None-default to inherit the general value:
   - speed_finish, plunge_rate_finish, feed_rate_finish
   - speed_drill, plunge_rate_drill, feed_rate_drill, default_peck_step_mm
2. pipeline.rs::synthesize_op_setup: when emitting per-op tool setup, pick the variant by op kind: Drill picks drill set; the finish pass within a Pocket / Profile picks finish set; otherwise general.
3. emit_drill_block: feed/plunge passed from synthesize_op_setup already; just thread the picked variant.
4. Frontend ToolLibraryDialog: add three collapsible sub-sections ('General' / 'Finish' / 'Drill') with override inputs. Empty input = inherit. Italic placeholder shows the inherited value (mirroring the rt1.6 default_step pattern).
5. Tests:
   - finish_pass_uses_finish_rpm
   - drill_op_uses_drill_set
   - all_unset_falls_back_to_general

Estimated: 4-5 days. Mostly plumbing.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_TP.cs (enum variants), Tool_Wrapper.cs lines 55-200 (T_F / T_FZ / T_RPM / T_DPP with finish/drill bool selectors).
close_reason: ToolEntry extended with speed_finish/plunge_rate_finish/feed_rate_finish + _drill variants + default_peck_step_mm; new PassKind enum + resolve_tool_rates helper; ToolConfig carries resolved finish-set; PolylineOffset.is_finish flag tags Pocket wall ring at level=0; emit_offset + multi_pass switch to finish set when is_finish=true; Drill ops route through PassKind::Drill; tool peck cycles fall back to default_peck_step_mm; ToolLibraryDialog UI: collapsible Pass overrides panel; OpenAPI schema regenerated; pipeline_cache version bumped to 3; 7 new tests (resolve helper, finish ring uses finish RPM/feed, fallback when unset, drill set selection, peck fallback, serde round-trip) + all 262 wiac-core + 94 FE tests pass.

title: Schlichtzugabe: XY finish stock allowance per pocket op (different from Z finish_step)
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.2 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's _I.cs line 85: every pocket / profile item carries a Schlichtzugabe_Soll value — the XY thickness of material LEFT UNCUT during the roughing pass, removed by the dedicated finishing pass. Standard CAM workflow: rough at 0.2 mm offset, finish at 0 mm. Roughing runs fast and heavy, the finish takes a thin chip for surface quality.

wiac has finish_step (a Z-direction smaller-step parameter, smaller LAST cut) and finish_cut_direction (climb/conventional for the wall-defining pass). These cover the BOTTOM finish but not the WALL finish stock allowance.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs OperationParams: add finish_xy_allowance_mm: Option<f64>. Default None = no allowance (current behavior). Some(x) = roughing pass shrinks the boundary by x; a final finish pass walks the original boundary.

2. cam/offsets.rs pocket_for_object: when finish_xy_allowance_mm is Some, run the existing pocket algorithm against a boundary inset by allowance + tool_radius. Then emit an additional finish-pass PolylineOffset along the actual boundary at level=0 (the wall-defining pass).

3. pipeline.rs: route the new finish-pass offset through the existing finish_cut_direction logic so the wall pass picks its winding from finish_cut_direction.

4. Frontend OpPropertiesPanel: add 'XY finish stock' number input under the existing 'Z finish step' field, with mm unit chip. Tooltip: 'Material left uncut on the walls by roughing passes. The dedicated finish pass walks the actual boundary to remove it.'

5. Tests:
   - pocket_finish_xy_allowance_emits_extra_boundary_pass
   - round-trip serde
   - integration: a closed square with allowance=0.3 produces a roughing boundary at -0.3 + a finish boundary at 0.

Estimated: 4-5 days. Algorithm is small; the test fixtures + frontend wiring take more time than the math.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs line 85, 196 (Schlichtzugabe_Soll affects Anfahrpunkt offset), 459 (carried across clones).
close_reason: OperationParams.finish_xy_allowance_mm added; pocket_for_object now takes xy_allowance — rough cascade walks an inset boundary at (tool_radius + allowance), dedicated finish ring at tool_radius tagged is_finish; greedy_nearest_among tiebreak prefers non-finish before finish at equal d+level so finish wall runs last; OpPropertiesPanel: XY finish stock input under Finish step (pocket-only); 3 new tests (extra boundary pass, finish ring uses finish feed end-to-end, serde round-trip); 265 wiac-core tests pass.

title: Implement OperationKind::Chamfer (Prog_Fasen / Kontur_Fase / Bohrloch_Fase)
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.1 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's Prog_Fasen (_I.cs line 2093) drives a V-bit or chamfer tool along part edges to break sharp corners. Two variants:
- Prog_Kontur_Fase (line 2124) — chamfer along a profile contour. Drives the cutter at a partial depth along the offset path so the cone cuts the edge bevel.
- Prog_Bohrloch_Fase (line 2184) — chamfer around a drilled-hole rim. Walks a small circle at partial depth.

wiac has OperationKind::Chamfer declared but pipeline.rs raises UnimplementedKind. The variant currently carries no fields.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs: extend Chamfer to Chamfer { chamfer_width_mm: f64, finish_pass: bool }. The chamfer width sets the partial depth at which the V-bit walks the contour. finish_pass is a second light cut for surface quality.

2. cam/chamfer.rs (new file): for each closed boundary in the source set, walk the offset path at z computed from the V-bit cone angle and the desired chamfer_width_mm:
       z = -chamfer_width_mm / tan(half_apex_rad)
   Like V-Carve but at constant z along the boundary, not varying.

3. pipeline.rs: route OperationKind::Chamfer to chamfer::emit_chamfer. Mirror V-Carve dispatcher shape.

4. For drilled-hole chamfers: when the source object is a closed circle smaller than the chamfer tool's working diameter, emit a tiny circular pass at the computed depth instead of an offset contour.

5. Tests:
   - chamfer::tests::partial_depth_from_width
   - chamfer::tests::drilled_hole_circular_pass
   - pipeline integration: closed square + Chamfer op emits an inset boundary at the expected depth.

6. Frontend (OpPropertiesPanel.svelte): when op.kind === 'chamfer', expose chamfer_width_mm + finish_pass. Require ToolKind::VBit.

Estimated: 3-5 days. Algorithm is simpler than V-Carve (constant-depth pass, no medial axis needed).

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs lines 2093-2220.
close_reason: OperationKind::Chamfer now carries width_mm + finish_pass fields (defaults 1.0 / false; legacy unit-variant payloads deserialize cleanly via serde defaults). cam/chamfer.rs added with chamfer_depth(width_mm, tip_angle_deg) helper (z = -width / tan(half_apex)); 4 unit tests. pipeline.rs synthesize_op_setup overrides depth/start_depth/step for Chamfer ops so multi_pass emits a single constant-Z pass; chamfer_non_vbit warning when tool isn't a V-bit; rt1.27 finish-set rates kick in for the optional finish pass; build_op_offsets emits source-path PolylineOffsets (no XY offset; cutter walks the contour like Engrave); pipeline_cache.hash_operation_kind hashes width_mm + finish_pass too. OpPropertiesPanel: Chamfer fieldset with Width + Finish pass inputs + tool-kind warn. 3 new pipeline tests (depth Z-1.732 for 60° V-bit + 1mm, finish_pass dual-feed, non-V-bit warning); 276 wiac-core + 94 FE tests pass.

title: Implement OperationKind::Thread (internal + external helical thread cutting)
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.1 against Estlcam.

Estlcam ships internal-thread (`Prog_IG` / `Prog_AG` in `_I.cs` line 1098/1150) and helical descent (`Prog_Spirale` line 2012). wiac's OperationKind has the Thread variant declared but pipeline.rs raises `UnimplementedKind(Thread)` — the dispatch doesn't exist.

Concrete plan:

1. **`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/thread.rs`** (new file): a helical-thread emitter. Takes a closed circular boundary, a thread tool (pitch, lead, depth), and produces a helical toolpath:
   - Walk N revolutions around the boundary's inscribed circle.
   - Z descends linearly by `pitch` per revolution.
   - Each revolution emits a G2 (or chord-tessellated G1) at constant Z step.
   - Internal vs external = inset (tool inside boundary) vs offset (tool outside).

2. **`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs`**: extend OperationKind::Thread variant with fields:
   
   Or add a separate ThreadConfig struct similar to DrillCycle for future extensibility (passes, finishing-pass enable, etc.).

3. **`crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs`**: route OperationKind::Thread to thread::emit_thread instead of returning UnimplementedKind. Mirror the V-Carve dispatcher's shape (rt1.1's run_vcarve_op).

4. **Tests** (`cargo test -p wiac-core --lib`):
   - thread::tests::single_revolution_at_pitch_descends_z
   - thread::tests::internal_thread_inside_circle
   - thread::tests::external_thread_outside_circle
   - pipeline integration: a Thread op on a closed circle emits arcs descending Z

5. **Frontend** (`OpPropertiesPanel.svelte`): when op.kind === 'thread', show pitch_mm + internal-vs-external radio. Tool kind must be 'thread mill' (new ToolKind variant) or carbide single-point — surface a tool_kind_mismatch warning chip if a generic endmill is assigned.

Estimated: ~1 week (algorithm + UI + post-processor coverage).

References:
- Estlcam decompile: `/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs` lines 1085-1224 (Prog_Thread / IG / AG), 1891-2055 (Prog_Spirale).
- Helical descent for plunging into the pocket is already shipped (rt1.2 inscribed_circle + multi_pass helix). Thread-cutting is the SAME motion shape but emitted as the primary toolpath rather than plunge.

Tool-library follow-up: add ToolKind::ThreadMill so the kind-mismatch warnings make sense.
close_reason: OperationKind::Thread now carries pitch_mm + internal + climb fields (defaults 1.0 / true / false; legacy unit-variant payloads still parse via serde defaults). cam/thread.rs added with helix_waypoints (XYZ tessellation along a helix); 6 unit tests (descent, on-circle, climb direction, multi-rev, degenerate). pipeline.rs: new run_thread_op driver (parallel to run_vcarve_op) that walks closed-circle source objects, picks internal/external radius via bore ± tool_radius, emits via emit_vcarve_block (existing XYZ polyline emitter). thread_no_circles / thread_tool_too_large / thread_no_depth warnings cover misuse. pipeline_cache.hash_operation_kind hashes the new fields. OpPropertiesPanel: Thread fieldset with Pitch / Direction (internal/external) / Climb inputs. 3 new pipeline tests (helical descent on a circle, no-circle warning, oversized-tool warning); 285 wiac-core + 94 FE tests pass.

title: Audit: Cut-path features (tabs, leads, plunge, finishing, climb, multi-tool)
description:
## What

Audit Estlcam's **cut-path features**: tabs, leads, plunge/entry strategies, finishing pass behavior, climb/conventional handling, multi-tool sequencing, depth scheduling. These are the knobs that turn "a shape" into "a toolpath that doesn't break bits". Produce the `## Cut-path features` section of the parity doc.

## Decompile sources to read

1. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs`** — most of this. Key methods:
   - `Prog_Normale_Kontur` (1266) — main contour driver
   - `Prog_Simple_Kontur` (1242) — simple-form driver
   - `Prog_Sin_Tab_Kontur` (1374) — tab variant
   - `Dive_Forward` (1452) — ramp-along-contour entry. See `wiaconstructor-rt1` discussion of Estlcam's finishing-pass approach for context.
   - `Helix_2_Level` (1981) — helix entry
   - `Z_Levels` (1576), `Create_Z_Levels` (1545), `Fasen_Levels` (1609) — Z step scheduling
   - `Flüchten` (2038) — "escape" move at end of cut
   - `Bogenüberleitung` (2080) — arc transition
   - `Has_Anfahrpunkt`, `Anfahrpunkt`, `Startpunkt`, `Has_Startpunkt` — approach/start point semantics
2. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_Gcode.cs`** — `Anfahren` (843), `Eintauchen` (856), `G00_Sicher` (391) — entry/exit machinery.
3. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_Parallelräumer.cs:374-425`** — `Direkt_Anfahrbar_LL` + `Taschenanfahrt_LL` — direct-vs-retract decision for pocket entries.

## German terms to grep

```
Tab / Anbindung / Tab_Rounded / Sin_Tab
Lead / Anfahr / Abfahr / Eintauch / Bogenüberleitung
Plunge_Angle / Eintauchstrecke / Helix / Spirale
Schlichten / Finishing_Same_Tool / Direkt_Schlichten
Anfahrpunkt / Startpunkt / Anfahren / G00_Sicher
Gleichlauf / Climb / Conventional
Fasen_Levels / Z_Anbindung / Fase
Inseln / Multi.tool / Tool.change
Fortsetzung / Continuation
Through / Durchbruch
```

## wiac code to compare against

- **`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/setup.rs`** — `TabsConfig`, `LeadsConfig`, `PlungeStrategy`, `MillConfig` (depth / step / finish_step / through_depth / depth_list).
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:OperationParams`** — has cut-direction, plunge, leads, tabs, overcut, finish-direction, feed/plunge overrides, corner-feed-reduction, finish_step, through_depth, depth_list.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:48`** — `attach_tabs_to_offsets`.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:419-470`** — `enforce_winding`, `apply_cut_direction`.
- Existing planned issues:
  - `wiaconstructor-rt1.2` (auto helix radius)
  - `wiaconstructor-rt1.10` (interactive tab placement)
  - `wiaconstructor-rt1.11` (two-sided machining)
  - `wiaconstructor-rt1.6` (per-tool default step)

## What to catalog

| Category | Estlcam feature | wiac status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tabs** | Rectangular tab (`T_Tab_Rounded == false`) | ✅ | TabType::Rectangle |
| | Rounded tab (`T_Tab_Rounded == true`) | ✅ | TabType::Ramp |
| | Sinusoidal-Z tab (`Prog_Sin_Tab_Kontur`) | ❌? or ⏳? | Different shape — Z varies sinusoidally over tab length. Useful for low-vibration cuts. Decide. |
| | Manual placement on contour | ⏳ | rt1.10 |
| | Per-tab width / height override | check | Estlcam likely allows; wiac plans (rt1.10). |
| **Leads** | Off / Straight / Arc | ✅ | LeadKind |

| **Finishing pass** | Same-tool auto-finish on contour | ✅ | finish_cut_direction + finish_step |
| | Finish pass on pocket walls only (not interior) | ✅ | Confirmed — Estlcam's `Prog_Räumen` finishes wall-only via `Prog_Simple_Kontur(Schlichten:true)` |

## Method

Same as previous audits.

## Deliverable

## Follow-up issues filed by this audit

- rt1.33 (P2) dual-tool roughing + finishing per op (T1 + TS auto-toolchange)
- rt1.34 (P4) insert-pause op (M0 / optional stop)

## Net assessment

wiac at session-end has parity on tabs, leads, plunge, Z scheduling, climb/conventional, and almost all single-tool cut-path features. title: Audit: Tool table & tool subtypes
description:
## What

Audit Estlcam's **tool table**: every per-tool field, every "tool subtype" (V-bit / chamfer / form / drill / laser), every tool-aware setting that affects toolpath math. Produce the `## Tool table & tool subtypes` section of the parity doc.

This audit is the second-most important after operations — wiac's `ToolEntry` is already a sensible base, but Estlcam stores many *per-tool* knobs that wiac stores per-op. Identifying these is what unlocks shareable tool libraries.

## Decompile sources to read

1. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs`** — the canonical accessor for per-tool data. Grep:
   ```
   grep -nE "public static.*T_" /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs | head -80
   ```
   You'll see ~30-50 `T_*` getters. Each is a tool field worth a row.
2. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_TT.cs`** (`grep -rn "enum _TT\b"`) — tool-type enum. Likely values: `End`, `Ball`, `Gravur`, `Fase`, `Profil`, `Obenunten`, `Drill`, `Laser`, `DragKnife`. Catalog them all.
3. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_TLS.cs`** — tool list / library storage.
4. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_TP.cs`** — tool-parameter enum (e.g. `Cool_Mist`, `Cool_Flood`, `H_Cut`, `Comment`). Inspect the values.
5. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/dlg_TLO.cs`** — tool library editor dialog. Look at every field the user can edit.
6. Search for `T_R_Final`, `T_D_Final` — wear-compensated radius/diameter. Already filed as `wiaconstructor-rt1.14`; verify wiac's planned schema matches Estlcam's semantics.

## Searches to run

```
grep -nE "T_R\b|T_D\b|T_R_Final|T_D_Final" /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs
grep -nE "T_RPM|T_F\b|T_FZ|T_DPP|T_Räumzustellung|T_Schlichtzugabe" /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs
grep -nE "T_Plunge_Angle|T_Eintauchstrecke|T_Pierce_Time|T_Step_Height" /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs
grep -nE "T_Wirbeln|T_Wirbel_Stepover|T_Laser|T_Tab_Rounded|T_Nr|T_Typ" /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs
grep -nE "T_R2Z|T_Fasenabstand" /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs
```

For each `T_*` getter you find, decide where the data lives in `_TLS` (the actual tool table) — usually `Globale_Variablen.TLS.GV(_TP.X, T)` (numeric) or `GS(_TP.X, T)` (string).

## wiac code to compare against

- **`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:43`** — `ToolEntry { id, name, kind, diameter, tip_diameter, tip_angle_deg, dragoff, flutes, speed, plunge_rate, feed_rate, coolant }`. ~12 fields.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:83`** — `ToolKind { Endmill, BallNose, VBit, Engraver, DragKnife, Drill, LaserBeam }`.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/sim/heightmap.rs:142`** — `ToolProfile` (the simulator's per-tool geometry). Closely linked.
- Existing planned schema extensions:
  - `wiaconstructor-rt1.6` adds `ToolEntry.default_step`
  - `wiaconstructor-rt1.14` adds `wear_offset_mm`, `last_calibrated`
  - `wiaconstructor-rs8.3` adds `flute_length_mm`, `shank_diameter_mm`, `holder: Option<HolderShape>`
  - `wiaconstructor-bv6` adds UI hint for overrides
  - `wiaconstructor-dr5` adds `default_xy_overlap`

Build the table after applying all of these mentally.

## What to catalog

For each Estlcam `T_*` field:

```
| Estlcam field        | wiac field                              | Status | Notes |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------------|--------|-------|
| T_D / T_R            | diameter                                | ✅     | — |
| T_D_Final / T_R_Final| diameter (effective via wear_offset_mm) | ⏳     | rt1.14 |
| T_RPM (rough/finish/drill variants) | speed                    | partial| Estlcam has 3 distinct RPM values per tool. wiac stores one. File a follow-up. |
| T_F (rough/finish/drill variants)   | feed_rate                | partial| Same — 3 distinct feed rates. File a follow-up. |
| T_FZ (rough/finish/drill variants)  | plunge_rate              | partial| Same. File a follow-up. |
| T_DPP (rough/finish/drill variants) | default_step (planned)   | partial| rt1.6 covers default; per-variant likely needs new issue. |
| T_Räumzustellung     | (no equivalent; computed)               | ⏳     | rt1.6/dr5 partially? File if not covered. |
| T_Schlichtzugabe     | finish_step (?)                         | check  | Estlcam's "stock for finish" is per-tool; wiac's finish_step is per-op. Different semantics. File. |
| T_Plunge_Angle       | PlungeStrategy::Ramp { angle_deg } (per-op) | partial | Per-tool vs per-op mismatch; file if making per-tool default makes sense. |
| T_Eintauchstrecke    | (derived; entry ramp length)            | ❌? or ⏳? | Per-tool entry ramp length. Decide. |
| T_Pierce_Time        | (no field)                              | ⏳     | Laser pierce-delay. File. |
| T_Step_Height        | (no field)                              | ⏳     | 3D step-height for ball-nose roughing. Likely out of scope unless STL roughing lands. |
| T_Wirbeln + T_Wirbel_Stepover | (no field, see rt1.4)           | partial| Auto-chip-thinning. Different from explicit Trochoidal. File. |
| T_Tab_Rounded        | TabsConfig.tab_type                     | ✅     | Maps Ramp ↔ Rounded. |
| T_R2Z                | (computed from tip_angle_deg)           | ✅     | wiac computes on demand. |
| T_Fasenabstand       | (no field)                              | ⏳     | Chamfer-offset for `_TT.Fase` tools. File. |
| flute_length_mm      | (planned)                               | ⏳     | rs8.3 |
| shank_diameter_mm    | (planned)                               | ⏳     | rs8.3 |
| holder (cone/cylinder)| (planned)                              | ⏳     | rs8.3 |
| Mist / Flood         | coolant                                 | ✅     | — |
| Comment              | (no field; name is the only string)     | check  | Is a free-text comment per tool useful? Probably yes. File or wontfix. |
```

For each `_TT` value (tool subtype) like `Gravur`, `Fase`, `Obenunten`, `Profil`: row how wiac models it.

- `Gravur` (engraving V-bit) ≡ `ToolKind::Engraver`
- `Fase` (chamfer V-bit) ≡ `ToolKind::VBit` (same shape, different intent)
- `Obenunten` (top+bottom chamfer) → no wiac equivalent; file
- `Profil` (form tool with custom profile) → no wiac equivalent; file as ❌ unless someone asks

## Method

Same as the previous audits. Build the table; file gap issues under `wiaconstructor-rt1` with label `parity-audit`; replace placeholders with bd ids.

## Deliverable

1. `## Tool table & tool subtypes` section in `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md`.
2. Aim for 25-35 rows.
3. New gap issues filed under `wiaconstructor-rt1`.
4. Summary note on this issue.

## Anti-goals

- Do not propose tool-table schema changes in this issue. The audit identifies gaps; the gap issue proposes the schema change. (Exception: trivial 1-field adds like adding a `comment` string can be filed as a single-line gap issue.)

## Time budget

1.5-2 days.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `wiaconstructor-fpa1.1` (operations audit ships the doc file).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `## Tool table & tool subtypes` section in parity doc.
- [ ] All `T_*` getters rowed.
- [ ] All `_TT` subtype values rowed.
- [ ] Gap issues filed.
- [ ] Summary note on this issue.

title: Audit: Pocketing strategies & parameters
description:
## What

Audit Estlcam's **pocketing strategies and parameters**: every value of the `_PK` (`Räumstrategie`) enum, every per-strategy tuning knob, plus the parameters that affect *all* pockets (stepover, finish allowance, climb, chip-thinning, etc.). Produce the `## Pocketing strategies & parameters` section of `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md`.

## Decompile sources to read

1. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_PK.cs`** (or wherever the `_PK` enum lives). Find with:
   ```
   grep -rn "enum _PK\b" /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/
   ```
   Known values: `Parallel`, `Peel`, `Peel_I`, `Peel_O`, `Linear_X`, `Linear_Y`, `Halfpipe`. Verify the complete list.
2. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_Parallelräumer.cs`** — pocket orchestrator. Key methods: `Prog_Pocket_Loadlimiting` (line 438), `Prog_Konturfolgend` (646), `Prog_Fallback` (742), `Calc` (277), `Direkt_Anfahrbar_LL` (374), `Taschenanfahrt_LL` (407). For each strategy, document what method handles it and what parameters it consumes.
3. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_DBB.cs`** — bitmap-based pocket engine (the actual offsetting). For audit purposes you don't need the algorithm; you need to know it exists and what parameters it takes (`Auflösung = Zustellung / Präzisionsfaktor`, `Präzisionsfaktor = 50.0`).
4. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_Räumkontur.cs`** — clearing-pass data model.
5. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs`** — tool-side pocket params: grep for `Räumzustellung`, `Wirbeln`, `Wirbel_Stepover`, `Schlichtzugabe`, `Plunge_Angle`, `DPP`.
6. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs`** — the Item's pocket-related fields: `Räumstrategie`, `Räumen`, `Schlichtzugabe_Soll`, `Anfahrpunkt`, `Inseln`. Also `Helix_2_Level` (1981) for helix entry, `Prog_Spirale` (2012) for the spiral entry pattern.

## German terms to grep for

```
Räumstrategie / Räumen / Räumkontur / Räumzustellung / Räumer
Schlicht / Schlichten / Schlichtzugabe
Anfahrpunkt / Anfahren / Eintauchen / Eintauchpunkt
Zustellung / Wirbeln / Wirbel_Stepover
Konturfolgend / Loadlimiting
Gleichlauf / Helix / Spirale
Inseln / Boundary / Boundaysegments
Plunge_Angle / Eintauchstrecke
```

## wiac code to compare against

- **`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:234`** — `PocketStrategy { Cascade, Zigzag, Spiral }`. Will grow with `Trochoidal` (rt1.4) and `LinearAngled` (rt1.9).
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:524`** — `pocket_for_object` strategy dispatch.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:179-450`** — zigzag, cascade, spiral implementations.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/setup.rs:159`** — `PocketConfig { islands, zigzag, insideout, nocontour }`.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:OperationParams`** — `xy_overlap`, `finish_step`, `helix`, `cut_direction`, `finish_cut_direction`, `plunge`.
- Existing planned issues: `wiaconstructor-rt1.2` (auto helix radius), `rt1.3` (Pocket-Outside), `rt1.4` (Trochoidal), `rt1.6` (per-tool default step), `rt1.9` (linear pocket angle).

## What to catalog

For each Estlcam `_PK` value:

- What it does conceptually (1 sentence).
- What tool parameters it consumes (which `Tool_Wrapper.T_*` calls).
- What item parameters (Schlichtzugabe, Anfahrpunkt, …).
- The wiac equivalent strategy (with caveats about parameter differences).

Specific oddities to flag:

- **Estlcam `Parallel` uses `Konturfolgend`** (contour-parallel). But wiac calls its analogous strategy `Cascade`/`Spiral`. The name "Parallel" is overloaded. Document the mapping.
- **Estlcam `Peel` overrides the user's strategy when no islands**: `_Parallelräumer.cs:447` — `Item.Räumstrategie` is silently overridden to `Peel`. Document this Estlcam-specific quirk so the parity row notes it.
- **Halfpipe** is unusual: a slot-cutting pattern that goes back and forth. Decide if wiac users need it; if yes, file a follow-up; if no, mark ❌ with reason "niche slot-machining, deferred until requested".
- **Wirbeln** (chip-thinning trochoidal *per tool*): a per-tool boolean that enables a trochoidal-flavored stepover when the engagement falls below tool-radius/2. Different from `rt1.4`'s explicit Trochoidal strategy — `Wirbeln` is automatic, strategy-agnostic. Decide how to map this; may merit a new issue.
- **Schlichtzugabe** (finish stock allowance): wiac doesn't have an explicit "stock-for-finish" per-op field; the finish offset is implicit in the pass schedule. Verify. If missing, file a new issue.
- **Plunge_Angle** per tool: see how it's used. Compare to `PlungeStrategy::Ramp { angle_deg }` (per-op) — the tool/op distinction matters.

## Method

Follow the same procedure as `wiaconstructor-fpa1.1` (the operations audit): build the comparison table; mark each row ✅ / 🟡 / ⏳ / ❌ / n/a; file new gap issues where needed.

Suggested row count for this section: 25-40 (every strategy × variant × parameter).

## Deliverable

1. Append a `## Pocketing strategies & parameters` section to `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md`.
2. File gap issues for any unmapped strategy / parameter under `wiaconstructor-rt1` with label `cam,estlcam-merge,parity-audit`.
3. Summary note on this issue with counts.

## Anti-goals

- Do not document the **algorithm** for each strategy. That's for the implementation issue (`rt1.4` etc.) — and the algorithm there must come from public sources, not the decompile. The audit only catalogs *that the feature exists*, its *UX shape*, and its *parameter names*.
- Do not copy parameter formulas like `main_overlap = 1 - sin(angle/2)` — those are public-knowledge but should appear in the implementation issue (rt1.4 has it already), not in the audit doc.

## Time budget

1.5-2 days.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by audit `wiaconstructor-fpa1.1` (operations & project structure) — it ships the `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md` file. This audit appends a section.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `## Pocketing strategies & parameters` section in the parity doc.
- [ ] All 7 known `_PK` values rowed.
- [ ] All pocket-related per-tool params from `Tool_Wrapper` rowed.
- [ ] All pocket-related per-item params rowed.
- [ ] Every ⏳ links to an issue; every ❌ has a one-sentence reason.
- [ ] Findings summary appended to issue notes.

title: Audit: Operations & project structure
description:
## What

Audit Estlcam's catalog of **operation kinds** (what kinds of toolpaths can you create) and **project structure** (how multiple operations + objects are organized). Produce the first section of `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md`.

## Decompile sources to read

Read in this order:

1. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_KT.cs`** (if present) — operation/object-type enum. May be named `_KT`, `c_KT`, or similar. Find it via:
   ```
   grep -nr "enum _KT\|enum.*KT" /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/ | head
   ```
   Values: typically `Hole`, `Part`, `Engraving`, `Drill`, `Carve`, `Halfpipe`, `Circular_Pocket`, `Linear_X`, etc. Catalog them.
2. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs`** — the milling-object class. Massive (~3500 LOC). Of interest: `Prog_*` methods (one per operation kind), `Typ` field, `Räumstrategie` field, `Groups`, `Inseln`, `Machining_ID`, `Text_ID`. Skim `Prog_Räumen` (3515), `Prog_Normale_Kontur` (1266), `Prog_Simple_Kontur` (1242), `Prog_Carve`, `Prog_Halfpipe`, `Prog_Braille_Dome` (2057), `Prog_Drill_*`, `Spiralbohrung` (1891 — helical thread).
3. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Beschriftungsfunktionen.cs`** — text-as-operation styles (`_SS.Engraving / Carve_Inside / Carve_Outside / Pocket_Inside / Pocket_Outside / Outside / Inside / Layer`).
4. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_Carve.cs`**, **`c_Carveprogger.cs`**, **`m_Carve.cs`** — V-carve specifics (the rt1.1 issue describes the algorithm in detail; for this audit just catalog UX).
5. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_Rotationskörper.cs`** — 4th-axis / lathe operation, if present.
6. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_QR.cs`**, **`_Dowel.cs`**, **`_Gehrung.cs`**, **`c_Laserengraver.cs`** — specialty operations.
7. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Gruppierungen.cs`** — group / hierarchy semantics.
8. The `dlg_*` files for any "Add X" dialog — `dlg_Inlay.cs`, `dlg_Dowel.cs`, `dlg_Gehrung.cs`, `dlg_QR.cs`, `dlg_RO.cs` (rotation body), `dlg_BS.cs` (back-side machining?), `dlg_Pic_Select.cs` (raster source picker).

## German terms to grep for in the decompile

```
grep -rn "Räumen\|Bohren\|Fasen\|Spirale\|Halfpipe\|Gravur\|Carve\|Inlay\|Gehrung\|Dowel\|Drill\|Engrav\|Thread\|Profil\|Rotation" /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/ | wc -l
```
will give you a count of relevant hits per term. Pick terms with high counts; those are real features.

Cross-reference each `Prog_*` method in `_I.cs` to its operation kind — `Prog_Räumen` is pocketing, `Prog_Drill_KT` is drilling, etc.

## wiac code to compare against

- **`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:176`** — `OperationKind` enum. Today: `Profile / Pocket / Drill / Thread / Chamfer / Engrave / DragKnife / Helix` (+ planned: `VCarve / Inlay / RasterEngrave` from rt1).
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:83`** — `ToolKind` enum.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/setup.rs`** — operation-aware setup tree.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs`** — `OperationKind` dispatch logic; find with `grep -nE "OperationKind::" crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs`.
- **`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/source_combine.rs`** — selection / combine logic. Roughly maps to Estlcam's `Inseln` (islands).
- Existing planned issues: `wiaconstructor-rt1.*` covers V-Carve / Inlay / RasterEngrave / QR / Pocket-Outside / Add Text / two-sided / linear pocket angle. Audit verifies these cover the actual Estlcam surface.

## Method

For each Estlcam operation kind found, write a row:

```
| Estlcam feature | wiac status | Where in wiac | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Räumen (Parallel)        | ✅       | OperationKind::Pocket{Spiral}      | Konturfolgend strategy in Estlcam ≡ Spiral in wiac |
| Räumen (Peel)            | ⏳       | rt1.2 + rt1.4 covers      | Helix-entry pocket; helix-radius auto from inscribed circle |
| Räumen (Halfpipe)        | ❌? or ⏳? | —          | Slot-machining trick; unsure if hobby users need this. Decide. |
| Carve_Inside             | ⏳       | rt1.1 + rt1.5            | V-carve flow |
| Drill (helical-thread)   | partial  | OperationKind::Thread    | Verify wiac's helical-thread matches Estlcam's Spiralbohrung |
| Braille_Dome             | ❌       | —                        | Niche. Won't do unless someone asks. |
| Rotation body (lathe)    | ❌       | —                        | 4th-axis is out of scope; document in epic out-of-scope list. |
```

Status decisions:
- ✅ if a wiac OperationKind covers it with the same parameter shape.
- 🟡 if there's an open PR.
- ⏳ if an `rt1.*` / standalone issue covers it.
- ❌ if it's out of scope (document the reason in one sentence).
- n/a for controller-side things — but for operations this shouldn't apply much.

If you find a feature that is **not** in any existing wiac issue and is in scope:
1. Mark the row ⏳ with a placeholder.
2. File a new bd issue under `wiaconstructor-rt1` (the wiaconcam epic). Use this issue command pattern:
   ```bash
   bd create --title="<feature>" --type=feature --priority=3 --parent=wiaconstructor-rt1 \
     --labels=cam,estlcam-merge,parity-audit \
     --description="Surfaced by parity audit <this-issue>. <one-paragraph description of the Estlcam feature based on decompile reading>" \
     --deps "discovered-from:<this-issue>"
   ```
3. Replace the placeholder with the new issue id.

If you find a feature that's **already covered** by an `rt1.*` / `rs8.*` / `eb8.*` issue: link it without filing a new one.

If you find a feature that's **out of scope**: mark ❌ and write the reason in the row's Notes column. Don't file.

## Deliverable

1. Create `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md` (this audit ships the file; subsequent audits append their sections). Include the legend from the parent epic at the top.
2. Add a `## Operations & project structure` section with the comparison table. Aim for 20-40 rows in this section.
3. Append a one-line summary of findings to this issue's notes: "N rows total, K filed new (ids: …), M marked won't-do."
4. Link the new gap issues you filed in this issue's notes too.

## Anti-goals

- Do not write any new Rust or TypeScript in this issue. Cataloging only.
- Do not estimate time for the filed gap issues. The gap issues themselves get effort estimates when they're claimed.
- Do not editorialize on Estlcam's algorithm choices — that's not parity-audit work. Note UX and parameter shapes only.

## Time budget

- Reading the decompile sources: 0.5 day.
- Producing the table: 0.5-1 day.
- Filing follow-up gap issues: depends on count; typically 0.5 day for ~10 new issues.

Total: 1.5-2 days. If the audit takes longer than 3 days, you're going too deep — pull back to UX-level cataloging.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md` exists with the operations section populated.
- [ ] Table has at least 20 rows.
- [ ] Every ⏳ row links to a bd issue id.
- [ ] Every ❌ row has a one-sentence reason.
- [ ] One reviewer (anyone with bd access) signs off that the table is coherent.
- [ ] No code ported from the decompile (visual check of any gap issues filed).
acceptance_criteria: docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md created with operations section; ≥20 rows; every ⏳ links to bd issue; every ❌ has reason; one reviewer signoff; no code ported.

title: Estlcam feature-parity audit
description:
## What

Systematically catalog every Estlcam CAM feature and compare it against wiaconstructor's state today. The deliverable is **one living document**, `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md`, structured as a comparison table per subsystem. Each table row maps an Estlcam feature to either ✅ (in wiac main), 🟡 (PR open), ⏳ (issue filed), ❌ (won't do — with reason), or n/a (Estlcam-only and irrelevant). The work is meta: junior developers read the decompile, compare against wiac code, and *file follow-up issues* for each new gap they discover — they do **not implement features** in this epic.

Why now: we've filed ~36 known-gap issues across `rt1` / `rs8` / `eb8` / `kt2`, but those came from a partial-by-eye scan of the decompile. A systematic audit catches what we missed. It also produces the user-facing migration reference (`kt2.5`) needs.

## Hard constraints

- **Do not port code from the Estlcam decompile.** The decompile lives at `/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/` (407 .cs files, partially obfuscated, originally VB.NET). It is a *requirements catalog*, not a source of algorithm code. wiaconstructor is GPL-3; copying structure from a proprietary decompile is an IP risk. This rule is also stored in bd memory (`bd memories estlcam`). The audit tasks reinforce it; junior devs reading this epic must understand it.
- Document UX, parameter names, behavior — never copy algorithm code.
- Each audit task produces a section of `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md` and, separately, one follow-up gap issue per ⏳ row that doesn't already have one. Existing `rt1.*` / `rs8.*` / `eb8.*` issues count.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- Implementation. The follow-up gap issues are filed; the work is done in later sprints.
- CNC-controller-side Estlcam features (`Estlcam13_CNC.exe` — joystick, ATC, hotkeys, firmware, EEPROM). wiaconstructor is CAM-only; these are n/a.
- License / DRM features in Estlcam (the obfuscated `īiī` / `íìì` / `ïĭī` classes). n/a.

## Children — one audit task per subsystem

1. Operations & project structure
2. Pocketing strategies & parameters
3. Tool table & tool subtypes
4. Geometry input formats
5. Cut-path features (tabs, leads, plunge, entry, finishing, climb, multi-tool)
6. Post-processor framework & G-code emission
7. Simulation, preview, caching
8. CAD-light editing & transforms
9. UI, dialogs, workflows, hotkeys, i18n

## The artifact

`docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md` (created by the first audit task to land; subsequent ones append). One section per audit, each with a comparison table. Top of the file: legend, last-updated date, link to this epic.

Status legend:

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✅ | In main today — link the wiac code path |
| 🟡 | PR open — link the PR |
| ⏳ | Issue filed — link the bd id |
| ❌ | Won't do — one-sentence reason |
| n/a | Estlcam-only feature, irrelevant to wiac (controller side, DRM, etc.) |

Example row:

| Estlcam feature | wiac status | Where in wiac | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| V-Carve (Carve_Inside) | ⏳ | `wiaconstructor-rt1.1` | Medial-axis based; rt1.1 in flight |
| Pocket strategy: Konturfolgend | ✅ | `cam/offsets.rs:pocket_cascade` | Maps to Cascade strategy |
| Tool length sensor probing | n/a | — | Controller-side, out of scope |

## Acceptance

- All 9 children closed.
- `docs/feature-parity-estlcam.md` exists, linked from `README.md` Documentation section and from `kt2.5` (Estlcam migration guide — they share content; the migration guide becomes a curated narrative view, the parity doc is the exhaustive table).
- Every ⏳-marked feature has a filed issue (new or existing).
- The 9 audits collectively cover the entire Estlcam decompile class list (verify by spot-checking a few un-mentioned classes).
- One outside reviewer (an Estlcam user from the maker community) reads the doc and confirms no major category is missing.

title: UI: Scene3D should always show translucent stock box, not only in sim mode
description:
StockPanel lets the user set stock dimensions (mode/margin/customX/Y/thickness), but the Scene3D doesn't visualize the stock envelope unless sim is active. The user can't see whether their toolpath fits the stock without enabling sim playback.

CAM users expect a translucent box (the work envelope) visible at all times in the 3D view, so they can:
- Sanity-check that the import is positioned within the stock.
- See clearance between the toolpath and stock edges.
- Catch 'this op cuts off the side of the workpiece' before generating.

Fix: render a semi-transparent box in Scene3D from project.stock dimensions (computed via the existing footprint logic from sim/driver.ts's computeFootprint). Stock bottom at z = -thickness, top at z = 0. Use a low opacity (~0.08) edge-rendered box (THREE.BoxGeometry + THREE.LineSegments + THREE.EdgesGeometry) so it doesn't interfere with the wireframe but is always present.

Toggle via a new project.settings.showStockBox boolean, default true. Add a checkbox to SettingsDialog.

~1-2 hours.
