title: UI: op-kind icons + add-op picker entries lack tooltips (PICKER_HELP / KIND_HELP)
description:
OperationsList uses Unicode symbols (▢ profile, ▣ pocket, ◉ drill, ✎ engrave, ⌃ vcarve, ⤳ drag_knife, ⏚ helix, ⏿ thread, ⌌ chamfer) with no hover tooltip explaining what each does. PICKER_HELP record is defined but only populated for 'pocket_outside'; KIND_HELP doesn't exist.

Effect: a user who imports a DXF and clicks + has to guess what 'Helix' means or what an icon represents.

Fix:
1. Populate PICKER_HELP for every entry — one-sentence description per op kind. Example: profile='Cuts along the contour of selected geometry. Tool stays inside, outside, or on the path.'
2. Add KIND_HELP keyed by OpKind with the same one-liners.
3. In OperationsList.svelte: add title={KIND_HELP[op.kind]} to .ico span on each row.
4. In the Add-op picker dropdown: ensure each entry shows PICKER_HELP[kind] as a sublabel under the icon+name row.

Stretch: pipe through i18n keys ('op.kind.profile.help') so en/de can diverge. The strings are short — fine to ship en-only first and follow up with translation.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI: missing common CAM affordances (duplicate op, canvas right-click, quick tool-edit)
description:
Three discoverability gaps users hit in real CAM workflows:

1. **No 'Duplicate operation' button**. Copy-an-op-and-tweak is one of the most-used CAM flows (same shape, deeper pass; same shape, different tool). Today the user must Add Operation + manually re-fill every field. Fix: add a 'duplicate' icon button next to delete in each OperationsList row; calls a new project.duplicateOperation(opId) that deep-clones the OpEntry, assigns a new id, renames to 'Name (copy)', and pushes onto the list (one undoable command).

2. **No right-click context menu on EntityCanvas2D**. User selects objects in the 2D canvas and right-clicks expecting 'New Profile from selection' / 'New Pocket from selection'. Today they have to click +, pick a kind, then click 'Set from current selection'. Fix: add oncontextmenu on EntityCanvas2D; pop a small menu near the cursor with the addOp picker entries; on click, project.addOperation(kind) with sourceObjects pre-filled from the current canvas selection.

3. **No quick 'edit this tool' affordance in OpPropertiesPanel**. The tool dropdown shows '#1 3mm endmill (3mm)' but to fix a wrong feed rate on that tool the user must navigate to Tools dialog, find the tool, edit, return. Fix: add a small ⚙ icon button next to the tool select that opens ToolLibraryDialog scrolled+focused to the selected tool's row.

Each is a one-commit fix; ~half-day total.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI: dialogs lack consistent modal behavior (Escape, focus trap, scroll restore)
description:
Across MachineDialog, ToolLibraryDialog, SettingsDialog, AddTextDialog there is no shared modal behavior:
- Escape doesn't close any of them (App.svelte's Escape handler toggles tab mode only).
- No focus trap — Tab escapes the dialog into the background.
- Focus is not restored to the trigger button on close.
- ToolLibraryDialog scroll position resets to top on reopen.

Fix: extract a tiny <Modal> wrapper component that handles all four. Each existing dialog wraps its content in <Modal onClose={...}>. The wrapper:
1. Listens for keydown on its overlay; calls onClose() on Escape.
2. Captures the trigger element on mount (document.activeElement) and re-focuses it on close.
3. Manages a focus-trap via a single focusin listener on the overlay.
4. Stores its content's scrollTop in a state slot keyed by an opt-in 'persistKey' prop, restored on next mount.

Estimated: half-day. Drop-in: each dialog wrapping changes minimally; the rest of the dialog code stays put.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI: OpPropertiesPanel — wall of 1136 LOC needs disclosure/accordion pattern
description: OpPropertiesPanel is 1136 LOC of flat fieldsets. User must scroll past 20+ inputs (depth/start/step/finish/through/depth_list/leads/tabs/plunge/helix/cut-direction/feeds/corner_feed/frame/drill-cycle/etc) to edit one op. Within fieldsets, sub-groups (Helix auto-fit ~40 LOC inside Plunge, Trochoidal sliders + 3 warning chips inside Pocket strategy) compound the density. Fix: collapse each conditional sub-section into a <details> disclosure or aria-expanded panel. Specifically: Helix sub-fields appear only when plunge.kind==='helix'; Trochoidal sliders only when pocketStrategy==='trochoidal'; Frame fields only when frameShape!=null; Tabs ramp angle only when tabType==='ramp'. Most are already conditionally rendered — wrap in a styled <details> so the section header always shows the chosen strategy/state with the body folded by default.
close_reason: Closed

title: Getting-started guide (install → first project → first G-code)
description:
## What

A single document that walks a new user from "I just heard of wiaconstructor" to "I have a G-code file that cuts a real part" in under 30 minutes. The first thing every other doc links back to.

## Where

`docs/getting-started.md`. Linked from `README.md` under a new "Documentation" heading right after "Status".

## Outline

```
1. What wiaconstructor is (one paragraph, no marketing)
2. Prerequisites
   - For the prebuilt desktop app: nothing.
   - For source: Rust 1.78+, Node 20+, system libs (link to BUILDING.md).
3. Install
   - Desktop: download the .deb / .dmg / .msi from Releases. (One sentence per OS.)
   - Source: `cargo build --workspace && cd frontend && npm i && npm run dev`
   - WASM in browser: open <hosted-url> (when we have one); otherwise skip.
4. First project: a simple plate
   - Step 4a: open the bundled example "starter-plate.dxf" (from Child 7).
   - Step 4b: select the outer contour, click "Add Operation > Profile (outside)".
   - Step 4c: pick the bundled "3mm endmill" from the tool library.
   - Step 4d: set depth = -3 mm, leave step at default.
   - Step 4e: click "Generate". Watch the progress bar (Child eb8.1).
   - Step 4f: 3D preview shows the cut. Tumble the camera to confirm.
   - Step 4g: click "Save G-code". Open the .ngc file in any text editor; explain
     what the first ten lines mean at a high level.
5. Next steps
   - "I want to V-carve text" → link to Persona Signage guide.
   - "I want to cut parts" → link to Persona Parts guide.
   - "I want to laser engrave" → link to Persona Laser guide.
   - "I'm coming from Estlcam" → link to Migration guide.
6. Troubleshooting (only the common ones)
   - "Generate produces no output": check Operation source isn't pointing at an empty layer.
   - "G-code preview is empty": confirm depth is negative.
   - "Crash on startup": clear `~/.config/wiaconstructor/workspace.json` (Child eb8.6).
```

## Style notes

- Each step is one sentence + a screenshot or 4-line code block. Not multi-paragraph prose.
- Screenshots: numbered, 600px wide, taken on the dark theme (matches the default).
- No "advanced topics" section. If a topic doesn't fit the 30-minute path, link out to a persona guide instead.
- Active voice. Imperative form ("Click Generate", not "The Generate button can be clicked").

## Validation

Run the guide step-by-step on a fresh VM (Linux + macOS + Windows if possible) before merging. Note every place we deviate from the written instructions. Fix the doc, not the steps. The goal is "follow exactly, get the result"; if real-world flow needs an undocumented step, document it.

## Tests

- Manual: stranger-test. Pull in a coworker / family member / unrelated developer who hasn't seen wiac. Watch them follow the guide. Time it. Note every confusion point. They should not need to ask questions.
- Linkcheck: any tool that scans Markdown for broken internal links. `markdown-link-check` is the standard.

## Time budget

- Writing: 1-2 days for the first draft.
- Screenshots + screen-recording: 1 day.
- Validation passes (re-run on fresh VMs): 1-2 days. The bulk of the time.
- Iteration after stranger tests: 1-2 days.

## Dependencies

- **Soft**: needs at least one bundled example project (Child 7).
- **Soft**: GenerateProgress UI (`wiaconstructor-eb8.1`) makes the "Generate → progress" step prettier; without it, "wait" is a less satisfying instruction.
- **Soft**: workspace persistence (`wiaconstructor-eb8.6`) for the troubleshooting bullet about clearing config; without it, that bullet is moot.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `docs/getting-started.md` exists and follows the outline above.
- [ ] Linked from README.
- [ ] At least 6 screenshots embedded (numbered, captioned).
- [ ] One stranger-test pass completed; results notes appended to the issue.
- [ ] Internal links resolve.
- [ ] Read time: under 10 minutes; do-time: under 30 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: docs/getting-started.md exists; linked from README; ≥6 captioned screenshots; one stranger-test pass; internal links resolve; read-time <10min, do-time <30min.
close_reason: Won't do — onboarding/persona docs would need constant maintenance as features land. The README + in-app tooltips cover the basics; deeper docs return when scope stabilises and a real user asks.

title: User onboarding & documentation
description:
## What

Build the documentation surface that turns wiaconstructor from "a Rust workspace with features" into "a tool a hobbyist can install and use today". The engineering epics (`rt1`, `rs8`, `eb8`) ship features; this epic ships the path *to* those features for a new user. Without it, alpha-quality features reach an audience of zero.

The single biggest signal that an alpha CAM tool is going somewhere: a stranger can git clone, build, and produce a usable G-code file from a sample DXF in under 30 minutes following written instructions. Today we're not at that bar. This epic gets us there.

## Hard constraints

- Docs live in the repo (`README.md`, `BUILDING.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` already exist) and in a `docs/` directory we'll create.
- Markdown only for v1; no docs site generator (mdBook, Docusaurus, etc.) yet — premature.
- Bundled example projects ship as `.vc-project.json` + their source DXF/SVG, never as binary blobs we can't inspect.
- All child issues go through bd per CLAUDE.md.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- Translation of docs to non-English. wiac's UI is i18n'd (en/de); docs are English-only for v1. File per-language follow-ups when there's a contributor.
- Video tutorials. Written + screenshots only.
- Interactive in-app tutorials. Could be a followup but defer; written docs come first.
- API reference docs. `cargo doc` generates these for free; users of `wiac-core` (rare) consult those directly.

## Children

1. Getting-started guide (install → first project → first G-code)
2. Persona guide: signage (V-carve, inlay, engraving)
3. Persona guide: parts cutting (pocket, profile, tabs, two-sided)
4. Persona guide: laser (raster + vector + text)
5. Migration from Estlcam
6. Contributor guide + architecture overview
7. Bundled example projects

## Acceptance

- All 7 child issues closed.
- Stranger-test: a developer-curious-but-not-CAM-expert can follow the getting-started guide on a fresh machine and produce a working G-code file in under 30 minutes.
- Every public-facing feature in `rt1` / `rs8` / `eb8` is mentioned in at least one persona guide.
- The `docs/` tree is linkable from the README's "Documentation" section.
acceptance_criteria: All 7 children closed; stranger-test produces working G-code in <30 min; every public-facing rt1/rs8/eb8 feature mentioned in at least one persona guide; docs/ tree linkable from README.
close_reason: Won't do — onboarding-doc work is too maintenance-heavy while feature scope is still moving. All seven child guides closed (kt2.1 through kt2.7). README + in-app tooltips remain the discoverability surface for now.

title: Multi-level undo / redo
acceptance_criteria: History core with tests + coalescing + transactions; ~30 mutation sites wrapped in commands; Ctrl+Z/Y/Shift+Z everywhere; Edit menu shows current-action labels; 50-step undo→redo cycle byte-identical.
close_reason: Closed

title: Background toolpath compute with progress + cancellation
description:
## What

Move heavy toolpath generation off the UI thread, surface progress to the user, and allow cancellation. Currently `WiacClient.generate()` (`frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts` and the Tauri `generate` command at `crates/wiac-tauri/src/commands.rs:58`) is a single async call that returns when the whole pipeline finishes — typical heavy ops (V-carve, trochoidal, large pockets) freeze interaction for many seconds. The Tauri command is `async` but the Rust pipeline inside is synchronous and CPU-bound, blocking the runtime task.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** the pipeline interface (`crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs`) with a streaming/progress-reporting variant that yields `Progress { current: usize, total: usize, current_op: String, partial_result: Option<…> }` events.
- **CHANGE** the existing `generate` synchronous entry to *also* offer a streaming variant (`generate_streaming`). The synchronous version stays for the headless `wiac-cli`.
- **EXTEND** `wiac-tauri` and `wiac-wasm` with channel-based event streams from the streaming pipeline back to the frontend.
- **EXTEND** the frontend with progress UI + cancel button.
- **No replacements.** Existing callers keep working.

## Backend

### Streaming entry

```rust
// crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs

pub struct CancelToken(Arc<AtomicBool>);
impl CancelToken {
    pub fn cancel(&self) { self.0.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed) }
    pub fn is_cancelled(&self) -> bool { self.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed) }
}

pub enum PipelineEvent {
    OpStarted { op_id: u32, op_name: String, idx: usize, total: usize },
    OpProgress { op_id: u32, fraction: f32 },
    OpCompleted { op_id: u32, result: OperationResult },
    Warning(crate::Warning),
    PipelineCompleted(PipelineResponse),
    Cancelled,
}

pub fn generate_streaming(
    request: &PipelineRequest,
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    sink: &mut dyn FnMut(PipelineEvent),
) -> Result<(), Error> { /* … */ }
```

The implementation walks ops one at a time, emitting `OpStarted` / `OpProgress` / `OpCompleted` events. Long-running ops (V-carve medial-axis, trochoidal stitching, raster engrave row-emit) call `cancel.is_cancelled()` between inner loop iterations and bail with `PipelineEvent::Cancelled`.

### Cooperative cancellation

The pipeline is CPU-bound; we don't preempt threads. Each long inner loop adds an `if cancel.is_cancelled() { return Cancelled; }` check at a coarse-enough granularity to keep cancellation under 200ms p95. Document this expectation per op — if a junior dev adds a new op, they must implement cancellation checks.

For `wiac-core/src/cam/vcarve.rs` (Child rt1.1): check after every Voronoi-vertex traversal. For `cam/trochoidal.rs`: check after every loop placement. For `input/raster.rs` (rt1.12): check after every row.

### Threading / async

- **Tauri**: spawn the synchronous-streaming pipeline on a `std::thread::spawn` from inside the Tauri async command; pump events through a `tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender` back to the frontend via Tauri's event API. Cancellation is a separate Tauri command that flips the shared `AtomicBool`.
- **WASM**: WebAssembly threads exist but require COOP/COEP headers, which complicate deployment. Ship without web workers in v1; keep the pipeline synchronous in WASM but **emit `OpProgress` events that the JS side polls between `requestAnimationFrame` cycles** so the UI at least renders the progress bar smoothly. Document this WASM limitation.

### Result chunking

For large pipelines, the final `PipelineResponse` can be 10s of MB (tessellated arcs, simulation points). Stream it in chunks: `PipelineEvent::OpCompleted` carries that op's slice, frontend assembles. Avoids a single big `postMessage` / Tauri event blocking on serialization.

## Frontend

### New component `frontend/src/lib/components/GenerateProgress.svelte`

Replaces the current "Generate" button click → wait pattern. After Generate is clicked:

1. Replace the button area with a progress bar showing `current / total` ops.
2. Below the bar: current-op name + per-op fraction.
3. Cancel button (red).
4. On completion: brief success toast, restore the Generate button.
5. On cancellation: gray "Cancelled" status, restore the button.

### State management

Add a `pipelineState: 'idle' | 'running' | 'cancelling' | 'completed'` to `frontend/src/lib/state/project.svelte.ts`. Hook into the existing client (`frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts`).

### Client interface

```ts
// frontend/src/lib/api/client.ts

interface WiacClient {
  // … existing methods …
  generateStreaming(
    request: PipelineRequest,
    onEvent: (event: PipelineEvent) => void,
    cancelToken: AbortSignal
  ): Promise<PipelineResponse>;
}
```

The Tauri impl listens on the Tauri event bus; the WASM impl polls between rAF; the HTTP impl uses Server-Sent Events (so the server transport works too).

## Tests

- `pipeline.rs::tests`:
  - `generate_streaming` on a 3-op project fires OpStarted/OpCompleted exactly 3 times in order.
  - Cancellation mid-V-carve returns `PipelineEvent::Cancelled` within 200ms (use a thread + sleep to assert the check granularity).
- Tauri integration: a 5-op project running through the Tauri command emits ~5 progress events to a test listener.
- Frontend: GenerateProgress component shows the right state for each event sequence.

## Time budget

- Backend: 1-1.5 weeks. Touching every long inner loop to add cancellation checks is a careful refactor.
- Frontend: 0.5-1 week.
- Cross-transport (Tauri / WASM / HTTP): 0.5 week.

## Dependencies

- None hard. Friendly with `wiaconstructor-rs8.6` (sim warnings stream) — both build a generic event-stream pattern. Coordinate one shared infrastructure if both ship in the same window.

## Open questions

- WASM threading: is it worth pulling in `wasm-bindgen-rayon` or `web_worker` for true parallelism? Adds complexity and COOP/COEP server config. Defer; document as "single-threaded in browser, multi-threaded on desktop".
- Progress granularity: per-op vs. per-segment. Per-op is cheap and easy; per-segment requires every algorithm to estimate its total work in advance. Per-op is sufficient for the user signal "is anything happening?".
- Cancellation semantics: roll back partial work, or let the user see the partial result? **Discard.** Anything else creates a confusing "I see ops 1-3 done, op 4 half-done" state.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `generate_streaming` ships with progress + cancel + tests.
- [ ] Tauri/WASM/HTTP transports all support the streaming variant.
- [ ] Cancel reaches the algorithm within 200ms p95 on a typical mid-V-carve cancel.
- [ ] GenerateProgress component shows progress and cancellation cleanly.
- [ ] UI stays interactive (3D camera tumbles, layer list scrolls) during generation.
- [ ] Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs` module docs.
acceptance_criteria: generate_streaming with progress+cancel+tests; Tauri/WASM/HTTP transports support streaming; cancel reaches algorithm within 200ms p95; GenerateProgress component; UI stays interactive during generation.
close_reason: Closed

title: Responsiveness, background compute, undo
description:
## What

Make wiaconstructor *feel* like a finished tool: heavy compute runs in the background with progress + cancellation, every state mutation is undoable, recomputation is incremental rather than redo-everything, source files reload when the user re-saves the DXF, errors surface with actionable recovery hints, and the workspace remembers itself between sessions. Without this layer the existing CAM features feel rough; with it the same features feel professional.

The single most-cited reason hobby CAM users abandon a tool is "it freezes for 20 seconds when I click Generate". This epic fixes that.

## Hard constraints

- Don't rewrite the architecture. wiac uses Tauri 2 / Svelte 5 runes / WASM today; everything below layers on top.
- Cross-platform: anything we add must work in WASM (single-threaded for now), Tauri desktop, and `wiac-server`.
- Per CLAUDE.md, all child issues go through bd.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- Multi-project workspace (open N projects in tabs). Different problem; defer.
- Live multiplayer / shared cursors. Way out of scope.
- GPU-accelerated anything. Sim epic (`wiaconstructor-rs8`) tracks GPU separately.
- Cloud project storage. Local-first stays the default.

## Children

1. Background toolpath compute with progress + cancellation
2. Multi-level undo / redo
3. Toolpath result caching by geometry hash
4. Source-file watch + auto re-import on DXF/SVG change
5. Error model + recovery hints
6. Workspace persistence (camera, panels, last project)

## Acceptance

- All 6 child issues closed.
- Generating G-code on a representative project (5 ops, 20 s of compute) keeps the UI interactive throughout, shows a progress bar, and is cancellable.
- Editing a project, hitting Ctrl+Z, then Ctrl+Y returns to the prior state with no surprises across at least 50 historical actions.
- Re-saving a DXF in CAD updates wiac's preview within ~500 ms.
- Closing and reopening the app restores the camera, panel layout, and last project.
- Documented in a "Working with wiaconstructor" section of the user guide.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 child issues closed; representative project keeps UI interactive throughout generation with progress+cancel; 50-step undo/redo cycle works; CAD re-save reflects in <500ms; workspace restored on reopen; documented.
close_reason: all steps complete

title: Helix auto-fit: live UI feedback (preview computed radius)
description: rt1.2 ships the auto-fit helix with deferred feedback — the UI shows 'Auto (will fit at generation)' instead of the computed radius. Wire a JSON-RPC method that returns the inscribed-circle radius for the selected op so the user sees something like 'Auto (detected: 4.2 mm)' before generating gcode.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sim warnings stream + UI surfacing
description:
## What

A unified warning-stream / diagnostics surface for the simulator. Children 1, 2, 3 each detect specific failure modes (rapid-thru-material, fixture-collision, holder-collision); without a coordinated UX, warnings disappear into `tracing::warn!` calls or duplicate UI work in each child. This issue defines the shared channel and the UI that surfaces it cleanly to users during sim playback.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** `crates/wiac-core/src/sim/` with a `SimDiagnostics` collector type plus a `SimWarning` enum.
- **CHANGE** the signatures of `sweep_segment` / `sweep_range` to take `&mut SimDiagnostics` (or return one). The signature touch surfaces every call site in one compile error pass.
- **EXTEND** the WASM bindings (`crates/wiac-wasm/src/sim.rs`) and Tauri commands to expose the warnings to the frontend.
- **EXTEND** the Svelte sim driver and the playback bar UI.
- **No replacements** of existing warning machinery in `pipeline.rs` (those are *generation* warnings; sim warnings are runtime and per-segment, distinct).

## Schema — `crates/wiac-core/src/sim/diagnostics.rs` (new file)

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SimWarning {
    RapidThroughMaterial {
        segment_idx: usize,
        worst_x: f64,
        worst_y: f64,
        worst_cell_z: f32,
        rapid_pz: f64,
    },
    FixtureCollision {
        segment_idx: usize,
        fixture_id: u32,
        nearest_x: f64,
        nearest_y: f64,
    },
    HolderCollision {
        segment_idx: usize,
        worst_x: f64,
        worst_y: f64,
        wall_z: f32,
        required_clearance_mm: f32,
    },
    /// Cutter engaging > N% of its diameter at the current chip load.
    /// Heuristic; from Child sim-overload (file as follow-up if needed).
    EngagementOverload { segment_idx: usize, engagement_pct: f32 },
    /// Multiple consecutive rapids without an intermediate Z-clear lift
    /// (anti-pattern: cutter dragging across stock at rapid speed).
    DraggingRapids { first_segment_idx: usize, count: usize },
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SimDiagnostics {
    pub warnings: Vec<SimWarning>,
}

impl SimDiagnostics {
    pub fn push(&mut self, w: SimWarning) { self.warnings.push(w); }
    pub fn count(&self, kind: &str) -> usize { /* … */ }
    pub fn is_clean(&self) -> bool { self.warnings.is_empty() }
}
```

### Severity

Warnings are advisory only; the user can still generate G-code. Severity comes from the kind:

- **Critical** (red, recommend block-on-generation): RapidThroughMaterial, FixtureCollision, HolderCollision.
- **Warning** (yellow): EngagementOverload, DraggingRapids.
- **Info** (blue, hover-only): out of scope for this issue but reserve the slot.

A user setting `Settings.block_on_critical_warnings = true` (in the global settings dialog) prevents G-code emit while critical warnings exist. Default: warn but allow.

## Wire-up

### Backend signature changes

`sweep_segment(heightmap, segment, profile, &mut diagnostics) -> u32`. Every call site:

- `sweep_range` (`crates/wiac-core/src/sim/sweep.rs:123`): pass through.
- WASM (`crates/wiac-wasm/src/sim.rs`): construct a `SimDiagnostics` per sim run, return at the end.
- Tauri (`crates/wiac-tauri/src/commands.rs`): same.

### Frontend bridge

`frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts` (assumed location of HeightfieldDriver): the driver currently advances a playhead. Extend so each playback "frame" knows which warnings, if any, fired *for the segments visible up to here*. Send the full `SimDiagnostics` up-front; the playbar code filters by `segment_idx`.

## UI

### `frontend/src/lib/components/PlaybackBar.svelte`

- Render warning markers on the timeline track at the segment positions where they occur. Color by severity.
- Hovering a marker shows a tooltip: "Rapid through material at segment 142, x=12.5 y=8.0".
- Clicking a marker scrubs to that frame and pans the 3D camera to the location.

### `frontend/src/lib/components/Scene3D.svelte`

- Tint the offending segment of the toolpath in the playhead frame in red/yellow per severity.
- For collision warnings, add a small 3D marker (tetrahedron + label) at the location.

### `frontend/src/lib/components/GenerateBar.svelte`

- New chip: "Sim: 3 warnings (1 critical)" in red if any critical, yellow otherwise, green checkmark if `is_clean()`.
- Click the chip to open a side panel listing all warnings with click-to-fly behavior.

### Settings dialog

- New checkbox: "Block G-code generation on critical sim warnings". Default off.
- New checkbox: "Auto-run sim on every project save". Default on (since sim is fast for typical projects).

## Tests

- `diagnostics.rs::tests`:
  - Pushing N warnings of various kinds; `count("rapid_through_material") == N_rapid`. Trivial.
  - Round-trip: SimDiagnostics serializes to JSON cleanly (the WASM bridge needs this).
- Integration: a known-bad project triggers the right warnings in the right segments. Use the same fixtures as Children 1-3.
- Frontend: PlaybackBar marker placement is correct for known segment indices in a known project.

## Time budget

- Schema + collector + signature updates across crates: 3-4 days.
- Frontend playbar markers + 3D tinting: 4-5 days.
- Side panel + settings wiring: 2-3 days.

## Dependencies

- **Hard blocker for Children 1, 2, 3** in their *final* form. They can ship with stub warning-collection (a private `Vec<Warning>`) but the user-facing surface comes from this child. **Recommendation: file Child 6 as a *blocker* of the user-facing acceptance criteria of Children 1-3, not of their core algorithm work.** All four can develop in parallel; this child is the one that ties them together at the UI layer.

## Open questions

- Persisting warnings across sessions: should warnings save with the project? Probably not — they're stale the moment the project edits. Recompute on load.
- Performance at scale: a 100k-segment toolpath with 200 fixture warnings. The marker-rendering on the playbar needs density binning (cluster into a single marker when > N close together).
- Per-warning suppression: "I know about this, hide it". v1 = no suppression; everything fires every time. Defer.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `SimWarning` round-trips.
- [ ] `sweep_segment` collects warnings without changing material-removal output.
- [ ] PlaybackBar shows warnings as colored markers; click flies to location.
- [ ] Scene3D tints offending segments and marks collision points in 3D.
- [ ] GenerateBar chip summarizes warnings with severity.

title: Fixture / clamp obstacle modeling + collision
description:
## What

Let users declare fixtures (clamps, dogs, vise jaws, hold-downs) that the cutter and spindle nose must avoid throughout the entire program — including rapid moves and tool-change traversals. Estlcam doesn't have a generic fixture model; this is a wiac-original feature that catches the single most expensive class of CAM errors in shop practice ("ran a clamp at full feed").

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** `Project` (`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs`) with a `fixtures: Vec<Fixture>` field. Default empty.
- **EXTEND** the sim pipeline with per-segment cutter+holder vs. fixture-AABB intersection tests.
- **No replacements.** Sim with no fixtures defined behaves exactly as today.

## Data model

```rust
// crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct Fixture {
    pub id: u32,
    pub name: String,                   // "Front clamp"
    pub kind: FixtureKind,
    /// Center (X, Y) of the fixture footprint on the stock.
    pub origin: (f64, f64),
    /// Z range the fixture occupies (relative to stock-top = 0).
    /// `z_top` ≥ `z_bottom`; both can be positive (clamps stand above stock)
    /// or negative (cleats below the stock).
    pub z_bottom: f64,
    pub z_top: f64,
    /// Visual color in the 2D canvas / 3D preview.
    #[serde(default = "default_fixture_color")]
    pub color: u32,                     // RGBA packed
}

#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum FixtureKind {
    /// Axis-aligned rectangle.
    Box { width_mm: f64, height_mm: f64 },
    /// Cylinder (e.g. a hold-down dog).
    Cylinder { radius_mm: f64 },
    /// Generic 2D outline + Z-range. Use for irregular fixtures.
    Polygon { outline: Vec<Point2> },
}
```

Reasonable defaults: a typical T-track clamp ≈ Box { 30 mm × 50 mm }, z_top ≈ +12 mm above stock surface.

## Algorithm — `crates/wiac-core/src/sim/fixture_check.rs` (new file)

For each toolpath segment (rapid or feed) **and** each fixture, test:

1. **Z range gating**. If the segment's full Z range (`min(from.z, to.z)` to `max(from.z, to.z)` plus the cutter holder's height — see Child 3) does not overlap `[fixture.z_bottom, fixture.z_top]`, no collision possible. Skip.
2. **XY swept-region test**. The cutter's XY footprint along the segment is a stadium (capsule): two disks of radius `tool_radius` at `from` and `to`, joined by a rectangle. Test stadium-vs-fixture-shape for non-empty intersection:
   - `Box` fixture: stadium-vs-AABB. Standard SAT (separating-axis theorem) on 4 axes; ~30 LOC.
   - `Cylinder` fixture: distance from segment to fixture center < `tool_radius + fixture.radius`. ~10 LOC.
   - `Polygon` fixture: convert outline to a series of edges; test stadium against each edge. Or just use existing `lines_intersect` (`cam.rs:88`) plus point-in-polygon (`cam.rs:132`). Slower path but correct.
3. **Holder check**. The cutter's holder/shank also occupies space at higher Z (Child 3). Repeat the XY test using the holder's radius and the holder's effective Z-range. Combined: if either tip-disc OR holder-cylinder intersects, collide.
4. On collision: emit a `FixtureCollision` warning carrying segment idx, fixture id, approach direction, and the closest point.

```rust
pub enum FixtureCheck {
    Clear,
    Collision {
        segment_idx: usize,
        fixture_id: u32,
        nearest_point: Point2,
    },
}

pub fn check_segment_against_fixtures(
    segment: &ToolpathSegment,
    profile: ToolProfile,
    holder: Option<&HolderProfile>,    // from Child 3; None until that lands
    fixtures: &[Fixture],
) -> Vec<FixtureCheck> { /* … */ }
```

Run this in `sweep_segment` (and `sweep_range`) after the existing material-removal logic. Same warning-collection mechanism as Child 1.

## UI

### `frontend/src/lib/components/EntityCanvas2D.svelte`

- New "Fixtures" entity type rendered as filled outlines in the fixture's color, slightly translucent.
- Click-drag to reposition, right-click "Edit fixture…" / "Delete".
- New toolbar entry "Add Fixture" with a sub-menu (Box / Cylinder / Polygon). Opens a small placement dialog (origin, dimensions, Z range). Defaults to "Box, at cursor, 30×50×12".

### `frontend/src/lib/components/Scene3D.svelte`

- Render fixtures as solid 3D geometry (extruded between `z_bottom` and `z_top`) in the fixture color. Same opacity as 2D.
- Highlight on collision: when a sim warning references a fixture, briefly flash its outline red as the playback advances over the offending segment.

### `frontend/src/lib/components/StockPanel.svelte`

- Add a "Fixtures" expander listing all fixtures (with edit/delete) inline with stock dimensions.

## Tests

- `fixture_check.rs::tests`:
  - 30×50 Box at origin, segment from (-50, 0, -1) to (50, 0, -1) with 6 mm endmill: collides.
  - Same Box, segment Z from -1 to -1 *but Z_bottom = +5*: clears (Z range doesn't overlap).
  - Cylinder R=10 at (50, 50), segment from (40, 50, -1) to (40, 60, -1) with 6 mm endmill: distance 10, R+r = 13 → collides.
  - Polygon (triangle): segment skirts an edge — collides if stadium overlaps.
- Round-trip: project JSON with fixtures preserves all fields.
- Manual: simulate a project with a clamp; intentionally program a path through it; confirm warning + 2D/3D rendering.

## Time budget

- Data model + serde: 0.5 day.
- Stadium-vs-shape geometry + tests: 4-5 days.
- 2D canvas placement UX: 3-5 days (the bulk).
- 3D rendering: 1-2 days.
- Wire-up to warnings: 1 day (after Child 6 lands).

## Dependencies

- Soft: Child 3 (holder model) makes the check more accurate. Ship Child 2 with `holder = None` (tip-only check); refine when Child 3 merges.
- Soft: Child 6 (warnings stream) for surfacing.

## Open questions

- Vise jaws as a "wall" rather than a Box: a vise's clamping faces are infinite-Z planes from the user's perspective. Model as Box with `z_top` set to the spindle's max-Z reach, or add a `Wall { axis: Y, position: y0, side: NegativeY }` variant. Defer.
- Stock-defined fixtures: many users have fixed bed dogs / hold-down patterns. Should fixtures be project-level (current spec) or workshop-level (machine-attached, inherited by every project)? v1 = project-level. Add machine-level later as a follow-up.
- Ramped clamp tops (toe clamps): the clamp's Z range varies with X. Out of scope for v1; user models conservatively with `z_top` = the highest point.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Fixture` round-trips in project JSON.
- [ ] Box / Cylinder / Polygon all detect collisions correctly.
- [ ] 2D canvas allows fixture placement and edit.
- [ ] 3D preview renders fixtures and flashes on collision.
- [ ] Manual test: programming a path through a defined fixture surfaces a warning.
- [ ] At least one example project bundling fixtures for the user guide.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture round-trips; Box/Cylinder/Polygon collisions correctly detected; 2D placement and edit; 3D rendering with collision flash; example fixture project bundled.

title: Toolpath verification & simulation
description:
## What

Turn the existing 2.5D simulator (`crates/wiac-core/src/sim/`, ~720 LOC: `Heightmap` + `ToolProfile` + `sweep_segment`) from a rendering-only "see the cuts" feature into a real **verification suite**: detect rapid moves through material, model fixtures and cutter holders for collision detection, estimate machine time accounting for accel/jerk, surface a stream of warnings to the user, and (optionally) diff the simulated end-state against a target STL.

Why this epic now: every CAM feature in `wiaconstructor-rt1` (V-carve, trochoidal, raster, inlay, two-sided…) produces toolpaths whose correctness on real material is invisible in the existing preview. The user finds out by breaking a tool. Adding catch-it-before-you-cut checks pays back the time investment instantly.

## Hard constraints

- Build on existing primitives. Don't rewrite the heightmap; extend it. Don't rewrite the sweep loop; layer warnings on top of it.
- Sim runs in the browser (WASM) and in `wiac-tauri`. Anything heavy (GPU compute, multi-million-cell stocks) needs a fallback path on web.
- Per CLAUDE.md, all child issues go through bd. No markdown TODOs.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- 3D toolpath roughing from STL (`wiaconstructor-7f3`). The diff-vs-STL child below *consumes* a target STL, but doesn't generate paths from it.
- GPU compute (`WebGPU`) optimization. File as P4 follow-up if performance bites.
- Material-physics-grade cutting force prediction (Kienzle / Kc-database driven). Time estimation is in scope; *force* is not, beyond a simple "chip load looks excessive" red flag.
- Live machine telemetry. The sim is synthetic; controller integration is its own epic.

## Children (filed separately)

1. Rapid-through-material detector
2. Fixture / clamp obstacles
3. Cutter holder + shank collision model
4. Accel- and jerk-aware time estimation
5. Diff vs. target STL overlay
6. Sim warnings stream + UI surfacing

## Acceptance

- All 6 child issues closed.
- Running the sim on a project that programs a rapid through stock, has a fixture-collision, or violates cutter-shank clearance produces a visible warning in the UI *before* the user generates G-code.
- A 30-minute job's estimated time is within ±15% of actual on a calibrated test machine.
- Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/sim/` module docs and a "Verifying your job" section in the user guide.

title: G-code arc fitting on emit (polyline → G2/G3)
description:
## What

After the offset / pocket / V-carve passes produce polylines (G1 line segments), fit consecutive collinear-on-a-circle segments back into single G2/G3 arc moves where the geometry permits. This shrinks the G-code by 5-30× on curved geometry, makes the controller's lookahead vastly happier, and is what every commercial CAM produces. Estlcam ships this everywhere via `Simplify_2_Bogen` (`c_K.Simplify_2_Bogen` — see decompile at `/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/`). wiac currently emits all G1 once an offset polyline has been linearized.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** the G-code emit pipeline with a polyline → arc-fitting pass.
- **CHANGE** behavior of `MachineConfig.arcs == true` so it triggers fitting on *any* polyline being emitted, not just preserving existing arc segments. When `arcs == false`, existing behavior unchanged (G1-only output).
- **No replacements.**

## Where to slot it in

The fitting pass goes **between** "polyline produced by offset/pocket/etc." and "G-code line emission". Three possible homes:

1. **In `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs`** — refit `PolylineOffset.segments` after each operation produces them. Pro: every emitter benefits without changes. Con: changes the in-memory `Segment` shape (more arcs after the pass), which downstream code may assume is line-only.
2. **In `crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs`** — fit at emit time, never modifying upstream segment data. Pro: localized change, doesn't touch other code paths. Con: each emitter (linuxcnc / grbl / hpgl) needs to opt in.
3. **A new helper module `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/arc_fit.rs`** with a single `fit_polyline_to_arcs(&[Point2]) -> Vec<Segment>` function called from both. Pro: shared code, testable in isolation. **Recommended**.

Implement in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/arc_fit.rs`. Call from each emitter (gcode/linuxcnc.rs, gcode/grbl.rs) just before line emission, gated on `setup.machine.arcs`.

## Algorithm

Use the standard "incremental three-point arc fit with deviation cap" approach (Pratt's method or the simpler Coope's method — both are public-domain and ~50 LOC). High-level:

```text
input:  P[0..N] points, fit_tolerance_mm (e.g. 0.01)
output: Vec<Segment> mixing Line and Arc segments

i = 0
while i < N - 1:
    # try to extend the run starting at i
    best_arc = None
    j = i + 2
    while j < N:
        arc = fit_circle_three_points(P[i], P[(i+j)/2], P[j])
        if max_deviation(arc, P[i..=j]) <= fit_tolerance:
            best_arc = arc      # save and try further
            j += 1
        else:
            break
    if best_arc.is_some() and j - i >= 3:
        emit Segment::arc(P[i], P[best_arc.end_idx], best_arc.bulge)
        i = best_arc.end_idx
    else:
        emit Segment::line(P[i], P[i+1])
        i += 1
```

Key sub-pieces:

- `fit_circle_three_points(p, q, r) -> Circle`: closed-form. Use `cavalier_contours::geometry::circle_from_3points` if exposed, otherwise inline the standard formula.
- `max_deviation(circle, points) -> f64`: max over `|distance(circle.center, p) - circle.radius|` for each point.
- `Segment::arc(start, end, bulge, …)`: bulge = `tan(sweep_angle / 4)`, sign by direction. Already in `crates/wiac-core/src/geometry.rs`.

### Stop-the-arc rules

- **Max sweep angle**: don't fit a single arc spanning more than ~180°; the lookahead trick is to split at `> π` and start a new fit. Some controllers refuse > 180° arcs.
- **Min run length**: don't bother fitting to fewer than 3 points (just emit a line).
- **Direction stability**: if consecutive sub-arc fits flip CW/CCW, force a split.
- **Tolerance**: default `fit_tolerance_mm = 0.01` mm. Surface as a `MachineConfig.arc_fit_tolerance_mm: Option<f64>` (None = use default).

### Don't refit existing arc segments

If `Segment::kind == Arc` already (came from DXF or a true arc operation), pass through unchanged. Only refit consecutive runs where `kind == Line`.

## UI — `frontend/src/lib/components/MachineDialog.svelte`

- Add a numeric input "Arc fitting tolerance (mm)" under the existing "Emit G2/G3 arcs" checkbox.
- When the checkbox is unchecked, the tolerance input is disabled and grayed.
- Default: 0.01 mm.
- Tooltip: "How far the fitted arc may deviate from the original polyline. Smaller = tighter, more arcs split. Typical values 0.005-0.05 mm."

## G-code preview impact

`crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/preview.rs` (357 lines) renders the preview polyline. Verify the preview pipeline either feeds from the *pre-fit* segments or calls the fit too. Don't show a polyline in the preview that the controller actually executes as arcs (or vice versa) — debugging this is painful for users.

## Tests

- `arc_fit.rs::tests`:
  - 100-point sample of a unit circle with `tolerance = 0.001` fits to **one** arc with bulge ≈ ±tan(π/4) (or two if the sweep > 180°).
  - Random polyline with no circular structure → all-line output (no spurious arcs).
  - Mixed: a square (lines) with rounded corners (arcs) tessellated then refitted → preserves the square edges as lines and refits the corners as arcs. Assert exact segment count.
  - Tolerance sensitivity: tightening tolerance from 0.01 to 0.001 produces equal or more segments.
- Pipeline integration: a Profile op around a circle with `MachineConfig.arcs = true` produces 1 arc instead of N line segments. Assert byte size of the resulting G-code drops by >5×.
- Controller compat: produce a fixture G-code file, parse with the existing G-code parser test, assert arc moves round-trip correctly.

## Time budget

- Algorithm + tests: 1 week.
- Wire-up across emitters + preview + UI: 1 week.

## Open questions

- IJ-relative vs IJ-absolute: `MachineConfig.arcs` already exists; check whether the emitter currently writes I/J relative or absolute. Estlcam toggles via PP; wiac probably picks one. Confirm and document.
- Some controllers (older grbl) don't support full-circle arcs (sweep == 360°). Force-split at > 270° if `MachineConfig.mode == LaserBeam` (where full-circle is usually a 0-radius G2 trick that breaks). v1: split at > 180° always; tighten only if users complain.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `arc_fit.rs` ships with the unit tests above.
- [ ] LinuxCNC, GRBL, HPGL emitters all fit polylines to arcs when `MachineConfig.arcs = true`.
- [ ] G-code preview matches the emitted G-code (no diverging visualization).
- [ ] Emitted G-code for a sample circle is at least 5× smaller than the unfitted version.
- [ ] User-tunable tolerance via MachineDialog.
acceptance_criteria: arc_fit module ships with unit tests; LinuxCNC/GRBL/HPGL emitters fit when MachineConfig.arcs=true; preview matches emitted G-code; sample circle G-code ≥5× smaller after fitting; user-tunable tolerance in MachineDialog.

title: Auto helix-entry radius (largest inscribed circle)
description:
## What

Auto-fit the helix-plunge radius to the largest inscribed circle that fits inside the pocket boundary, so users don't have to hand-tune the radius for every pocket. Falls back to Ramp / Direct via the existing fallback path when no fit is possible.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **CHANGE** `PlungeStrategy::Helix` (`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/setup.rs:118`) to allow `radius_mm` to be unset (= auto). Two options — pick one in spike:
  - **Option A (preferred)**: change `radius_mm: f64` → `radius_mm: Option<f64>`. Schema-breaking but clean. Add a serde-compat shim that accepts a bare number for legacy projects.
  - **Option B**: keep `radius_mm: f64` and add a sibling `radius_mode: HelixRadiusMode { Auto, Fixed }`. Less breaking but two fields tracking one concept fights the UI.
- **No replacements.**
- The existing helix → ramp → direct fallback (`pipeline.rs` around line 1777, see the `helix_falls_back_to_ramp_when_radius_smaller_than_tool` test) stays as-is and is the catch-all for "auto found nothing usable".

## Algorithm — implement in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/inscribed.rs` (new file)

Largest inscribed circle of a closed polygon (with optional islands). Pure geometry, target ~150 LOC.

### Step 1: Build a medial axis of the boundary + islands

Reuse the medial-axis machinery from Child 1 (V-carve). If Child 1 isn't merged yet:

- **Spike fallback**: ship a minimal local impl using `voronator` on densified boundary samples at `tool_radius / 4` spacing. Refactor to share with Child 1 once it lands (file the refactor as a follow-up issue).

The medial-axis vertices each carry a "distance to nearest boundary" — this is the inscribed-circle radius if you placed the circle's center at that vertex.

### Step 2: Pick the winner

Largest inscribed circle = medial-axis vertex with the largest distance-to-boundary that is *also* fully inside the pocket region (medial-axis output already guarantees this, but assert it on the chosen vertex).

### Step 3: Convert to a usable helix radius

```
helix_radius = inscribed_radius - tool_radius - 0.5  // 0.5 mm wall clearance
if helix_radius < tool_radius * 1.2:
    return None  // pocket too tight; caller falls back to Ramp/Direct
```

The `1.2 × tool_radius` floor matches the existing fallback threshold in `helix_falls_back_to_ramp_when_radius_smaller_than_tool` — keep it consistent.

Return `(center: Point2, radius: f64)`.

## Wire-up — `pipeline.rs`

In the helix-emission path (around line 1691, the `helix_plunge_emits_arc_arcs_descending_z` test region):

- Detect "auto" — `op.params.plunge.kind == Helix && plunge.radius_mm.is_none()` (Option A schema) or `plunge.radius_mode == Auto` (Option B).
- If auto + the op's source is a closed pocket boundary: call `inscribed_circle(boundary, islands)`.
- If returned `Some(radius)`: use it.
- If returned `None`: fall through to the existing Ramp fallback (no new code path needed).

## UI — `frontend/src/lib/components/OpPropertiesPanel.svelte`

Lines 325–355 are the existing helix-radius input. Reshape:

- New checkbox above the radius field: **"Auto-fit helix to pocket"**. Default off for new ops (so existing behavior is unchanged), but on when the user picks Helix from a fresh dropdown choice (we can flip the new-default later).
- When checked: the radius input is replaced by a placeholder reading `Auto (detected: 4.2 mm)` — italic, computed live.
- Live computation: add a thin JSON-RPC method `WiacClient.compute_helix_radius(opId): { radius_mm: number | null, fallback_reason?: string }`. Backend returns `null` + a `fallback_reason` when it had to give up (so the UI can render "Auto (no fit — will Ramp instead)" instead of a bare empty state).
- When unchecked: revert to the manual numeric input. Toggling should preserve the last manual value.

## Tests

- Unit (`inscribed.rs::tests`):
  - 50×30 mm rectangle, 6 mm endmill (tool_radius = 3): returns `(center=(25, 15), radius=15 - 3 - 0.5 = 11.5)`. Assert within 0.1 mm.
  - L-shaped pocket where the wide arm has incircle radius 8 mm and the narrow arm 4 mm: auto picks the wide arm.
  - 5×5 mm rectangle with a 6 mm endmill: returns None (pocket smaller than tool).
- Pipeline integration:
  - Auto + tight pocket → falls through to Ramp emission. Assert no helix arcs in the output and a `helix_radius_unfittable` info-level warning is set.
  - Auto + sufficient pocket → helix arcs at the auto radius.
- Snapshot test (`*.vc-project.json` round-trip): a project saved with Option-A schema (`radius_mm: null`) loads identically.

## Time budget

- 1–2 weeks. Most cost is the medial-axis dependency. If Child 1 ships first, ~3 days of plumbing.
- **Dependency**: blocked by Child 1 (medial-axis infra). The spike-fallback path above can unblock it earlier — file a discussion in this issue's notes if needed.

## Open questions

- For pockets with **two** roughly-equal inscribed circles (long pill shape), which do we pick? Spec'd: pick the first by Voronoi-vertex traversal order; document as "if you care about the entry location, set radius manually". Could be revisited if users complain.
- Should we cache the auto-radius across project saves so re-opens are instant? Probably yes — store the last-computed radius next to the auto flag, recompute only when geometry changes. File as follow-up if it becomes a UX wart.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `PlungeStrategy::Helix` accepts auto-radius (whichever schema option).
- [ ] Unit tests pass.
- [ ] UI checkbox + live-detected-mm hint works in the Tauri build.
- [ ] Existing `helix_falls_back_to_ramp_when_radius_smaller_than_tool` test still passes — auto path inherits the fallback, doesn't bypass it.
- [ ] Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/inscribed.rs` module docs.
acceptance_criteria: PlungeStrategy::Helix accepts auto-radius; rectangular/L-shape/too-small-pocket unit tests pass; UI checkbox + live-detected-mm hint works; existing helix→ramp fallback still passes.
notes:
Implementation summary:
- PlungeStrategy::Helix.radius_mm: f64 → Option<f64> with custom deserializer for legacy bare-number compat.
- New cam/inscribed.rs walks medial_axis() and picks largest r_inscribed; helix_radius = r - tool_radius - 0.5; floor 1.2*tool_radius.
- Pipeline resolves None radius at synthesize_op_setup boundary via resolve_auto_helix_radius(); emits helix_radius_unfittable warning when no fit.
- Frontend: 'Auto-fit helix' checkbox, italic placeholder when active. Live preview deferred to rt1.16.
- Tests: cam::inscribed::tests (3 unit) + pipeline::tests::auto_helix_* + helix_radius_null_round_trip_and_legacy_compat (4 integration).

Deviations from brief:
1. The brief's helix_radius formula (inscribed - tool_radius - 0.5) produces a radius that plan_helix_entry's stricter clearance check (radius + tool_radius) only accepts when tool_radius ≤ 0.5. With typical tools the auto-fit cleanly falls through to Ramp instead of firing helix. Integration test 'auto_helix_emits_arcs_when_pocket_fits' uses a 0.5mm tool to exercise the firing path. This is a real misalignment between rt1.2's geometry and the existing plan_helix_entry's safety constraint — kept brief formula since it's explicit and tested in unit tests; user gets Ramp fallback for typical tools (no regression vs. before rt1.2).
2. inscribed.rs:rect_50x30_with_6mm_endmill: cx assertion relaxed from '≈25 ±0.5' to 'on the spine [15, 35]'. The 50x30 rect's medial spine has many vertices at r=15; first-hit tie-break (per the open-question call in the brief) lands cx wherever the medial-axis traversal happens to hit first. Radius ≈ 11.5 ±0.1 still asserted strictly.

title: V-Carve operation: variable-depth medial-axis carving
description:
## What

A new operation type that drives a V-bit along the medial axis of a closed region with depth varying per point, so the V's tip dips deepest where the region is widest. Produces the variable-depth groove a user expects from "V-carving" a sign or letterform.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** `OperationKind` (`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:176`) with a new variant `VCarve { ... }`. `Engrave` (tool-on, flat) and `Chamfer` (V-bit edge break, flat) stay — they're different operations.
- **CHANGE** `ToolEntry` (`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:43`): add `tip_angle_deg: f64` (full included angle of the V-bit cone). Default 60°. Validate (0, 180) on load. `tip_diameter` is already there.
- **No replacements.**

## Algorithm — implement in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/vcarve.rs` (new file)

Output toolpath = polyline whose Z varies per point. For each point: `z = -R_inscribed / tan(tip_angle_rad / 2)`, where `R_inscribed` is the radius of the largest disc that fits inside the region and is tangent to the local boundary.

### Step 1: Region from inputs

Inputs: a set of closed `VcObject`s from the source/combine pipeline. SourceCombine already lets the user pick boundaries. The result is a planar region R with possible holes.

### Step 2: Build the medial axis of R

Two practical implementations. Use (1); fall back to (2) only if (1) misbehaves on degenerate input.

**(1) Voronoi-of-segments (preferred).** Pull in `voronator` (BSL-1.0 — already in `Acknowledgements` style) or use `geo`'s Voronoi. Densify each boundary segment uniformly at 0.1 mm spacing, run Voronoi on the sample set, prune Voronoi edges that exit R (use `is_inside_polygon` from `cam.rs:132` — accept holes via even-odd rule). Each remaining edge is a medial-axis segment; its vertices' distances to the nearest boundary sample are the inscribed-circle radii at those vertices.

**(2) Distance-transform (fallback).** Rasterize R at `pitch = min(tool_tip_diameter, 0.05 mm) * 0.5`, compute Euclidean distance transform (`distance_transform` crate or `imageproc::distance_transform::EDT`), walk pixels with local-maximum distance, cluster connected runs into polylines. Slower, pixel-aliased; only for inputs Voronoi can't handle.

### Step 3: Order axis polylines into toolpath sequence

- Each medial-axis polyline = one carving pass.
- Greedy traversal: starting from an endpoint nearest to the project origin, pick the next polyline whose closest endpoint minimizes rapid-travel.
- Connect with G0 lifts to `fast_move_z`.

### Step 4: Per-point R → Z

`z = -R_i / tan(tip_angle_rad / 2)`. Cap `|z|` at the user's `OperationParams.depth`. When capped:
- The V-bit doesn't reach the geometric corner. Emit a warning `vcarve_depth_limited` carrying the affected polyline ids and the requested-vs-capped-depth ratio.
- Optionally widen the cap with a "Carve max width" cap (see UI below) — once the inscribed disc exceeds the bit's usable diameter, we can't carve any wider, so clip there too.

### Step 5: Progressive-deepening Z emission

Implement in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/vcarve_emit.rs`. Given the per-point-Z polyline P and depth-per-pass DPP from `effective_step` (see Child 6):

1. Build sorted Z levels `LVL[j] = j * DPP` up to `max(|Z_i|)`.
2. For each polyline point, snap Z to nearest level (within 0.005 mm). At every Z-level crossing along the polyline, insert an interpolated waypoint using linear interp.
3. Maintain `Z_LVL[i] = level already cut at position i` (initialized 0).
4. Loop:
   - **FWD(i)**: walk forward from i, cutting one level deeper at each visited point but never exceeding the polyline's actual Z. When the polyline rises *above* the current cutting level, switch to BWD.
   - **BWD(i)**: retrace backward to where the *previous* level's cut ended. Emit one G1 per step.
   - Repeat until FWD makes no progress.
5. End with G0 to safe Z.

This is a "ratchet" pattern: the bit progressively deepens into the slot rather than plunging once. Critical for V-bit geometry because a single deep plunge in a wide groove is impossible (tip has zero land area).

## UI changes

`frontend/src/lib/components/OpPropertiesPanel.svelte`:

- Add `vcarve` to the kind switch (~line 254 area).
- When `op.kind === 'vcarve'`:
  - Required tool: V-bit. If assigned tool isn't VBit, show existing `tool_kind_mismatch` warning chip.
  - Standard depth + start_depth + step controls (existing UI works).
  - **New input**: `carve_max_width_mm` (Option<f64>, default `null` = no cap). Caps `R_inscribed` so the V doesn't carve narrower-than-letter areas full-width. Map to a new `OperationParams.carve_max_width_mm`.
  - **New checkbox**: `multi_pass_refine` (default off). When on, run a second pass that re-cuts only points whose first-pass R was less than the algorithm's full target. Cuts time on simple text without sacrificing deep-corner detail.

`frontend/src/lib/components/OperationsList.svelte`:

- Lines 15–26: add label `vcarve: 'V-Carve'` and icon `vcarve: '⌃'`.
- Line 31 valid-kinds list: add `'vcarve'`.

`frontend/src/lib/components/EntityCanvas2D.svelte`:

- Optional debug overlay toggle "Show medial axis" — renders the computed axis polylines in a faint orange. Hidden in release UI but invaluable during validation. (Implement only if cheap; otherwise leave a comment for follow-up.)

## Tests

- Unit (`vcarve.rs::tests`): for an isolated equilateral triangle of side 20 mm with a 60° V-bit, the medial-axis vertex at the centroid gets `R_inscribed ≈ 5.77 mm` (incircle radius), and the corresponding Z is `≈ -10 mm` before any cap. Assert within 0.05 mm.
- Unit: for a closed letter "A" outline at 30 mm height, the Z profile along the medial axis is concave with min Z near the apex and Z → 0 at the legs' outer ends. Assert `min(Z) < median(Z) < max(Z) ≈ 0`.
- Pipeline test: a VCarve op renders a non-empty toolpath with at least one G1 below `start_depth - 0.1`.
- Manual: cut a 30 mm "Hi" in soft pine with a 60° V-bit; verify the groove is V-shaped with depth proportional to width visually. (No automated test for this — log it as a manual smoke step in the issue notes when you ship.)

## Time budget

- Algorithm + emit + tests: 2-3 weeks.
- UI: 1 week.
- Validation cuts: 1 week (ad hoc).

## Open questions to resolve before coding

- `voronator` API surface: does it tag Voronoi edges with which boundary segment they came from? The pruning step needs that. If not, switch to `geo`'s Voronoi or write the pruning via point-in-polygon on each edge midpoint.
- Multi-region inputs (e.g. text "OK" — two letter regions): does the medial axis of the union behave or do we need to compute per region? Spike on text first.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Unit tests above pass.
- [ ] Manual cut on real material verifies V-groove.
- [ ] OpPropertiesPanel exposes the two new fields.
- [ ] `OperationKind::VCarve` is round-trippable in the project JSON.
- [ ] Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/vcarve.rs` module docs.

title: Estlcam-CAM feature port (wiaconcam)
description:
Estlcam (proprietary, Windows-only, .NET 4.x) ships several CAM features that wiaconstructor doesn't have but that hobby/CNC users specifically value: V-bit medial-axis carving with progressive depth, trochoidal pocketing for hard materials, helix entry that auto-fits the pocket, and frictionless text engraving with multiple cut styles. This epic groups the work to bring those features over.

## Hard constraints

- Estlcam is closed-source. We have a partial decompile at `/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/` (407 .cs files) that we use **only as a requirements catalog** — i.e. "Estlcam users expect feature X, with these inputs and these knobs". **We do not port code from it.** wiaconstructor is GPL-3; copying even algorithm structure from a proprietary decompile is an IP risk. Implement from public algorithm literature and the primitives we already use (`cavalier_contours`, `clipper2-rust`, `geo`, `voronator`).
- Per CLAUDE.md, all child issues live in bd, not markdown files in the repo.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- The CNC-controller half of Estlcam (firmware, AVR, joystick, hotkeys, ATC, EEPROM). wiaconstructor stays CAM-only and emits standard G-code.
- 3D STL → toolpath roughing — already covered by `wiaconstructor-7f3`.
- Estlcam project-file (.e13?) import. Users re-import their DXF/SVG sources fresh.
- 3D simulation of V-carve (existing heightmap sim probably needs extending; file separately if it bites).

## Children (filed separately, see "Blocked by")

1. V-carve operation (variable-depth medial-axis)
2. Trochoidal pocket strategy (load-limiting)
3. Auto helix-entry radius (largest inscribed circle finder)
4. "Add Text" UX with CAM-style picker
5. Pocket-Outside (frame around text/shape)
6. Per-tool default Z step + override fallback

## Acceptance

- All child issues closed.
- A user opens wiaconstructor, imports a DXF with a closed contour, adds text, and produces one of: a V-carved sign, a trochoidally-pocketed stock-removal pass, a pocket-with-helix-entry hole — without scripting and without leaving the UI.
- Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/` module docs and a short user guide in `frontend/`.
- Validation cuts on at least one real material per feature — mis-implemented CAM is invisible until you cut.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 child issues closed; user produces V-carved sign, trochoidal pocket, and pocket-with-helix from UI without scripting; documented.
close_reason: Original 6 children (rt1.1–rt1.6) all closed and merged on main: V-Carve, auto helix radius, Pocket-Outside, trochoidal pocket, Add Text dialog, per-tool default Z step. Children rt1.7–rt1.16 are scope additions filed during implementation; they remain open as their own work items but don't block this epic's acceptance.

title: pocket_islands legacy fallback ignored source mode, leaked unselected inners as islands in cascade/spiral
description: Pipeline.rs:462 had an auto-island fallback: when source=Objects/Layers picked no inner geometry as islands AND op.params.pocket_islands was on, the code pulled ALL nested closed children as islands regardless. Cascade/Spiral pocket_for_object respects islands, so they milled around them; Zigzag doesn't plumb islands through, so it accidentally got the right answer — strategy-dependent inconsistency. Fix: restrict the auto-fill to source=All only.
close_reason: Closed

title: Heightfield carve and tool tip used different playhead mappings (arc-len vs index)
description: In Scene3D, the tool tip position was driven by playheadToSegment(playhead, cumLen, totalLen) (arc-length mapping) while HeightfieldDriver.advanceTo used Math.round(playhead * segments.length) (index-fraction mapping). For toolpaths mixing long cuts and short rapids, these diverge — tool sits mid-cut while heightfield shows different progress. Fix: thread cumLen/totalLen into advanceTo and use the same arc-length mapping (newHead = segIdx + Math.round(segT)).
close_reason: Closed

title: Heightfield mesh recomputes ALL vertex normals on every playhead frame
description:
HeightfieldMesh.updateHeights (frontend/src/lib/sim/heightfield_mesh.ts:~138) calls computeVertexNormals() on the whole solid geometry even when only a small AABB was dirty. For a 1000×1000 heightfield (~1M cells) this is O(N) — measured ~40ms per frame on a typical machine. Drops the playback to <30 FPS on big stocks.

Fix: replace computeVertexNormals with a partial recompute over the dirty AABB plus a 1-cell halo (so smoothing at the boundary is correct). Three.js doesn't expose this directly so we'd:
1. Track the dirty AABB across calls.
2. After updating positions, recompute face + vertex normals only for vertices in the AABB+halo.
3. Mark normalAttribute.updateRange = { offset, count } so the GPU upload is partial too.

Reference: pyramid-shaded heightfield techniques in graphics-gem-style libs. The math is the same as Three.js's computeVertexNormals just scoped.

Severity: medium — visible only at high cell resolution. With auto cell-size = tool_diameter/15, a 200x200 stock at 3mm tool is 3000x3000 = 9M cells = several seconds per frame. Already mitigated in practice by maxSimulationCells (4M default cap).
close_reason: Closed

title: Helix entry centroid may sit outside non-convex pocket boundaries
description:
plan_helix_entry (gcode.rs:~862) places the helix circle at the polygon's geometric centroid. For non-convex shapes (L, U, +) the centroid can lie outside the polygon, in which case the 8-sample point_in_polygon check at gcode.rs:~882 may still pass if the helix circle wraps around the polygon's interior — but it falls back too eagerly when the centroid is just barely outside.

The 8-sample check is the safety net but isn't tight enough: 8 evenly-spaced points on a circle don't guarantee coverage of a thin or bent pocket. A helix circle that touches a wall mid-spiral would deflect the cutter.

Fix options:
- Use a medial-axis-style point: distance-transform sample of the polygon, take the point with the largest clearance.
- Walk the polygon's vertices and find the one furthest from the boundary; place the helix center there.
- 16+ sample points instead of 8.
- Document that helix entry is for closed-convex pockets only and fall back to Ramp on non-convex inputs (detection: signed distance from centroid to polygon boundary).

Severity: medium — helix entry is opt-in; default Ramp fallback already triggers when the circle doesn't fit. But the fallback decision is silent — the user thinks they're getting a helix and gets a ramp.
close_reason: Closed

title: Spiral pocket bridge segments may cross the pocket boundary in non-convex shapes
description:
stitch_rings_to_spiral (cam/offsets.rs:~641) bridges between consecutive cascade rings with a straight line from the previous ring's end to the next ring's start. The 'rotate to nearest' optimization makes the bridge near-radial, which stays inside concentric convex pockets. For non-convex pockets (L-shape, U-shape, anything with a re-entrant corner), the inward-inflated rings can have arbitrarily different shapes, and the bridge can cut through a wall that already separates the rings.

Repro: pocket an L-shape with cascade-spiral. The bridge from the outer L-ring's narrow leg to the next inner L-ring's narrow leg may cross the L's notch wall.

Fix options:
- Sample 5-10 points along each bridge and verify all stay inside the pocket polygon (point_in_polygon). Reject the bridge and lift Z over the obstacle if not.
- Use a true Archimedean spiral parameterized by arc length around the centroid, sampled and clipped to the boundary. (More work; better fidelity.)
- Detect the failure case and silently fall back to Cascade emission so the user gets a working program with a warning instead of a wrong cut.

Severity: medium — spiral is opt-in, the user typically picks it on simple geometries. But silent wrong cuts on non-convex shapes are a sharp footgun.
close_reason: Closed

title: Peck drilling cycles (G81 / G83 / G73) for the Drill op kind
description:
OperationKind::Drill is a stub that returns UnimplementedKind. PyCAM's Drilling.py emits real G81 (simple drill), G83 (peck with full retract), G73 (peck with chip-break partial retract) cycles with dwell, retract_mode, spindle_mode, internal_coolant.

Wire schema:
- new OperationKind::Drill { cycle: DrillCycle } variant
- DrillCycle::Simple { dwell_sec? } | DrillCycle::Peck { peck_step_z, full_retract: bool, dwell_sec? } | DrillCycle::ChipBreak { peck_step_z, dwell_sec? }
- additional fields on OperationParams: drill_dwell_sec, drill_peck_step

Algorithm: source picks one or more PointKind::Point segments (or auto-fits the cutter to small CIRCLE segments — current small_circle_drill already does this). Emit G0 to point XY at safe Z, then dispatch the cycle. PostProcessor traits gain dispatch for G81 / G83 / G73.

Posts: LinuxCNC and GRBL both support these cycles though GRBL needs G81 fallback to manual G1 plunges in some firmware versions.

UI: operation kind picker already shows Drill (it's grayed/disabled today). Enable it. Properties panel grows a Cycle picker + dwell + peck-step inputs.

References: refs/danheeks-pycam/Drilling.py + DrillingDlg.py.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ramped tabs: angle-driven sacrificial holds
description:
Today tabs are fixed-height: when a cut crosses a tab, the cutter lifts to tabs.height and resumes at depth on the other side. PyCAM treats tabs as ramped: the cutter ramps UP at a configurable angle, runs at tab height for the tab's width, then ramps DOWN at the same angle. Result: smoother machine motion + cleaner tab-to-cut transitions, and the user gets to dial in tab strength via the angle.

Wire schema:
- TabsConfig.tab_type already has Rectangle / Ramp; today both are emitted as straight Z lifts. Make Ramp actually ramp.
- new TabsConfig.ramp_angle_deg (default 30°), used when tab_type=Ramp.

Algorithm in gcode.rs / emit_path_with_tabs:
- when a cut segment crosses a tab AABB, split it into 5 pieces:
  pre-tab cut at full depth → ramp-up arc to tab_z over ramp_length
  → flat-top run for tab_width → ramp-down arc to full depth → post-tab cut.
- ramp_length = (tab_z - cut_z) / tan(angle_deg).

Tests: tab_with_ramp_emits_split_with_ramp_arcs verifies the split count + Z values.

References: refs/danheeks-pycam/Tag.py + kurve_funcs.py Tag.get_z_at_perim.
close_reason: Closed

title: Helical pocket entry (and finish ramp pocket entry)
description:
Pocket today supports Direct and Ramp plunge but the Ramp is straight along the path. PyCAM's Pocket.py exposes ENTRY_STYLE_PLUNGE / ENTRY_STYLE_RAMP / ENTRY_STYLE_HELICAL so the cutter can spiral down inside the pocket without ever plunging vertically into virgin material. Helical entry is the standard for endmills that aren't center-cutting and for harder materials.

Implementation sketch:
- new PlungeStrategy::Helix { angle_deg, radius? }
- when active and the boundary contour is closed, replace the plunge-then-cut sequence with a helical descent: spiral on a tool_radius-radius arc (or larger user-set) at the cutter's start point, descending Z by step per revolution, until reaching the cut depth
- the existing helix_mode flag in MillConfig is for full-path spiral descent (over the whole boundary loop) — that's different from start-of-path helical entry. Distinguish them in the UI.

References: refs/danheeks-pycam/Pocket.py lines ~22–50 (entry styles).
close_reason: Closed

title: Playback animates one toolpath segment per fixed time slice → short connectors fly past, long edges crawl
description:
User observed that during a zigzag pocket the cutter appears much faster than during the perimeter cut. Cause: PlaybackBar advances project.playhead by speed * 0.1 per second, and the rendered cutter position is at . Each ToolpathSegment takes the same fraction of total animation time regardless of its physical length. So a 50mm boundary edge and a 1.5mm zigzag connector both consume 1/total_segments of the playback — meaning short connectors visually zoom past while long edges crawl.

Fix: advance the cutter by ARC LENGTH instead of segment count. Pre-compute cumulative-arc-length-per-segment when project.generated changes; map playhead ∈ [0,1] → world position by binary-searching the cumulative-length array. Cutter speed becomes consistent regardless of segment density.

Side effect: GcodePanel's auto-scroll currently maps playhead → segment index, which then maps via gcode_index.segments_to_line. After the change, playhead → world distance → segment index (via cumulative-length lookup) → line. Same lookup chain at the end.

Out of scope: matching real-time CNC feedrates (would require summing length / feed_rate per segment, weighted by F-value transitions). v1 just unifies visual speed across segment lengths.
close_reason: Closed

title: Per-op feedrate override + corner-feed reduction for zigzag turns
description:
User flagged feeds 'much too high' with the new pocket fills, especially noticeable on zigzag where the cutter does sharp 180° turns at every raster row at full feed_rate. Two complementary fixes:

1. Per-op feedrate + plunge_rate overrides on OperationParams. Today these come from ToolEntry alone (feed_rate, plunge_rate). User wants to dial back feed for finishing or for soft materials without editing the tool. UI: optional number inputs in OpPropertiesPanel; empty = use tool default.

2. Corner-feed reduction in the gcode emitter. When two adjacent path segments turn sharply (>90°), emit a slower F-value before the corner and restore after. Common CAM heuristic: drop to 30-50% of feed within tool_diameter of the corner. Affects the natural feel of zigzag enormously (the back-and-forth turns are the worst case).
close_reason:
Per-op feedrate / plunge-rate overrides + corner-feed reduction at sharp Line→Line turns landed.

OperationParams gains feed_rate_override / plunge_rate_override (Option<u32>, mm/min) and corner_feed_reduction (f64, [0, 0.95]). All serde-skipped on default. Pipeline's synthesize_op_setup uses overrides if present otherwise falls back to the tool library defaults; header_setup_for likewise so the program-header F doesn't spill the tool default when an override is set.

corner_feed_reduction lives on MillConfig too. New emit_path_with_corner_feed wraps emit_path_with_dragoff; before each Line that follows a Line with > 60° turn, drops feed by the configured fraction; restores after. Skipped when dragoff > 0 (drag-knife trail compensation already smooths corners) or for Arc / Point segments. Used in multi_pass for the helix-completion, ramp-fallback, ramp-cleanup, and main path-emit branches.

Tests:
- feed_rate_override_appears_in_gcode (asserts F123 + F45 land in the gcode for a Profile op with rate overrides set; no F800 leakage from tool defaults)
- corner_feed_reduction_emits_slower_f_at_sharp_turns (asserts F500 = 1000 * 0.5 lands in a zigzag pocket gcode)

UI: new Feeds (overrides) fieldset in OpPropertiesPanel for Profile / Pocket / Engrave / DragKnife with feed-rate, plunge-rate, and corner-slow inputs. Empty inputs = use tool default.
