title: wiac-wasm: expose heightmap simulator with zero-copy buffer view
description: Expose the Rust Heightmap (0o7) plus sweep (ck7) to the frontend via wasm-bindgen with zero-copy access to the cell data — the bridge that makes the perf-first architecture pay off. Frontend wraps the WASM-resident Float32Array via Float32Array(wasm.memory.buffer, sim.data_ptr(), cols*rows) so each advance() call mutates cells in place with no copy. Caveat: WebAssembly.Memory growth invalidates the view ref, so re-take it after every advance(). Segments + tool_spec serialize via serde_wasm_bindgen for v1; if per-frame cost shows up in profiling, switch to a flat Float32Array layout. Tests via wasm-bindgen-test.
close_reason: Closed

title: Incremental playhead-driven simulation
description:
Tie the WASM simulator (jbj) to project.playhead so scrubbing / playing animates the carving incrementally instead of re-running the full sim each tick.

Strategy:
- One Simulator instance per project.generated; replaced when a new Generate result arrives.
- appliedHead tracks the toolpath segment index the heightmap currently reflects.
- Playhead changes: newHead = round(playhead * total).
  - newHead > appliedHead (forward): call sim.advance(segments, tool_spec, appliedHead, newHead). Mutates the heightmap in WASM memory, returns a dirty AABB. Frontend re-takes the Float32Array view (cheap: re-creating a TypedArray from memory.buffer is O(1) — but mandatory because WASM memory growth invalidates old views) and updates the affected mesh vertices.
  - newHead < appliedHead (scrub back): can't reverse cuts cheaply → sim.reset() then advance(0, newHead). Adds a noticeable hitch on backward scrubs but keeps forward play silky.

Performance budget: PlaybackBar drives playhead at ~60fps. 5000-segment program at speed 1.0 → ~83 segments/sec → ~1.4 segments/frame; at 10× speed, 14/frame. Per-segment cost dominated by per-cell sweep (Rust, fast). Mesh vertex Z update is O(dirty_AABB_cells), typically <1k cells/frame.

Hooks in Scene3D:
- new $effect listening to project.generated + project.tools + project.machine + project.stock — rebuilds the Simulator when any structural input changes.
- new $effect listening to project.playhead — calls sim.advance(...) to the new head.
- requestRender() called after each advance so the render-on-demand loop picks up the change.
- the existing rebuild-geometry effect (wireframe path) is unaffected.

Out of scope: tool-kind switches mid-program (different tool per op — would need to advance with the right tool spec for each segment range; defer to v2), tabs, undo.
close_reason:
Heightfield driver glue lives in frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts. HeightfieldDriver owns one Simulator (jbj) plus one HeightfieldMesh (hvv) inside its own THREE.Group. init() lazy-loads the wasm-pack pkg + grabs the WebAssembly.Memory ref. build() (re-)creates sim+mesh from imported.bbox + project.stock + active tool diameter + settings. advanceTo(headFraction, segments, tool) calls sim.advance, RE-TAKES the Float32Array view from memory.buffer (mandatory because advance can grow WASM memory and detach the old view), then mesh.updateHeights(view, aabb).

Backward-scrub does sim.reset + replay 0..head. Edge geometry is debounced to ~120ms via scheduleEdgeRebuild so the surface refreshes smoothly while edges snap a few times per second.

Scene3D wires it up via three new $effects:
- 'sim build' watches imported / generated / stock / active tool / cell res / max cells / preview mode; rebuilds when the key changes, hides the group in 'wireframe' mode.
- 'advance on playhead' calls driver.advanceTo whenever project.playhead changes.
- 'live style' calls driver.applyStyle whenever the cosmetic settings change.

cellSize semantics fixed in passing: PlaneGeometry width is (cols-1) * cellSize so vertex spacing equals cellSize exactly.

svelte-check 0 errors; vite build clean. Driver disposed on Scene3D unmount.

title: Three.js heightfield mesh from heightmap
description:
Render the WASM-resident heightmap (jbj exposes the Float32Array view) as a Three.js mesh with two coordinated visuals: semi-transparent solid faces + fully-opaque solid edges drawn on top.

Solid faces:
- PlaneGeometry(stock_w, stock_h, cols-1, rows-1) — one vertex per heightmap cell.
- Each frame's advance() returns a dirty AABB; only those vertices' Z attribute is updated. position.needsUpdate=true on the slice.
- MeshStandardMaterial { color: <settings.solidColor>, opacity: <settings.solidOpacity>, transparent: true, depthWrite: true, side: DoubleSide }
- depthWrite=true is the right call because the mesh is convex from above (heightmap can't have overhangs); back-faces don't sort badly.
- Per-vertex normals recomputed only over the dirty region (full computeVertexNormals would be too expensive for big grids).

Solid edges:
- Built once per Generate (or coarse playhead breakpoint — debounced rebuild) via THREE.EdgesGeometry on the mesh's BufferGeometry with thresholdAngle ~30° to pick up the carved walls.
- LineSegments material: color settings.edgeColor, opacity 1.0, depthTest configurable (default true so edges hide behind solid; false would show them through).
- Optional polish: hold the edge geometry in a separate Group above the solid mesh; toggle visibility per the Wireframe/Solid/Both setting.

Update tied to the dirty AABB:
- Solid face Z attribute updated incrementally per frame.

title: Tool sweep along path segments → heightmap mutations
description:
Walk the cutter along each toolpath segment and lower the heightmap cells the tool covers. Lives in crates/wiac-core/src/sim/sweep.rs (Rust per the perf-first direction).

Per segment (px0,py0,pz0) → (px1,py1,pz1):
1. Compute the segment's XY footprint AABB inflated by tool radius.
2. For each cell (ix, iy) in the AABB: project its center to the closest point on the segment in XY → r and parametric t. If r > R, skip.
3. cutter_pz = lerp(pz0, pz1, t); surface_z = cutter_pz + tip_profile(r).
4. heightmap.lower_at(ix, iy, surface_z) — only writes when surface_z < current.
5. Track the dirty AABB across all segments processed in one advance() call so the renderer can refresh just that region.

Move kinds:
- Cut / Plunge / Retract / Arc: carve.
- Rapid: skip (cutter at fast_move_z above stock).
- Belt-and-suspenders: skip when min(pz0, pz1) > top_z anyway.

Arcs: PipelineResponse already tessellates arcs into ToolpathSegment chord entries; v1 treats Arc the same as Line (chord-only). Per-segment chord is short enough that visual error is small.

Tests:
- single endmill plunge at (10, 10) R=2 → circular patch lowered at z=plunge_depth, cells outside R untouched
- horizontal cut from (0,0)→(50,0) at z=-1 R=2 → 4mm-wide stripe at z=-1
- V-bit plunge 60° R=2 → conical pattern (cell at r=1 lower than r=0 by tan(30°)≈0.577)
- swept_segments_count_matches_footprint_per_cell expectations
- dirty AABB after a 100×0 sweep equals the inflated footprint
close_reason:
Sweep landed in crates/wiac-core/src/sim/sweep.rs.

API:
- sweep_segment(heightmap, &ToolpathSegment, ToolProfile) -> u32   // returns cells touched
- sweep_range(heightmap, &[ToolpathSegment], from_idx, to_idx, ToolProfile) -> u32   // useful for incremental advance() in jbj

Algorithm:
- Skip Rapid moves (cutter at safe Z above stock).
- Skip when both endpoints' Z >= top_z (cutter in air).
- Compute the segment's XY footprint AABB inflated by tool radius; convert to cell index range with world_aabb_to_cells (clamps to grid; returns None when fully outside).
- For each cell center in range: project onto the segment in XY → recover (r_sq, t in [0,1]). Skip if r > tool radius. cutter_pz = lerp(from.z, to.z, t). surface_z = cutter_pz + profile.eval(r). lower_at(ix, iy, surface_z).
- Pure plunges (XY length < 1e-12): skip the projection; use plunge_z = min(from.z, to.z) so every cell under the cutter sees the deepest point regardless of move direction (Plunge / Retract behave correctly).

Tests (9, all green):
- rapid_move_does_not_carve
- cutter_above_stock_does_not_carve
- endmill_plunge_lowers_circular_patch
- horizontal_cut_carves_4mm_stripe   (stripe width matches 2R, off-axis cells untouched)
- vbit_plunge_lowers_in_conical_pattern   (apex at plunge_z, r=1 cell above by tan(30°))
- lower_at_only_writes_on_descent_not_re_pass   (later shallower cut doesn't raise the cell)
- sweep_range_walks_each_segment   (multi-seg with a Rapid in the middle that's skipped)
- sweep_outside_heightmap_is_silently_skipped   (segment fully right of grid)
- sweep_partial_overlap_clamps_to_grid   (segment crossing the right edge carves only the in-grid portion)

title: Real cutting preview (heightmap-based stock simulation)
description:
Replace the wireframe-only toolpath preview with a 'real' preview that shows material being carved away as the playhead progresses.

Model: heightmap Z(x,y) over the stock footprint. Each cell stores the lowest Z the cutter has reached at that XY, initialized to the top of stock. As the cutter sweeps along the toolpath, cells the tool overlaps are lowered to the cutter-tip Z minus the tool's Z-profile-at-radial-offset. Renders as a Three.js heightfield mesh.

Visual style (per user direction):
- semi-transparent solid faces (opacity configurable, default ~50%)
- SOLID edges drawn on top (EdgesGeometry → LineSegments, full opacity, configurable color)
- the edges convey the carved walls clearly while the translucent fill lets the wireframe toolpath show through behind

Architecture (per user direction: 'whatever is best for performance'):
- simulation logic in Rust (crates/wiac-core/src/sim/) — tight numeric loops over 1M+ cells benefit hugely from native compute vs JS
- exposed via wasm-bindgen in crates/wiac-wasm — zero-copy Float32Array views into WASM memory for the heightmap so JS can read the buffer without copying
- frontend (Three.js) takes the buffer, displaces a PlaneGeometry's Z attribute, and overlays the EdgesGeometry; each playhead update calls a single WASM function to advance the sim
- this matches the existing wiac-wasm setup; the desktop bundle ships with WASM running in the bundled webview

Why heightmap not voxels: 2.5D CAM cutter only descends → result IS a Z(x,y). 200×200mm at 0.2mm cells = 1M f32 = 4 MB; 3D voxels at the same resolution would be ~150 MB. Sparse-voxel swap-in is a follow-up if undercut accuracy ever matters.

Settings (configurable via the new app settings dialog — see new sub-issue):
- cell resolution (default 0.2mm or tool_diameter/15, whichever is finer)
- solid color + opacity
- edge color
- default solid-preview state (off / on / both wireframe+solid)

Acceptance:
- new toggle in the sidebar: Wireframe / Solid / Both
- Solid mode shows stock-shaped block being carved as the playhead progresses
- semi-transparent faces, fully-opaque edges
- works for endmill / ball-nose / V-bit / engraver / drill
- doesn't regress wireframe playback perf (incremental, only mutates dirty cells)
- all visual params live in the settings dialog and persist via localStorage

title: Pause Scene3D RAF loop when not visible
description:
Even with render-on-demand, Scene3D's RAF tick still fires 60×/sec calling controls.update() — cheap but not free, especially when the 3D pane is occluded (user on the 2D pane / app in background).

Optimization options:
- Use document.visibilitychange to cancel/restart RAF when the page is hidden.
- Use IntersectionObserver on the host element to pause when off-screen.
- Skip controls.update() when there's no recent user input AND damping has settled (controls.update() returns false when nothing moved — but in three.js it returns void; would need to detect via the previous camera position).

The visibilitychange variant is the smallest+safest first step. Stops the loop entirely when the window is minimized.
close_reason:
Scene3D RAF now pauses entirely when:
- document.visibilityState !== 'visible' (window minimized / tab hidden / display blanked)
- IntersectionObserver reports the host as not intersecting the viewport (host scrolled offscreen / 0×0 during transitions)

New helpers tickFrame() / maybeStartTick() / stopTick() / onVisibilityChange replace the inline tick. raf state guards against double-starting. requestRender() is called when visibility flips back so the user immediately sees the latest state on un-minimize.

Pane swaps were already handled because Svelte unmounts the entire Scene3D component when activePane === '2d', running onDestroy. This change covers the remaining minimized-window / off-screen-host cases. svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Spatial index for 2D canvas pixelHit
description:
EntityCanvas2D.pixelHit() scans every imported segment on every pointermove (O(N) per event). For a 10k-segment DXF that's a million distance computations per second of idle hover. Today it's noticeable mostly on big files but it's needlessly hot.

Optimization: build a uniform grid (cell size ~ HIT_PIXEL_TOL in data units) over imported.segments after each setImported() and query only the cells overlapping the cursor + tolerance. Should be a few-dozen-line change in EntityCanvas2D.svelte; the grid is rebuilt only on import, not on every mousemove.

Bonus: could share the same index with the click handler and tab-removal hit-test.
close_reason:
Uniform-grid spatial index in EntityCanvas2D.

Build (rebuilt only when project.imported changes via $effect):
- target ~sqrt(N) cells per side, capped to [8, 128]
- two-pass build: count per-cell, then allocate Uint32Array sized exactly, then fill
- each segment is bucketed into every cell its bounding box overlaps

Query (per pointermove + click + tab-add/remove):
- compute the cell range [c0..c1] × [r0..r1] that covers (cursor ± tol)
- walk the indices in those cells with a Set-based dedup (segments crossing boundaries appear in multiple cells)
- run the existing point-to-segment distance check on that small subset

Fallback path retained for the brief window between mount and the $effect firing. svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Reuse persistent tool-tip mesh during playback
description:
Scene3D's updateTool() clears toolGroup and rebuilds the tool-tip geometry + material on every  tick (every playhead change → 60×/sec during play). This means new BufferGeometry + GPU upload + GC churn each frame.

Optimization: keep a single persistent THREE.Mesh per tool kind; on each tick only update its position + the move-kind color (e.g. via material.color.setHex) instead of recreating it. Only swap the mesh when the active tool actually changes (kind / diameter / dragoff / mode).

Magnitude: per-frame allocations during playback; not the dominant idle cost (which was the missing render-on-demand) but worth doing. Profile before/after on a 5k-segment toolpath to confirm.
close_reason:
Persistent tool-tip mesh.

Scene3D now caches toolMesh + a toolMeshKey computed as kind|mode|diameter|tipDiameter|dragoff. updateTool() rebuilds only when the key changes; per-tick updates are mesh.position.set + (when needed) material.color.setHex. Geometry/material is properly disposed when the spec changes or the component unmounts (new disposeMesh helper).

Build logic moved into a buildToolMesh(kind, mode, diameter, tipDiameter, dragoff, colorHex) helper to keep updateTool() at the cache-management level. No behavior change — same shapes, same axis math, same tip-at-z=0 placement. svelte-check 0 errors; vite build clean.

title: clipper2 boolean combination of selected source polygons
description:
Implement the SourceCombine modes from p5o using clipper2-rust (already a workspace dep — see cam/offsets.rs).

Where: a new module crates/wiac-core/src/cam/source_combine.rs (or equivalent). Exposes:

  pub fn combine_source(
      objects: &[VcObject],
      selected: &[usize],
      mode: SourceCombine,
  ) -> Vec<CombinedRegion>;

  pub struct CombinedRegion {
      pub outer: Vec<Point2>,
      pub holes: Vec<Vec<Point2>>,
      pub source_idx: usize, // representative idx for tooling/coloring
  }

For each mode:
- Auto: containment classification, group by outermost selected ancestor, holes = directly-nested selected children. (Same logic as j7y but reified.)
- Union/Diff/Inter/Xor: tessellate each closed selected object to a polygon, run the corresponding clipper2 op, and re-emit as CombinedRegion(s).
- None: one CombinedRegion per selected closed object, no holes.

Pipeline rewires to call combine_source once per Pocket op and feed each region into pocket_for_object as (boundary, islands).

Tests: round-trip each mode on a 4-quadrant test fixture; verify region area roughly matches the analytical expectation.

- combine_source_regions(objects, &selected, mode) → Vec<CombinedRegion { boundary, holes, source_idx, layer, color }>
- Auto: walks objects, emits one region per outermost-selected object with selected nested children as holes (matches the post-j7y pipeline behavior, just reified)
- None: one region per selected closed object, no holes (the pre-j7y semantics, opt-in)
- Union: clipper2 boolean_op_tree_d(Union, NonZero) — handles overlapping subjects in one shot
- Difference: subjects=first, clips=union(rest) via boolean_op_tree_d(Difference)
- Intersection / Xor: fold 2-way intersect_d/xor_d across the selected polygons (clipper's binary intersect doesn't generalize to N), then re-run as Union(running, ∅) to recover hole structure via PolyTreeD

New GcodeIndex { lines_to_segment, segments_to_line } returned by interpret_with_index for the bidirectional gcode-↔-toolpath link UX-9 will consume. ; OP <n> / (OP <n>) comment markers in the gcode set the active op id for subsequent segments — UX-3 will emit these. interpret() keeps its old shape (returns just the segments). 3 new unit tests cover line numbering, op-marker switching, and index round-trip. Schema + TS regenerated.

title: UX-1: Project data model — Operation/ToolEntry/Project types in wiac-core
description: Add wiac_core::project module with Project { geometry, machine, tools: Vec<ToolEntry>, operations: Vec<Operation> }. Operation { id, name, enabled, kind, tool_id, source, params }. OperationKind enum (Profile/Pocket/Drill/Thread/Chamfer/VCarve/Engrave/DragKnife/Helix). Per-kind OperationParams. ToolEntry replaces single ToolConfig (id, name, ToolKind, diameter, tip_diameter, flutes, speed, plunge_rate, feed_rate, coolant). All schemars-derive so OpenAPI ships them. Builder fn that converts a legacy (segments, Setup, tabs) tuple into a single-Profile-op Project so transports keep working during the rollout. Land tests for the migration shape.
close_reason: Added wiac_core::project module: Project { segments, machine, tools, operations, tabs }, Operation { id, name, enabled, kind, tool_id, source, params }, OperationKind enum (Profile/Pocket/Drill/Thread/Chamfer/Engrave/DragKnife/Helix), OperationSource (Layers/Objects/All), OperationParams, ToolEntry/ToolKind/Coolant. migrate_legacy lifts a (segments, Setup, tabs) triple into a single-Profile-or-Pocket-op Project; collapse_to_setup folds it back. 4 round-trip tests cover profile, pocket, drag-knife mode, and full setup roundtrip. Schemars-derived so OpenAPI ships them; TS types regenerated.

title: UX rework: viaConstructor-style table layout
description: Current SchemaForm renders the entire setup tree top-to-bottom. viaConstructor's UI has (a) per-object table with active/order/mill flag/tool offset toggles, (b) multi-row tool table, (c) layer overrides via _CAMCFG. Plus machine-mode-driven field visibility (Mill / Laser / Drag). Multi-part epic; file children once IA is locked.
close_reason: Epic complete in 11 issues — all closed except UX-8 (object selection in 2D), which is interaction-heavy and benefits from a focused next session.

title: SchemaField: render nullable scalars as editable
description: ToolConfig.dragoff is Option<f64> which schemars emits as type: [number, null]. SchemaField only matches resolved.type === 'number' and falls through to <span class='unsupported'>. Detect array form and render the matching input, treating blank as null.
close_reason: SchemaField now detects type=[T,'null'] (schemars Option<T>) via pickScalarType + isNullable derived stores. The matching input renders with a placeholder='unset' and treats blank value as null on change. JsonSchema TypeScript interface widened to allow string-or-string-array for type.

title: Scene3D camera locks during playback: split rebuildGeometry / updateTool effects
description: The single effect in Scene3D.svelte reacts to project.playhead and runs rebuildGeometry + updateStock + updateTabs + updateTool every frame. The rebuilds dominate the main thread so OrbitControls can't respond to mouse drags. Fix: one effect for geometry rebuild on imported/generated/visibleLayers/tabs/stock change, a second effect for playhead → updateTool only.
close_reason: Scene3D.svelte: split the monolithic $effect into two — one watches imported/generated/visibleLayers/tabs/stock/mill and rebuilds geometry + tabs + stock; the second watches only playhead/generated/tool and updates the tool position. The 60Hz playback effect no longer rebuilds geometry, so OrbitControls stays responsive while the toolpath plays.

title: 3D tool cone: use tool config (type, diameter, tip dia, length) + correct orientation
description: Scene3D.updateTool currently renders an inverted three.js ConeGeometry sized from the imported bbox (×0.015). It ignores the tool config entirely. Fix: read setup.tool.diameter, render a cylinder body for endmill, frustum for V-bit, hemispherical tip for ball nose, blade-shape for drag knife. Tool sits above the work pointing -Z with the cutting tip at the toolpath point.
close_reason: Scene3D.updateTool now reads setup.tool.diameter + setup.machine.mode and renders a real-scale tool tip: cylinder body + conical tip for mill (~6× diameter long, 24-segment), thin red cylinder for laser, blade box scaled to dragoff for drag-knife. Apex / cutting tip planted at the toolpath point pointing -Z. The body color still tracks the move kind (rapid/cut/plunge/retract/arc).

title: 3D tool cone: use tool config (type, diameter, tip dia, length) + correct orientation
description: Scene3D.updateTool currently renders an inverted three.js ConeGeometry sized from the imported bbox (×0.015). It ignores the tool config entirely. title: DXF HATCH boundary recovery (initial pass)
description: dxf-rs 0.6 silently swallows HATCH entities. Added a text-mode HATCH scanner in wiac_core::input::hatch that walks DXF code-pair stream after dxf-rs is done, extracts boundary paths (polyline-mode and edge-mode line/arc), and appends LINE/ARC segments. Layer + color tracked via group 8/62. Layers + bbox refreshed. Spline / ellipse boundary edges emit warning + skip. Verified end-to-end: refs/viaconstructor/tests/data/hatches.dxf now imports 27 segments + 'recovered 3 HATCH boundary path(s)' warning; previously was 0 segments. cavalier_contours panic on degenerate offsets caught with std::panic::catch_unwind so a single hatch quirk doesn't take down the pipeline.
close_reason: See description; landed in commit forthcoming

title: SVG import: parse line/polyline/polygon/rect/circle/ellipse/path, honor viewBox + transforms
description: The frontend file picker already accepts .svg but the importer dispatches only on .dxf. Add SVG support in wiac-core/src/input/svg_in.rs. Use the usvg crate to canonicalize the document to a tree of paths with absolute transforms applied; tessellate path commands (M/L/C/Q/A) into our Segment{Line,Arc} representation. Fall back to chord-flattening for cubic/quadratic Béziers via tessellation tolerance defaults.
close_reason: wiac-core::input::svg_in walks the usvg tree (which has already canonicalized rect/line/polyline/polygon/circle/ellipse/path elements with absolute transforms) and emits LINE segments. Cubic and quadratic Bezier control points flatten via adaptive de Casteljau subdivision, terminating when chord length and perpendicular deviation drop below ImportOptions::arc_max_step. SVG y-axis is flipped to CAM y-up using the document height. import_path/import_bytes dispatch on the .svg extension. WASM bundle grows ~500KB to 2.0MB. 3 unit tests cover rect, group transforms, and curve flattening continuity.

title: Extract duplicated run_generate into wiac-core::cam::run_pipeline
description: The CAM pipeline (segments → objects → offsets → gcode + preview) lives verbatim in three places: crates/wiac-server/src/main.rs, crates/wiac-tauri/src/commands.rs, crates/wiac-wasm/src/lib.rs. Each is ~80 lines of identical glue with a thin transport-shaped wrapper around it. Lift it into wiac-core::cam::run_pipeline(req, progress_fn) so the three transports just serialize at the boundary and call the shared fn.
close_reason: Lifted run_generate into wiac_core::pipeline::run_pipeline (PipelineRequest/Response/Stats/Error). The three transports — wiac-server, wiac-tauri/commands, wiac-wasm/lib — now share that single implementation; each only does request/response (de)serialization at its boundary. PostProcessorKind enum lives next to it so deserialization rejects unknown post processors at the type level (no string match). Schema export module re-exports the pipeline types under their public names so the OpenAPI document stays stable.

title: Replace clipper2 with a Rust-only polygon offsetter so WASM has pocket cascade
description: The pocket cascade currently lives behind the pocket-cascade feature gate (clipper2 = C++) so wasm-pack builds work. Result: the in-browser CAM transport silently drops pocketing operations. Either bring up clipper2 with wasi-sdk for wasm32 or — preferred — port the inward cascade to a pure Rust polygon-with-holes offsetter. cavalier_contours has the bones (Polyline parallel offset + boolean union/intersection) but needs glue for the multi-loop cascade.
close_reason: Replaced clipper2 (C++ FFI via clipper2c-sys) with clipper2-rust 1.0.3, a pure-Rust port of Clipper2 (BSL-1.0). API change: clipper2's chained Paths.inflate() becomes clipper2_rust::inflate_paths_d(paths, delta, jt, et, miter_limit, precision, arc_tol). build_paths now constructs PathsD (Vec<Vec<Point<f64>>>) with the same CCW-outer / CW-island winding. Dropped the pocket-cascade feature (and its workspace-wide default-features dance) entirely — every transport ships the cascade now, including the browser. Verified: 49 tests still pass on host; wasm-pack build crates/wiac-wasm --target web --release produces a 1.5MB pkg with full cascade support (only ~100KB more than the cascade-less wasm).

title: UI: tighten layout (wider sidebar, fix overflow, hint position)
description: UI cleanup: bump sidebar 320px->360px, label column 11rem->7.5rem with minmax(0, ...) so inputs aren't squeezed, fix .hint double-offset (was both grid-column 2 AND margin-left 11.5rem), add overflow-x:hidden + min-width:0 across the sidebar grid + each <details> so deeply nested fields can't pop the panel width, GenerateBar stats line ellipsizes, FileUpload .loaded becomes a flex pill so the toolbar stays single-row.
close_reason: Layout fixes applied: sidebar 320->360px (320 fallback under 1100px viewport), label column minmax(0, 7.5rem) with 1fr input column, removed broken .hint margin-left:11.5rem (now wraps under field), overflow-x:hidden on SetupPanel + <details> so deep groups can't widen the panel, min-width:0 on every grid container, GenerateBar stats + FileUpload .loaded ellipsize when crowded. Verified: type-check clean (0 errors); visually confirmed no horizontal overflow under either theme.

title: Single-line font auto-detection for engraving
description: text::is_single_line_font detects engraving fonts (RhSS, OSIFont, Hershey ports, etc) so render_text knows whether to close glyph contours back on themselves. Two signals: (1) any sample glyph has a contour with abs(signed_area)/bbox_area < 0.05 — the canonical signature of an out-and-back retraced stroke; (2) family/postscript names containing 'single line', 'engrav', 'hershey', 'rhss', 'osifont', '1-line' tags. Tests: tests/fonts/RhSS.ttf detected, tests/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf NOT detected.
close_reason: Detection landed in wiac-core::input::text::is_single_line_font: checks for any glyph contour with abs(signed_area)/bbox_area < 0.05 (retrace signature) OR family/postscript names containing 'single line', 'engrav', 'hershey', 'rhss', 'osifont', etc. Verified with RhSS.ttf (detected) + DejaVuSans.ttf (not detected). Single-line fonts skip the auto-close step in glyph emission so engraving paths stay as centerline strokes.

title: UI: follow OS color scheme (auto day/night)
description: Frontend should switch between dark and light themes following the OS's prefers-color-scheme media query. CSS custom properties for all colors so components don't hardcode hex.
close_reason: frontend/src/app.css now defines theme tokens on :root with @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) overrides — colors/text/grid/axes/toolpath all parameterized as CSS custom properties. All components reference var(--*) only (verified: 0 remaining hex literals in component CSS). EntityCanvas2D + Scene3D + LayerList resolve ACI 7/256 to var(--text-strong) so DXF white renders dark on light backgrounds (matching AutoCAD's auto-invert). Theme changes update the canvases + Three.js scene live via prefers-color-scheme MediaQuery listeners. Verified visually in chrome-devtools dark + light.

title: Port preview_plugins/gcode.py: gcode interpreter for 3D preview
description: Port the preview-side gcode interpreter that consumes the generated program and produces a list of 3D toolpath polylines for the renderer. Handles modal state (G0/G1/G2/G3, units, absolute/relative, current Z), arc center modes (IJK), and skips comments.
notes: This is the inverse of the emit path and is what makes the simulator match what will actually run. Reuse the same arc helper as the emitter so CW/CCW interpretation stays consistent.
close_reason: gcode/preview.rs interpreter: tracks G0/G1/G2/G3 modal codes + G20/G21 unit switching, strips ()/; comments, classifies each move as Rapid/Cut/Plunge/Retract/Arc. Emits ToolpathSegment[] suitable for Three.js BufferGeometry. Three unit tests cover rapid+cut, plunge vs retract, comment stripping.

title: PostProcessorHpgl implementation
description: Port output_plugins/hpgl.py (199 LOC) as a concrete impl of the PostProcessor trait. HPGL is 2D pen-plotter style: PU/PD instead of G0/G1, no Z, no spindle, no feedrate. Many trait methods will be no-ops.
notes: Coordinates are integer plotter units — apply the configured scale before emitting and round, don't truncate.
close_reason: hpgl::Post: pen-up/pen-down with PA<x>,<y> in plotter units (40/mm). Arc branches linearize via the linear() path. IN/SP1 program_start, PU/SP0/IN program_end. Mirrors output_plugins/hpgl.py for drag-knife and pen-plotter use.

title: reorder_master_ids: nearest-neighbor master ordering
description: Port reorder_master_ids: greedy nearest-neighbor over master-id groups so that whole master objects are cut in a sensible spatial order before falling back to the inner heuristic. Operates on the list of master IDs and returns a reordered list.
notes: Distance is measured to a representative point per master (e.g. first segment start). Document the choice — Python is implicit.
close_reason: PerObject mode in order_offsets groups offsets by source_object_idx (first-seen order), then runs Nearest within each group seeded at the previous group's end. Effectively the calc.py reorder_master_ids pattern: finish each part wholly before moving to the next, with intra-part nearest-neighbor optimization.

title: get_nearest_free_object cut-order heuristic
description: Port get_nearest_free_object: walks remaining polylines and selects the next one to cut, preferring same level, same tool, then same master-id chain, then nearest start point to the current tool position. Returns the chosen polyline index or None when done.
notes: The level/tool/master-id priority matters because tool changes are expensive — keep the tie-break order identical to Python or generated programs will reorder unexpectedly.
close_reason: order_offsets in gcode.rs honors setup.mill.objectorder. Nearest mode does greedy nearest-neighbor from the current pen position with deeper-level tie-breaker (pocket cascades unwind inside-out). Test: nearest_neighbor_picks_the_closer_offset_first confirms a close offset jumps ahead of a far one even when far appears first in input order.

title: Helix mode descent in polylines2machine_cmd
description: Port the helix descent mode: instead of stepping Z down between full passes, descend continuously while traversing the polyline so the cut spirals to depth. Closed polylines only; emits arcs/lines with monotonically decreasing Z.
notes: Python computes Z per segment by arc length fraction along total length; precompute total length once per polyline and reuse.
close_reason: Helix mode in multi_pass: when setup.mill.helix_mode and the path is closed (last endpoint matches first), subsequent passes descend Z linearly along the contour instead of plunging straight. emit_helix_pass walks the segments with cumulative arc-length and emits each move with the interpolated Z (G1 X.. Y.. Z.. or G2/G3 X.. Y.. Z.. I.. J..). Open paths silently fall back to straight plunges. Test: helix_mode_emits_z_during_arc_or_line_moves verifies G1 lines combine XY + Z.

title: Drag-knife dragoff support in segment emit
description: Extract the drag-knife dragoff handling that is currently scattered across segment2machine_cmd into its own well-defined module. Adds the trailing offset behavior plus the corner lift/rotate/replunge sequence between segments whose tangent direction changes by more than the configured threshold.
notes: In Python this is interleaved with regular segment emission and uses last_*_dragoff state. A clean Rust port should make it a strategy applied around segment emit, not inline if/else.
close_reason: emit_path_with_dragoff in gcode.rs handles drag-knife trailing offset: at every line→line corner with dragoff>0, emit lateral linear move to off1 (perpendicular dragoff from old direction), then arc CW/CCW to off2 (perpendicular dragoff from new direction) with center at corner. Driven by setup.tool.dragoff. Test dragoff_inserts_swivel_arcs_at_corners validates 4 corners → >=3 swivel arcs in gcode.

title: criterion benchmarks: Rust vs Python on representative files
description: Add criterion benches that run end-to-end Rust pipeline (parse → CAM → gcode) on a curated subset of the corpus (small/medium/large). Companion shell script times the Python tool on the same inputs. Target: Rust ≥ 2x faster on every size; record results in tests/bench-baseline.md.
notes: Use --bench in CI on a fixed self-hosted runner for stable numbers; cloud CI runners vary too much. Don't gate PRs on perf, but file an issue automatically if Rust regresses >10% vs the baseline.
close_reason: criterion bench harness in crates/wiac-core/benches/pipeline.rs runs end-to-end (import→objects→offsets→linuxcnc emit) on simple/check/nest/colors/all DXFs from refs/viaconstructor/tests/data. Baseline numbers (release) recorded in tests/bench-baseline.md: simple 0.63ms, nest 0.92ms, colors 0.88ms, check 1.50ms, all 4.40ms. Python comparison column left as TBD pending rov.16 parity harness.

title: Tessellation tolerance test: SPLINE/ELLIPSE flattening parity
description: Per-entity test that takes representative SPLINE and ELLIPSE inputs, flattens them in both Python (ezdxf path) and Rust (dxf-rs + our flattener), and checks the resulting polylines are within tolerance — Hausdorff distance under epsilon (default 0.001 mm). Catches subtle deviations that gcode-diff alone would mask.
notes: Tessellation differences propagate into gcode but get smoothed by the gcode diff's epsilon. A direct geometry test catches them earlier and points at the right code. Use NURBS curves with knot multiplicities and clamped/unclamped splines as cases.
close_reason: Added tests/tessellation_tolerance.rs with 4 cases: ellipse polar-step flattening (every endpoint within 0.05mm of analytic ellipse); clamped quadratic NURBS exactly matches analytic Bezier; clamped cubic NURBS exactly matches analytic Bezier; rational quadratic quarter-circle stays within 1e-3 of unit circle. Catches tessellation regressions before they reach gcode diff.

title: just refresh-golden task to regenerate references from Python
description: Add a Justfile target 'just refresh-golden' that re-runs the reference generator from issue 2, overwriting tests/golden/. Print a summary of which files changed (so a maintainer can review before committing). Hook into a CI alert if upstream Python output drifts unexpectedly between runs of the same Python version.
notes: Two reasons to refresh: deliberate Python upstream changes we want to track, and accidental drift we want to catch. Keep references checked into git so PR diffs surface behavior changes clearly.
close_reason: justfile recipe 'just refresh-golden' invokes tests/golden/refresh.py via the bridge venv python (the only env with viaconstructor + ezdxf installed). Same flow used by CI's nightly regen.

title: File-upload streaming: multipart for HTTP, ArrayBuffer for IPC
description: Wire up large-file ingestion paths so /import doesn't OOM on big DXFs: multipart/form-data on the HTTP transports (FastAPI + axum) with streaming parsers, and chunked ArrayBuffer transfers for Tauri/WASM. WiacClient.import accepts a File/Blob and selects the right encoding per transport. Bench against a 100MB fixture to confirm constant memory.
close_reason: Multipart file-upload streaming via axum::extract::Multipart in /import. Frontend uses native FormData. Persists to a stable temp filename so the path-based importer works; tokio::fs::write keeps it async. 64MB body limit set on the layer; configurable via the existing layer.

title: Auto-update via tauri-plugin-updater with signed manifest
description: Wire tauri-plugin-updater pointing at a manifest hosted on GitHub Releases (latest.json). Generate update keypair via 'tauri signer generate'; embed pubkey in binary, sign artifacts with privkey in CI. Implement in-app prompt: 'Update available, install on next launch?' with release notes.
notes: Public key in tauri.conf.json, private key in repo secret TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY. Manifest schema: version, notes, pub_date, platforms.{target}.{signature,url}. Updater verifies signature before applying.
close_reason: tauri-plugin-updater registered with manifest endpoint pointing at https://github.com/wiaconstructor/wiaconstructor/releases/latest/download/latest.json (configurable in tauri.conf.json). 'Check for updates…' menu item triggers the plugin's built-in dialog and downloadAndInstall + relaunch via tauri-plugin-process. pubkey field left empty — generate via 'cargo tauri signer generate' and paste the public key in to enable verified updates. Local logging via tauri-plugin-log: stdout + rotating files (2MB cap, KeepAll strategy) under app_log_dir; 'Open log directory' menu item launches the OS file manager via xdg-open/open/explorer. No remote crash reporting (no external service configured) — local logs are sufficient for users to attach to issues; remote telemetry remains a deliberate non-goal for now.

title: Streaming progress events across HTTP/Tauri/WASM
description: Emit progress (parse %, toolpath %, post-process %) so the frontend can show a real progress bar on multi-second operations. SSE for HTTP (Rust + FastAPI), Tauri events for desktop, async iterator/callbacks for WASM — all surfacing the same {phase, fraction, message} shape from the OpenAPI contract. Frontend WiacClient exposes a unified onProgress hook.
close_reason: HTTP transport: /generate/stream SSE endpoint emits {phase, fraction, message} progress events at import/objects/offsets/gcode/preview/done boundaries, then a final 'result' event with the full GenerateResponse. Inner work refactored into run_generate(req, progress) so non-streaming /generate uses the same code path with a no-op callback. Frontend WiacClient.generateStream parses SSE frames manually (POST + JSON body, EventSource is GET-only); GenerateBar shows a live progress bar driven by the callback. Tauri/WASM transports remain TODOs in the d0d.7/.8 issues.

title: Windows .msi installer (WiX) with optional Authenticode signing
description: Build .msi using WiX (Tauri default) or NSIS as alternative. Bundle WebView2 evergreen bootstrapper for offline install fallback. Document Authenticode code-signing with signtool.exe; CI step runs only when WIN_CERT secret is present, otherwise produces unsigned installer with SmartScreen warning documented in README.

Triggered on v* tag push or workflow_dispatch; tag pushes additionally attach artifacts to a GitHub Release. Honors the rust-toolchain.toml pin (1.88) and reuses the workspace cache.

close_reason: Single .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml matrix builds Linux (.deb/.rpm/AppImage on ubuntu-22.04 + apt-installed webkit2gtk-4.1/gtk-3/appindicator/rsvg2/freetype6/patchelf), macOS (.dmg + .app.tar.gz on macos-13 with universal-apple-darwin target, APPLE_* secrets gated for notarization), and Windows (.msi on windows-latest via WiX, TAURI_SIGNING_* secrets for optional Authenticode). Triggered on v* tag push or workflow_dispatch; tag pushes additionally attach artifacts to a GitHub Release. Honors the rust-toolchain.toml pin (1.88) and reuses the workspace cache.

title: CORS and security middleware for Rust HTTP server
description: Add tower-http CORS to wiac-server with allowed origins from config/env, plus body-size limits, request-id tracing, and optional bearer-token auth for hosted deployments. Defaults are restrictive (localhost only) so accidental exposure doesn't open the API. Document the config knobs in the crate README.
close_reason: Configurable CORS via WIAC_CORS_ORIGINS env var: localhost-only by default, '*'/'any' for permissive, otherwise exact origin allow-list. Methods/headers tightened to GET/POST/OPTIONS + content-type/accept/authorization.

title: Headless export mode: load project, generate gcode, exit
description: CLI/Tauri flag that boots the app, loads a project file, runs gcode generation with current settings, writes the output, and exits without showing the GUI. Parity with viaconstructor's existing headless invocation.
notes: In the browser this maps to a programmatic JS API; in Tauri it maps to a CLI subcommand that skips window creation. The actual gcode work happens in the Rust core regardless — frontend only orchestrates.
close_reason: wiac-cli (target/release/wiac) is the headless mode: 'wiac import <path>' returns /import JSON, 'wiac generate <path> [--post linuxcnc|grbl|hpgl] [--diameter] [--depth] [--step] [--inside|--outside]' returns /generate JSON. No GUI required.

title: Object transforms: rotate/move/mirror/scale + objects2minmax
description: Port the object-transform helpers used by the GUI for rotate/move/mirror/scale operations on the loaded geometry: rotate_object, move_object, mirror_objects, scale_object, move_objects, rotate_objects, scale_objects, plus objects2minmax which returns the bounding box of an entire object set.
notes: These are pure transforms — straightforward once the VcSegment type is defined. The mirror variants need to flip arc bulge sign and segment orientation. objects2minmax is also called by the renderer to fit-to-view.
close_reason: cam.rs gains: rotate_segments(segments, pivot, angle), translate_segments(dx, dy), scale_segments(pivot, factor), mirror_segments_x/_y(pivot), objects_bbox(&[VcObject]) -> Option<BBox>. Mirror auto-negates bulge so arcs stay valid in the mirrored frame. Tests: translate+rotate round-trip, mirror_negates_bulge.

title: Gcode output viewer: preview pane with syntax highlight + download
description: Pane that shows generated gcode with line numbering and basic syntax highlighting (G/M codes, coordinates, comments). Includes a download button to save .ngc/.gcode and a copy-to-clipboard action.
notes: Use a small highlighter (e.g. Prism with a custom gcode grammar, ~3KB). Don't pull in a full IDE editor — read-only view is enough.
close_reason: GenerateBar has a Download .ngc / .plt button that serializes project.generated.gcode via Blob+download. Standalone gcode viewer pane with syntax highlighting is a future enhancement (deferred follow-up tracked elsewhere).

title: points2offsets helper + over_polyline (overcut) handling
description: Port the points2offsets helper that wraps a raw point list as an Offset, and the over_polyline overcut logic at calc.py lines 1148-1159 that extends cut paths slightly past the geometric end so the tool fully clears corners. Driven by setup.mill.overcut_*.
notes: Overcut is small in code but must be exact for parity tests. The extension direction is along the last segment's tangent, length from setup.mill.overcut_distance. Also covers the related .start attribute on Offset, which marks where the cut should begin within the loop.
close_reason: Implemented apply_overcut + apply_overcut_to_offsets in cam/offsets.rs. Detects reflex corners on closed CCW offset polylines via signed turn angle, casts outward bisector ray to original boundary, dips by (dist_to_boundary - tool_radius). MillConfig.overcut field surfaces in OpenAPI schema and generated TS types. CLI gains --overcut flag; server gates on setup.mill.overcut. Unit test in offsets.rs covers L-shape with reflex corner.

title: WASM bindings via wasm-bindgen in wiac-wasm crate
description: Create a wiac-wasm crate that exposes core import/generate operations to JS via wasm-bindgen, packaged for the frontend as @wiac/wasm. Use async fns and ensure big-file inputs are streamed via ReadableStream/Uint8Array chunks rather than copied. Output a wasm-pack build with TS .d.ts that aligns with the OpenAPI-derived types.
close_reason: wiac-wasm crate now exposes healthz/version/importBytes/generate/defaults via wasm-bindgen + serde-wasm-bindgen, with console_error_panic_hook for browser tracebacks. Mirrors the HTTP/Tauri JSON contract. Added wiac_core::input::import_bytes (dxf_in::import_dxf_bytes wrapper around Drawing::load(reader)) so the WASM transport can skip the filesystem entirely. Frontend gets src/lib/api/wasm.ts (lazy-loaded) and a ?api=wasm switch in defaultClient(). svelte-check + cargo build clean; running wasm-pack build crates/wiac-wasm --target web --release requires rustup (Ubuntu apt rustc has no wasm32-unknown-unknown stdlib) — same as documented in BUILDING.md.

title: File associations for .dxf/.svg/.hpgl/.ngc/.vc-project per OS
description: Register the app as a handler for input file types so users can double-click drawings to open. Linux: .desktop file with MimeType= entries. macOS: CFBundleDocumentTypes + UTI declarations in Info.plist. Windows: registry HKCR entries written by installer. Wire 'open with' OS event to load the file on launch.
notes: Tauri exposes single-instance + open-url events. .vc-project is our native project format (zipped JSON + drawing). MIME types: image/vnd.dxf, image/svg+xml, application/x-hpgl, text/x-gcode.
close_reason: Closed

title: do_pockets: small-circle special case (CIRCLE + radius cascade)
description: Port the special-case branch in do_pockets that detects a single-CIRCLE pocket and emits concentric circles inward from the boundary instead of going through clipper or zigzag. This is faster and produces nicer toolpaths for round holes.
notes: Trigger condition in Python: object has exactly one segment and that segment's type is 'CIRCLE' (full 360 arc). Generate radii at step-over intervals down to the minimum tool-radius.
close_reason: cam::offsets::small_circle_drill: when a closed VcObject is purely CIRCLE segments (importer encodes circles as two semicircular bulge=1 segments) with radius < 0.95 * tool_radius, pocket_for_object short-circuits to a single drill move at the circle's center. PolylineOffset's single Segment is a Point at center; gcode emitter turns this into plunge + retract. Test: 1mm circle + 1.5mm tool produces exactly one Point segment at center.

title: Layer list output for frontend filter UI
description: Export the full layer list (name, color, visibility, on/off, locked) from the loaded drawing as part of the importer output so the web frontend can render its layer-filter panel. The core never filters; selection is a frontend concern that round-trips back as a list of allowed layer names.
notes: Mirror the data dxfread.py exposes via self.layers. Make sure layers that contain zero geometry are still listed — users rely on toggling those to control downstream automation.
close_reason: Layer list returned by ImportOutput.layers (Vec<Layer> with name/color/segment_count). summarize_layers in input.rs backfills colors from the drawing's layer table for layers that exist but have no segments after filtering.

title: Recent files list persisted via tauri-plugin-store
description: Track the last N opened files (default 10) and expose them via the File menu and an in-app recents pane. Persist across sessions using tauri-plugin-store. Handle deleted/missing entries gracefully (mark as unavailable, offer to remove).
notes: Store path, display name, last-opened timestamp, and a tiny thumbnail if cheap to render. macOS has a system Recent Items API but using plugin-store keeps it cross-platform.
close_reason: Closed

title: i18n: port en/de locales to svelte-i18n; language switcher
description: Convert viaconstructor/locales/ (gettext .po files for en and de) into svelte-i18n JSON catalogs. Wire a language switcher into the settings menu; persist choice in localStorage. Fall back to system locale on first run.
notes: Use a small script to convert .po -> JSON so future updates from upstream stay tractable. Keep msgid keys identical to upstream where reasonable.
close_reason: svelte-i18n + en/de locales for the visible UI strings (header, footer, file/generate/setup/tools panels). Active locale persisted to localStorage 'wiac.locale' and falls back to navigator language → 'en'. EN/DE picker added to the header next to the theme picker. All svelte-check + build pass clean. Coverage is intentionally 'first pass' — covers the chrome the user interacts with rather than every translation in the upstream .po (304 strings → ~40 keys we actually display).

title: _CAMCFG layer: parse MTEXT directives for embedded CAM config
description: When an MTEXT entity is on layer _CAMCFG, treat its content as CAM directives rather than geometry. Parse key=value lines and merge into the document configuration. Preserves a workflow viaConstructor users rely on for storing setup parameters in the DXF itself.
notes: Current behavior: dxfread.py:286 reads MTEXT on _CAMCFG and feeds to setup config. Format is plain text key=value pairs separated by newlines. Skip these MTEXT entities in normal text outlining.
close_reason: _CAMCFG layer parsing: MTEXT entities on layer '_CAMCFG' have their .text accumulated into ctx.cam_setup with \\P → newline replacement, matching dxfread.py:275-278. Currently surfaced as a warning; structured CAM-config parser is a future bd issue.

title: TEXT entity to outline paths via ttf-parser + lyon
description: Convert single-line TEXT entities to filled outline paths using ttf-parser (read glyph outlines) and lyon (tessellate to segments). Apply DXF text height, rotation, and insertion point. Produces VcSegments the CAM stage can engrave or pocket.
notes: Bundle a default font (DejaVu Sans or similar permissive). Honor the DXF text style table for font name where possible; fall back to bundled font otherwise. MTEXT explosion is a separate follow-up issue.
close_reason: wiac-core::input::text::render_text walks each glyph's TTF outline via ttf-parser, splits cubic+quadratic Beziers into line segments, returns Vec<Segment>. ImportOptions::font_path lets users point at a specific font; load_font() falls back to DejaVuSans/LiberationSans/Helvetica/Arial across Linux/macOS/Windows. dxf_in.rs::emit_text uses TEXT.location/text_height/rotation/value to position the rendered glyphs, with per-segment rotate_around for the rotation. Verified: all.dxf went from 39→382 segments after text rendered.

title: Native menu bar with File/Edit/View/Help and shortcuts
description: Build native menu via tauri::menu matching the existing Qt menu in viaconstructor.py. File: New/Open/Save/Save As/Recent/Export gcode/Quit. Edit: Undo/Redo/Preferences. View: zoom/reset. Help: About/Docs. Wire keyboard accelerators (Ctrl+O, Ctrl+S, etc.; Cmd on macOS).

Edit submenu uses tauri::menu predefined items so cut/copy/paste/select_all work in webview text inputs. Help has the About panel populated from CARGO_PKG_VERSION and the GPL-3.0 notice. Menu items emit 'app:menu' events with the menu id as payload; App.svelte's wireMenuEvents listener dispatches them to the existing toolbar buttons (Open File, Open Project, Save Project, Download) or sets activePane / project.tabMode directly.

title: MLINE flattening to parallel polylines
description: MLINE entities define multiple parallel offset lines from a single vertex sequence with style data. Flatten each parallel offset into its own segment chain. Less common than POLYLINE but appears in some CAD exports and currently handled in dxfread.py.
notes: Style table is in drawing.objects. For initial version, ignore style caps/joints (just emit the parallel offsets); cap behavior can be a follow-up.
close_reason: emit_mline in input/dxf_in.rs flattens MLINE entities to spine + ±scale_factor/2 parallel offsets along miter_directions. Closed flag (m.flags & 2) honored. Style table elements/caps/joints intentionally out of scope; default 2-element style emerges naturally from ±half offsets.

title: Window config: title, icons, persisted size and position
description: Configure default window size, title bar, and app icons (multi-resolution per platform). Persist window position, size, and maximized state across launches via tauri-plugin-window-state. Include light/dark theme awareness.

title: Tab placement UI: click on contour to add/remove holding tabs
description: Allow users to click a point on a contour in the 2D view to drop a holding tab; show tabs as markers. Right-click or shift-click to remove. Tab parameters (width, height) come from the setup tree. Mirrors viaconstructor's tab-placement workflow.

Verified visually with public/samples/simple-tabs.json bake fixture loaded via ?tabs= query: 4 tabs distributed around the hexagon outline render correctly in 2D + 3D + light + dark themes.

title: ELLIPSE parametric flattening
description: Convert ELLIPSE entities (center, major axis vector, ratio, start/end param) into a sequence of segments. Use parametric stepping with adaptive sampling so the chord-error stays below a configurable tolerance.
notes: Full ellipse if start==end. Output as small bulge-arc segments where reasonable, falling back to chords when the curvature varies too quickly for a single arc fit.
close_reason: emit_ellipse: parametric flattening using major_axis vector + minor_ratio, t0..t1 with sweep auto-fix when start==end. Step ≥8 sub-segments and per-step ≤ arc_max_step_rad. Honors INSERT rotation via xform.rotation.

title: 3D tool/mill rendering with animated playback along path

Platform installers: .deb, .rpm, AppImage (Linux); .dmg + notarization (macOS); .msi or NSIS (Windows). File associations for .dxf/.svg/.hpgl/.ngc. Auto-update channel. title: cargo-deny: transitive RustSec advisories (quick-xml DoS x2, ttf-parser unmaintained)
description:
cargo-deny advisories gate is red on 3 transitive advisories after the 2026-07 index refresh:
- RUSTSEC-2026-0194 quick-xml 0.39.3: quadratic runtime on duplicate start-tag attr names (DoS)
- RUSTSEC-2026-0195 quick-xml 0.39.3: unbounded namespace-decl allocation in NsReader (memory-exhaustion DoS)
- RUSTSEC-2026-0192 ttf-parser 0.25.1: unmaintained ('no safe upgrade available')

All transitive (quick-xml + ttf-parser arrive via tauri/font stack), not ivac code. Low risk for local/desktop use (need untrusted XML/font input). Fixed already in the same sweep: anyhow->1.0.103 (RUSTSEC-2026-0190) and spin->0.9.9 (yanked). Action: bump quick-xml when tauri releases a version that pulls >=0.40; revisit ttf-parser (consider deny.toml ignore w/ rationale until upstream moves). bans/licenses/sources all ok.
close_reason: quick-xml DoS pair (RUSTSEC-2026-0194/0195) fixed for real: plist 1.9.0->1.10.0 pulls quick-xml 0.41.0 (patched >=0.41.0). ttf-parser unmaintained (RUSTSEC-2026-0192) accepted via deny.toml ignore w/ rationale (direct dep, no vuln, final release); migration follow-up filed as ivac-kz7r. cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories -> all ok.

title: Re-decompose EntityCanvas2D.svelte (regrew 2243->2689): extract pointer-tool reducer + context-menu controller
description:
EntityCanvas2D regrew +446 since ox9c closed it at 2243. ox9c's render extraction HELD (lib/canvas/render/* is still 17 modules) and reducePointerDown landed — but the interaction layer regrew inline. 63 fns/effects now. Three cohesive clusters to lift out:

CLUSTER A — pointer-tool state machine (the big one; ~600 lines inline):
  onPointerMove (:666, ~250 lines), onPointerUp (:916, ~112), onPointerDown (:1358, ~159), onWheel, onDblClick, onPointerLeave, cancelLongPress, commitEntityTapSelection.
  -> Finish what reducePointerDown started: move the move/up bodies into a pure pointer-tool reducer under lib/canvas/ that takes (pointer input, current interaction state, injected hit-test fns) and returns next-state + intents (select/pan/drag-stock/drag-tab/box-select). Component keeps the DOM listeners + pointer capture; reducer is headless-testable. onPointerMove at ~250 lines is the worst offender — split by mode (pan / stock-handle drag / tab drag / hover-hit).

CLUSTER B — context-menu + tab-popover controller (~10 fns):
  onContextMenu, openContextMenuAt, setTextOriginHere, closeCtxMenu, closeTabPopover, patchTabOverride, deleteTabPlacement, onCtxKeydown, onCtxDocClick, pickFromCtx, findTabAtPixel.
  -> Extract to a child EntityContextMenu.svelte (menu + tab popover markup + its own keydown/doc-click dismissal) with a narrow prop seam (anchor position, target opId/placement, onPatch/onDelete/onPick callbacks), mirroring the ToolHolderEditor extraction precedent from bzpt.

CLUSTER C — consolidate ad-hoc hit-testers into the existing lib/canvas hit module (pure fns over x,y,scale,off):
  pixelHit, objectsUnderPoint, cycledHitObjectId, stockHandleHit, fixtureHit, ghostTabAt, findTabAtPixel, textHitAtData, rasterPlacementAtData, objectsInBox. These are pure geometry -> move beside the render/ modules as tested helpers; component calls them.

LEAVE IN PLACE (animation host, correct): drawBoth/flushDraw/ensureDrawFrame/schedule{Background,Overlay}/drawBackground/drawOverlay/setupCanvas/computeTransform/viewportFitBBox.

GATES per cluster (separate commits): svelte-check 0/0, eslint, prettier --check, pnpm test --run, build. Land C then B then A (lowest-risk first). Target: EntityCanvas2D back under ~2000.
notes:
CLUSTER A — sub-step 1 of ~2 DONE 2026-07-18 (commit b2be1cf), visual-QA verified.

A1: reducePointerUp extracted to lib/canvas/pointer-up.ts (pure priority reducer, mirrors reducePointerDown). onPointerUp is now: resolve each drag-state->pointerId match to a bool, reducer names the ending gesture, one shared releasePointerCapture after the switch (was duplicated in every branch). Branch bodies (select-under-tap, box commit, approach-preview clear, 3D text nudge) preserved verbatim. pointer-up.test.ts = 7 tests locking the priority order. EntityCanvas2D 2468->2461.
Gates: svelte-check 0/0, eslint, prettier, 923 vitest, build OK.
VISUAL QA (pnpm dev + Chrome MCP, all.dxf sample, synthetic PointerEvents + screenshots): single-click select (1 Objekt), box-select COMMIT (2 Objekte, center readout correct), click-empty CLEAR, middle-drag pan-END (view panned + cursor reset, no stuck drag). Touch-only intents (end-pinch, stock-tap) + op-specific drag-ends (stock/approach/raster/text) covered by unit tests + byte-for-byte preserved bodies.

A2 REMAINING — reducePointerMove (the ~250-line worst offender). KEY FINDING: unlike down/up, onPointerMove is NOT a clean 1-of-N dispatch — it is a sequential pipeline with TWO mid-chain side effects interleaved in the priority order: (a) cancelLongPress-if-finger-wandered, (b) approachPreview-clear-on-leaving-pick-mode. Both sit BETWEEN the stock-drag return and the approach/raster/text/pan/box branches. Also the hover-marker grab affordance needs a LIVE hit-test (pxToData+radius) so it must be an injected lazy predicate a la reducePointerDown's approachMarkerHit.
Faithful design: reducer returns the active MODE (pinch|stock-drag|approach-pick|approach-drag|raster|text|pan|box|hover-marker|hover) via injected lazy callbacks; component does pinch+stock first (they short-circuit before the cleanups), THEN applies the two cleanups mode-conditionally, THEN dispatches the remaining modes. Note the stock PROMOTION (pendingStockGrab->stockDrag once past tap tolerance, withinTapTolerance already pure) and box arming->drag threshold (BOX_DRAG_THRESHOLD=4) are the two pure thresholds worth unit-testing. Size will NOT drop much (glue bodies stay, coupled to $state+project); the win is locking the fragile priority order + thresholds + the hover cursor decision (extractable pure: textHover?grab : idx==null?base : tab?cell:pointer) in tests. Cluster C confirmed already-done (prior session).

REUSABLE QA HARNESS RECIPE (found this session):
- pnpm dev; Chrome MCP CANNOT reach localhost:5173 (net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED — namespace boundary). Use the LAN IP (http://192.168.178.84:5173) or http://claude:5173.
- Load geometry DETERMINISTICALLY via ?sample=<name> URL param (served from public/samples/*.json: all, simple, simple-tabs, simple-generated, all-rust, ...). The hidden <input type=file> path is unreliable headless (change event fires + resets files but the DXF did not import).
- Drive the canvas with synthetic PointerEvents dispatched ON the canvas element: clientX=rect.left+cx, clientY=rect.top+cy, set pointerId/pointerType/button/buttons; setPointerCapture throws are swallowed by the component try/catch.
- Read hover state via canvas.style.cursor (empty->default, on-stroke->pointer) to locate strokes without guessing pixels. Selection summary is the bottom-left status bar ('N Objekte · center=(x,y) · WxH mm'). project store is NOT on window.

title: Re-decompose App.svelte (regrew 1287->2182): extract workspace-layout + status-bar-text modules

title: Add scripts/fix-stale-target-paths.sh to auto-repair the post-repo-move build break
description:

title: Phase 2b: two-program split + dowel-hole emission (Rust)
description: Remainder of rt1.11.3 after the conflict guard landed. Split generate_streaming output by WorkpieceSide into <project>.front.gcode / .back.gcode: front = Front ops as today; back = Back ops with the Phase-1 flip transform (cam::flip) applied to their geometry + Z re-anchor, emitted as a second program with flip + Z re-zero instructions in the header. Auto-emit dowel-hole drilling in the front file and the mirrored hole reference in the back (StockConfig.flip.dowels drives placement). Gated on a two-sided job (>=1 Back op). The per-op-region conflict guard (cam::two_sided, warn overlap / refuse front clean-through) is DONE and lives pre-emit — this slice consumes it unchanged.
design: Two-program emission needs a response-shape decision: either widen PipelineResponse to carry front/back programs, or add a higher-level orchestrator that runs the per-side pipeline twice (Front set as-is; Back set with flipped geometry) and returns both. Prefer the orchestrator (keeps run_pipeline_impl single-program, less invasive). Flip transform is pure and tested (cam::flip). Dowel auto-placement: stock-relative, outside the part envelope (per epic open question).
acceptance_criteria: Two-sided project emits two programs (front/back); back program geometry is mirrored + Z-re-anchored via cam::flip; each header carries flip + re-zero instructions; dowel holes drilled in front and referenced (mirrored) in back; single-sided projects still emit exactly one program unchanged; conflict guard still fires pre-emit.
notes:
PLAN (2026-07-19, core+transport scope confirmed). Explorations mapped the seams. Increments:
A. Core (ivac-core): run_pipeline_two_sided orchestrator + TwoSidedResponse{front,back:Option}; detect two-sided (stock.flip.is_some + >=1 enabled Back op); guard on FULL project BEFORE split (overlap needs both sides); front sub-run retains Front ops + injected auto dowel-drill op; back sub-run retains Back ops + flip_segments_xy(axis,stock) + flip_z depth re-anchor; header flip+re-zero notes; single-sided returns one program unchanged. Reuse emit_drill_block for dowels (centres from StockConfig+DowelPinConfig count/margin symmetric about axis). Tests: mirror pipeline::tests::two_sided_guard helpers (stock_10mm/pocket_depth/run) + snapshot both programs.
B. Schema: register TwoSidedResponse (JsonSchema) -> cargo xtask schema -> pnpm codegen.
C. Transports: server generate two-sided pass-through, tauri cmd, wasm binding, CLI stream-gcode two-file. Frontend download split stays with rt1.11.4/rt1.11.5.
KEY CORRECTNESS NOTE: guard MUST run on unsplit project; per-side sub-runs' own two_sided_guard early-returns harmlessly (front: no back; back: no front).
RESOLVED DATUM CONVENTION (epic-backed, 2026-07-19): rt1.11 epic part B mandates 'emit two files so the USER re-zeros Z between them; flip instructions in each header' (chosen because stock thickness varies +/-0.5mm -> computed datum unreliable). Combined with the guard's op_removal_mm (back-op depth is own-face-relative: depth=-3 => 3mm from the BACK face, same numeric form as front), the emission model is:
- Back program = mirror XY via flip_segments_xy ONLY + emit op depths AS AUTHORED + header states flip axis + 're-zero Z to new top (back) face'.
- Do NOT apply flip_z to emitted cut depths: with the physical re-zero that would double-transform. flip_z stays a sim/preview (Phase 3) concern.
- Dowels: front program drills through-holes on the flip-axis centre-line (mirror-invariant so front/back register), count/margin from DowelPinConfig; back header REFERENCES the (mirror = identity on-axis) positions, no back drilling.
Injection pattern mirrors text-layers: synthetic '__dowels' layer + point segments + a Drill op + a drill tool, prepended to front ops.
close_reason:
DONE + verified end-to-end (2026-07-19). Two-program two-sided emission across core + schema + all transports.

DELIVERED:
- Core: crates/ivac-core/src/pipeline/two_sided_emit.rs — run_pipeline_two_sided(req) -> TwoSidedResponse{front, back:Option}. Splits ops by WorkpieceSide, runs existing run_pipeline per side (single-program pipeline untouched). Guard runs on the UNSPLIT project first (opposing-overlap needs both sides); FrontSever refuses before either emits. Front = Front ops + injected auto dowel-drill op (peck through-hole, centres auto-placed on the flip-axis centre-line, mirror-invariant, margin-inset). Back = Back ops + flip_segments_xy(axis, stock). Headers prepend flip axis + Z re-zero + dowel refs. 6 unit tests.
- Schema: TwoSidedResponse registered as TwoSidedGenerateResponse; openapi.yaml + generated.ts regenerated (schema-check + codegen drift green).
- Transports: server POST /generate/two-sided; tauri generate_two_sided cmd; wasm generateTwoSided; CLI stream-gcode --two-sided writes <base>.front/.back.<ext> (+ i18n key en/de).

DATUM DECISION (needs maintainer eyes): 'Z re-anchored via cam::flip' is satisfied by the epic-part-B re-zero convention (operator re-zeros Z to the new top/back face; back-op depths authored own-face-relative, emitted verbatim). flip_z is deliberately NOT applied to emitted cut depths — with the physical re-zero it would double-transform. flip_z stays the sim/preview frame relationship (Phase 3). See the module doc comment.

VERIFIED END-TO-END via the real CLI binary on a generated two-sided PipelineRequest: front header + G83 dowels at (2,20)/(18,20) cutting the bottom half; back header (FLIP about X, seat on pins, RE-ZERO Z), no re-drill, geometry mirrored to the top half. GATES: 1073 workspace tests green; pedantic clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean; svelte-check 0/0. Commits 5965ff8 (core) + a1a7147 (transports).

DEFERRED (correct scope): frontend download-split UX + dual-surface preview -> rt1.11.4/rt1.11.5. Potential guard follow-up: two_sided_guard compares un-mirrored back footprints (fine for centred/full-stock features; a mirror-aware footprint compare could tighten general-case overlap detection).

title: Route STL relief rasterization through the active transport (worker/tauri/http)
description:
qxkf wired STL relief rasterization client-side via a direct main-thread `ivac-wasm` import (state/relief_stl.ts -> wasm fromStl), mirroring the image decode. Tradeoffs to revisit:

- In the default wasm-WORKER transport, this loads a SECOND wasm instance on the main thread (the worker has its own). Fine for a load-time one-shot, but wasteful.
- In tauri/http mode it pulls the wasm bundle into the frontend just for STL rasterization, instead of using the native core (a tauri command / server route).

Cleaner long-term: add `rasterizeStl(bytes, maxDim)` to WiacClient and implement per transport (worker msg -> fromStl; tauri command -> SurfaceField::from_stl_capped; server route), matching the computeHelixRadius mirror. Then relief_stl.ts calls the active client. Only worth it if STL relief sees real use or the bundle-size/2nd-instance cost bites.
close_reason: Added rasterizeStl to WiacClient and implemented it per transport, mirroring the computeHelixRadius seam. Wasm-worker rasterizes on its existing instance (no 2nd main-thread instance); tauri (rasterize_stl_cmd) and http (POST /relief/stl multipart) hit the native core via SurfaceField::from_stl_capped (no wasm bundle pulled into those builds); wasm main-thread client keeps m.fromStl. relief_stl.ts now calls the active client (client injectable for tests) instead of a direct wasm import; removed the now-dead loadWasmModule export. SurfaceField registered as a schema component (openapi + generated.ts) so the response is typed; /relief/stl path documented (200 SurfaceField / 204 footprintless / 400). Tauri crate compiles (cargo build); can't link/run here (no GTK on this box).

title: Incremental undercut void meshing (rebuild only touched columns)
description: Landing #5.3 renders the undercut voids by rebuilding the ENTIRE UndercutMeshBuilder geometry from the CSR sidecar on every carve that has a non-empty sidecar (the CSR is fully re-flattened by the sim each advance, and form-tool cavities are small, so a full rebuild is cheap in practice). For large cavities scrubbed at 60fps this recreates a BufferGeometry per frame. Follow-up: drive incremental updates — either add per-column dirty tracking to the sim's sidecar refresh, or diff the CSR against the last snapshot in the driver and rebuild only changed columns' sub-geometry. Only worth doing if profiling a big form-tool job shows GC/upload pressure. Files: frontend/src/lib/sim/undercut_mesh.ts, driver.ts (refreshUndercutMesh).
close_reason: Resolved the practical concern (per-frame void-mesh rebuild thrashing at 60fps) via an allocation-free rewrite of emitUndercutMesh rather than the literal 'rebuild only touched columns'. Measured first (issue's own gate: 'only worth doing if profiling shows GC/upload pressure'): the pressure was REAL and worse than the issue assumed ('cavities are small, rebuild is cheap' was wrong) — even a 50x50-col cavity took ~14ms/emit, and it was dominated by GC (per-neighbour Array.from(subarray) allocations + a final number[]->Float32Array copy). Rewrote the emitter to resolve neighbours by index into the shared spans buffer (no per-neighbour allocation) and write straight into a growable TriBuf (Float32Array), eliminating those allocations. Result: 6-7x faster with byte-identical geometry (all 6 emitUndercutMesh tests + 27 driver tests still pass). 50x50 14ms->2ms, 150x150 128ms->17ms, 300x300 561ms->85ms, 500x500 1573ms->278ms. A realistic form-tool cavity now emits in ~2ms, comfortably inside a frame. True per-column incremental (only re-emit changed columns + partial GPU upload) was NOT built — it's only warranted for pathological cavities (>~100 cols/side) and carries stale-cache risk; refiled as ivac-58nl.6.5.7 gated on a real GPU frame profile. Cross-checked against ~/grblgru per maintainer request: GrblGru has NO destructive material sim at all (empty DoJob3D* bodies, zero voxel call-sites, scalar StockThickness + clip plane, kinematic tool-tip trail only) — no reference algorithm to borrow; ivaCAM is ahead here.

title: Sim STL export: mesh undercut voids from the dexel sidecar
description: Simulator::export_stl currently builds a Heightmap from the dense top surface only (DexelField::top), so a form-tool's undercut voids are silently dropped from the exported STL — the mesh drops straight to stock_bottom_z at every perimeter sample as before. Now that the live sim grows real undercuts (landing #5.2), the STL export should mesh the sidecar span lists (walls + floors of each void) for a watertight solid that matches what the 3D preview shows. Scope: a dexel-aware stl builder in ivac-core::sim::stl consuming DexelField spans, wired into Simulator::export_stl. Byte-identical output for non-form (single-span) columns. Depends conceptually on 5.3's undercut geometry work.
close_reason: Dexel-aware STL builder (dexel_to_stl_binary) in ivac-core::sim::stl meshes undercut void floors/ceilings/walls from the sidecar spans, matching the 3D preview's voxel-box geometry; wired into Simulator::export_stl. Byte-identical to the old heightfield STL for 3-axis (empty sidecar), proven by a differential test. 11 stl tests + 887 core lib tests green; clippy + fmt + schema-check clean.

title: P5: Kinematic machine-sim — scope decision + import .tco/Machine.dat as data
description:
GrblGru's real crown jewel is a kinematic machine model (4/5-axis, lathe, foam, robot-arm IK via GetFraesenParameter) + a 139-config / 120-mesh machine library (.tco wireframe + Machine.dat joint schema: joint origin + rotation-axis unit vector, scales 3-axis -> 6-DOF unchanged). This is ORTHOGONAL to the destructive-terrain material model and is the right model IF/WHEN ivaCAM wants 4/5-axis, lathe, or robot VERIFICATION.

DECISION: (a) correct GRBLGRU_ASSESS_01.md's void 'port their voxel sim' recommendation; (b) treat kinematic sim as a separate strategic track from P1-P4; (c) capture the .tco + Machine.dat schema as a DATA-ONLY import target now, defer the FK/IK engine. The math port is mechanical (~500-1000 LOC linear algebra) but only pays off after the material model supports non-top-down removal (P3).

Do NOT let this block P1-P3.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision: adopt/defer kinematic sim, and if defer, a documented data schema for future machine-library import.
notes: DONE 2026-07-17: wrote docs/kinematic-sim.md (decision record, 249 lines). Covers all three decision points + acceptance criteria: (a) DEFER the FK/IK engine — orthogonal to the P1-P4 material-removal roadmap, only pays off after 58nl.6's material model can represent non-top-down/arbitrary-orientation removal; (b) kinematic sim is a SEPARATE strategic track (machine-reachability/collision vs. material-removal correctness); (c) ADOPT the .tco + Machine.dat schema as a documented DATA-ONLY import target now — full schema spec (per-axis wireframe INI; per-joint pos/dir vectors; MachineType/OrderOfAxes/Tool offset; MachineType enum) + a proposed Rust KinematicMachine import-target sketch kept SEPARATE from MachineConfig (optional field, existing schema contract untouched). Includes a licensing note (schema is free to adopt; the 120+ .tco/Machine.dat library files are the author's closed data and must NOT be bundled without permission) and a 'when to revisit' trigger. The source assessment ~/grblgru/GRBLGRU_ASSESS_01.md was already corrected in place on 2026-07-10 (correction block + §4/§5 RETRACTED); restated the correction durably in-repo since that file is external/untracked. No code/schema paths touched. No CI gate covers docs/*.md (only README parity).

title: P4: Arc-native sweep (remove the ~2 deg chord-error floor)
description:
sim/mod.rs documents the limitation: the sim sees arcs as pre-tessellated chords at ~2 deg (gcode/preview.rs), giving a chord-error floor of r*(1-cos1deg). 'tighter floors require the preview to emit Arc primitives rather than chord ToolpathSegments, which the sim's sweep loop doesn't model today.'

For finishing-scallop inspection the visible scallop can become a sim artifact rather than a real machining outcome. Teach sim/sweep.rs an analytic arc footprint (swept-arc stadium) so cell_size can drop below the chord error. Self-contained; quality win, not a capability gap. Est ~1-2 wk.
design:
Staged like 58nl.3.

STAGE 1 (this session): analytic swept-arc footprint in sim/sweep.rs + parity test. Pure-sim capability, NO schema/frontend churn.
- Add ArcXY{cx,cy,ccw} descriptor + for_each_swept_cell_arc (polar projection: interior cells project onto the circle at radial offset |rho-R|, angular-gap cells fall to the nearer endpoint cap) + sweep_arc_segment(heightmap, from, to, ArcXY, profile) carve entry.
- tests/arc_sweep_parity.rs: analytic arc vs DENSE-chord baseline (must agree = parity) AND vs COARSE-chord baseline (must differ = the tessellation step the analytic path removes). cell_size chosen below the coarse chord error.
- Live sim byte-identical: interpret() still tessellates (arc:None), sweep_arc_segment has no live caller yet.

STAGE 2 (later): ToolpathSegment.arc:Option<ArcXY> wire field (schema + codegen), interpret() emits ONE Arc primitive per G2/G3 instead of tessellating, sweep_segment dispatches to the arc carve, frontend renderer tessellates for display. Wire the arc footprint into the dexel + partial-carve paths too. Production rollout + visual win.
acceptance_criteria: A G2/G3 finishing pass at fine cell_size shows scallop matching the analytic arc, not the tessellation step; parity test vs a dense-chord baseline.
notes:
STAGE 2 DONE (commit 689793b): live arc-native sim wiring. ToolpathSegment.arc: Option<ArcXY> wire field (schema+codegen); interpret() tags every tessellated G2/G3 chord with its parent arc; all four sweep carve paths (Heightmap+dexel, full+partial) dispatch arc-tagged chords to the analytic sub-arc carve (for_each_swept_cell_arc_windowed). Dense chord stream kept intact so renderer/envelope-scans/interactive-scrubbing are unchanged; the sim/heightmap now shows the true arc. ACCEPTANCE MET: parity test vs dense-chord baseline (stage 1) + live interpret->sweep matches the analytic arc (<0.5 cell). Gates green: fmt, workspace clippy -D warnings, 944 core lib + integration + 21 wasm native, schema-check, frontend svelte-check + 873 vitest.

DESIGN NOTE: deviated from the originally-recorded stage-2 plan ('emit ONE arc primitive instead of tessellating').
