title: audit 2026-05-16: naming inconsistency — Operation vs Op vs OpKind across BE/FE
description:
The 'operation' concept has three names depending on which file:
- `crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs` — `struct Operation`, `enum OperationKind`, `OperationSource`
- `crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs` — modules `op_drivers`, function `run_per_op`, `run_vcarve_op`, `run_halfpipe_op`, vars all `op.kind` / `op.id`
- `crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline_cache.rs` — `op_cache_key_with_finish`, `OpCacheValue`
- `frontend/src/lib/state/op_types.ts` — `OpEntry`, `OpKind`, `OpBase`
- `frontend/src/lib/components/OpKindPicker.svelte`, `OpPropertiesPanel.svelte`, `OperationsList.svelte`

A junior reading the codebase has to mentally translate three names for the same concept.

## Fix
Pick one and rename. Recommendation: `Op` is shortest, already dominates field/var/module references, and is what the frontend uses. Rename:
- `struct Operation` → `struct Op` (or `type Op = Operation` as a transitional alias)
- `OperationKind` → `OpKind`
- `OperationSource` → `OpSource`
- `OperationsList.svelte` → `OpsList.svelte`

## Risks
- Schema regen required; serde rename attributes might already paper over part of this.
- Single large rename PR is the cleanest path; do not interleave with feature work.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-16: OperationParams is a junk drawer — push per-kind fields into OperationKind variants
description:
`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs` `OperationParams` (around line 992+) is a flat struct mixing:
- Universal: depth, start_depth, step, fast_move_z
- Pocket-only: pocket_islands, pocket_nocontour, pocket_insideout, xy_overlap
- Tool-compensation: overcut, reverse, objectorder
- Plunge-only: helix radius, peck step
- VCarve-only: carve_max_width_mm
- Thread-only: thread_pitch, thread_passes

A junior cannot tell which fields apply to which op kind without reading the pipeline dispatch. The type system carries no invariant.

## Fix
Carry per-kind fields inside the `OperationKind` variant directly:

```rust
enum OperationKind {
    Profile { offset: ProfileOffset },
    Pocket { strategy: PocketStrategy, params: PocketParams },
    VCarve { params: VCarveParams },
    Thread { params: ThreadParams },
    // ...
}

struct OperationParamsCommon {
    depth_mm: f64, start_depth_mm: f64, step_mm: f64, fast_move_z_mm: f64,
}
```

Operation = { id, name, common: OperationParamsCommon, kind: OperationKind, plunge: PlungeStrategy, tabs: TabsConfig, … }.

## Risks
- OpEntry discriminated union on the FE was just refactored (sue, 8d019ba) — good time to do the matching refactor on the BE side.
- Will require schema regen + frontend codegen update.

## Related
Pairs with epic 82pe maintainability theme; would simplify the per-op-driver split in 55o4 because each driver becomes `fn run(op: &Operation, kind: &XParams)` with no ad-hoc field lookups.
notes:
Reviewed end-to-end: 'OpParams' (now renamed via 29ks) holds ~40 fields mixing universal (depth, step, fast_move_z, plunge), tool-comp (overcut, reverse, objectorder), per-kind (xy_overlap / pocket_*, carve_max_width_mm, chamfer_after_width_mm, frame_shape, …), and behaviour-tags (helix, multi_pass_refine).

Properly migrating means:
1) Design new per-kind structs (PocketParams, VCarveParams, ChamferParams, DrillParams, ThreadParams) and embed them in OpKind variants.
2) Migrate ~50 readers of op.params.X to the new variant data — every pipeline/op_drivers, every offset_builder branch, every gcode emitter.
3) Serde backward-compat: every existing saved .wiac-project.json uses the flat shape. Need migration deserialisers that read flat-and-rewrite-into-variants. This alone is a careful design pass (which fields stay common, which move, how to handle ambiguity when an old project sets pocket-only fields on a Profile op).
4) Frontend OpEntry already discriminated-union (sue refactor) — wire conversion in build-project.ts would re-flatten to send to BE, OR BE updates to the new schema and the FE codegen flows through. Either way the wire contract changes.
5) Schema regen + every TS consumer of WireOp updates.

Estimate: 6–10 focused hours, in 3–4 commits, with a project-file migration test corpus. Doing it in one go without that test corpus risks silently breaking customer projects. Recommended approach when this lands: write a roundtrip test that loads every fixture under refs/viaconstructor/tests/data/*.json (whatever's there) before vs after, AND a synthetic 'flat schema' fixture to test the legacy-deser path. Then the refactor lands with confidence.
close_reason: all 3 steps shipped: per-kind variant structs (336345d), migration deserializer + reader migration (3d53a78 + 68e4c1d), drop flat fields (3f428aa). Pattern moved to OpKind::Drill only.

title: 3D-sim audit #6: re-tune computeCellSize for mesh-perf reality (not just memory)
description:
frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts:190-195 — `computeCellSize` targets toolDiameter/15 clamped to [0.05, 2.0]mm. A 1mm tool on a 500mm stock gives 7.5M cells (over the 4M cap, silently rescaled to ~0.09mm).

After fixes #1 + #2 land, the perf characteristic changes: bottleneck is mesh upload + GPU triangle count, not WASM serde. Re-tune the heuristic against the new realities — e.g.:

* Target cells × cell_byte_cost per frame, not absolute cell count.
* Honor a higher floor for fine work; honor a lower ceiling for huge stocks where each cell would be sub-pixel anyway.

Low-priority polish; comes AFTER #1 + #2 are profiled in practice.
close_reason: Closed

title: 3D-sim audit #5: inline cell write, drop lower_at's redundant bounds check
description:
crates/wiac-core/src/sim/heightmap.rs:60-77 — `lower_at(ix, iy, z)` does an `ix >= cols || iy >= rows` check on every cell write, but `for_each_swept_cell` already clamps the AABB to [0, cols) × [0, rows) so the check is redundant.

## Fix

In `for_each_swept_cell`'s body closure, write directly: `heightmap.data[iy * cols + ix] = z.min(prev)`. Update the dirty AABB ONCE per segment (segment's clamped AABB) instead of accumulating per cell. lower_at can stay as the public safe API for external callers; the sweep loop just bypasses it.

Per-cell save: 1 branch, 1 mul (we already compute idx), 1 dirty-AABB update.
Estimated win: small (<5%); the inner loop is already tight.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-2: tessellation cache for combine_auto + region_previews + per-op driver
description:
\`cam/source_combine.rs:197-204\` — \`combine_auto\` calls \`segments_to_points(..., TESS_INTERPOLATE=6)\` for every selected object every time. \`build_region_previews\` calls \`combine_source_regions\` again with the same data the per-op driver later reuses.

## Fix

Cache tessellated boundaries on \`VcObject\` (lazy \`OnceCell<Vec<Point2>>\`) keyed off TESS_INTERPOLATE. Both region preview and offset emission reuse them. Tessellation is one of the dominant costs for big DXFs.
notes: Deferred. Caching tessellated boundaries on VcObject with OnceCell requires the type to leave Copy-bound contexts; sizable refactor for a marginal win on typical project sizes.
close_reason: Scoped TessCache deduplicates segments_to_points calls across combine_auto and the boolean modes within a single combine_source_regions invocation (commit). Wider build_region_previews / per-op driver dedup is out of scope — those go through distinct entry points with separate VcObject snapshots.

title: audit 2026-05-2: history mirror + 'as unknown as never' transaction casts
description:
Two related cleanups around the History engine:

1. **historyVersion mirror** — project.svelte.ts:357 mirrors history.ts:_version as a $state field just so reactive readers fire. The mirror is the only reason the \`void this.historyVersion\` ceremony exists in undoLabel / canUndo / etc. If \`History\` were a \`.svelte.ts\` module with a \`$state\` version field directly, the mirror + the ceremony disappear.
2. **\`as unknown as never\` casts** — \`EntityCanvas2D.svelte:816\`, \`OperationsList.svelte:140\`, \`AddTextDialog.svelte:261\` all call \`project.history.cancelTransaction(project as unknown as never)\`. The History.cancelTransaction signature is \`state: unknown\`, so the cast is overdefensive but ugly. Either change call sites to pass \`project.target()\` (and expose target() as pub or via a wrapper) or add \`project.cancelTransaction()\` that handles the typing once.

Both add maintenance friction without buying anything.
notes: Partial: the 'as unknown as never' casts at EntityCanvas2D.svelte:843 / OperationsList.svelte:140 / AddTextDialog.svelte:261 are gone — replaced by a public project.cancelTransaction() façade that hides the CommandTarget cast (commit 5beebad). The historyVersion mirror is still in place; moving History to .svelte.ts would drop it but requires test-runner changes — deferred.
close_reason: Two-part issue. Part A ('as unknown as never' casts) was already fixed via the project.cancelTransaction façade in 5beebad. Part B (historyVersion mirror removal) is blocked by vitest's no-svelte-plugin config — attempting the .svelte.ts conversion immediately fails History tests with 'state is not defined'. Documented the blocker inline so the next attempt either upgrades the test runner first or skips re-walking the same path.

title: audit 2026-05-2: command discipline — dirty in revert, addImported bypass, empty-patch entries, missing coalesce keys
description:
Five small but adding-up undo/dirty hygiene issues in \`frontend/src/lib/state/commands.ts\` + project state:

1. **dirty in revert** — every \`revert()\` sets \`t.dirty = true\` (commands.ts:69, 122, etc.). Undoing back to a clean state still marks the project dirty. Fix: snapshot the prior dirty flag in apply, restore in revert.
2. **addImported bypasses commands** — \`project.svelte.ts:576\` directly assigns \`this.imported = {...}\` (no undo) while \`appendImportedSegments\` correctly routes through a command. Wrap addImported in \`replaceImportedCommand\` so drag-and-drop merges are undoable.
3. **empty-patch entries** — \`updateOperationCommand\`/\`updateFixtureCommand\`/\`updateTextLayerCommand\` create undo entries even when the patch is empty. \`setStockCommand\` already short-circuits; do the same in the others.
4. **missing coalesce keys** — \`setMachineCommand\` and \`replaceToolsCommand\` have no coalesce_key; rapid edits in MachineDialog / ToolLibrary each create a separate undo entry.
5. **lowerSimResolutionCommand** mutates t.settings without saveSettings() — the change is lost on reload. commands.ts:666-682.

title: audit 2026-05-2: schema.rs hand-maintained registry — silent codegen gaps on new types
description:
\`schema.rs:69-130\` — \`components_schemas()\` is a hand-maintained list of 40+ \`insert::<T>(..)\` calls. Adding a new pub JsonSchema-deriving type to \`project.rs\` (e.g. the recent \`TextLayer\` / \`ImportedTextEntity\` / \`work_area\` additions) and forgetting to register it here silently breaks frontend codegen — no compile error.

L132-147 — \`insert::<T>\` swallows definitions silently with \`or_insert\`; two types named the same drop one without warning.

## Fix

Add a build-time check (\`xtask schema --check\`) that asserts every JsonSchema-deriving pub type in the crate is present in the registry. Optionally turn the hand-list into a static \`SCHEMA_REGISTRY: &[(&str, fn() -> Schema)]\` so registration lives next to the type.

title: audit 2026-05-2: explicit O(n²) ptr-eq lookup in push_ramp_with_arcs_warning
description:
\`pipeline.rs:1399-1400\` — \`push_ramp_with_arcs_warning\` does
\`objects.iter().position(|o| std::ptr::eq(o, obj))\` inside
\`objects.iter().any(|obj| ...)\` — explicit O(n²) lookup that pointer-compares (fragile under Vec realloc) and silently produces a usize::MAX sentinel via \`.unwrap_or(usize::MAX)\` that's later used as an array-like index.

## Fix

The outer \`enumerate()\` gives the index directly:
\`\`\`
objects.iter().enumerate().any(|(idx, obj)| op_includes_object(op, obj, idx) && ...)
\`\`\`
Drops the unwrap_or sentinel + the O(n²).

title: Text engraving phase 4: DXF TEXT/MTEXT imported as editable TextLayers
description:
Stop baking DXF \`TEXT\` / \`MTEXT\` entities to opaque segments at import. Round-trip them as editable TextLayers instead.

## Scope

- \`crates/wiac-core/src/input/dxf_in.rs\`: when a TEXT or MTEXT entity is encountered, emit a TextEntity record (text + style + size + position + rotation + font ref) alongside the geometry segments instead of rendering inline.
- Importer output gains a \`text_entities: Vec<TextEntity>\` field.
- Frontend converts these to TextLayer records on import.
- Fallback: when no font is available (current behavior warns), still emit a TextEntity record but flag \`needsFont: true\` so the user can pick one in the UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- A DXF with TEXT entities imports as both layer-list entries (geometry layers) and text-list entries (text layers).
- Editing the text content of an imported TEXT entity re-renders correctly.
- Re-import (source watcher) preserves any user edits to the text contents? Open question — likely treat as new on re-import.

## Depends on

- wiaconstructor-xnia (phase 1)
- wiaconstructor-5tfd (phase 2)
- wiaconstructor-dug4 (phase 3 — needed for users to edit imported text)

## Out of scope

- DXF EXPORT preserving TextLayers as TEXT entities (separate future work).
notes: User confirmed (post-creation): no migration needed. The 're-import preserves user edits' question becomes 'always treat re-import as new' — simpler.
close_reason: Phase 4 shipped in 5efdfee: DXF TEXT/MTEXT entities now flow through ImportOutput.text_entities (editable metadata) instead of being rendered to opaque polylines. Frontend convertImportedTextEntities() creates a TextLayer per imported entity with bundled DejaVu Sans, all under one undo step. All four phases of the text-engraving rework complete (xnia, 5tfd, dug4, nfwl).

title: WebKitGTK 4.1 SEGV on app close (shutdown atexit handlers)
description:
On Linux Tauri AppImage launches, closing the window emits a SEGV in WebKitWebProcess. Trace lands in libc \`exit()\` running atexit-registered destructors of WebKit / GLib shared libraries — no application frames, signal 11.

## What the trace shows

\`\`\`
#0  0x00007fd90ba3e784 n/a (n/a + 0x0)
#1  0x00007fd906041101 n/a (libc.so.6 + 0x41101)
#2  0x00007fd9060411de exit (libc.so.6 + 0x411de)
#3  0x00007fd906027748 n/a (libc.so.6 + 0x27748)
#4  0x00007fd906027879 __libc_start_main (libc.so.6 + 0x27879)
\`\`\`

## Why this isn't a regression from our code

- The crashing process is the WebKitWebProcess renderer, not wiac-desktop.
- The crash is during shared-library teardown after the JS context is gone, so Svelte onDestroy / three.js disposal don't get to run anyway.
- Scene3D.svelte already does correct teardown for the cases where onDestroy fires (route change, HMR, programmatic unmount).

## Workarounds for users hitting it today

- \`WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 ./wiaConstructor_*.AppImage\`
- \`WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 ./wiaConstructor_*.AppImage\`
- Ignore (process is exiting; OS reclaims resources).

## Things to investigate longer-term

- Bundle a newer libwebkit2gtk-4.1 or migrate to webkit2gtk-6.0 once Tauri's GTK runtime story stabilises.
- Try the upstream fixes shipped with Ubuntu / Debian backports for webkit2gtk.
- Move the AppImage build to a base image where the crash doesn't reproduce.
close_reason: User-confirmed: SIGKILL-on-ExitRequested fix lands the renderer via signal before its main() can return, so the libgallium atexit destructor never runs. App exits cleanly on Arch + Mesa 26.0.6.

description: LayerList.svelte:45-50 — the empty state uses an underlined link, while OperationsList's empty state uses a primary-CTA card. Visually inconsistent for adjacent panels.
design: Match LayerList's empty state to OperationsList's primary-CTA card style. Factor a shared <EmptyState> component if there isn't one yet.
close_reason: Fixed in da53fe3.

title: ToolLibraryDialog: 'Wirbeln (auto chip-thin)' German jargon needs translation
description: ToolLibraryDialog.svelte:679 — the label 'Wirbeln (auto chip-thin)' is German jargon that only readers fluent in German machining vocabulary will recognise as trochoidal milling.
design: Translate to 'Trochoidal milling (auto chip-thin)' in the English UI. Route through the i18n layer if the project has one so future locales pick the right term.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: Dialog save semantics inconsistent across Settings, Machine, Tools
description: Settings commits live (no Cancel), Machine and Tools require explicit OK/Cancel. Three near-identical dialogs follow two different rules. A user editing Tools and clicking the X icon believes they saved but loses changes.
design: Pick a single rule and apply it everywhere: either all dialogs commit live (with an Undo affordance), or all dialogs require OK to commit and warn on dirty-close. Tools/Machine/Settings should agree.
close_reason: Closed

title: OpPropertiesPanel: '(0-1)' next to XY overlap and corner-slow reads as units
description: OpPropertiesPanel.svelte:1143 and :1324 — the '(0-1)' annotation next to XY overlap and corner-slow inputs reads as a unit. Users mistake it for mm or percent rather than a fraction.
design: Use 'fraction' or '(fraction 0-1)' as the annotation, or replace the numeric input with a slider whose label reads 'X% overlap' so the meaning is unambiguous.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: OperationsList: expanded OpPropertiesPanel pushes rows below the fold
description: OperationsList.svelte:426-430 — selecting an op expands the embedded OpPropertiesPanel inline (600+ px). On typical viewports the panel pushes subsequent rows and the '+ New group' button below the fold without scrolling them into view.
design: After expansion, scrollIntoView the selected op's row (or the top of the expanded panel) with smooth behaviour so the user keeps context. Account for the panel height so the row doesn't end up clipped above the top.
close_reason: Fixed in 2b81bac.

title: ToolLibraryDialog: default step >=0 marked invalid with no inline message
description: ToolLibraryDialog.svelte:359 — default step >= 0 marks the input with .invalid but never displays an inline message. The user sees a silent red box and has to guess the rule.
design: Add an inline error message under the input describing the rule (e.g. 'Step must be > 0 mm'). Reuse the validation-message pattern from elsewhere in the form.
close_reason: Fixed in 2b81bac.

title: OpPropertiesPanel: tool-default inheritance shows reset link only for step
description: OpPropertiesPanel.svelte:336-366 vs :1276-1310 — tool-default inheritance is shown via placeholder + reset-link for the step input only. Feed and plunge overrides show a placeholder but no reset button. Inconsistent: users can revert step but not feed/plunge.
design: Add the same reset-to-tool-default link/button next to feed and plunge inputs. Factor the placeholder+reset pattern into a small component so it stays consistent for any future overridable field.
close_reason: Fixed in dd90778.

title: PostProcessorEditor: JSON import has no preview/confirmation step
description: PostProcessorEditor.svelte:102-138 — JSON import overwrites the draft with one click and no confirmation. A wrong-file import destroys in-progress edits.
design: Show a preview/diff of the imported profile before committing. Add a confirm step. Optionally remember the previous draft and offer a one-click undo.
close_reason: Fixed in dd90778.

title: PostProcessorEditor: preview pane lacks context about the synthetic toolpath
description: PostProcessorEditor.svelte:373 — the live preview pane does not say what the example represents. Users see a block of gcode and can't tell whether it's a circle, a rectangle, a contour, etc.
design: Add 1-2 lines above the preview block naming the synthetic toolpath ('Preview: 20x20mm rectangle contour at depth 3mm' or similar). Tie the label to the actual toolpath generator.
close_reason: Fixed in da53fe3.

title: cam/post-profile-preview: <tools> token substitutes single line in TS vs full listing in Rust
description: cam/post-profile-preview.ts:53 — the TS <tools> token substitutes a single line 'T<n> (<name>)' while the Rust post substitutes the full multi-line tool-library listing. Live preview misrepresents what the user will see in the actual output.
design: Feed the preview a real tools_listing string built from the active tool library, matching the Rust formatting. Either expose a helper in cam/post-profile-preview.ts that builds the same listing, or reuse the Rust output via a wasm binding.
close_reason: Fixed in da53fe3.

title: cam/tabs.ts vs wiac_core::cam::tabs: no FE/Rust round-trip cross-check
description: There is no FE/Rust cross-check test for cam/tabs.ts versus wiac_core::cam::tabs. Tiny epsilon differences between the two implementations could land tab placement on the wrong side of a vertex, with the FE preview disagreeing with the actual gcode.
design: Add a known-fixture round-trip test: pick a handful of edge-case polylines (near-vertex placements, near-zero-length segments), compute placements via the FE TS code and via the Rust crate, and assert positions match within a tight epsilon.
close_reason: Fixed in 49acc1a.

title: history: coalesced exec keeps original revert, undo loses recent ticks
description: history.ts:65-90 — history.exec coalesces consecutive commands but keeps the original revert. Undo of a coalesced run therefore reverts to before the entire run, not the most recent tick. This is correct IFF the revert target is stable across ticks, but nothing enforces that.
design: Add an assertion (or runtime check in dev) that coalesced commands share a stable revert target. Optionally, support coalescing only when the new command's revert equals the previous one.
close_reason: The audit's recommendation was 'Consider asserting the coalesced commands share a stable revert target.' Currently impossible to assert in code: the revert closure is a function reference, not data we can compare. The behavior IS documented at history.ts:78-86 ('keep the original revert so the single undo step takes the user back to before this run started'). No further action without a richer Command shape.

title: PostProcessorEditor: JSON import accepts axes without inner schema validation
description: PostProcessorEditor.svelte:125-131 — JSON import accepts parsed.axes if every key is present, without validating the inner AxisFormat shape (format string type, precision range, etc.). A malformed JSON gets accepted and may crash later in render.
design: Add a per-AxisFormat schema validation step on import: check field presence, types and reasonable ranges. Report a clear error and refuse the import on failure.
close_reason: Fixed in 2b81bac.

title: MachineDialog: profilePreset matches on name only
description: MachineDialog.svelte:59-65 — profilePreset matches presets on name only. A user that imports a JSON profile named 'LinuxCNC default' but with different templates sees 'linuxcnc' in the dropdown even though the templates diverge from the preset.
design: Match on name AND template-set equality (e.g. compare a stable hash of axis formats + templates against the preset). If different, show 'Custom' or '(modified)' instead of the preset name.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: project.svelte.ts: visibleLayers/selectedEntities saved in two places, workspace wins
description: project.svelte.ts:319-336 and :620-633 — snapshot() writes visibleLayers and selectedEntities into the .vc-project save, but workspace.per_project[path].visible_layers also stores them. On reopen the workspace path wins, so the in-project save is effectively dead state and confusing for users moving projects between workspaces.
design: Pick one source of truth. Either drop visibleLayers/selectedEntities from the project snapshot (workspace canonical) or make the project snapshot canonical and have workspace defer to it on reopen.
close_reason: Fixed in dd90778.

title: Scene3D: mega-effect reads 7 project.* fields and rebuilds everything
description: Scene3D.svelte:362-376 — a single $effect reads 7 different project.* fields and rebuilds geometry + tabs + stock + fixtures together. Toggling a fixture color rebuilds toolpath geometry that did not change.
design: Split the mega-effect into per-concern $effects: one for toolpath geometry, one for tabs, one for stock, one for fixtures. Each reads only the fields it needs.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a9cf0c: mega-effect split into four focused effects (geometry / tabs / stock / fixtures). Bonus: tessellate + tool_mesh extracted into lib/scene3d/ as pure helpers with their own unit tests.

title: OperationsList.onDrop: cross-group drag emits two non-transactional commands
description: OperationsList.onDrop — cross-group drag calls setOpGroup + reorderOperation as two separate history commands. Undo of one drag takes two Ctrl+Z.
design: Wrap the two commands in beginTransaction / commitTransaction so they coalesce into a single undo step.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: OperationsList: statusFor rebuilds Set(imported.objects) per op per render
description: OperationsList.svelte:120-161 and :367-368 — statusFor constructs a new Set from imported.objects for every op on every render. Quadratic in op count * import size for what should be a constant cost.
design: Lift the Set into a $derived at the parent (or in project.svelte.ts) so it's built once per imported.objects change and read O(1) per op.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: Scene3D: updateTabs rebuilds polyline cache per placement (O(N*M))
description: Scene3D.svelte:980-993 — updateTabs builds buildObjectPolylines(imp) once but the manual-placement loop then calls resolveTabPlacementToWorld(imp, tp), which internally rebuilds the polyline cache per placement. With many imports and many manual placements this is O(N*M).
design: Reuse the locally-built objects polyline array. Either pass the precomputed polylines into resolveTabPlacementToWorld via an overload, or hoist the cache into a value that resolveTabPlacementToWorld can accept directly.
close_reason: Fixed in 2b81bac.

title: Scene3D: lastSimKey uses gcode.length, hides same-length different-content runs
description: Scene3D.svelte:441-451 — lastSimKey uses gcode.length as a cheap stand-in for 'is this a new gen?'. Two runs with identical gcode length but different content silently deduplicate and the simulation pane stays stale.
design: Replace gcode.length with a monotonic version counter incremented on every gcode generation, or with a content hash (e.g. quick FNV/xxhash of the string). Update both producer and consumer side of the dedup check.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: EntityCanvas2D: altDown sticks when Alt released outside window
description: EntityCanvas2D.svelte:1192-1201 — Alt-tracking via <svelte:window onkeyup> only clears altDown on keyup. If the user holds Alt + tabs away and releases the key outside the window, altDown stays true until the next Alt press inside the canvas.
design: Add a window blur listener that clears altDown (and any other modifier flags). Optionally also listen to visibilitychange to handle tab switches.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: PostProcessorEditor: exportJson serializes $state proxy directly
description: PostProcessorEditor.svelte:88-100 — exportJson calls JSON.stringify(draft) directly on a Svelte 5 $state proxy. Same hazard the MachineDialog OK regression addressed; the exported JSON can be missing nested fields or carry proxy markers.
design: Wrap with the same JSON workaround used elsewhere: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify($state.snapshot(draft))) or the project's existing proxy-safe deep-clone helper. Add a small test that exports and re-imports to round-trip.
close_reason: Audit premise was wrong on rereading: PostProcessorEditor.exportJson at line 89 uses JSON.stringify(draft, null, 2). JSON.stringify is exactly the proxy workaround (it skips symbol-keyed properties and traverses via [[Get]] traps cleanly — unlike structuredClone). DataCloneError is a structuredClone-only failure mode. No fix needed.

title: MachineDialog: nested modal overlay z-index collides with PostProcessor editor
description: MachineDialog.svelte — two simultaneous <div class='overlay'> z-index:100. Clicking the outer overlay while the PostProcessor editor is open closes the MachineDialog underneath the editor, leaving the editor floating over a closed parent.
design: Either bump the inner PostProcessor editor overlay to a higher z-index and make the outer overlay non-dismissive while a child modal is open, or close the editor automatically when the parent MachineDialog closes.
close_reason: Fixed in 6230890: PostProcessorEditor was moved INSIDE MachineDialog's {#if open} block. Both modals' lifecycles are tied — closing the parent unmounts the child editor. The audit's specific concern (clicking outer overlay while child is open leaves an orphaned editor) cannot happen now. The editor's own Modal overlay is rendered later in DOM order so it stacks above MachineDialog's overlay; click-outside-editor closes the editor, not the parent.

title: OperationsList: pendingEmptyGroups referenced before let declaration
description: OperationsList.svelte:74-104 — pendingEmptyGroups is referenced inside commitNewGroup before its let declaration. Works today via hoisting but is fragile under Svelte 5's state_referenced_locally rules; a future compiler tightening can break this without warning.
design: Move the let pendingEmptyGroups = ... declaration above commitNewGroup so the reference order matches lexical order.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: OpPropertiesPanel: helix preview $effect re-tracks op as dependency in debounced .then
description: OpPropertiesPanel.svelte:118-150 — the helix preview $effect reads op?.id inside its 300ms-debounced .then callback. Because the effect runs on the same reactive pass, op gets re-tracked as a dependency every fire and the .then closure may capture a stale id by the time the debounce settles.
design: Capture opIdAtStart = op?.id outside the .then closure (before the setTimeout/debounce), then compare against the captured id inside the callback. Make sure no $state read remains inside the closure.
close_reason: Fixed in 2b81bac.

title: HPGL post: no post-profile/token-ctx impls; templates silently dropped in drag mode
description: There is no set_post_profile / set_token_ctx implementation in hpgl.rs. When the machine mode is drag, the user's typed post templates are silently dropped without any UI surface. At minimum the MachineDialog should surface a hint; ideally the templates should be honored.
design: At minimum: surface a UI hint in MachineDialog when the machine is HPGL/drag-mode that custom post templates are not honored. Preferred: implement set_post_profile / set_token_ctx for the HPGL post and apply the same token substitution rules used by the standard post.
close_reason: Fixed in dd90778.

title: pipeline: V-Carve copies rough+finish RPMs but emits only rough
description: pipeline.rs:1349 — V-Carve setup copies both rough and finish RPMs/feeds into the op state but emit_vcarve_block only honors the rough values. The finish-set rates the user configured are silently dropped.
design: Pipeline the finish-set spindle/feed values through to emit_vcarve_block (emit an S/F change before the finish pass), or drop the finish RPM/feed fields and the UI controls that feed them.
close_reason: Reconsidered: V-Carve is single-pass by design (no rough/finish split in the ratchet sweep), so the tool's finish_speed/feed/plunge fields are intentionally unused for V-Carve ops. Per-op overrides (feedRateOverride / plungeRateOverride) still apply through synthesize_op_setup. The qwt 'Refine pass' field (which would gate a future second-pass finish) is now disabled in the UI as 'not yet implemented'. Will reopen when a real V-Carve refinement pass ships and needs distinct rates.

title: cam/chaining: find_neighbor breaks on first match, ignores distance
description: cam/chaining.rs:113-136 — find_neighbor tracks 'best' via Option<(usize, f64)> but breaks on the first match within tolerance; the recorded distance is never used to keep a closer candidate. The result is either-first or accidentally-best depending on input order.
design: Pick one. (a) If first-match is the intent, drop the f64 entirely and document the policy. (b) If best-match is the intent, scan all candidates within tolerance and keep the minimum-distance one. Option (b) gives more stable chaining at sharp Y-junctions.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: pipeline: run_per_op takes &mut Vec<VcObject> but never mutates
description: pipeline.rs:run_per_op takes &mut Vec<VcObject> but never mutates it. The .clone() at the call site is therefore defensive against a non-existent contract, and the function signature actively misleads readers about ownership.
design: Rename and re-sign. Either take &Vec<VcObject> (or &[VcObject]) by shared reference and drop the call-site clone, or take by value if the call site has an owned vec to give. Update callers accordingly.
close_reason: Fixed in 6230890: synthesize_pocket_outside_objects extraction means run_per_op's objects: &mut Vec<VcObject> is now actually mutated (line 947: *objects = new_objects). The previous read-only contract has been replaced with a real mutation — the &mut signature is now load-bearing.

title: gcode: drag-knife first-corner compensation uses uninitialized last_a
description: gcode.rs:emit_path_with_corner_feed — drag-knife first-corner trail compensation runs against uninitialized last_a (defaults to 0). The first corner therefore compensates as if the previous heading was 0deg, producing a wrong lift/swivel on the very first corner of every path.
design: Either seed last_a from the first segment's heading before entering the corner loop, or skip compensation on the first corner. Add a test that exercises a first-corner-non-zero-heading path.
close_reason: Audit misread the guard. emit_path_with_dragoff uses  (gcode.rs:1965) — the first segment's compensation block is skipped entirely until last_motion has been set by the previous segment. No uninitialized 0-default path exists. Confirmed by reading lines 1957-2026: last_motion starts as None and is only consumed inside the Option-guard.

title: pipeline: source_combine_mode returns Auto for OperationSource::All
description: pipeline.rs:source_combine_mode returns Auto for OperationSource::All. Non-pocket ops therefore get legacy semantics for Layers{combine: Union} when the source is All. Document the legacy behaviour or implement the documented union semantics across all op kinds.
design: Either explicitly document that combine_mode for OperationSource::All falls through to per-op legacy behaviour, or replace the Auto branch with a per-op-kind decision so the documented Union semantics applies uniformly.
close_reason: Documented in source_combine_mode doc-comment; the Auto-for-All routing is intentional, not a placeholder. Per-op-kind handlers (Pocket containment loop, Profile per-object path, etc.) are the source of truth for 'All' semantics.

title: pipeline: OperationParams.multi_pass_refine exposed but never inspected
description: pipeline.rs:run_vcarve_op — OperationParams.multi_pass_refine is part of the public OperationParams type but the pipeline never reads it. Either wire it through to the V-Carve solver or drop the field.
design: Decide intent. If the multi-pass refinement was planned for the V-Carve solver, wire it through (extra rough passes at refined offsets before the finish pass). Otherwise remove the field from OperationParams and any FE that sets it.
close_reason: Fixed in da53fe3.

title: cam/vcarve: medial_axis_cancellable uses circumradius instead of inscribed-circle radius
description: cam/vcarve.rs:140-145 — medial_axis_cancellable uses the triangle circumradius as the inscribed-circle radius. At re-entrant corners a nearby edge sample can be closer than the three witnesses, so the radius is wrong (too large). Same problem in run_halfpipe_op, which reuses VPoint.r.
design: Compute the actual distance from the medial-axis sample to the nearest input edge (signed distance to boundary), not the circumradius of the three witness triangle. Update VPoint.r consumers accordingly.
close_reason: Closed

title: cam/offsets: ramp pass ignores arcs crossing ramp boundary
description: cam/offsets.rs emit_ramp_pass treats arcs that cross the ramp boundary as regular segments and descends instantly at the arc's start. Either document the limitation prominently or implement arc-boundary handling (subdivide the arc at the ramp transition).
design: Split arcs at the ramp boundary parameter so the descent occurs along the arc rather than at its start. Compute the arc parameter at which cumulative arc length equals the ramp length and emit two sub-arcs.
close_reason: Fixed in fd83b97.

title: pipeline: OperationSource::Objects fallback hashes whole segment list
description: pipeline.rs:796-806 — the OperationSource::Objects fallback hashes the entire segment list of the import. Adding any unrelated geometry to the file invalidates every Object-source op's cache.
design: Hash by object-id-chained segments instead of the full segment list. Walk only segments belonging to the selected objects, in object-id order, and hash that subset.
close_reason: Closed

title: gcode/arc_fit: fit_arc_run uses stale midpoint witness
description: In gcode/arc_fit.rs:114, fit_arc_run picks points[j/2] as the midpoint witness — but j/2 indexes the original full-points slice, not the middle of the current run. The witness should be derived from the run's actual start/end indices.
design: Replace points[j/2] with points[(start + j) / 2] so the midpoint witness is taken from the middle of the current arc run rather than the original slice.
close_reason: Fixed in 2b81bac.

title: gcode/arc_fit: closing tolerance ignores tolerance_mm
description: gcode/arc_fit.rs:73-78 falls back to all-Lines when the last fitted arc's end is off by even 1e-9 from points.last(). The rest of the fit uses tolerance_mm; the closing check should use the same epsilon to avoid silently degrading well-fit runs.
design: Replace the hard-coded epsilon used in the final closing check with the configured tolerance_mm (or a small multiple thereof) so the closing check matches the rest of the arc fit.
close_reason: Fixed in 2b81bac.

title: gcode: build_z_schedule drops finish-step on single-pass ops
description: In gcode.rs:1746-1753, build_z_schedule drops the finish-step pass when only one main pass is scheduled (step == total_depth). Single-pass operations with finish_step set silently lose the intended finish quality.
design: Detect the single-pass case (step >= total_depth) and still emit the finish-step pass after the main cut when finish_step is configured. Ensure depth math doesn't double the cut by treating the finish pass as a separate trailing step.
close_reason: Fixed in 9a0b66c.

title: Per-axis name / format / scale / enable in PostProfile
description: rt1.15 follow-up. v1 covers program-level templates (header/footer/toolchange/coolant) but axis-level formatting still routes through the hand-written linuxcnc/grbl posts. Estlcam's c_Coordinate supports per-axis Name (output label), Format (printf-ish '%.3f'), Scale (-1.0 for Z-up inversion), Enable, Repeat (modal). Extend PostProfile with an AxesConfig {x, y, z, i, j, f, s} of AxisFormat structs. linuxcnc.rs's coords() helper consults them when set.

title: Disconnected-tabs toast when an op's source changes
description: rt1.10 follow-up. When the user removes objects from an op's source, any tab placements whose object_id is no longer in scope become orphaned (pipeline silently drops them). Detect on edit and surface an info-toast 'N tabs disconnected from this op — clear?' with a one-click action that strips the orphans. Mirrors the n79 click-picker UX pattern.
close_reason: Inline cleanup chip in OpPropertiesPanel's Tabs fieldset (less intrusive than the originally-proposed toast — the user is already on the panel when they edit the op's source, so inline is more visible at the moment that matters). disconnectedTabCount(op) walks tabPlacements + filters by (a) imported.objects still containing the id, (b) op.sourceObjects (when set) including it. clearDisconnectedTabs(op) one-click strip via updateOperation. Renders only when count > 0; gated on Manual/Mixed mode like the other placement hints.

title: Per-tab popover: width / height override + delete
description: rt1.10 follow-up. Right-clicking on a tab marker should open a compact popover with width/height number inputs (placeholders showing the op's defaults) plus a delete button. Position-aware (flip when near the canvas edge). Esc / click-outside dismisses. Commits via updateOperation on the op's tab_placements with the user's overrides.
close_reason: EntityCanvas2D: tabPopover state + findTabAtPixel hit-test (10 px screen tolerance, walks every op's manual/mixed placements). Right-click on an existing tab opens the popover with Width / Height number inputs (placeholder = inherited op default) + a Delete tab button + close (×). Position clamped to canvas bounds on open so the popover doesn't open off-screen at edge clicks. Updates route through updateOperation (single undoable history entry). Esc + click-outside close. CSS styled inline.

title: Tab placement snap to vertex / midpoint / existing tab
description: rt1.10 follow-up. The ghost-tab projection currently snaps only to the closest point on the contour. Add three secondary snap targets: (a) within 4 px of a polyline vertex; (b) within 4 px of the midpoint of any segment; (c) within 2mm of an existing tab on the same op (lets the user stack manually). When snapped, render a small accent dot next to the ghost so the user sees the snap. Hold Alt to disable for the current gesture (CAD convention).
close_reason: cam/tabs.ts vertexAndMidpointTs helper collects vertex + segment-midpoint t parameters. projectGhostTab in EntityCanvas2D promotes the contour projection to (a) vertex within 4 px screen-space, (b) midpoint within 4 px screen-space, (c) existing tab on same op+object within 2 mm data-space — precedence by closest. Alt-held disables secondary snaps (CAD-convention escape hatch). Ghost render adds a small accent dot next to the rectangle when the snap is non-contour so the user sees which target was caught.

title: Wirbeln: corner-only trochoidal loop emission
description:
rt1.25 followup. v1 ships Wirbeln as a global cascade-step reduction (xy_step clamped to tool_radius/2 across the entire pocket). EstlCam's actual Wirbeln behavior is different from this issue's original description:

After reading Flooper.cs in the EstlCam decompile: Wirbeln is a **post-emission helical-spiral overlay** applied to every G1 cut move while a Wirbeln-tagged tool is active. NOT corner detection. NOT trochoidal loops at concave vertices.

For each cut move:
  - subdivide into stride steps of length Vorschub = T_Wirbel_Stepover / Schritte
  - at each step, displace (x, y, z) by:
      x' = x + cos(winkel * dir) * R
      y' = y + sin(winkel * dir) * R
      z' = z + cos(winkel * 3) * Osc - Osc    (small Z-wobble for chip clearance)
      winkel += 360 / Schritte
Where R = T_D * T_Width / 200, Schritte ≈ LIM(360 / (11.5 / sqrt(R)), 36, 360), Dir = +1 climb / -1 conventional, Osc is the per-tool Z-wobble amplitude. The cutter centerline traces a small circle that itself slides along the cascade ring — effective cut width D + 2R.

## Plan (Option B — EstlCam-faithful)

1. ToolEntry: add `wirbeln_extra_width_mm: Option<f64>` (EstlCam's Wirbelzusatzbreite — the spiral diameter R*2 in mm). Existing `wirbeln_stepover_mm` keeps its meaning (stride along path per revolution).
2. New module `gcode/walk/wirbeln.rs` with `apply_wirbeln(segments, radius, stepover, climb, osc) -> Vec<(x, y, z)>` that subdivides + applies the helical offset.
3. Hook in `gcode/multi_pass`: when `setup.tool.wirbeln_extra_width_mm > 0`, route each cut pass through the wirbeln overlay (no corner-feed / dragoff — the spiral motion supersedes them).
4. Drop the xy_step clamp in offset_builder.rs:230 — the overlay bounds engagement on its own.
5. Schema regen + frontend codegen + ToolLibraryDialog field for the new param.
6. Tests: golden gcode for a square cascade with R=1, stepover=2, climb (verify subdivision count, max XY excursion, full revolution phasing); R=0 path matches baseline.

The bd issue's original plan (engagement detection + corner-only trochoidal loops) is a separate feature idea — orthogonal to Wirbeln. If we want it later, file as a new issue.
close_reason: implemented Option B (EstlCam-faithful helical overlay). New module gcode/wirbeln.rs with 5 unit tests; new ToolEntry fields wirbeln_extra_width_mm + wirbeln_osc_mm; gcode emit dispatches through emit_cut_path. v1 xy_step clamp removed. PIPELINE_VERSION→23. 373 BE / 189 FE tests pass.

title: Per-kind geometry inputs + sim cross-sections for rt1.28 cutter variants
description: rt1.28 follow-up: BullNose / Compression / TSlot / FormProfile variants are now in the schema, but (a) ToolLibraryDialog doesn't yet expose the corner_radius_mm / tslot_neck_diameter_mm / tslot_neck_length_mm inputs (currently the labels show but the fields are not editable), and (b) the sim/heightmap ToolProfile collapses these to Endmill — true cross-section math is needed for sim accuracy. Plan: (1) Add per-kind sub-panels in ToolLibraryDialog (corner_radius for BullNose, neck dia + length for TSlot). (2) Add new ToolProfile variants BullNose/TSlot/FormProfile with their eval(r) functions. References: rt1.28's original concrete plan.
close_reason: Closed

title: Approach-point click picker in 2D canvas
description: rt1.26 follow-up: the backend supports OperationParams.approach_point and the OpPropertiesPanel exposes numeric XY inputs, but the click-to-pick UX in EntityCanvas2D is still missing. Add a 'pick approach point' mode toggled per-op via a button in OpPropertiesPanel, similar to the existing tab-placement mode. Click anywhere inside the pocket; the point is stored. A small '▼' marker icon renders at the chosen point in both 2D and 3D previews. References: EntityCanvas2D's existing tab-placement mode for the pattern.
close_reason: implemented per EstlCam UX shape: sticky pick mode with vertex snap (Shift = free), draggable marker for refinement, accent status bar, 3D needle. 9 new vitest cases for the snap data layer. 189 FE + 367 BE tests pass.

title: Project report view: printable summary (toolpath stats, est time, tools, materials)
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.9 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's dlg_Report.cs renders a printable project report: total cut time, per-tool time breakdown, distance traveled, tool list used, estimated material removed, sim warnings count. Standard CAM tool feature; used for shop documentation and customer quotes.

title: Preset bundle: save/load complete setup (machine + tools + operations) as a shareable file
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.9 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's dlg_Preset.cs exports/imports a bundle: machine config + tool library + a representative op set. Users (especially shops) share these between PCs and team members. Without it, every new install re-types every machine param + tool entry.

wiac today: machine + tools persist in the project file; opening a new project starts from app defaults (the seeded 3mm endmill etc). No way to bring a curated tool library to a fresh project.

Concrete plan:

1. New file format .wiac-preset.json containing { machine: MachineConfig, tools: ToolEntry[], settings: AppSettings? }. Optionally pinned operations as a 'starter ops' list.

2. crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs: small Preset struct with serde round-trip.

3. frontend ToolLibraryDialog: 'Export tools' button that saves the current tool library as .wiac-preset.json (Tauri save dialog).

4. frontend FileUpload or a new 'Apply preset' menu entry: loads a .wiac-preset.json and overlays its tools + machine onto the current project (with confirm-overwrite prompt).

5. Edge cases: tool id collisions — when an imported preset has a tool with id=1 and the current project also has id=1, prompt 'replace / skip / renumber'.

6. Optional starter bundle: ship a sample preset in samples/ with a few common tool entries so new users have a starting point.

Estimated: 3-5 days.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/dlg_Preset.cs.
- Related: rt1.6 default_step + dr5 default_xy_overlap which raise the value of a curated tool library.
close_reason: Superseded by h0tx (Toolset + machine save/load files). The h0tx work shipped .wiac-toolset.json and .wiac-machine.json as separate side-files, which cover the core 'share my shop setup across machines' use case. Save Project on an empty (no-geometry) project handles the residual 'everything in one file' scenario. The 'starter ops' template idea in the original eld plan was never well-defined — operations are normally tied to specific imported objects rather than standalone templates, so the abstraction doesn't fit. If we later want a one-file machine+tools bundle, that's a thin wrapper on top of h0tx (just {machine, tools} in one envelope) — file a new issue when there's user demand.

title: Snap to endpoint / midpoint / intersection / grid in the 2D canvas
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.8 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's Transform.cs Snaps[] array tracks the 8 nearest snap candidates (endpoints, midpoints, intersections) while the user moves the cursor in transform mode. Standard CAD snap behavior; without it, placing a tab exactly on a corner or aligning a transformed shape to an existing feature requires manual coordinate entry.

wiac's EntityCanvas2D has only free pan / zoom — no snap. Tabs are placed approximately and tab-rounding handles imprecision.

Concrete plan:

1. Frontend EntityCanvas2D: add a snap subsystem. On mouse-move, walk visible objects in a small radius around the cursor, find the closest snap candidate of each type, render a small icon (square for endpoint, triangle for midpoint, X for intersection). Click snaps to that point.

2. Snap types: endpoint (segment start/end), midpoint, intersection (where two segments cross), grid (project.settings.snap_grid_mm — new field). Each toggleable.

3. Performance: 1k segments → walk only the visible-via-camera-frustum subset. Estlcam pre-computes a spatial index; wiac can do similar (a simple bucket grid keyed by floor(x / cell)).

4. Frontend SettingsDialog: 'Snap' section with checkboxes per type + snap-grid number input.

5. Integration with the planned transform mode (rt1.x): snaps drive the pivot / handle drag.

6. Integration with tab placement (rt1.10): snaps make tab-on-corner pixel-perfect.

7. Tests: vitest covering the snap query function on synthetic geometry.

Estimated: 1-2 weeks. The intersection-snap query is the hardest piece; everything else is straightforward.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Transform.cs Snaps array.
close_reason: OSnap engine with 5 kinds (endpoint/midpoint/intersection/center/grid). 13 vitest cases. n79 picker now snaps to all kinds. Per-kind glyphs on canvas. Settings UI + tab integration filed as P4 follow-ups (li0m, ffhp).

title: UI transforms on selection: rotate, mirror, scale, translate (backend exists, no UI)
description:
REVISED scope (2026-05-19 user discussion): transforms apply only at the FILE level, not per-object — purely a layout convenience to place a drawing on stock for material efficiency.

## Model

`project.fileTransform` — single non-destructive transform attached to the current import:
```ts
interface FileTransform {
  translate: { x: number; y: number };  // mm, world coords
  rotateDeg: number;                    // around original bbox center
  scale: number;                        // uniform, around original bbox center
  mirrorX: boolean;                     // across horizontal axis through bbox center
  mirrorY: boolean;                     // across vertical axis through bbox center
}
```

Order of application (single pivot = ORIGINAL file bbox center):
1. uniform scale around pivot
2. mirror X / Y around pivot
3. rotate around pivot
4. world-space translate (dx, dy)

Bulge handling matches `cam.rs`: scale/rotate/translate leave bulge alone; each mirror negates bulge. Two mirrors = no change (180° rotation), which is correct.

## Storage / persistence

- Lives in project JSON (under `fileTransform` next to imported).
- Undo / redo via the existing command pattern (new `SetFileTransformCmd`).
- Reset = drop back to identity.

## Application

- Pure TS `applyFileTransform(imp: ImportResponse, t: FileTransform): ImportResponse` returning a fresh ImportResponse with transformed `segments` + `bbox`. Object ids, layer names, object_meta, warnings unchanged.
- Derived `project.transformedImport` lights up; consumers (2D canvas, 3D scene, OSnap precompute, footprint, build-project payload, sim) read it instead of `project.imported`.
- Identity transform short-circuits to original.

## UI

LayerList header gets a 'File transform' foldout above the layer rows. Inputs:
- Translate X / Y (mm)
- Rotation (degrees)
- Scale (uniform multiplier)
- Mirror X / Mirror Y checkboxes
- Reset button (drops to identity)

## Out of scope (v1)

- Multi-file imports / per-file transforms (each becomes its own `fileTransform` when that lands).
- Layer-level transforms (explicitly rejected — don't rip apart someone's layers).
- Click-pivot rotate / interactive bbox handles (numeric inputs only for v1).
- Object-level transforms.

## References
- Backend primitives: crates/wiac-core/src/cam.rs:226–286.
- Replicated in TS for now; pipeline receives already-transformed segments.
close_reason: v1 shipped: file-level FileTransform (translate/rotate/scale/mirror around bbox center), LayerList foldout UI, declarative non-destructive application via project.transformedImport derived; canvas + Scene3D + footprint + Generate payload all transformed. Tests 8/8, svelte-check clean. Follow-up 43l2 filed for fileTransform-vs-stored-op-coords reconciliation.

title: Sub-op geometry caching: medial-axis / inscribed-circle / cascade-rings invariant under depth changes
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.7 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's m_Cache.cs (Get_Cache_Kontur / Set_Cache_Kontur) caches CONTOUR-LEVEL geometry (offset polylines). Same shape + same offset distance = cache hit. Reused across the rough + finish passes of one op, AND across re-runs where the depth changed but the shape didn't.

wiac's eb8.3 PipelineCache (shipped) caches whole-op output keyed by the full op + tool + machine state. When the user changes depth on a V-Carve op, the op_cache_key changes — so we re-run medial_axis even though the boundary segments haven't changed. medial_axis on a 1000-segment outline is slow (~2-4 sec).

Concrete plan:

1. cam/vcarve.rs / cam/inscribed.rs / cam/offsets.rs: identify the expensive sub-op computations that only depend on GEOMETRY (boundary segments + tool radius), not on depth / feed / leads / tabs:
   - medial_axis(region) — V-Carve, helix inscribed-circle.
   - pocket_cascade_with_islands(boundary, islands, step) — Cascade / Spiral rings.
   - inscribed_circle(region, tool_radius) — auto helix radius.
   - parallel_offset_inward / outward — Profile single-pass offset.

2. Add a separate cam/geometry_cache.rs that keys by (segments_hash + tool_radius + algorithm_id). Returns the computed output. Bounded LRU like pipeline_cache.

3. Call sites: wrap each expensive call with . The cache is process-global like pipeline_cache.

4. PIPELINE_VERSION-bump discipline: same as eb8.3. When any algorithm changes, bump.

5. Tests:
   - same_segments_cached_across_depth_change
   - tool_radius_changes_misses_cache
   - boundary_changes_misses_cache

Estimated: 3-5 days. Tedious but mechanical — find each expensive call, wrap it.

Expected speedup: V-Carve regenerate with a depth tweak should drop from ~3s to ~50ms. Cascade regenerate with feed tweak: similar.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/m_Cache.cs (12 LOC, very simple contour-level cache).
- wiac eb8.3 pipeline_cache.rs is the model — extend the pattern one level deeper.
close_reason: Closed

title: Configurable decimal separator + line numbering (N<n>) for European controllers
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.6 against Estlcam.

Two small post-processor knobs that European / vintage controllers need:

1. **Decimal separator**: Estlcam c_PP.Decimal_Point lets the user pick '.' or ','. Mandatory for some Siemens / Heidenhain controllers configured in EU locale. wiac always emits '.'.

2. **N-line numbering**: Estlcam c_PP.N_Start sets a starting line number (typically N10 or N100) and each emitted line gets numbered. Required by some FANUC / vintage controllers; useful for operator reference even on modern ones. wiac doesn't number lines.

These are standalone tweaks that don't require the full rt1.15 template engine.

Concrete plan:

1. cam/setup.rs MachineConfig: add decimal_separator: char (default '.') and line_number_start: Option<u32> (None = no numbering).

2. gcode emitters: a tiny formatter helper that produces decimal-respecting numbers. A line-prefix helper that emits 'N<n> ' before each command and increments by 10. Plumb both through the existing PostProcessor trait.

3. Frontend MachineDialog: 'Decimal separator' radio (. / ,). 'Line numbering' checkbox + start input.

4. Tests:
   - comma_decimal_emits_correctly
   - line_numbering_increments_by_10
   - off_state_unchanged

Estimated: 2 days. Stand-alone; doesn't block on rt1.15.

- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_PP.cs Decimal_Point (line 92), N_Start (line 80).

PostState carries the resolved values; new PostProcessor::configure(separator, line_start) trait method threads them in at program_begin. fmt_num + line_number_prefix + configure_post_state helpers in gcode.rs. LinuxCNC + GRBL posts override configure (HPGL ignores). LinuxCNC's write/fmt/coords moved to Post-methods so they consult state. pipeline_cache hashes the new fields; PIPELINE_VERSION bumped to 5. title: Plot-mode Z (laser / plasma / 3D-printer): pen-up at safe Z, pen-down for cut moves
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.6 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's c_PP.Z_Up_Dn boolean turns Z into a binary pen-up / pen-down toggle (plot-mode). Laser, plasma, drag-knife, pen plotter, 3D-printer extrusion — all use this pattern: no continuous Z values, only 'beam on at safe Z' / 'beam off at retract Z'. Cleaner gcode for those controllers, plus avoids confusing them with f64 Z values they ignore.

wiac's current emitters always write the literal Z value. For pure 2D operations on laser/plasma this is harmless but verbose; for drag-knife it's required to be a constant.

Concrete plan:

1. cam/setup.rs MachineConfig: add plot_mode_z: bool (default false). When true, emit only two Z values — z_down (the cutting plane, taken from op.depth at the cut start) and z_up (fast_move_z).

2. gcode emitters (linuxcnc / grbl / hpgl + future template): when plot_mode_z is true, the linear / move_to helpers clamp Z to {z_down, z_up} based on which side of mid-stock it is. Cut moves write z_down once at the start of the cut; retracts write z_up.

3. Frontend MachineDialog: 'Plot-mode Z' checkbox under the existing mode picker. Tooltip: 'Use binary pen-up / pen-down Z values instead of continuous Z. Cleaner gcode for laser / plasma / 3D-printer / pen-plotter controllers.'

4. Tests:
   - plot_mode_emits_only_two_z_values
   - plot_mode_off_emits_continuous_z

Estimated: 2-3 days. Standalone feature; doesn't require the full rt1.15 template engine.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_PP.cs Z_Up_Dn (lines 70, 232, 384).
close_reason: MachineConfig.plot_mode_z bool added. multi_pass short-circuits when active — emits ONE pass at the op's cut depth (clamped to <= 0), bypasses helix / ramp / finish_step / through_depth / depth_list / tabs descent stages. Z values in resulting gcode are limited to {fast_move_z, cut_depth, 0}; intermediate descent values do not leak. pipeline_cache hashes the new field; PIPELINE_VERSION bumped to 10. MachineDialog: 'Plot-mode Z' checkbox under the toolchange row. 1 new test (plot_mode_emits_only_two_z_values exercises depth=-3 + step=-1 + plot_mode_z=true and verifies Z=-1/Z=-2 never appear); 299 wiac-core + 94 FE tests pass.

title: Raster bitmap → ball-nose milling toolpath (heightmap engraving for milling, not just laser)
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.4.

Estlcam's c_Halftoner.cs + c_BMP.cs + Modul_Paint_Halftoner.cs cover TWO use cases:
1. Laser raster engraving: grayscale → laser-power modulation along raster lines. Covered by rt1.12.
2. Ball-nose milling of grayscale: grayscale → Z-depth modulation per pixel. The cutter is a ball-nose endmill; the tool descends to a depth proportional to pixel brightness, producing a relief from the bitmap. Famous wood-relief-from-photo / lithophane workflows.

wiac has rt1.12 (laser raster) but NOT the milling-relief variant.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs: new OperationKind variant RasterMill { z_min_mm: f64, z_max_mm: f64, stepover_mm: f64, scanlines: ScanlineDirection } — where ScanlineDirection is { XAxis, YAxis, Diagonal }.

2. Reuse the rt1.12 raster source pipeline (image file → pixel grid → wiac unit space). Extend its output to include a Z map for each pixel (vs rt1.12's power map).

3. New emitter cam/raster_mill.rs: walk scanlines, at each pixel emit G1 X Y Z<computed>. Z = lerp(z_min, z_max, brightness). For ball-nose tools, the simulator's existing ball-nose ToolProfile produces a smooth relief.

4. Tool requirement: ToolKind::BallNose. Tool-kind mismatch warning otherwise.

5. Frontend: same Pic-select dialog as rt1.12 with an additional 'output type' radio (Laser power vs Mill Z depth).

6. Tests: pipeline integration covering a 4x4 test image producing the expected Z grid.

Estimated: 1-2 weeks. Shares the picture-loader plumbing with rt1.12.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_Halftoner.cs, _PIC.cs, c_BMP.cs.
- Companion to rt1.12 (laser raster engraving).
notes: MERGED into the f60x relief-surfacing plan (2026-05-27): the bitmap→mill-Z (relief) variant of rt1.32 is delivered by f60x-A (SurfaceField + grayscale→Z) + f60x-C (ReliefMill op) + f60x-D (image picker UI). Do NOT build separately. rt1.12 still covers the laser-power raster variant. Close rt1.32 when f60x-D lands.

title: Per-tool Z_Shift: origin offset for multi-tool setups without ATC tool-length probing
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.3 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's _TP::Z_Shift stores a per-tool Z origin offset. Use case: hobby machines without auto tool-length probing (the vast majority). User chucks a 4 mm endmill, sets Z=0 at the top of stock. Swaps to a 6 mm endmill, the new tool's tip is at a different absolute Z; the user manually re-zeros OR offsets via a software Z_Shift.

wiac has no per-tool Z offset. Toolchange (M6) is emitted but assumes the controller re-probes.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs ToolEntry: add z_shift_mm: Option<f64> (default None / 0). Positive = tool sticks out further; negative = shorter.

2. gcode.rs emit_toolchange: after the M6 toolchange, emit a G92 Z<shift> (or G10 L20 P<offset> if the post supports work-offset registers) for the new tool. On finish_op, restore the previous offset.

3. Per-post: linuxcnc has G92 / G10 L20; grbl has G10 L20 (limited); hpgl irrelevant. Verify support, gracefully skip on grbl if work-offset is unsupported.

4. Frontend ToolLibraryDialog: 'Z origin offset' number input per tool with mm chip. Tooltip: 'For machines without automatic tool-length probing. After toolchange, your software adds this to the Z origin so the new tool's tip stays at stock-top zero.'

5. Tests:
   - toolchange_emits_z_shift_when_set
   - toolchange_skips_z_shift_when_zero_or_unset
   - round-trip

Estimated: 2-3 days. Risk: post-specific quirks in how work offsets are emitted.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_TP.cs Z_Shift enum value.
close_reason: ToolEntry.z_shift_mm added; new PostProcessor::tool_z_shift trait method emits 'G92 Z<shift>' bracketed by an explanatory comment. LinuxCNC + GRBL impls override (HPGL ignores). pipeline.rs emits the shift at program_begin for the first enabled op's tool AND right after every emitted M6 toolchange (currently the dual-tool rt1.33 finish-tool path). pipeline_cache hashes z_shift_mm; PIPELINE_VERSION bumped to 6. ToolEntry literals across pipeline / pipeline_cache / sim/holder / sim/holder_check / sim/heightmap / wasm-sim updated. ToolLibraryDialog gets a 'Z shift (mm)' input in the Pass-overrides panel. 3 new tests (first-tool shift after program_begin, finish-tool shift after M6, no-shift no-G92); 291 wiac-core + 94 FE tests pass.

title: Laser-tool specifics: pierce_time + lead_in distance
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.3 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's Tool_Wrapper.cs exposes laser-specific tool fields:
- T_Pierce_Time (line 234): per-tool seconds of dwell BEFORE the cut starts so the beam burns through stock. Critical for lasers on thick acrylic / wood — without it the first millimeter is gouged.
- T_Lead_In (line 229): per-tool distance the head travels before reaching the cut path. Reduces edge entry burn.

wiac's ToolEntry has no laser-specific fields. LaserBeam tool kind is recognized but treated like an endmill in the emit path.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs ToolEntry: add laser_pierce_sec: Option<f64> and laser_lead_in_mm: Option<f64>. None = laser off (or 0). Only populated when kind == LaserBeam.

2. gcode emitters: when the active op's tool is LaserBeam, prepend a G4 P<pierce_sec> dwell before the first cut's M3/M4 spindle-on (laser-on); insert a lead-in run of laser_lead_in_mm along the entry tangent at low/zero power before the actual cut path.

3. Per-post extension: linuxcnc supports G4 P; grbl supports G4 P / S<power>; hpgl is moot for laser. Verify each post's emit_dwell helper.

4. Frontend ToolLibraryDialog: laser tool kind reveals two new inputs with sec/mm unit chips. Tooltip explains the physics.

5. Tests:
   - laser_op_emits_pierce_dwell_before_cut
   - laser_op_emits_lead_in_run
   - non_laser_tool_ignores_pierce_field

Estimated: 2-3 days.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs lines 229 (T_Lead_In), 234 (T_Pierce_Time).

ToolConfig carries resolved pierce_sec (0 for non-laser tools). synthesize_op_setup + header_setup_for populate pierce_sec from ToolEntry when kind==LaserBeam. New PostProcessor::dwell(sec) trait method emits G4 P<sec>; LinuxCNC + GRBL implement it. emit_offset emits the pierce dwell between rapid-to-entry and the Z=0 plunge for all three lead-in shapes (Straight/Arc/None). pipeline_cache hashes both new fields; PIPELINE_VERSION bumped to 8. ToolLibraryDialog: laser-only sub-panel (gated on kind === 'laser_beam') with Pierce time + Lead-in inputs. 2 new tests (laser pierce emits G4 P0.3 in gcode; non-laser tools ignore the field); 296 wiac-core + 94 FE tests pass.

title: Extend ToolKind with missing cutter geometries: Radius, Profil, Compression, T-slot
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.3 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's _TT enum has tool types wiac doesn't model:
- Radius — flat endmill with rounded corners (common: 0.5 / 1 / 2 mm corner R). Differs from Endmill: the corner produces a fillet on the floor edge; from BallNose: shaft is cylindrical, not spherical.
- Profil — form / profile cutter with custom shape (bullnose, ogee, cove, dovetail). Standard in woodworking; cuts a fixed profile along the tool path.
- Obenunten — compression / up-down spiral endmill. Cuts down on top, up on bottom — clean edges on both faces of sheet material. CNC router staple.
- T_Slot — keyway / undercut cutter. Goes in vertically, then offsets laterally to cut a wider slot below the surface.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs ToolKind: add variants Radius, FormProfile, Compression, TSlot. Frontend types ditto.

2. project.rs ToolEntry: add geometry fields used by these kinds:
   - corner_radius_mm: Option<f64>  // Radius
   - profile_shape: Option<FormProfileShape>  // FormProfile (enum: BullNose, Cove, Ogee, Dovetail{angle_deg}, Custom{points: Vec<(f64,f64)>})
   - tslot_neck_diameter: Option<f64>  // T_Slot
   - tslot_neck_length: Option<f64>  // T_Slot
   All Option<...>, skip-when-default in serde, default None for backwards compat.

3. sim/heightmap.rs ToolProfile: extend with new variants that match each kind's cross-section. Sim sweep already takes profile.eval(r) for the cone shape; extend for the new types.

4. Frontend ToolLibraryDialog: per-kind sub-sections in the tool editor. Hide non-relevant fields when the kind doesn't use them.

5. Compression endmill flags: when used with a Profile op, the gcode emitter could split the depth schedule so the first half of Z descends climb (cutting down) and the second half climb-up (cutting up) — but this is op-strategy work, file as a follow-up issue if anyone asks. For v1: just expose the tool-kind variant so the user can label their tools accurately; the cutting algorithm treats them as endmills.

6. Tests: tool round-trip per kind; sim sweep emits the right cross-section for each.

Estimated: 1 week. Most time spent on the sim-cross-section math.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_TT.cs (enum), Tool_Wrapper.cs T_Typ usage.
close_reason: ToolKind extended with BullNose / Compression / TSlot / FormProfile (snake_case wire labels). ToolEntry gets corner_radius_mm + tslot_neck_diameter_mm + tslot_neck_length_mm geometry fields. sim/heightmap.rs ToolProfile::from_tool maps the new kinds to Endmill profile for v1 (true cross-section math is a rt1.28.x follow-up). pipeline_cache.hash_tool hashes the new fields + the extended kind discriminator; PIPELINE_VERSION bumped to 11. FE: op_types.ts + WireToolKind extended; ToolLibraryDialog kindLabels gets 'Bull-nose (radius)' / 'Compression' / 'T-slot' / 'Form / profile'. 1 new test (extended_tool_kinds_serde_round_trip covers all 4 new variants + round-trips the geometry fields); 300 wiac-core + 94 FE tests pass. Per-kind geometry inputs (corner_radius / tslot neck) in ToolLibraryDialog + sim cross-section math for the new variants deferred to a follow-up.

title: User-pickable pocket approach point (Anfahrpunkt) — let user choose where the cutter enters
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.2 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's _I.cs lines 97-99: each pocket carries Has_Anfahrpunkt + Anfahrpunkt — an optional user-clicked approach point. When set, the cutter enters the pocket at that XY position instead of the algorithm-chosen default. Used for two cases:
1. Aesthetic: the approach-mark on a visible surface goes in a hidden corner the user picked.
2. Geometric: complex pockets with multiple safe entry points; the user knows which is best.

wiac's pocket emitters auto-pick the entry point (helix inscribed-circle center for Helix plunge, the boundary's first vertex for Direct/Ramp). No way to override.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs OperationParams: add approach_point: Option<(f64, f64)>. None = auto. Some((x, y)) = enter here.

2. cam/offsets.rs + cam/vcarve.rs entry-point selection: when approach_point is Some, validate it lies inside the inset boundary; if yes, use it. If outside the safe envelope, emit an approach_point_unreachable warning and fall back to auto.

3. Frontend EntityCanvas2D: extend the tab-placement mode pattern. New 'pick approach point' mode toggled per-op via OpPropertiesPanel. Click anywhere inside the pocket; the point is stored. A small marker icon ('▼' downward arrow) renders at the chosen point in both 2D and 3D.

4. OpPropertiesPanel: 'Approach point' row with 'click to set' / 'clear' buttons + XY readout when set.

5. Tests:
   - approach_point_inside_boundary_is_used
   - approach_point_outside_boundary_emits_warning
   - round-trip serde

title: Wirbeln: automatic chip-thinning (trochoidal stepover) when engagement exceeds tool capacity
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.2 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's Tool_Wrapper.T_Wirbeln (line 50) is a per-TOOL boolean (different from a per-OP strategy). When enabled, ANY pocket strategy (Parallel / Linear / Peel) automatically switches to a trochoidal stepover when the cutter's radial engagement exceeds tool_radius / 2 — the classic 'chip thinning' rule for cutter life on hard materials.

wiac has rt1.4 PocketStrategy::Trochoidal as an EXPLICIT op choice. Wirbeln is the AUTOMATIC sibling: user keeps Cascade/Spiral, the cutter chooses chip-thin loops only at the high-engagement spots (typically inside corners of pockets where the tool gets fully embedded).

The two are complementary — rt1.4 covers the 'I want trochoidal everywhere'; Wirbeln covers 'I want fast straight cuts in most places and trochoidal only when the tool would overload'.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs ToolEntry: add wirbeln: bool (default false) and wirbel_stepover_mm: Option<f64> (None = trochoidal_stepover_default_for_tool_diameter()).

2. cam/offsets.rs pocket emitters: at each xy_step the cascade / spiral algorithms emit, compute the radial engagement from the previous-ring offset. When engagement > tool_radius / 2, replace the next stepover with a trochoidal loop sequence (reuse rt1.4 trochoidal::loop_at_point). Otherwise continue normal stepover.

3. Tests:
   - wirbeln::tests::engages_only_in_high_load_zones
   - wirbeln::tests::no_loops_when_tool_doesnt_overload
   - integration: a rectangular pocket with Wirbeln off vs on: off produces straight rings, on produces loops only at the corners.

4. Frontend ToolLibraryDialog: add Wirbeln checkbox per tool. When checked, expose wirbel_stepover_mm number input. Tooltip on Wirbeln: 'Automatic chip-thinning: drops in trochoidal loops only when the cutter would otherwise overload. Use for hard materials with normal Cascade/Spiral pockets — no need to switch to Trochoidal strategy.'

Estimated: 1 week. The engagement-detection math is the new piece; loop emission is reused from rt1.4.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/Tool_Wrapper.cs lines 33 (call site), 50 (definition), 68-98 (related stepover calculation).

Note: this is the SIMPLE 'global stepover reduction' implementation. The corner-only / engagement-detection version (drop trochoidal loops ONLY at high-engagement zones) is a follow-up — see issue body. pipeline_cache hashes both new fields; PIPELINE_VERSION 13. ToolLibraryDialog gets a Wirbeln subsection with Enable checkbox + Step (mm) input. 2 new tests (offset count grows when Wirbeln is on; serde round-trip); 308 wiac-core + 94 FE tests pass.

title: Operation grouping (Gruppierungen) — hierarchical organization for complex projects
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.1 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's Gruppierungen.cs lets users assign operations to named groups (GRP_Create, GRP_Select, GRP_Aufheben). Groups can be expanded/collapsed in the ops tree, selected as a unit ('disable all ops in this group'), and reordered together. Heavy CAM projects (~30 ops on a single workpiece) become unmanageable without it.

wiac's OperationsList is a flat list. Today users prefix names like 'Pocket: lid', 'Pocket: tabs' to fake grouping.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs Operation: add group: Option<String> (group name, None = ungrouped).

2. frontend/src/lib/state/project.svelte.ts: derive groupedOperations  that splits operations into groups for the OperationsList view. Drag-and-drop reorder logic stays per-group.

3. OperationsList.svelte:
   - Show ops grouped by op.group. Ungrouped ops live in an implicit 'Other' bucket at the bottom.
   - Each group header: name, expand/collapse arrow, batch-disable toggle, drag handle for reordering the whole group.
   - 'New group' action in the + picker.
   - Drag-and-drop between groups: dropping op A onto group G's body sets op A.group = G.name.
   - Right-click on group header: rename, delete (releases members to ungrouped), duplicate group (copies every op via the existing duplicate command).

4. Persistence: groups are part of the project save (no schema bump needed since group is Option<String> with serde default).

title: Stufenfase: drilled-hole countersink as a drill-cycle extension
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.1 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's Prog_KTD_Stufenfase (_I.cs line 1815) chains a hole + a chamfer pass on the SAME hole. After drilling, the bit (or a swap to a chamfer tool) walks a partial-depth circular pass at the hole rim to create a countersink. Common workflow for woodworking and fastener prep.

wiac has Drill cycles (Simple/Peck/ChipBreak) and a planned Chamfer op (above). What's missing: the chained workflow where one operation handles both the bore AND the rim chamfer.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs DrillCycle: add chamfer_after: Option<ChamferAfter> where ChamferAfter is { width_mm: f64, tool_id_override: Option<u32> }. None means just drill; Some means follow the drill plunge with a small chamfer pass using the same tool (V-bit drill or chamfer drill) or the override tool.

2. gcode.rs emit_drill_block: when chamfer_after is set, after the drill cycle's retract, emit a tool change (if override) + a circular pass at the rim at the computed z.

3. Frontend: OpPropertiesPanel drill cycle picker gains a 'Chamfer after' checkbox + width input + optional tool override picker.

4. Tests:
   - pipeline::tests::drill_with_chamfer_emits_two_phases
   - pipeline::tests::drill_with_tool_override_emits_M6
   - round-trip serde

Estimated: 2-3 days.

- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs lines 1815-1900.
