title: Halfpipe pocket strategy (slot machining with constant tool engagement)
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.1 against Estlcam.

Estlcam ships _PK::Halfpipe (in _PK.cs) and Prog_Halfpipe (in _I.cs line 216). It's a pocket strategy specifically for SLOT-shaped pockets where the goal is a uniform-bottom 'half-pipe' channel rather than a flat-floored pocket. The toolpath walks the slot centerline at a constant z that traces the desired pipe-bottom curve (often a circular arc seen from the side).

wiac has PocketStrategy::Cascade/Zigzag/Spiral/Trochoidal. No Halfpipe equivalent.

Use cases: drainage channels, decorative grooves, water-stop seals, mortise prep for round-bottomed inlays.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs PocketStrategy: add variant Halfpipe { profile: HalfpipeProfile } where HalfpipeProfile is { CircularArc { radius_mm: f64 }, VBottom { included_angle_deg: f64 } }.

2. cam/offsets.rs PocketEmit: add PocketEmit::Halfpipe { profile }.

3. cam/halfpipe.rs (new file): given the pocket boundary, build the medial axis (reuse cam/vcarve.rs::medial_axis from rt1.1). The slot centerline IS the medial axis. Walk it; at each point emit Z = -profile.depth_at(distance_from_boundary). For CircularArc profile, z = -(radius - sqrt(radius^2 - r^2)) where r = inscribed-circle distance at that medial-axis point. For VBottom profile, z = -r / tan(half_apex). Cap to the user's depth setting.

4. pipeline.rs: route the new PocketStrategy::Halfpipe arm. Similar shape to Spiral/Trochoidal handlers.

5. Tests:
   - halfpipe::tests::circular_profile_uniform_slot_depth
   - halfpipe::tests::v_profile_matches_vcarve_at_constant_width
   - pipeline integration: a narrow slot + Halfpipe with 5mm radius → toolpath dips to -5mm at the centerline.

6. Frontend: OpPropertiesPanel pocket strategy dropdown gains 'Halfpipe'. Sub-fields: profile picker + radius / angle for the chosen profile. Tool kind requirement: ball-nose (CircularArc) or V-bit (VBottom).

Estimated: 1 week. Reuses medial-axis infrastructure from rt1.1.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_PK.cs (enum), /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs lines 207-1080 (Prog_Halfpipe and helpers).

Manual Serialize/Deserialize/JsonSchema updated to handle the new variant + nested profile. cam/halfpipe.rs ships depth_at + polyline_to_z helpers (CircularArc: z = -(R - sqrt(R²-r²)) capped at -R; VBottom: z = -r / tan(half_angle)). New run_halfpipe_op pipeline driver reuses cam/vcarve medial-axis + vcarve_emit ratchet + emit_vcarve_block — same XYZ-polyline path V-Carve uses. Tool-kind mismatch + radius-mismatch + depth-limited warnings. pipeline_cache.hash_pocket_strategy hashes the new variant; PIPELINE_VERSION bumped to 12. title: Audit: Post-processor framework & G-code emission
description:
## What

2. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_Gcode.cs`** — the generic emitter. Methods of interest: `G0X` (542), `Parse_Tool_Str` (307) — token substitution, `Object_Start` (125), `Prog_Start` (223), `Prog_End` (251), `Write_Code_Line` (105), `Format_Gcode_Number` (70).

title: Audit: Geometry input formats
description:
## What

Audit Estlcam's **geometry input** surface: every file format it imports, every entity type it understands within each format, font handling, raster import, QR / lathe / dowel generators. Produce the `## Geometry input formats` section of the parity doc.

## Decompile sources to read

2. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_Spline.cs`** — spline tessellation.
3. **SVG import** — search for `SVG` in class names and methods. There may be a dedicated parser or SVG may go through DXF conversion. `dlg_SVG_Unit.cs` exists; what does it do? Catalog SVG entity coverage.
4. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_STL.cs`**, **`c_STL_BMP.cs`** — STL import (3D silhouette vs. heightmap). Document the modes.
5. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/m_Font_Import.cs`** — Estlcam's custom font format (`.dat`) plus TTF/OTF import. Look at supported font types.
6. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_QR.cs`** — QR code generator (already filed as `wiaconstructor-rt1.13`).
7. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_Rotationskörper.cs`** — lathe geometry (out of scope for wiac but document as ❌).
8. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_Dowel.cs`**, **`DWLS.cs`**, **`dlg_Dowel.cs`** — dowel placement helper. Decide scope.
9. **`/tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/c_Halftoner.cs`** — photo / grayscale → engraving (raster). Partially filed as `wiaconstructor-rt1.12` for laser; what about milling-on-photo (variable-depth ball-nose) like Estlcam supports? File as separate gap if relevant.

- Existing planned: `wiaconstructor-7f3` (STL importer), `wiaconstructor-rt1.13` (QR), `wiaconstructor-rt1.12` (raster engraving), `wiaconstructor-n4y` (license-clean single-line TTF bundle).

title: UI: 2D canvas keyboard-shortcut help affordance (no '?' button or cheatsheet)
description:
EntityCanvas2D supports several mouse/keyboard interactions (drag to pan, scroll to zoom, click to select, Shift+click to multi-select, right-click to deselect, etc) but the UI gives no hint they exist. A new user pokes around blindly.

Fix: add a small floating '?' button in the corner of the 2D canvas that opens a small overlay listing the shortcuts:

  - Click: select object (under cursor)
  - Shift+Click: add to selection
  - Ctrl+Click (or Cmd+Click): remove from selection
  - Drag: pan
  - Scroll: zoom
  - Right-click: deselect / context menu (after issue rt1.x context menu lands)
  - T: Add Text (existing shortcut)
  - Esc: cancel tab placement mode

Same overlay can list 3D shortcuts (orbit, pan, zoom). Bind to '?' or F1 to open. Close on Escape or click outside.

~hour.

title: UI: 'Set sources from selection' button hides when disabled — surface as ghost button with explanation
description:
OpPropertiesPanel ~252-261's 'Set from current selection' button is only visible when project.selectedObjects.size > 0. When 0, it's hidden (or disabled without a tooltip), so a user who hasn't yet picked objects in the canvas can't discover the workflow.

Fix:
- Always render the button.
- When disabled (no selection), add tooltip 'Select one or more objects in the 2D canvas first', dim the button (opacity: 0.5).
- When enabled, show its current count: 'Set sources from 3 selected'.

Same pattern applies to any other 'requires-selection' affordance. Audit OperationsList's source-mode picker for similar issues.

~30 min.

title: UI: 'Sim: not run' baseline chip in GenerateBar before first Generate
description:
GenerateBar's sim-warning chip only renders when project.simDiagnostics is populated — which only happens after the first Generate. Before that, there's nothing in the GenerateBar suggesting that sim verification is a feature at all.

A new user clicks Generate, sees gcode, downloads, runs it on their machine, and discovers fixture/holder collisions the hard way.

Fix: when project.simDiagnostics is null AND project.generated is null, render a muted chip 'Sim: not run yet — Generate first' (greyed background, italic). Once the user runs Generate, the diagnostic chip replaces it.

Also nice: add a tooltip explaining what sim verification catches (rapid-thru-stock, fixture collisions, holder/wall collisions).

~30 min.
close_reason: GenerateBar now renders a muted 'Sim: not run yet — Generate first' chip when project.simDiagnostics is null AND project.generated is null. .sim-chip.idle styling: var(--bg-elevated) bg, var(--text-muted) italic text, var(--border) outline. Tooltip via title explains what sim verification catches. Once simDiagnostics arrives the existing clean/warning/critical chips take over. Commit 8095eac.

title: UI: accessibility — icon-only buttons missing aria-label; color-only state indicators
description:
Several icon-only buttons + sim-warning chips rely on shape/color alone with no a11y affordance:

- OperationsList delete button (✕) — has no aria-label, screen readers announce 'button'.
- OperationsList drag handle (⋮⋮) — same.
- OpPropertiesPanel 'Set from current selection' icon button — same when icon-only.
- StockPanel fixture add buttons — labels are emoji-like glyphs.
- GenerateBar sim chip: critical = red, warning = yellow, clean = green. Color-only signal; colorblind users can't distinguish red/green clean vs critical.

Fix:
1. Add aria-label to every icon-only <button>. Example: aria-label='Delete operation {op.name}'.
2. Sim-chip: add a redundant icon prefix per severity ('⚠' for warning, '⛔' for critical, '✓' for clean) so the shape carries information independent of color.

Mostly mechanical, ~3-4 hours for full audit + fixes. Verify with axe-core or similar a11y scanner.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI: GenerateBar time-estimate hover is plain text in a title attr, not a popover
description:
GenerateBar ~260-268 renders the time-estimate breakdown via the title attribute on the ⏱ chip:
`title="Total: HH:MM:SS\nCut: M:SS\nRapid: M:SS\nPlunge: ...\nToolchange: ...\nSpindle: ..."`

This:
- Renders as the OS's native tooltip — single-line truncated on small windows.
- Doesn't format well (each line literal '\n' becomes a soft wrap or gets dropped).
- Has a long hover delay (browser-default).
- Is invisible on touch devices.

Fix: replace with a small popover <div class='time-breakdown'> that opens on hover (CSS :hover) or click, anchored under the chip. Each row is a flex {label, value} pair with the value right-aligned. Use the existing card styling (var(--bg-panel), 1px border, 4px radius).

20 LOC of Svelte + 30 LOC of CSS. ~hour.
close_reason: Time-estimate chip now uses a CSS :hover/focus-within popover instead of a title attr — content is a small 2-col table (Total / Cut / Rapid / Plunge / Retract / Arc / Tool change / Spindle warm-up) styled per spec (var(--bg-panel), border outline, box-shadow, 0.74rem). Chip wrapper is tabindex=0 so keyboard users can reveal the breakdown via focus. Commit 8095eac.

title: UI: no loading spinner during import — FileUpload silent on slow DXF loads
description:
FileUpload's loadFromPath / openFileNative / loadProjectFile set project.loading = true but no UI feedback appears in the canvas area during the import. A 10 MB DXF with 100k segments takes 5-10 seconds and the user sees nothing happen.

Fix: add a translucent overlay over the EntityCanvas2D + Scene3D panes whenever project.loading is true. Center a spinner + the current activity text ('Parsing DXF…' / 'Loading project…'). When project.loading flips back to false, fade out 100ms.

Implementation:
- Add a <LoadingOverlay /> component (50 LOC).
- Mount it inside the canvas layout (App.svelte).
- Subscribes to project.loading and project.loadingMessage (new optional state).
- FileUpload sets project.loadingMessage = 'Parsing DXF…' before await import_path, clears after.

Same overlay can be reused by Generate (rs8.1 already shipped GenerateProgress for the gcode-generation case; this issue covers the import case).

title: UI: hard-coded English in *_HELP records — CUT_DIR_HELP, PLUNGE_HELP, TAB_TYPE_HELP, COMBINE_HELP
description:
OpPropertiesPanel ~19-47 defines four help-text records as inline TS constants with English strings — they don't go through the i18n system (svelte-i18n + en.json / de.json):

- CUT_DIR_HELP (conventional/climb explanations)
- PLUNGE_HELP (direct/ramp/helix)
- TAB_TYPE_HELP (rectangle/ramp)
- COMBINE_HELP (auto/union/difference/intersection/xor/none)

German users still see English tooltips here. The op-kind help (issue rt1.x KIND_HELP/PICKER_HELP) has the same shape — fix together.

Fix:
1. Add entries to en.json + de.json under op.help.cut_direction.conventional / etc.
2. Replace const records with  getters that call $_('op.help.cut_direction.' + value).
3. de.json gets professional translations later — file a translation follow-up. For now, the en.json move alone removes the hard-coded English; de can fall back to en automatically via svelte-i18n's missing-key behavior.

~half-day.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI: empty-state hints — LayerList/OperationsList/OpPropertiesPanel give weak guidance
description: Three empty states are too terse and miss the chance to guide a new user: 1. **LayerList**: 'No file loaded' with no hint to open one. New user sees the panel and is stuck. Fix: change to 'No file loaded. Open a DXF or SVG…' that triggers FileUpload's open dialog (or focuses the FileUpload area). 2. **OperationsList empty state**: 'No operations. Click + to add one.' is OK but the '+' button is small; users miss it on small screens. Fix: when the list is empty, render a centered placeholder card with a big '+ Add operation' button as a primary call to action. 3. **OpPropertiesPanel embedded mode**: when embedded=true and no op is selected, the panel renders NOTHING because the 'Select an operation…' message is gated on !embedded. Users see a blank space and can't tell why. Fix: drop the embedded gate so the placeholder shows in both modes; style differently for embedded (smaller, centered). Each fix is ~10 LOC. Bundle.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI: persistence gaps — post processor / last-used op picker / dialog scroll
description:
Workspace state (eb8.6) persists camera, panels, recent projects — but several obvious 'I want this remembered' settings are not:

1. **Post processor choice**. GenerateBar.svelte ~50: `let post = 'linuxcnc'` is a local $state, reset on every mount. User switches to GRBL, generates, closes the app, reopens → post is back to LinuxCNC. Fix: save `workspace.update({ lastPostProcessor: post })` on change; restore on mount.

2. **Last-used Add Operation picker entry**. OperationsList opens the picker fresh every time. Users tend to add the same kind repeatedly (5 Profile ops in a row, then switch to Pocket). Fix: track last-picked kind in workspace; show it at the top of the picker or pre-highlight it.

3. **ToolLibraryDialog expanded-holder Set**. Holder panel expansion state is local — closes when the dialog closes. Frequent CAM users routinely tweak the same tool's holder. Fix: persist expanded tool IDs in workspace.

4. **Scroll position in ToolLibraryDialog**. With 10+ tools, scrolling to the bottom one and re-opening dumps the user back at the top. (Overlaps with the modal-management issue but worth noting separately.)

Each is ~30 LOC. Bundle into one PR.
close_reason: Post processor selection is now persisted in workspace state. Added last_post_processor: string (default 'linuxcnc') to WorkspaceState + parser + DEFAULT_WORKSPACE. New WorkspaceStore.setLastPostProcessor(post) method (notify + scheduleSave; no-op when unchanged). GenerateBar.svelte initializes `post` from workspace.get().last_post_processor and uses a $effect to write back on change. Round-trip test added in workspace.test.ts. 90 tests pass (was 89). Commit 8095eac.

title: UI: theming gaps — hard-coded hex colors instead of CSS vars (sim chips, playback markers, shadows)
description:
Several components bypass the theme system with hard-coded hex / rgba colors that don't adapt to light/dark mode and don't follow the established CSS-variable convention:

- GenerateBar.svelte ~409-423: .sim-chip.clean / .warning / .critical use rgba(95, 208, 110, 0.18) and #5fd06e / #f0c020 / #e54848 inline.
- PlaybackBar.svelte ~193-201: .marker.critical = #e54848, .marker.warning = #f0c020 hard-coded.
- ToolLibraryDialog / MachineDialog modal: box-shadow: 0 10px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4) is the same regardless of theme.
- Scene3D.svelte: a few cssColor() fallbacks (0xff5555, 0xffd23a, 0x5fd06e) — those are intentional defaults when CSS var is missing, OK.

Fix: define new CSS variables in the theme file ( or wherever the existing --accent / --bg-panel etc. live):
  --sim-clean, --sim-warn, --sim-critical (paired bg + text)
  --shadow-modal (different rgba for light vs dark)

Then replace the hard-coded values in the three components. Verify dark mode + light mode + high-contrast (if any) look right.

Severity: low aesthetic; matters for users on light theme and for future palette changes.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI: number inputs missing unit labels (mm, RPM, mm/min, deg, mm/s²)
description:
Number inputs throughout the UI omit their units, forcing users to infer from context or the Machine dialog:

- OpPropertiesPanel: depth / start_depth / step / finish_step / through_depth — all mm, none labeled inline.
- ToolLibraryDialog: speed (RPM), feed (mm/min), plunge (mm/min), diameter (mm), tip_diameter (mm), tip_angle_deg (deg), flute_length_mm (mm), shank_diameter_mm (mm), default_step (mm). Only some carry inline labels.
- MachineDialog: accel X/Y/Z (mm/s²), jerk X/Y/Z (mm/s³), toolchange_s (s), rapid_speed (mm/min), arc_fit_tolerance_mm (mm) — most have label text in the parent <label> but no inline unit chip.
- OpPropertiesPanel sliders (Trochoidal engagement_angle_deg 5-90, loop_radius_factor 0.3-1.0) show the current value but not min/max bounds.

Fix: a tiny .unit-chip span next to every number input, font-size: 0.7rem, color: var(--text-muted), reading the appropriate suffix. Add min/max flanking labels for sliders. ~half-day mechanical pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Orphan-op recovery after source reload (eb8.4 follow-up)
description: After auto re-importing a source DXF/SVG (eb8.4), ops whose sourceObjects reference ids no longer present in the new geometry currently just emit a console.warn. Wire up a proper inline warning chip on each affected op row in OperationsList, and offer a 'Re-pick from selection' shortcut. Also consider: mtime-based detection at startup so the user gets a 'these files changed while you were away — reload?' prompt for projects where the source was rewritten between sessions.
close_reason: Inline Re-pick button on orphan-source rows. orphansFor(op) helper computes missing object ids + layer names against the current import. With objects selected, click replaces op.sourceObjects in one tap; without selection, button disabled with explanatory tooltip. svelte-check 0/0/0.

title: Bundled example projects (examples/ tree)
description:
## What

Bundle a small, opinionated set of example projects that the docs reference and that users can open as starting points. Each example pairs an `.vc-project.json` with its source DXF/SVG/PNG; nothing binary or hand-edited.

## Where

`examples/` at the repo root. Each example in its own subdirectory with a `README.md` describing what it demonstrates.

## Examples to include (v1)

| Name | What it demonstrates | Files |
|---|---|---|
| `starter-plate` | First-cut walkthrough from getting-started.md | `plate.dxf`, `starter-plate.vc-project.json`, `README.md` (3 lines) |
| `bracket` | Pocket + profile + tabs + drill, single-sided | `bracket.dxf`, two `.vc-project.json` (plywood + aluminum trochoidal) |
| `vcarve-sign` | V-carve text + frame demo | `sign.dxf` (or generated from text), `.vc-project.json` |
| `inlay-pair` | Inlay (Both side) example | source DXF, `pocket.vc-project.json`, `plug.vc-project.json` |
| `laser-coaster` | Vector + raster combination | `coaster.svg`, `photo.png`, `.vc-project.json` |
| `qr-asset-tag` | QR + small text combo | `.vc-project.json` (QR generated from sample data) |
| `two-sided-block` | Front + back pockets demonstrating flip | `block.dxf`, `.vc-project.json` |

Drop any example whose underlying feature isn't merged yet; ship the ones that are. Add more as features land.

## Constraints

- Source DXF / SVG / PNG must be **license-clean**. CC0 or wiac-team-authored only. Bundled fonts already cover this; for DXFs, draw them in QCAD/LibreCAD/Inkscape and dedicate to public domain.
- `.vc-project.json` files committed pretty-printed (so `git diff` is meaningful when the schema evolves).
- Each example's README:
  - One-paragraph description.
  - Required tools.
  - "Open `<file>` in wiac" instruction.
  - "Generates G-code in: ~3 minutes on default machine" estimate.
  - Photo of the resulting cut where applicable.

## Schema migration

When the `Project` schema changes, all examples must be re-saved through wiac to bump to the new format. Add a CI check that loads every example and re-saves it, asserting no errors and a stable bytewise output (modulo the version field). This catches schema breaks early.

## File-size discipline

- DXFs: < 50 KB each. Strip metadata, prefer simple shapes.
- PNG: keep raster engraving demo image < 200 KB.
- Total `examples/` tree under 1 MB. Measure in CI.

## Tests

- CI: `cargo test --test examples_load` — a test that loads every example through the same pipeline as the CLI and asserts non-empty output.
- CI: file-size check.
- Manual: cut at least one example per cut-feature on real material; photo goes in the example's README.

## Time budget

- Authoring + DXF drawing: ~0.5-1 day per example.
- CI integration: 1-2 days.
- Photos / cuts: parallelizable across the persona-guide work.

## Dependencies

- Each example loosely depends on the feature it demonstrates being merged. File the example bundle as a single child but track per-example readiness in this issue's notes — close only when all v1 examples are present.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `examples/` directory with at least 5 examples present (the simplest ones gated on rt1.1 / rt1.4 / rt1.7 etc. as those merge).
- [ ] CI test loads every example without error.
- [ ] CI file-size check passes (< 1 MB total).
- [ ] Each example has a README with the required fields.
- [ ] At least 3 have photos of real cuts.
- [ ] Each persona guide (Children 2 / 3 / 4) references at least one example.
acceptance_criteria: examples/ has ≥5 examples (gated on respective rt1 children merging); CI loads each without error; CI file-size check (<1MB total); each has README; ≥3 have real-cut photos; persona guides reference at least one example each.
close_reason: Won't do — examples tree would need constant maintenance as features change. Re-file when scope stabilises.

title: Contributor guide + architecture overview
description:
## What

A docs entry for engineers who want to contribute. Covers the architecture (where the code is, why it's structured that way), the build/test workflow, and a "your first PR" walkthrough that produces a real one. Today we have `BUILDING.md` (build setup) and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (basic policy); this child fills the gap between those two: the *map* of the codebase.

## Where

- New file `docs/architecture.md` for the map.
- Update existing `CONTRIBUTING.md` to link out to `architecture.md` and `docs/getting-started-as-dev.md` (also new).

## Outline

### `docs/architecture.md`

```
1. The 30-second pitch (what's where)
   crates/wiac-core   — Rust library: pure CAM math, no I/O concerns
     ├── input/      — DXF / SVG / NURBS / text / hatch parsers
     ├── cam/        — chaining, offsets, pocketing strategies, V-carve, …
     ├── gcode/      — emit pipeline + per-dialect emitters
     ├── sim/        — heightmap, sweep, target diff
     └── pipeline.rs — top-level orchestrator: ops × geometry → toolpaths
   crates/wiac-cli     — headless CLI binary (file in → G-code out)
   crates/wiac-server  — axum HTTP server (web mode)
   crates/wiac-tauri   — desktop shell binary
   crates/wiac-wasm    — browser cdylib (in-process WASM mode)
   frontend/          — Svelte 5 + Vite + Three.js UI
   schema/            — JSON Schemas auto-generated from Rust types
2. Data flow at a glance (ASCII diagram)
   user → frontend → WiacClient (Tauri/HTTP/WASM) → wiac-core::pipeline
                                                     ↓
                                         operations × VcObjects
                                                     ↓
                                              gcode → frontend → user
3. The schema-driven UI
   - ToolEntry / Operation / Project structs derive `JsonSchema`.
   - The frontend reads the schema and renders the setup tree dynamically.
   - To add a field: add it to the Rust struct; UI follows for free.
4. Conventions
   - Module docs (`//!` at top of file) describe purpose; no `mod.rs` files.
   - Public functions get doc comments; internals only when non-obvious.
   - Tests live in the same file under `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
   - One feature per PR; small PRs are easier to review.
5. Performance notes
   - cavalier_contours for offsets: pre-tessellation kept; bulge-aware.
   - Heightmap stored packed; bit twiddling described in sim/heightmap.rs.
   - Pipeline cache (eb8.3) keyed on stable hashes; never derive `Hash`.
6. The dependency story
   - dxf-rs / usvg / ttf-parser → input
   - cavalier_contours / clipper2-rust → CAM math
   - voronator / bvh / image → sim, V-carve, raster
   - tokio + axum → server
   - tauri 2 → desktop
   - wasm-bindgen → browser
   See Cargo.toml workspace dependencies.
```

### `docs/getting-started-as-dev.md`

```
1. Prerequisites: Rust 1.78+, Node 20+, system libs (link BUILDING.md).
2. Clone, build, test:
   git clone …
   cargo test --workspace
   cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev
3. Make your first PR
   - Pick an issue from `bd ready` (link bd docs).
   - Run `bd update <id> --claim`.
   - Branch: `git checkout -b <id>-<slug>`.
   - Make changes; `cargo test` + `npm run check` clean before push.
   - Open the PR; reference the bd id in the description.
   - Run `bd close <id>` after merge.
4. Where to ask
   - GitHub Discussions for design questions.
   - GitHub Issues for bugs (label `bug`).
   - bd for active work tracking.
5. Coding-agent friendly note
   - The repo includes `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` for AI coding agents;
     human contributors can ignore those files.
```

## Update to `CONTRIBUTING.md`

- Add a "Map" section linking to `docs/architecture.md`.
- Add a "First PR" section linking to `docs/getting-started-as-dev.md`.
- Keep the existing license / sign-off / behavior policy intact.

## Validation

- Pull a developer who hasn't seen wiac through "first PR" on a tagged `good-first-issue`. Time it. Note confusion points.
- Cross-link check: every public crate / module mentioned in `architecture.md` is real.

## Time budget

- Writing both docs: 2-3 days.
- Validation: 0.5-1 day.

## Dependencies

- None hard. Independent of feature work.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` exists and follows the outline.
- [ ] `docs/getting-started-as-dev.md` exists and follows the outline.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` updated with links.
- [ ] One first-time-contributor walkthrough completed and notes appended.
- [ ] All cross-links resolve.
acceptance_criteria: docs/architecture.md + docs/getting-started-as-dev.md exist; CONTRIBUTING.md updated with links; one first-time-contributor walkthrough + notes appended; all cross-links resolve.
close_reason: Won't do — onboarding/persona docs would need constant maintenance as features land. The README + in-app tooltips cover the basics; deeper docs return when scope stabilises and a real user asks.

title: Migration guide: from Estlcam
description:
## What

A reference document for users coming from Estlcam who want to know "where's that feature in wiac". Maps Estlcam's UI labels and concepts to wiaconstructor's equivalents, calls out what's intentionally different, and flags what's not yet implemented.

## Where

`docs/migrate-from-estlcam.md`. Linked from getting-started's "Next steps" and from the wiaconcam epic (`wiaconstructor-rt1`) acceptance.

## Outline

```
1. Why the rewrite
   - Cross-platform: wiac runs on Linux and macOS, Estlcam doesn't.
   - Wayland-native (Estlcam is Win32-only).
   - Open source (GPL-3 — see CONTRIBUTING).
   - No CNC controller side: wiac emits standard G-code; you bring your own
     controller (LinuxCNC, GRBL, FluidNC, Mach3, Fanuc — see PP framework rt1.15).
   - State of feature parity (link to a status table maintained per-feature).
2. What Estlcam users will recognize quickly
   - Tool library with diameter / RPM / feed / plunge / cooling.
   - Operation list per project.
   - 2D entity canvas, 3D toolpath preview, simulation.
   - V-carve with tip-angle-driven Z mapping (rt1.1).
   - Pocketing strategies: cascade / spiral / zigzag / linear-angled (rt1.9) /
     trochoidal (rt1.4).
   - Tabs, leads, helix entry.
   - DXF / SVG import.
3. Concept-to-concept map (table)
```

A table of equivalents:

| Estlcam term | wiac equivalent | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Räumen / Pocket | OperationKind::Pocket | Strategies map: Peel→Spiral, Linear_X→Zigzag@0°, Konturfolgend→Cascade |
| Carve | OperationKind::VCarve (rt1.1) | Same medial-axis approach; auto carve-width cap |
| Carve Inside | Add Text style "Carve Inside" (rt1.5) | One-click flow |
| Carve Outside | Add Text style "Carve Outside" (rt1.5) | Frame auto-generated |
| Pocket Inside | Add Text style "Pocket Inside" (rt1.5) | — |
| Pocket Outside | Add Text style "Pocket Outside" (rt1.3, rt1.5) | — |
| Engraving | OperationKind::Engrave / Add Text style "Engraving" | Single-line fonts auto-detected |
| Inlay (dlg_Inlay) | OperationKind::Inlay (rt1.7) | Pocket+plug pair with clearance |
| Anbindungen / tabs | Project.tabs + per-op TabsConfig (rt1.10) | Manual interactive placement supported |
| Helix entry | PlungeStrategy::Helix (rt1.2 for auto-radius) | Auto-fits to inscribed circle |
| Räumzustellung | OperationParams.xy_overlap (eventually per-tool default) | Stored as 1−overlap fraction |
| Zustellung (Z step) | OperationParams.step / ToolEntry.default_step (rt1.6) | Inheritable from tool |
| Gleichlauf / climb | CutDirection::Climb (with separate finish_cut_direction) | Stiffer separation than Estlcam |
| Schlichten / finishing pass | finish_cut_direction + finish_step | — |
| 2-side flip | OperationKind side: Front/Back (rt1.11) | Two G-code files |
| QR generator (c_QR) | OperationKind via Add QR dialog (rt1.13) | — |
| Photo engraving | Raster engraving (rt1.12) | Floyd-Steinberg / Bayer / Threshold curves |
| Custom postprocessor | PostProcessor framework (rt1.15) | Per-axis format strings, tokens, replacements |

```
4. What's intentionally different
   - No CNC controller: wiac doesn't talk to your machine. Use a sender
     (cncjs / FluidTerm / LinuxCNC's GUI / Mach3) to run the G-code.
   - No 3D STL → toolpath: out of scope (wiaconstructor-7f3 is exploratory).
   - No ATC / tool-length-sensor: wiac assumes a single tool change happens
     between op groups.
   - License: GPL-3.0-or-later, not closed-source.
   - No license activation / online check.
5. What's not yet implemented
   - Live status table linked to the rt1 / rs8 / eb8 epics.
   - Mark each as: ✅ in main / 🟡 PR open / ⏳ planned / ❌ won't do.
   - Examples of ❌: ATC, license activation, 3D STL roughing.
6. Migrating projects
   - wiac doesn't import .e13 files.
   - Workflow: re-import the source DXF in wiac, recreate ops by referencing
     this doc's term map.
   - Bundled "Estlcam→wiac" example project shows the same DXF with both the
     Estlcam screenshot and the wiac equivalent op list (Child 7).
```

## Tone

- Factual, not adversarial. Estlcam is a fine tool; wiac differs in scope (CAM-only) and platform (open / cross-platform).
- Don't make promises about timelines.
- Forward-link aggressively to the matching rt1 / rs8 / eb8 issue for in-flight features.

## Validation

- Two passes: one by an Estlcam user (find one in the maker community); one by a wiac developer who *hasn't* used Estlcam, to make sure the migration concepts make sense without prior Estlcam knowledge.

## Time budget

- Writing first draft: 2-3 days. The table is the bulk.
- Two validation passes + iteration: 2-3 days.
- Status table maintenance going forward: ~1 hour per epic close.

## Dependencies

- **Soft**: most of the rt1 children. The doc describes target state; lacking-feature rows show as ⏳ planned with the issue id. As children close, flip to ✅.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `docs/migrate-from-estlcam.md` exists and follows the outline.
- [ ] Term map table is complete with at least 25 entries.
- [ ] Linked from getting-started, README, and from `wiaconstructor-rt1` epic.
- [ ] At least one Estlcam-user reviewer pass.
- [ ] Links to in-flight issues for ⏳-marked rows.
acceptance_criteria: docs/migrate-from-estlcam.md follows outline; term-map table ≥25 entries; linked from getting-started, README, and rt1 epic; ≥1 Estlcam-user reviewer pass; ⏳-rows link to in-flight issues.
close_reason: Won't do — onboarding/persona docs would need constant maintenance as features land. The README + in-app tooltips cover the basics; deeper docs return when scope stabilises and a real user asks.

title: Persona guide: laser (raster + vector + text)
description:
## What

A guide for the "I have a laser cutter / engraver" workflow. Anchors the LaserBeam tool kind, raster engraving (rt1.12), and laser-suitable text styles to a concrete walkthrough.

## Where

`docs/persona-laser.md`. Linked from getting-started and from rt1.12 acceptance criteria.

## Outline

```
1. What you'll make
   - A small wooden coaster with a vector logo + raster photo.
   - Photo of finished result.
2. Hardware notes
   - Diode laser (5W / 10W / 20W) typical hobby setup.
   - CO₂ laser (40W+) sees the same wiac, different power tuning.
   - Laser as Z=binary tool: explain the M3/M5 + S sequence.
   - Air assist + smoke extraction reminders (with safety boilerplate).
3. Workflow A: vector cutting
   - Import a closed contour SVG.
   - Add a Profile op with the LaserBeam tool.
   - Set "depth" via passes count (laser doesn't have a Z; passes = repeat-cut).
   - Generate.
4. Workflow B: raster engraving a photo (rt1.12)
   - Add Raster Engrave from the toolbar.
   - Pick a JPEG; set physical size 50×50 mm; resolution 254 DPI.
   - Power curve: start with Threshold @ 128. Show the live preview.
   - Cycle through Linear / Threshold / Dithered / Bayer; explain the choice
     for photos vs. line art.
   - Set scan direction; explain bidirectional vs. unidirectional with
     dithered output (alignment warning).
   - Generate. Explain that S values modulate per-segment.
5. Workflow C: text engraving (vector single-line)
   - Add Text (rt1.5) with style "Engraving"; pick a single-line / Hershey font.
   - Note the auto-detection warning for filled-outline fonts.
6. Tuning power and feed
   - Suggested starting feed/power table per material (basswood, plywood, MDF, leather, anodized aluminum).
   - "Calibrate" advice: cut a 5-step power scale, pick the best.
7. Common pitfalls
   - "Engraving is lighter than expected" → check power curve, reduce feed, add overscan.
   - "Edges show alignment artifacts" → bidirectional + dither don't mix; use Bayer or unidirectional.
   - "Long burn times" → drop DPI; the diff between 254 and 200 is invisible to most photos.
   - "Charring around dark areas" → add air assist; reduce power on the high end of the curve.
```

## Required screenshots

- The Add Raster Engrave dialog with photo loaded + curve preview.
- Side-by-side: Threshold vs. Floyd-Steinberg vs. Bayer on the same photo.
- M4 dynamic-power G-code excerpt with annotations explaining `S<n>`.
- Finished coaster.

## Validation

Cut at least one vector + one raster job following the guide. Try at least one of each power-curve type.

## Time budget

- Writing: 1-2 days.
- Cutting + photos: 1-2 days.
- Iteration: 0.5 day.

## Dependencies

- **Hard**: rt1.12 (raster engraving) merged for Workflow B.
- **Soft**: rt1.5 (Add Text) for streamlined Workflow C.
- **Hard**: at least one bundled photo + vector example (Child 7).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `docs/persona-laser.md` exists and follows the outline.
- [ ] At least 4 screenshots / photos embedded.
- [ ] All three workflows produce a real cut documented.
- [ ] Linked from getting-started and from rt1.12 / rt1.5.
- [ ] Power/feed table covers ≥4 materials.
- [ ] One stranger-test pass.
acceptance_criteria: docs/persona-laser.md follows outline; ≥4 screenshots; all 3 workflows cut and documented; power/feed table covers ≥4 materials; linked from getting-started + rt1.12/rt1.5; one stranger-test pass.
close_reason: Won't do — onboarding/persona docs would need constant maintenance as features land. The README + in-app tooltips cover the basics; deeper docs return when scope stabilises and a real user asks.

title: Persona guide: parts cutting (pocket, profile, tabs, two-sided)
description:
## What

A guide for the "I want to cut a part for an assembly" workflow. Anchors the pocketing / profile / tabs / two-sided features to a concrete part. Audience: hobby CNC users who came from an Estlcam / Fusion / Carbide-Create background.

## Where

`docs/persona-parts.md`. Linked from getting-started's "Next steps" and from rt1.4 / rt1.9 / rt1.10 / rt1.11 acceptance criteria.

## Outline

```
1. What you'll make
   - A simple bracket: 80×40 plate with two M5 mounting holes, a pocket cavity,
     and an outer profile cut. Photo of the finished part.
   - Estimated total cut time: 20 min in 6 mm aluminum, 8 min in 9 mm plywood.
2. Tools and materials
   - 6 mm endmill (square, 2-flute) for plywood.
   - 6 mm endmill (3-flute, AlTiN-coated) for aluminum.
   - 5 mm drill or center bit for the holes.
3. Workflow: profile + pocket + drill, single-sided
   - Step 1: Import the bundled `bracket.dxf` (Child 7).
   - Step 2: Identify the layers — outer profile, pocket, holes.
   - Step 3: Create a Pocket op on the inner cavity. Pick strategy:
     - Plywood: Spiral or Cascade (default settings).
     - Aluminum: Trochoidal (rt1.4) with 30° engagement.
   - Step 4: Create a Profile (outside) op on the outer contour. Add tabs (rt1.10) to keep the part attached.
   - Step 5: Create a Drill op on the holes layer with G83 peck.
   - Step 6: Order ops: pocket → drill → profile (rough → finishing).
   - Step 7: Sim → check for warnings (rs8.6).
   - Step 8: Generate.
4. Workflow B: same bracket with a back-side pocket (two-sided machining)
   - Add a back-side pocket op (rt1.11), side = Back.
   - Set up the flip axis.
   - Generate produces two G-code files. Explain the flip workflow on the bed.
5. Common pitfalls
   - "The profile cut my pocket" → ordering: pocket before profile, or use tabs.
   - "Tabs are visible after cleanup" → place tabs on a non-show edge.
   - "Aluminum is chattering" → switch to trochoidal; reduce engagement.
   - "Bit broke on plunge" → use Ramp or Helix plunge (rt1.2 / setup.rs).
6. Going deeper
   - Linear pocket angle for grain alignment (rt1.9).
   - Tool wear compensation (rt1.14) for precision joinery.
   - Fixture modeling (rs8.2) for shop holdings.
```

## Required screenshots

- Bracket DXF in 2D canvas.
- 3D preview with all three ops generated.
- Tabs interactive placement (rt1.10).

title: Error model + recovery hints
description:
## What

Replace generic stringly-typed errors with a structured error model that tells the user what went wrong, *why*, and *what to try*. Today an error like "Failed to parse DXF" surfaces a bare string in a toast. Users guess. Switching to typed errors with `cause`, `recovery_hint`, and where-applicable a "Fix it for me" action turns errors from dead-ends into normal interactions.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **CHANGE** `crates/wiac-core/src/error.rs` from a thin `Error` enum to a richer one with `kind`, `cause`, `recovery_hint`, `affected_objects`, optional `auto_fix`.
- **CHANGE** all `Result<T, String>` and `Result<T, Box<dyn Error>>` returns in `crates/wiac-core` to typed Errors. Compile errors surface every site.
- **EXTEND** the frontend with an error toast component that renders rich errors.
- **No replacements** of existing happy paths.

## Schema — `crates/wiac-core/src/error.rs`

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct Error {
    pub kind: ErrorKind,
    /// One-sentence human-readable summary. Translated; key-driven if
    /// the i18n layer (`frontend/src/lib/i18n.ts`) supports it.
    pub message: String,
    /// Originating cause if this is a wrapping error.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub cause: Option<Box<Error>>,
    /// Human-readable hint about how to recover. Often something the
    /// user can do directly: "Try saving the SVG without text", "Check
    /// that the layer name matches a project layer", etc.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")]
    pub recovery_hint: String,
    /// Object/operation IDs affected (when known). The frontend uses
    /// these to highlight the offending entity in the canvas/list.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub affected_object_ids: Vec<u32>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub affected_op_ids: Vec<u32>,
    /// When Some, the frontend can offer a "Fix it" button that applies
    /// this `AutoFix` (e.g., "convert text to outlines", "delete invalid
    /// op", "snap-merge gap"). Auto-fixes are a `Command` (Child 2);
    /// applying one goes through the undo stack.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub auto_fix: Option<AutoFix>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ErrorKind {
    /// Source file failed to parse.
    Malformed { path: String },
    /// Source loaded fine, but a fundamental check failed (e.g.
    /// open polyline where closed was needed).
    Invalid,
    /// Operation can't run with the current input (tool too big,
    /// pocket too small, V-bit assigned to a Drill op, etc.).
    OperationInfeasible,
    /// Output emitter problem (PP missing a token, format string bad).
    EmitFailed,
    /// External I/O — file write, etc.
    Io,
    /// Internal bug — please report. Always include `cause`.
    Internal,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AutoFix {
    /// Convert SVG-rendered text (which we can't pocket properly) into
    /// outline polylines. Calls into the existing SVG re-render path.
    SvgConvertTextToOutlines { source_path: String },
    /// Snap-merge two adjacent endpoints that should have been one.
    /// Used by chaining errors when the source polyline has tiny gaps.
    SnapMergeGap { object_id: u32, tolerance_mm: f64 },
    /// Reassign an operation to a compatible tool kind.
    ReassignTool { op_id: u32, suggested_tool_id: u32 },
    /// Delete an operation that's invalid and can't be salvaged.
    DeleteOp { op_id: u32 },
}
```

### Migration

Every `Result<T, String>` / `anyhow::Error` site migrates to `Result<T, Error>`. The `thiserror`-based existing one (if any — confirm in spike at `crates/wiac-core/src/error.rs`) gets reshaped or replaced.

The change is mechanical but touches the entire core. Sequence:

1. Define the new `Error` + `ErrorKind` + `AutoFix`.
2. Add a `From<anyhow::Error> for Error` shim so the migration can be incremental.
3. Walk one module at a time, replacing string-returns with typed ones, adding hints, populating affected_*_ids.
4. Eventually delete the shim.

## Frontend

### `frontend/src/lib/components/ErrorToast.svelte` (new component)

Renders a structured error:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⚠ Operation 'Profile of layer 0' can't run          │
│ The 6 mm endmill is too large for the smallest      │
│ feature (3 mm).                                     │
│                                                     │
│ Try: assign a smaller tool, or skip this op.        │
│                                                     │
│ [Fix it: Use 3 mm endmill] [Show offending object]  │
│ [Dismiss]                                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The "Fix it" button applies the `auto_fix` via the undo stack (Child 2). "Show offending object" pans the 2D camera to the first id in `affected_object_ids`.

### Error log

Persist the last 50 errors of a session (in-memory) in a side panel reachable from the status bar. Power users can review what happened during a run-of-many-ops generation. No PII; safe to log.

### Internal-error reporting (privacy-respecting)

`ErrorKind::Internal` errors get a "Report this bug" link. Click → opens a GitHub Issue template with the error JSON pre-filled (and a checkbox to include the project file, off by default). No automatic phoning home.

## Tests

- `error.rs::tests`:
  - `Error` round-trips through serde (the WASM bridge needs this).
  - Cause chain: a wrapped error preserves its inner cause.
- Migration regression: a few representative error paths are tested to surface the right `kind` + `recovery_hint`.
- Frontend (Svelte): ErrorToast renders the auto_fix button and triggers the right Command on click.
- E2E: import a known-broken DXF, observe the right error kind + hint + (if applicable) auto-fix.

## Time budget

- Schema + serde: 2 days.
- Migration sweep across `wiac-core`: 1-2 weeks. Most of the work; tedious but mechanical. Pair with code-review per module.
- Frontend toast + log: 4-5 days.
- AutoFix wiring per fix-kind: 2-3 days each, ship 2-3 in v1.

## Dependencies

- Soft pair with **Child 2 (undo/redo)**: AutoFixes go through the history stack as commands. If undo lands first, AutoFix is straightforward.
- Soft pair with **`wiaconstructor-rs8.6` (sim warnings stream)**: warnings and errors are conceptually similar but distinct (warnings are advisory; errors block). Don't merge them; share UI patterns.

## Open questions

- i18n: error messages should be translatable, but `recovery_hint` carries dynamic content (op names, dimensions). Templates with placeholders, formatted client-side via `i18n.ts`. Spike before committing the schema.
- Catastrophic errors (panic in core): catch with `std::panic::catch_unwind` at the WASM/Tauri boundary, surface as `ErrorKind::Internal` with the panic message. Don't crash the renderer.
- Audit: which errors actually need a `cause` chain? Pipeline-internal errors usually do; user-input errors usually don't.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Error` schema ships with serde + JSON Schema.
- [ ] Every `Result<T, String>` in `wiac-core` migrated to `Result<T, Error>`.
- [ ] At least 3 `AutoFix` kinds wired and tested.
- [ ] ErrorToast component shows kind + hint + auto-fix.
- [ ] Internal errors offer a bug-report link.
- [ ] E2E: a representative bad-DXF input surfaces the right structured error end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria: Error schema ships with serde+JSON Schema; every Result<T,String> in wiac-core migrated; ≥3 AutoFix kinds wired; ErrorToast renders kind+hint+auto-fix; Internal errors offer report link; E2E bad-DXF surfaces structured error.

title: Toolpath result caching by geometry hash
description:
## What

Memoize per-operation toolpath results by a content hash so unrelated edits don't redo the expensive work. Today every Generate runs the full pipeline; editing the depth on one of five ops re-runs all five. Heavy ops (V-carve medial-axis, trochoidal, raster) take seconds-to-minutes, so the wait compounds.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** the pipeline (`crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs`) with a per-op result cache keyed by `(op_hash, geometry_hash, tool_hash, machine_hash)`.
- **EXTEND** `Operation`, `ToolEntry`, etc. with hashing impls (use `seahash` or `ahash` for stable cross-platform hashing — *not* the default Rust `Hasher` since its randomization changes per process).
- **No replacements** of existing pipeline behavior. Cache miss = same work as today.

## Algorithm — `crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline_cache.rs` (new file)

```rust
pub struct PipelineCache {
    // keyed by full hash → (cached_at, result_blob_or_segments).
    entries: std::collections::HashMap<u64, CacheEntry>,
    // soft cap so we don't eat all RAM on a 1000-op project.
    capacity: usize,
}

pub struct CacheEntry {
    pub op_id: u32,
    pub computed_at: std::time::Instant,
    pub result: OperationResult,
    pub last_used_pipeline_version: u32,  // bump on schema/algorithm changes
}

pub fn op_cache_key(
    op: &Operation,
    objects_used: &[&VcObject],
    tool: &ToolEntry,
    machine: &MachineConfig,
    pipeline_version: u32,
) -> u64 {
    let mut h = seahash::SeaHasher::new();
    op.hash_stable(&mut h);
    for o in objects_used { o.hash_stable(&mut h); }
    tool.hash_stable(&mut h);
    machine.hash_stable(&mut h);
    h.write_u32(pipeline_version);
    h.finish()
}
```

### Stable hashing

Each schema struct gets a `hash_stable(&self, h: &mut impl Hasher)` impl that walks fields in a documented, never-changing order. Don't derive `Hash` automatically — derived hashing depends on field order in source, which someone will reorganize someday and silently invalidate caches without bumping the version. Manual impl + a `#[test]` that hashes a known value to a stable u64 catches accidental changes.

```rust
impl Operation {
    pub fn hash_stable(&self, h: &mut impl Hasher) {
        h.write_u32(self.id);
        h.write(self.name.as_bytes());
        h.write_u8(if self.enabled { 1 } else { 0 });
        // … kind variant tag + fields …
        // … params fields in documented order …
        // skip self.pattern? include? — INCLUDE; it changes geometry.
    }
}
```

For floats, hash bit patterns (`f64::to_bits()`) — exact equality is what we want for cache keys.

### Cache lifecycle

- Pre-pipeline: walk ops, compute keys, look up. Cache hit → reuse `result`, skip the op.
- Post-pipeline: insert new results.
- Eviction: LRU based on `computed_at`; `capacity = 200` ops by default.
- Persistence: ship in-memory only for v1. Disk persistence is harder (need to pickle `OperationResult`, hash project schema version, locate the cache directory) — defer to follow-up.
- Pipeline-version bump: any change to op semantics or output shape MUST bump `PIPELINE_VERSION` constant (`crates/wiac-core/src/lib.rs`). Junior devs should treat this like a SemVer breaking change. Document.

### Frontend integration

The frontend's `WiacClient.generateStreaming` (Child 1) returns the full pipeline result. Add a "from-cache" flag per op event: `OpCompleted { op_id, result, from_cache: bool }`. The progress bar shows "(cached)" next to ops that were skipped.

## Tests

- Cache hit/miss correctness:
  - Generate a project, hash all keys, generate again with no edits → 100% cache hits.
  - Edit one op's depth → that op is a cache miss, others hit.
  - Edit a tool used by 2 ops → both ops miss; ops on other tools hit.
  - Edit machine config → all ops miss (machine is in every key).
- Stable-hash regression: a snapshot test that hashes a fixture project to a known u64. If anyone reorders fields, this breaks loudly.
- Round-trip-and-hash: load the same project file twice, hash both, assert equal.
- Capacity: 250 ops on a 200-cap cache → 50 evicted by LRU.

## Time budget

- Stable-hash impls + test: 4-5 days. Tedious but mechanical.
- Cache machinery: 2-3 days.
- Pipeline integration: 2-3 days.
- Frontend "from-cache" flag: 1 day.

## Dependencies

- Soft: **`wiaconstructor-rt1.1`** (V-Carve) and **`wiaconstructor-rt1.4`** (Trochoidal) benefit most. The Estlcam decompile already uses content-hashed caching for the same reason (we noted this in the original analysis as a gap-with-no-version-invalidation). Our version-bump discipline avoids the bug they have.
- Hard: depends on the streaming pipeline (Child 1) for the from-cache progress reporting. Cache itself can ship without progress; just produces results faster silently.

## Open questions

- Hash stability across compiler upgrades: `seahash` is stable; document that switching algorithms (`ahash`, `xxh3`, etc.) requires a version bump too.
- Cache vs. determinism: if the algorithm has any non-determinism (random seed somewhere), the same key can produce different outputs. **Audit:** every op must be deterministic for the cache to be safe. Probably already true; verify with a "same input = same output bytes" test per op kind.
- Disk persistence: `~/.cache/wiac/<project_hash>/<op_hash>.bin`? Useful for big projects across restarts. Defer to follow-up.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `op_cache_key` produces stable u64s across runs (regression test).
- [ ] Re-Generate with no edits results in 100% cache hits.
- [ ] Edit-one-op-out-of-five results in 1 miss + 4 hits.
- [ ] PIPELINE_VERSION bump invalidates the entire cache.
- [ ] Frontend shows "(cached)" indicator on hits.
- [ ] Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline_cache.rs` module docs, with the stable-hashing discipline written down so juniors don't break it.
acceptance_criteria: op_cache_key produces stable u64s (regression test); re-Generate without edits = 100% cache hits; 1-of-5-edit = 1 miss + 4 hits; PIPELINE_VERSION bump invalidates; from-cache UI indicator; stable-hashing discipline documented.
close_reason: Closed

title: Diff vs. target STL overlay
description:
## What

After running the heightmap simulation, compare the simulated end-state against a *target* shape supplied as an STL or another mesh and visualize the delta — surplus material left ("not cut deep enough") and over-cut material removed ("cut too deep"). Catches "I designed a 5 mm pocket and programmed a 4.8 mm pocket" before it's too late.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** `crates/wiac-core/src/sim/` with a target-mesh comparison module.
- **EXTEND** `Project` with an optional target STL path + transform.
- **EXTEND** `Scene3D.svelte` with an overlay rendering mode that color-codes cells by delta.
- **No replacements.**

## Schema

```rust
// crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs

pub struct Project {
    // … existing fields …

    /// Optional target shape used by the verification overlay. The user
    /// designs in CAD, exports to STL, and points wiac at it. The sim
    /// compares the cut result against this mesh.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub target_mesh: Option<TargetMesh>,
}

pub struct TargetMesh {
    pub stl_path: String,                  // relative or absolute
    /// Translation applied to the mesh before comparison (mm).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub origin_offset: (f64, f64, f64),
    /// Rotation around Z (degrees) — most user STLs need a yaw.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub rotation_z_deg: f64,
}
```

## Algorithm — `crates/wiac-core/src/sim/target_diff.rs` (new file)

### Step 1: Slice the target STL into a heightmap

Loaded via the `stl_io` crate (BSD-3, simple, well-tested). For each (x, y) cell of the simulation heightmap, ray-cast straight down through the mesh and record the topmost intersection's Z. Result: a `Heightmap` with the same grid as the cutting sim.

```rust
pub fn target_heightmap_from_stl(
    stl_path: &Path,
    target_offset: (f64, f64, f64),
    target_rotation_z_deg: f64,
    template: &Heightmap,        // grid template; same origin/cell/size
) -> Result<Heightmap, Error>
```

Performance: a 100k-triangle STL on a 500×500-cell grid is ~25M ray-triangle intersections. Use a BVH (`bvh` crate, MIT) over the triangles to bring it to ~5M ops; runs in well under a second on web. Cache by mesh hash + grid hash so re-running the diff doesn't repeat the slicing.

### Step 2: Per-cell delta

```rust
pub struct DiffMap {
    pub width: u32,
    pub height: u32,
    /// Per-cell delta = simulated_z - target_z. Positive = surplus
    /// material remaining; negative = over-cut. NaN for cells where
    /// either side has no data (e.g. STL doesn't cover that cell).
    pub data: Vec<f32>,
}

pub fn compute_diff(simulated: &Heightmap, target: &Heightmap) -> DiffMap;
```

Define tolerance bands:
- `|delta| < tolerance_mm` → green ("on target").
- `delta > tolerance_mm` → yellow→red gradient ("surplus / not cut enough").
- `delta < -tolerance_mm` → blue→purple gradient ("over-cut").

`tolerance_mm` is per-project (`TargetMesh.tolerance_mm: Option<f64>`, default 0.1).

### Step 3: Aggregate stats

```rust
pub struct DiffStats {
    pub total_cells: u32,
    pub on_target_cells: u32,
    pub surplus_cells: u32,
    pub overcut_cells: u32,
    pub max_surplus_mm: f32,
    pub max_overcut_mm: f32,
    pub rms_delta_mm: f32,
}
```

Surface in the UI: "98.4% on target; max overcut 0.3 mm at (12.5, 8.0); RMS error 0.04 mm".

## UI

### `frontend/src/lib/components/StockPanel.svelte` or new `TargetMeshDialog.svelte`

- "Target mesh" expander: file picker + offset/rotation inputs + tolerance.
- Live preview: render the target mesh as a translucent reference in the 3D viewport when set. Color: distinct neutral (light blue?) so it's distinguishable from the cutting sim.

### `frontend/src/lib/components/Scene3D.svelte`

- New view mode toggle: "Cutting result / Diff overlay / Both".
- Diff overlay: color the heightmap cells by their delta (green/yellow/red/blue gradient as above). Solid heatmap on the simulated surface.
- "Both" mode: cut surface as solid, target mesh as translucent overlay. User sees alignment visually.

### `frontend/src/lib/components/GenerateBar.svelte` (or a new `DiffStats` panel)

- After sim completes, show the `DiffStats` numerically.
- Click on the "max overcut at (x, y)" link → 3D camera flies to that location.

## Tests

- `target_diff.rs::tests`:
  - STL of a simple flat plane at z=-2: target heightmap has every cell at -2.
  - Sliced rectangular pocket vs. a flat-pocket STL of the same dimensions: diff is < tolerance everywhere inside the pocket; outside cells = NaN.
  - Off-target: a 5 mm-deep target vs. a sim that only got to -4.8 mm: every cell shows +0.2 surplus.
- Round-trip: project with `target_mesh` preserves all fields.
- Performance: 100k-triangle STL on a 500×500-cell heightmap completes diff in < 2 seconds on a typical dev machine.

## Time budget

- STL slicing + BVH integration: 4-5 days.
- Diff math + tests: 2-3 days.
- 3D overlay rendering: 3-5 days.
- UI / TargetMeshDialog: 2-3 days.

## Dependencies

- Soft: `wiaconstructor-7f3` (STL importer) — once that's done, share STL-loading code. Until then, this child does its own minimal STL load. The child's STL load is *one-purpose* (for diff slicing) and small; doesn't conflict with the broader STL importer.
- No hard blockers.

## Open questions

- Mesh alignment UI: rotating + translating an STL via numeric input is awkward. v1 ships numeric only; manual drag-to-align in the 3D viewport is a follow-up.
- Diff over time vs. final-state diff: the user might want to see "after pass 3, am I on target?" not just "at the end". Replay the sim playhead with the diff active. Defer.
- Tolerance per region: a sign with a 1 mm V-carve and a 0.1 mm precision pocket benefits from per-region tolerance. v1 = global tolerance.
- Backside / two-sided projects: target mesh is two-sided. Compare front result against front-facing-down portion of the mesh; back against back-facing-down. Requires Child (rt1.11) two-sided machining; coordinate.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `TargetMesh` round-trips.
- [ ] STL slice produces correct target heightmap on test fixtures.
- [ ] Diff stats fire correctly on a known surplus / overcut setup.
- [ ] 3D viewport shows the heatmap overlay and the click-to-fly-to behavior.
- [ ] Performance target hit on the 100k-triangle / 500×500 grid case.
- [ ] User-guide section: "How to verify against your CAD model".
acceptance_criteria: TargetMesh round-trips; STL slice produces correct target heightmap; surplus/overcut stats fire on test setups; 3D heatmap overlay + click-to-fly; performance target hit on 100k-tri/500x500 case.
close_reason: Won't do — overengineering for a simple 2.5D CAM tool. STL slicing + BVH + heatmap overlay + UI is ~2 weeks of work to surface a feature most hobby users won't reach for (they trust the gcode preview + a test cut). Users who genuinely need 'did my cut match the model' have a calliper. If a real user requests this, re-file fresh.

title: Accel- and jerk-aware time estimation
description:
## What

Estimate program run-time accounting for machine acceleration and jerk limits, not just `path_length / feedrate`. The naive estimate underpredicts real time by 1.5-3× on hobby machines because every short segment forces an accel/decel cycle that never reaches commanded feed. Estlcam exposes a basic estimate; wiac currently uses simple length/feed.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** the project's `MachineConfig` (`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/setup.rs:249`) with per-axis accel and jerk limits (already present in many controllers; we just need to record them on the CAM side).
- **EXTEND** the simulation pipeline with a trapezoidal (or S-curve) profile integrator that walks segments and computes per-segment time accounting for entry/exit speed at each junction.
- **REPLACE** the existing simple-length-divided-by-feed estimator with the new integrator. Behind a feature flag on first ship so users can compare.

## Schema

```rust
// crates/wiac-core/src/cam/setup.rs

pub struct MachineConfig {
    // … existing fields …

    /// Per-axis acceleration limits in mm/s². None = use a conservative
    /// default that matches the controller's defaults for the dialect.
    /// (LinuxCNC default 250, GRBL $120 typically 200, Mach3 varies.)
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub accel: Option<AxisLimits>,
    /// Per-axis jerk limits in mm/s³. Many controllers don't expose
    /// jerk (they use trapezoidal accel only); leave None and the
    /// integrator uses a trapezoidal profile.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub jerk: Option<AxisLimits>,
}

pub struct AxisLimits {
    pub x: f64,
    pub y: f64,
    pub z: f64,
}
```

## Algorithm — `crates/wiac-core/src/sim/timing.rs` (new file)

A standard "trapezoidal velocity profile with junction-speed look-ahead" integrator. The literature here is well-established; see "Constant Jerk Equations for a Trajectory Generator" (Macfarlane & Croft, 2003) or any motion-control textbook.

### Step 1: Per-segment kinematics

For each `ToolpathSegment`:

- `length` (XY-Z 3D distance).
- `feed` (commanded feed for cuts; rapid speed for G0).
- `dir` (unit XYZ direction).

### Step 2: Junction speeds (look-ahead)

At each segment-to-segment junction, compute the maximum tangential speed the machine can carry through the corner without exceeding accel limits. Standard approach: the centripetal-acceleration formula for the cosine angle between adjacent segments.

```
cos_theta = dot(dir_i, dir_{i+1})
v_junction = sqrt(accel * (length_i.min(length_{i+1})) * (1 - cos_theta) / 2)
v_junction = min(v_junction, feed_i, feed_{i+1})
```

For `cos_theta == 1` (collinear segments), `v_junction == feed` (no slowdown). For `cos_theta == -1` (180° turn), `v_junction == 0` (full stop).

### Step 3: Per-segment trapezoidal profile

Given segment length `s`, entry speed `v0`, exit speed `v1`, max feed `vf`, accel `a`:

```
# Time to accelerate v0 → vf:  t_acc = (vf - v0) / a, distance s_acc = (vf² - v0²)/(2a)
# Time to decelerate vf → v1:  t_dec = (vf - v1) / a, distance s_dec = (vf² - v1²)/(2a)
if s_acc + s_dec > s:
    # Triangular profile (we never reach vf). Solve for peak vp:
    vp = sqrt(a * s + (v0² + v1²) / 2)
    t_acc = (vp - v0) / a; t_dec = (vp - v1) / a
    t = t_acc + t_dec
else:
    s_const = s - s_acc - s_dec
    t_const = s_const / vf
    t = t_acc + t_const + t_dec
```

For arc segments (`MoveKind::Arc`), the same logic applies, but `length` is the arc's chord-equivalent path length and the centripetal-accel constraint adds a per-arc maximum `v_max_arc = sqrt(a_centripetal * radius)`.

### Step 4: S-curve refinement (optional)

When `MachineConfig.jerk` is Some, replace each linear accel ramp with an S-curve (cubic polynomial during the transient). The math is more involved (~80 LOC); literature reference: Macfarlane & Croft 2003. Skip for v1; ship trapezoidal first, S-curve as Phase 2.

### Step 5: Aggregate

Sum `t` across segments. Add tool-change time (from ToolEntry, default 5 seconds; surface as a configurable per-machine value). Add spindle warm-up time.

## Wire-up

Replace `Prog_Time` (or wiac's equivalent — find with `grep -nE "estimated.*time|prog_time|total_time" crates/wiac-core/src/`). Pipeline produces a `TimeEstimate { total_s, breakdown: {cut_s, rapid_s, plunge_s, tool_change_s, ...} }` instead of a single number.

## UI

### `frontend/src/lib/components/MachineDialog.svelte`

- New "Acceleration" section with X / Y / Z inputs (mm/s²), defaults filled from a controller-aware defaults table.
- "Jerk" section with X / Y / Z inputs, default empty (= trapezoidal).
- Tooltip: "If you don't know your machine's accel limits, leave the defaults — they're conservative. Tighter values predict run time more accurately but require knowing your controller's settings."

### `frontend/src/lib/components/GenerateBar.svelte`

- Replace the current "Estimated time: HH:MM:SS" display with a hover-tooltip breakdown:
  ```
  Total: 23m 47s
  ── Cutting:    18m 02s
  ── Rapids:      2m 14s
  ── Plunges:     1m 31s
  ── Tool changes: 2m 00s
  ```

### Validation

- After running real jobs, surface a "calibrate" link near the time estimate. Link opens a small dialog: user enters actual run time, system suggests adjusted accel values to match. (Optional follow-up; ship the calibration math but the dialog can wait.)

## Tests

- `timing.rs::tests`:
  - Single 100 mm segment at feed 1000 mm/min, accel 250 mm/s²: trapezoidal sums to expected time. Manually compute reference value.
  - Two 50 mm collinear segments, same feed: junction-speed = feed (no slowdown), total time = single 100 mm equivalent.
  - Two 50 mm 90° segments, same feed: junction-speed = 0 (or whatever the formula gives), total time > single 100 mm equivalent.
  - Triangular profile: 1 mm segment at high feed with normal accel → never reaches feed; time = `2 * sqrt(s / a)`. Assert.
  - Arc: 90° quarter-circle at radius 5, feed 1000, accel 250 — arc's effective max speed `sqrt(250 * 5)` ≈ 35 mm/s ≈ 2100 mm/min, which is faster than 1000 mm/min, so no centripetal slowdown. Verify time ≈ 0.47 s.
- Round-trip: `MachineConfig.accel` and `jerk` preserve through serde.
- Integration: a known fixture project produces a time estimate within 5% of a hand-computed reference.

## Time budget

- Schema + integrator + tests: 1.5-2 weeks.
- UI updates: 0.5 week.
- Calibration validation against a real machine: parallel; assume ±15% on first version, refine with user feedback.

## Dependencies

- None hard. Friendly with the controller-integration epic (option C from the planning) — actual machine accel readback would auto-fill these fields.

## Open questions

- Per-axis accel for diagonal moves: a simultaneous X+Y move at 45° is bound by `min(accel_x, accel_y)` along that direction. Trivial. Document.
- Z-axis accel is usually much lower than X/Y (gravity + screw vs. linear belt). Tabular axes-respect-limits, no special handling needed.
- Look-ahead window: real controllers look ahead 64-256 segments. The integrator can do this exactly (it has the whole toolpath in memory). v1 = unlimited look-ahead; documented.
- Pause/dwell time (e.g., M0, M1, G4): the segment list doesn't currently include these as discrete events. File a follow-up for "hand-edit M-code time annotations" if anyone asks.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `MachineConfig.accel` and `jerk` round-trip.
- [ ] Unit tests above pass with hand-computed reference values.
- [ ] Real-machine calibration: a 30-minute job's estimate is within ±15% of measured wall-clock.
- [ ] GenerateBar shows time breakdown.
- [ ] Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/sim/timing.rs` module docs with citations to the kinematics literature.
acceptance_criteria: MachineConfig.accel/jerk round-trip; trapezoidal/junction/arc/triangular unit tests pass with hand-computed references; real-machine 30-min job within ±15%; GenerateBar shows breakdown.

title: User-configurable post-processor framework
description:
## What

A user-configurable post-processor (PP) framework: ship a small dialect-description language so users can target controllers we don't have a hand-written emitter for, without code changes. Estlcam's killer feature here is `c_PP` — a dozen-or-so config entries (per-axis name/format/scale, line-end, decimal point, replacement tokens, prologue/epilogue templates) that let users target Mach3 / Mach4 / FANUC / Siemens / Heidenhain / oddball home-made controllers. wiac currently has hand-written `linuxcnc.rs` / `grbl.rs` / `hpgl.rs`; users can't add a new dialect without a Rust PR.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** with a new generic emitter `gcode/template.rs` that consumes a `PostProcessor` config struct (or template file) and produces G-code from the same internal toolpath stream the existing emitters consume.
- **EXTEND** the project with a "post-processor library" (similar to the tool library): named PP profiles the user can pick.
- **CHANGE** existing `linuxcnc.rs` / `grbl.rs` / `hpgl.rs`: keep them as the fast paths *or* re-implement them on top of the template engine for consistency. Recommendation: ship the engine, leave the existing emitters in place, add a "Custom" emitter that uses the engine. Migrate the built-ins later if the engine proves complete.
- **No replacements** of the built-in emitters in v1.

## Data model — `crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/post_processor.rs` (new file)

```rust
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct PostProcessor {
    pub name: String,                // e.g. "Mach3 metric"
    pub file_extension: String,      // ".tap"
    pub line_ending: String,         // "\r\n"
    pub decimal_separator: char,     // '.' (sometimes ',' on Siemens)
    pub use_arcs: bool,
    pub ij_relative: bool,           // I/J relative to current pos vs. absolute
    pub line_numbers: Option<LineNumberConfig>,

    pub axes: AxesConfig,            // per-axis name, format, scale, enabled
    pub commands: CommandsConfig,    // G0/G1/G2/G3 strings per controller

    pub program_start: String,       // template body
    pub program_end: String,
    pub tool_change: String,
    pub object_start: String,        // emitted before each operation
    pub coolant_mist_on: String,
    pub coolant_mist_off: String,
    pub coolant_flood_on: String,
    pub coolant_flood_off: String,

    pub modal_axis_suppress: bool,   // skip an axis word when value unchanged
    pub modal_g_suppress: bool,      // skip Gn when same as previous line
}

pub struct AxesConfig {
    pub x: AxisFormat,
    pub y: AxisFormat,
    pub z: AxisFormat,
    pub i: AxisFormat,
    pub j: AxisFormat,
    pub feed: AxisFormat,            // "F"
    pub speed: AxisFormat,           // "S"
}

pub struct AxisFormat {
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub name: String,                // "X", "Y", "Z", "F", …
    pub format: String,              // "%.3f" or "%.4f", controllers vary
    pub scale: f64,                  // *1.0 default; * -1.0 for Z-up-positive controllers
    pub order: u8,                   // emit order on the line; lower first
}

pub struct CommandsConfig {
    pub rapid: String,               // "G0"
    pub linear: String,              // "G1"
    pub arc_cw: String,              // "G2"
    pub arc_ccw: String,             // "G3"
    // … further if needed
}
```

### Token replacement

The string templates support tokens substituted at emit time:

- `<f>` — feed value
- `<s>` — spindle speed
- `<t>` — tool number
- `<n>` — tool name
- `<d>` — tool diameter
- `<op>` — operation kind / name
- `<time>` — estimated total program time (hh:mm:ss)
- `<tools>` — full tool list (one per line)
- `<version>`, `<build>` — wiac version metadata
- `<unit>` — "mm" or "in"

```rust
pub fn substitute(template: &str, ctx: &EmitContext) -> String {
    let mut out = template.to_string();
    out = out.replace("<f>", &fmt(ctx.feed, &ctx.pp.axes.feed));
    out = out.replace("<s>", &fmt(ctx.speed, &ctx.pp.axes.speed));
    // …
    out
}
```

Special escape: `<!N>` suppresses line-numbering on that line (some prologue templates already include their own numbering and don't want a second N applied).

## The generic emitter — `crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/template.rs` (new file)

Walks the same internal toolpath the existing emitters do (`Vec<ToolpathSegment>` or whatever the abstraction is — confirm in spike). For each segment:

1. Build a `Line` struct: `{ g_code: u8, x: Option<f64>, y: Option<f64>, z: Option<f64>, i: ?, j: ?, f: ?, s: ? }`.
2. Apply modal suppression (drop axes equal to the previous line's value if `modal_axis_suppress`).
3. Format each enabled axis using `format!(format_string, value * scale)` ⇒ replace decimal point if needed.
4. Sort by `axis.order`.
5. Join with the configured delimiter (default `" "`).
6. Append line ending.
7. Optionally prefix with `Nxxxx` per `LineNumberConfig`.

Emit prologue from `program_start`, then per-op `object_start`, then the toolpath, then `program_end`.

## UI — `frontend/src/lib/components/PostProcessorEditor.svelte`

A new dialog accessible from MachineDialog: "Edit post-processor…". Flat form over the `PostProcessor` struct, plus a live preview pane that renders the first 20 lines of an example G-code sequence using the current config. Edits update the preview live.

`frontend/src/lib/components/MachineDialog.svelte`: replace the current dialect dropdown with a dropdown over the saved PP profiles + "Edit current…" + "Import / Export PP file…" buttons. Bundled profiles: `LinuxCNC default`, `GRBL default`, `Mach3 metric`, `Mach3 imperial`, `FANUC`, `Heidenhain`. Same internal engine; bundled config files in `frontend/public/post_processors/*.json`.

PP files exportable as a self-contained JSON so users can share controller configs.

## Tests

- `template.rs::tests`:
  - Default LinuxCNC PP config produces output byte-identical to `linuxcnc.rs` for a sample toolpath. (This is the crucial regression test.)
  - GRBL likewise.
  - Modal axis suppression works: `G1 X10 Y10` followed by `G1 X10 Y20` emits only `Y20` on the second line.
  - Decimal-separator replacement: a config with `decimal_separator = ','` produces `X10,000`.
  - Token substitution: `program_start = "; gen by wiac <version>"` + version "0.0.0" produces `"; gen by wiac 0.0.0"`.
- Snapshot: each bundled PP profile produces a known-good fixture for a toy project.
- Round-trip: PP config → JSON → PP config preserves all fields.

## Time budget

- 4-6 weeks. This is the largest single feature in this batch. Most of it is ground-truthing existing emitter behaviors as PP configs (so byte-identical regression matters), bullet-proofing the format-string parser (controllers exhaustively test edge cases), and shipping enough bundled profiles.
- Two-phase delivery: Phase 1 = engine + LinuxCNC/GRBL config equivalence + Custom-PP UI. Phase 2 = additional bundled profiles + import/export.

## Dependencies

- None hard. Friendly overlap with `wiaconstructor-rt1.6` (per-tool defaults — some PPs format `S` differently for different tool types). No blocker.
- May invalidate / extend `wiaconstructor-rt1.4` (Trochoidal) — that issue assumes G2/G3 arc support; this introduces the per-PP `use_arcs` flag. Confirm both honor it.

## Open questions

- Migration vs. coexistence: at some point the built-in `linuxcnc.rs` / `grbl.rs` should be deleted in favor of the engine. Probably after one release cycle of the engine running in parallel and proving byte-identical regression. File the migration as a follow-up.
- Custom-PP user UX: the editor exposes ~30 fields. Most users only edit 2-3. Group with collapsible sections; default collapsed. First-time editor users get a wizard ("which controller?" → fills the form).
- Format-string syntax: Rust's `format!` is awkward for runtime-constructed format strings. Use a tiny printf-ish parser limited to `%[width].[prec]f`. ~50 LOC.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `PostProcessor` struct round-trips JSON.
- [ ] Generic `template.rs` emitter produces byte-identical output to `linuxcnc.rs` and `grbl.rs` for sample toolpaths.
- [ ] PostProcessorEditor reachable from MachineDialog with live preview.
- [ ] At least 4 bundled PP profiles ship.
- [ ] Import / export of PP files works and roundtrips.
- [ ] Modal suppression, decimal separator, token substitution, line-ending all configurable and tested.
acceptance_criteria: PostProcessor struct round-trips; generic template emitter byte-identical to existing linuxcnc.rs/grbl.rs for samples; PostProcessorEditor with live preview; ≥4 bundled profiles ship; PP import/export; modal/decimal/tokens/line-end all configurable+tested.
notes:

## Per-axis (c_Coordinate)

Axes covered: X / Y / Z / I / J. Plus F (feed) and S (spindle) which have the same Format/Repeat shape but no Scale/Enable.

## Replacement tokens (c_Gcode.cs grep output)
<version>, <build>, <project>, <op>, <name>, <order>, <time>, <tools>,
<f>, <s>, <t>, <n>, <d>, <i>, <string>,
<t_pierce>, <t_pierce_ms>,

## Top-level config (c_PP fields)
