title: Photo / grayscale → laser raster engraving
description:
## What

Photo / grayscale image → laser raster engraving. The user opens a JPEG/PNG, picks a target size, and the system emits G-code that walks the laser back-and-forth modulating power per pixel. Estlcam ships this through `dlg_Pic_Select` + `c_Laserengraver`. wiac has `ToolKind::LaserBeam` (`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:91`) but no raster operation today.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** `OperationKind` (`project.rs:176`) with a new variant `RasterEngrave { ... }`.
- **EXTEND** the input pipeline with image import (`crates/wiac-core/src/input/raster.rs` — new file).
- **EXTEND** the G-code emitters (LinuxCNC + GRBL) with laser-power-modulated raster output.
- **No replacements.**

## Data model

```rust
// crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs
pub enum OperationKind {
    // … existing variants …
    /// Photo / grayscale raster engrave with a laser. Burns one row at
    /// a time, modulating S (spindle speed = laser power) per pixel.
    RasterEngrave {
        /// Per-pixel scan resolution in mm (e.g. 0.1 mm = 254 DPI).
        resolution_mm: f64,
        /// Horizontal raster direction. Vertical is just X-Y swap;
        /// expose for grain alignment / aspect-ratio considerations.
        scan_direction: ScanDirection,
        /// Pixel value → laser power mapping.
        power_curve: PowerCurve,
        /// How rasters are connected at row ends.
        link: RasterLink,
        /// 1.0 = no overscan; >1.0 extends each line by this fraction
        /// past the image edge so the laser reaches its commanded
        /// power before crossing pixels (controllers ramp S on accel).
        overscan_factor: f64,
    },
}

pub enum ScanDirection { LeftRight, BottomUp }

pub enum PowerCurve {
    /// Power = brightness * scale + offset; clip to [min, max].
    Linear { min: u32, max: u32 },
    /// Black & white at threshold; full-power below threshold, 0 above.
    Threshold { value: u8 },
    /// Floyd-Steinberg dithered to ON/OFF.
    Dithered { threshold: u8 },
    /// Bayer-matrix-ordered dither (less artifact-y than F-S on lasers
    /// because errors don't propagate; predictable).
    Bayer { matrix_size: u8, threshold: u8 },
}

pub enum RasterLink {
    /// Lift between rows, M5 between, M3 at row start.
    LiftBetween,
    /// Bidirectional (boustrophedon) — emit alternating rows in opposite
    /// directions; saves traversal but doubles the number of accel/decel
    /// transitions on the rapid axes. Use with low-inertia gantries.
    Bidirectional,
}
```

## Algorithm — `crates/wiac-core/src/input/raster.rs` (new file)

1. **Image load.** Use the `image` crate (already in our dep tree via `usvg` transitively, or add directly — minimal binary cost). Convert to single-channel grayscale via the standard luminance weights `(0.299·R + 0.587·G + 0.114·B)`.
2. **Resample to target resolution.** Image's pixels-per-mm → target's `resolution_mm`. Use `image::imageops::resize` with Lanczos3 or CatmullRom filter for quality. Avoid nearest-neighbor (visible "stairs" at typical raster resolutions).
3. **Apply `power_curve`** per pixel:
   - Linear: `P = round((1 - bright/255) * (max - min) + min)`. Inverted because dark = more burn.
   - Threshold: `P = if bright < threshold { max } else { 0 }`.
   - Dithered (Floyd-Steinberg): walk pixels in scan order, propagate the quantization error to neighbors per F-S weights `[7/16, 3/16, 5/16, 1/16]`. Output is binary (max or 0).
   - Bayer: lookup pixel against the ordered-dither matrix; threshold-compare.
4. **Hand to G-code emitter** as a 2D `[[u32; W]; H]` of S-values plus the resolution.

## G-code emit — `crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/laser.rs` (new file, or extend existing emitters)

Two output flavors:

- **M3/M5 + S** (LinuxCNC, fluidNC): `M3 S0` to enable laser. Each move's `S` parameter modulates power. Crucially, `G1 X<x> Y<y> S<s>` per pixel — the controller's lookahead ensures the S commanded matches the segment.
- **GRBL M4 dynamic-power** (newer GRBL with `$32=1` / "laser mode"): `M4 S0`. Same per-segment S syntax, but `M4` lets GRBL ramp S with acceleration so corners don't over-burn. *Strongly preferred* for any GRBL controller.

Pseudocode:

```
emit "G21 G90"
emit "M3 S0"        ; or M4 S0
for each row y:
    G0 to (overscan_left, y)
    G1 to (overscan_left, y) F<feed>      ; reach feed
    for each pixel (x, y):
        emit "G1 X<x> Y<y> S<power[x][y]>"
    G1 to (overscan_right, y) S0
emit "M5"           ; laser off
emit "M2"           ; program end
```

For huge images (millions of pixels = millions of G-code lines), generate the file streamingly — don't build the whole `Vec<String>` in memory. The existing emitters likely buffer everything; check and refactor if needed.

## UI

### New dialog `frontend/src/lib/components/RasterEngraveDialog.svelte`

Triggered from the toolbar "Add Raster Engrave" or via Add Text-style menu.

Fields:
- Image picker (drag-drop or file dialog).
- Target physical size (W mm × H mm, locked aspect or free).
- Position (X, Y).
- Resolution (DPI dropdown: 150 / 200 / 254 / 300 DPI; or custom mm).
- Power curve (radio: Linear / Threshold / Dithered / Bayer + the curve's parameters).
- Scan direction.
- Link mode.
- Overscan factor.

Live preview pane: shows the current image with the curve applied so the user sees what will burn. A small histogram next to the image shows the brightness distribution and the threshold cursor (for Threshold curve).

### `frontend/src/lib/components/EntityCanvas2D.svelte`

A new entity type renders as a faint screen-space-only image at the engrave's position. Distinguishable from vector geometry. Click-drag to reposition.

### `frontend/src/lib/components/Scene3D.svelte`

Render the toolpath at the laser side as densely-sampled lines colored by S value (heatmap). For visual sanity at huge raster counts, downsample to ~10000 visible segments — controllers see them all, the user just needs to see *what's covered*.

## Tests

- `raster.rs::tests`:
  - Load a 4x4 grayscale image; assert `power_curve = Threshold { 128 }` produces the expected ON/OFF pattern.
  - Floyd-Steinberg on a uniform 50% gray produces near-50% on/off pixels in the output.
  - Bayer matrix-size 4 and 8 produce expected predictable patterns.
- Snapshot: a 16x16 test image emits a known G-code line count.
- Pipeline integration: a RasterEngrave op + a Profile op in the same project produce a single G-code file with the raster portion bracketed by `M3/M5` and the profile portion using the existing milling sequence (no S-modulation interference).

## Time budget

- 3-4 weeks. The dithering math is well-known; the streaming-emit refactor is the time sink.
- Validate on a real laser cutter early — power curves vary wildly across diodes / CO₂ / fiber; the Linear defaults are likely wrong for any specific machine.

## Dependencies

- None hard. ToolKind::LaserBeam already exists. May want to coordinate with `wiaconstructor-rt1.6` (per-tool defaults — set per-tool default power curve) but not blocked.

## Open questions

- Image cache: import once, store as base64 or path-reference in project JSON? Path-reference breaks portability; base64 inflates project files. Probably store both: relative path if available, base64 fallback.
- Bidirectional dithered output suffers from "alignment artifacts" between left-right rows (errors propagate differently). Either restrict dithered mode to unidirectional, or use Bayer (matrix-only, no propagation, no alignment problem).
- Estimated burn time: dynamic estimate in the dialog so the user doesn't kick off a 6-hour engrave by accident.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `OperationKind::RasterEngrave` round-trips.
- [ ] Image import loads JPEG and PNG.
- [ ] Linear, Threshold, Dithered, Bayer curves all produce visually-correct test outputs.
- [ ] G-code emitter produces M3/M5-bracketed laser sequences.
- [ ] Manual cut on real laser: a 50×50 mm photo engraving completes and visually matches the preview.
- [ ] Streaming emit for >100k pixels doesn't OOM the renderer or the writer.
acceptance_criteria: OperationKind::RasterEngrave round-trips; PNG/JPEG import; Linear/Threshold/Dithered/Bayer curves correct; M3/M5-bracketed laser sequences in G-code; real-laser smoke test passes; streaming emit doesn't OOM on >100k pixels.
notes: BACKEND COMPLETE (phases 1-3): cam::raster power/dither core (d3041c2), OpKind::RasterEngrave wire variant reusing ReliefSource (bf7e239), run_raster_op scanline gcode emitter (c926fa1). RasterEngrave round-trips AND emits real M3/S-modulated/M5 laser gcode end-to-end. Remaining: phase 4 UI (502f — dialog/2D/3D/burn-estimate) and follow-up (streaming emit + GRBL M4). Architecture note: reuses ReliefSource brightness grid (frontend-decoded), no Rust image crate.
close_reason: Already shipped (issue predates the implementation): OpKind::RasterEngrave + crates/ivac-core/src/cam/raster.rs implement the full data model from this issue (resolution_mm, scan_direction, PowerCurve linear/threshold/floyd_steinberg/bayer, RasterLink lift_between/bidirectional, overscan_factor); frontend has the op-picker entry and RasterEngraveSection with JPEG/PNG import via decodeImageFile -> addReliefSource. Verified by code audit 2026-06-11.

title: Two-sided machining (flip stock workflow)
description:
## What

Two-sided machining: cut the front, flip the stock around one axis, cut the back. Common for joinery, two-sided signs, deeper-than-stock pockets, 3D-effect carving.

## Scope correction (2026-06-15 design review)

The original spec said "the math is trivial." That part is true and is NOT where the work is. Two findings reframe this feature:

1. **Toolpath generation is genuinely easy and does NOT need side-1 state.** When flipped, side 2 cuts into the previously-flat, uncut back face. Side-2 toolpaths = mirror geometry (mirror_segments_x/y in cam.rs:249) + re-anchor Z. The only case where side-1 state matters is side 2 cutting deep enough to REACH side-1 material — that is the error case to detect, not the normal path.

2. **The preview cannot represent a two-sided part today.** sim/heightmap.rs:19 is a single 2.5D grid: one Z per (x,y), only ever lowered from top_z. It is structurally single-sided. Shipping the original spec (mirror + two files, reuse the single heightmap) yields a preview that silently shows only ONE side — worse than no preview, because users trust it to verify alignment. driver.ts owns exactly one Simulator per project.

## The two real hard parts

### A. Dual-surface simulation (the bulk of the work)
- Second Simulator instance (back), fed the flipped/Z-inverted back toolpath, carving DOWN from the new top (= old stock bottom).
- Render front carve as the top surface and back carve as the bottom surface of one solid (export_stl already drops to stock_bottom_z for watertightness — precedent in driver.ts:73).
- Per-cell conflict detection: front_depth + back_depth vs thickness. Warn on overlap; refuse to emit if both sides cut clean through.

### B. Registration UX — opinionated, automated, ONE workflow
- v1 ships DOWEL PINS ONLY (drop fence/index-pin from original spec — fewer options, fully automated = the thing that makes it great).
- Front program drills the dowel holes; back program references the mirrored hole positions. Auto-placed; user does not hand-enter coordinates.
- ONE flip axis, picked once, communicated with an unmistakable visual (arrow/animation, not a bare dropdown). Flip-axis ambiguity (X vs Y) is the #1 user error.
- Z re-referencing: real stock thickness varies ±0.5mm. Emit two G-code files (front/back) so the user re-zeros Z between them; flip instructions in each header. (Single-file + M0 Pause is rejected: most controllers can't cleanly re-zero Z mid-program after M0.)

## Schema
- Op gains `side: WorkpieceSide { Front (default), Back }` (skip_serializing default).
- StockConfig gains flip-axis + dowel-pin registration config.

## Verdict
Do it properly or decline — there is no good half-version. Realistic budget 3-4 weeks, DOMINATED by part A (dual-heightfield sim + dual-surface render), not the 2-3 originally claimed. Known-good UX exists (Carbide Create Pro / Fusion two-sided) to copy.

## Open questions
- Dual-surface render: two meshes vs one stitched watertight solid? Spike part A first.
- Where do dowel holes live relative to imported geometry/stock margin? Probably stock-relative, outside the part envelope.
- Stock-thickness probe/entry: trust nominal, or prompt to measure-and-enter actual before back program?
acceptance_criteria: Op.side round-trips; dual-surface preview shows front+back carve as one solid; per-cell conflict detection warns on overlap and refuses clean-through; dowel holes auto-placed in both programs at mirrored positions; flip axis communicated with unmistakable visual; two G-code files (front/back) with flip+re-zero instructions in headers; real two-sided test cut documented.
notes:
Reframed from 'trivial math' to 'do-it-right-or-decline'. Hard part is dual-heightfield sim (part A), not the toolpath flip. See description scope-correction section. User decision 2026-06-15: rewrite + plan rather than ship the original under-scoped version.
FRONTEND PLAN (2026-07-19) — RE-SEQUENCED. Backend (Phase 2 = rt1.11.3 + rt1.11.3.1) DONE: run_pipeline_two_sided emits front/back programs, exposed on all transports + CLI. Remaining frontend work re-ordered around a shared foundation (nominal 11.4->11.5 is backwards — can't preview a two-sided job without one existing):
  Foundation (ivac-lhqu, NEW) = model fields + generateTwoSided wiring. Blocks 11.4 + 11.5.
  -> C (config UX, in 11.5): Side dropdown + flip/dowel panel.
  -> P (preview, 11.4): productionize the Phase-0 dual-surface spike in driver.ts.
  -> U (polish, 11.5): op-list grouping, gcode Front/Back tabs, unmistakable flip visual.
  -> V (11.6): verify + document a real two-sided cut.
Critical path: foundation -> C -> P. Once foundation lands, P and U parallelize. Full seams + file:line in each issue's notes.

title: Interactive tab placement on contours
description:
## What

Let the user click on a closed contour in the 2D canvas to place / move / delete tab bridges. wiac already has the data model (`TabsConfig` in `cam/setup.rs`, `Project.tabs` placement map) and tab cutting logic; what's missing is the interactive placement UX. Estlcam users get this — they click a contour and a tab appears there. wiac currently generates tab placement automatically (or via numeric inputs); manual placement on irregular contours is unavailable.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** `frontend/src/lib/components/EntityCanvas2D.svelte` with a "Tab placement" interaction mode.
- **EXTEND** the project's tab placement schema to record per-tab anchor (contour id + arc-length parameter).
- **No replacements.** Existing auto-placement remains as the default; manual mode is opt-in per op.

## Data model

Currently `Project.tabs` is a placement map. Inspect its current shape — if it stores raw `(x, y)` points, switch to `(object_id, t)` where `t ∈ [0, 1)` is the contour-arc-length parameter, so tabs slide with the geometry as the user edits points or applies transforms. This is the same fix viaConstructor made post-rewrite.

```rust
pub struct TabPlacement {
    pub object_id: u32,
    pub t: f64,            // arc-length parameter, 0..1
    pub width_override: Option<f64>,    // if None, use op.params.tabs.width
    pub height_override: Option<f64>,
}
```

When the operation pipeline hands tabs to `attach_tabs_to_offsets` (`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:48`), resolve `(object_id, t)` to a world point against the *current* polyline.

## UI: tab placement mode

Three sub-modes in EntityCanvas2D, gated by a toggle in the op's PropertiesPanel ("Tabs: Auto / Manual / Mixed"):

- **Auto** — current behavior. Tabs are spaced evenly around the contour; user sets count and width.
- **Manual** — user clicks anywhere on the contour to add a tab there. Right-click to remove. Drag to reposition.
- **Mixed** — auto-spaced tabs *plus* user-added tabs from manual mode; the union.

### Interaction details (`EntityCanvas2D.svelte`)

- When manual or mixed mode is active for an op, hovering over the closest contour shows a translucent ghost-tab at the cursor's projection onto the contour. Click commits.
- Tabs render as small filled rectangles oriented perpendicular to the contour at the placement. Width = `tab_width` from op params; visual length = `2 × tab_height`.
- Hover over an existing tab: highlight; cursor changes to "grab".
- Right-click on tab: context menu "Delete tab" / "Edit tab" (the latter opens a small popover with width/height overrides).
- ESC exits placement mode.
- Keyboard: `Tab` (key) cycles between Auto / Manual / Mixed for the selected op.

### Snap behavior

- Snap to contour: use the closest-point-on-polyline projection at cursor position. Tolerance = 5 px in screen space.
- Snap to existing tab positions: snap if cursor is within 2 mm of an existing tab so users can drag-stack precisely.
- Snap to contour midpoints, endpoints (closed contours have no endpoints; for open contours the endpoints are common tab anchors).

## Pipeline wiring

`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:48` `attach_tabs_to_offsets` takes a list of `TabPoint`. Add a resolver:

```rust
pub fn resolve_tab_placements(
    placements: &[TabPlacement],
    objects: &[VcObject],
    interpolate: usize,
) -> Vec<TabPoint> {
    placements.iter().map(|tp| {
        let obj = &objects[tp.object_id as usize];
        let pts = segments_to_points(&obj.segments, interpolate);
        let total = polyline_length(&pts);
        let target = total * tp.t;
        let (point, _local_t) = polyline_point_at_arc_length(&pts, target);
        TabPoint { point, /* … */ }
    }).collect()
}
```

`polyline_length` and `polyline_point_at_arc_length` are tiny helpers in `cam.rs` (the math is trivial — accumulate segment lengths and binary-search).

## Visualization in 3D

`Scene3D.svelte` already renders tabs as raised features in the toolpath preview. Confirm tabs from manual placement render identically to auto-placed ones (they should — by the time Scene3D sees them, they're just `TabPoint` entries).

## Tests

- `tabs.rs::tests` (new file under `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/`):
  - `polyline_point_at_arc_length` correctness on a square contour: t=0 → corner 0, t=0.25 → corner 1, t=0.5 → corner 2, t=0.75 → corner 3.
  - `resolve_tab_placements` returns the same world point after a 90° rotation of the source object — the parameter is geometry-relative.
- Frontend (Svelte component test): clicking on a contour in manual mode adds an entry to the project store with the right `(object_id, t)`.
- Snapshot: project JSON with both auto and manual tabs round-trips.

## Time budget

- 1-2 weeks. Most of it is the canvas interaction polish (snap, hover, drag). The data-model migration is small; the math is trivial.

## Dependencies

- None hard. Some friendly overlap with `wiaconstructor-rt1.6` (per-tool defaults) — if both ship, share a common "override or inherit" UI pattern. Not a blocker.

## Open questions

- Existing projects might have tabs stored as `(x, y)` points. The schema migration converts them by finding the nearest contour at load time and storing `(object_id, t)`. Spike: confirm the migration round-trips on the test fixtures.
- "Mixed" mode arithmetic: do auto-spaced tabs *avoid* the regions where manual tabs are placed, or do they pretend manual tabs aren't there? v1: pretend. Cleanest. File "auto-avoid-manual" as follow-up if requested.
- For dynamic tab width (`width_override`), the auto-place algorithm needs to know about explicit widths. Pass through the override to `attach_tabs_to_offsets`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `TabPlacement` schema with `(object_id, t)` round-trips.
- [ ] Manual mode in EntityCanvas2D supports add / drag / right-click delete.
- [ ] Tab parameters survive 90°-rotation of source geometry (integration test).
- [ ] Auto / Manual / Mixed mode toggle in OpPropertiesPanel.
- [ ] Existing fixture projects load and render tabs identically (regression test).
acceptance_criteria: TabPlacement schema with (object_id, t) round-trips; manual mode supports add/drag/right-click delete; tab parameters survive 90° rotation; Auto/Manual/Mixed mode toggle; existing fixtures regression-clean.
close_reason: Per-op tabs: ProjectParams gains tab_mode (Off/Auto{count}/Manual/Mixed{auto_count}) + tab_placements (Vec<TabPlacement{object_id, t, width_override_mm, height_override_mm}>). Legacy Project.tabs (segment-keyed (x,y) map) deleted outright — no migration needed. cam/tabs.rs ships polyline_arc_lengths / polyline_project / polyline_at_t / auto_tab_ts / resolve_tab_placements with 7 unit tests including geometric invariance under rotation. pipeline.rs build_op_tabs_by_object resolves per-op placements + auto-spacing to the (object_idx → Vec<TabPoint>) map attach_tabs_to_offsets already consumes. cache key drops the tabs HashMap parameter — per-op tabs flow through hash_operation_params. PIPELINE_VERSION 14. FE: cam/tabs.ts mirrors the arc-length math (same densification as Rust). EntityCanvas2D — tab placement mode bound to the selected op's tabMode; ghost-on-hover (projects cursor onto the op's source contour within 6 px); click toggles (Estlcam-style: click empty contour adds, click near existing tab removes, tolerance 0.01 of contour length); tabs render as filled rectangles oriented along the tangent + zoom-resistant px floor. OpPropertiesPanel — segmented Mode toggle (Off/Auto/Manual/Mixed), Count input for Auto/Mixed, Width/Height inputs. Scene3D walks each op's placements and renders 3D markers; auto-spaced 3D rendering deferred (rbk). commands.test rt1.10 toggleTabPlacementCommand suite (add, remove-within-tolerance, per-op isolation). 317 wiac-core lib tests + 94 FE tests pass; svelte-check 0 errors 0 warnings. Drag-to-reposition deferred per Estlcam pattern (click-to-toggle instead). Snap-to-vertex/midpoint, per-tab popover, and disconnected-tabs toast filed as 3 follow-ups.

title: Linear pocket strategy with arbitrary angle (extends Zigzag)
description:
## What

Extend the Zigzag pocket strategy with a configurable angle so users can set the raster direction. Estlcam exposes `Linear_X`, `Linear_Y`, and a free-angle linear pocket strategy; we have only "Zigzag" with an implicit X-axis direction. Useful when grain direction matters (carving wood with the grain), or when a long thin pocket clears more cleanly along its length than across it.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** `PocketStrategy::Zigzag` (`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:234`) with a parameter:
  ```rust
  Zigzag { angle_deg: f64 }   // default 0.0 (X-axis = current behavior)
  ```
  Or, less breaking: keep `Zigzag` parameterless and add a new `LinearAngled { angle_deg: f64 }` variant. The unit-variant choice is cleaner schema-wise but breaks every existing project file.
- **PREFERRED**: Adopt the new variant and keep `Zigzag` as an alias for `LinearAngled { angle_deg: 0.0 }` via a serde-compat shim. Existing project JSON loads as the new variant with default angle 0.0, behavior unchanged.
- **CHANGE** `pocket_zigzag` (`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:188`) to accept an `angle_rad` parameter and rotate the raster lines accordingly.
- **No replacements.** Behavior unchanged for default angle 0.0.

## Algorithm

The core change is in `pocket_zigzag(boundary: &[Point2], stride: f64, tool_diameter: f64, angle_rad: f64)`:

1. **Rotate the boundary** by `-angle_rad` around its centroid. Now the user-requested raster direction is the X-axis.
2. **Run the existing X-axis raster fill** (current implementation).
3. **Rotate the resulting strokes back** by `+angle_rad`.

That's it. The math reduces to "let the existing code do X-aligned fill in a rotated frame". `cam.rs:rotate_segments` already handles the rotation primitives.

```rust
pub fn pocket_zigzag_angled(
    boundary: &[Point2],
    stride: f64,
    tool_diameter: f64,
    angle_rad: f64,
) -> Vec<Segment> {
    if angle_rad.abs() < 1e-9 {
        return pocket_zigzag(boundary, stride, tool_diameter);
    }
    let centroid = polygon_centroid(boundary).unwrap_or(Point2::ZERO);
    let mut rotated_boundary = boundary.to_vec();
    rotate_points(&mut rotated_boundary, centroid, -angle_rad);
    let mut strokes = pocket_zigzag(&rotated_boundary, stride, tool_diameter);
    rotate_segments(&mut strokes, centroid, angle_rad);
    strokes
}
```

(`rotate_points` is a small helper to mirror `rotate_segments`'s logic for `[Point2]`.)

## UI — `frontend/src/lib/components/OpPropertiesPanel.svelte`

Around line 506 (the pocket-strategy `<select>`):

- When `op.pocketStrategy.kind === 'zigzag'` (or the new variant name): show an additional input "Raster angle (°)" with range 0-180°, default 0.
- Tooltip: "Direction of the raster lines. 0° = horizontal (X-axis). 45° = diagonal. Useful for grain alignment in wood."
- Add quick-pick buttons next to the input: `0°` `45°` `90°` `135°` for one-click common angles.

## Tests

- For a 20×20 mm square pocket with `angle_deg = 0`: existing zigzag test output unchanged.
- For the same pocket with `angle_deg = 90`: same number of strokes as 0°, but rotated 90°. Assert by checking each stroke is parallel to Y-axis.
- For `angle_deg = 45`: strokes are diagonal. Stroke count = `ceil(diagonal / stride)`.
- Round-trip: save+load preserves `angle_deg` exactly.
- Snapshot: existing project fixtures with `Zigzag` (no angle) still load.

## Time budget

- 2-3 days. Tiny algorithm change; bulk of the work is the schema migration shim and UI input.

## Open questions

- Variant naming: `Zigzag` keeps the historical name; `LinearAngled` is more explicit. Pick one and document. Recommendation: keep `Zigzag { angle_deg }` (parametrize the existing variant), schema-break in one shot. wiac is alpha; this is the right time.
- Should `Spiral` and `Cascade` get analogous angle parameters? They don't really need it (concentric strategies don't have a preferred axis), but a "first-pass direction" hint could help on long-thin pockets. Defer to a follow-up if requested.

## Dependencies

None. Lands independently of other rt1 children.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `PocketStrategy::Zigzag { angle_deg }` round-trips.
- [ ] Existing project fixtures load (with implicit `angle_deg = 0.0`).
- [ ] Unit tests above pass.
- [ ] OpPropertiesPanel exposes the angle input + quick-pick buttons.
- [ ] Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs` module docs.
acceptance_criteria: PocketStrategy::Zigzag{angle_deg} round-trips; existing fixtures load with implicit angle 0; unit tests for 0/45/90 deg pass; OpPropertiesPanel exposes angle input + quick-pick buttons.

title: Inlay generator (V-carve based, male+female pair with clearance)
description:
## What

A V-carve "Inlay" generator: from one drawing, produce two G-code programs that together make an inlay — a tapered pocket in the base material, plus a matching tapered plug. Glue the plug into the pocket and you get a flush, hand-cut-looking inlay. This is *the* feature woodworkers buy CAM software for after V-carve; Estlcam ships it (`dlg_Inlay`).

The geometry trick: a V-bit produces a *tapered* pocket (walls at the bit's half-angle). If you cut the same shape *inverted* into a contrasting material, the plug's tapered walls match the pocket's tapered walls, and pushing the plug down into the pocket wedges the two together. The user controls the depth of the join (= height of plug above the pocket floor) and a small radial clearance (= friction fit vs. drop-in vs. epoxy gap).

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** with a new operation type `OperationKind::Inlay { side: InlaySide, gap_mm: f64, plug_height_mm: f64 }`.
  - `side: InlaySide { Pocket, Plug }` — Pocket = cut into base; Plug = plug to glue in.
  - `gap_mm` — radial clearance per side (default 0.1 mm; user typically picks 0.05-0.2 mm).
  - `plug_height_mm` — vertical engagement of plug (default 1.5 mm).
- **REUSES** the V-carve algorithm from `wiaconstructor-rt1.1`. Inlay is "V-carve at this depth, with this offset, against these walls". No new core algorithm — just a different parameterization.
- **No replacements.** Existing V-carve operation stays.

## Algorithm — implement in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/inlay.rs` (new file)

The geometry, with `α` = V-bit half-angle, `d_p` = plug_height, `g` = clearance:

### Pocket side (cut into base material)

- Region: the source contour(s).
- Carve cap: the deepest point reaches `-d_p`. Anything deeper would be invisible after gluing.
- Per-point inscribed-radius `R_i` is **clamped to `R_i ≤ d_p · tan(α)`** so the pocket walls have constant slope = bit's half-angle.
- Use `wiac-core::cam::vcarve` (Child 1) with `OperationParams.depth = -d_p` and `carve_max_width_mm = 2 · d_p · tan(α)`.

### Plug side (cut into contrasting board)

- Region: same source contour(s).
- Cut starts from the **top** of the stock at depth = -plug_height_mm. The plug is *inverted* — what was a deep V in the pocket becomes a tall ridge on the plug.
- Apply a **uniform inward offset of `g`** before V-carving so the plug is `g` mm smaller per side than the pocket.
- The plug result is sliced off the host board after cutting, flipped, and glued in.

### Concrete steps in code

```rust
pub fn build_inlay_op(
    source_objects: &[VcObject],
    tool: &ToolEntry,        // must be VBit with tip_angle_deg set
    side: InlaySide,
    plug_height_mm: f64,
    gap_mm: f64,
) -> Result<Operation, Warning> {
    let half_angle = tool.tip_angle_deg / 2.0;
    let max_w = 2.0 * plug_height_mm * tan_deg(half_angle);

    let region = match side {
        InlaySide::Pocket => source_objects.to_vec(),
        InlaySide::Plug => offset_inward(source_objects, gap_mm)?,
    };

    Ok(Operation {
        kind: OperationKind::VCarve { /* ... */ },
        // … per side: pocket has -plug_height_mm; plug has -plug_height_mm too but drawn from the *top* of stock
        params: OperationParams {
            depth: -plug_height_mm,
            carve_max_width_mm: Some(max_w),
            // … inherit other defaults from V-Carve
        },
        // … source = region
    })
}
```

The `offset_inward` step uses `cavalier_contours::PlineSource::parallel_offset(-gap_mm)` (already in our dependency tree).

### Important detail: stock-relative Z

For Plug side, `start_depth` and `depth` are interpreted relative to **the top of the plug stock**, not the same datum as the pocket. The user runs the two G-code programs on different physical pieces; we don't try to merge into one program. UI must make this clear.

## UI — `frontend/src/lib/components/`

New flow: `InlayDialog.svelte`. Either entered from the Add Operation menu or from a button on a selected V-Carve op ("Convert to Inlay").

Fields:
- Side: radio (Pocket / Plug / Both).
- Plug height: number_mm (default 1.5).
- Gap (per side): number_mm (default 0.1).
- Tool: dropdown filtered to V-bits.
- Source: re-uses Operation source picker (Layers / Objects / All).

When `Both`: creates two ops at once with the same source — one Pocket op, one Plug op — and groups them under a name like "Inlay: <source>". Each op exports to a separate G-code file when generated.

OperationsList rendering: an Inlay op shows a chain icon; clicking it expands to show both Pocket and Plug sub-ops (only when Side=Both was used to create them).

OpPropertiesPanel: editing Plug Height or Gap on either op updates *both* in the pair (they're geometrically linked).

## Tests

- `inlay.rs::tests`:
  - For a 50×30 mm rectangle V-carved with a 60° V-bit, `plug_height = 2 mm`, `gap = 0.1 mm`:
    - Pocket op produces a polyline whose Z floors at `-2 mm`.
    - Plug op produces a polyline 0.1 mm smaller per side (assert via bbox).
    - The two ops together would mathematically nest with 0.1 mm gap on every wall (assert by sampling).
- Integration: project save/load of a Both-side inlay preserves the linkage between the two ops.
- Manual: cut the pair on real material (oak base, walnut plug — the canonical demo). Sand flush, photograph for the docs.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by `wiaconstructor-rt1.1`** (V-Carve). Inlay is a thin wrapper on top.

## Time budget

- 1-2 weeks once V-Carve lands. Most of the effort is in UI ergonomics, not algorithm.

## Open questions

- "Pour-fill" inlay: instead of a wood plug, the user pours epoxy into the pocket. In that case `gap_mm` is irrelevant — just need the pocket. Should "Pour" be a third value of `InlaySide`, or just "Pocket" with a docs note? Probably the latter; flag in user guide.
- Multiple disjoint regions in one drawing: do we generate one big plug board with all plugs, or split? v1 = single board with all plugs at original positions; user trims by hand. Sufficient.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `OperationKind::Inlay` round-trips in project JSON.
- [ ] Pocket and Plug ops produce mathematically-mating geometry (unit tested).
- [ ] InlayDialog supports Pocket / Plug / Both modes.
- [ ] Editing one half of a "Both" pair updates both consistently.

title: Per-tool default Z step + override fallback
description:
## What

Let the tool library carry a default depth-per-pass (Z step), and have operations fall back to that default when they don't specify their own. Estlcam stores DPP per tool because it's a property of the cutter+material combination, not of the operation. This makes the wiac tool library actually *useful* as a reusable library — pick a tool, and step / xy_overlap auto-fill from sensible defaults.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **CHANGE** `ToolEntry` (`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:43`): add `default_step: Option<f64>` (= depth-per-pass default; negative or zero number, mm). None = no default.
- **CHANGE** `OperationParams.step` (`project.rs:333`): from `f64` to `Option<f64>`. None = "use the tool's `default_step`; if that's also None, error with `step_unspecified`".
- **CHANGE — schema-breaking but with serde compat**: existing `*.vc-project.json` files have `step: -1.0` as a bare number. Add a serde transform that accepts both bare-number and null/absent forms. New writes prefer null when the value matches the tool's default (so the project JSON stays clean). Pure additive on `ToolEntry`; the only friction is on `OperationParams.step`.
- **No replacements**.

## Implementation

### Core schema (`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs`)

```rust
// ToolEntry — add field
pub struct ToolEntry {
    // … existing fields …
    /// Default depth-per-pass for ops using this tool. None = ops must
    /// specify their own step. Always negative (depth, not height).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub default_step: Option<f64>,
}

// OperationParams — change step type
pub struct OperationParams {
    // … other fields …
    /// Per-pass Z step. None = inherit from the assigned tool's
    /// `default_step`. If both are None, the op fails to emit with a
    /// `step_unspecified` warning.
    #[serde(default, deserialize_with = "deserialize_optional_step",
            skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub step: Option<f64>,
}

fn deserialize_optional_step<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<f64>, D::Error>
where D: serde::Deserializer<'de>
{
    // Accept null, missing, or a bare number.
    // Bare 0.0 → None (legacy "use default" sentinel).
    // Any other number → Some(n).
    // …
}
```

### Resolution helper (`crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs`, near top)

```rust
/// Resolve the effective per-pass Z step for an op, honoring the
/// op-level override → tool default fallback. Errors with
/// `step_unspecified` if neither is set.
pub(crate) fn effective_step(
    op: &Operation,
    tool: &ToolEntry,
) -> Result<f64, Warning> {
    op.params
        .step
        .or(tool.default_step)
        .filter(|v| *v < 0.0)  // must be negative (depth)
        .ok_or_else(|| Warning {
            kind: "step_unspecified".into(),
            // …
        })
}
```

### Call-site migration

`grep -nE "op\.params\.step|params\.step" crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs` and route every read through `effective_step`. The compile error after changing the type to `Option<f64>` will surface every site mechanically — no manual hunt.

### G-code emitters (`crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/*.rs`)

Same migration: any place that reads `op.params.step` directly switches to using the resolved value passed down from the pipeline.

## UI

### `frontend/src/lib/components/ToolLibraryDialog.svelte`

- Add a "Default Z step" number input, next to plunge/feed rates.
- Tooltip: "Operations using this tool inherit this when they don't specify their own. Negative number, mm."
- Empty input = `None`. Validate: must be < 0.

### `frontend/src/lib/components/OpPropertiesPanel.svelte`

- The existing `step` input changes from "always required" to "optional".
- When the op's step is unset (None) and the assigned tool has a `default_step`:
  - Show a placeholder in italic: `-0.5 (from tool)` (with the actual tool value).
  - Add a small "(reset to inherit)" link next to the input that nulls out the override.
- When unset and the tool also has none:
  - Show a red error chip: "Step required (set per-op or in the tool library)."

### Schema migration UX

On project load, any existing project that explicitly stored a `step` in `OperationParams` keeps that value (now wrapped as `Some`). Nothing breaks. The first save after the migration writes the new shape; users notice nothing unless they diff the JSON.

## Tests

- Round-trip: load every `*.vc-project.json` fixture in the repo, assert no errors. The serde compat shim is the riskiest piece; this catches it.
- Resolution unit tests:
  - `step` set, `default_step` set → uses `step`.
  - `step` unset, `default_step` set → uses `default_step`.
  - Both unset → returns `step_unspecified`.
  - `step = 0.0` (legacy zero-sentinel) deserializes to None.
- UI snapshot: a tool with `default_step` and an op without step shows the italic placeholder.
- G-code emit smoke: pipeline emits the same G-code for `(step=Some(-0.5), default_step=None)` and `(step=None, default_step=Some(-0.5))` given the same tool — i.e. resolution is transparent to the output.

## Time budget

- 3–5 days. The migration shim is the only fiddly piece; everything else is plumbing. Half a day in the UI.

## Open questions

- Should `xy_overlap` (`OperationParams.xy_overlap`) get the same per-tool-default treatment? Probably yes — same reasoning. File a follow-up issue once this lands; don't bundle, the change pattern repeats and the review is cleaner one-at-a-time.
- Should `feed_rate_override` and `plunge_rate_override` (already `Option<u32>`) get a UI hint when the op is using the tool's value? Yes; small follow-up.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `ToolEntry.default_step` round-trips.
- [ ] `OperationParams.step` accepts None / null / absent / bare-number-zero / bare-number-negative — all the listed cases.
- [ ] Existing project fixtures load unchanged.
- [ ] UI placeholder + error states render correctly.
- [ ] Resolution unit tests pass.
- [ ] G-code output is byte-identical when the value is set on the op vs. inherited from the tool (with the same number).
acceptance_criteria: ToolEntry.default_step round-trips; OperationParams.step accepts all listed legacy/null/number forms; existing fixtures load unchanged; UI placeholder+error render; resolution tests pass; G-code byte-identical when inherited vs explicit.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add Text dialog with CAM-style picker
description:
## What

A single-dialog flow for "add text to the project and turn it into a CAM op of style X". Estlcam users get this in one click; in wiac today they have to: (1) figure out how to import text, (2) manually create an op of the right kind, (3) wire its source to the text. This consolidates the workflow.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** the frontend with a new dialog and an "Add Text" toolbar entry.
- **No core changes.** The backend already has `render_text` (`crates/wiac-core/src/input/text.rs:125`), single-line-font detection (`is_single_line_font`, line 205), and all the OperationKinds we need (Profile, Pocket, Engrave, VCarve from Child 1, plus the Pocket-Outside wrapper from Child 5).
- **No replacements.** The current "import a DXF/SVG containing text" path stays untouched.

## What gets built

### New component `frontend/src/lib/components/AddTextDialog.svelte`

Fields (Svelte form, validated on input):

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | textarea (multiline) | `"Text"` |
| `font` | file picker + bundled-font dropdown | bundled "Inter" or first user font |
| `size_mm` | number | 12 |
| `position` | (number, number) | center of stock |
| `style` | radio group (8 options — see below) | "Engraving" |
| `tool_id` | dropdown sourced from project tools | first matching tool for the picked style |
| `depth` | number | style-dependent default |

Style picker — eight options matching what Estlcam users expect:

| Style | What gets created |
|---|---|
| **Engraving** | one `OperationKind::Engrave` op on the rendered single-line/centerline. If the chosen font is filled-outline, show "use a single-line font" warning chip with a one-click "switch to bundled engraving font" button. |
| **Carve Inside** | one `OperationKind::VCarve` op (Child 1) with the text contours as the closed region. Default tool: V-bit. |
| **Carve Outside** | renders the text + a frame (`text_bbox + 3 × tool_diameter` padding). Creates a VCarve op on the *difference* (frame − text outlines) via `SourceCombine::Difference`. Default tool: V-bit. |
| **Pocket Inside** | one `OperationKind::Pocket` op per closed letter region. Multi-letter texts batch into one op via `SourceCombine::Auto`. Default tool: small endmill. |
| **Pocket Outside** | delegates to Child 5's Pocket-Outside helper. Default tool: small endmill. |
| **Outline Inside** | `OperationKind::Profile { offset: ToolOffset::Inside }`. |
| **Outline Outside** | `OperationKind::Profile { offset: ToolOffset::Outside }`. |
| **Plain (no op)** | adds the text segments to the geometry layer only. Equivalent to Estlcam's "Layer" style — useful when the user wants to edit the text before assigning a CAM op. |

Style-dependent defaults for `depth`:
- Engraving: `-0.5`
- Carve Inside / Carve Outside: `-3.0` (V-bit auto-clamp will reduce)
- Pocket Inside / Pocket Outside: `-2.0`
- Outline Inside / Outside: `-2.0`
- Plain: N/A

Default-tool resolution (when the user has more than one of a kind in the project tool table): pick the first by id whose `kind` matches the style's required kind. If there's no matching tool, prompt "no V-bit in your tool library — add one?" with a deep link to the Tool Library dialog.

### Bundled fonts

Place under `frontend/public/fonts/`:

- One filled-outline TTF for outline/carve/pocket styles (OFL-licensed, e.g. *Inter* or *Source Sans*).
- One single-line / engraving TTF for Engraving style. Hershey-Sans port (public domain) or *0xPro Stick* (OFL).

Plus support for OS-installed fonts via the existing file-picker.

### Toolbar wire-up

`frontend/src/App.svelte` toolbar:

- New button: **"Add Text"** with a pen-on-paper icon.
- Keyboard shortcut: `T` (when no text input is focused).
- Opens `AddTextDialog`.

### Transactional behavior

Adding the text + the op(s) must be a single undoable action. If the project state already supports compound undo (check with the Svelte state container), wrap the dialog's `Apply` handler in a `beginTransaction` / `commit`. If not, file a follow-up issue and ship the simpler "two-step undo" version with a comment noting the gap.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Add Text` button visible on toolbar.
- [ ] Each of the 8 styles produces the expected geometry + op state. Snapshot-test the resulting project JSON for each.
- [ ] Style switching on an existing text-driven op (via OpPropertiesPanel — out of scope for v1) is filed as a follow-up.
- [ ] Single-line font detection drives the warning chip on the Engraving style with a non-engraving font.
- [ ] At least 2 bundled fonts ship with the build.
- [ ] Documented in `frontend/src/lib/components/AddTextDialog.svelte` JSDoc + a short user guide section.

## Time budget

- 1–2 weeks. Mostly Svelte dialog plumbing + the style→op mapping + bundling fonts.
- **Dependencies**: Child 1 (V-Carve) for Carve styles; Child 5 (Pocket Outside) for that style. Other styles don't need them and can ship independently — implement Engraving + Outline + Plain first, then add Pocket / Carve as the children land.

## Open questions

- Bundled font location: `frontend/public/fonts/` shipped as static assets vs. user's `~/.fonts` for variety. Probably both — bundle a sane minimum, allow user-load. File license-vetting follow-up.
- Multi-letter texts where letters touch (kerning into overlap): `SourceCombine::Auto` handles this for Pocket Inside, but Carve Inside on overlapping letters needs a union pass first. Spike — likely cheap.
acceptance_criteria: Add Text button in toolbar; 8 styles each produce expected geometry+op snapshot; single-line font detection drives warning chip; 2 bundled fonts ship; documented.

title: Trochoidal pocket strategy (load-limiting)
description:
## What

A new pocket strategy that walks the cutter along the pocket centerline while looping repeatedly to keep radial engagement bounded. Used for stock removal in hard materials (aluminum, steel) on hobby-rigidity machines where a Spiral or Cascade pocket would chatter or break the bit.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **EXTEND** `PocketStrategy` (`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:234`) with a new variant `Trochoidal { engagement_angle_deg: f64, loop_radius_factor: f64 }`. Existing Cascade / Zigzag / Spiral are unchanged.
- **EXTEND** `pocket_for_object` (`crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:524`) with a new match arm.
- **No replacements.**

## Algorithm — implement in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/trochoidal.rs` (new file)

Trochoidal milling holds radial engagement constant by walking small circular loops along a centerline. For an *area* pocket we adapt the technique:

### Step 1: Centerline from cascade rings

Reuse `pocket_cascade_with_islands` (`offsets.rs:287`) to produce concentric inward offsets at spacing:

```
step_main = tool_diameter * (1 - main_overlap)
main_overlap = 1 - sin(engagement_angle_deg / 2)
```

For the default `engagement_angle_deg = 30°`: `main_overlap ≈ 0.74`, i.e. very tight ring spacing. That's intentional — trochoidal trades stepover for engagement control.

### Step 2: Stitch rings into a centerline polyline

Reuse the stitching logic from `stitch_rings_to_spiral` (`offsets.rs` ~line 595) but **return the stitched point sequence P_0 … P_N rather than emitting it directly**. The outer ring's start point seeds the walk, each subsequent ring's start is rotated to be nearest the previous ring's end (smallest bridge segment).

### Step 3: Emit the trochoidal motion along the centerline

For each pair (P_i, P_{i+1}) along the centerline, emit a small loop:

```
r_loop = tool_radius * loop_radius_factor      // default 0.6
direction_normal = unit_normal(P_i → P_{i+1}, side opposite to engagement)
loop_center = P_{i+1} + r_loop * direction_normal
```

The motion shape per centerline step:

1. G1 from current pos to a tangent-entry point on the loop circle (small bridge).
2. G2/G3 arc 270°–300° around `loop_center` (CCW for climb, CW for conventional). Don't close the full 360° — overlap with the next loop's entry.
3. G1 to P_{i+2} bridge (or directly to next loop entry).

The exact arc angle is determined by tangency at entry/exit so the path stays smooth (no sharp G1 turns inside the cutter's working envelope).

### Step 4: Handle approach + retreat

- Lead-in: **force PlungeStrategy::Helix**. If user picked Direct/Ramp on a Trochoidal pocket, override to Helix and emit a `plunge_overridden` warning. Trochoidal exists to protect bits; a straight plunge defeats the purpose.
- Lead-out: simple G1 retract along the last loop's tangent to safe Z.
- **Tabs are not supported in v1.** If `op.params.tabs.active && strategy == Trochoidal`, emit a `tabs_with_trochoidal_unsupported` warning and ignore tabs. File follow-up.

### Step 5: Cut direction

`cut_direction` controls the loop direction (CCW = climb, CW = conventional). `finish_cut_direction` is irrelevant here (no separate finish ring); skip it.

## UI

`frontend/src/lib/components/OpPropertiesPanel.svelte` (~line 506 — pocket-strategy `<select>`):

- Add `<option value="trochoidal">Trochoidal (load-limiting)</option>`.
- When selected, expose two inputs:
  - `engagement_angle_deg` — slider 5–90°, default 30°. Tooltip: "Smaller = lighter cut, more loops, slower; larger = heavier cut, fewer loops, faster. 30° is the standard recommendation for aluminum on a hobby mill."
  - `loop_radius_factor` — slider 0.3–1.0, default 0.6. Tooltip: "Loop size as a fraction of tool radius. 0.6 is a balanced default."
- **Inline warnings** (chips, same style as existing `tool_kind_mismatch`):
  - If `cut_direction == Conventional`: "Trochoidal usually pairs with climb."
  - If `plunge.kind != Helix`: "Trochoidal will override plunge to Helix."
  - If `tabs.active`: "Tabs ignored on trochoidal pockets."

## Tests

- For a 100×60 mm rect pocket with 6 mm endmill, `engagement_angle_deg=30°`, `loop_radius_factor=0.6`:
  1. Emitted toolpath covers the full pocket interior (assert union of cutter envelope ≥ 99% of region area, modulo edge tolerance).
  2. Every emitted G2/G3 arc has radius `r_loop ≈ 1.8 mm` (= 3 mm × 0.6) within 0.05 mm.
  3. Total path length is between 1.0× and 1.4× the equivalent Spiral pocket.
- For an L-shaped pocket: trochoidal still produces a connected toolpath without crossing pocket walls. Re-use the wall-crossing checker from `stitch_rings_to_spiral`'s containment guard.
- Pipeline integration test: the `tabs_with_trochoidal_unsupported` warning fires when both are configured.
- Manual: cut a 60×40×3 mm pocket in 6061-T6 aluminum with the wiac defaults, 6 mm 3-flute, 18000 RPM, 1 mm DOC. Should complete without bit breakage.

## Time budget

- 3-4 weeks. Most of that is *correctness validation*, not coding. The algorithm is ~400 LOC; the rest is tuning defaults so the out-of-the-box experience produces good cuts.

## Open questions

- At concave boundaries, the chord between consecutive centerline points can be much longer than `step_main` — degenerate loop placement. Spike: render the path on a U-shape pocket and inspect; if chord-length > 2 × step_main, subdivide before placing the loop.
- Expose `main_overlap` directly *instead of* `engagement_angle_deg`, *as well as*, or compute it silently? Engagement-angle is the term toolmakers' charts use; overlap is what wiac speaks elsewhere. Pick engagement-angle as the canonical input, expose overlap as a derived read-only display.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `PocketStrategy::Trochoidal` round-trips in project JSON.
- [ ] Unit tests above pass.
- [ ] Manual aluminum cut completes.
- [ ] Three warning chips render correctly in the UI under the conditions above.
- [ ] Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/trochoidal.rs` module docs.
acceptance_criteria: PocketStrategy::Trochoidal round-trips; loop-radius/coverage/length unit tests pass; aluminum cut completes; 3 warning chips render; documented.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 30c5da9. Backend: PocketStrategy::Trochoidal variant, new cam/trochoidal.rs module, pipeline routing + plunge override + tabs warning. Frontend: 'trochoidal' option in pocket strategy select, engagement angle / loop radius sliders, inline warning chips. 8 new tests pass (140/142 wiac-core lib tests pass; the 2 fails are pre-existing DXF fixture path issues unrelated to this work). Frontend npm build succeeds. svelte-check has 2 pre-existing type errors (dwell_sec optionality + wasm Simulator missing) that exist before and after these changes.

title: Pocket-Outside (frame around selection)
description:
## What

Pocket the area *between* a frame and a selection — useful for "raised text" plaques, signs where the text and graphics are the high parts and the surrounding area gets removed. Estlcam users expect this as a single click; today in wiac it's a manual "create a frame VcObject + create a Pocket op with `SourceCombine::Difference`" dance.

## Replace / Change / Extend

- **No core changes.** Uses existing `OperationKind::Pocket` + `SourceCombine::Difference` (`crates/wiac-core/src/project.rs:283`).
- **EXTEND** the frontend with a frame-generator helper + an "Add Pocket Outside" entry in the operations list.
- **No replacements.**

## What gets built

### Frame helper (frontend or backend, see below)

Given a list of selected `VcObject` ids, generate an outer boundary at `bbox(selection) + padding`, in one of these shapes:

| Shape | Parameters |
|---|---|
| Rectangle | padding_mm |
| Rounded rectangle | padding_mm, corner_radius_mm |
| Oval | padding_mm |
| Tight outline | padding_mm; uses the convex hull of the selection then offsets outward |

For v1 ship Rectangle and Rounded Rectangle. Defer Oval and Tight outline to follow-ups (file them when this issue closes).

Default values:
- `padding_mm = 3 * tool_diameter`
- `corner_radius_mm = padding_mm` (pleasant default; gives a stadium shape on small selections)

**Where the helper lives**: implement in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/source_combine.rs` (it's already there for Auto / Union / Difference plumbing) as `pub fn build_frame(selection: &[&VcObject], shape: FrameShape, padding_mm: f64) -> VcObject`. Frontend calls it via a new `WiacClient.build_frame` JSON-RPC method. Putting it in core means CLI / WASM / Tauri all share it, and snapshot tests are easy.

### Operation wrapper

When the user picks "Pocket Outside" (from the Add Operation menu, or from Child 4's text dialog):

1. Call `build_frame` on the current selection with default shape + padding. Add the frame as a new `VcObject` on a layer named `Frame_<n>` (auto-numbered). Layer color: a dim cyan, distinct from cut layers.
2. Create a `Pocket` op with:
   - `tool_id`: project's first endmill (or whatever the dialog picked).
   - `source: OperationSource::Objects { ids: [frame_id, *selection_ids], combine: SourceCombine::Difference }`. The frame is first; everything else is subtracted.
   - `params`: `OperationParams::mill_default()` with `pocket_islands = true` so islands are honored.
3. The frame's parameters (shape, padding, corner radius) live on the Pocket op itself so editing them re-runs `build_frame` and the Pocket op auto-recomputes. Add fields `OperationParams.frame_shape: Option<FrameShape>` and `OperationParams.frame_padding_mm: Option<f64>` (and `frame_corner_radius_mm`) — present only for Pocket ops generated by this wrapper.

### UI

`frontend/src/lib/components/OperationsList.svelte` — under the existing "Add Operation" menu, add an entry **"Pocket Outside"**. Disabled when no selection. Clicking runs the wrapper above on the current 2D-canvas selection.

`frontend/src/lib/components/OpPropertiesPanel.svelte` — when the op was created via the wrapper (detect by `op.params.frame_shape.is_some()`), show three extra inputs in a "Frame" sub-section:

- Shape: dropdown (Rectangle / Rounded Rectangle).
- Padding: number_mm, default `3 × tool_diameter` (auto-recomputes when tool changes if the user hasn't manually edited the padding).
- Corner radius: number_mm, only visible for Rounded Rectangle.

Editing any of those calls `build_frame` again and replaces the existing frame VcObject in-place (preserves its id and layer).

`frontend/src/lib/components/EntityCanvas2D.svelte` — render frame layers in the dim cyan above. Hover over the frame: tooltip "Frame for op #N — edit in op properties".

## Tests

- `source_combine.rs::tests`: `build_frame(rect_shape, pad=10mm, [single_obj_at_origin_10x10])` → a 30×30 mm rect VcObject centered at the origin.
- Pipeline integration: a project with a text-rendered "OK" + a Pocket-Outside op produces a toolpath whose XY footprint covers `frame_bbox − text_glyph_unions`, and only that region.
- Snapshot: round-trip a project containing a frame-driven Pocket op preserves the frame fields.
- Manual: in the UI, select an imported logo, click "Pocket Outside", expect a frame drawn around it and the pocket op shown in the operations list.

## Time budget

- 1 week. The hardest part is the wire-up so `build_frame` re-runs on edits without leaving stale frame VcObjects.
- **Dependencies**: none. Can ship before any other child issue.

## Open questions

- Should the frame VcObject be hidden in the LayerList (it's an output of an op, not user geometry) or shown there as a manageable layer? Probably show but mark as auto-managed (italic name, lock icon). Decide in spike.
- Multi-op-frame share: if two Pocket-Outside ops select the same geometry, do they share one frame or get two? v1 = two (simpler); single-frame sharing is a follow-up.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `build_frame` exposed and unit-tested in core.
- [ ] "Pocket Outside" entry in Operations List wires up the frame + op.
- [ ] Frame fields editable in OpPropertiesPanel; edits regenerate the frame.
- [ ] 2D canvas renders frame layers distinctly.
- [ ] Documented in `crates/wiac-core/src/cam/source_combine.rs` and the user guide.
acceptance_criteria: build_frame exposed and unit-tested; Pocket Outside entry wires up frame+op; frame fields edit-and-regenerate; 2D canvas renders frame distinctly; documented.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ramped tabs only ramp on Line segments; arc tabs use straight Z lift
description:
emit_path_with_tabs (gcode.rs:~1115) handles tab crossings on line segments via the new ramp-up / flat / ramp-down trapezoid (05f). When a tab AABB overlaps an Arc segment, the code falls back to a rectangular Z step regardless of tab_type=Ramp.

The agent that landed 05f explicitly punted arcs to v2 with a code comment. Worth filing for completeness: extend the ramp logic to arcs by parameterizing along arc length and inserting a sub-arc at the ramp Z, OR by approximating the arc with short line segments through the tab and applying the line ramp.

Trade-off: arc tabs are uncommon (boundaries that pass through tabs are usually straight). If the user uses arcs through tabs, they get a step pulse instead of a ramp — works but harsher on the spindle.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pattern expansion clones segments O(n × instances) on every Generate; add a transform cache
description:
apply_pattern_to_segments (pipeline.rs:~310) walks all selected objects' segments for every pattern instance and clones them. For Polar pattern with count=64 + a 1000-segment source = 64k segment mutations on every Generate.

Two-step optimization:
1. Compute the per-instance affine transform ONCE (translate / rotate / center).
2. Build the expanded objects list lazily — store transforms alongside indices into the original segments and apply during emission, not up-front.

Or: implement a simpler 'shared geometry + per-instance transform offset' where pocket_for_object / parallel_offset_inward etc. accept an optional Affine2 and apply at offset time.

Trade-off: pre-expansion is simple and reuses all existing pipeline code unchanged; lazy is faster for big patterns but more invasive.

Severity: low — patterns are user-initiated, big patterns are rare. File for the day someone makes 1000-instance grids of 5000-segment SVGs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Profile lead-in tangent rolls + finishing pass with independent feed/cut-mode
description:
Today Profile leads are Off / Straight / Arc with simple in/out lengths. PyCAM auto-computes a roll-on/roll-off arc tangent to the contour at the entry/exit point so the cutter eases into the cut without dwelling at the start. The roll center is offset perpendicular to the path by tool_radius + a configurable margin.

Wire schema:
- LeadsConfig.in_lenght / out_lenght become RADIUS (when type=Arc) or LENGTH (when type=Straight)
- new LeadsConfig.in_roll_radius (Option<f64>) — auto-computed if None, manual otherwise
- algorithm: take tangent at start point (= first segment direction), construct an arc whose center is perpendicular to the tangent at distance , walk from arc start (tangent-perpendicular offset) into the cut

PyCAM also has a Profile-level finish-pass with separate feed and cut direction — partially covered by our existing finish_cut_direction, but PyCAM additionally lets the user set a separate finish_feed_rate. Worth adding a per-op feedrate override (already filed as 9vr from an earlier session — link).

References: refs/danheeks-pycam/Profile.py auto_roll_radius / roll_on_point / roll_off_point.
close_reason: Closed

title: Custom Z depth schedule (per-pass list, finish-depth, through-depth)
description:
Today Z is depth + step (negative numbers, evenly spaced). PyCAM's depth_params.py exposes:
- step_down (current)
- finish_depth: final pass at a smaller step than the rest (better surface finish on the bottom of the cut)
- through_depth: extend the cut past the material's bottom by this amount (clean through-cuts on edge-clamped sheet)
- depth_list: optional explicit list of Z values (for custom schedules — e.g. shallow first, deeper later)

OperationParams gains finish_step (Option<f64>), through_depth (default 0), and depth_list (Option<Vec<f64>>). multi_pass walks the schedule directly when depth_list is set; otherwise the current step-down loop runs but uses finish_step for the last pass and through_depth as the effective bottom.

Useful for hard materials (slow finish pass), and for pocketing with intentional residue (leave a stock-to-leave shoulder). UI: optional fields next to the existing depth/step inputs.
close_reason:
Custom Z depth schedule shipped:

OperationParams gains:
- finish_step (Option<f64>) — smaller last-pass step for cleaner bottom
- through_depth (f64) — extends total cut by that many mm past depth
- depth_list (Vec<f64>) — explicit ordered Z values; overrides step + finish_step + through_depth when non-empty

MillConfig mirrors all three; pipeline plumbs them into the synthesized setup; multi_pass calls a new build_z_schedule helper that walks the user's depth_list verbatim or computes the step-down sequence from start_depth → (depth - through_depth) with an optional finish-step splice before the final pass.

Tests:
- finish_step_emits_extra_thin_final_pass: depth=-2, step=-1, finish_step=-0.2 → gcode contains Z-1, Z-1.8, Z-2.
- through_depth_extends_final_z: depth=-2, through_depth=0.5 → gcode reaches Z-2.5.
- depth_list_overrides_step_schedule: depth_list=[-0.5,-1.5,-3] → those Zs appear, intermediate step values don't.

UI: 3 new inputs in the Cut fieldset (Finish step / Through depth / Depth list). Depth list takes a comma-separated string and parses to a Vec<f64>; empty clears it.

118 wiac-core lib tests green; svelte-check 0 errors; vite build clean.

title: Real spiral pocket strategy (currently aliased to cascade)
description:
PocketStrategy::Spiral is currently aliased to Cascade in pocket_for_object — same concentric-ring algorithm. PyCAM's area-based spiral generates a true Archimedean spiral: one continuous path that wraps inward at constant radial step. Visually unmistakable and slightly faster than cascade (one continuous cut, no rapid between rings).

Implementation: requires a real spiral generator. clipper2-rust doesn't have one out-of-the-box, but for convex pockets a parametric Archimedean spiral works:
  r(θ) = r_outer - (θ / 2π) * step
sampled around the pocket centroid, with each sample clipped to the boundary polygon.

For non-convex pockets the offset-spiral approach (PyCAM uses libarea / kurve_funcs.py) is needed: walk an offset polyline inward, then linearly bridge the ends of consecutive offsets to form one continuous path. Moderate complexity.

Acceptance: spiral emits ONE PolylineOffset (open) instead of N concentric closed rings. Test that the spiral covers the pocket interior with the configured xy_overlap.
close_reason:
Real spiral pocket strategy: PocketStrategy::Spiral no longer aliases to Cascade. New PocketEmit enum (Cascade / Zigzag / Spiral) replaces the boolean zigzag in pocket_for_object. Spiral builds one continuous open polyline by:

- generating cascade rings (same step from xy_overlap)
- threading them: each ring's start point rotated to the vertex nearest the previous ring's end, walked forward, with a straight bridge segment connecting consecutive rings

Result: ONE PolylineOffset per object instead of N concentric closed rings → cleaner cut, no rapid lift-and-replunge between rings.

Test spiral_emits_one_continuous_polyline_not_concentric_rings: same 50x50 pocket → cascade gives N pocket=2 blocks, spiral gives exactly 1.

CLI + cli tests + offset internal test all updated for the new PocketEmit enum signature. 126 wiac-core lib tests green; cargo check workspace clean.

title: Solid preview UI toggle + stock integration
description:
Wire the heightfield mesh into the existing 3D scene with the new mode toggle, fed by the settings dialog (m1r):

- new project.previewMode rune: 'wireframe' | 'solid' | 'both' (default from settings.previewMode, which itself defaults to 'wireframe' until the sim is dogfooded)
- toggle UI in the sidebar (next to or replacing the Stock summary): three-way pill switch
- 'wireframe' = current behavior (LineSegments toolpath)
- 'solid' = heightfield (semi-transparent + solid edges) only; toolpath lines hidden
- 'both' = heightfield underneath, toolpath lines on top with their existing colors
- the existing translucent stock box (Scene3D's stockGroup) hides when previewMode is solid OR both — the heightfield IS the stock
- when no /generate has run, render a flat unmilled stock heightfield so the toggle is meaningful before the user clicks Generate
- material params (solid color + opacity, edge color + opacity) read from project.settings live, so the dialog updates the mesh without rebuilding the BufferGeometry — just material.color.set / material.opacity = ... and material.needsUpdate=true

Out of scope: animated transitions between modes, per-op preview overrides.
close_reason:
Three-way preview-mode toggle added to the sidebar (App.svelte). 'Wireframe' / 'Solid' / 'Both' pill switch under the Stock panel, only writes through to project.settings.previewMode (already a settings key from m1r) — Scene3D's c28 effects pick up the change and show/hide the heightfield mesh accordingly. Tooltip explains the modes.

Pill style added to the global CSS (rounded inflex buttons, accent fill on the active variant) — same visual language as the existing topbar pickers. svelte-check 0 errors; vite build clean (Scene3D bundle 559 KB).

title: Cache Path2D for region preview between Generates
description:
EntityCanvas2D.drawRegions() walks every region's outer + holes and re-traces each polygon on every redraw (which fires on hover, selection, layer toggle, etc.). For a few large pocket regions with hundreds of tessellated points each, the path-build cost adds up.

Optimization: when project.generated.regions changes, build a Map<op_id, Path2D> once and reuse the Path2D objects on subsequent draws. Invalidate the cache when regions change (or just when project.generated changes — coarser but simpler).

Magnitude: negligible for tiny pockets; visible on multi-thousand-point regions when the user moves the mouse over the canvas.
close_reason:
Path2D cache for region preview in EntityCanvas2D.

Each region's outer + holes are baked into a single Path2D in *data space* (no canvas transform applied). The cache key is reference identity of project.generated.regions — when generate runs, the regions array is replaced and the cache invalidates naturally.

drawRegions now does ctx.save / ctx.transform(scale,0,0,-scale,offX,offY) / ctx.fill(path,'evenodd') / ctx.restore, stamping the data-space paths into canvas space via the transform matrix instead of re-tracing every redraw. The y-flip is folded into the matrix as -scale on the Y axis.

Result: redraws on hover/selection/layer-toggle no longer re-walk the tessellated polygon points — they just hand the cached Path2D to the GPU. svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Theme MutationObserver should diff data-theme value
description:
Scene3D's MutationObserver on documentElement.attributes (filter: ['data-theme']) fires applyTheme() whenever the attribute is *set*, even if the value is unchanged. applyTheme() rebuilds the grid and re-runs rebuildGeometry — non-trivial for big imports.

Optimization: store the previously-seen value and bail when it equals the current one. Same pattern would help EntityCanvas2D's MutationObserver (which calls draw() on every attribute mutation).

Magnitude: only matters when something else flips data-theme rapidly (rarely happens in practice), but it's a cheap guard that makes the MutationObserver feel less of a footgun.
close_reason:
data-theme MutationObserver guards in both Scene3D and EntityCanvas2D.

Each observer now snapshots document.documentElement.dataset.theme on entry, and the callback bails when the post-mutation value matches. applyTheme() / draw() only run when the theme has actually flipped, not on every same-value attribute write.

svelte-check 0 errors.

title: In-place color update for selection in Scene3D
description:
Scene3D.rebuildGeometry() throws away and recreates the entire BufferGeometry whenever project.selectedObjects changes. For a click that toggles one object, that's a full re-tessellation + buffer upload of the whole scene.

Optimization: keep the BufferGeometry persistent; record per-line-pair {start_color_offset, n_pairs, objectId} during the initial build; on selection change, walk the small set of affected pairs and only mutate the color attribute (geom.attributes.color.array) + setNeedsUpdate(true). Geometry rebuilds stay reserved for project.imported / generated / visibleLayers / etc.

Same idea applies to the future 'live machined region' overlay if we ever compute it client-side.
close_reason:
In-place selection update in Scene3D.

rebuildGeometry now records per-object color ranges into objectColorRanges: Map<objectId, ColorRange[]> where each ColorRange is { start, count, base } in the linesObject color attribute. The base color is the non-selected baseline (ACI or faded) so toggles can revert without recomputing.

Split the :
- big rebuild watches imported / visibleLayers / generated / tabs / stock / operations (does full re-tessellation)
- new selection-only $effect watches *just* project.selectedObjects; runs applySelectionDelta() which:
  - paints accent into ranges for newly-selected ids
  - restores base color into ranges for newly-deselected ids
  - sets attr.needsUpdate = true (no buffer reupload of positions)
- snapshot appliedSelection after each rebuild so the next delta computes against the right baseline

Result: clicking an object in 3D no longer re-tessellates every imported segment; it just touches the color triplets for the affected object. svelte-check 0 errors; vite build clean (Scene3D bundle 548KB).

title: UX-11: .vc-project format migration + tests
description: Add a  field to the project file. v1 (legacy) = today's snapshot. v2 = the new Project shape. ProjectState.restore detects the version, runs the legacy→v2 migration via the wiac_core::project::migrate_legacy helper introduced in UX-1. Add round-trip tests with a baked v1 fixture.
close_reason: ProjectFile.version bumped 1→2; restore() leniently accepts v1 files (no operations/tools/machine fields → keep defaults + legacy setup tree). buildProject(state) in lib/api/build-project.ts converts the frontend ProjectState to the wire Project shape (camelCase → snake_case, OpKind tagged enum, OperationParams synthesized from flat OpEntry fields). GenerateBar now sends project.* on the request when project.operations.length > 0; legacy segments+setup path remains for users who haven't migrated. Backend already accepts both shapes via PipelineRequest.project (UX-3). svelte-check + cargo test 60 unit + 8 integration green.

title: UX-10: Color toolpath segments by op_id in 3D
description: Scene3D.rebuildGeometry currently colors by move kind (rapid/cut/plunge/retract/arc). Layer in op_id-based coloring so the user can see each operation's contribution at a glance. Palette derived from a project-wide stable hash of the op id, with the move-kind hue applied as a brightness multiplier.
close_reason: Scene3D rebuildGeometry now derives a per-op base hue from a stable (op_id × golden-ratio-conjugate mod 1) hash and modulates by move kind: cuts get a 1.15× brightness boost, rapids 0.5×, plunges/retracts 0.85×. op_id=0 segments (program-header rapids that aren't part of any operation) keep the legacy single-color palette via cssVar fallback. Played-past segments retain the same op_palette but at full brightness; future segments fade to ~0.25× as before. Renamed gcode::preview::SegmentKind → MoveKind to disambiguate from geometry::SegmentKind in the OpenAPI schema (single 'SegmentKind' was being clobbered).

title: UX-5: Machine settings modal dialog
description: Frontend MachineDialog: opens from toolbar 'Machine…' button. Renders project.machine (post processor, units mm/inch, fast_move_z, supports_toolchange, comments, arcs). Replaces the machine.* fields in the current setup tree. Same persist via .vc-project.
close_reason: Two project-scoped modal dialogs surfaced from the toolbar. project.machine + project.tools added to ProjectState (with snapshot/restore round-trip via .vc-project so selections persist). MachineDialog edits unit/mode/comments/arcs/toolchange/fastMoveZ in a working copy that commits on OK or discards on Cancel/Esc. ToolLibraryDialog renders an inline-editable table (id/name/kind/⌀/tip/flutes/speed/feed/plunge/coolant) with Add and Delete buttons; minimum 1 tool enforced. Both keep parity with the existing setup tree until UX-6/-7 wire the operations list to drive Generate.

title: LayerList: hide layers with zero segments
description: DXF files always carry a Layer 0 in their layer table even when nothing's drawn on it. summarize_layers backfills empty layers from drawing.layers() so the UI shows 'Layer 0 (0)'. Filter count==0 entries out of the panel.
close_reason: LayerList filters layers with segment_count == 0 before rendering, and only shows the panel when at least one layer has segments. The phantom 'Layer 0 (0)' from DXF files where every entity is on a different layer is gone.

title: HPGL/PLT and STL importers
description: The frontend file picker accepts .hpgl/.plt/.stl but the importer only knows .dxf. HPGL is a small subset of plotter pen commands (PU/PD/PA/AA) flattening to LINE+ARC segments; STL parses ASCII or binary triangles and projects to XY for laser/cnc planning (or just the bounding outline). Both feed segments_to_objects so the rest of the pipeline lights up automatically.
close_reason: Won't do as filed — splitting: HPGL/PLT importer dropped on user direction ("HPGL has no widespread use nowadays, we could generate dxf equally well"); STL importer deferred under a fresh issue because the path from triangle mesh to a usable 2D toolpath isn't a straight port of the DXF path and needs design work first.

Updated justfile to drop the 'bridge' target and route refresh-golden via plain python3. Updated tests/golden/refresh.py docstring to point at .venv-golden venv setup. The Tauri @tauri-apps/* modules and the WASM client also split off into their own small chunks via the existing dynamic-import path. description: Write BUILDING.md covering prerequisites (Rust toolchain, Node, platform webview deps), checkout, and the single 'cargo tauri build' command per platform. Include verification steps (run tests, check binary). Aim for users who don't trust prebuilt signed binaries to reproduce them locally.
