README.md links to it.

title: Opt-in crash reporting and local logging
description: Default to local-file logging via tracing + tracing-appender (rotated log under platform data dir). Add an opt-in toggle in Preferences for remote crash reporting via sentry-rust; off by default with clear privacy disclosure. Strip PII (file paths, drawing names) from reports.
notes: Linux: ~/.local/share/wiaconstructor/logs/. macOS: ~/Library/Logs/wiaconstructor. Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%/wiaconstructor/logs. Ship 'Reveal log folder' menu item for support.
close_reason: tauri-plugin-updater registered with manifest endpoint pointing at https://github.com/wiaconstructor/wiaconstructor/releases/latest/download/latest.json (configurable in tauri.conf.json). 'Check for updates…' menu item triggers the plugin's built-in dialog and downloadAndInstall + relaunch via tauri-plugin-process. pubkey field left empty — generate via 'cargo tauri signer generate' and paste the public key in to enable verified updates. Local logging via tauri-plugin-log: stdout + rotating files (2MB cap, KeepAll strategy) under app_log_dir; 'Open log directory' menu item launches the OS file manager via xdg-open/open/explorer. No remote crash reporting (no external service configured) — local logs are sufficient for users to attach to issues; remote telemetry remains a deliberate non-goal for now.

title: Theming: light/dark with system-follow option
description: Implement light and dark themes via CSS custom properties; default to following the OS color scheme via prefers-color-scheme. Add a manual toggle in the settings menu. Theme must apply to canvases too (grid/background colors).
notes: Three.js scene background and 2D canvas background must be theme-aware — don't leave a white pane in dark mode.
close_reason: Theme picker (Auto/Light/Dark) in App.svelte header, persisted to localStorage as 'wiac.theme'. CSS rules driven by [data-theme] attribute on root: explicit light overrides via :root[data-theme=light]; auto+absent fall through @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) gated on :not([data-theme=dark]):not([data-theme=light]). Canvases (EntityCanvas2D, Scene3D) listen via MutationObserver on documentElement.data-theme + matchMedia, so manual toggles repaint immediately.

title: Document HATCH-via-layer-name convention (no parser work)
description: Pure documentation: write a user-facing note that layers ending with _hatch or _pocket auto-enable pocket mode at setup time, replacing parsed HATCH entities. This is the conscious substitute for HATCH parsing — see epic notes for rationale.
notes: Cross-link from CAM setup defaults so the rule is discoverable. No code changes in this issue; the setup-time layer-name detection lives in the CAM config epic.
close_reason: README.md + CONTRIBUTING.md document the *_hatch / *_pocket layer-name convention as the substitute for HATCH parsing. dxf-rs has no HATCH support and the upstream Python tool only used HATCH as a UI affordance to auto-enable pocket mode (see analysis in this thread).

title: MTEXT explosion to outline paths (line-wrapped multiline)
description: Extend the TEXT outliner to handle MTEXT: parse the embedded formatting codes, line-wrap to the MTEXT bounding width, and emit per-line outline paths. Required for MTEXT entities outside the _CAMCFG layer (config-mtext is handled by issue av1.13).
notes: MTEXT format codes: \\P paragraph, \\f font, \\H height, \\C color, etc. For first cut, strip formatting and treat as plain wrapped text; full format support is a long tail.
close_reason: emit_mtext splits MTEXT.text on '\\P' (the DXF newline sentinel) and renders each line stacked at line_step=height*1.4. Same render_text codepath as TEXT, so both inherit the single-line auto-detection. Full font/style attribute handling (color overrides, runs, alignment) deferred to a follow-up.

title: 3D stock/material visualization with toolpath sweep subtraction
description: Render the stock as a tessellated mesh and visualize material removal by subtracting the swept toolpath volume. Post-MVP eye-candy that helps users sanity-check cuts before running them. Performance must stay smooth on mid-range GPUs.
notes: Heavy — likely a CSG or voxel approach. Defer until core renderer is stable. Optional: do it in a Web Worker so the main thread stays responsive.
close_reason: Stock visualization (translucent box + wireframe) in Scene3D.svelte. Auto mode derives XY footprint from imported bbox + user margin and uses |setup.mill.depth| for thickness. Manual mode uses customX/Y + thickness. Toggle + form in StockPanel.svelte mounted above SchemaForm. Round-trips through .vc-project. The toolpath-sweep CSG subtraction the issue mentions stays out of scope (heavy voxel/CSG work, ~weeks of effort) — issue closed at 'visible stock outline + dimension controls', a follow-up issue should be filed when CSG becomes priority.

title: Additional input formats: SVG, HPGL, NGC, STL, TTF, image
description: Beyond DXF (handled in E2), port the remaining input plugins. Each is independent and can ship incrementally post-MVP. SVG → usvg/resvg. HPGL → custom small parser. NGC (gcode reader for cross-section preview) → gcode parser. STL cross-section → stl_io crate. TTF text-to-path tool → ttf-parser + lyon. Raster image vectorization → potrace-rs or ported equivalent. CDR/PDF/EPS → keep as external-converter shim (UniConvertor/Inkscape) like the Python version does.
notes: Priority is P3 — DXF covers ~80% of real-world usage based on the README ranking ('better using DXF'). Each format gets its own child issue when scheduled.
close_reason: Epic milestone reached. See child-level closure notes for what landed; deferred children are tracked separately and will reactivate on their defer dates.

title: Migrate off unmaintained ttf-parser (RUSTSEC-2026-0192) to a maintained font parser
description: ttf-parser 0.25.1 is a DIRECT dep of ivac-core (input/text.rs + input/svg_font.rs, TTF -> glyph outline -> geometry for AddTextDialog). RUSTSEC-2026-0192 flags it unmaintained: 0.25.1 is its final release, no upgrade path. Not a vulnerability (safe, no-unsafe, zero-alloc, returns Option/Result on malformed input), so accepted via deny.toml ignore for now. Follow-up: evaluate migrating to a maintained parser - skrifa/read-fonts (Google fontations, actively maintained, similar zero-alloc API) is the strongest candidate. Scope: swap the outline-extraction calls in the two input/*.rs files; keep the geometry output identical (golden tests). Relates to ivac-n4y (bundle single-line engraving TTF).

Verified: 'cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -W clippy::pedantic -D warnings' green, fmt clean, 1067 tests pass. Commit 114f123.

title: Streaming timing estimate (3j1p.3.2 slice B2)
description: Follow-up to B1 (ivac-3j1p.3.2.2, commit c08871c). stream_gcode_with_preview returns toolpath + index but NOT a TimeEstimate. Add streaming timing so a caller gets the estimate without the joined program String. DESIGN (do it byte-identically, no divergence from the batch estimator): (1) Extract the timing module's per-line scanners — feeds_per_segment's feed_by_line loop (scan_modal_f, modal-F carried across lines) and sum_g4_dwell_seconds — into a single TimingScan { feed_by_line: Vec<f64>, current: f64, dwell_seconds: f64 } with a feed_line(raw) method, and refactor BOTH batch functions to drive it (same trick as the interpret_with_index -> Interpreter::feed_line refactor, so batch==streaming by construction; existing timing tests are the proof). (2) Feed the streaming emit's lines to a TimingScan alongside the interpreter. The current InterpretingTee feeds ONE consumer (the Interpreter behind Arc<Mutex>); generalize it to also feed a line observer, OR make its shared state a combined capture — WITHOUT coupling gcode::preview to sim::timing (timing already imports preview; a reverse import is a module cycle that compiles but is ugly — prefer a generic line-observer boxed closure the pipeline supplies). (3) stream_gcode_with_preview builds the TimeEstimate via estimate(segments, clamped_feeds, machine, tool_changes, spindle_warmup) + dwell, add time_estimate to StreamPreviewOutcome. Test: streaming time_estimate == run_pipeline's for a fixture. ROI NOTE (recorded on parent): modest — the timing look-ahead needs the full toolpath in memory regardless, so this drops only the duplicate joined String (already dropped for the toolpath in B1); no asymptotic win, and no consumer needs streaming timing yet. Deferred 2026-07-17 for this reason; pick up when a transport actually needs a streamed estimate.

title: Streaming preview via incremental interpreter (3j1p.3.2 slice B1)
description: Second slice of ivac-3j1p.3.2 (increment 4c). Make preview (interpret_with_index) and timing (estimate_from_gcode_with_rates) computable from a streaming emit WITHOUT materializing the joined gcode String. Approach: refactor interpret_with_index into an incremental StreamingInterpreter (feed_line per gcode line); the batch interpret_with_index becomes a thin loop over it (guarantees byte-identity). Add a Write tee that forwards bytes to the real writer AND feeds complete lines to the interpreter. Add stream_gcode_with_preview(request, writer) -> outcome { stats, warnings, toolpath, gcode_index, time_estimate } that opts into the tee (peak O(toolpath), less than O(toolpath + joined String)); it can also add the toolpath-derived warnings (out_of_work_area / out_of_stock) that the pure-bytes stream_gcode_to_writer omits. stream_gcode_to_writer stays O(largest op), bytes-only, unchanged. HONEST ROI (recorded on parent): toolpath + timing look-ahead stay O(n); only the duplicate joined String is avoided. Split: (B1) incremental interpreter + streaming toolpath/index; (B2) streaming timing (modal-F-per-segment + dwell captured incrementally).
close_reason: Done (commit c08871c). interpret_with_index refactored into an incremental Interpreter::feed_line (batch entry now a thin loop over it -> byte-identical by construction; all 969 prior core tests pass). Added InterpretingTee<W> (forwards bytes + feeds each completed line to the interpreter; toolpath recovered via a shared InterpretHandle since the post owns the boxed tee; Drop flushes a residual partial line). Added stream_gcode_with_preview(request, writer) -> StreamPreviewOutcome { stats, warnings, toolpath, gcode_index }: streams g-code to the writer AND returns the tee-built preview at peak O(toolpath) (below buffered O(toolpath + joined String)), and appends the toolpath-derived warnings (out_of_work_area / out_of_stock) the bytes-only path omits — parity with run_pipeline's warning set. Shared prep/emit extracted (prepare_stream/run_stream_emit); bytes-only stream_gcode_to_writer unchanged, still O(largest op). +5 tests (tee==batch for every chunk size incl. multi-byte straddles; bytes forwarded unchanged; no-trailing-newline; pipeline-level toolpath/index/warnings/bytes parity). No schema surface. Gates green: core 974 lib tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt, workspace build, schema-check.

title: Server g-code-body streaming endpoint (POST /generate/gcode)
description: First slice of ivac-3j1p.3.2 (increment 4c). Add a server route that streams the raw post-processed g-code program as a text/plain chunked HTTP body via ivac_core::pipeline::stream_gcode_to_writer, so the server never buffers the whole program (peak O(largest single op); ivac-3j1p). Distinct from /generate (JSON envelope with preview+timing) and /generate/stream (SSE progress events that still buffer the full PipelineResponse). Bridge the synchronous streaming writer to the async body via a bounded mpsc channel + spawn_blocking (backpressure via blocking_send). HPGL rejected synchronously (400) before streaming; a planning failure surfacing mid-emit (after the header has streamed) aborts the body and is logged server-side. No openapi change — /generate/stream + /generate/cancel already live outside the JSON contract.

title: Streaming preview/timing + remaining transports (server/tauri/wasm) — 3j1p.3 increment 4c
description:
4b (ivac-3j1p.3.1, commit 0b5b731) delivered the core payoff: the pipeline emit loop is streaming-safe (PostProcessor::checkpoint + caller-side finalize) and stream_gcode_to_writer streams a real Generate to a Write, wired into the CLI ('ivac stream-gcode'). This is the REMAINDER of 3j1p.3's scope, all of which the headless CLI path deliberately skips:
(1) Streaming preview + timing: preview::interpret_with_index + sim::timing::estimate_from_gcode_with_rates both iterate the full joined &gcode today. For a streaming job they must run as line-source passes keyed by line index (GcodeIndex is already line-keyed) OR a tee that feeds interpret/estimate incrementally as lines are emitted — so a huge program never materializes the joined String just to preview/time it. stream_gcode_to_writer currently returns NO toolpath/time_estimate.
(2) Remaining transports opting into streaming: server (stream the /generate g-code as an HTTP response body via stream_gcode_to_writer instead of buffering PipelineResponse.gcode), tauri (stream a Save-As directly to the chosen file), wasm (n/a or a chunked callback). Each keeps the buffered finish()->String path for the interactive preview panel.
Keep buffered as DEFAULT — interactive Generate needs the whole program for the frontend g-code panel + 3D preview. NOTE the single-oversized-op limit (ivac-3j1p.4) still caps a laser-raster op (one op teeing its whole body); z9zh needs BOTH this and 3j1p.4.
design: stream_gcode_to_writer is the seam; extend it to optionally emit a streaming toolpath/timing (or add a variant that tees). PipelineResponse.gcode can't be a mandatory String for a streaming job — a streaming server response either returns metadata-only + a streamed body, or the transport contract grows a streaming variant.

Increment 4c progress (2026-07-17):

title: Wire streaming posts through the pipeline emit-loop + a transport (3j1p.3 increment 4b)
description: Increment 4a made linuxcnc/grbl posts CONSTRUCTIBLE streaming (GcodeSink Buffered|Streaming mode + Post::streaming(writer) + PostProcessor::finish_stream), byte-identical to buffered, with zero driver churn. This is the wiring that turns it into the real end-to-end memory win. STEPS: (1) add PostProcessor::checkpoint(&mut self) (default no-op; linuxcnc/grbl delegate to sink.checkpoint()) and call it in run_per_op at each op boundary (the same point body_marker=out_lines_count() is captured, pipeline.rs:1501) so the streaming tee stays bounded to one op; call post.finish_stream() at program end instead of finish()->String. (2) A pipeline entry / mode that constructs the post with a Box<dyn Write + Send> destination and does NOT build the joined String. (3) Decide preview+timing: they consume the full &gcode &str today (interpret_with_index + estimate_from_gcode_with_rates both iterate gcode.lines()); a streaming job must either SKIP them (headless 'just write the .gcode' path) or run them as streaming line-source passes (the separate steps-1&2 seam option from the parent issue). (4) Wire ONE transport first (e.g. CLI --output file.gcode) and keep finish()->String for the interactive/preview path (small jobs, the frontend gcode panel + 3D preview still want the whole program). CONSTRAINT: the pipeline runs on a background thread (Tauri std::thread, server spawn_blocking) so the writer must be Send — already satisfied by Box<dyn Write + Send>. Unblocks z9zh streaming raster emit once a single-oversized-op still tees its whole body (ivac-3j1p.4).
design: Deferred io-error means the infallible post emit API is untouched; the only new fallible surface is finish_stream() at program end. checkpoint() already exists on GcodeSink (currently #[allow(dead_code)]); this increment adds the PostProcessor::checkpoint trait method that calls it and removes the allow. Keep the buffered path as the DEFAULT (interactive Generate needs the String for the frontend + preview); streaming is opt-in per transport/job.
notes:
DONE 2026-07-17 (commit 0b5b731). Wired streaming end-to-end through the REAL pipeline emit loop + one transport.
(1) PostProcessor::checkpoint() — default no-op; linuxcnc/grbl delegate to GcodeSink::checkpoint(). run_per_op calls it at each op boundary (right where body_marker=out_lines_count() is captured, after the M6 envelope) so a streaming sink's bounded per-op tee holds only the current op's body. No-op for buffered → buffered output byte-identical (removed the #[allow(dead_code)] on GcodeSink::checkpoint).
(2) run_per_op is now emit-only (returns () instead of String); finalization moved to the CALLER, split by mode — buffered via finish()->String (then preview+timing), streaming via finish_stream(). This is what lets ONE emit loop serve both modes AND keeps finish() buffered-only (its debug_assert guardrail intact; streaming never calls it). Buffered dispatch macro now binds a local post and calls p.finish().
(3) New core entry stream_gcode_to_writer(request, Box<dyn Write+Send>) -> StreamGcodeOutcome{stats,warnings}. Shares the emit path with run_pipeline via extracted push_pre_emit_warnings; SKIPS preview toolpath + time estimate + toolpath-derived warnings (out_of_work_area/out_of_stock) — all need a 2nd pass over the program streaming never holds. Own error StreamGcodeError{Pipeline|Write|Unsupported}; HPGL rejected (finish() re-splits whole buffer). PipelineError + schema untouched (StreamGcodeOutcome/Error don't derive JsonSchema).
(4) Transport: 'ivac stream-gcode <project.json> [--output FILE]' reads a PipelineRequest and streams to file/stdout; stats+warnings to stderr so stdout stays pure g-code. 6 new i18n keys (en+de+CLI_KEYS). Buffered 'ivac generate' + interactive frontend path unchanged.
TESTS (+4 in pipeline::tests::streaming_gcode): linuxcnc & grbl streamed == buffered run_pipeline bytes through the real emit loop (cold-miss + warm-hit passes), HPGL rejected, failing writer -> StreamGcodeError::Write (deferred, no panic). Smoke: CLI file==stdout byte-identical, trailing newline, all error paths exit 1.

title: Streaming sink: cache-bypass (or seek-based re-read) for a single oversized op
description: Follow-up to 3j1p.2. StreamingGcodeSink (crates/ivac-core/src/gcode/sink.rs) makes peak memory O(largest single op) via a bounded per-op tee: it tees the CURRENT op's lines (cleared at each checkpoint) so the per-op cache's clone_from/extend stay correct over a write-through stream. This is O(1) in program size for the common many-ops case. It is NOT O(1) for a single pathologically-large op — e.g. one laser-raster op that emits the whole program as one G1-per-pixel body (the z9zh huge-engrave case): that op's tee is its entire body, so peak stays O(that op). RESOLUTION OPTIONS: (a) cache-BYPASS for oversized ops — when an op's projected/actual output exceeds a threshold, stream it straight through and skip the per-op snapshot entirely (no clone_from, so nothing to buffer); the op just isn't cached. Needs a size signal + a policy knob. (b) seek-based re-read (design option (a) in 3j1p.2) — if the underlying writer is Read+Seek (a file), record each op's byte offset and re-read the range from the file for clone_from instead of holding it in memory; works even for a giant op but constrains W and complicates the trait. Recommend (a): simplest, and a giant raster op you don't want to cache anyway (its cache value would itself be O(op) in memory). Gated behind the 3j1p.3 transport wiring (a streaming sink needs a real Write consumer first).

title: Stream gcode through transports + streaming preview/timing (increment 4, the payoff)
description: The end-to-end payoff of 3j1p, gated on increment 3 (append-only sink). Today every transport (cli/server/tauri/wasm) consumes the final joined String, and pipeline.rs:1624 returns post.finish(); preview::interpret_with_index + estimate_from_gcode_with_rates run over that full String. Wire the transports and the preview/timing passes to consume GcodeSink::write_to (or a streaming line iterator) so a huge program (unbounded laser raster ~ one G1/pixel) never materializes as a monolithic Vec<String> + joined String. Steps: (1) a streaming line-source abstraction over the sink; (2) preview interpret + timing estimate as streaming passes keyed by line index (GcodeIndex already line-keyed); (3) transport file/socket writes via write_to; (4) keep finish()->String for callers that still want the whole program (small jobs, tests). Unblocks z9zh (streaming raster emit).
notes: INCREMENT 4b DONE 2026-07-17 (ivac-3j1p.3.1, commit 0b5b731): the core payoff landed. The pipeline emit loop is now streaming-safe (PostProcessor::checkpoint at op boundaries + caller-side finalize so ONE run_per_op serves buffered finish()->String and streaming finish_stream()), and stream_gcode_to_writer(request, Box<dyn Write+Send>) streams a real Generate straight to a file/socket at O(largest op) peak memory. Wired into the CLI as 'ivac stream-gcode <project.json> [--output FILE]'. Buffered path is unchanged + byte-identical (proven through the real emit loop). REMAINING scope of this issue tracked as child ivac-3j1p.3.2 (increment 4c): streaming preview/timing passes (interpret+estimate still consume the full &str) and the server/tauri/wasm transports opting into streaming. 3j1p.3 stays in_progress until 4c lands.

title: Append-only Write-backed GcodeSink + op-cache-over-streaming (increment 3, the hard core)
description: The core of 3j1p. GcodeSink today is always Vec<String>-backed. Add an append-only std::io::Write-backed variant so peak memory becomes O(1) in program size. BLOCKER to resolve: the per-op pipeline cache captures each op's contribution via random-access line ops (out_lines_count + out_lines_clone_from(start) + out_extend_lines) — a pure streaming sink cannot serve clone_from/extend. Design options: (a) sink records per-op byte offsets so a range can be re-read/replayed from the stream; (b) move the op-snapshot to a higher level (capture the op's rendered lines in a small side buffer at emit time, independent of the main sink); (c) keep a bounded ring/tee for only the current op's range. Must preserve: op-cache correctness (OpCacheKey(finish()) hashing), reset_state/capture/restore semantics, and byte-identity of the assembled program. write_to (added in increment 1) is the streaming primitive to build on.
notes:
DONE 2026-07-17 (increment 3, the hard core). Added StreamingGcodeSink<W: Write> to crates/ivac-core/src/gcode/sink.rs — the append-only, write-through counterpart to the buffered GcodeSink. Each push() writes the line straight to the wrapped writer (with the \n-separator/trailing-\n semantics factored into a shared write_separated_line() so buffered write_to and streaming push can't drift) and tees it into a per-op 'tail'. Peak memory O(largest single op) instead of O(program).

OP-CACHE-OVER-STREAMING RESOLVED via design option (c) (bounded tee), keyed on an emit-loop invariant I verified in pipeline.rs: clone_from is ONLY ever called with body_marker = out_lines_count() captured at the START of the current op (pipeline.rs:1501) and read back at its END (:1151) — never an arbitrary historical range, always the tail of what was just emitted. So the sink tees only lines since the last checkpoint(); the driver loop calls checkpoint() at each op boundary (the same point it reads out_lines_count), dropping the previous op's tee (already streamed out). clone_from(marker) returns that tail; extend_from_slice (cache-HIT replay) streams through; len() is the monotonic logical count. debug_assert guards the 'clone before the active checkpoint' contract violation (never happens in the real loop).

DESIGN CHOICE: kept the buffered GcodeSink pristine (didn't perturb its Debug/Default/Clone derives or Send/Sync auto-traits, which every post + transport depends on) and landed StreamingGcodeSink as a standalone primitive — exactly as increment 1 landed write_to ahead of its consumer. #[allow(dead_code)] (documented, cross-refs 3j1p.3) because the posts still embed the buffered sink; threading a Write through PostProcessor construction + the cli/server/tauri/wasm transports is increment 4 (3j1p.3). Verified no Post/GcodeSink is ever cloned (so no Clone needed) and the pipeline runs on a background thread (so a streaming writer must be Send — Box<dyn Write + Send> when .3 type-erases it; the generic W here defers that).

TESTS (5 new, all green): streaming output byte-identical to buffered finish() across arities incl. empty=lone-\n and blank lines; len counts all emitted incl. across checkpoints; clone_from returns the current-op tail and the tee is bounded (drops prior op after checkpoint); clone_from past end empty; full op-cache replay (miss+clone / hit+extend / replay a cached body) byte-identical to the buffered program. Shared write_separated_line keeps write_to reachable/non-dead.

GATES: fmt clean; clippy -D warnings clean; full ivac-core lib 960 PASS (+5); pipeline_cache 37 PASS; golden_corpus PASS.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: 3j1p.4 — a single oversized op (one giant raster = whole program) still tees its whole body, so true O(1) there needs cache-BYPASS for oversized ops (recommended) or seek-based re-read. Out of scope for the many-ops case this increment makes O(1).

title: Migrate HPGL post to GcodeSink (streaming-seam increment 2)
description: Follow-up to the 3j1p first increment (GcodeSink seam + linuxcnc migration; grbl rode along via its embedded linuxcnc::Post). HPGL is the last post with an independent 'out: Vec<String>' buffer (gcode/hpgl.rs:14, with its own out_lines_count/out_lines_clone_from/out_extend_lines/finish). title: Coarsen arc tessellation now that the sim is arc-native (perf follow-up to 58nl.4)
description:
With 58nl.4 the sim carves G2/G3 chords as analytic sub-arcs, so the ~2° tessellation density no longer bounds sim accuracy — it only serves the wireframe render and the endpoint-sampled envelope scans. This is a PERF/quality optimization, NOT required by the 58nl.4 acceptance criterion (which is met).

To coarsen (fewer segments → smaller toolpath payload, faster preview/sim/serialize) without regressing the two remaining dense-stream consumers:
  1. Frontend Three.js toolpath builder (frontend/src/lib/scene3d/toolpath*.ts): tessellate arc-tagged segments on READ for the wireframe, using seg.arc (center+dir) — so a coarse stream still renders smooth curves.
  2. Envelope scans (pipeline/warnings.rs count_cuts_outside): make arc-aware — sample the arc's extreme points, not just chord endpoints, so a coarse arc that bulges outside the work area / stock still triggers out_of_work_area / out_of_stock.
  3. Interactive per-segment sim indexing: verify the playbar/picker/scrubbing still line up when arc segment count drops (they index into the dense array today).
  4. THEN raise the preview::interpret arc step (e.g. 2°→ a coarser angle or a chord-tolerance-driven count) and confirm the sim stays analytic (arc descriptor drives the carve).

Acceptance: a G2/G3 program emits materially fewer ToolpathSegments; wireframe still smooth; envelope warnings still fire on an out-of-bounds arc bulge; sim carve unchanged (still analytic).
notes: PLAN (3 commits): A) warnings.rs count_cuts_outside arc-aware — sample each arc chord's cardinal bulge extremes (mirror sweep.rs t_of), so a coarse arc bulging outside work-area/stock still fires. B) frontend toolpath.ts tessellate-on-read: add pure tessellateArc(from,to,arc,stepRad) in toolpath_buffers.ts; build() emits sub-lines per arc seg, all owners/colors tagged seg=backendIdx; applyFade maps playhead segIdx -> render-line boundary via binary search on colors' seg field (also fixes latent disabled-op fade drift). C) arc-aware cumLen (sub-arc length, uniform playback) + raise preview.rs interpret step 2deg->15deg; update guard n_arc>=40 in arc_sweep_parity live test -> >=4 and the arcs.len()>=4 stays. Sim carve is chord-count-independent (analytic), so parity test unaffected (builds own baselines). gcode emission unchanged (G2/G3 direct) so no stable-hash impact.
close_reason:
Done in 3 commits. All four steps landed; acceptance met.

A (e7fc7e1) — Envelope scans arc-aware. warnings.rs count_cuts_outside now
samples each arc chord's cardinal bulge extrema (arc_chord_extremes, mirrors
sim::sweep t_of), not just endpoints, so a coarse chord that clears the work
area / stock at its crest still fires out_of_work_area / out_of_stock. Tests:
crest-past-+X trips while the same chord with arc:None stays silent.

B (45c0843) — Frontend tessellate-on-read. toolpath.ts tessellates arc-tagged
chords via new pure tessellateArc(from,to,arc,stepRad) at ~2deg/render-line, so
a coarse payload still draws round. One backend seg now maps to many render
lines; each carries its backend seg index so picking/fade/warning-tint stay
correct. applyFade maps the playhead's backend-seg boundary to a render-line
boundary via lowerBoundSeg (also fixes a latent disabled-op/raster-stride fade
skew). Pure helpers unit-tested; 881 vitest green, svelte-check clean.

C (07e19a2) — Coarsen interpret() 2deg->15deg (~7.5x fewer arc segments).
Sim carve is chord-count-independent (analytic), so parity + ball_nose
smoothness (0.02mm centerline variance) still hold at 15deg — those tests now
double as proof the coarse stream carves smooth. Guards updated (45->4,
40->4); quarter arc now 4..=12 chords. gcode emission unchanged (G2/G3 direct)
so no gcode-hash/golden impact; schema unchanged.

Step 3 (interactive scrub/pick indexing) needed no code: the sim's
partial_advance already carves the analytic sub-arc window within a chord
(58nl.4), cumLen/playheadToSegment index the same backend array whatever its

Deliberately skipped as negligible: arc-aware cumLen (chord under-measures its

title: True per-column incremental undercut void meshing (profiling-gated)
description: Residual of ivac-58nl.6.5.5 after the allocation-free emitUndercutMesh rewrite. That rewrite removed the GC pressure 6.5.5 named (per-neighbour Array.from + number[]->Float32Array conversion) and made a FULL re-emit 6-7x cheaper: a realistic 50x50-col cavity (25mm at 0.5mm cells) now emits in ~2ms, well within a 16.6ms frame, so 60fps scrub of realistic form-tool cavities no longer thrashes. What remains UNBUILT is true incremental meshing: on each advance the sim re-flattens the whole CSR and the driver re-emits ALL undercut columns; only the O(tool-footprint) columns near the cut actually changed. For PATHOLOGICAL cavities (>~100 undercut cols per side: >50mm at 0.5mm cells, or a very fine grid), the full O(n) re-emit + full GPU re-upload still exceeds frame budget (150x150 ~= 17ms emit; 300x300 ~= 85ms). Building it needs per-column dirty tracking (diff CSR + neighbour tops vs last frame, or thread the advance's affected-rect through refreshUndercutMesh) + a persistent geometry with per-column slots for partial GPU upload. Higher complexity/risk (stale-cache correctness) with real payoff only at extreme cavity sizes. Do NOT build speculatively: gate on a real GPU frame profile (no CNC/GPU hardware here per project memory) showing the full re-emit+upload is the bottleneck for a genuinely large form-tool job. Files: frontend/src/lib/sim/undercut_mesh.ts, driver.ts (refreshUndercutMesh).
design:
GATE-CHECK RECIPE (updated 2026-07-13). Cannot run here (no CNC/GPU hardware
per project memory 'no-cnc-hardware-available-for-validation'; GPU BufferGeometry
upload is unmeasurable headlessly). Run this on a GPU-backed browser to settle
build-vs-park, so the gate is a 10-min checklist, not a research task.

STATE CONFIRMED 2026-07-13: driver.ts refreshUndercutMesh (~L960) still reads the
FULL CSR every carve and calls undercut.build(...) over ALL columns; no
per-column dirty tracking, no perf seam. Emit CPU already characterized in 6.5.5
(50x50 ~2ms, 150x150 ~17ms, 300x300 ~85ms). The ONLY unknown this profile must
resolve is the GPU cost of swapping the whole BufferGeometry + re-upload per
frame -- the part no node/jsdom bench can measure.

STEPS
1. Build a genuinely large form-tool cavity: a wide T-slot/dovetail pocket sized
   so the sidecar exceeds ~100 undercut columns per side (>50mm at 0.5mm cells).
   Confirm scale live via Simulator.undercut_column_count() -- want many
   thousands of columns, i.e. past the 150x150/300x300 rows in the table above.
   (Realism caveat: real T-slot/dovetail features are NARROW; a 50-150mm-wide
   undercut cavity is already unusual. If you cannot construct one a real user
   would plausibly make, that itself argues for park/won't-fix.)
2. Chrome DevTools Performance panel (or the chrome-devtools MCP
   performance_start_trace, which IS available in-session but still needs the
   app running against a GPU browser + this large job -- not set up here).
   Scrub the sim timeline at 60fps: drag the scrubber or play at 1x.
3. Measure per advance frame: (a) refreshUndercutMesh CPU -- wrap undercut.build
   in performance.now() deltas or read the flame chart; (b) GPU upload /
   renderer.render cost attributable to the new BufferGeometry (GPU track + long
   Commit/Paint frames); (c) total frame time + dropped frames (fps meter).
4. DECISION THRESHOLD: if build()+upload consistently pushes total frame time
   past ~16.6ms (60fps) -- or the ~33ms 30fps floor -- for a cavity a real user
   would plausibly make, THEN build true incremental: thread the advance's
   affected-rect through refreshUndercutMesh for per-column dirty tracking +
   a persistent geometry with per-column slots for PARTIAL GPU upload (only the
   O(tool-footprint) changed columns re-uploaded). Scrubbing a large existing
   cavity is the case incremental fixes and a whole-field 'did anything change'
   guard does NOT (something always changes near the cut). If frames stay under
   budget (expected for realistic <=50mm cavities per the emit table), keep
   parked or close won't-fix -- 6.5.5's alloc-free rewrite already covers
   realistic form-tool cavities (~2ms at 25mm).
notes: Cannot advance here: gate is a GPU frame profile (no CNC/GPU hardware) and the issue forbids speculative building. Emit CPU already optimized (6.5.5) + characterized; the unmeasured unknown is GPU BufferGeometry re-upload. Sharpened the gate into a runnable checklist + decision threshold in --design so a future hardware session settles build-vs-park quickly. Stays OPEN/parked.

title: Sim STL export: truly watertight merge of interpolated top mesh + voxel undercut voids
description: dexel_to_stl_binary (landing #5.4) meshes undercut voids as voxel boxes (floor/ceiling/walls per column), matching the 3D preview exactly. But the dense top surface stays an interpolated point-sample mesh, so the seam where a void opens back to a neck is NOT a closed manifold: the interpolated top ramps from the neck floor up to the overhang top while the voxel void meshes the true cavity underneath — the two interpenetrate rather than share edges (same as the preview). A fully watertight STL needs the top surface near undercut columns to be voxelized/stitched to the void walls (or a marching-cubes-style unified surface). Out of scope for #5.4 (which targets preview parity). Only worth doing if a downstream consumer needs a manifold solid (e.g. boolean ops, 3D-print slicers that choke on non-manifold input).
design:
DEFERRED 2026-07-13 (gate not met). The STL export is user-reachable (File
menu "Export simulated stock as STL...", GenerateBar STL button ->
Simulator::export_stl -> dexel_to_stl_binary), but NOTHING in-repo consumes
it as a manifold solid: no boolean ops, no strict slicer. Documented uses are
visual inspection and regression-diffing a reference STL, neither of which
needs manifold. Pure 3-axis exports are ALREADY watertight (closed top +
perimeter skirt + bottom). Only form-tool (undercut) jobs are non-manifold.
Realistic external demand (3D-printing a simulated undercut milled stock) is
niche and slicer-auto-repaired. So this stays open until a concrete manifold
consumer exists AND states which tradeoff it accepts (see paths below).

== EXACT NON-MANIFOLD SEAM (crates/ivac-core/src/sim/stl.rs) ==
- push_shell_tris meshes field.top() (top of each column's highest span) as a
  SMOOTH interpolated surface: 2 tris per 2x2 sample block, adjacent column
  tops joined by a bilinear ramp.
- push_void_tris meshes interior voids (gaps between consecutive solid spans)
  as axis-aligned boxes: FLOOR (+Z at lower span hi), CEILING (-Z at upper
  span lo), side WALLS only over Z where the 4-neighbour is solid. Openings
  back to a neck (neighbour void over the same Z) are left UNWALLED by design.
- The interpenetration: at an undercut region boundary, an undercut column
  (top = overhang top) sits beside a column whose top is the neck floor (much
  lower). The smooth shell emits ONE steep interpolated tri-pair spanning
  overhang-top down to neck-floor. That ramp passes THROUGH the volume where
  the void ceiling + walls live. The two surfaces cross without sharing edges
  -> self-intersecting, non-manifold. The intentionally-unwalled void openings
  also never close against matching shell edges.

== PATH A -- voxelized-solid unified mesh (exact, blocky, cheap, low-risk) ==
Drop the smooth top; mesh the whole solid from the spans as per-column boxes:
  * per column, per solid span [lo,hi]: +Z face at hi, -Z face at lo;
  * per lateral neighbour: side wall over (this span) minus (union of neighbour
    spans) -- i.e. where this column is solid and the neighbour is air; off-grid
    neighbour = full wall;
  * the top face of each column's highest span IS the (flat, per-cell) top.
Watertight/hole-free with consistent winding; all faces on span-boundary planes
and walls split at neighbour span edges, so edges coincide -> no gaps. NOT
strictly 2-manifold at voxel corner edges (up to 4 faces meet where 4 columns
share a vertical edge) but slicers/most boolean engines accept it. BREAKS
3-axis byte-identity (stair-stepped top), so ship as a SEPARATE opt-in export
fn; keep dexel_to_stl_binary as the smooth preview-parity default. Cost: ~1 fn
mirroring push_void_tris over all spans + tests. This is basically LDNI/surface-
nets on the dexel field. Downside: a consumer wanting a SMOOTH manifold surface
is not satisfied -- trades non-manifold for non-smooth.

== PATH B -- smooth-top (+) void stitched surface (high fidelity, hard) ==
Keep the smooth interpolated top for the bulk; at undercut columns replace the
into-void ramp tris with: a top face at the column's true top, a vertical
curtain wall dropping to meet the void ceiling / neck floor at the region
boundary, stitched edge-to-edge with the void walls, plus marching-squares-style
handling of the 2x2 corner cases where undercut meets 3-axis diagonally.
Essentially dual-contouring / marching-cubes-lite over the top layer with
shared-vertex/edge bookkeeping to avoid T-junctions. Preserves smooth look AND
watertightness AND 3-axis byte-identity. Cost: large; risk: high (FP snapping of
interpolated Z to voxel planes, corner-case explosion).

== PICK-UP TRIGGER ==
When a real manifold consumer appears: ask whether it accepts a blocky top
(-> Path A, cheap/exact/low-risk) or requires the smooth surface (-> Path B,
large/FP-fragile). Do NOT build either speculatively -- the correct tradeoff is
consumer-dependent, which is why this is deferred rather than pre-built. Cheap
stopgap for a user who just needs "printable": the current non-manifold STL
feeds fine through any slicer's auto-repair; only undercut jobs are affected,
3-axis is already watertight.
notes: BUILT Path A (rethink for fitness of purpose, 2026-07-13). The rethink found the original gate ('a downstream manifold consumer appears') was unmeetable — no in-repo/roadmap consumer does CSG/strict-slicing on the simulated-stock STL (the nearest issues 6.5.2/6.5.3 depth-sample STL, tolerant of non-manifold), and the 3D preview already ships the identical non-manifold seam by design (5.4 preview-parity). The realistic trigger is a PRODUCT call ('should undercut exports render cleanly in a generic mesh viewer / feed a slicer?'), not a technical consumer. Maintainer chose to build Path A now. Delivered: dexel_to_stl_solid_binary(field) in crates/ivac-core/src/sim/stl.rs — meshes the whole solid as per-column voxel boxes from the spans (+Z@hi, -Z@lo per span; walls = this-span minus neighbour-span-union; floor intrinsic to the field's spans, no skirt param). Watertight (hole-free, consistently wound), NOT strictly 2-manifold at shared voxel edges (T-junctions; slicers/booleans accept). Ships as a SEPARATE opt-in fn; dexel_to_stl_binary stays the smooth preview-parity default (3-axis byte-identity preserved). 19 stl tests (was 12): vertical-ray parity reconstructs every column's spans (watertightness proof tolerant of non-2-manifold edges), sealed-undercut-void (the win over the smooth exporter), single-box + flat-field strict 2-manifold via directed-edge cancellation, step wall, top/bottom balance, determinism, not-byte-identical-to-smooth. Path B (smooth+void stitched) DROPPED as speculation — no consumer needs a smooth manifold. REMAINING: exposing it through transport + File-menu opt-in tracked in ivac-58nl.6.5.8.
close_reason: Closed

title: Streaming gcode output path (write-through sink) — unblocks unbounded raster + huge programs
description:
Today the whole gcode program is buffered in memory end to end: every PostProcessor accumulates lines into `out: Vec<String>` (e.g. gcode/linuxcnc.rs:23), `finish()` does `self.out.join("\n")` into one monolithic String, and the pipeline then runs preview::interpret_with_index AND estimate_from_gcode_with_rates over that full String. Peak memory is therefore O(total program size), dominated by the emitted gcode itself — not by any single driver's intermediate grids. A genuinely huge laser raster (run-length output ≈ one G1 per pixel in the worst case) can be hundreds of MB of Vec<String> + the joined String.

This is the architectural blocker behind z9zh's 'streaming emit' half: no driver-local change can stream output while the post buffers everything. A real fix is a write-through sink — PostProcessor emits to a `std::io::Write` (or chunked callback) instead of `Vec<String>`, and preview/timing run as streaming passes over the same stream. CONSTRAINTS to design around: (1) the op cache snapshots per-op line ranges via out_len/out_lines_clone_from/out_extend_lines (gcode.rs:359-376) — needs a streaming-compatible equivalent; (2) preview::interpret_with_index returns a GcodeIndex keyed by line; (3) every transport (cli/server/tauri/wasm) consumes the final String today. Large, cross-cutting; scoped as its own feature, not a raster follow-up. Found while working z9zh (2026-06-07).
notes:
INCREMENT 1 DONE 2026-07-17 (the write-through seam). Added crates/ivac-core/src/gcode/sink.rs: GcodeSink centralizes the line-buffer contract (push / len / clone_from / extend_from_slice / finish) that linuxcnc, hpgl, and grbl (via its embedded linuxcnc::Post) each re-implemented over a bare 'out: Vec<String>'. Added GcodeSink::write_to<W: Write> — the streaming primitive: emits the program line-by-line (join-with-trailing-newline semantics, empty program = lone '\n') WITHOUT materializing the monolithic joined String. finish() is now derived from write_to (single canonical output path). Migrated linuxcnc::Post: out: Vec<String> -> sink: GcodeSink; grbl came along free through composition (it delegates all buffer ops to self.inner). Still Vec-backed, so peak memory is unchanged for now — the seam is in place, the O(1) win lands in increments 3-4.

GATES: golden_corpus (byte-identity of emitted gcode) PASS; pipeline_cache 37 tests (op-cache out_* through the sink, incl. grbl) PASS; full ivac-core 954 lib tests PASS; clippy -D warnings clean; rustfmt clean; workspace build OK. 5 new GcodeSink unit tests (incl. write_to pinned to literal bytes).

FOLLOW-UPS FILED (children): 3j1p.1 migrate HPGL onto GcodeSink (last independent buffer); 3j1p.2 append-only Write-backed sink + op-cache-over-streaming (the hard core — random-access clone_from/extend are what a pure stream can't serve); 3j1p.3 stream through transports + streaming preview/timing (the payoff, gated on .2). 3j1p stays in_progress until the streaming goal is actually met.

title: WorkOffset Z field is in the UI but unused in sim/pipeline (reserved-only)
description:
The new abdk WCS UI in StockPanel.svelte exposes a Z input alongside X/Y, but the tooltip openly admits:

  title="Reserved — Z offset participates in the wire-format but the sim and pipeline currently use stock-top z=0."

This is friction: the user sees a Z spinner, types a value, sees it stick, and then it has no effect on generated gcode. The setting persists in the project file, gets hashed into the cache key, but doesn't actually shift cuts.

Two paths:
  a) Wire Z through. The pipeline + sim already consume work_offset.z_mm via the WorkOffset struct (it's in the cache key); the missing piece is whatever post / setup_resolver step expects 'cuts are emitted relative to stock-top z=0'. Audit what would change in gcode output (G54 z-shift, G10 L20 P<n>, etc.) and either wire it in or document why it's a no-op (e.g. some posts already handle it via the controller's G10 G54 line).
  b) Hide the Z input until the feature is real. Keep it in the wire format for forward-compat, but don't show a UI control for something that does nothing.

Recommended: (b) for the short term, (a) when there's a real demand. Showing a control that lies is worse than not exposing it.
notes:
Lives inside the uncommitted abdk WCS UI work — should be resolved at the same time as wiaconstructor-5kcj (commit-or-revert decision). If we land the UI as-is, we should at minimum re-style the Z row to look 'disabled' or flag it as reserved-future so the user doesn't waste effort tuning it.

Acceptance:
- Either Z affects emitted gcode in a documented way
- OR the Z input is hidden / clearly marked as reserved-not-active (e.g. disabled with explainer)
close_reason: Z spinner removed from StockPanel WCS fieldset. work_offset.z_mm stays in the wire format + cache key for forward-compat; UI no longer exposes a control that does nothing. svelte-check clean.

title: Remove _math_unused() stub functions or remove TWO_PI alias — pure slop
description:
Two identical no-op stub functions exist solely to silence unused-warning on the math::TWO_PI constant:

  crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:2021-2024
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    fn _math_unused() {
        let _ = math::TWO_PI;
    }

  crates/wiac-core/src/input/text.rs:601-604
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    fn _math_unused() {
        let _ = math::TWO_PI;
    }

Reality:
  - math::TWO_PI is defined in crates/wiac-core/src/math.rs:17 as 'pub const TWO_PI: f64 = std::f64::consts::TAU;'
  - It is used 4 times inside math.rs itself.
  - Every other reference in the codebase uses std::f64::consts::TAU directly (44 occurrences in cam.rs, gcode.rs, drill.rs, etc.).
  - There is no external consumer of math::TWO_PI.
  - The _math_unused() stubs are placebo glue from when the constant was migrated to math.rs — they should have been deleted at that time.

Fix (either-or):
  a) Delete the two stub functions. math::TWO_PI stays (it's used internally in math.rs).
  b) Delete math::TWO_PI too (replace its 4 internal usages with std::f64::consts::TAU) and then delete the stubs. Strictly less code.

Recommended: (b). The thin alias adds zero value over std::f64::consts::TAU and the rest of the codebase already prefers TAU.
notes:
Acceptance:
- _math_unused() is gone from both files
- 'cargo build --release' compiles clean with no new warnings
- 'cargo test -p wiac-core --lib' passes
close_reason: Cleaned up in commit. TWO_PI alias deleted (4 usages migrated to std::f64::consts::TAU). Both _math_unused() stubs and now-dead 'use crate::math' imports deleted from cam/offsets.rs + input/text.rs. -18 / +4 lines net. wiac-core builds clean.

title: audit 2026-05-23: Heightmap::new doesn't check cols*rows overflow on 32-bit usize (WASM32)
description:
FILE: crates/wiac-core/src/sim/heightmap.rs:36-49
REPRO: Coarsening regression leaves cols=70000, rows=70000 (4.9e9 cells). WASM32 usize=u32 (max 4.29e9). len = cols*rows overflows in release — wraps to small value — vec![top_z; len] allocates wrapped tiny buffer; subsequent cell writes index OOB into adjacent WASM memory.
CONSEQUENCE: Heap corruption on giant stock + small cell. cell_size_coarsened path intended to prevent this but if driver miscomputes or constructor called directly, UB.
FIX: Replace len calc with .checked_mul().expect('heightmap dim overflow'). Same for from_bbox.

description:

CONSEQUENCE: 0.0001 in = 0.00254 mm coordinate precision — borderline for sub-mil work (jewelry engraving, micro-milling). Some posts use 5-6 decimals.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-hpgl-no-finish-newline: single-line HPGL output joins all commands without separators
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/hpgl.rs:97-99 (`fn finish`).

**Problem:** `finish` joins with empty string `self.out.join("") + "\n"`. So an HPGL program looks like `IN;SP1;PU;PA400,0;PD;PA400,800;...PU;SP0;IN;\n` — all on ONE line.

HPGL is whitespace-tolerant (`;` is the actual statement separator), so this is legal. But several real plotters reject lines longer than 1024 chars (the protocol predates modern UART buffers). A 200-segment path goes well past 1024 chars. Several USB-to-RS232 HPGL converters also choke on a single mega-line.

The convention in HPGL output (per HP's spec and every commercial HPGL emitter I've checked) is to insert a newline after every `;`, OR after groups of ~80 chars. Today wiac emits one mega-line.

**Worked example:** a 300-point polyline produces a single ~5000-char line. Older Roland plotters reject it (input buffer overflow on lines > 256 chars). Modern HP DesignJets accept it but render slowly.

**Acceptance:** `finish` joins with "\n" instead of "". Or split at each `;`. Test hpgl_emits_one_command_per_line covers.
acceptance_criteria: Each HPGL command is on its own line.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P3+P4 gcode emission commits on main (cacb01b..ba7ba22). 557 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 pipeline|setup: tools list is iterated by linear find() in hot paths — quadratic on tool-rich projects
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline.rs:526-532, 638-647 and crates/wiac-core/src/pipeline/setup_resolver.rs (multiple project.tools.iter().find(|t| t.id == ...)).

**Problem:** Every per-op cache lookup, every header_setup_for and synthesize_op_setup invocation walks project.tools linearly to find the tool by id. With N ops + M tools, this is O(N*M). Projects with a tool library of 50-100 tools and 50 ops would do 2,500-10,000 linear scans every Generate. Not currently a bottleneck (tools typically <20, ops <30), but a polish item.

**User-visible failure:** Performance only, on tool-library-heavy projects. Not user-facing yet.
acceptance_criteria: Build a HashMap<u32, &ToolEntry> once per Generate, pass it through. Or memoize lookup inside Project. Bench-test with 100 tools / 100 ops; expect generation time to drop.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 drill: peck default fallback retract-and-re-enter rapids to previous depth (no clearance offset)
description: **Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:106-137 trait-default fn drill_peck (used by GRBL and any post that doesn't override). **Problem:** Between pecks the fallback issues 'move_to(None, None, Some(r))' to fully retract, then 'move_to(None, None, Some(current_z))' to re-enter at rapid to the just-cut depth. The comment at line 130-134 acknowledges this: 'A real machine would step off a hair to avoid rubbing'. Rapidding back down to the EXACT previous depth means the cutter momentarily lands on the chip-clogged bottom at rapid speed (potential side load on flute). **Real-world impact:** GRBL-style controllers running the fallback see this on every peck step. With a slow-moving smol-Z servo it's harmless; on a fast Z it can chip the cutter tip. **Acceptance:** Re-enter to (current_z + 0.5mm) rapid, then G1 to current_z at plunge feed. Pinned test confirms the small clearance and the plunge transition.
close_reason: Fixed in worktree-agent-ad8c441bd24d556ce commit 9fb3a9f. 8 audit polish items resolved + 4 snapshot tests added. Follow-up wiaconstructor-szy0 filed for true thread-whirling.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-feedrate-before-g0: F<rate> emitted before first G0 with no purpose (G0 ignores F)
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:452-453 (`program_begin` writes `post.feedrate(setup.tool.rate_h)` then `post.move_to(..fast_move_z)`).

**Problem:** The first emitted line after the unit/absolute setup is a bare `F<rate>` followed immediately by a `G0 Z<fast>` rapid. The F-word is irrelevant to G0 (rapid moves ignore F), but is set before any G1 has happened. This is mostly harmless — modal F carries forward — but it surprises operators reviewing the file ('why is F set before any cutting?') and on some controllers the F-word on its own line is rejected unless a motion mode is active.

LinuxCNC and GRBL accept F-on-its-own. FANUC accepts it. Mach3 sometimes warns. Heidenhain doesn't accept lone F.

Lower priority because it's modal carry, but it's also one of those 'why is this here' lines a CAM-review catches in the gcode output.

**Worked example:** the program prologue is currently:
```
G21
G90
F800
G0 Z5
M3 S12000
...
```

Preferred:
```
G21
G90
G17 G40 G94    (* if the modal-state fix lands *)
G0 Z5
M3 S12000
```

— defer the F until just before the first G1.

**Acceptance:** suppress the F emission inside program_begin; the first F-word appears next to (or just before) the first G1. Existing tests still pass because feedrate IS surfaced before every cut path in emit_offset.
acceptance_criteria: program_begin no longer emits F as the third line. Test gcode_no_premature_f checks the F-word does not appear before any G0/G1 in the prologue.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P3+P4 gcode emission commits on main (cacb01b..ba7ba22). 557 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 gcode-coolant-repeat: M7/M8 emitted on every offset, no de-duplication
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/gcode.rs:507-512, 325-330, 383-388 (`emit_offset` / `emit_drill_block` / `emit_vcarve_block` unconditionally call `coolant_flood` / `coolant_mist`). `crates/wiac-core/src/gcode/linuxcnc.rs:256-269` (coolant_flood / coolant_mist write the M-code without checking state).

**Problem:** Coolant M-codes have no state tracking. `coolant_flood(` writes `M8` every single time it's called, so a job with 100 offsets emits 100 `M8` lines. The controller is happy to receive duplicate coolant-on commands (no-op after the first), but the gcode file is ~100× larger in coolant directives than necessary, and the operator scrolling through the file thinks something is wrong.

Some shop controllers (notably some Mazak / Hurco posts) will RE-TRIGGER the M-function each time, dropping coolant pressure briefly each line. Unlikely on hobby controllers but possible.

**Worked example:** pocket op with 30 offsets and `flood = true`:
- Emits 30 lines of `M8` interleaved with cuts.
- Expected: one `M8` at the start, no further M8s until coolant changes.

**Acceptance:** add `last_coolant: Option<CoolantMode>` to `PostState`; coolant_flood / coolant_mist emit only on state change. coolant_off emits only when state is non-Off.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-offset op emits M8 exactly once. Existing tests pass. New test gcode_does_not_repeat_coolant covers.
close_reason: Fixed by integrated P3+P4 gcode emission commits on main (cacb01b..ba7ba22). 557 wiac-core lib tests pass.

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: pocket_cascade hard caps at 1024 rings, large pockets truncate silently
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:508 pocket_cascade_with_islands — `if rings.len() > 1024 { break; }`.

**Problem:** Defensive cap breaks silently at 1024 rings. A 1000x1000 mm pocket at 0.4 mm step needs 1250 rings; truncation leaves a 50x50 inner area uncut, no warning. Cap is needed against infinite loops but is too low for legitimate high-overlap pockets in soft materials.

**Reproduction:** pocket_cascade_with_islands(1000x1000, [], 0.4) returns 1024 rings; inner area silently uncut.

**Impact:** Silent truncation surfaces at machining time.
acceptance_criteria: Raise cap to 10k AND add convergence check on per-ring area shrink. Warning fires on either bound.
close_reason: Closed

title: audit 2026-05-22 offsets: rotate_offsets_to_approach_point picks nearest segment-start regardless of distance, no warning
description:
**Where:** crates/wiac-core/src/cam/offsets.rs:645 fn rotate_offsets_to_approach_point.

**Problem:** When the user's approach point is far from any offset, the function silently picks the closest vertex regardless of distance. The function's own doc-comment notes this — but no caller validates.

**Reproduction / evidence:** AP at (1000, 1000) for an offset in [0, 50] mm rotates to whichever vertex is closest to (1000, 1000) without warning.

**Why this matters:** Polish-grade: visible in preview but unreliable AP feature on big workpieces.
acceptance_criteria: Reject AP further than some bbox-relative tolerance from every offset and emit a pipeline warning. Test: AP at (1000,1000) for a [0,50] offset emits a warning.
close_reason: Closed

title: Scene3D: '?' or toolbar button to manually 'Fit view'
description:
Today fit-to-view fires only when imports.length changes (file added / removed). Users who panned away and want to re-frame the whole scene have no manual trigger — they'd have to remove + re-add a drawing.

title: Refactor: replace OpPropertiesPanel ':global(.props X)' rules with a shared CSS module
description:
OpPropertiesPanel.svelte has 53 `:global(.props X)` rules that style sub-components (op_properties/TabsSection / ProfileSection / PocketSection / DrillSection / VCarveSection / ChamferSection / ThreadSection / PatternSection). Svelte's component-scoped CSS makes :global() necessary so the parent's styles cross the child-component boundary.

The pattern is namespaced (always prefixed with .props), so the global pollution is bounded — but it's still an escape hatch that obscures which styles belong to which component.

## Audit findings
- AddTextDialog / ToolLibraryDialog / PostProcessorEditor / ShortcutHelp — 4 modal :global rules were just removed by switching Modal.svelte to a width/maxHeight prop pattern.
- App.svelte one rule (`.toolbar :global(.bar)`) is a single targeted cross-component override; acceptable as-is or fixed by giving GenerateBar a 'flat' prop.
- OpPropertiesPanel — 53 :global(.props X) rules. The hot path.

## Fix options
1. **Shared CSS module**: extract the 53 rules into `lib/components/op_properties/op-properties.css`. Each sub-component does `import './op-properties.css';` so the styles load with the chunk. Net effect: same global scope but in ONE file, removing 53 :global wrappers.
2. **Per-component scoped styles**: each sub-component defines its own scoped .row, .num-cell, etc. Means duplication across 7 components — DRY violation but pure component-scoped.
3. **CSS custom properties**: parent sets --row-padding etc., children read them. Most idiomatic but requires re-mapping every property used today.

Recommendation: option 1. Smallest change, biggest legibility win. Filed as a follow-up to today's modal-:global removal.

## Why deferred today
The 4 modal cases are isolated and clean to fix. The 53 OpPropertiesPanel rules need an audit pass + co-ordinated extraction, plus dev-time validation that the imported-CSS pattern plays nicely with Vite's build pipeline. Multi-hour task.
close_reason: Extracted 53 :global(.props X) rules to op_properties/op-properties.css, static-imported once from OpPropertiesPanel.svelte. .props prefix keeps namespacing; 0 errors / 0 warnings.

title: bww follow-up: reconcile fileTransform changes with stored op coords (approach points + tab placements)
description:
Filed during bww v1 (2026-05-19). Approach points stored as { x, y } in world coords don't move with the part when fileTransform changes — user has to re-pick. Tabs stored as { objectId, t } are mirror-sensitive (mirroring reverses contour traversal, so t→1-t).

## Fix paths

Option A: track delta between previous and new fileTransform; transform every stored approach point through the delta inside patchFileTransform. Tabs: detect mirror toggle, flip t→1-t per affected placement.

Option B: store ALL op-attached coords in raw-imported-space; transform at pipeline / display time. Bigger refactor but cleaner.

## Workaround for now

User workflow today: apply layout transform BEFORE adding ops with approach points / tabs. If transform changes later, redo the affected ops.

## Test plan

- DXF with profile op + approach point; toggle Mirror Y; verify approach point reflects across the same axis.
- Same with tab placements; verify each tab moves with the corresponding contour vertex.
close_reason: Closed

title: OSnap integration with tab placement
description:
64p generalized snap to a multi-target engine but the tab-placement code path (rt1.10) still uses its own ad-hoc snap logic in `projectGhostTab` — t-parametric projection onto the contour plus vertex+midpoint matching via `vertexAndMidpointTs`.

## Fix

Route the tab-placement preview through `findOSnap` so:
- Endpoint snap latches the ghost tab to a contour vertex (already in tab code, but inconsistent across kinds).
- Midpoint snap latches to the contour midpoint of a segment.
- Intersection snap latches a tab to a line-line crossing on the contour.

Tab logic still needs the t-parametric output (object_id + t) so the tab can stay attached to the contour through transforms. Approach: take the OSnap result's (x, y), then project it back to a (objectId, t) pair via `polylineProject` over the active contour. Removes the duplicate vertex/midpoint scanning in the tab path.

## Related
Spawn of 64p (closed). Lower priority because tabs already snap well in practice; the win is consistency + code dedup.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sim terrain destruction lags tool: switch to fractional per-segment carve
description:
## Symptom

The 3D simulation's stock destruction visually pre-empts the cutter. Most obvious on a Drill cycle: the full hole pops into existence the instant the playhead enters the drill segment, before the simulated tool has plunged. Looks like the material disappears under a tool that hasn't moved yet.

## Cause

`crates/wiac-wasm/src/sim.rs::Simulator::advance(prev_idx, next_idx)` carves the entire swept volume of every segment in [prev, next] as a single bulk pass. Granularity = segment, so any segment that takes more than one frame to visually traverse (drill, long cut, helix descent) destroys all of its terrain on the first frame that touches it.

## Fix idea: fractional per-segment carve

Add a sibling `Simulator::partial_advance(seg_idx, t)` where `t ∈ [0,1]` is the parametric position along the current segment. Carve only the volume up to t:

* **Drill segment** (XY constant, Z plunge): single tool-column at constant XY; carve down to `lerp(start.z, end.z, t)`. Cheap — one column.
* **Straight cut** (XY varies, Z constant): sweep the tool footprint from segment-start XY to `lerp(start_xy, end_xy, t)`. Cells touched ∝ t × full-segment footprint.
* **Arc / helix**: same shape, interpolate the arc parameter.

The existing `advance(prev, next)` stays for warm-restart / scrub-backward (it resets and replays). The frontend driver (`frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts`) calls `partial_advance` per render frame using `playhead - seg_start_index` as t, and switches to `advance` only when crossing segment boundaries or scrubbing.

## Map playhead → (seg_idx, t)

`project.toolpathCumLen` (the Float64Array of per-segment arc-length running totals from `setGenerated`) already provides the data. For a given playhead s ∈ [0,1]:

1. `s_len = s × project.toolpathTotalLen` — physical arc length.
2. Binary-search `toolpathCumLen` for the segment whose [cum, cum+len] contains `s_len`.
3. `t = (s_len − cum) / len`.

PlaybackBar already does step 1+2 implicitly to drive the playhead readout — would be lifted to a shared helper.

## Pros

* Visual coupling between tool tip and destruction matches a real CNC.
* Same total carve work; just spread across many partial passes. No new allocation per frame (the heightfield buffer is reused).
* Pure-additive change: existing `advance()` keeps working for scrub / reset.

## Cons

* More JS ↔ WASM boundary crossings per second (60 × number of in-flight partial segments). Each crossing today is a few µs but the rate goes up ~10×.
* `HeightfieldMesh::updateHeights` partial-upload range tracking gets finer-grained — many small dirty AABBs vs one bigger one per segment. Risk surface for a recurrence of the euxi-class partial-upload bug.
* Sub-segment carves on arcs / helixes need interpolation logic that today lives only in the toolpath emitter — duplicates the geometry math at carve time.

## Risks / unknowns

* Stepped voxel mesh memory pressure (already 1 M-cell default per auim) — need to profile per-frame upload sizes at 1 M and 4 M cells before merging.
* Backward scrub during partial carve: needs the bulk `advance` reset path to also reset partial state.
* Helix cuts have many tiny segments — partial carve might end up no-op per frame if t goes from 0 → 1 across one frame on small segments. Acceptable degenerate case (matches today's behaviour).

## Acceptance

* Visually: drill cycle's hole grows from the surface downward as the simulated tool plunges, not at start of segment.
* Same total carve cells visited at any given playhead position.
* No regression in 3D preview frame rate at the 1 M-cell default on the existing test corpus.
* Scrub-backward + auto-restart still works.

## References

* `crates/wiac-wasm/src/sim.rs::Simulator` — owns the heightfield + advance / reset.
* `frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts` — drives advance() from playhead changes.
* `frontend/src/lib/sim/heightfield_mesh.ts::updateHeights` — partial upload.
* `project.toolpathCumLen` / `toolpathTotalLen` (now on GeneratedState slice) — playhead → segment mapping.
* auim (3e6fdfe) — context on stepped voxel mesh memory cost.
* euxi (now closed) — prior bug from partial-upload range mismatches; lessons to remember.
notes:
Implemented per the original design.

WASM side (crates/wiac-core, crates/wiac-wasm):
- sim/sweep.rs: extracted run_segment_warnings + sweep_chord_carve from sweep_segment. New sweep_segment_partial builds a synthetic chord lerp(from, to, [t_start..t_end]) and carves only that slice. Diagnostics (fixture/holder/rapid) fire only on the first slice (t_start ≈ 0) so a 60 fps driver doesn't dupe warnings every frame. Pre-tessellated arcs come through as Cut-kind chord segments, so the same lerp handles arcs / helixes uniformly with no extra geometry math.
- wiac-wasm Simulator: added partial_advance(tool, seg_idx, t_start, t_end). Mirrors advance(): clears dirty AABB + diagnostics, calls sweep_segment_partial, returns AABB as Vec<u32>. Test-only partial_advance_inner mirrors advance_inner.
- Tests: 3 new unit tests (plunge grows with t, cut only touches swept chunk, rapid warning fires once).

Driver (frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts + playhead.ts):
- New playhead.ts::planAdvance: pure planner. Inputs (appliedSeg, partialT, targetSeg, targetT, total). Outputs (reset, finalizePartial?, bulkAdvance?, startPartial?, newAppliedSeg, newPartialT) plus null for no-op. Encodes the per-frame state machine.
- HeightfieldDriver state: replaced appliedHead (segment count) with appliedSeg + partialT (fractional within in-flight segment).
- advanceTo dispatches plan ops in order: optional reset → optional finalize-in-flight → optional bulk-advance over skipped segments → optional start-new-partial. AABBs from each WASM call are unioned per frame so HeightfieldMesh.updateHeights still gets one tight rectangle (avoids the euxi-class partial-upload risk).
- Snap rule: (N, 1) → (N+1, 0) when N is not the terminal segment so the next forward call doesn't bulk-re-carve.

Tests: 10 new planAdvance unit cases covering fresh-start, extend, finalize+bulk+start, no-finalize when partialT==0, snap behavior, terminal handling, backward scrub variants, and clean boundary case.

Acceptance:
- Visual: drill cycle's hole grows from the surface downward (verified by partial_advance_plunge_grows_as_t_advances). ✓ (test-validated)
- Same total carve cells at any given playhead (heightfield-monotonicity preserves correctness). ✓
- No frame-rate regression at 1M-cell default: union-aabb upload keeps to a single mesh.updateHeights per frame; per-frame WASM crossings up from 1 → 1–3.
- Backward scrub: reset-then-replay path preserved via the planner's reset flag.
close_reason: Implemented: WASM Simulator::partial_advance + driver state machine (appliedSeg, partialT) + planAdvance pure helper. Visual coupling between tool tip and 3D-sim destruction restored. 3 new Rust tests + 10 new TS planner tests. Full cargo workspace test, clippy::pedantic, wasm-pack release, svelte-check, vitest all green.

title: audit 2026-05-16: App.svelte hosts file-ops + menu logic — extract to lib/state/app-menu.ts
description:
`frontend/src/App.svelte` is 1307 lines. Most is layout + dialog state (acceptable for a top-level shell), but lines 117-150 (Tauri detection, file-ops wiring, menu callbacks) are business logic in a UI file.

## Fix
Move the file-ops + menu callbacks to `frontend/src/lib/state/app-menu.ts`. App.svelte imports and invokes; it owns no logic beyond reactive composition.

Pairs naturally with dqnd (centralize isTauri()) — the menu callbacks are the loudest `isTauri()` consumer.
notes: Reviewed: App.svelte's file-ops already delegate to state/file_ops.ts (cleaned up in dqnd). The remaining App.svelte script is menu open/close state, keyboard-shortcut dispatch, and reopen-prompt orchestration — each tightly coupled to component-local $state. A clean extraction would need a rune-store pattern (e.g. `appMenu` factory returning getters/setters) that's a separate design decision. title: 3D-sim audit #7: LOD downsampling for sub-pixel cells when zoomed out
description:
When the 3D camera is far enough that each heightmap cell maps to <1 screen pixel, drawing every cell wastes GPU work. A pyramid of max-pooled mip levels (2×2, 4×4, ...) chosen per-frame based on camera distance would reduce triangle count proportionally.

## Why deferred (the user-case analysis)

After #1 + #2 land, the bottleneck is gone for the common case:
* Small project (≤500k cells, ~1M triangles after sparse-wall stepped mesh) — fits comfortably in 60fps budget on integrated GPUs.
* Typical project (~2M cells, ~5M triangles) — borderline on integrated, fine on desktop.
* Pathological project (≥4M cells, hits the cap) — `maxSimulationCells` already throttles by halving cell density.

LOD only kicks in when zoomed out far enough that the perf gain matters AND the user spends time there. In practice CAM users stay near fit-to-part zoom while watching playback, occasionally zooming in to inspect cuts — not zooming out. The implementation cost (multiple level buffers, swap logic, downsample passes, memory doubling) is high for marginal benefit.

Revisit if profiling on a hand-held / low-end GPU shows it actually matters.
design:
## Architecture: static LOD pyramid

Pre-build N parallel HeightfieldMesh instances at successively coarser resolution (default 4 levels: L0=full, L1=2×2 max-pooled, L2=4×4, L3=8×8). One is added to the scene at a time; level swap is a single Object3D add/remove. Memory cost = sum 1/4^k ≈ 1.33× the single-level baseline.

**Pool with MIN, not MAX.** Heights drop as we carve — MIN-pool keeps the deepest cut visible at every LOD. MAX would hide cuts at coarse levels (undesirable).

## Two LOD triggers, one mechanism

1. **Distance** — project cell-width through camera → pixel size. When cell < ~1 px, bump to coarser level.
2. **Render budget** — new AppSettings.maxRenderTriangles (default 2M). Pick smallest k where `cells / 4^k * 6 ≤ budget`.

Pick the coarser of the two. 20% distance hysteresis to avoid pan-induced thrashing.

## Strict upgrade over MESH_CELL_HARD_LIMIT

Today MESH_CELL_HARD_LIMIT halves SIMULATION cell density when cells exceed the cap — degrading carving accuracy. LOD keeps sim resolution intact and only degrades RENDER. Keep maxSimulationCells as the WASM-heap cap; add maxRenderTriangles for the LOD ceiling. Drop the hard limit's role in cell-size scaling.

## Dirty-AABB propagation

advance() returns an AABB in L0 cell coords. The driver re-pools that span (padded +1 to absorb pool-block edges) from L0 → Lk for the active level only, then calls mesh.updateHeights(Lk.data, Lk.aabb). Per-frame cost is O(dirty_area), same as today, with the +33% mem overhead being one-time.

## Phases

1. **Pyramid construction** — HeightfieldMeshPyramid wraps N HeightfieldMesh + a per-frame `active` level. Includes the L0→Lk MIN-pool pass.
2. **Driver-side level swap + dirty-AABB fan-out** in sim/driver.ts.
3. **Level selector** — distance + budget + hysteresis, called from Scene3D's render loop.
4. **Edge rebuild per active level** + settings UI for maxRenderTriangles + tests.
5. **Profile** on integrated GPU at 4M cells across zoom levels; tune thresholds.

## Risks

- Edge rebuild is O(verts) per active level. Active verts ≤ budget by construction, so bounded.
- Backward scrub must reset every level mesh — fan out from existing reset path.
- MIN-pool loses sub-pixel-wide cut traces at coarse LOD; acceptable since at that camera distance they were sub-pixel anyway.

## Files touched

- frontend/src/lib/sim/heightfield_mesh.ts — pool helper + pyramid class
- frontend/src/lib/sim/driver.ts — pyramid integration + level swap + dirty-AABB fan-out
- frontend/src/lib/components/Scene3D.svelte — level selector wired to camera distance + budget
- frontend/src/lib/state/project.svelte.ts — AppSettings.maxRenderTriangles
- frontend/src/lib/components/SettingsDialog.svelte — UI knob
notes: Deferred per audit analysis — over-engineering for the typical CAM use case. The 4M-cell cap + the fixes in #1/#2 already keep the GPU within budget; LOD's marginal benefit doesn't justify the multi-level mesh complexity.
close_reason: Implemented phases 1-4: HeightfieldMeshPyramid with min-pool semantics, budget-driven minLevel (skip unaffordable fine levels), hysteretic LOD selector wired to camera-change in Scene3D, new AppSettings.maxRenderTriangles + SettingsDialog input. Cell-density halving via MESH_CELL_HARD_LIMIT dropped — sim accuracy preserved. 8 new unit tests, all 234 vitest + 396 cargo-core tests pass, svelte-check 0 errors. Profiling follow-up tracked in 9gpa.

title: audit 2026-05-2: errors.rs vs PipelineError — two parallel error universes
description: \`pipeline.rs:135 PipelineError\` enum + structured \`crate::Error\` via \`to_structured\`. The structured form drops the panic backtrace. Either fold \`PipelineError\` into \`crate::Error\` (with appropriate kinds) or document \`to_structured\` as a lossy boundary explicitly. Today the duplication is silently leaky.
notes: Reviewed: PipelineError carries Cancelled as a sentinel for cooperative cancel semantics that crate::Error has no equivalent kind for. The to_structured() boundary (documented after luf1) is now the single conversion point — HTTP/Tauri/WASM transports all flow PipelineError → Error::structured at the boundary, never inside the pipeline. Folding the enum into crate::Error would scatter the cancel-semantics dispatch across every callsite. Closing the issue's spirit (no silent leak) is satisfied by luf1; deferring the full fold as the cost/benefit doesn't pencil.
close_reason: Closing per existing notes (audit 2026-05-16 review): the spirit of the issue — no silent leak between PipelineError and crate::Error — is already satisfied by luf1, which made to_structured() the single, documented conversion point at HTTP/Tauri/WASM transport boundaries. PipelineError::Cancelled has no equivalent kind in crate::Error and exists specifically for cooperative cancel semantics in the pipeline; folding it would scatter the dispatch across every pipeline callsite. The cost/benefit doesn't pencil.

title: Touchscreen on-screen numpad / keyboard for shop-floor PCs (dlg_Numpad)
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.9 against Estlcam.

Estlcam targets touchscreen shop-floor PCs. dlg_Numpad and dlg_keyboard pop up an on-screen numeric / text input when the user taps a number / text field. wiac assumes desktop with keyboard.

For users running wiaconstructor on a touchscreen panel-PC next to the machine, this is the difference between 'works' and 'needs a USB keyboard'.

Concrete plan:

1. SettingsDialog: new 'Input' section with 'On-screen numpad / keyboard' checkbox (default off — desktop users don't need it).

2. Frontend: a global event handler on every <input type='number'> and <input type='text'>: on focus, when the setting is on, render an overlay numpad / keyboard sized for finger input.

3. Two components: NumPad.svelte (digits + decimal + +/- + Enter + Backspace) and OnScreenKeyboard.svelte (QWERTY layout, language follows project.settings.language).

title: Insert-pause op (M0 optional stop) for manual intervention between operations
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.5 against Estlcam.

Estlcam's _I.cs Is_Pause (line 3394) checks if an item is a Drill-typed item with Name starting with 'Pause'. When it is, the op emits:
  M5 (spindle off)
  M00 (Pause name) — optional stop, controller waits for user
  M3 (spindle on)

Hobby workflow: 'Drill bores done, now I want to verify chip clearance before the finish pass starts'. The user inserts a pause op between Drill and Profile; the controller halts; the user inspects; presses cycle-start; the program continues.

wiac has no equivalent. The user would have to hand-edit the emitted gcode, which loses on regenerate.

Concrete plan:

1. project.rs: add OperationKind::Pause { message: String }. No source, no tool, no params besides message.

2. pipeline.rs op loop: when kind is Pause, emit M5 + M00 ($message) + M3 in the post-relative way (each post processor's pause helper). Pre-existing M6 toolchange machinery is the model.

3. Per-post: linuxcnc supports M0 / M00; grbl partial (M0 stops, M00 same); hpgl irrelevant.

4. Frontend OperationsList add-picker: 'Pause' entry with a small clock icon. When kind === 'pause', OpPropertiesPanel shows just a 'Message' text field (rendered to the operator console).

5. Tests:
   - pipeline_emits_m0_for_pause_op
   - pause_op_skips_tool_validation
   - round-trip serde

Estimated: 2 days. Tiny but the feature unlocks a real workflow.

References:
- Estlcam decompile: /tmp/estl_decomp/CAM/Estlcam/_I.cs lines 3394-3411.
close_reason: Closed

title: NGC + HPGL importers — let users preview existing programs / cutter-plotter sources
description:
Surfaced by parity audit wiaconstructor-o90.4.

Estlcam has DXF + STL + raster importers. wiac today has DXF + SVG. The file picker advertises hpgl/plt/ngc/stl (see rt1-related issue on filter bug) but the backend doesn't implement them.

Two importers worth filing:

**NGC (G-code re-import)**: the user has an existing program from another CAM tool or a hand-tweaked file; wants to preview it as a wiac toolpath, scrub the playhead, verify on the sim.
